Counting truncation lowers two measured budgets: a heatmap in a stacked pane holds 3 rows (was 5), and a waterfall in a side pane holds 2 steps (was 7) before a three-word step name is cut.

- **`flowchart`, a free-form chart written as a list.** Every item is a shape, a sub-list of shapes makes its parent a group (a tinted background, like a Mermaid subgraph), and an arrow in a row connects shapes by name: `A -> B`, `A => B` for the heavy main path, `-label->` for a labeled line, `&` to fan out. A trailing code span styles what it follows: eight outlines (`:box` `:square` `:pill` `:diamond` `:circle` `:cylinder` `:io` `:doc`), the chart palette's eight slots (`:c1`…`:c8`, or one channel with `:fill-cN` `:border-cN` `:text-cN`), a status word, dashed or dotted lines, `open` / `dot` / `cross` heads, and `:loose` for a line that stays out of the layout. The chart draws its own key from what it uses; a bracketed span below the list renames entries. A `>` blockquote under a shape is a note on a dotted tether. `lr` / `tb` pin the direction, and otherwise the chart takes whichever direction sets the type larger. The browser lays the chart out with the shared elbow router, which weighs every line against one cost: a line never runs through a shape or along another line; crossings, a label that would collide or sit across a group's border, and a line through a group's title cost most; then balance and symmetry (an org chart's children hang from their parent's side middles, a fan is drawn as a mirror image, and a diamond is met at its points); then fewer turns.
- **`lint:deck` reads flowcharts** with the same grammar the render uses, and names each mistake: a shape style on a line, a sub-list under a connection, a shape in two groups, a near-duplicate name, an arrow that is probably a comparison.
- **A backslash escape of `-`, `=`, `<`, `>` or `&` now survives into the rendered HTML** as `<span data-esc>`, so a flowchart can tell an escaped `\->` from a real arrow. It renders exactly as before.
- **A flowchart or state chart pasted into a Studio deck that had none now draws at once.** The preview frame loads the layout engine only if the deck already holds such a chart when the frame is built, so a pasted chart showed as plain tiles until a reload. The runtime now fetches `lattice-dagre.js` from beside itself when a chart needs it.
- **Typing into a large flowchart in the Studio no longer holds the keyboard.** The Studio's editing preview lays a chart out in a background worker when it redraws one it has already drawn, and shows the last drawing until the new one is ready. On a 17-shape chart, sixteen fast keystrokes now go through in 1.2 s instead of 2.5 s. Exports and every other preview still draw synchronously.

- **Trama has its own mark and a live demo at `/trama`.** The mark is the weft: two
  right-angled terracotta threads woven over and under each other around the family hub,
  with one straight gold thread for the main path (`docs/public/trama-{mark,mark-min,lockup}.svg`,
  palette locked in `engineering/decisions/2026-07-18-sibling-brand-system.md`). The page runs
  the real kernel on every keystroke: type rows and watch `layout()` place and route them,
  pin the direction across or down, turn on the wrapping chain, and drag a box (or nudge it
  with the arrow keys) to watch `route()` weave the lines again, with all ten
  `geo.quality` counters on screen. Trama joins the site's Libraries menu.

- **Code packages get the slide's plain facts beside its HTML.** A package's `slide` now carries `facts`: the slide's classes and directives, its title, its content as blocks (headings, paragraphs, nested list items, tables with their captions, code, quotes, images), all of its text, and the palette token names every theme defines. Text is plain (`**Kickoff**` arrives as `Kickoff`, math as its TeX), and beside it each heading, paragraph and list item carries `runs`, which mark what the text loses: a code span as a value, a `{DONE}` pill as a state, bold, a link's address. A loose list item keeps each of its paragraphs. The running header and footer are not content; they are in the directives. `facts` is the stable input: a package that draws something new from the author's content (a Gantt chart from dates, a map from place names) reads it and never parses Lattice's markup. `slide.html` stays for packages that tweak the finished slide, and its markup may still change. The CLI and the Studio read the facts the same way, before the package runs, and the package gets them frozen.
- A code package's output no longer has to repeat every class the engine put on the slide (`content`, `form`). The door puts back any it leaves off, so a package that builds its section from the facts draws instead of failing with a note.

- The chart family is a plugin (`lib/plugins/chart-family/`): it offers the `kernel` extension point,
  and every chart fills it from the `kernel` block its manifest already carries. A host can switch
  it off (`createEngine({ plugins: { disabled: ['chart-family'] } })`, `--disable-plugin
  chart-family`): each chart slide then shows the list it was written as, carries
  `data-lattice-off="chart-family"`, and the render reports `plugin/component-needs-plugin`. On a
  host that narrowed its default set, a chart slide class loads the family. Default renders are
  byte-identical.
- Plugin manifests gain `contributes.extensionPoints` (spec/LPM.md §3.3): a slot a plugin offers and
  components fill. Filling a slot is requiring the plugin.

- **A zip plugin runs through the CLI.** `lattice packages add <plugin folder or .zip>` installs a plugin that arrives as data (one fence, one `render.js`, its CSS), `lattice packages trust plugin/<name>` approves its code at its SHA-256, and a deck that lists it under `plugins:` draws its fence in the PDF, the HTML and the other exports. A deck that uses it before approval fails with the digest and the command to run. A plugin whose fence is a code language or a shipped plugin's, or that declares `render.exec`, `payload` or `vendor`, is refused at `add`.
- **`lattice packages add` says when it leaves something out.** A package folder or zip that held files below its top level (a plugin's `shared/`) now reports them instead of dropping them silently.
- **`lint:deck` warns about attributes after a plugin fence's name.** ```` ```gantt title="Q3" ```` ignores `title="Q3"` today; the warning (`plugin-fence-attributes`) says so, because the words may take on a meaning later. A listed zip plugin is no longer reported as an unknown plugin.

- **A zip plugin the deck did not list shows a placeholder, and one click approves it.** Where a block of an installed plugin's fence sits in a deck whose `plugins:` line does not name the plugin, the preview draws a Nacre-toned placeholder with the plugin's name, and a strip above it offers **Approve**: it adds the plugin to the deck's `plugins:` line and records consent for the plugin's code in this browser.
- **A plugin can no longer take over a code language.** A plugin whose fence is a highlight.js language (`python`, `js`, …) is refused at import, and a plugin that conflicts with another in the same zip is refused with the reason instead of being saved and silently not run. A renderer with a lone UTF-16 surrogate is refused (two files could share one approval).
- **A plugin's output loses a `name=` attribute and an empty `<img src="">`.** Both are dropped in the Studio and the CLI door.

- **A zip plugin can draw its fence in the Studio.** Import a plugin's `.zip` in the Library (it stays in this browser: never in a deck, a `.lattice` project or a backup), list it in the deck's `plugins:` front matter, and approve its code from the notice above the preview. The fence then draws in the preview and in Share → PDF, in a sandbox with no network, through the same door and the same rules as the CLI's (the 400-fence allowance, the output cap, the `lp-<name>` id and class namespace, no drawing on a slide a shipped pass rebuilds from its text). A plugin the deck does not list runs nothing. The Plugins tab lists installed plugins with Remove.
- **A plugin that returns a media element with no source no longer breaks Share → PDF.** An empty `<video>`, `<audio>`, or `<img>` / SVG `<image>` with no address is dropped from a plugin's output in both doors (a `data:` image stays); before, the Studio's PDF writer failed on it.
- **A plugin zip may not declare `render.exec`, `payload` or `vendor`.** The gate refuses them by rule (`refusePluginCode`), not by prose.

- **A guide to writing a code package** (`/guides/code-packages/` on the docs site). It covers the one shape Lattice runs, the `"facts": 1` line every code package's manifest needs, the slide a transform receives (`facts` as the stable promise, `html` as the markup it may adjust), `kit.measure`, the worker it runs in (no document, no network), the class and address rules its output follows, how a user approves it, and a complete package to copy. An integration test installs and renders that example from the page itself, so the guide cannot drift from what runs.

- **A code package declares which slide facts it reads.** Its manifest carries `"facts": 1`, the version of `slide.facts` it was written for, and Lattice hands it facts in that version. A code package without the line, or with a version this Lattice does not know, is refused by name at `lattice packages add`, at render and at the Studio's Library import, with the line to add. So the day the facts change shape, a package written for the old shape is kept on it or refused plainly, never handed a shape it cannot read.
- `tools/verify-code-sandbox` is a guided check a tester runs on Linux, macOS or Windows: each step shows a command, runs it, checks the result and asks the tester to confirm, and the tool writes a report to send back. It proves a code package is refused until approved, reaches no server once approved, and that the OS sandbox Lattice reports is the one the system applied.

- **Segno has a live demo at `/segno`, and joins the site's Libraries menu.** Segno is a new
  general-purpose grammar engine: it refuses any grammar it cannot read in one pass, and writes
  the parser it accepts as straight-line code. The page runs the real library: write a grammar
  and parse with it, try the inline notation against example slots, and see how it compares
  with six parser libraries on the same inputs. Nothing in a deck uses Segno yet.

- Hub-spoke takes icons: `{icon=database}` on the hub or any satellite, branch or leaf draws that icon inside its disc, and `{icon=database, icon-only}` drops the label beside the disc while the name stays its hover title and its accessible name. The icon's ink clears 3:1 against every disc kind in all 14 palettes in both modes, under every chart finish and in `mode: sketch`. A chart with no icon written renders exactly as before, and so does one whose deck switched the icons plugin off.
- A component that owns its list rows' inline code can now say how deep it reads (`rowDepth` on its Segno slot). Hub-spoke owns its hub, satellite and `tiered` leaf rows; pills and icons in a satellite's detail sublist still render as they do anywhere else.

- **Inline icons**, as a plugin (`lib/plugins/icons/`, on by default). `^{database, c3, lg}` draws
  one of 265 curated icons (Tabler, MIT, plus two of ours) at the size of the text around it,
  framed by default or bare, in the sparks' three looks, with the deck's chart colors; `{S3, icon=bucket, c4}`
  leads a pill with one. An `icon:` front-matter register and `icon-*` slide classes set the frame,
  look and corners, axis by axis. No vendor logos: `lint:deck` coaches `^{s3}` to `^{bucket}`
  beside the service's name (`icon-literal`). The drawings load only for a deck that writes an
  icon. Demo: `examples/inline-icons.md`. A deck that does not load icons leaves `^{…}` and an
  icon-only pill as code on every surface: the engine marks the span `data-lattice-off="icons"`, as it marks an
  unadmitted plugin's fence, and the browser runtime leaves it alone.
- The plugin host gains four contribution points: `inline` (an inline-code kind in the host's
  dispatch table), `services` (a function other code asks the host for), `registers` (a
  front-matter axis register declared as data) and `data` (data loaded only when the deck uses the
  plugin). The inline-code dispatcher is now that table; marks, pills and sparks render
  byte-identically through it.
- The Studio's class completions offer the `icon-*` slide classes (framed/bare, the three looks,
  the two corners), from the same modifier vocabulary the linter reads.

- The Studio editor completes icon names: typing `` `^{da `` (or `icon=da` inside a pill or a chart record) offers the icon names that start with it, aliases included, and each row shows the icon's drawing. The drawings load the first time the menu opens with an icon in it.

- Plugins load explicitly. A deck can name the plugins it needs in a front-matter import list, `plugins: [math, mermaid]`, and a slide class that requires a plugin (`math`, `diagram`, `scene`) loads it. Every shipped plugin stays on by default, so a deck with no `plugins:` key renders exactly as before, and listing a plugin that is already on changes nothing. The list only adds: no deck can switch a plugin off. In the engine and the CLI bake, using a plugin's syntax no longer decides whether the plugin loads; it decides only when its library loads and its bake runs, and `render()` reports `plugin/used-not-loaded` for a plugin a deck uses that nothing loaded.
- The Studio's deck settings have a **Plugins** tab. It shows each plugin, whether it is on for this deck and why (on by default, listed in this deck, or needed by a slide class), and its checkbox adds or removes the plugin in the deck's `plugins:` line, so the choice travels with the deck into every export.
- `lint:deck` warns `unknown-plugin` on a `plugins:` name no plugin has, and `render()` reports it as the diagnostic `plugin/unknown-plugin`. `createEngine({ plugins: { defaults } })` lets a host narrow the default set.

- **Trama gains a radial layout, `radialLayoutKernel()`**: one node in the center, the rest on one ring around it (`solveStar`) or on two (`twoRings`), joined by straight bands, with a label placer that puts every label where it touches no node, band, other label or stage edge, and reports what it cannot place. Like the rest of Trama it knows nothing of what it lays out; a chart passes what its marks mean as plain numbers. It needs no dagre and no browser, and closes over nothing, so it could also ship as browser source. The paint paths, collision tests and label placer are general; the two solvers are hub-spoke's, calibrated to its linter's envelope.
- **`hub-spoke` now lays out through Trama.** Every hub-spoke chart draws the same bytes as before: 3,636 outputs (the demo deck, the gallery and 600 seeded slides per stage, in the monospace and the sketch face) hash identical before and after. `hub-spoke.transform.js` keeps what the marks mean and the drawing, and shrinks from 1,336 lines to 811. `_chart-family/arrowhead.js` is gone; its triangle lives in the kernel.

- `lint:deck` asks for one spelling per deck (`mixed-spelling`): a deck that writes one meaning two
  ways — an icon as `^{db}` and `^{database}`, a waterfall closing on `total` and `sum` — gets a
  warning on each minority span, and `--fix` rewrites it to the spelling the deck uses most.

- A backslash before a broken pill (`\{A|B}`, the escape `pill-literal` suggests) now keeps the
  literal text without leaving a visible backslash, as it already did for a broken spark. Braces
  that belong to another language (a backslash inside them, a regex interval like `{2,3}`, a
  `{{template}}`) are not pill attempts and keep every character as written.

- **Segno: `attempt(x, { max, next })`, a bounded ordered choice.** It reads `x` on at most `max`
  characters and keeps it only if a `next` character or the end of the input follows; otherwise
  it rewinds, and as an `alt` branch it hands the character to the branches after it. The checker
  accepts that overlap and no other, and refuses nested attempts, `until()` inside one and an
  attempt that can match nothing, so every grammar that compiles still parses in linear time.
  Both runtimes (`compile()` and `generate()`) support it, and a grammar without one generates
  byte-identical code. A flowchart-row grammar built on it reads all 442 corpus rows and
  200,096 fuzzed rows exactly as `splitRow` does (`npm run parser:bakeoff:flow`).
- **Fixed: Segno lints a grammar of thousands of rules in linear time.** A chain of 2,000 rules
  whose choices grow took 6.5 s to lint and 4,000 overflowed the stack; 8,000 now take about
  150 ms. The "expected …" text in a parse error is built only when a parse records an error,
  `lint()` no longer builds a parser, and the checker's walks no longer recurse, so `lint()` reads
  10,000 levels of nesting (`compile()` still overflows building one rule nested about 3,000
  deep, as before). Every error message reads as before.
- **Fixed: `lint:deck` warns when a pill label needs quoting.** Since pills moved onto Segno, a
  label holding `|` `=` `[` `]` `{` or `"` (`{A|B, tag}`, `{5" screen}`) leaves the span as plain
  code, and nothing said why. The new `pill-literal` warning names the reserved character and the quoted spelling
  that renders (`{"A|B", tag}`). It stays silent on chart points, journey steps and the other
  brace records a component reads; across the shipped decks it fires 0 times.
- **Fixed: on a slow phone, the Playground's Explore walk bar no longer paints under the toolbar
  and then jumps to the foot.** The page is parsed and painted in chunks, and a chunk that ended
  inside the bar painted it before the deck pane below it existed. The bar now takes no space
  until the pane is parsed.

- **Added: a Privacy page on the docs site, linked from Live.** The Live start card and the lobby already said that people in a session, and the public servers that help browsers find each other, see your IP address. Both now end in a **Who sees what** link to `/privacy/`, which says it in full: who sees the address and when (a guest's knock connects before the host admits), what the STUN servers and the relays that pass connection messages see, that edits and chat go browser to browser, that no backup server (TURN) carries a session, and what you can do about it.

- **Edit a deck together, live, in the Studio.** A new **Live** button on the left toolbar (and
  a *Collaborate live* row at the top of the Share sheet) starts a session and copies an invite
  link. The person who opens it sees who invited them and to which deck, types a name and
  **knocks**; you admit or deny them from a toast or the Live panel. Once in, everyone edits the
  same source with colored carets, the slide navigator shows who is on which slide, you can
  **follow** someone or **bring everyone to your slide**, and the panel carries the session's
  chat — bubbles like the Architect chat, with times and "is typing…", in one order for
  everyone (the host numbers each line), so someone whose connection drops for a moment (a
  phone switching tabs) shows as reconnecting rather than "left" and comes back to the lines
  they missed (the last 500 at most). A line sent while the host is away waits as "Sending…"
  and goes out when it is back. The session runs on the host's clock, so once a phone has
  synced (within a second of joining) its own clock setting does not matter. Up to
  **4 people**. Undo only undoes your own edits. A guest keeps a copy of the deck
  when the session ends, and reloading the same tab (host or guest) picks the session back up;
  closing the tab ends your part in it. Audio and video are not in this release.
- **No server of ours is involved.** Edits travel browser to browser over WebRTC; peers find
  each other through public Nostr relays (Trystero 0.26.0), and the link's secret lives in the
  URL fragment, which browsers never send anywhere. The link also carries a fingerprint of the
  host's signing key, so nobody else holding it can pose as the host. Treat the link like a
  key: it works for as long as the session runs, from wherever it was pasted (an email, a chat
  thread), and removing someone does not change it — they can knock again, and you decide. Office networks that block
  direct browser-to-browser traffic will not connect. (`docs/src/components/studio/live/`)
- **New library: Tavola** (`docs/src/lib/tavola`, `@laticent/tavola`) — the invite link, the
  knock-and-admit handshake, the roster gate (only admitted members send or receive the
  document, and view-only members' edits are refused by every honest peer), the cap and rejoin
  by token, with the transport and document passed in. `checkTavolaBoundary` keeps it
  dependency-free apart from its Trystero adapter. `tools/live-session-check.mjs` drives a real
  two-browser session on demand.

- **Graph charts cross fewer lines.** When a flowchart's or a state chart's layout routes
  with a crossing, Trama now tries dagre's other two rankers. When a wrapped state chart's
  layout crosses, Trama tries moving one line break by one shape, then turning the lines the
  other way. It keeps either change only when that clears every crossing, and reading order is
  kept. On the shipped state-chart slides, crossings fall from 9 to 4. A layout that routes
  clean is unchanged, and live typing in the Studio is as fast as before.
- **`rearrange`, a new state-chart and flowchart modifier.** A chart that wraps onto several
  lines places its states in the order you wrote them, so a side state written last (Blocked,
  Escalated) can end up far from the state it leaves, with lines running back across the
  chart. With `rearrange`, the chart may move such a state beside its neighbor, ordering by
  the graph (Coffman–Graham), but only when that crosses fewer lines or takes a line off a
  state it ran through. A chart with nothing to fix draws as before. On the shipped state-chart slides, crossings fall from 4 to 2. It is
  off unless you add it: `<!-- _class: state-chart rearrange -->`.

- **Editable `.odp` and `.pptx`: cards, tags and rules are native shapes now, grouped with their text.** `--editable` (and the Studio's editable export) used to lift only the words; every box stayed pixels in the slide picture. Calco's reader now also lifts each plain box (a solid fill, solid borders, round corners, one outer shadow) and draws it as a real shape. A tag carries its own word inside it, a border that differs from its card's outline becomes a line along its edge, and a card is grouped with everything inside it (`draw:g` in the `.odp`, `p:grpSp` in the `.pptx`), so dragging a card moves its tag, its rule and its text together and leaves no ghost behind. A box that would cover something the picture keeps above it (an icon, a chart, a `::before` tag, list bullets, unread text) stays in the picture whole, and so do gradients, textures, sketch strokes and elliptical corners. On card-tags, 41 shapes come out; on the 58-slide jargon gallery, 370; each `.pptx` validates against the OOXML schema and the Open XML SDK with zero errors.
- **The /calco page and the composed PDF's html-to-image camera now draw CSS counters, as the Studio does.** Their captures passed html-to-image no property list, so a slide numbered with `counter()` would have captured as 0. All three captures now take one list from `lib/core/capture-style-properties.mjs`. The /calco demo slides write their numbers as text, so their exports do not change.

- `@laticent/lattice/slides.css` and `@laticent/lattice/palette/<name>.slides.css` (33) are the packed slide form: link one of each around the markup `render()` returns, and a page draws slides the way the CLI does, with a palette swap that needs no second render. Measured on six galleries (51 slides): 51/51 match in `indaco` and in `cuoio-dark`, linked from `dist/` and through a Vite 8.2.2 build; the two published files before this (`css` + `palette/<name>.css`) matched 0/51. 16:9 only and no panes; use `render()`'s own `css` for `size: story`, other canvases and panes.

- **Added: `tools/palette-slide-parity.js`, the harness that measures whether an importable
  stylesheet draws a slide the way the CLI does.** It diffs every slide against the CLI's HTML
  render under three arms: `render()`'s own stylesheet, an unpublished packed palette candidate,
  and the published engine-plus-palette pair. `--bundled` adds a fourth arm for a stylesheet a
  bundler built, such as a Vite build of the candidate. It is on-demand and backs the open decision in
  `followups.d/2580-p3-packed-palette-form.md`.

- The Playground's Galleries sheet has an "All examples" section: a searchable list of every `examples/*.md` deck by title, with its slide count. Choosing one opens it in Explore, so a per-feature demo deck can be reviewed without pasting its source. A new example appears with the next build — there is no list to edit. The decks are static files fetched on demand (the index when the sheet first opens, a deck when you pick it), so the Playground page does not carry them: +0.6 KB eager JS gz measured.

- **Added: step between photos in the `collage` lightbox.** With a photo open, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (or PageUp and PageDown), Home and End, a horizontal swipe, or the two new arrow buttons move to the collage's other photos in written order, with a "2 / 5" counter. It works on the Playground, the Studio and the exported HTML player. A deck with a collage gains the two input rules (`keyAction`, `swipeAction`) in its player script; a deck without one is unchanged to the byte.

- **Added: the collage lightbox steps with a mouse wheel and jumps with the number keys.** A decisive plain-wheel flick moves to the next or previous photo, with the deck's own wheel gate and cooldown, so one flick is one step. Ctrl or cmd plus wheel still zooms, and a trackpad pinch never steps. While a photo is zoomed the wheel does not step. The keys 1 to 6 jump to that photo while one is open; a number past the set is ignored, and with no photo open the digits stay the deck's. The Studio, Playground and exported HTML player all take both, from the shared transport kernel (`createWheelGate`, new `digitAction`). A collage deck's exported player grows by about 1.5 KB; other decks are byte-identical.

- **Added: zoom the open `collage` photo.** A two-finger pinch, ctrl (or cmd) and the wheel, a trackpad pinch, the `+` `-` `0` keys or a double click zoom the photo from 100% to 500%; a one-finger or mouse drag pans it, and a percentage pill returns it to fit. It works on the Playground, the Studio and the exported HTML player, and uses the one shared zoom rule (`createZoomGesture`) the Studio preview already uses. A deck with a collage gains that rule in its player script; other decks are unchanged to the byte.

- The Library has a **Videos** tab. Add a clip from the Library's picker (MP4, MOV or WebM, up to 50 MB) and it shows with a poster and length and plays in place. A video you send in the Studio chat is now saved there too, so it keeps its poster after a reload and Regenerate sends it again. Before, the chat held the clip in memory for the one message and lost it on reload.
- A workspace backup carries videos and a restore puts them back, checking each file's bytes against its type.
- A slide cannot show a video yet, so a deck that writes `asset:<video name>` shows the missing-image placeholder, and the chat is not offered a video to put on a slide.
- Opening a `.lattice` file now skips any video in it and says so: a `.lattice` carries photos only.
- A video's location, make, model and creation date are removed when you add it, as they are from photos: an MP4 or QuickTime clip has those metadata boxes overwritten in place (no re-encoding, same file size), and a clip restored from a backup gets the same treatment. A clip whose structure cannot be read is refused with a message. Some cameras write a position per frame into a timed track or a caption track (GoPro, Insta360, Sony, DJI with captions on); that is not removed.

- **Compose edits every inline kind an installed plugin declares.** A kind that declares no `slot` used to stay plain code in Compose; it is now one tappable object whose panel holds its record as a line of text, and a change writes `@kind{…}` whole. Compose and the plugin door now share one rule for what a whole `@kind{…}` call is (`lib/core/named-span.mjs`), so Compose never writes a span the door would not draw.

- A chart data row written as one `{…}` record (`- Uptime `{4.2M, target=5.0M}``, `- EMEA `{4.2}``, a heatmap cell `{4.2}`, a matrix-grid cell `{done}`) now draws what its old spans drew, on all 16 charts in the chart authoring model, in the engine, the runtime and the narration. A pill in the row's label, in its `>` description, in a detail row (per the chart's `rows.nested`), in a later list or in a later table still renders as a pill. A record reads numbers as written (`{1200}`, not `{1,200}`, since the comma separates fields), so a funnel shows `1200` where an old-form `1,200` showed the comma. A chart list inside a `>` quote does not read records; lint `chart-row-record-unread` says so, and also when a badge before a row's label holds a value too, so the row's record is not read (`` `{1}` North `{40}` ``, `` `1` North `{40}` ``; `{1, circle}` reads as a badge).
- A `{N}` that is the only value in a chart data row's first paragraph is now that row's value (it was a pill the chart did not read); on `map` any `{word}` is now the region's value, and on a `matrix-grid` slide a sole-cell `{done}`, `{partial}` or `{todo}` (any case) is a state, not a label pill. A deck that writes no such record renders as before. Narration reads a record the way the engine does, a record in a double-backtick span and one in a quoted table included (it used to skip both).
- Lint `chart-table-unescaped-pipe` warns on a bare `|` inside a table cell's `{> …}` description, which adds a cell and shifts every value after it, and names the fix: write `\|`.

- **`@code{indent=2|4|tab, quotes=single|double}`** — the code record and the deck's `code:` default set the formatter's indentation and string quote. Prettier, ruff and sql-formatter honor the indent; the quote changes only languages with a choice (JSON, Java and SQL keep theirs). A block that sets `indent=` draws a tab that wide (`tab` is four columns) instead of the browser's eight.
- **`lint:deck` measures code lines on plain slides.** `code-line-clipped` now covers a fence on a slide with no layout, not only `code` and `compare-code`; it no longer reports a `wrap` block, which cannot clip, and it counts a tab at the block's `indent=` width.
- **Code block options in Compose.** With the caret in a fence, a **Code block options** button beside the language picker sets the block's `@code{…}` record with switches and boxes: title, line numbers, focus and mark lines, diff, wrap, copy buttons, keep formatted, and the formatter's indent, quotes, width and SQL dialect. Only the edited word changes, so the rest of the record stays as written.

- `lint:deck` now warns on a front-matter key Lattice does not read (`unknown-key`, with a did-you-mean: `finsh:` → `finish:`), and on a wrong value for `theme:`, `size:`, `motion:`, `motion-style:`, `motion-speed:`, `player-motion:`, `glossary:`, `logo-on:`, `logo-style:` and `profile:` (`unknown-<key>`). Before, a typo in any of them rendered the default without a word.
- `lint:deck` now warns on a `tint-*` or `mark-*` class that paints nothing (`unknown-treatment`), and on `tint-corner` or `tint-edge` without a placement it accepts (`treatment-placement`).
- Every front-matter key now lives in one engine table, `lib/core/deck-settings.js`. The Studio editor completes from it, so `icon:`, `avatar:`, `plugins:`, `greeting:`, `closing:` and `code:` now complete, and hovering a key shows what it does, its values and its default.
- `npm run build` writes `dist/schemas/front-matter.schema.json`, a JSON Schema of the same table, for editors outside the Studio.
- LFM 1.1 §2.3 now lists `spectrum-card:`, `spectrum-card-edge:`, `spectrum-trim:` and `avatar:`, each with a shared conformance case.
- `dist/engineering/conformance.md` is the generated checklist of what each kind of thing owes, starting with deck settings; `npm test` runs its clauses.

- A component contract runs in `npm test`: every folder under `lib/components/` must have its manifest and stylesheet, its shared sheets wired into the build, every variant drawn in its gallery and known to `lint:deck`, coherent `variantAxes` and `capacity`, a label in the card-row corpus, and `cards` declared if the corpus says it has a card row. `stats`, `actors` and `kpi` are recorded as debt with a reason.
- Component CSS may not add physical `left`/`right` declarations: 44 components carry 402 today (shorthands, positions and case included), recorded per component with a ceiling that may only fall, so the layouts can mirror under `dir="rtl"` later.
- `npm run conformance:render` renders every gallery slide (all 75 components, 858 slides) and reports overflow, axe violations, the card-row trigger's hit and miss rate against the hand-labeled corpus, and WCAG AA contrast in every shipped palette, light and dark. It is report-only and not part of `npm test`: the nightly runs the whole matrix, and each PR runs `--changed` (the components its diff touches, on three palettes) into the job summary.
- The conformance debt ledger checks an entry's date against git: debt may be added only in the commit that adds its clause, a ceiling may only fall, and a deleted-and-re-added entry counts as added later. A shallow clone cannot answer and answers nothing.

- Share → Webpage can now ask the reader before it loads another site's pictures, as the CLI's `--player-consent` does: under "Embed pictures from other sites", tick the sites the deck uses, and the file shows a "Load pictures" banner; nothing loads until the reader presses it, and with scripting off the pictures are listed as links.

- **`asset:<name>` now renders in the CLI.** `![](asset:team-shot)` reads `assets/team-shot.jpg` from a folder beside the deck, the same name rule the Studio Library uses. A name the folder lacks draws the missing-picture stand-in instead of a dead reference, and `lint:deck` warns (`asset-missing`) with the slide. Decks that never write `asset:` are unchanged.

- `lattice packages fetch [dir]` downloads the npm plugins listed in a project's `lattice-plugins.json`. Each entry names an exact version and pins the bundle's SHA-256. The command reads the one bundle file out of the registry tarball and keeps it only at its pin. It never runs `npm install` and never runs the bundle. It then asks for your approval, naming the list, the package, the version and the hash. A deck that lists the plugin under `plugins:` draws it from that cache, in the locked sandbox page, with no network. An npm plugin is not approved, and does not run, where the OS sandbox reads OFF or cannot be determined. `lattice packages trust plugin/<name> [dir]` approves one later.
- An npm plugin bundle that holds an HTML-like comment (`<!--`, or `-->` at the start of a line) is refused. A browser reads one as a comment where the admission check did not.
- An npm plugin bundle whose bytes are not UTF-8 text is refused. Its approval and its render would otherwise hash different bytes, so it could never run.

- A sandboxed plugin can now hand back values besides its drawing. It declares them under `contributes.returns.fields`; each is a `word` from a list, a `number` in a range, a `flag`, plain `text` (256 characters at most) or `markdown` with no HTML, link, image or fence (2,000 at most). The host checks every value and writes it as `data-returned-<plugin>--<field>` on the slide's `<section>`. One value outside its declaration disables the plugin for the whole render, with a warning in the CLI and a note in the Studio. The declaration is part of what you approve, so a plugin that widens it asks again.

- Plugins: a plugin can be **embedded** (`"embedded": true` in its manifest, in-tree only). The host admits it on every render, and no `plugins:` list, host narrowing, `disabled` setting or `--disable-plugin` turns it off. A zip or npm package that declares `embedded` is refused.
- Plugins: a plugin manifest can declare an `untagged` inline kind (the bare record `{…}`); only the embedded plugin may claim it, and only one may.
- Docs: the Plugins page gains a Pills page (a demo with three live examples, and the Learn guide) and the site navigation lists it. The hub now says there are eight plugins and that pills are always on.
- Build gate `checkHandRolledPills`: no stylesheet outside `lib/plugins/pills/` may read a `--pill-*` or `--lat-pill-*` token, counted per file against a measured allowlist that only shrinks (a stale entry fails too).
- Pill interface property `--lat-pill-cap`: how much of the surrounding text a pill may fill (0.85 by default). A component whose pill sits beside a caption sets it to 1 so the pill matches the caption instead of undercutting it.
- Pill interface properties `--lat-pill-case` (uppercase labels) and `--lat-pill-tracking` (letter spacing, with the optical-centering indent following it), for components whose pills read as stamps.
- Pill interface property `--lat-pill-size`: a component whose type follows something other than the surrounding text (a chart label sized from its grid cell) states the pill's font size outright.
- Plugin classes have names: **embedded** (always on), **essential** (comes with Lattice; what the docs called a "shipped plugin"), **external** (from an author). `lib/plugins/README.md` and `spec/LPM.md` §3.1a say what each can do. The pill's full contract moves from `base.docs.md` to `lib/plugins/pills/pills.docs.md`.
- The demo deck `examples/pills-plugin.md` replaces `examples/universal-pill.md` (which described the removed universal trailing-code rule): one pill, placed and tinted by cards, a KPI tile, an owner row, a legal update, a roadmap header and a glossary.

- Share → Webpage now says when a deck's fences will ship as source because their plugin is off ("1 mermaid fence will ship as source: the Mermaid diagrams plugin is off for this deck"), in the options panel before the export and in the completion message after it. Nothing shows when the plugin is on or the deck has no such fence.

- **Added: every Studio export that draws diagrams says when a fence will ship as source, and can turn its plugin on.**
  PDF, PowerPoint, LibreOffice, Images, Webpage, the Marp bundle and Print now show the same notice when a deck holds a
  fence whose plugin is off, and the completion message repeats it. Its **Turn on** button lists the plugin in the
  deck's `plugins:` front matter, so the next export draws the diagram (#2758).

- `@laticent/mosaico` (unpublished) gains a `grid` strategy (uniform cells, the column count chosen to make the items biggest) and a `justified` goal for `rows` (every row fills the width at one height, as a photo gallery does). The library's demo page has a tab for each.

- `@laticent/mosaico` (unpublished) gains a `template` strategy: give an arrangement such as `V(0,H(1,2))` and items with a shape, a shape range, floors, caps, a weight and `fit: 'contain'`, and it returns exact boxes with exact gutters. Nothing in Lattice renders through it yet.

- **`lattice migrate meta <deck.md>` rewrites a deck's directive comments as slide records.** Each slide's comments
  become one record per scope on the same lines, so nothing below them moves: `<!-- _class: cards-grid dark -->` and
  `<!-- _footer: Q3 -->` become `<!-- {layout=cards-grid, class=dark, footer=Q3} -->`. A class that opens with a component is
  written as the typed `layout=` field. `--check` writes nothing and exits 1 when a deck would change; line endings and a
  byte-order mark are kept. A directive inside a list item or a blockquote is left as written and named, because a
  record there is not read. (`lib/cli/migrate-meta.mjs`, `lib/cli/meta-migrate.mjs`)

- **Added: slide metadata as one record in a comment.** A slide's settings can now be written as a record: `<!-- {layout=cards, footer="Q3 review"} -->`, or the long form `<!-- @meta{…} -->`. Field names are kebab-case (`focus-steps`, `background-color`); `layout`, `variant`, `universal` and `modifiers` build the slide's class, and a plugin register is a field too (`icon=bare`). A record sets its own slide; add `carry` for "from here on". A record writes exactly the `<section>` the directive comments it replaces write: all 354 example and gallery decks render byte for byte the same when every directive is rewritten as a record. Directive comments (`<!-- _class: cards -->`) still work; a later change in this line of work retires them, with a codemod.
- **Added: notes in a record, and a reader note.** Long text goes on `key: |` lines inside the same comment. `note` is the speaker note; the new `reader` field is a note for whoever opens the exported file: PDF note annotations, PowerPoint notes and the notes sidecar carry it as a paragraph labeled `Reader:` after the speaker note, and the HTML player keeps it as its own hidden channel. `--strip-notes` removes a record's `note` and keeps its `reader`; `--strip-say` removes its `say`. A comment cannot hold `-->`, so a note writes `--\>` (and `--!\>` for `--!>`).
- **Breaking:** a comment whose first line opens with `{` or `@meta{` is now a slide record, not a speaker note: `<!-- {TODO} check the numbers -->` used to be the slide's note and now reports `meta/record` and sets nothing. Write such a note without the leading brace, or put the brace on the line after `<!--`, which stays a note. None of the shipped decks has one.
- A record that does not read, sets a deck-only key (`theme`, `lang`, `size`), names an unknown field, or a comment written in the engine's internal form (`lat-meta`, `lat-note`, `lat-pane`) is reported in the render's diagnostics (`meta/record`, `meta/forged`) and applies nothing; it never falls through to the speaker note. `lint:deck` reports a record inside a list item or blockquote (`meta-not-own-line`), including one indented under a list item with no marker on its line.
- **Added for plugin authors: the `source` contribution** (spec/LPM.md §3.3, 0.13-draft): an embedded, in-tree plugin's pure transform of the deck at engine entry, before plugin admission. Additive under `api: 1`; a zip plugin may not declare it, so existing plugin approvals are unchanged.
- **Export to Marp keeps records working.** The Marp bundle (CLI and Studio) writes each record back as the directive comments Marp reads, quoting values Marp would read as YAML, with the speaker note as a plain comment and the reader note labeled `Reader:`. Checked with `@marp-team/marp-core` on the exported demo deck.
- **Fixed:** a speaker note reading `$100` in a Studio-shared HTML player no longer corrupts the slide markup (the note was injected with a replacement string, where `$1` is a backreference; the CLI had the same fix).
- **Fixed:** the Studio's code-package notice now offers a package used only inside a `_pane:` pane (its marker reader matched only the `pane:` alias).

- The Studio's slide map now keeps a still picture of each slide it has shown live, and shows it on tiles past the live budget and under a tile whose live picture is still loading, so a fast scroll through a long deck shows slides rather than sketches.

- **See what the others in a live session are doing.** Each person's row in the Live panel now says whether they are in Coach, Views, Library, Fabricate, reading, or presenting, next to their slide. What someone asks the AI never shows.
- **Follow goes wider.** Following someone on a desktop also opens the panel and view they have open, except Fabricate. If you are typing, you get a Go button instead of being moved. Opening another panel or view yourself stops following, as moving to another slide already did.
- **See each other's pointers.** When people are on the same slide, each one's mouse pointer shows over it, with their name and a ring where they click. It is only drawn: it can never click, type or scroll anything of yours. Hiding your slide hides your pointer too, and a finger on a touch screen sends none.
- **Two new switches in Your settings:** "Show what I'm doing" and "Show my pointer", both on by default.

- **See AI work in a live session.** The people list shows when someone is asking the AI (never what they ask), and the chat says when someone applies an AI edit, with a link to each slide it changed. A finished AI reply has "Share with the session", which posts that question and answer to everyone as a card.

- **Comments sync in a live session.** A comment you write on a slide appears for everyone in the session under your name, and stays on everyone's copy of the deck afterward. Anyone can resolve a comment; only its writer, or the host, can delete it. Comments you wrote before the session stay yours until you press Share in the Live panel.

- **The presenter's narration reaches everyone on the call.** While the host presents to everyone and is on the call, the narration their Present reads goes out with their microphone, so everyone on the call hears the presenter's voice from the presenter's own playback, with no second speaker in the room. It still goes out when the presenter mutes their microphone, which then silences only their voice. Only the presenter's browser makes the narration.
- **A presentation shows the deck as it was when it started.** While presenting to everyone, the host's and the followers' Present keep the deck from the moment it started, so an edit made meanwhile cannot shift slides under the people following or add to the narration the presenter pays for. Edits show when the presentation ends.

- **Present to everyone in a live session.** The host can choose "Present to everyone" in the Live panel's session menu. Everyone who is not typing opens Present on the host's slide and follows along as the host moves; someone who is typing gets a Join button instead of being pulled away. A Present the room opened ignores the keyboard until you click into it, so a keystroke meant for the editor cannot jump slides or go fullscreen. Moving on your own stops following, and "Rejoin" brings you back. When the host stops, everyone's Present closes. Someone who already has Present open is offered to join rather than moved, and someone who joins the session mid-presentation joins it where it is.

- **A live session shares the saved themes and finishes the deck uses.** A guest used to see fallbacks wherever the host's deck used a saved theme or finish from the host's own Library. The host now sends the ones the deck used when sharing started: themes pass the same safety check as a theme in a file from someone else, and finishes travel as recipes each browser rebuilds. A guest holds them only for the session; nothing is added to their Library, and their exports are unchanged.
- **The Live panel lists what the others don't have yet.** When the deck uses a saved theme, finish or custom component the session does not have, or the host's own site palette is a saved theme, it stays listed under "Not shared yet" with a Share button until the host shares it. Custom components are shared by name only, which stops the others' editors from flagging them; their code is not shared yet.

- **Show me plays for everyone in a live session.** When the host presses a tour, it starts on every member's screen at the same moment; someone who is typing gets a Watch button instead. In a session the tour builds its deck on a throwaway practice deck, so the shared deck, the session's look and everyone's Library stay exactly as they were, and the shared deck comes back when the tour ends.

- Present together now plays the presenter's narration for a member who is not on the call. When the presenter presents to everyone with Voice on, a member's Present asks for each sentence's clip by the hash of its text, and the presenter sends back what it already holds, compressed to mp3. The member's Voice button reads "Tap to listen" until they tap it (the tap that unlocks sound on an iPhone), and a listening member's Present starts each slide the presenter reaches without ever moving them. No member calls a voice engine or uses a key of their own, and a presenter's key is never spent for a request: the host serves only clips it has already made, only for slides near the presenter, one at a time, at most 4 requests a second per member, and a member checks each clip's mp3 header (bitrate, sample rate and length) before decoding it, and a member keeps at most 96 clips (24 MB) in memory, dropped when the presentation ends. A member on the call with the presenter still hears it there, once.
- `tools/live-narration-check.mjs` runs this on two real browsers (Chromium, Firefox or WebKit; `--iphone` and `--ios-gate` for a touch tap and a stand-in for iOS's gesture rule) against a stub voice endpoint, and checks that sound reaches the guest's audio output and that the guest never calls the voice endpoint. `tools/live-narration-call-check.mjs` runs the case where both are on the call.

- Live: when the person you follow has Present open, following them opens Present for you at the same slide, page and view. It is quiet: the keyboard does nothing until you click, it starts muted, and it never narrates on your key. Closing it keeps it closed until their Present ends and another starts. A Present you opened, or one the host started for everyone, is never replaced; if you are typing you get a "Join" instead.

- Live: following someone now also opens the Slide or Deck settings panel they have open, and the section inside it (Look, Brand, Notes and so on). It follows the same rules as a panel: never while you are typing (you get a "Go" instead), desktop only, and opening a section of your own ends the follow.

- Live: the settings row the person you follow is in wears a ring with their name, the Live panel says where each person is in Deck, Slide or Setup settings ("in Deck · Brand", "in Setup · AI"), and a row someone just changed shows as "changed Theme" for a short while. These show a place and a row name only: never what was typed or picked, and Setup is only ever shown, never opened for you.
- Live: a person's `changed <row>` line sits under their name in the Live panel, and a new on-demand check (`tools/live-follow-check.mjs`) drives two real browsers through Follow: the Deck panel and section, the row ring, Present, and Setup shown but never opened.
- Live: following someone ends, with a notice, when they leave or when you move yourself (a click or key, not a panel finishing loading); a Present that following opened closes when the follow ends, and stays closed if you close it. Awareness is harder to abuse: a forged clock no longer survives a removal, caret updates are bounded per sender, and the Present place follows "Show my slide". The ring is drawn only in the same panel as the person you follow, and Go and Join prompts wait while an Undo is showing.
- Live: following from the Deck panel to the Slide panel on a section both have (Look) now moves the Slide panel too; a Present you closed stays closed across an earlier absence; and Follow's "Go" prompts no longer stay silent after an Undo has faded.

- **Compose edits a checklist.** A slide whose list items lead with a state marker (`- [x] done`, and the other five: `[ ]` `[-]` `[!]` `[?]` `[/]`) used to lock read-only, which held 40 of the 96 locked slides in the shipped decks. The serializer now keeps a list item's leading marker as written, the same way it does in a table cell, and a click on the marker chip flips `[ ]` and `[x]`. `[X]` (GFM's checked box, not one of the six) still locks the slide. (`docs/src/lib/compose/deck-markdown.ts`, `deck-source.ts`, `ComposeView.tsx`)

- **Compose edits slides that hold math or a block of HTML.** Inline math (`$x^2$`), a `$$` display block and a block of HTML used to lock their slide read-only, which held 51 of the 96 locked slides in the shipped decks (30 for math, 21 for HTML). Each is now one unit that writes its source back byte for byte: a math span and a math block are drawn as the formula (the engine's KaTeX, as native MathML), and a tap opens a panel with a TeX field and a live preview; a block of HTML is drawn as a labeled box and opens a source field. The panel refuses what would break the deck (a blank line inside an HTML block, a `$` inside inline math) and says why. The same constructs inside a list item still lock the slide, because modeling them there would change the render, and so does a slide with an escaped dollar (`\$5`) or an HTML block of the `<?php` / `<!DOCTYPE` kind. (`docs/src/lib/compose/raw-block.ts`, `raw-objects.ts`, `math-draw.ts`, `docs/src/components/studio/RawPanel.tsx`, `lib/playground/katex-provider.js`)

- Compose edits a note in place. Opening a `say:`, `describe:` or plain note puts its words in a field with the caret already in it (on a touch screen the note opens for reading, and a tap on the words starts writing, so the keyboard does not rise on every tap); Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or leaving the field writes them, and Escape restores them. Remove stays beside it. Only the words change: the comment's opener, closer and `say:` or `describe:` prefix keep their bytes, and a note that is opened and left is never written. A plain note that would end the comment early, read as a directive (`footer:`, `class:`, `_class:`), a panes marker or `stress-slide`, or a `say:`/`describe:` note that would switch channel or be empty, is refused with the reason and the words stay in the field. The three channels now draw different icons (speech bubble, eye, folded note).
- The Insert menu gains **Motion**. It opens the Library on its Motion scenes; a pick there adds the scene as a slide after the current one, the way it always has from the Library.
- In Compose, Backspace at the start of a block just after a note (or Delete at the end of the block just before one) now selects the note first; a second press removes it. A caret that only sits beside a note, as after picking a slide in the rail, no longer costs the author the note. Typing, pasting or composing text while a note is selected goes to the nearest text instead of replacing the note, and a note on a folded slide opens its panel in view.
- Folding a slide while a note is half typed writes the words first (they were lost), and Shift or Ctrl with Backspace or Delete beside a note also selects it first. Picking a slide that holds only a note leaves the caret on that slide.
- The note field keeps a note's line breaks: a note that spans lines is shown without its hanging indent and written back with it, so changing one word changes that word only. Any slide control (delete, fold, add, settings) writes half-typed words before it acts; Undo and Redo step the history as it stands. Tapping another note, or the open note's own pill, writes the open one first; words the note refuses keep it open with the reason. Choosing Motion again brings the Library back to its Motion tab after the author moved to another one.

- Compose opens an installed plugin's inline object (`@gantt-bar{…}`) in a panel drawn from the kind's `slot` in its manifest: a text field for a text word, chips for a vocabulary, a toggle for a flag, numbered slots for a deck color. A pick changes only that word. The span shows as written in the editor (the plugin's code runs only in the preview's sandbox); a parameter the writer cannot take (a list, a range) is named, with "Edit as text" for it. A plugin cannot take an in-tree name (`pill`, `spark`, `icon`, `avatar`).

- **The photo picker can add a photo.** A new author with an empty Library no longer has to leave Compose to find the Library first: "Add a photo" in the picker imports through the Library's own flow (the same format dialog, the same naming, saved to all decks), then puts the new photo on the slide. The import loop now lives in one place, `media-import-batch.ts`, and the Library uses it too. (`docs/src/components/studio/PhotoPicker.tsx`, `Library.tsx`)

- Compose now shows what an outside change changed. When an AI edit, a rename, an Inspector edit or an undo rewrites text while you are not typing, the changed line fades in with a tint and an accent rule on its leading edge, the exact new words get a stronger tint a moment later, and both fade out slowly. Where words were only deleted, a thin accent mark stands where they were. With reduced motion the tint holds and goes without a fade. A change out of view shows a "N changes above" or "below" chip that scrolls to it on a tap; nothing scrolls on its own. The paint is decorations only: it never changes the deck's bytes or the undo history.

- `lint:deck` now judges a one-block prose slide (`big-number`, `citation-card`, `collage`, `image`, `redline`, and their registers) at a venue on a square, tall or strip deck by the words that canvas holds, not only on a wide one: a tall `big-number` holds 3 words at `venue: hall`, not 12. The rows are `venueCapacity.prose.families`, measured by `tools/calibrate-venue-prose.js`, and `check:venue-conformance` renders each slot at its row to hold it true. Count budgets are still wide-only.

- **Added: `@callout` on `flowchart` and `state-chart`.** A note names a shape or state by `for=`; the chart rings it, numbers it, and sets the words under the figure (or beside it with `side=beside`), in the Studio and in every export. The state chart's `inline` variant keeps the callout paragraph as written. Demo: `examples/callouts-schedule.md`.

- **Segno can cap a parse's tree, label node kinds with roles, and report facts about a
  parse.** A grammar's `maxNodes` stops a parse with `code: 'nodes'` instead of growing its tree
  without limit; `node(kind, x, { role })` labels a kind, exposed as `grammar.roles` and a
  generated `ROLES` table; and `facts(spec, input, result)` reports which cap a parse hit, the odd
  characters in the input (NUL, lone surrogates, bidi controls, zero-width and C1 characters, a
  bare CR, a BOM) and the ranges no node covers. A grammar that uses none of these generates the
  same parser as before.
- **Fixed: the `ci` check no longer passes a test tier that was cut off on the PR's current
  commit.** A shard stopped by its own timeout or by hand used to read green, because a
  cancelled tier was always taken for a run superseded by a newer push. The gate now reads the
  PR's head and lets a cancelled tier pass only when a newer push replaced the run.
- **Fixed: the Studio offers to load a deck's Mermaid diagram link.** A deck whose only web
  address sat in a diagram's `click … href` line showed no "Load" strip, although the address was
  counted and refused like a web image. The strip now appears for it.

- **Studio:** every slide in the strip (the slide pills and the slide map) has a menu with New slide after, New slide before, Duplicate, Move before, Move after and Delete, each with its icon. Open it from the ⋯ at the right end of the current slide's pill, a right-click, Shift+F10, or a tap on the slide you are already on. The command palette offers each of them, and an empty deck's strip offers "+ Add your first slide".
- **Studio:** the slide strip is a keyboard surface. Tab reaches the current slide, and the arrows, Home and End walk the deck with focus following. While a strip slide has keyboard focus, Ctrl+D duplicates it, Ctrl+Shift+Left and Right move it, Ctrl+Enter and Ctrl+Shift+Enter add a slide after or before it, and Delete removes it (⌘ instead of Ctrl on a Mac). A screen reader hears what each action did, and "?" lists every shortcut. A focused thumbnail no longer drops keyboard focus to the page when the map scrolls it away.
- **Studio:** drag a slide in the strip to move it. With a mouse, press and move; on a touch screen, hold the slide, then move it. A copy follows the pointer, a bar shows where it lands, the strip scrolls at its ends, and one Undo takes the whole move back. Holding a slide and letting go without moving opens its menu.
- **Studio:** the four slide buttons that led the strip (Duplicate, Delete and the two moves) are gone; every one of them is in the slide menu, and moving is also a drag. The strip's slides now start at its edge.

- `@laticent/segno-markdown`, the deck model: one CommonMark block pass (markdown-it's block rules, ported rule for rule and held to markdown-it token for token on every committed deck, a rule-surface fuzz and the 652 CommonMark spec examples) that returns a deck's slides, slide boundaries, front matter, directive, fence, plugin-block and leaf ranges from one tape, and re-parses only the edited slide after a keystroke. About 3x faster than markdown-it's block parse on the gallery, 4x on the corpus.
- Slide boundaries now come from the deck model in `slide-boundaries.mjs` (and through it the Studio's outline and rail, and the linter) and in narration export's per-section split. No deck renders, splits or numbers differently.
- `lib/plugins/blocks.generated.mjs` exports `BLOCK_TRIGGERS`, each plugin block rule's start characters from its manifest, so the deck model tries a plugin rule only on lines it can open.

- **Every kind of table now has a narrow layout.** When its box runs out of width, a measure-over-time or cross-tab table (Revenue × Q1–Q4, Region × Product) splits its columns into blocks of two, each block repeating the row labels, and goes to one column per block at the narrowest; an option comparison becomes one block per option, each listing the criteria beside its values; a ranked list and a schedule become two-line rows (rank, name and figure on one line; the date above its item), the other columns labeled beneath. Independent lists (Strengths · Weaknesses · Risks) become one block per column; the engine cannot tell them from a record list, so the author names them with the new `table-lists` modifier. The switches stay low (below 20em of the table's own box), so a full-width or half-pane 16:9 slide never changes, and on a slide a layout that would overflow keeps the table form, as the first two layouts already did. A text label column over a body of one number format is now read as a cross-tab (one of five or more columns switches below 24em, as the card table it used to be did), and a year column over figures (`Year | Revenue | Growth`) is a record list rather than a schedule. `matrix-grid` and `roadmap` still keep their grid. In a table whose layout repeats the row labels, each value cell carries its row's label as `data-lat-row`.
- **Fixed:** in a box only a few words wide (a record table in a narrow pane of a 16:9 deck viewed on a phone in the fluid view), a card's fixed label column left its value one letter per line. Below 12em (8em for labels of up to six characters) each label now sits above its value; option and run blocks do the same below 10em, and a ranked row puts its figure under the name. No 16:9 slide reaches these widths.

- The Studio has a **Content** tab in both Deck Settings and Slide Settings, with a control for each switch that had none: below-note, heading period, table row label, pane spine and callouts. The deck sets each one for every slide, and a slide can override it with Auto, On or Off. Every switch now has a Studio control or a stated reason it has none, and a test fails when a new switch lands without one.

- **Gift links:** `lib/core/gift-link.mjs` turns a spend-capped OpenRouter key into a link of the form `<site>/gift#v1.<key>.<check>` and back. The key rides after the `#`, so the site never receives it; a 24-bit check catches a damaged or mistyped link, and an optional PIN locks the key against someone who only photographed the card. One codec serves the Studio and the admin CLI.
- **`/gift` route:** a gift link opens a small welcome page that stores the key in this browser (sealed, through the one key writer), removes it from the address bar, asks for the PIN when the link is locked, asks before replacing a key already there, and opens the Studio with chat ready on OpenRouter. On a phone it offers **Send to my laptop** through the phone's own share sheet, or copies the link.
- **Workspace › AI:** the OpenRouter key field also takes a whole gift link.
- **`tools/gift-cards.mjs`:** an admin CLI that makes spend-capped OpenRouter keys with the giver's own management key. `make` makes one key by default and prints its gift link; `--count N` writes a batch as `cards.csv`, a `cards.md` deck, `cards.pdf` and `cards-sheet.pdf` (ten cards to a Letter or A4 sheet with crop marks). `--pin` locks each card with its own PIN, and `--with-links` adds the links to the CSV. `report` shows spend per key, and `revoke` deletes a batch.
- **`card` and `card-iso` sizes:** business-card canvases, US 3.5 × 2 in and ISO 85 × 55 mm, exact in shape so a page prints at its physical size.
- **`gift-card` component (connect):** a business card whose QR opens a gift link, with a warm line, an optional PIN printed apart from the code, a caption and a card number. The link is encoded in the QR only, never printed as text.

- **Added: a nightly check of every model id the Studio names, and one file that holds them.** The
  Studio's chat, image and voice defaults, its curated families and its picker lists now come from
  `docs/src/lib/models.config.json`, so a provider retiring a model is a one-line fix. The
  `model-guard-nightly` workflow checks each id against OpenRouter's public lists and, when their
  secrets are set, Gemini's, Anthropic's and OpenAI's, and opens one rolling issue when an id is gone.
  An id in the file's `retired` list makes a stored selection read "Model retired" at once, with no
  substitute model. Its first run removed three gone ids from the pickers: `qwen/qwq` and the two
  `zyphra/zonos` voices.

- **Added: Gemini's 2,000+ locale voices, behind a language filter.** The Gemini voice panel in
  Workspace › AI has a Language menu listing the 39 languages Gemini has voices in. It starts on the
  open deck's `lang:`. The 30 named, multilingual voices stay first; the language adds its locale
  voices, grouped by region (Portuguese · Brazil, Portuguese · Portugal) and labeled by name and
  role ("Authoritative Advisor 1 · Lawyer").

- **`typography:` front-matter key — curated type sets.** One word picks the heading and body faces, the eyebrow's voice and the chart's text voice together: `classic` (Playfair Display + Outfit, the default), `ledger` (Newsreader + Inter), `poster` (Barlow Condensed + Inter) and `festival` (Fraunces + Inter). The four new faces ship self-hosted and embed in every export; a deck that names no set never loads them, and the player's Read · Article view follows the deck's set. **Existing `preset: editorial` and `preset: brand` decks change faces**: `editorial` now carries `ledger` and `brand` carries `poster`; write `typography: classic` to keep the old faces. A slide can return to classic with `_class: typography-classic`. In the Studio: Look → Typography.
- **The eyebrow now reads as content, not chrome.** Every deck's eyebrow (the code-only line above a heading) is set in the heading face's italic, as written, a step larger than the header beside it, and half the heading's size on a title, divider or closing. `eyebrow:` still picks its mark; `mode: sketch` keeps its own hand-drawn eyebrow.
- **Chart text speaks the body face.** Axis ticks, category labels and legend keys moved from the mono face to the body face with aligned figures, so they no longer read as the page number and footer. Data labels take the heading face only in `ledger`, whose Newsreader has tabular figures; every other set draws them in the body face. The quote credit is set in tracked capitals.
- New lint: `unknown-typography` for a typo, `type:` answered with "did you mean `typography:`?", and `typography-style-override` when a deck's own `style:` re-points a face the set owns.
- **A deck's own `font-family: Inter` now draws the bundled Inter at 87%.** The set faces ship under their real names with an `@font-face` `size-adjust` that holds Outfit's x-height, so an author's `style:` that names Inter, Newsreader, Fraunces or Barlow Condensed gets that face and its size factor rather than a system install.
- **Translucent text in an ODP is written as the color it appears as**, also over a gradient (the dark title, divider and closing slides). Collabora Online drew each letter of a translucent run as a solid block, which turned the new italic eyebrow on those slides into a gray bar; the PPTX keeps its opacity.

- A `bleed` slide picks its words' ink from its photo: white words and a darkening scrim over a dark photo, dark words and a lightening veil over a light one, read from the band under the heading (the middle of the photo for a layout that centers its words) as the slide crops the photo. A slide whose own or carried class names a color mode keeps it, and a `print` deck keeps print's ink. The CLI's PDF, picture and HTML exports decide before the page renders, the Studio and the Playground in the preview, and Export-to-Marp writes the choice into the slide's class. No shipped deck changes; `examples/bleed-auto-ink.md` shows each case.

- **System panel** (Workspace settings → Diagnostics, or `?system`): what Lattice sees of this device — browser,
  graphics chip (and whether the browser draws in software), memory, CPU cores, storage, network and preferences —
  the tier it would run in (Full or Lite) and why, an on-demand speed test, and a "Copy report" button for bug
  reports.

- The docs site now serves `/robots.txt` and `/llms.txt`, a short router for AI agents to the pages they need to write a deck (#3207).
- Every docs, component and catalog page has a plain-Markdown copy at its own path plus `.md` (`/guides/cli/` → `/guides/cli.md`), linked from the page; a component's copy is its `.docs.md`.
- Every page outside the Starlight docs carries a canonical link and an Open Graph card, and each page sets its title and description once. A shared link now shows a preview image drawn from real engine renders.
- The sitemap no longer lists pages marked `noindex`, and each URL carries the date of its page's last content commit.
- 75 routes (and the 404 page) carry a strict Content-Security-Policy: inline scripts only by exact hash, and images, fonts and fetches from the site itself. Pages with live slide previews, Calco and the voice demos get theirs in a later change. PR previews send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, and search engines are kept off the `.md` copies.

- **The Studio chat's find and replace take a pattern and keep case.** `replace_text` gains `preserve_case`: each
  match keeps its case, so replacing `oct` with `October` writes `OCTOBER` in an all-caps eyebrow, `October` in a
  title and `october` in a sentence. `find_text` and `replace_text` gain `regex`: the words to find are a JavaScript
  regular expression, and the replacement can use `$1`, `$<name>` and `$&`. A pattern runs in a Worker, never on the
  page's main thread, and the Studio stops it after 2 seconds, so a pattern that backtracks forever cannot freeze the
  page (#3208).
- **The Studio chat knows the deck may have moved since its last card.** When it is told what the author did with
  its earlier cards, it is now also told how many slides the deck has and that slide numbers from earlier turns may
  name other slides, so it re-reads the deck instead of acting on a stale number (#3208).

- **The Studio assistant can find and replace across a deck.** Ask it to change "Oct. Tenth" to
  "October Tenth" and it searches every slide at once (`find_text`), then stages the change
  (`replace_text`) on one review card with a row per slide, instead of reading slides one by one and
  rewriting each in full. It works the way a word processor does: the words change and their
  formatting stays, so a bold word stays bold. Characters Markdown would read as formatting are
  escaped for you, so replacing "five" with "$5" shows $5, not a math formula, and searching for "$5"
  finds it again. It replaces words in headings, eyebrows, body text, quotes, alt text, spoken lines,
  speaker notes and descriptions, and never touches link or image targets, URLs, layout directives,
  code blocks, math, HTML or the front matter. It tells you what it left alone, such as a phrase that
  runs across bold and plain text.
- **Fixed: a word change across two identical slides no longer shows as a slide insert and delete** on
  the assistant's review card. When the deck keeps its slide count, the card now lists a plain change
  for each slide that changed.
- **Fixed: the Studio assistant's speech preview reads what the voice reads.** On a slide with a
  spoken line (`<!-- say: … -->`), `preview_speech` showed the on-screen text, words the voice never
  says. It now follows the same order as Present and the export: the spoken line, a front-matter
  `say:` entry, chart narration, then the slide text, which it labels approximate. It previews up to
  10 slides at once, lists each term that fired as written and as spoken (a possessive or plural on
  its own line), and names words no term covers that a voice may stumble on, such as `Ilcea.K` or
  `McKinsey`.

- The exported HTML player (`--player`, the Studio's Webpage) now opens a chart's detail cards in Present: hover a mark, or tap it on a phone, and its card opens beside it with the mark's name, value and description in the deck's own theme and mode. Digits 1–9 open mark *n*, 0 or Escape closes, and each chart with details is one Tab stop whose arrow keys walk its marks. A deck without chart details ships none of the card code.
- `@laticent/cenno`, a new zero-dependency popover library (`docs/src/lib/cenno/`): placement that matches Floating UI, the top layer above fullscreen, steady size under pinch zoom, hover with a grace corridor, tap-to-pin, and a card skinned by `--cenno-*` tokens and named parts. 5.4 KB gzipped.
- The exported HTML player no longer turns the slide on a tap in Mobile Safari. Safari reported the end of every touch at the page's top-left corner, so the player read a tap as a long drag; it now measures a swipe from where the finger went down to where it last moved.

- **`backdrop:` gains two keep-outs for pattern finishes, `clear-footer` and `clear-hero`.**
  `clear` empties the whole content box, which suits a wash and throws a pattern away. The
  keep-outs leave a grid, dot or ruled finish running behind the content and clear only the
  footer band (the footer text, the section rail and the page number), and with `clear-hero`
  the content box of a `big-number` slide too, so the pattern never runs under the hero number. On a split slide the band also clears the panel's
  own copy of the finish under the page number.
  They use the same soft clear layer as `clear`, so an exported PDF keeps every word as text.
  Write `backdrop: clear-hero` in the front matter, or `_class: backdrop-clear-footer` on one
  slide; the Studio's backdrop mask menu lists both. `clear` is unchanged. Demo:
  `examples/backdrop-keepouts.md`. (`lib/core/resolve-backdrop.js`, `lib/base/base.finish.css`)

- **An empty agenda fills itself from the deck's dividers.** Write an `agenda` slide with a
  heading and no list, and it lists one item per `divider` slide, named by the divider's heading.
  Each filled item ends with the page its section starts on, and the same empty agenda placed inside a
  section also gets that section's `progress-N`. A list you write always wins. A hidden divider and a
  divider inside a code fence do not count. With fewer than two dividers there is nothing to fill from, and `lint:deck` warns (`agenda-empty`). It works
  in the CLI, the Studio and Export to Marp.
- **A deck-wide `agenda:` setting.** One line, up to one word per axis: the style (`ledger`, `circles`,
  `checks`) and whether filled agendas show page numbers (`pages`, `no-pages`), for example
  `agenda: circles no-pages`. The default is the ledger with page numbers. The editor completes it,
  the Deck Inspector sets it (Look → Agenda), and `lint:deck` flags an unknown word. An agenda you write
  keeps its own list and page numbers.
- **Breaking:** the agenda's `rail` and `cards` styles are retired. The agenda keeps three styles:
  the default `ledger`, `circles` and `checks`. A slide that still names `rail` or `cards` renders as
  the ledger, and `lint:deck` warns (`agenda-retired-style`) with a one-click fix: `rail` becomes
  `circles`, and `cards` is removed.
- **Fixed: page references on `circles` and `checks` agendas sit at the right edge, as on the
  ledger.** They used to render as pills stuck to the end of the title. `checks` rows are now as
  tall as `circles` rows, so the two styles have the same row spacing.

- **The agent kit now has a small-context read path.** `README.md` is the routing file — a read-path table costed in tokens, the 13 component families with their members, and the cross-cutting authoring rules — and every component now ships as its own `components/<name>.md`. An agent that knows which layout it wants reads **~3.2k tokens** instead of the **~108k** the full catalog costs; one that needs to choose adds `components.pick.md` for ~7.4k. The aggregate files are unchanged for anyone who wants them whole.
- **Fixed a dangling pointer inside the kit.** `components.pick.md` tells the reader to open `lib/components/<bucket>/<name>/<name>.docs.md` — a repository path a kit consumer with no clone does not have. Every such reference in the kit is now rewritten to the file's own kit path, and a test resolves every link in the kit and fails on any that dangles.
- The shared `chart-family` contract ships as `components/_chart-family.md`; eight of the chart component docs point at it, and it was previously unreachable from the kit for the same reason.

- **New LLM agent kit, published to the orphan `dist-kits` branch under `agent/`.** Everything a model or coding agent needs to author a Lattice deck, fetchable one file at a time with no clone, no `npm install` and no build: the deck canon and authoring rules, one file per component, the seven `design/skills/` guides, a runnable deck checker, and the machine catalogs. Its authoring primer is the **same** one the Studio chat sends to its own model, generated from the live manifests by the same two functions the Studio calls, so it cannot drift into a second source of truth.
- **`dist-kits` replaces `dist-marp-kit`,** carrying both kits (`marp/` and `agent/`) behind one name, one ruleset and one publish. It is republished on every push to `main` that changes an input, with a nightly backstop, by `.github/workflows/publish-kits.yml`.
- **The branch root carries a `.vscode/settings.json` fallback.** Moving the Marp kit from the branch root into `marp/` would otherwise break its workspace-relative theme paths and render **unstyled slides with no error**; opening either the branch root or `marp/` as a VS Code workspace now works.
- **`npm run build` gained an `agent kit (dist/agent-kit)` step** (`tools/build-agent-kit.mjs`), behind the same freshness gate as every other generated artifact.
- The three places that route an agent to `dist/docs/components.pick.md` — `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` — now say the file is generated, name the command that produces it, and link the published branch for anyone without a clone.
