  is not `topic`.
- **Changed: the track's CSS is scoped to `ul.tile-track`.** A stray list on a `topic` slide is no
  longer styled as a scale it is not.

- **Changed: the portrait gantt band's constants carry their measurement.** The comment
  above `GANTT_GEOM_TALL` said the band "carries the same 0.8 the landscape one took",
  which is the mechanism rather than the justification. It now states the margin the way
  the landscape band's does: on `test/fixtures/chart-fit.md` p9 at portrait, 68.7px of headroom, 21.2
  viewBox units against a 21-unit bar-row pitch, so the chart holds one more row in
  reserve — by 0.67px, which is inside `check-chart-fit`'s own slack and a property of
  that stage rather than of the constants. `laneNameH` staying at 15 while the bar band
  shrank is recorded as deliberate: at 12 the lane name would cross the lane rule.
  The numbers are unchanged; only the reasoning is now checkable.

- **Changed: a `deferred` gantt bar is drawn dashed, and the key names the neutral.**
  `deferred` and a task with no status both take the family's mute ramp, separated only
  by an 18% wash and a 1.67-unit accent sliver — so a reader met two pale bars and could
  not tell "we pushed this" from "nobody said". `deferred` now keeps the hollow body and
  gains a dashed edge, and the key gains a `no status` chip whenever a chart carries an
  unstated task and already draws a key. The chip is dropped rather than pushed past the
  frame once the row is full: with the ten status words in the order the key emits them,
  that is beyond eight in landscape and five in portrait.
  **The dash is a semantic cue, not this chart's accessibility channel.** Gantt reaches
  none of the engine's three redundant channels — texture tiles, `stroke-dasharray`
  ladders, and a shape glyph on `.chart-status` — because its statuses are bar fills
  carrying neither text nor glyph. That gap is **#2274** and is not closed here. What the
  dash answers is the one distinction no ramp-keyed channel can, texture included: these
  two land on the same ramp and differ only in `data-s`.
  **Verified on one surface** — rendered under `a11y-achromatopsia`, where both bars
  resolve to the same gray and the dash is the whole distinction. The other three a11y
  palettes, grayscale print, a photocopy and the `print` finish are **UNVERIFIED**.
- **Added: `examples/gantt-status-key.md`** — the demo deck for the above.

- **Breaking:** `quadrant` names its axes with the bracketed axis list that `matrix-grid` and `scatter` already use, one paragraph above the chart: `` `[{Effort, 0..10}, {Reach, 0..100}]` ``. Each member is `{name, min..max, threshold}`, so a threshold now sits inside the axis it cuts (`` `[{Effort, 0..10, 5}, {Reach, 0..100, 50}]` ``). The old `` `Effort 0–10 → Reach 0–100 · targets 5, 50` `` eyebrow now renders as a plain eyebrow: the axes lose their names and the points move to a data-derived scale. `lint:deck` reports the old eyebrow as `quadrant-retired-axis` and its autofix rewrites it. It also names an axis part the chart ignores (`quadrant-axis-part`).
- `quadrant` no longer prints its axes twice. The axis list is removed from the slide and drawn on the axes, the way `scatter`'s is. A plain eyebrow beside it stays on the slide.
- The typed-glyph gate (HARD RULE #29) no longer exempts anything: `isQuadrantAxisEyebrow` is deleted, and an arrow in a quadrant eyebrow now counts like any other typed glyph.
- Fixed: the documented ASCII spelling `` `Effort 0-10 -> Reach 0-100` `` never worked. markdown-it escaped the arrow before the parser saw it, so `examples/adaptive-sweep.md` drew an x-axis named "Effort 0-10 -&gt; Reach" on a 0–100 domain. The migrated deck draws "Effort" on 0–10.
- Narration speaks a quadrant's axes as one sentence each, with name, domain and threshold ("The horizontal axis, Effort, runs zero to ten, with a threshold at five."). It no longer reads the eyebrow aloud, arrow included.
- Fixed: `lint:deck` warned twice on every braced axis list above a chart body (`label-set-above-body` and `label-set-unbound`). On `scatter` one warning told the author to delete a correct axis. A list above the body is now reported as a misplaced key only when it names one of the component's key members.
- `gantt` also accepts the bracketed axis list: `` `[{Timeline, 2026 Q1..2026 Q4, Q3}]` `` gives the window and the `today` point in one span, in either order, and draws the same chart as `` `2026 Q1 .. 2026 Q4` `today Q3` ``. The keyword pills still work and stay on the slide as an eyebrow; the list is removed from the slide. A gantt draws no axis caption, so the name is not drawn. `lint:deck`'s mixed-time check reads the window in both forms.
- **Breaking:** on `quadrant`, a plain code eyebrow no longer names the x-axis as well. The old parser drew any eyebrow without an arrow as the x-axis title, so `` `Impact vs effort` `` appeared twice: once as the eyebrow and once under the chart. The eyebrow now stays and the axes are named only by an axis list. `examples/legend-below-portrait.md` gains `` `[Impact, Effort]` ``, which also names the y-axis it never had.
- Fixed: an axis list with more members than the component has axes is no longer removed from the slide with its extra members discarded. `quadrant`, `scatter`, `matrix-grid` and `gantt` leave such a list on the slide as text, narration speaks it as text, and `lint:deck` names it on `quadrant`.
- Fixed: an apostrophe inside an axis name split the list wrong. In `` `[Customer's spend, Churn rate]` `` the apostrophe opened a quote that swallowed the comma, so the two axes merged into one and the second axis was never drawn. A quote now opens only at the start of a name, and only when a matching quote later ends a name (it is followed by `,`, `}` or `]`). A leading apostrophe with no such partner, as in `'90s cohort`, is plain text, even when a later name holds an apostrophe of its own.
- Fixed: an empty member keeps its place. `` `[, Teams adopting]` `` names only the second axis. Before, the blank was dropped and the name moved onto the first axis.
- Fixed: `label-set-above-body` now finds the chart body where the render finds it. A bullet inside an HTML comment no longer counts as the body, and a list or table inside a blockquote does.

- **Breaking:** a chart's axis is now ONE bracketed list in its own paragraph, replacing the two- and three-code-span form `matrix-grid` and `scatter` used — `` `[Wider reach, Deeper cognition]` `` and `` `[Annual cost, Teams adopting, Seats]` ``. Quotes are optional, single or double, and protect a comma inside a name, so `` `["Cost, excluding tax", Value]` `` is two axes. The grammar also ACCEPTS a member carrying its range and threshold — `` `[{Effort, 0..10, 5}]` `` — but no component reads those parts yet; only the name is used, and the rest is ignored rather than honored.
- **Breaking:** POSITION now says which construct a bracketed span is. A list ABOVE the chart body names the axes; a list BELOW it renames the label set. `matrix-grid` decks that authored their key above the grid must move it below. The retired rules — an axis discriminated by holding exactly two code spans, a label set by holding exactly one — are gone, along with the constraint that made one construct's grammar a hostage of the other's.
- Axis names are never invented. Range and threshold still derive from the data, but where no name can be derived the axis renders unnamed; the editable starter wording lives in each component's scaffolder skeleton instead.
- `scatter`'s scaffolder skeleton no longer hands the author the placeholder `` `X measure` `Y measure` ``.

- **The label-set grammar no longer drags an HTML extractor into the browser.** `liftLabelSet`
  — and with it `plainText`/`stripTags` — moved out of `lib/core/label-set.js` into
  `lib/core/lift-label-set.js`. The split is by INPUT rather than convenience: `label-set.js`
  parses a string an author typed and the deck LINTER imports it, on the CLI and in the bundle
  the docs Studio loads; the lift parses markdown-it's OUTPUT and only a transform wants it.
  Measured on the built Studio route: 5 occurrences of `liftLabelSet`/`stripTags` in
  `authoring-core.generated.js` before, 0 after.
- **The `studio` route budget is raised 679500 → 681300** for what the new deck-lint rule
  legitimately costs. Measured twice off one tree with the bundles regenerated both times:
  677756 bytes gz with the rule stubbed, 679301 with it — **+1545**, chunk count unchanged at
  84. Set against the EXPECTED CI reading rather than the local one, per that route's own note
  (local + the recorded ~896-byte CI offset ≈ 680197, cleared by ~1.1KB). The previous budget
  passed locally with 199 bytes of headroom and CI still read it over, which is that warning
  working exactly as written. (`docs/route-budget.json`)

- **`obligation-matrix` draws its own marker key.** Until now the key was a prose sentence
  the author retyped on every slide — *"Filled = applies, half = partial, empty = exempt"* —
  bound to nothing, and the component's own docs listed forgetting it as an authoring
  mistake. The grid now builds the key from the markers its cells actually carry, in a
  canonical order, with no key at all when no cell carries one. The five shipped gallery
  slides that restated the key in prose no longer do; that sentence is what the feature
  replaces.
- **Its words can be renamed.** `Applies` / `Partial` / `Exempt` / `Out of scope` suit a
  compliance matrix and not a licensing or diligence grid, so they are now the default
  declared in `obligation-matrix.manifest.json`, overridable with a label set above the
  grid: `` `[{[x], In force}, {[ ], Not subject}]` ``. Naming a subset is the normal case.
  Demo deck: `examples/obligation-matrix-label-sets.md`.
- **The key's swatch takes the CELLS' own classes**, and the stylesheet adds that one class
  to the existing cell-disc selectors rather than restating the recipe. A key painted by a
  different rule than the cells it names is the worst kind of stale legend, because it stays
  plausible. (`lib/components/legal/obligation-matrix/obligation-matrix.styles.css`)
- **A component can now declare WHO draws its key.** `labelSet.keyedBy` is `component` by
  default — a component with a figure builder builds its own, as `roadmap` does — or
  `transformer`, for one that has no section transform at all and so had nowhere to build
  one. The new shared post-pass reads that declaration from the generated catalog rather
  than carrying a list of component names, which is the drift this construct exists to end.
  (`lib/transformers/label-set-key.js`, `lib/components/manifest.schema.json`)

- **A journey's mood scale can be renamed at its poles.** `Pain` and `Delight` were string
  literals in the transform — duplicated verbatim in both board builders — and they assert a
  polarity the engine cannot derive. They suit a customer journey and not an on-call
  rotation, a procurement trail or a cost review. They are now the default declared in
  `journey.manifest.json`, overridable with a label set beside the board:
  `` `[{1, Friction}, {5, Flow}]` ``. Naming one pole leaves the other on its default.
  Demo deck: `examples/journey-label-sets.md`.
- **Only the two poles are keyable, and the manifest says why.** The steps between them show
  their number, which IS the scale, so `2` / `3` / `4` are declared in `labelSet.unkeyed`
  with their reason — `lint:deck` quotes it back rather than reporting an unknown key.
- **The rename reaches the key's accessible name.** That `aria-label` was a second
  hard-coded copy of the same two words, so a renamed scale would have left a screen reader
  hearing the old polarity. One source now feeds both.
- **The mood key and the actor key each have ONE builder.** Both were duplicated verbatim
  across the landscape and portrait boards — two copies of a decision is two places to
  change it and one to forget. Pinned by a test asserting the two shapes emit the same key.
  The shipped gallery renders byte-identical.
  (`lib/components/chart/journey/journey.transform.js`)

- **A roadmap's status key can be renamed.** `Shipped` / `In flight` / `Planned` /
  `Out of scope` are right for a product plan and wrong for a legislative or research one,
  and until now no deck could say otherwise — the words were a constant in the transform.
  They are now the default declared in `roadmap.manifest.json`, and an author overrides any
  of them with a label set above the grid:
  `` `[{[x], Enacted}, {[-], In committee}]` ``. **Naming a subset is the normal case** —
  the states you do not name keep their defaults. The key is the MARKER you already type in
  a cell, brackets included; a bare space key collapses to empty and would drop its row, so
  `[ ]` is the spelling that works. Everything the key already did, it still does: one chip
  per state actually present, canonical lifecycle order, no key at all when the grid carries
  no markers, and none under the `status` variant, which labels every cell itself.
  `lint:deck` warns on a key that would be dropped, naming the keys that would work.
  Demo deck: `examples/roadmap-label-sets.md`.
  (`lib/components/chart/roadmap/roadmap.transform.js`)

- **`matrix-grid` draws its cell key on the slide.** Its shape vocabulary shipped in a
  `STATE_LABELS` map rendered into a visually-hidden span — the words existed for a screen
  reader and for nobody looking at the slide, while a sighted reader got an unparsed prose
  sentence the author wrote by hand. The grid now names the shapes its cells actually carry,
  and draws no key at all when there is nothing to decode.
- **`[x]` is deliberately NOT keyed, and the manifest says why.** A filled cell's own
  trailing text is its label (`[x] Senior`), so the shape has no general name; a key row
  reading "filled" would repeat on every slide what the cell already says better. That
  refusal is declared in `labelSet.unkeyed` with its reason rather than left as an absence,
  so `lint:deck` can tell an author who keys `[x]` what is actually wrong instead of calling
  the key unknown.
- **The two keyable shapes can be renamed.** `reachable` / `not applicable` suit a
  capability rubric and not a coverage or eligibility grid, so they are now defaults,
  overridable with `` `[{[-], within reach}, {[ ], out of band}]` ``. The TWO-code axis
  eyebrow is untouched — two code spans in one paragraph is still the axis discriminator,
  and a one-code paragraph that is not a label set is left alone. Demo deck:
  `examples/matrix-grid-label-sets.md`.
- **The key's swatch shows the border treatment without asserting a row.** A matrix-grid
  cell is colored by its ROW's category rather than by its state, so a key cannot borrow a
  cell's color. The outlined swatch takes `--accent`, which is the cell rule's own fallback
  when no row hue is set; an earlier cut neutralized both swatches and, measured on the
  rendered gallery, the two read as the same box.
  (`lib/components/chart/matrix-grid/matrix-grid.styles.css`)
- **A rename now reaches the screen reader too, which is the whole point of the
  construct.** The parse-time cell rule stamps `.cell-sr-label` from `STATE_LABELS`
  before any author label set has been lifted, so an author who renamed `[-]` to
  "Partially reachable" got the new word on the visible key and the old "reachable" in
  the accessibility tree — the same cell announced with words the slide does not show,
  and the surface that disagreed was the one nobody can see to check. The transform is
  the first point that holds both the cells and the resolved rows, so it re-points the
  labels there; both render paths reach it, so one pass fixes both (HARD RULE #1).
  Measured before and after on a real engine render AND the shipped runtime bundle in
  real Chromium. `[x]` is untouched — it is `unkeyed` and emits no such label.
  (`lib/components/chart/matrix-grid/matrix-grid.transform.js`)

- The nine shipped finishes are now generated from their recipes. `npm run build` runs `lib/finishes/finish-generate.js`, the same generator the Finish Studio uses, over every `lib/finishes/<name>/<name>.recipe.json` and writes each `section.finish-<name>` rule into `lib/base/base.finish.css`. Retuning a recipe now changes what decks render, and "Start from preset" in the Studio now reproduces the shipped finish. Measured against the old hand-written rules, the export (print) face matches on eight of nine finishes; nimbus's vignette differs by at most 3 of 255 levels. The screen face differs by at most 6 of 255 levels, on at most 0.02% of pixels.
- The finish vocabulary gains four terms the shipped finishes needed: a thin `rule` mark (atrium's margin rule), a `wash.hairline` strip (strata's top line), a corner-anchored glyph (`mark.anchor: "corner"` with `mark.inset`, as used by meridian, savile and gallery), and a hand-tuned screen face for the fold (`edge.rich`, ledger's). In the Studio, moving an anchored glyph turns it into a free one.
- A Studio-made finish's texture on screen is one accent step lighter (+2 instead of +3, matching the shipped finishes), its monogram mixes at 9% like the numeral, and its inset frame is sized in the slide's own units, as the shipped gallery frame always was.

- **Breaking:** each shipped theme now lives in its own folder, `themes/<name>/<name>.css` beside `themes/<name>/<name>.manifest.json`, like every other Lattice package. The published import path is unchanged: `@laticent/lattice/themes/<name>.css` (and `<name>.manifest.json`) resolves to the folder's file through the package's `exports` map. Code that read `node_modules/@laticent/lattice/themes/<name>.css` straight off disk, or a CDN's raw file URL such as unpkg's (CDNs ignore `exports`), must use `themes/<name>/<name>.css` instead. Build outputs keep their layout: `dist/themes/<name>-min.css`, the Marp export's `themes/` folder and the Marp kit are still flat.
- `npm run new:theme -- <name>` writes the new palette and its `-dark` twin into their own folders.

- **Breaking:** `list-steps` (its side-by-side row, including `phase`, `stage` and `tier`), `compare-prose` (both panes, except `decision`) and `cards-stack horizontal` now opt into the `cards:` register with a `center` default. Sparse cards size to their text and the row centers on the stage instead of stretching to fill it. A slide that ends in a key-insight or note still stretches. Add `cards: stretch` to the front matter, or `_class: … cards-stretch` on one slide, to restore the old look. `cards: center | stretch | top | spread` and `cards-*` now work on all three (#2317).

- **Breaking:** the CLI's PDF, PPTX, PNG and image-set renders are kept off the network. Every browser a render starts refuses web requests (images, media, fonts, stylesheets, script fetches, WebSockets), WebRTC traffic and DNS lookups. A remote image in a deck shows the browser's broken-image mark, as it already did in the Studio preview and the `.html` export; local images, `data:` URIs and the bundled fonts, Mermaid and KaTeX are unaffected. Pass `--allow-remote` to fetch as before. No shipped deck is affected: the data-viz gallery renders byte-identical PDFs either way.
- A component's sample slide may not carry an inline `<script>`, a `data:` or `javascript:` script source, an event-handler attribute or a `javascript:` URL; a package carrying one is refused on import. A script loaded by a relative path with an empty body, as the shipped diagram gallery does, is still allowed.

- **Breaking:** a deck's images from the web (`http:`, `https:`, `//host`) no longer load by default in the Studio's PDF, PowerPoint and image exports, as already in its preview, and in the CLI's exports. Each one shows as a drawn placeholder: a hatched box with a picture mark, in the deck's own colors, that keeps the image's address. A web `url()` background shows the same hatch. Loading a web image tells its server who opened the deck and when.
- The Studio shows "This deck loads N images from these sites" above the preview, with a **Load them** button. The choice is remembered for that deck and those sites only: a new site asks again, **Block again** takes it back, and a restored workspace backup never carries it. Your own decks are not trusted automatically, because a paste or an AI edit can add a web image too. The preview, Present (its overview grid included), the Stage window, Read · Article and the Studio's PDF, PowerPoint and image exports all follow the choice; the Webpage (player) export never loads a web image and always shows the placeholder.
- The CLI prints one line saying how many web images it left out, and from which sites (`--quiet` silences it); `--allow-remote` still loads them.
- The Studio's raster exports no longer fetch a web image from the page that drives the export: right before each slide is captured, every web image and `url()` outside the deck's choice is swapped for the placeholder, whatever its spelling, and put back afterwards. Read · Article, which shows the deck inside the Studio's own page, gets the same treatment.

- **Breaking:** `assemblePlayer` (`lib/export/player-core.mjs`) takes `narration` as
  `{ slides, inputs, voice, captions }`, one entry per slide carrying the narration text, its
  Cadenza track and one clip per sentence. The old array of per-slide cue lists is refused with
  an error rather than exported silent. The Studio's webpage export is the only caller in this
  repository.
- **Changed: the LTT audio layer holds one clip per sentence** (`audio.clips[]`, each naming its
  cue), not one per slide, matching how every producer records and how the player advances.
- **Changed: the manifest's `readAlong` section is version 2.0.** It carries `timing`, which names
  the embedded LTT block, and a captions-only export now gets the section too.

- `venue:` and `scale-l` / `scale-xl` / `scale-2xl` are fixed sizes, like desktop zoom. Every slide renders at the size the deck asks for on every surface — the PDF, the exported `.html`, the Studio preview and Present — and nothing steps a too-full slide, or the deck, down to fit. A slide too full for its venue clips, and three places name it: `lint:deck` (`capacity-scale`), the Studio's ring and clip notice, and the export's `⚠ OVERFLOW` line. (An automatic step-down, with a `↓ SCALE` report and a hidden whole-deck measuring frame in the Studio, was on `main` from #2378 to this change and never released.)
- The Studio's deck settings have a **Venue** menu (Look → Venue: Default, Laptop, Huddle, Conference, Hall) that writes `venue:`.
- Present has a **venue switch** that changes the room size for one showing without editing the deck.
- When a slide is too full for the deck's venue, the Studio shows a notice under the preview with two one-click fixes: **Split slide** (halves the slide's main list or table onto a second slide that repeats the heading) and **Use <next venue down>**.
- An ordered list that starts past 1 (`4. Report`) now keeps its number in layouts that draw their own counter (`list-steps` STEP badges, `q-and-a`, and the others); they used to restart at 01. A list the author started past 1 also keeps its numbers when the engine splits it across portrait pages.
- `lint:deck`'s venue budget (`capacity-scale`) is closer to what a real deck renders. It interpolates between measured word lengths, reads a variant's own row (`list takeaway` holds far more than a bare `list`), counts the height of a trailing `> …` callout, and now covers components with a venue row but no count budget (`compare-prose`). On a 74-slide talk it names 16 / 25 / 38 of the 17 / 31 / 47 pages that clip at huddle / conference / hall (was 9 / 18 / 29), with 3 / 4 / 1 false warnings (was 10 / 6 / 4), and it no longer claims a slide clips at the designed size when it does not. That includes the slides that clip at `venue: hall` because the venue lifts labels past the body.
- `tools/calibrate-capacity.js` takes `--variant <token>` and `--insight`, to measure a register's own row and the cost of a trailing callout.
- `lint:deck` names a `scale-*` or `venue-*` set on some slides rather than the whole deck (`spot-scale`): those slides change size as you click through. A spot `venue-*` is a warning; a spot `scale-*` is a note. The directive still works.
- A component's capacity can state what it holds with `compact` (`withCompact` in its manifest). `q-and-a` now holds four pairs bare and five with `compact`, as measured, so `lint:deck` names a bare five-pair slide (which clips) and suggests `compact`, and stays silent on a five-pair `compact` slide (which fits).
- `compare-code` and `obligation-matrix` now state what they hold at each venue: 20 / 17 / 15 / 13 code lines per pane (19 / 16 / 14 / 11 under an eyebrow), and 7 / 6 / 6 / 5 rows, at laptop / huddle / conference / hall. `lint:deck` warns on an `obligation-matrix` slide past its room's number.

- `lint:deck`'s `capacity-scale` now judges `list` (bare, `takeaway`, `takeaway numbered`), `cards-grid` (bare, `three`, `four`) and `list-steps` (written `1.`, two to five steps) by the lines their eyebrow, heading, items and trailing callout wrap to at the deck's `venue:`, instead of by how many items of how many words they hold. A title over a body now costs its own line whatever its word count, and a narrow card column wraps by each glyph's width. Scored against five real decks forced to each venue, lint finds 14 more of the slides the export clips (summed over huddle, conference and hall), raises 7 fewer false warnings, and neither drops a slide it caught before nor raises a new false one. All four false warnings on the agentic-practices talk at `venue: huddle` are gone, and on 22 more decks rendered the same way it adds no false warning. Inline `code` spans are measured as the mono pills they are, and a slide carrying a modifier that may change the geometry (`spectrum-card`, a `class: sketch` deck) keeps its count row, as does every slide of a deck whose front matter sets a key that may (`meta:`, `logo:`, `preset:`, `inline-code:`, …). The claim panel's wrap uses the same glyph widths and now also catches `seven-steps` slide 11 at hall. `venueCapacity.rows` in those three manifests holds the geometry, measured by `tools/calibrate-capacity.js <component> --rows`. A slide the geometry does not describe (another register, `compact`, a paragraph or fence under the heading, six or more steps) keeps its count row. On a deck with no `size:` (720 px high), both line budgets now allow the export's own overflow tolerance, so a slide within it no longer reads as clipped.

- **`lattice video` muxes its captions as `tx3g`**, the 3GPP timed-text format QuickTime, iOS
  and macOS use for subtitles, in place of the WebVTT-in-MP4 (`wvtt`) track no player offered.
  The track is off until the viewer picks it, and each caption shows exactly while its sentence
  plays and clears between sentences. It suggests an on-brand look: light bold text on the
  deck's own dark color at 86% opacity, both from the theme. iOS applies the colors and opacity;
  the viewer's caption style keeps its own font and weight. The `.vtt` sidecar is unchanged.
  Whether QuickTime on a Mac, PowerPoint and Keynote offer the track is not yet verified.

- Nine more chart pane budgets are measured: gantt, journey, kanban, matrix-grid, progress, quadrant, roadmap, state-chart and word-cloud (`tools/calibrate-capacity.js --pane` has a builder for each now). Four fall to their measured ceiling, so `lint:deck` warns sooner: a matrix-grid side pane holds 3 rows (was 4) and a progress side pane 4 tracks (was 6), since a three-word label wraps a word to a line; a word cloud holds 6 words in a side pane and 8 in a stacked one (was 20), before its lightest words fall under the type floor or the packer drops one.

- The type-floor probe now measures Mermaid's HTML labels (`<foreignObject>`) instead of reporting them as "not measured". A diagram whose labels shrink under the floor now gets the export's `⚠ TYPE FLOOR` line, and the "Text too small" tab at `--overflow-marker=author`, on a slide or in a pane. Four shipped example slides are newly flagged (`mermaid-sketch-labels` 4 and 5, `diagram-narration` 5, `typed-diagram-narration` 4). At the default `reader` marker, the exported PDFs are byte-identical.

- **Breaking:** the state chart moves to the flowchart's grammar (state chart v2). A transition is an arrow to a state's NAME, `- -approve-> Approved`, not `` `approve => 4` ``; a self-loop names its own state. `:::token` tints are gone: paint with a status word, a palette slot `:c1`…`:c8`, `=>` for the main path or `:dashed` / `:dotted`. A prose sub-bullet under a state now makes a composite state; write detail as a `>` blockquote. `lint:deck` names the old spellings with their fix (`state-chart-v1-transition`, `state-chart-v1-tint`), every deck in the repo is migrated, and the export now warns on each v1 slide. `node tools/migrate-state-chart-v1.js --write <deck>` migrates a deck of your own, and checks every rewrite against the new parser before it writes.
- The state chart lays out and draws on Trama, the graph-chart library the flowchart uses: lines are the router's elbows, which never cross a state; labels sit on their line; a chain still wraps into rows in reading order and needs no layout engine; typing in the Studio lays a large machine out in a worker. New: composite states (a sub-list of states), shape words on a state, an authored key, and `unnumbered` to drop the badges.
- **Breaking:** on both graph charts a `>` blockquote under a shape or state is HIDDEN DETAIL — shown on hover or tap in Present, Practice and Preview, and folded into the speaker notes — instead of a visible note card on the flowchart. A PDF does not show it; write text the page must carry as a caption.
- `curved` rounds the lines' corners generously on both charts (new on the flowchart).
- A graph chart's key shows words that paint the same tone as one entry (`On track · Done`), on the flowchart as it already did on the state chart.
- Status words fold case in both charts' grammar (`AT-RISK` is `at-risk`).
- **Breaking** (for hosts that read the figure): the state chart's figure carries `data-sc-model` (was `data-sc-transitions`) and marks a drawn chart `data-sc-drawn` (was `data-sc-svg`). `installStateChartLayout` moved from `state-chart.transform.js` to `state-chart.layout.js`, and the v1 helpers (`parseStateLi`, `TRANSITION_RE`) are gone.
- A line into a composite state enters its first state, and a line out leaves from each state inside it, in the roles, the narration and the `inline` rows; `inline` also names each composite. The `inline` chips draw their arrows as shapes instead of typed glyphs.
- A status wins over a palette slot on one state, as on the flowchart, so the key never names a status the chart does not show.
- A graph chart too dense for its slide, under half size with a fit that cannot settle, is drawn after two fit rounds instead of four: raising its type floor only shrinks it further, and two rounds are enough to measure that. A chart under half size whose fit does settle still reaches the type floor. A `--fluid` page with a 36-state machine took 29 s to load; with one round it took about 6.5 s, and the second round adds about 1.5 s to the type-floor watcher test. A stage collapsed to no height is no longer laid out until it has one.
- A chart finish (`marks-pigment` / `-etch` / `-tone`) repaints a state chart's key with its tiles: the key is now the shared graph key, and its status swatches take the same finish as the states they key, in the default and `inline` variants alike.

- A self-presenting deck now lets a slide's last sentence land before the next slide appears. The Studio's Present holds the finished slide for the pace's leave beat (400 ms `brisk`, 700 ms `natural`, 1,100 ms `deliberate`) before it advances, and the exported player does the same: each slide's timing track holds at least that long after its last sentence. Pausing inside the beat and playing again moves on to the next slide rather than rereading the finished one.

- Chart narration now reads each item's `detail` sublist right after that item, as its own sentence, instead of as a list at the end of the slide. A stacked bar used to say all three years and then "Services priced per seat. Services moved to fixed-fee." with nothing saying which year each belonged to; it now says "FY24: Licenses, nineteen point one; Services, nine point eight. Services priced per seat. FY25: …". This covers bar, stacked-bar, line, slope and dumbbell, scatter, map, piechart, waterfall, funnel, radar and quadrant, and a journey task's nested note. A line chart reads a category's detail once, after the first spoken point in that category; a category no series speaks a point for (a gap, or a long line's summary) is named first, after the chart ("M5. Pricing change."). A radar reads an axis's detail after the sentence that names the axis. The Guide, in the Studio and in an exported player, keeps the item focused while its detail is read; on a line chart, a category's note keeps the point just read in focus instead of lifting it.
- The `radar quadrant` variant now reads an axis's detail sublist, with any HTML comment in it left unsaid. Its narrator used to drop the detail without a word.

- The read-aloud voice now says common board-deck terms without an `acronyms:` block: the sales regions EMEA, APAC, LATAM (and LatAm), AMER and ANZ; the short months Feb, Apr, Jul, Aug, Sep, Sept, Oct, Nov and Dec; Jan, Mar and Jun when a year, a day or another month sits beside them ("Jan 2026", "3 Mar"), so the name "Jan" and the verb "mar" still read as themselves; and cohort columns M0 to M36 as "month zero" to "month thirty-six". `NA` stays unexpanded because it also means "n/a". A deck's own `acronyms:` entry still wins.

- **Studio:** a browser that has shown a diagram or opened Fabricate now keeps the Mermaid bundle cached after each deploy, so a diagram it meets offline draws instead of showing its source. It is not warmed for anyone else, or under Save-Data.

- **Flowcharts draw once, in the deck's own fonts, and sooner.** On a cold page load Trama's pipeline used to lay every flowchart out three times, twice in fallback fonts it then threw away. It now waits for the page's fonts (at most 2 seconds), then draws each chart once: a 7-chart deck goes from 32 layouts to 13, and its last chart appears about 550 ms sooner. The CLI export of that deck takes about 0.6 s less.
- **A flowchart the fit shrinks hard keeps its 11 px type floor on its first draw.** The fit and the type floor are solved together, and a chart that needed many rounds to agree used to stop short after three when it had no earlier draw to start from (a chart pasted into the Studio, say, or now every cold load): the typing test deck's 17-shape chart painted its smallest text at 10.2 px. The third and later rounds now take a secant step, so such a chart settles in 4 layouts at the floor. Charts that settled before draw exactly as they did.

- **Each `delivery:` is now its own style, not a louder or quieter copy of the others.** `restrained` focuses every part of a chart the narration names, one quiet crossfade at a time, with no ink and no cursor. `expressive` leads with the cursor and inks every act: it underlines the slide's claim, brackets the figure, traces a line, taps each bar or point, washes a detail and circles the highest or lowest. `somber` stays still until the slide's key beat, then makes one slow focus, as deep as `restrained`'s, and holds it. Before, the three ran the same moves and differed only in how many they got, so `restrained`'s limit of two moments a slide left most of a chart dark.
- The Guide no longer guesses which part of a chart a sentence is about from its words. The chart narrator binds each sentence to the bar, point, stage, cell, row or state it names, and each chart component declares how that part is drawn (its manifest's new `scene`). A new test resolves every bound sentence on every chart gallery slide against the real render, and a score file per chart pins what each delivery does with it.
- The moment budget is retired: `restrained` and `expressive` focus every sentence that names a part of the slide.
- Vetrina has a new gesture, `trace`: a stroke drawn through a series' points in order, the hand riding it.
- A narrated webpage export of a `delivery:` deck carries each chart's bindings, so the sent file focuses the same parts the Studio does. The export still draws no cursor or ink, so a sent `expressive` deck shows its focus but not its ink. The Guide adds about 49 KB to such an export (37 KB before).

- The chart family's code and stylesheet live in its plugin now. The section dispatch and chart
  frame moved from `lib/components/chart/_chart-family/chart-family.js` to
  `lib/plugins/chart-family/chart-family.dispatch.js`, the generated dispatch table to the plugin's
  `shared/chart-registry.generated.js`, and the chart-frame stylesheet to
  `chart-family.styles.css`, the plugin's `styles` contribution. In `dist/lattice.css` that sheet
  now sits in the plugin slot, after the forms and accent finishes rather than before the
  treatments; every element's computed style is unchanged across the tracked decks, and the
  Guide's focus and highlight inside a chart paint as before. Rendered HTML is byte-identical.
- Moved module paths (no compatibility shims: pre-GA): `lib/components/chart/_chart-family/chart-family.js`
  is now `lib/plugins/chart-family/chart-family.dispatch.js`, and
  `lib/components/chart/_chart-family/chart-registry.generated.js` is now
  `lib/plugins/chart-family/shared/chart-registry.generated.js`.
- A plugin that offers an extension point ships `<name>.dispatch.js`, the module that calls its
  fillers (spec/LPM.md §2); the build fails a slot with no dispatch, and a dispatch with no slot.

- **Mermaid's browser half runs on the plugin host.** The Studio, the Playground, the landing previews and the Stage load the diagram library as the Mermaid plugin's declared payload, which the runtime's plugin host fetches from beside `lattice-runtime.js` (`mermaid.min.js`, preloaded by the frame that needs it), instead of a URL each page threaded into every frame. The runtime can now also draw a fence patched into a live document without a rebuild (the docs site's frames still rebuild when a deck gains its first diagram). A library that fails to load hands every fence back to its source before the page's `load`, as before, and Mermaid's own on-load pass no longer paints its error graphic into an empty diagram slot.
- **Breaking:** a diagram fence's `<pre>` carries the plugin host's settle markup — `data-lattice-hydrate="mermaid"` and `data-lattice-settle` (`pending` · `hydrating` · `rendered` · `error` · `unavailable`, plus `data-lattice-final`) — instead of `data-mermaid-state` and `data-mermaid-final`. CSS or scripts that read the old attributes (a custom theme, an integration waiting on diagrams) should read the new ones; the old `rendering` state is now `hydrating`. A page that serves `lattice-runtime.js` and wants diagrams must now either serve `mermaid.min.js` beside it or write its own Mermaid `<script src>` before the runtime (the old shape, still honored); `buildSrcdoc` and the single-slide renderer no longer take a `mermaidUrl`. Exports are unchanged: the CLI's PDFs are byte-identical, and the Studio's PDF export of the diagram gallery is pixel-identical.

- **The plugin placeholder takes space the way the plugin says.** A zip plugin declares `contributes.fences.<fence>.placeholder` in its manifest (new in `plugin.schema.json`): `placement` is `stage` (fills the stage, like a diagram), `figure` (the default: the content width at an `aspect`, within the stage's height, like an image) or `chip` (a mark-only square in the avatar size scale, `size` `sm` to `xl`). For a figure, the proportions of the plugin's last drawn output, remembered in this browser, win over the declared `aspect`. It was a thin strip.

- Typing in the Studio shows a graph chart's new text after one layout instead of three. On an 11-state machine the drawing now moves about 270 ms after a key instead of 1.3 s, and catches up 0.8–1.1 s after a burst instead of 1.6–2.3 s. The drawing that remains is the same as before.
- The layout kernel is about a third faster on both graph charts with byte-identical layouts: it skips boxes and lines a candidate's bounding box cannot reach, walks the boxes as an array, and reads a line's end loads once per line.
- A graph chart that wraps (the state chart) routes only the layouts that can still win: dagre's layout only when its ceiling could beat the grid, and often just the one grid it picks. The state chart's stress deck lays out in 533 ms instead of 1,152 ms (routing passes 77 → 30), with byte-identical layouts.
- While an author types, a graph chart that wraps keeps the rows it had: each keystroke lays out that one grid instead of searching every wrap again, so a key shows sooner (an 11-state state chart: 158–202 ms instead of 280–325 ms; the flowchart of the same machine: 193–214 ms instead of 230–241 ms) and the rows hold while typing (unless an edit leaves the grid unable to hold the shapes, or the direction changes). 300 ms after a live redraw's last round lands, the chart searches once and takes its choice, so the drawing at rest still matches the export; a chart whose new content wants other rows reflows then, once. A chart whose search picked dagre's layout (a chart with groups, or half-typed text) keeps that too, and the pause search runs in its own worker, so a key never waits behind it: on the real Studio at 600 ms a key, a key's layout lands in 150 ms at the median and 214 ms at p90 on an 11-state chart (was 178 / 417 ms), and in 242 / 423 ms on a 12-state chart with a composite (was 366 / 500 ms).
- The Studio's drawing of a graph chart at rest no longer depends on how the text was reached: once the author pauses, the chart settles with the same fit an export starts from, so paste, reload, typing key by key and fast bursts all end on the drawing the export makes (before, the same text could draw with a different width after typing).

- The flowchart wraps a long flow into rows in reading order, as the state chart does, instead of shrinking it onto one line: a ten-step onboarding flow keeps its type (new slide in `examples/flowchart.md`). A fan-out that already reads at size keeps its shape; every shipped flowchart but two keeps its layout.
- A chain row (`A => B => C`) now lists its shapes in that order on both graph charts, so a wrapped chain reads in order and the state chart numbers its states the way they were written. A single connection never moves its target; a chart with no chain row is unchanged. Two flowchart demo slides written with chain rows re-lay out (Checkout, Release train).
- A state machine that branches keeps dagre's layout when it already reads at 0.8 scale or more, rather than wrapping for a little more type; this re-lays out the long-labels slide in `state-chart-branching` with its fan-out intact.

- **The Guide's focus now takes color.** The part the narration names takes the accent (somber's takes the heading ink) while the rest steps back to 0.7, so the emphasis is visible at phone size. Measured on all 33 themes in both modes: the accent as text, the highlight's text on its band and the heading ink all hold 4.5:1, and receded text holds 3:1; `test/unit/palette/guide-contrast.test.js` keeps it that way. Chart shapes still recede to the chart hover's 0.45.
- The Guide can also highlight a part (a soft accent band behind it) or ring it (an outline, nothing else changes). Neither changes any box's size.
- Vetrina has two new gestures: `encircle`, a hand-drawn loop fitted to its target (a circle for a compact one, an ellipse for a wide one), and `connect`, a curved arrow from one part to another with the hand traveling it.
- Every component manifest now declares a `gesture`: which of ten structures it renders (statement, list, grid, table, compare, three chart shapes, flow, media) and any unit its render names differently. A gate checks that each component's gallery draws its archetype's primary unit.
- The Studio loads about 11 KB less JavaScript on first load: it shipped the Vetrina walkthrough engine twice (its tours read the prebuilt copy, the demo read the source), and now every docs import reads the source.
- **The Guide now focuses prose, bullets and table rows from what the narration was built from**, not by matching the spoken words against the slide. Each sentence carries the heading, paragraph, item or row it was read from, in Present, in a webpage exported from the Studio, and in the CLI's narrated player (`--player --narrate`, so `lattice video` too), and a slide with no component class plays as a statement. What steps back around the focused part is unchanged: a bullet's siblings, a row's other cells, never the headline. A sentence the builder could not trace to one element, or an author's `say:` that replaces the narration, still falls back to matching words.
- **In Present, the Guide's focus now lands with the word instead of just after it.** It moves to each sentence ahead of the reader, by a lead that calibrates itself to the device: Present measures how long each focus move takes to be painted, and after three sentences the lead becomes the recent median of that delay plus the fade's settle (starting at 120 ms, capped at 300 ms). The Guide never steps back a sentence when a clip starts later than estimated. A webpage exported from the Studio does not lead yet. Measured on desktop Chromium it settles near 90 ms. The focused part fades in fast and settles slowly, so it is fully on as the first word is heard. The captions and the word-by-word read-along keep the audio's own timing.

- The Mermaid plugin owns its copy of the Mermaid library: `lib/plugins/mermaid/vendor/mermaid.min.js`,
  recorded in the plugin's manifest (`payload.vendored`: version and SHA-256). Every surface ships
  that one copy: the Studio and Playground pages, the CLI's diagram bake (which used to load a second,
  unminified build), the Marp kit and the Export-to-Marp bundle (still as `mermaid-v11-min.js`).
  Nobody downloads Mermaid, and an install cannot change it: `mermaid` is pinned to an exact version,
  the build fails a copy that stops matching its record, and `npm run vendor:plugins` refreshes the
  copy when we decide to upgrade. The repo-root `mermaid-v11-min.js` is gone. Diagram gallery PDFs are
  byte-identical.
- The diagram gallery's and `examples/gallery-jargon.md`'s `<script>` tags load the plugin's copy.
  For the diagram gallery that also fixes its VS Code preview: its two paths had pointed at files
  that did not exist since the galleries moved into bucket folders.
- Plugin manifests gain `payload.vendored` and plugin folders an in-tree `vendor/` (spec/LPM.md §2, §3.4).

- A drawn plugin figure now carries the host's marker, `data-lattice-figure="<plugin>"`, on its container on every surface (the Mermaid pass's `div.mermaid` in a browser, the CLI bake's `div.mermaid-svg`). The Studio's exports, the CLI player capture, Anima's diagram host, the Guide, the diagram layout's CSS and the fit and label gates select it instead of Mermaid's own classes; diagrams look and export exactly as before. A plugin manifest may declare its own output classes as `render.figureClasses` (LPM 0.5-draft), and `checkPluginMigration` keeps every selector outside the plugin off them.
- The CLI has a `--disable-plugin <names>` flag (comma-separated). It switches the plugins off for the engine **and** their CLI bakes, which until now ignored a switched-off plugin and baked its figures anyway; an unknown name fails the run.
- The Studio's and the docs site's previews take a generic `drawn` prop where they took `mermaid` (the sample holds a fence a runtime draws).

- Every plugin library is now a copy its plugin owns, as Mermaid's became in #2557. function-plot
  (`lib/plugins/function-plot/vendor/function-plot.js`), KaTeX with its stylesheet and fonts
  (`lib/plugins/math/vendor/katex/`), and the CLI diagram bake's ZenUML and mermaid-cli render page
  (`lib/plugins/mermaid/vendor/`) ship from the plugin folder to every surface: the engine, the CLI
  export and bake, the HTML player, `dist/lattice.css` and the docs site. Each is pinned to an exact
  version, recorded with its SHA-256 in the manifest, and refreshed with `npm run vendor:plugins`;
  the build fails a copy that drifts. Gallery PDFs are byte-identical.
- Each vendored library's MIT `LICENSE` now ships beside its copy, Mermaid's included.
- Plugin manifests gain `vendor` for owned copies that are not the browser payload; a copy may be a
  file, a directory or one directory's files of one extension (spec/LPM.md §3.4).
- The CLI's warning for a plot whose library is missing now names the file and says to reinstall
  Lattice, since `npm install` no longer provides it.
- Fixed: the installed `lattice` command (the `dist/` bundle) exported every function plot showing
  its config since #2557, because it looked for the plugin's library one folder above the package.
  It now finds every plugin library from the package root, as the source entry does.

- The CLI now warns when the `.html` it leaves, or the `.html` sidecar beside a PDF, PPTX or PNG, keeps a deck's own `<script>`, `on…` handlers, `srcdoc` frames or `javascript:` URLs live, and points at `--player`, which sanitizes them. The exported bytes do not change: a plain `.html` running the deck's raw HTML is by design, because the PDF is captured from that same page (`engineering/decisions/2026-08-17-theme-css-is-a-preview-sink.md` § 10).

- A PDF, PPTX, ODP, PNG or ZIP export no longer leaves a live `<out>.html` sidecar on disk. The emulator captures the raster from that file and then deletes it on success, because the file keeps the deck's own raw HTML and runs it when opened (theme-css note § 10). Pass `--keep-html` (or set `LATTICE_KEEP_HTML=1`) to keep it. An `.html` output, an extensionless output (the sidecar idiom), and the `--player`/`--fluid`/`--read` viewers are unaffected — there the `.html` is the deliverable.

- **Changed: inline code renders faster on both paths.** The inline-code dispatcher asked all five kinds (state mark, pill, spark, icon, avatar) about every span. It now looks up the span's first character and asks only the kinds that open with it, so `` `npm run build` `` reaches none. Per ordinary span on the markdown-it path (the escape, `renderHtml`, `offPlugin`) that is 112 ns down to 18 ns, and with one plugin switched off 1,426 ns down to 58 ns. The backslash escape also stopped building reasons it threw away: `` `\^{databse}` `` searched the whole icon set for a "did you mean" (173 µs) only to decide whether to strip a backslash, and now takes about 1.6 µs. Render output is unchanged.
- **Changed: an inline kind's `resolve` and `diagnose` take a trailing flag.** `resolve(text, off, probe)` may return `true` without building its fields, and `diagnose(text, off, explain)` may return `true` without building its reason. A plugin kind that ignores them is still right, only slower (`plugin.schema.json`).

- **Tooling:** npm script descriptions for the capability index now live one file each in `tools/script-docs/<script>.md` (`:` written `+`) instead of the shared `SCRIPT_META` map in `tools/build-capabilities.js`; adding a script touches `package.json` plus one new file. `capabilities:check` also fails on a description file with no script, an unknown group, or an empty description (this recovered `parity:transforms`, which an unknown group had silently dropped from the catalog).

- The `collage` lightbox is now covered by a real-browser suite: the Studio preview (click, Escape, click-away, and a tap on a phone-width and WebKit touch profile) and the exported player (axe over a collage slide and the open lightbox, plus Escape, click-away and Space). No product code changed; the suite found nothing to fix.

- A reference PDF you add is now stored with its real size and typed as a PDF, and a restore refuses a PDF row whose data is not valid base64 or is over the 5 MB a reference doc may be, and names it.
- A workspace backup stores photos and videos as they are instead of compressing them again: those files are already compressed, so the second pass spent several times the CPU to save 0 to 9%. Text in the backup is still compressed, and backups made before this change restore as before.
- A backup that cannot read one photo, video or PDF in this browser now leaves out just that file and names it in the backup's warnings, instead of leaving out every photo or failing.
- Storage-full and private-window messages now say "photos or videos" instead of "photos".

- The chat's attach controls are now two buttons in the message box: the **paperclip** opens your phone's or computer's own picker straight away (photos, videos, take one now, or files, each sent where it belongs), and a **Library button** next to it lets you tap saved photos, videos and files to attach them, with a check on what's attached. The one popover that sat on top of the phone's picker, with its search box and extra rows, is gone. Taking a clip you picked from the Library off a message leaves it in the Library; one you added from the device is removed again. The message box now gives the text its own full-width line, with the buttons on a bar underneath, and the two attach buttons are larger and further apart so a tap on one cannot land on the other. In dark mode the message box no longer draws a second, faintly filled box inside its own border; it looks the same as in light mode.

- **The Segno bakeoff's ratios hold still across runs.** `npm run parser:bakeoff:segno` now times a row's columns in alternating ~150 µs slices and reports each ratio as the median of the per-slice ratios, timed back to back. Five runs of unchanged code read the shipped dispatcher's every-span ratio at 1.32x to 1.40x (a spread of 0.08); the old harness divided two fastest rounds and spread by 0.20 (1.34x to 1.54x). The ns columns are now each column's median slice, not its fastest round.
- **Segno's `isDirective` is about 15 ns a span faster on ordinary code again.** Since #2513 it ran a `TAGS.includes(text[i])` substring search on every span that does not open with `{`. It now compares the three tag characters as char codes, and a test holds that comparison to `TAGS`. The bakeoff's Segno column returns from about 2.0x the retired kernel to 1.41x to 1.54x, in line with phase 1. Lattice's shipped dispatcher was not affected, but callers of the published `@laticent/segno` were.

- Playground: the 16 curated Galleries decks (4 showcases, 12 families) load when you pick one instead of shipping inside the page, so the Playground HTML drops from 555.5 KB to 429.9 KB.

- `spec/LPM.md` §3.3.1 documents what a zip plugin's inline kind is handed as `fields` for each field type, and a test pins it across the CLI's and the Studio's record readers. The zip half of `inline` stays provisional: the section names the changes #2686's reader is planned to make.

- The plugin consent text is versioned. Today's text is version 1, unchanged byte for byte, so every approval you already hold still counts; the CLI and the Studio accept a plugin approved under any version they still accept. An approval covers what its own version pinned, so a later version that pins more takes full effect once the older version is retired.

- Lint `chart-row-record-unread` no longer warns on a record the chart now draws. It reports a record with a field that has no span form yet (bullet's `band=` and `floor=`, progress's `note=`), one that follows another code span on the row, one in a later paragraph of its row or on the line after a heading item (the old spans draw a value there; a record is read only from the row's first line, so it stays a pill), and one the chart's row schema refuses that is not a pill either (`{3, targt=5}`), which used to drop the row from the chart silently.

- **Changed: the route budget watches every chart kernel, not only the largest.** A new
  Studio metric in `docs/route-budget.json`, `chartKernelsGz`, counts the union of all 24 chart
  kernels beyond the engine (195.6KB gzipped) with a 10% ceiling. Before this, a kernel smaller
  than chart-map could grow unseen until it overtook map. Now about 19.6KB of growth in any
  kernel fails the docs build.

- The Export-to-Marp bundle's README now states what the Marp for VS Code preview does with the deck's scripts, instead of saying nobody can confirm it. At VS Code's default preview security level (*Strict*) the scripts do not run, so Mermaid and the other runtime-built slides show as plain markdown. They run at one level only: trust the folder, then **Markdown: Change Preview Security Settings → Disable**. The two "Allow insecure … content" levels do not run them. VS Code stores the level per workspace, so the bundle cannot set it.

- Every `.vscode/settings.json` Lattice generates for Marp for VS Code (the Export-to-Marp bundle and the Marp kit) now writes `"markdown.marp.html": "all"` instead of `"markdown.marp.enableHtml": true`. marp-vscode deprecated the boolean key in 3.0.0 (2024-12-31), and 3.6.1 shows a warning popup when it is set. The new key needs Marp for VS Code 3.0 or later; an older extension ignores it and shows the deck's raw HTML as text.

- `stats`, `actors` and `kpi` follow the deck's `cards:` register (`center`, `top`, `spread`, `stretch`; `kpi compliance`, a flex column with its own spacing, does not follow it). By default `actors` rows and `kpi` tiles now size to their content and sit centered instead of growing to fill the stage; `cards-stretch` (per slide) or `cards: stretch` (deck-wide) restores the previous look. `stats` looks the same by default and gains the other three compositions on wide slides. Demo: `examples/cards-stats-actors-kpi.md`.

- Studio manifest autocomplete now offers every key and value in `manifest.schema.json` (it offered 9 keys and omitted `single-orientation` from `adapt.mode`).

- Inline code spends less time deciding what each backticked span is, most of all on brace text
  that is not a pill, such as a chart's `{2, 82}`, which no longer builds an error message nobody
  reads. Against the retired kernel on the bench fixture: 6.71x to 2.79-2.87x on one machine, and
  about half on GitHub runners (three runs, −48% to −53%). The gain depends on how many such spans a
  deck has; a deck with none gains a few nanoseconds a span.
- Segno gains three experimental APIs: `restrict(spec, { rules, nodes })`, which derives a smaller
  grammar the code generator can make its own parser of (it refuses to prune inside `greedy()` or
  `attempt()`); `kindsOf(spec)`, the node-kind order to seed such a parser with
  (`generate(small, { kinds: kindsOf(full) })`); and `slot.tryRead(text)`, `read`'s value or null,
  with no message built for a span that will not bind. The notation's plain-record parser is
  generated with the first two.
- The perf nightly now compares the inline-span tier head against base, so a per-span dispatcher
  regression past 12% files the rolling perf issue instead of waiting for someone to run
  `npm run bench:check`.

- The docs route-budget check gzips each chunk with the playground asset version (`/playground/v/<12 hex>/`) and Rollup's chunk-name hashes (`name.<8 chars>.js`) and esbuild's engine chunk names (`chunk-<8 chars>.js`) replaced by fixed strings of the same length, so two builds that differ only in those hashes measure the same and a bundle-free PR no longer owes a declaration for the noise. Measured chunk sizes fall about 1%.

- **Breaking:** where the host gives the render a `file:` deck folder (the CLI), a relative image or background that points outside that folder (`![bg](../assets/a.jpg)`, `![](/etc/hostname)`) now shows the drawn missing-picture stand-in. Keep pictures in the deck's folder or below. Before, `![bg](../x.jpg)` loaded. A `file:///…` address, a `data:` URL and the Studio's site-origin paths are unchanged.
- Internal: one `lib/core/media-sources.js` table now decides which picture sources (`data:`, relative path, `file:`, web, `sample:`, `asset:`) are local or remote, and `isRemoteUrl` is derived from it. Its answers are never looser than before.

- An npm plugin's approval is now kept per pinned version. Two projects that pin different versions of one plugin no longer replace each other's approval at every `lattice packages fetch`; each render reads the OS layer its own pin was approved at. `lattice packages untrust plugin/<name>` withdraws every pin. Zip plugins and components keep one approval, as before.

- The code door now measures Chromium's OS sandbox on macOS and Windows as well as Linux. Before, it assumed the platform default on those two. An npm plugin runs only where the sandbox reads on. A code package whose sandbox cannot be measured still renders, now with a warning, where before the line said the sandbox was on by default.

- **Breaking:** `cards-stack` draws its title-row pill with the pills plugin. Write the pill as `` `{shipped}` ``; a bare trailing `` `shipped` `` is now plain inline code. The first-party gallery and examples are migrated.
- **Breaking:** `cards-grid` draws its title-row pill with the pills plugin, the same way. A card whose title is only a pill now keeps the pill at the left of the row; before, the universal trailing-code rule pushed it right.
- **Breaking:** `logo-wall` draws the pill under each mark with the pills plugin. Write the pill as `` `{Series B}` ``; a bare code-only caption line is now plain inline code. The pill keeps its muted ink and no fill, and its size, through two new pill interface properties.
- **Breaking:** `policy-recommendation` draws the citation chip at the end of an evidence line with the pills plugin. Write it as `` `{FTC 2025}` ``; a bare code span there is now plain inline code. The panel keeps its quiet fill, hairline and secondary ink through the pill's color properties.
- **Breaking:** `list-tabular register` draws its row tags with the pills plugin. Write the tag as `` `{stable}` ``; a bare trailing code span in a register is now the ledger's plain meta cell. The register keeps its accent fill, uppercase label and wide tracking through the pill's color, case and tracking properties; the tag is slightly narrower than the old stamp.
- **Breaking:** `regulatory-update` draws the effective-date pill that closes each row with the pills plugin. Write it as `` `{Effective Feb 2026}` ``; a bare code span as the last nested bullet is now plain inline code. The citation (first nested bullet) stays inline code, since it was never drawn as a pill. The timeline counter and the `priority` tier badge are not pills; they keep their look on their own constants and a new base token, `--radius-full`.
- **Breaking:** `statute-stack` draws the citation and status pills with the pills plugin. Write them as `` `{15 U.S.C. §6501}` `` in the jurisdiction line and `` `{In effect since 2000}` `` as the last body bullet; bare code spans there are now plain inline code. Pill color follows the jurisdiction through `--lat-pill-edge` and `--lat-pill-ink`.
- **Breaking:** `roadmap` draws the meta pill on each phase header with the pills plugin. Write it as `` `Foundation `{Q2 2026}`` ``; a bare trailing code span in a phase header is now plain inline code, and the horizons layout no longer lifts it. The pill keeps its accent fill, its seat on the spectrum line and its grid-cell sizing; the canvas-colored ring around it is now a shadow outside the pill, so the filled pill is 1px larger on each side.
- `glossary` draws its auto-derived range pill (`A – N`) with the pills plugin in both render paths, marked `data-glossary-range`; the old `.range-pill` class is gone. The pill keeps the meta type step and the accent-soft colors.
- **Breaking:** `actors` draws the actor-name chip with the pills plugin. Write it as `` `{Head of Product}` `` at the end of the row; a bare trailing code span there is now plain inline code. The chip is outlined in the row's categorical hue and keeps the plugin's default padding.
- **Breaking:** the universal trailing-code pill rule is gone, with its `pill-tag` transformer. A trailing `` `code` `` on a list row is plain inline code in every layout; a pill is `` `{…}` `` (the pills plugin), and a label with a comma needs quotes, `` `{"a, b"}` ``. `checklist` takes its row pill the same way and keeps the right-edge push. The engine's split-page pointer states its own type and shape instead of reading the pill tokens.
- **Breaking:** `kpi` draws every status pill with the pills plugin. Write each as `` `{On plan}` `` on the tile row; a bare code span there is now plain inline code. The eyebrow above the heading stays a bare code span (it was never a pill). kpi keeps its uppercase labels, wide tracking, meta type step and status colors through the pill's case, tracking, size and color properties. The pill's legacy `--pill-border`, `--pill-bg` and `--pill-fg` hooks are removed: set `--lat-pill-edge`, `--lat-pill-bg` and `--lat-pill-ink`.
- `lint:deck` warns `bare-row-pill` where a bare code span sits in a place a component used to draw a pill from one (cards, kpi, actors, a register, a roadmap header and the rest), and names the `{…}` spelling to write, quoted when the label has a comma. The first-party exemplars and the kit sample are migrated.
- A pill whose author named a color (`{label, c5}`) keeps it inside every component that tints its pill by default, and the author's `sm` / `lg` still scale a pill a component sized outright. kpi's uppercase, tracking and size apply to the pills in its tile rows only, not to a heading's. The glossary range pill is skipped, with no stray space, for a first letter the notation reserves for a state mark (`-`, `/`, a space).
- `bare-row-pill` runs in `lint:deck` (the CLI), not in the Studio, to keep the Studio's lint bundle under its size ceiling; it covers the components the old universal rule reached (inventory, topic, cycle, citation-card, scene, obligation-matrix as well), reads a row indented up to three spaces as top-level, and stays quiet under `inline-code: literal`.
- Fixed two selectors left targeting `code` after the migration: regulatory-update's tall/strip row placement (the portrait pill sat in the head row and squeezed the body) and actors' dense-roster `order` (the pill landed before the name).

- Slide-comment metadata has one vocabulary and one reader. A new always-on `meta` plugin (`lib/plugins/meta/`) declares every comment key with its type; the engine, the linter, the notes extractor, the Studio and the packaged slide facts read the key list from it instead of five hand-kept copies. `meta` cannot be switched off, by a deck or by a host setting. No syntax changes: `<!-- _class: … -->` renders exactly as before, checked against the engine over 478 committed decks.
- The notes extractor treats `lat-meta`, `lat-pane`, `lat-panes` and the `<!-- stress-slide -->` marker as tooling, never as speaker notes.
- New lint rules for a record-shaped comment in a place that cannot be read: `meta-opener-bare`, `meta-not-own-line`, `meta-in-html-block`, `meta-block-in-container`. `legacy-directive-comment` exists and is off until the old form is cut.

- A logo wall is held back while its marks are measured on a first visit in the live preview, so it paints once, packed, instead of drawing the grid and jumping into rows. If a mark never arrives, the wall appears as the grid after 4 s.
- Studio exports (PDF, PowerPoint, images, webpage) and the Studio's print wait up to 4 s for a collage or logo wall to finish measuring before they capture, and never bake or print one that is still hidden.
- `collage` and `logo-wall` share one measuring kit, so a collage seen before also stamps at once on a revisit.

- **Changed: a record slide edits in the Studio as a directive slide does.** The "This slide" drawer edits a record in place (`<!-- {layout=cards, finish=ledger} -->`): a modifier joins it, a register word is written as its field (`head-left` becomes `headline=left`), and swapping the layout keeps `layout=` typed. The speaker note, say line and description editors read and write a record's `note`, `say` and `describe` fields. A key the slide does not set joins the slide's record; a slide written in directive comments keeps them (`<!-- _footer: Q3 -->`), and Compose rewrites a record pane marker in place, keeping its other fields, and writes a new one as `<!-- _pane: bar -->`, so the Studio does not put the record form into a deck Marp and VS Code still read. Lattice's own Marp export turns records back into the comments Marp reads; a raw `.md` opened straight in Marp does not see a record (step 4 of this line of work brings the full bridge).
- **The host's registers are record fields.** `finish`, `headline`, `rule`, `eyebrow`, `spectrum`, `spectrum-edge`, `spectrum-card`, `spectrum-card-edge`, `spectrum-trim`, `lift`, `stamp`, `tone` and `corners` take the values their front-matter register takes, on one slide: `{finish=ledger}` is `_class: finish finish-ledger`, and a register's default asks for its documented restore word (`{lift=off}` is `flat`). The two render the same `<section>`.
- **Completion inside a record.** After `<!-- {` the editor offers the record's fields, and after `field=` its values: components for `layout`, that layout's variants for `variant`, the class grammar for `class`, a register's own words for the rest.
- **Two lint rules for records.** `meta-record`: `lint:deck` reports what the engine drops from a record it reads: an unknown field, a value outside its register, braces or a quote that never close, a deck-only key, a repeated field. Each finding names the engine's code (`meta-unknown-key`, `meta-field-value`, `unterminated-record`, …). `meta-class-overridden` warns when two comments on one slide each set its class (`<!-- _class: stats -->` then `<!-- {headline=left} -->`): the class is one value, so the first one's words are dropped.
- The Studio's speaker-note editor no longer shows a record as the slide's note, and saving a note no longer deletes the slide's record.
- A plugin register named like a record field (`layout`, `note`, `pane`, `footer`) now fails plugin resolution even when the `meta` plugin is not among the plugins resolved.

- **Breaking:** a slide's `<!-- header: … -->` or `<!-- footer: … -->` comment now sets that slide only, with or without the underscore. It used to carry onto every later slide, as in Marp. Front matter is the one place to set them for every slide, and `_class: no-header` or `no-footer` drops them from one slide. Export to Marp writes these comments in the underscore form, so the exported deck renders the same. No example or baseline deck uses the plain form.

- **Breaking:** page numbers are on by default. Front matter `paginate: false` turns them off for the deck; a deck that leaves the key out is now numbered.
- **Breaking:** a `<!-- paginate: … -->` or `<!-- _paginate: … -->` slide comment does nothing. One slide opts out with the `no-pagination` class and back in with `with-pagination`. `lint:deck` reports the comment as `paginate-comment-retired`, and `--fix` deletes it where that changes nothing.
- **Breaking:** the `no-paginate` class is renamed `no-pagination`, to pair with the new `with-pagination`.
- A component opts its slides out of page numbers in its manifest, with `"chrome": { "pagination": false }`. Title, divider and closing do, so their skeletons no longer carry `_paginate: false`. A slide's class wins over the manifest.
- Export to Marp writes Marp's own `paginate` and `_paginate` directives, so a Marp render numbers the same slides.
- Slide facts (`lattice facts`) report `paginate: "true"` on every numbered slide, since numbering is now the default.
- `with-pagination` wins over every opt-out, including `silent`, collage and a statement image, which used to hide the number in CSS alone. `paginate:` reads the same everywhere: `false`, `no`, `off`, `0`, `skip` and `hold` are off, in the engine, the Studio and Export to Marp.
- `lint:deck` names `no-paginate` as renamed to `no-pagination`.
- The PDF writer draws a page number on a split slide under a finish as selectable text. Its `pointer-events: none` hid it from the hit test, so the number was kept in the photo layer.
- The Studio's preview bar puts previous, the slide count and next in one pill, with the slide-map toggle beside it. The map toggle moved up from the end of the slide strip. A divider now separates the slide actions (add, duplicate, delete, move earlier, move later) from the slide picker, and the actions wrap onto a second row, centered, where the strip is tall enough. On a phone the count reads "5 / 7", every control keeps a 44px touch target, and the bar keeps its height. In the Read posture, which has no preview bar, the toggle stays in the strip.
- Export to Marp loads its bundle builder on demand, so the engine every page boots with is about 24 KB (gzipped) smaller.

- The Studio's slide map replaces the slide pills at every width: with the map on, its thumbnails sit in the slide strip under the preview, where the pills were, and the pills come back when it is off. Live presence dots now show on the map's tiles, and outside Read each tile names its component.

- **Changed: a heatmap callout's marker is a shape and a color, and a chart draws at most six.**
  Callouts take six shapes in reading order, one each (circle, square, triangle, diamond, hexagon,
  star), and a color slot each, so a cell is matched to its label by shape as well as color. The
  callout's number rides inside the shape when the cell has room, and always in the lane, where it is
  as large as the label and centered on the digit's own height. On a grid whose values fill their
  cells, the shape now marks the cell on its own where the old numbered marker could not fit and left
  a bare ring. Every marker on a chart shares one size and one place: whole inside its cell's top-left
  corner, or a badge just outside it. A marker's size follows the cell's, and a cell's marker and its
  label's marker are the same solid color, and so is the ring around the cell. With a band key, a callout's words grow toward the key's
  label size as far as the lane holds them whole. The pill words still choose: `circle`, `tag` (the square) and
  `diamond` pick that shape, `c4` the color. A seventh callout and any after it are not drawn: the
  chart's description lists them, their `detail` still reaches the cell's hover card and the speaker
  note, narration stops at six, and `lint:deck` warns on each (`lib/plugins/legend/legend.docs.md`,
  `engineering/decisions/2026-10-19-universal-legend.md` § 18).

- The Studio's and the Playground's live previews no longer run function-plot in the page that holds your deck. A plot is drawn in a sandboxed frame (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`, an opaque origin, no network) and the drawing comes back as sanitized markup. The library is fetched and checked against its SHA-256 pin before the frame runs it, and only that frame may `eval`, because the library compiles expressions. The CLI exports and the plain `.html` have no host page and load the library as before, and the Studio's own exports (PDF, PNG, PPTX, Webpage) draw in-page too, so their bytes stay the CLI's. A plot's first draw is at parity with the in-page path (1247 / 1355 ms before, 1292 / 1496 ms after, headless Chromium).
- Mermaid in the Studio's and the Playground's live previews is drawn in a sandboxed frame too, and a first diagram takes about as long as drawing it in the page did, a little less on a first visit. The frame loads Mermaid's own ES-module build by URL (a 28 KB core, then only the chunks a diagram type needs) instead of inlining its 3.1 MB single file, so the page no longer parses 3 MB of HTML or runs a 350 to 500 ms script task. Measured in the real Studio, headless Chromium, 10 interleaved runs each, time from the editor change to the first diagram: median 1414 ms in the page before, 1342 ms in the frame now (ranges 1268 to 1654 and 1082 to 1493); a returning visit is 1112 ms on both; an edit redraw is 652 ms before and 670 to 825 ms now. An earlier CPU trace of one condition (1779 ms to 1366 ms) overstated the gain. The frame's policy names the one directory the modules load from and the engine's font folders, carries no `'unsafe-eval'`, and an import map's `integrity` pins the SHA-256 of every module, which a browser that supports it enforces (a changed module is refused). The ES modules are vendored beside the single file (`lib/plugins/mermaid/vendor/esm/`, pinned by tree hash, refreshed by `npm run vendor:plugins`) and staged under `frames/mermaid/`, which needs CORS: GitHub Pages sends it, the Cloudflare previews read `docs/public/_headers`, and the local servers are configured in `astro.config.mjs`.
- A flowchart's hover tooltip now takes the diagram's own palette (the rule in the diagram's sheet) in the Studio's previews, where the library's own tooltip showed a pale yellow. A link still opens and a click callback stays off at `strict`, as before.
- A Mermaid error in a preview keeps up to six lines (600 characters) of the library's message, the parse position and what was expected; a longer message is cut there, where the in-page library showed all of it.
- If the Mermaid frame cannot load its library (offline, a removed deploy), the preview stops offering Mermaid to the page and the next preview loads the library itself; the frame says so at once instead of after 30 s. The frame does not use the service worker or the HTTP cache, so a returning visitor fetches the modules again on each page load.
- A plugin now chooses the sandboxed preview frame from its manifest: an in-tree plugin declares `draw` (`frame`, `host`, `shim`) and ships `<name>.draw-frame.js` (and optionally `.draw-host.mjs`, `.draw-shim.mjs`); the registry generates the rest. The frame, host, warm-up and preload code name no plugin. Markup from the frame reaches the page through one sink, `ctx.drawInto`.
- A deck's or theme's own embedded fonts (`data:` faces within the size caps, and the engine's font folders) now reach the draw frame, so a diagram's label boxes match the font the slide paints.
- The Studio's deck-wide Mermaid check (what grounds the Architect chat in whether every diagram draws) now sends each diagram to the sandboxed preview frame instead of loading Mermaid into the Studio page, so the page no longer downloads the 857 KB library on the first edit. A frame that cannot answer gives no verdict, as before. The check starts 3 s after you stop typing (it was 0.9 s), so it no longer competes with the visible slide's own draw: on a 20-diagram deck an edit redrew in a median 1.47 s in the frame against 1.51 s in the page, where a 0.9 s start measured about 110 ms slower.
- Typing in a Mermaid diagram in the Studio takes about 50 ms longer through the sandboxed frame than drawing in the page (about 300 ms against 350 ms; measured, flat in the number of diagrams). It is the cost of the round trip, the sanitizing of the drawing and Mermaid's module build, not of the frame sharing the page's thread: with the frame in its own process the time is the same.
- Fixed: the first Mermaid diagram a preview gains no longer shows its source for seconds before drawing.
