A frame that draws answers the runtime's library request on the spot, and no load was left to run the pass again, so the fence stayed untagged and visible until a later edit (99 painted frames of source, then a draw about 6 s later, measured on the built Studio). The pass now runs itself; the same bench shows 11 source frames (10 in the page before the frame) and 270 ms to the diagram (651 ms in the page). Held-diagram edits were not affected: 0 source and 0 blank frames, as before.

- The Playground editor|preview split now starts at 46:54 with 300px minimums on both panes, the same pair contract as the Studio (was 45:55 with 280/320).

- Live: where a member is (side panel, editor or Read view, presenting, asking) now travels as a declared view on Tavola, beside the old `doing` field so tabs that have not updated still follow. Following someone no longer ends when they reconnect, and a slide change no longer moves a person who is typing: they get a "Go" instead.

- Live: awareness (presence) is now filtered by Tavola's Yjs adapter instead of a hand-written gate in the Studio. It bounds an update's size and entry count, ignores a forged clock, and rate-limits changes per member. A caret at the end of a deck keeps working, and a declared view key that fails its check is dropped by name without turning other fields off.

- **Changed: a deck with no `@callout` no longer downloads the callout layer in the Studio.** The lane, the markers and `legend-svg.js` load only for a deck that writes a callout; the largest chart download is about 6KB smaller (gzipped) and the rendered output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

- CI now runs `check:venue-conformance --strict` (integration shard 4). A PR that makes a component clip, drop a QR below its scan floor or leave the frame at any venue goes red unless the row is named in the tool's `KNOWN` list; deleting a fixed row's entry is required too. `--strict` now holds all four canvas families and fails when no Chromium is found.

- **Changed: a heatmap's callouts under the grid now flow side by side, like every other chart's.** They used to stack in one column. On a square slide with a key, the notes and the key now both sit under the grid, because the flowing notes cost less height; the notes beside the grid still win on wide slides.

- The Playground's Walk bar now ships the newcomer's first caption in the server-rendered HTML instead of filling it in after hydration and the plan fetch, so the page has text to paint at first paint. A returning visitor or a deep link never sees it: it stays hidden until their own plan lands.

- The Studio shows its first slide sooner on a phone. The code editor, which is hidden on the phone's opening view, now builds after the first slide, and the engine, base theme and preview runtime start downloading as soon as the Studio's own code has arrived. On a throttled phone profile over HTTP/2 (what production serves) the first slide moved from 3.97 s to 3.29 s (median of 15 cold loads; the 2026-09-22 build measures 3.86 s on the same machine).
- The Studio's loading animation, in the app and in the page shell that paints before any script, draws its grain with a gradient instead of an image. Chrome no longer counts the loader as the page's largest paint, so Lighthouse's mobile largest-contentful-paint reads 4.5-5.3 s instead of 13.6 s on the Studio. The loader looks the same.

- A chart component's **dispatch and framing** are now declared in its own manifest instead of wired into the chart family by hand. A chart declares `kernel: { figureClass }`, `tools/build-chart-registry.js` freezes every such block into a generated registry, and `chart-family.js` no longer names a single chart — the layout array, the kernel requires, the per-chart adapters and the figure-class alternation are all gone. Adding a chart used to cost four edits to that one file, one of which failed silently. The six kernels that were inlined in `chart-family.js` (`progress`, `timeline-list`, `piechart`, `gantt`, `kanban`, `matrix-grid`) moved to their own component folders, so all fourteen are alike. No authoring change: decks render exactly as before. *(A whole chart component is still not registration-free — the prose projection, image-set export, scorecard and docs family rosters remain hand-maintained; `design/skills/chart-component.md` lists them.)*
- Chart dispatch order is derived from the manifests instead of an array's line order — a chart is dispatched ahead of any chart it names among its own modifiers, so `<!-- _class: radar quadrant -->` still reaches radar rather than the quadrant chart.
- The live-preview runtime now transforms chart sections in document order rather than in layout order, so it numbers a deck's shared SVG ids the same way the export path does. Nothing rendered wrongly before — every reference stayed inside its own section — but two render paths disagreed about a shared counter.
- A kanban card's lane label no longer double-escapes an entity: a lane authored `Ops & IT` painted the literal `Ops &amp; IT`, and the two spellings counted as two lanes for color assignment.

- **Chart finishes are token swaps.** `pigment`, `etch` and `tone` each set a block of `--finish-*` values on the slide, the way `dark` does, and one shared set of mark rules reads them. The generated finish CSS drops from 194 KB to 79 KB raw (9.8 KB to 5.9 KB gzipped). Under pigment the token swap by itself changes no computed paint; the later changes in this release (first-hue neutral marks, the live dot, dark word-cloud ink) do. No chart stylesheet names a finish any more: the border a pill, bar or key tile drops under `etch` and `tone` is `--finish-border`, and the grouped-hub and quadrant-bubble ink moved into the generator.
- **A chart in a pane now drops the border under `etch` and `tone`**, as the same chart on its own slide does. The rule that dropped it named the chart's slide class, which a pane host does not carry, so a progress bar, status pill or key tile in a pane kept a halo outside its ink edge. The box holds: the pane's own pill padding now gives back the border a finish drops.

- **Every chart finish draws a no-category, no-status mark in the first hue instead of grey or slate, except where the first hue is already a category on that slide** (a hub-spoke with groups, a flowchart or state chart with category nodes, a `keyline` or `tinted` kanban board keep the neutral). This covers flowchart, state-chart and gantt neutral nodes, waterfall Plan / Actual columns, the hub-spoke hub and satellites, journey stage bars, and kanban cards and lane rules. Status and category marks keep their own colors.
- **`live`, `pilot` and `decision` status marks now carry a dot**, in SVG charts, in HTML status pills (`progress`, state-chart rows) and in the gantt key; under etch and tone a status mark is drawn in the heading ink so it shows on the pale wash. Print keeps its own typed glyph.
- **Under `tone`, line and ep-curve series are steps of the one ink told apart by dash pattern, and a slope's quiet lines are a pale step of the one hue** (its red/green direction signal is unchanged).
- **Pigment's risk matrix is less saturated, and etch's bullet measure is stronger than its range bands.**
- **Under `etch`, the heatmap and map ramps are a lighter wash (6% plus 0.5 of the step, was 0.82), the outline is heavier (2.6 hairlines), and the word cloud and slope take the one hue, as `tone` does.** The heatmap's top step against an empty cell loses magnitude contrast; each cell's value still picks its own ink.
- **On a dark slide, word-cloud words are 25% lighter toward the heading ink**, so every word clears AA (the raw category hue measured 3.1 to 3.9:1; the worst word is now 5.46:1 across the 32 themes).

- Under `tone`, a risk matrix's bands and a waterfall's up and down steps are shades of the one hue instead of status colors. Under `pigment`, a risk band, a slope's signal lines and a kanban card take quieter solids on a dark slide, and a card wears a wider solid accent bar.
- A pigment timeline's dots are solid, a pigment kanban lane rule is wider, and a risk matrix's legend discs wear the same band fill as its cells under all three finishes (one hue under tone).

- Under `tone`, pale shades keep the tone hue's color instead of turning grey (the light ladder mixes toward that hue lifted to near-white), dark-slide shades keep a floor (92 down to 29%) so low values no longer vanish into the background, journey personas take every other shade so they read apart, and a waterfall's down step is the dark shade it was meant to be.
- Under `etch` and `tone`, every status mark takes one level, the one a text-bearing status already used: a progress bar, a hub-spoke status disc, a gantt milestone and a state chart's pass or fail marker are now as quiet as a gantt bar or a state-chart node (etch 30/40% → 14/19%, tone 61% → 30/35%).

- **Tone is one ladder of shades on every chart.** A text-bearing mark (tower share, matrix-grid cell, key swatch; a journey persona dot later took every other step, see the tone-ladder fragment) used a second, paler ladder, so category 2 was a different shade on a tower than on a pie (closest pair of tower bodies 0.017 OKLab against 0.072). It now takes the same eight steps, and its text picks black or white from its own body. Tone outlines every mark in one ink, since the shades already tell the categories apart: a tone chart is one color plus status.
- **Under `tone`, a heatmap that prints its values uses the same ramp band as one that does not.** The top step against an empty cell rises from 3.10:1 to 4.19:1 at its worst on light and from 1.67:1 to 2.64:1 on dark, because each value already picks its own ink.
- Under `etch`, the heatmap and map ramps start as a wash and are lighter than first shipped here (6% plus 0.5 of the step; a later change in this release moved it from 0.82). A hub-spoke hub is a whisper of the first hue with a 2× edge instead of the page's heading ink, so a blocked or at-risk disc is the loudest mark on the slide. Demo: `examples/chart-finishes.md`.

- **Under `tone`, a word cloud colors each word by its weight tier in the tone hue**, instead of rotating through the categorical colors: the loudest word wears the one tone ink and each tier steps toward the theme's muted ink, so color repeats what size already says. Each word now carries `data-tier` (1 to 5). On dark, every word clears 4.5:1 (the default colors sat near 3.7:1).
- **Under `tone`, a matrix grid is one hue.** A row's label and its empty cells' outlines no longer wear the row's category color; they take the one tone ink, like the filled cells' shades.
- **Under `tone`, a matrix grid's filled cells are one flat pale tint with the heading ink**, like a quadrant's zones, instead of a deep ladder step. The row label carries the meaning.
- **Under `tone` and `etch`, a flowchart or state-chart node with no status, and a waterfall's Plan / Actual columns, take the first hue instead of grey.** Status nodes and the increase/decrease colors are unchanged; pigment keeps its neutral solid.

- **Changed: the Playground no longer loads or runs its lint while the editor is hidden.** In Explore and on a phone's
  preview pane the editor is not on screen, but it still fetched the 279 KB lint core and linted the draft in one long
  task. It now waits until the editor is shown and lints then, with no edit needed. Edit-first visits lint as before.

- **Changed: the Playground's component picker builds its search index on the first search, not on page load.** The
  index served only searches of two or more characters, but every visitor paid for building it during the page's largest
  startup task, about 160 ms on a mid-range phone.

- **The Playground no longer fetches or builds CodeMirror on a load that opens in Explore.** `EditorHost`
  built the editor in its mount effect and imported its code statically, so an Explore load paid for
  CodeMirror while the editor sat behind `display: none`. The host's adapter now holds the text as a string until
  the editor has a size, and the draft restore and the first render run through it as before. The editor's chunk
  loads, and the view is built, when the editor is shown (the switch to Edit, an Edit load), when something asks to
  focus it, or on an idle moment after the first sign of a reader (a key, a tap, the pointer). The caret and the
  slide band set in the meantime are replayed on the new view. On a phone profile (4x CPU) the page's blocking
  time fell from a median of 2,335 ms to 2,007 ms. An Edit load starts fetching the editor's chunk
  while the page hydrates, so it shows the editor as soon as before.
- **ArrowUp and ArrowDown no longer jump when the caret is scrolled out of the rendered lines.** After the
  preview scroll carried the editor away from the caret, CodeMirror stepped from the viewport instead of the caret
  (line 1 went to line 23 on an 8-slide deck). The Playground editor now steps by the document's lines from the
  caret whenever it is not drawn.

- **Changed: deleting a slide in the Studio now says what goes.** One block of Markdown can render as
  several slides when its headings split it, and deleting it removes all of them. Both delete buttons
  now name the block and count its slides before you confirm. The slide strip's armed button shows
  "Confirm delete “Pricing” (3 slides)" in a label above it, and Compose asks
  "Delete “Pricing” (3 slides)?". Before, they said only "Confirm delete slide" and "Delete?".

- **Changed: the Studio has one labeled "New slide" button instead of five ways to add a slide.** It floats
  over the preview's bottom-right corner, like Gmail's Compose, on a desktop, a tablet and a phone. When
  the preview is collapsed, it moves into the editor's toolbar. On a phone the edit pane floats one too,
  and it steps aside while you type. The gallery it opens is titled "New slide" too. The `+` in the
  strip's icon row, the editor's "Add" button and the phone menu's "Add slide" row are gone. The command
  palette entry is now "New slide…", and Compose keeps its "Add slide below". Tapping **New slide** splits it
  into **Before** and **After**, so you choose where the slide goes first; the gallery then says where your pick
  lands, and the button says "Added before …" or "Added after …" for a moment, as a plain message rather than a
  button (tapping it does nothing), instead of a pop-up notice.
- **Changed: slide actions in the strip confirm on the strip.** Duplicate, Delete and Move say what they did just
  above the slide strip, with an Undo button there, instead of in a pop-up notice.

- **Changed: slide actions are steps of the one undo history, and Delete takes one tap.** Add, duplicate, move and
  delete each go in as one labeled step ("Delete slide"), so ⌘Z from anywhere, the slide strip included, walks back
  actions and typing in order and shows the slide each undo changed. The note above the strip offers Undo until the
  deck changes again. In a Live session each action is a step of its own in your undo there. Because a delete can be
  undone, it no longer asks first, except while others are in a Live session with you.

- **Function plots run on the plugin host.** A ` ```functionplot ` fence is now the `function-plot`
  plugin (`lib/plugins/function-plot/`): one manifest, one fence renderer, and ONE browser function
  that draws the plot — the runtime bundles it, and the CLI export page runs the same function
  serialized. The two hand-kept copies it replaces had drifted (only the runtime's marked an error
  settled or showed the config when the library was missing). Plots draw exactly as before: the
  math gallery's PDFs are byte-identical in both themes.
- **Every capture waits for plugin figures to settle.** The CLI's PDF, PNG and PPTX captures, the
  `--player` bake and the Studio's export now wait until no plugin placeholder is `pending` or
  `hydrating` (bounded; a figure still waiting is exported showing its source, and the CLI says
  so). This used to hold only because function-plot happened to draw synchronously before `load`.
  The CLI also warns when a deck uses a plot and function-plot is not installed.
- **Added: a ` ```math ` fence** — display math the way GitHub and GitLab spell it. It typesets
  exactly like a `$$…$$` block; with math disabled it is an ordinary code block.
- **Fixed: a formula KaTeX cannot parse takes the theme's error ink.** KaTeX wrote failed math in an
  inline `#cc0000` — dark red on a dark slide, outside the token system. It now uses `var(--warn)`,
  on the error surface the math component had designed and never wired (`.katex-error` now; the
  dead `.math-error` rule is gone).
- **Fixed: a function plot that fails no longer overflows a `math canvas` slide.** Its error message
  (or its config, when the library is missing) was forced into the plot's aspect-ratio box and ran
  past the frame; the stage now sizes only a figure that is drawing or drawn.
- **Changed: a plugin fence is matched on the first word of its info string**, as markdown-it reads
  a language name. ` ```functionplot title ` used to be a code block and now draws; a
  ` ```math ` block that was plain code now typesets (no tracked deck had one).
- The fence wrapper chain is gone: one fence table in the plugin host owns every plugin fence, and
  a name a code language already owns (`json`, `tex`, …) cannot be claimed. ` ```anima ` moved onto
  it as the `anima` plugin.
- A ` ```latticeplot ` fence (the deprecated alias) now reports `function-plot/deprecated-alias` in
  `render().diagnostics`.
- **Breaking:** for deep importers only — `functionPlotFences` and `animaSceneFences` are no longer
  exported from `lib/integrations/markdown-it/plugins.js`, and `lib/core/function-plot-viewbox.js`
  is removed; the engine installs both fences through `installPlugins` (`lib/plugins/host.js`). A
  function-plot placeholder carries `data-lattice-hydrate` / `data-lattice-config` /
  `data-lattice-settle` (`pending` → `hydrating` → `rendered` / `error` / `unavailable`, plus
  `data-lattice-final`) instead of `data-fp-config` / `data-fp-inflated` / `data-fp-state` /
  `data-fp-final`.
- **Added: a component's plugins in `components.json` and the pick list.** A component that is
  designed around a plugin now carries `plugins: { requires, optional }` in
  `dist/docs/components.json`, and `components.pick.md` has a `plugins` column — so an agent
  choosing `math` sees that it needs the math plugin (and can use function-plot).
- **Added: `lattice packages new plugin <name>`** writes a plugin package — a manifest, a fence
  renderer, a token-only stylesheet, docs and two fixtures — into `lib/plugins/<name>/` (or
  `--dir`), refusing a name a plugin, a plugin fence or a code language already owns. It builds and
  passes the conformance harness unedited. **`spec/LPM.md`** is the first draft of the plugin
  contract: the package, the manifest, the module shapes, the `api: 1` host API and the settle
  protocol.
- The plugin conformance harness now also parses every fixture with the engine's own parser, and
  proves every plugin rule declines every character it does not declare as a trigger — the two
  limits phase A recorded.
- **Fixed: the Studio's Read pane no longer scans deck HTML in quadratic time** to decide whether
  to bake it. A run of unclosed `<code` tags (deck text can come from a shared link) took 247 ms
  at 8,000 and four times that at twice as many; the check is now one pass of the shared tag
  tokenizer.

- **Changed: every regular expression in `lib/**` now carries a complexity verdict, and the build fails on a new slow
  one.** `build:check` holds each regex literal to `tools/regex-census.json`, where the `recheck` checker recorded
  whether it runs in linear time, and holds each file's count of slow patterns so it can only shrink. A new pattern
  is decided with `npm run regex:census -- --write`, which refuses one that would add to a file's slow count.
  recheck is pinned in its own folder, `tools/recheck/`, so installing Lattice does not pull it in.
- **Changed: the slide map stamps the scroll offset its tiles were planned for** (`data-plan-at` on the rail's
  scroller), once that plan is on the page. A tile's `data-tier` follows a scroll one frame later, so a script that
  reads the tiers right after scrolling now has something to wait on.

- **Changed: a commit that changes a regex verdict by hand is refused.** A new pre-commit job,
  `regex-census-recheck`, re-decides with `recheck` every `safe` verdict the staged `tools/regex-census.json` adds or changes
  against `HEAD`, and blocks the commit on any that recheck answers differently. `build:check` trusts the table it is
  shown, so before this a typed `"safe"` passed it. The job runs only when the table is staged and costs about a second
  per changed verdict. It runs locally only. It needs recheck installed: `npm ci --prefix tools/recheck --omit=optional --ignore-scripts`.
- **Fixed: eleven regular expressions that could take quadratic time on hostile text now run in one pass.** The
  font-face and `var()` scans in the slide camera, the relationship label's clause and punctuation readers, the
  narration's link and Mermaid-directive strippers, the layout gate's fence, autolink and tag scans, and the
  masthead's footer-cell walk each read linearly now. A seeded differential test holds each one to the output of the
  pattern it replaced. Five tests that timed these paths with a stopwatch now check instead that every regex the
  path runs is linear.
- **Fixed: five more slow patterns, added in the agenda and progress work, now run in one pass.** The agenda lint's
  fence and HTML-block strippers, the agenda autofill's class-directive rewrite, and the progress transform's class
  attribute and first-heading reads. Each answers exactly as the pattern it replaced, held by a seeded differential
  test, and a work-count test holds every reader from this change to linear work.
- **Changed: the class-comment strip's speed tests count work instead of timing it.** Four stopwatch asserts in
  `test/unit/authoring/class-comment-strip.test.js` became a read count and a regex trace. They now fail on a
  rescanning strip on any machine, and a loaded runner cannot fail them. The flaky-test baseline drops from 476 to 472.

- The Studio now downloads the fonts your first slide did not need in the background, once the slide is on screen and you have paused. The first emoji, code block or `finish: sketch` you add then draws in its own font straight away, instead of showing a fallback font and swapping. It is skipped when the browser asks to save data.

- **Changed: the /cadenza and /suono library pages speak in the voice you chose in the Studio.**
  Both read the stored voice selection from Workspace › AI instead of their own ladder of whatever
  voice was ready first. A page's Kokoro voice picker changes the voice for that page only, and
  never moves the Studio's narrator. With no voice chosen yet, /cadenza uses the OpenRouter voice
  when a key is connected, else the browser's voice, and says which in its voice label.
  /cadenza says why it is silent ("needs a Gemini key"), and a stored on-device voice downloads only
  when you press Play, never on page load. /suono speaks a stored Gemini voice on a Gemini key alone.

- The Studio shows a first-time visitor the welcome deck's first slide about 1.3 s sooner on a phone. The build bakes the preview's first write, the page fetches it for a first visit only, and the preview writes it before the engine has loaded; the first real render then patches that same document in place. The bake carries no script nonce: the preview builds the document from its parts with this page load's own.

- `cuoio`'s ink ladder steps down instead of sitting on one value. In light decks body text read 5.95:1, secondary text 5.05:1 and the header, footer and page number 5.07:1, so only the font told a bullet from the footer. Body text now reads 8.5:1 and secondary text 6.5:1 (`--text-body` `#544639`, `--text-secondary` `#64574C`); the chrome keeps its ink. In dark decks secondary text moves from 7.0:1 to 8.5:1 (`--scheme-dark-text-secondary` `#BCAC95`) so it no longer matches the chrome. Hue and chroma are unchanged, so cuoio decks keep their warmth with body text a step darker.
- The docs site's Preview/Edit toggle labels its idle tab in body ink instead of muted ink. Its track stays a light wash over the bar, and the idle label measures at least 5.4:1 on every palette. Cuoio's lift had taken the muted label to 4.47:1.

- **Changed: the Studio no longer parses every saved deck at boot.** `loadDeckList` used to split
  each saved deck and count its slides for the deck switcher's label, in a menu that starts
  closed. It now splits a deck's `slides` on first read, and the switcher counts a row's slides
  when it opens (`deckMetaFor`, remembered by source). For an author with sixteen saved decks
  this takes about 140 ms of CPU off a phone's boot; a first visit is unchanged. `StudioDeck` no
  longer has a `meta` field.
- **Changed: `docs/scripts/react-mount-profile.mjs` takes `SEED=<file.json>`**, with
  `docs/scripts/seed-saved-decks.mjs` to write one, so the profile can measure a returning author
  with saved decks instead of only a first visit.

- **Changed: the Studio mounts its closed surfaces the first time they open.** The phone's ⋯ menu,
  its command palette, Send feedback, Version history, the compact Coach, Chat, Live, Reader views
  and Settings sheets, and both slide galleries used to mount at boot, closed. On a phone none of
  them is on screen at the first slide, and they cost about 50-65 ms of render work before it. They
  now mount on first open and stay mounted after, as Share and Workspace already did. Nothing
  changes on screen.

- **Breaking:** a Segno top-level value can no longer start with `>` (`>` is now the video record's tag); no shipped deck wrote
  one. Author HTML's `data-lattice-title`, `data-lattice-description` and `data-lattice-media` attributes are renamed to
  `data-author-…`, since only Lattice may stamp a media figure's words. The `video-slide-class` lint rule is removed.
- **`>{…}` is the video record's short form** (`` `>{"https://youtu.be/x", title="Tour"}` ``), as `^{…}` is an icon's and
  `!{…}` an avatar's; `@video{…}` still works. Segno's tag set (`TAGS`) gains `>`, so a top-level value can no longer start
  with `>`: no shipped deck wrote one (all 458 render byte-identically).
- **A video record draws its poster on any slide**, not only on a `video` slide: until now `@video{…}` elsewhere drew a bare
  text link, and `lint:deck` warned (`video-slide-class`, removed). The `video` slide still seats the clip beside its words.
- **Frames, finishes, tones and sizes for clips**: `@video{…}` takes `sm`/`md`/`lg`, a frame (`mat`, `keyline`, `float`,
  `device`, `corners`), a finish on the poster (`nimbus`, `halo`, `meridian`, with a strength such as `nimbus=40`), a tone
  (`duotone`, `grayscale`) and `show=title|all|none`; a deck sets them once with the `video:` register. The same shared layer
  (`lib/base/base.media.css`) serves pictures, so a clip and the photo beside it match.
- Narration speaks a media figure's title, then its description, from the record, whatever the slide shows; author HTML can
  no longer forge a figure's `data-lattice-title`, `data-lattice-description` or `data-lattice-media` (renamed `data-author-…`).
- **The `image` plugin**: `@image{photo.jpg, title="…", description="…"}` on a line of its own, with Markdown's
  `![title](src "description")` as its alias. The slide places it: an `image` slide makes it the photo panel (`mirror` puts it
  on the left), the new `bleed` class makes it a slide's background, and any other slide shows it as a figure with the shared
  layer's frames, finishes, tones and sizes (`image:` register). The address comes only from the author's own record.
- Marp's `![bg …](…)` keywords are retired: `lint:deck` warns (`image-marp-keyword`) and `--fix` writes the `@image{…}` record,
  moving the placement to the slide (`left` becomes `mirror`; a background on any other slide becomes `bleed`).
- The vector PDF keeps a picture's tone and finish (and a `bleed` slide's scrim): the writer used to draw the photo as a vector
  over its own blend layers, which take no hit test.
- A picture's box is known before it loads: the CLI reads the file's size, the engine knows every `sample:` picture's, and the
  Studio knows a Library photo's, so a slide lays out the same with the picture missing, and an `lg` picture under a heading no
  longer overflows.
- The docs site has an **Images** plugin page with a live demo (a framed figure, the photo panel, a `bleed` background, a
  tone), and the Video page now teaches `>{…}`, the frames, finishes and tones, and drawing on any slide. The Plugins hub
  counts its cards instead of saying "nine" over ten.
- On a portrait slide a stacked clip's poster gets shorter when the lead and caption need the room, instead of pushing the
  caption off the slide; with room to spare it fills the column at 16:9.

- The Studio's AI chat threads now live in IndexedDB instead of localStorage, so they no longer share the ~5.2 M-character space deck text needs. Threads saved by earlier versions move over once the page is idle, and a thread still shows while it moves.
- The Studio warns when localStorage is past 80% full, once a session and in Workspace → Data, because a full one stops deck edits saving. Clearing decks no longer resets your chat model choice.
- Applying or discarding a proposed edit while the AI is still replying now sticks: the reply used to put an applied edit back to unapplied (a second Apply edited the deck twice) and bring a discarded one back.
- Version history no longer parses every saved version to show its slide count: each version stores its count when it is saved.

- **Changed: exporting a narrated webpage keeps the Studio responsive while it packs the audio.**
  The export used to compress, encode and hash every clip on the main thread, about 0.1 s each,
  so the progress bar froze and Cancel stopped answering on a long deck. That work now runs in a
  small pool of background workers. On a 75-clip export, the main thread's blocked time fell from
  about 4.9 s to 2.4 s. If workers cannot run, the export packs on the main thread as before and
  produces the same file.
- **Changed: cloud voices speak up to six sentences at once, and a busy provider no longer
  fails a narrated export.** Live narration, Present's look-ahead and the export used to run
  three requests each against the same voice, with no shared view of what was already in
  flight. They now share one queue per voice model. The sentence being played goes first,
  then the look-ahead, then the export, and a sentence two callers both need is fetched once.
  When a provider answers "too many requests", the queue halves how many it sends, pauses (2 s,
  doubling if the limit repeats, or as long as the provider asks where the browser can read
  it), then climbs back. A provider that keeps failing pauses for 15 s
  before one test request. Each model starts at the parallel count we measured for it (six
  for most; one for CSM, whose provider serves one request at a time).
- **Added: Workspace › Narration › Parallel requests.** Choose how many sentences a cloud
  voice may speak at once (1 to 8), or leave it on Automatic. The on-device voice always
  speaks one sentence at a time.

- **Tests are fixed, never switched off without proof (HARD RULES #33 and #34).** `build:check`'s flaky-test census now
  fails on a test disabled by a literal (`{ skip: true }`, `test.skip('title', …)`, a bare `test.fixme()`) unless the
  comment above it gives what was tried, the evidence and what would re-enable it, and on any `.only`. Twelve integration
  files that skipped themselves when Chromium was missing, and so read as green in CI, now use `skipWithoutChrome`, which
  fails in any CI job that expects a browser. A machine-dependent skip in a node test must go through it or the new
  `skipUnlessCI`, or name the CI job that runs it instead (`// ci-skip:`); 94 existing ones are baselined.
- **Playwright no longer retries a failing test in CI.** `docs/playwright.config.ts` sets `retries: 0`, held by
  `checkPlaywrightRetries`; the nightlies now report a flaky test as a failure instead of a pass.

- Every PowerPoint file Lattice writes now comes from Calco's own PPTX writer: the plain picture-per-slide `.pptx` and the `--editable` one from the command line, and both from the Studio. pptxgenjs is no longer a dependency, so installing `@laticent/lattice` no longer pulls in `image-size` 1.x and its infinite-loop advisories. The files say the same thing (text, fonts, positions, notes, alt text and groups match the old writer's, tested), with these differences: identical pictures are stored once; a slide with no notes has no notes page; a note's line breaks become paragraphs; the document subject is no longer "PptxGenJS Presentation" when the deck gives none; a slide's picture is named "Slide N" rather than "Image 0"; the title and slide-number placeholders use the type and index PowerPoint itself writes; and a drawn mark whose corners the page rounds (`stroke-linejoin: round`) keeps round corners even when its line ends are square. The new bytes pass the ISO 29500 schema, Microsoft's Open XML SDK and LibreOffice; they have not yet been opened in PowerPoint, Keynote or Google Slides.
- **Breaking:** `@laticent/calco`'s `writePptx` takes JSZip as its first argument, `writePptx(JSZip, deck, outputType)`, as `writeOdp` does. `buildPptx(JSZip, deck)` returns the unwritten zip. `tidyPptxPackage`, `embedPptxFonts`, `groupShapes`, `applyRoles`, `uniqueShapeIds` and the `PptxGenJSClass` / `PptxGenJSLike` types are removed: there is no PptxGenJS output left to mend.
- The PowerPoint writer now follows the spec and the browser where pptxgenjs had its own defaults. Text is kerned at every size, as the browser kerns it, so small labels and letter-spaced headings no longer come out wider in PowerPoint. Each run carries the page's language (`lang:` in the front matter, or a `lang` attribute on an element) instead of always US English. A font the reader lacks is described by its own PANOSE and pitch, or by the deck's `serif` / `sans-serif` / `monospace` fallback, so a code font falls back to a fixed-pitch face, not Arial. A slide that is not exactly 16:9 keeps its own aspect at PowerPoint's 13⅓ in, and lengths and opacity are written exactly. A portrait deck's notes page shows its slide undistorted, and a layout that numbers its slides says so to PowerPoint's Header & Footer dialog. The file's properties state only what the deck says: its title is the deck's own title rather than the file name, with no "deck" stand-in, no "Lattice" or "Calco" author, no zero word count, and "Widescreen" rather than "On-screen Show (16:9)".

- `a11y-achromatopsia`'s light face now orders its status fills by lightness, so a reader who sees no color reads severity as one ramp. Done (the risk matrix's low band) is the lightest fill, at risk (medium) sits in the middle, blocked (high) is the darkest, and the critical band steps further still. Before, medium was the lightest band (luminance 0.098 against low's 0.039) and critical sat 1.09:1 under high. Now the steps are 1.59, 1.47 and 1.20:1. Every status mark on that face changes with it: gantt bars, checklist discs, kpi pills, state tiles. A palette may now set `--risk-critical-shade-keep`, the share of the fail fill critical keeps on the light face (82% by default); achromatopsia keeps 40%. Every other palette renders the same as before.

- `carbone`'s chart color cycle now starts with its blue, and its electric green moves to second. A chart paints a mark with no status in the first color, and green there sat so close to the on-track fill (0.075 OKLab on the light face, 0.053 on the dark) that an unstatused state tile or gantt bar read as on track. Blue sits 0.224 and 0.233 away. Everything that reads carbone's first chart color turns blue with it: single-series bars and lines, a chart's first group, the default icon tint, the default avatar ground and the first stop of a title or closing spectrum bar. The sequential ramps, a heatmap and a map choropleth, keep their green under every finish through two new optional tokens, `--ramp-hue` and `--ramp-ink`, so their range is unchanged (6.53:1 heatmap top step on light). Every color in the cycle is the same; only the first two swapped.

- CLAUDE.md now says Lattice is developed here and never consumed: a session measures, tests, renders and audits only on this repo's own install and `npm run build`, and stops and tells the owner when either fails.
- The cloud SessionStart hook now prints a plain "Lattice cannot be built in this session" banner when `npm install` or `npm run build` fails, and exits 0 so the banner reaches the session. It adds a likely-cause line only when `npm ping` cannot reach the registry, and withholds the "sandbox ready" line after a failed build.

- The rule that decides whether an overflowing slide can be fixed by splitting — and into how many pages — moved out of the export CLI into `lib/core/split-verdict.js`, beside the overflow probe it already shares. No behavior change: the splitting decks in the corpus render byte-identically. It is what lets a second measurer (the live runtime, per the Option B architecture) reach the same decision instead of re-deriving it.

- **The `progress-centre` Form cell is now `progress-center`.** The last UK-spelled
  identifier in the engine, renamed across the Cell directory and its two files, the
  `region` enum in `cell.schema.json` and `frame.schema.json`, ten Frame manifests, the
  progress Tile, `lib/forms/index.js`, and the docs-site Form diagram. Internal only —
  no deck-author surface names it, the id never reaches the DOM (the rail's class is
  `.tile-progress`), and nothing persists it, so no deprecation alias is needed. Two
  prose references to the footer's `footer-centre` zone went with it; the
  `--footer-center-*` tokens were already US-spelled.
- **Corrects the surviving-spelling claim in HARD RULE #21 and `engineering/house-style.md`.**
  Both said 71 British spellings remain in living prose, about 39 of them this cell. That
  cluster is gone, so both now read as history and neither restates a present-tense total —
  `checkUsEnglish`, the tool that measured 71, was deleted with the ratchet, so a fresh
  number would be a different measurement wearing the old one's clothes.

- **The agent kit is now organized by where you are putting it, not by what kind of file each page is.** `README.md` routes by destination — a Claude Project, a Custom GPT, a Gemini Gem, NotebookLM, Copilot, a coding agent, a local model, or one paste into any chat — and each `start/` page names the exact text to paste and the exact files to upload.
- **New `paste/`: three ready-made instruction texts**, each sized to a documented platform cap and gated in the build so it cannot outgrow it. `standard` fits every instruction box measured (Windsurf's 6,000-char global rules file truncates silently past it); `max` fits the 8,000-char Custom GPT and M365 caps; `solo` is self-contained — 20 layouts with their real skeletons and a worked deck — for a local model or a single paste.
- **New `upload/`: ten pre-bundled knowledge files** with globally unique names. Knowledge uploaders cap file *count*, not bytes, and flatten folders; the kit's 92 files cleared none of those caps and carried six files named `README.md`.
- **New `render/`: how to turn a finished deck into a PDF.** The kit previously documented no render step at all — a search of all 92 files for `npx`, `marp-cli` or an install command on the authoring path returned nothing.
- **New `examples/`: five complete, renderable decks.** The kit shipped none; the most `_class` directives in any single fenced block was one, and no two slides were ever separated by a `---`. The four real decks are copied from `exemplars/` with two transformations, both so they render through the route the kit documents: the palette line becomes `cuoio`, and the runtime `<script>` tags are appended.
- **New `repo/` and `plugin/`:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, a Cursor `.mdc` rule and a skill for coding agents, plus the same skill as an installable Claude Code plugin.
- **Fixed:** generated front matter and every worked example now say `theme: cuoio`, not `indaco`. The Marp kit published beside this one registers only `cuoio` and `cuoio-dark`, and Marp resolves palettes by name — so the kit told every model to write a theme its own no-install render route could not resolve, and the deck rendered unstyled with no error.
- **Fixed:** the 61 empty `## Demo deck` headings — every component file now links to its live page on the docs site, which carries every variant rendered plus an in-browser editor. Also 244 links that pointed at component files a bundle does not contain.
- **Fixed:** the docs-site URL in the generated component catalog pointed at `slidewright.github.io`, not `lattice.style`. It was the only navigational URL in the whole 2.2 MB kit.
- **Fixed:** the Claude Code skill named three `references/` files that did not ship, so it failed on activation; they now travel with it under both `repo/` and `plugin/`.
- **Fixed:** `plugin/README.md` documented `/plugin marketplace add`, which resolves a manifest at a repository's default-branch root — not where these files publish. It now leads with the copy route that works.
- **The small-model path is measured, not just designed.** 60 decks from three real small models (`Qwen2.5-3B`, `Llama-3.2-3B`, `Gemma-3-4B`) at Ollama's default 4,096-token context, scored by the kit's own checker: **60/60 with valid front matter and zero layout names invented outside the 20**. Every structural error across all three families — 16 of 16 — is the one nested-vs-inline title rule, at a sharply family-dependent rate (Gemma 11 decks of 20; Qwen and Llama 1 each), and the checker catches it with an autofix. Method, limits and a harness bug that nearly shipped as a finding: decision note §5.
- **A prose fix for that rule was tried, measured, and reverted.** Showing the wrong shape beside the right one made Gemma *worse* — 14 errors across 11 decks became 22 across 13. Warning-framed content is learned at the rate of direct exposure, which is the same reason `solo` carries no "not for" lines. The rule stays stated once, positively, and `check.mjs` catches the rest.

- The agent kit's render page now teaches a second route that does **not** move the deck: hand `marp-cli` the stylesheets with `--theme-set` and render the deck where it already sits. The page also names, for the first time, what Marp contributes and what Lattice contributes, the six things that make a deck Marp-renderable, and the three runtime `<script>` tags with the order they have to run in.
- It states where the assets come from — one `curl` of the published `dist-kits` tarball for everything including `fonts/`, a jsDelivr URL for the runtime scripts, and a warning that `raw.githubusercontent.com` serves JavaScript as `text/plain` with `nosniff`, so a `<script src>` pointing there is downloaded and never executed.
- Three asset rules, each measured by rendering the same deck both ways: `--theme-set` takes local paths only (a URL renders the deck in default Marp styling, silently), `fonts/` must sit beside the **output** file rather than the stylesheet, and the runtime scripts may be local or a CDN URL.
- The kit README said "the two runtime `<script>` tags" while every deck it ships emitted three. Both counts now derive from `RUNTIME_SCRIPT_SRCS`, the one list that names the runtime engines — the tag block is generated from it too, so the pair cannot desynchronise again.

- **The agent kit is organized by task, and now carries the quality canon.** Four folders, each answering a question a person actually has: `authoring/` (writing a deck), `components/` (which layout, and how), `skills/` (creating a new artifact from blank), `reference/` (machine records for tools). A fifth, `review/`, carries the checker. The root `README.md` routes by task and costs each path in tokens, and every folder has its own README.
- **`authoring/deck-canon.md` is new and is the most important thing in the kit.** It is `DECK_CANON` — the ~925-token statement of how a boardroom deck argues (one idea per slide, narrative arc, rhythm, restraint, bookends) plus the **17 traps the deck reviewer flags, each with its fix** — which the Studio chat sends itself on *every turn* and which the kit had never shipped. The component files say how to author a layout correctly; this says whether the deck is worth showing. The short on-device canon ships beside it for very tight contexts.
- **The seven `design/skills/` guides ship verbatim** under `skills/` — deck, theme, component, chart-component, finish, lens, speaker-notes. Each is self-contained: the 10/10 bar for that artifact, a mental model, a numbered recipe, a copy-paste contract, what good and bad look like, a ship checklist, and common mistakes. A test pins them byte-for-byte against `design/skills/`, because unlike everything else in the kit they are hand-written and could drift.
- **`reference/studio-prompts.md`** carries the generator canons the product sends its own model — `THEME_CANON` and `COMPONENT_CANON` — with an explicit note that the matching `skills/` file is fuller and wins on disagreement. A 2026-07-19 investigation found these prompts had silently drifted from the shared design canon in two confirmed places, so shipping them without stating precedence would invite a reader to follow the drifted one. **`FINISH_SYSTEM` is deliberately not shipped, and the file says why:** it is computed inside `architect.ts`, which imports `fuse.js` and `react` from the docs workspace, and reading it broke a root-only `npm ci`. `skills/finish.md` teaches the same four-layer system more fully, and a repo test already reconciles the two.
- The publish path filter now covers `design/skills/**`; without it, editing a skill would not have republished the kit.
- **Known gap, recorded rather than half-answered:** there is no motion/Anima skill. Anima has four decision records, a player bundle and shipped examples, but no `design/skills/` file — so the kit cannot teach it either. That is its own piece of authoring work.

- The agent kit teaches Lattice, not Marp. Every deck shape it hands a model now opens with `theme: indaco` and `paginate: true`, without `marp: true`, and its render page leads with `npx @laticent/lattice deck.md deck.pdf` and the Studio. Rendering with marp-cli moved to one page, `render/lattice-export-to-marp.md`.
- The agent kit has a single entry file, `start.md` (about 7.6k tokens): what a good deck is, the rules, all 80 layouts in one line each, the skeletons of the 19 most-used, and how to check and render.
- The kit's build fails when a link points outside the kit, or when any page but the export page teaches Marp.
- The kit's starter deck draws its kpi status pills again: `` `{On plan}` `` replaces a bare `` `On plan` `` span, which has rendered as plain code since 2026-10.
- `lint:deck`'s `bare-row-pill` fix now says the backticks are part of the notation. The old wording read as Markdown formatting, and the braces printed as text.
- lattice.style serves the agent pack at `/agents/` (`/agents/start.md`, one file per layout under `/agents/components/`, the craft guides under `/agents/skills/`, the checker at `/agents/review/check.mjs`). `/llms.txt` sends agents there first, and lists the 700 KB component reference last.
- A site page's Markdown copy now links other pages' Markdown copies instead of their HTML pages.
- The authoring guide links the agent pack and the modifier catalog. Its old link to a GitHub copy of the component reference was dead.
- A nightly eval (`tools/agent-pack-eval.mjs`) has a model write three decks from `start.md` alone, and a small model three from the solo paste text, then lints and renders each one.
- `start.md` lists each layout's variants and its words-per-item budget, and has an "Inline notation" section: one line and one example for each plugin (pills, icons, sparks, checks, avatars, image, video, callout, legend and the fence plugins). The pack now carries all 16 plugin docs under `plugins/`.
- `list-steps` teaches its real shape. Its skeleton showed `1. Title — body` on one line, which renders the whole sentence as the bold step title, and every copy of the skeleton (the component's docs, the agent kit's `start.md` and starter deck) inherited it. The skeleton is now `1. Title` with the body on an indented `- ` line. The variant guide adds `stage`, `milestone`, `rank` and `tier`.
- New `lint:deck` warning, `list-steps-inline-body`: a `list-steps` step with its title and body on one line. `--fix` splits it. The `timeline` variant is exempt. Five example decks that used the one-line form are fixed.
- `start.md` has a "Parts any slide can carry" section (eyebrow, subtitle, a pill on a row, the key insight, the below-note, annotations, corner tags, numbered cards) and lists every front-matter setting (`mode:`, `finish:`, `venue:`, `typography:` and the rest), each linked to its full rule. Each layout line says when that layout takes no key insight or below-note. The pack now carries the universal reference (`authoring/universal.md`) and the front-matter reference (`authoring/registers.md`).
- The universal reference's key insight example wrote cards as `- **Title.** body`, which `lint:deck` rejects on `cards-grid`. It now uses the nested shape, and a test lints every example in that reference.
- `start.md` and the render page show how to fetch the checker together with the catalog it reads (`/agents/review/check.mjs` and `/agents/reference/components.json`). Fetched on its own, the checker skips the word-budget checks.
- In `start.md`, each plugin example names the layout it needs when it needs one (a callout on a `heatmap`, check shortcuts on a `verdict-grid`), and the legend has no example, because no layout draws an authored `@legend{…}` key yet. Rendering every quoted example found three that print as raw text on a plain slide.
- The agent pack keeps code examples exactly as their docs write them. The link flattener had been rewriting links inside code too, so `![](asset:team-offsite)` and the avatars example's `![](marcus.jpg)` shipped as dead GitHub links. Folder links now go out as `tree/` URLs with no trailing slash (GitHub answers a folder's `blob/` URL, and a `tree/` URL ending in `/`, with 400), and the build fails on a link to a path that is not in the repo. That check found and fixed three dead links in the pills and universal references.
- `start.md` and the universal reference now say `silent` turns off all four running bands (header, footer, page number and section rail); they said three. `start.md` no longer tells authors a closing slide follows the title's `# H1` order; its closing skeleton shows the real `## ` shape.
- `start.md` now shows the speaker-notes syntax, says a `kpi` status pill takes its color from the row (with `kpi attention` for an off-plan metric), and carries `bar` and `piechart` skeletons. The `kpi` skeleton drops three decorative pills its own docs call an anti-pattern. A model given only `start.md` hit each of these gaps.
- `lint:deck`'s `list-steps-inline-body` no longer flags or rewrites a step-shaped line inside a speaker note, splits after a code span rather than inside it, keeps a mixed-case body's case (`iOS`), and catches a body indented two spaces under `1. ` (CommonMark does not nest it).
- `start.md`'s front-matter list now includes `profile:` (`general`, `teaching`, `mission`), which its canon names. The paste texts' rules now name the layouts a "ledger" or "statement" rule covers, read from lint's own sets; the solo text lists only its own layouts.
- `start.md` now says which `kpi` rows draw the warning color under each variant (the first real-model run put `{Breaching}` on a row drawn green with a check), that `big-number` and `quote` take an optional `##` claim, and the ten `timeline-list` status words.
- `start.md` says where a `kpi` key insight fits (3 rows, never on `ops`) and that `kpi compliance` holds 3 rows; past that the export clips.

- Anchor slides (title, divider, topic, closing) now keep or drop each chrome band by one rule: a band stays unless the slide already does its job. The title drops the running `header:`, because it names the deck. Every anchor keeps the `footer:`, so a "Confidential" or copyright line now shows on every slide that opens a section, including `divider numbered`, which used to hide both header and footer. Topic slides no longer show a page number, because their track says where you are. Bring a band back on one slide with `with-header` or `with-pagination`, or drop one with `no-footer`.
- A divider's section marker (`2/4` and the marks) sits where the deck's section rail sits on the slides after it: bottom-right by default, bottom-center under `progress-rail: center`, and as marks alone, upright on the right edge, under `edge`. Its count is set in the footer's own type, and the footer, the count, the marks and the page number now share one center line on every slide; the rail's marks are spaced in the marker's rhythm. Under a bottom-right logo the marker steps aside as the rail does, and `divider with-pagination` keeps the number clear of it. A `divider qr` at `venue: conference` or `hall` keeps its full code size again.
- The Studio's starter text for a new title, divider or closing slide no longer blanks the header and footer with `_header: ''` / `_footer: ''`.
- `npm run lint:deck` now warns `empty-section` (it was a suggestion) when a divider follows another divider, which leaves the first section empty and makes the first rail a reader sees say `2/4`.
- The section rail no longer moves within a deck. The footer band reserves a fixed column for the page number, so the rail holds still when the count reaches two digits and on a slide without a page number (it moved 10 px and 50 px), and a divider's marker ends on the same line.
- The footer, the page number and a divider's section marker share one baseline on every slide; a title's, divider's or closing's sat about 5 px lower than a content slide's. An image in `footer:` now sits inline at the height of a capital letter (it was drawn at its own size, a hundred pixels tall on a divider, or clipped away with the words after it), and a `<sup>` in the footer no longer moves the page number or the rail.
- The running header and the `meta:` line now speak as one: the same weight, letter spacing and muted ink. The meta line was a tinted label color that read as slide content. The eyebrow keeps its heavier, wider label voice.

- The Studio chat's Architect edits the deck only when you ask for a change. A question, about the deck, a photo or a video, gets an answer and no diff card, even when the deck has open review notes.
- The Architect talks in plain words: no "the checker", "warnings", "referent" or layout class names. The note under an edit reads "Worth a look before you apply this: …", and the line under a reply is one sentence ("Read about the big number layout, drafted changes to the slides and checked the deck.").
- The review note for a hero number reads "a hero number with nothing to compare it to" instead of "with no referent".
- Two more review notes drop jargon: "one item on this slide runs to 92 words" (was "a cards-grid element runs to …") and the scorecard's "hero numbers with nothing to compare to".

- **Changed: `progress` and `timeline-list` are recorded as whole-slide layouts**, not candidates
  for splitting. Both look sliceable — clean repeated blocks in the rendered DOM — and neither is:
  a progress chart's bars share one baseline and the comparison between them is the read, and a
  timeline's spine is a single rail across the whole set whose dot colors are picked by position,
  so one milestone per page draws a rule to nowhere under a dot that is always the first color.
  Nothing changes in any deck; the reasons are now on the record so the next sweep does not enroll
  them on the strength of their markup. `split-compare` was examined and declined for its own
  reason: it holds exactly two options by contract, and its verdict card would repeat on both.

- `backdrop: clear` now fades softly in exported PDFs, HTML and images, matching the Studio. It used to end in a hard-edged panel. In the CLI's PDF the fade is embedded as one image per cleared slide (about 80 KB); text and the finish stay vector.
- The Studio's PDF download draws a spotlight (`backdrop: spot-…`, or one baked into a Fabricate finish) with its soft edge instead of a solid arc, and draws the `clear` fade without the vertical stripes it showed over a dot texture.

- **Fabricate's "Clear behind content" now clears the whole content area.** It used to paint a central oval that missed the top-left heading and only faded the finish behind the edges of the text. A finish saved from now on clears the eyebrow, heading and body completely and shows only in the margin, with a soft edge on screen and a hard one in exports. Finishes saved earlier keep the old oval until you re-save them.
- **Changed: "clear behind content" fades out across the whole margin on screen.** The clean area no longer reads as a panel with a border; exports keep the hard edge.

- A finish's backdrop no longer comes out blotchy or grainy in an exported PDF. The writer used to store the glow and texture behind each slide as a low-resolution JPEG picture, which broke a faint glow into blocks and color patches; it now draws them: the glow as a smooth picture computed from the finish itself, the grid, weave, rings and dots as sharp lines, and a clear panel or spotlight as a smooth fade. The PDF also shows the finish's richer on-screen look instead of the flatter export look, keeps a `tint-edge` rail that a finish used to hide, and is usually smaller (a dark `loom` deck went from 455 to 165 KB). `--chrome-pdf` is unchanged.

- The issue mirror is now `backlog.d/`, one generated file per open issue, and `BACKLOG.md` is gone. Each file carries the issue's column, its area, type and priority labels, its `needs:` flags, and its swimlane and acceptance check, read by the triage gate's own parser. `npm run backlog` lists the open issues and every `followups.d/` item in one view, grouped by area and sorted by severity, and filters with `--area`, `--min`, `--issues` and `--followups`.
- Every `followups.d/` item now carries `area` (an `area:*` label name), `severity` (`high`, `medium` or `low`) and `swimlane` (the governing doc's repo path). `checkFollowups` requires all three and refuses `severity: critical`, which belongs on an issue. Every existing item was classified, and every new item must carry them.

- **The ten deck-level front-matter registers now live in `lib/base/base.registers.docs.md`.**
  `mode:`, `finish:`, `split:`, `stamp:` / `tone:`, `spectrum:` / `spectrum-edge:`, `rule:`,
  `eyebrow:`, `headline:`, `lift:` and `corners:` — with a table at the top naming what each
  one selects and its default. Nine of them were nested under `base.docs.md` § `sketch`, a
  **per-slide variant**: `mode: sketch` is how you turn sketch on deck-wide, so the first
  register landed there fairly and eight more followed it one at a time. A reader looking for
  `headline:` had no reason to open a section about handwriting.
- **`lib/base/base.docs.md` drops 24,504 → 15,682 tokens**, which matters because HARD RULE #6
  makes it a mandatory read before authoring a base modifier. The move is mechanical: nine of the
  ten register bodies are byte-identical to what left, with only the heading level changed, and
  the tenth (`eyebrow:`) carries a one-line edit because it pointed at a section that stayed
  behind. The other falsified cross-reference (a `tone-*` variant pointing at the `stamp:` /
  `tone:` registers "above") now names its file too.
- **The two files together are 26,121 — about 1,600 MORE than before.** The frequent read got a
  third cheaper and the rare one became findable; a reader who needs both pays more.
- **Every per-slide token the registers resolve to is listed in `base.docs.md`**, grouped by
  register and derived from the class names in `lib/base/*.css`. HARD RULE #6 sends `_class:`
  authoring to that file, and moving the registers out had cost **38 of 48** register-family
  tokens their only hit there — so `grep spectrum-card-edge-top lib/base/base.docs.md` worked
  before this branch, stopped working, and works again.
- Routing follows the content — `CLAUDE.md`, `design/skills/finish.md` and
  `design/design-system.md` point register questions at the new file.

- **The rasterize benchmark tier can now be blessed and checked, not just dumped.**
  `bench:bless -- --export` writes `exportDatasets` into
  `test/benchmark/baseline.json` and `bench:check -- --export` compares against it
  (±50%, same-machine, with the MISSING/workload mirrors the other tiers carry). The
  tier has had the right `{ main, summary }` shape since 2026-08-03, but `main()`
  handed that summary to the `--json` dump and to nothing else, so the only thing
  comparing it was the nightly — head-vs-base on one runner, leaving no durable
  before/after record (HARD RULE #19(b)). The apparatus shipped wired but inert; the
  record was written shortly after, and the block is in the committed baseline.
- **A rasterize cycle that screenshots nothing now fails instead of reporting a
  record time.** `exportTier` swallows a `setContent` failure by design — a
  `networkidle0` timeout over a fully laid-out page is a false alarm — and then
  screenshotted zero sections, which read as an enormous speedup.
  `tools/perf-nightly-compare.mjs` compensated downstream with a `-90%` "workload
  collapsed" heuristic that can only fire where there is a base arm to compare
  against; a `--bless` would have written the broken number into the committed
  baseline with nothing to catch it. The cycle now counts its own screenshots, and
  that count is the blessed workload signal.
- **A benchmark tier this repo has not blessed yet reports rather than failing the
  run.** Drift exits 1 on any machine because a blessed row has been recording
  nothing; a tier nobody has blessed has no rows to rot. Which tiers those are is a
  declared list, not a guess at the block — an absent block cannot distinguish "never
  blessed" from "blessed once and since deleted", and the second is the rot the check
  exists to catch. A partly blessed tier still drifts normally, so a newly added row
  stays red until it is blessed.

- **`lint:deck --fix` rewrites a Marp `![bg …](src "description")` line into Markdown's picture, `![description](src)`**,
  rather than an `@image{…}` record, and moves its placement to the slide as before (`left` becomes `mirror` on an `image`
  slide; any other slide gains `bleed`). On those slides Markdown's picture is the record's shortcut, so it draws the same
  photo, and the line stays the one an author already knows. A description that starts with `bg` becomes `Image: …`, so it
  never reads as the keyword again. A line with no description becomes `![](src)`, which `image-no-alt` then asks you to name.
- Every shipped example deck is swept off `![bg]`, and each swept photo gets a name a screen reader can say. 15 of the 16 swept decks render
  pixel-identically to `main`; `bg-on-any-slide`'s three background slides gain `bleed`'s scrim behind the heading.
  `examples/bg-split-ratio.md`, which showed a `![bg left:40%]` share being ignored, is removed.
- Exporting a deck with a locked figure (a drawing the CLI captures in its own page) to PNG or PDF no longer fails with
  `Cannot find module '../core/sanitize-slide-html.mjs'`: the bundled CLI read two files relative to `dist/`.
- The Studio's photo checks and Compose now see what a slide inherits from the slides before it. A running
  `<!-- class: image -->` set on an earlier slide, and a `backgroundImage` from the front matter or an earlier slide, change
  which picture is a slide's photo; the Studio read one slide's text, so its photo-contrast check stayed silent on such a
  slide, and Compose's Placement badge called a picture placed that the engine drew in the text. Both read the whole deck now,
  through the walk Export-to-Marp uses (lib/core/slide-carried.mjs).
- `lint:deck` (and the Studio's lint panel) now warns on every Marp `![bg …]` line (`image-marp-keyword`), and its fix
  rewrites the line as above. The `image` layout's samples, skeleton and slot description, the galleries and the component's
  docs now teach `![A name](path)` on an `image` slide.
- **Breaking:** the engine no longer reads Marp's `![bg …]` keywords. A `![bg](photo.jpg)` line draws as an ordinary
  picture in the slide's text, on every surface (CLI, Studio, Playground, player), and is never the slide's background or
  an `image` slide's panel. `lint:deck` warns on each one wherever it stands (a line of its own, a sentence, a list item, a
  quote, a table cell, a heading; any case), because while one is on a slide no other picture becomes its photo. `--fix`
  rewrites a slide's one `![bg]` when it stands alone on its line: Markdown's picture, `![A name](photo.jpg)`, with the slide's
  class saying where it goes (`image`, `image mirror`, or `bleed` for a background). It leaves the line for you, and says why,
  when the rewrite would lose the photo: two `![bg]` on one slide (Marp stacks them; a slide places one photo), a `![bg]` that
  shares its paragraph with text, or another picture already alone on the slide.
  Export-to-Marp still writes `![bg]`, because Marp reads it. The `bg-side-unread` and `bg-ratio-unread` lint rules are
  retired with it. **Security note:** the scheme allowlist used to drop a `![bg]` at an `http:`, protocol-relative (`//host`),
  `blob:` or `ftp:` address, with a `meta/url-scheme` diagnostic. It is an ordinary picture now, held to the same policy as
  any `![x](…)`: the preview shows a placeholder until the reader allows the site, the CLI export leaves it out unless run
  with `--allow-remote`, and `web-image` reports it (every one, since each loads). `javascript:` and `file:` are still refused
  by markdown-it. The photo a slide places still follows the allowlist.
- The Studio's photo-contrast check now runs on a slide whose photo is Markdown's picture or a record; it armed only on a
  `![bg]` line, so a swept deck's photos went unchecked. Its photo-size prefetch measures the photo each slide places, asked
  of the same rule, instead of `![bg]` lines.
- A Library photo whose description starts with "BG" is placed as the slide's photo; its description read as Marp's keyword.
- The Studio's chat is told to write a photo as a named `![…](…)` on an `image` or `bleed` slide and never `![bg]`, and the
  `image` layout's skeleton no longer says "bg image".

- **Every palette's `--border` is re-curated to clear 3:1 against both the canvas and the card fill.** A card boundary now reads as a boundary on all 32 themes in both color schemes, where 50 of 64 palette-modes previously shipped an edge no contrast meter could find — `indaco` was the worst at 1.11:1. Cards, table rules, kanban lanes, math and media frames, code panels and chart hairlines all pick this up: `--border` has 150 read sites across 52 files, so the change is visible on essentially every deck. Values move in-hue (lightness only), so each palette keeps its own temperature. `onyx` and the five a11y palettes that inherit it are unchanged — their deliberate heavy rule already cleared at 17-21:1.
- **New gate:** `test/unit/palette/surface-boundary-contrast.test.js` holds `--border` against `--bg` and `--bg-alt` on every theme in both schemes, so the boundary cannot silently dissolve again. It is derived from the filesystem and floored at 30 themes, so a new palette is covered the day it lands.

- Design note `2026-10-17-bridge-spec-and-plugin-format`: proposes a public bridge contract with two entry points (from source, from a rendered slide), a required declaration that generalizes the Marp fidelity ledger, a four-tier conformance harness, Calco as the second bridge, and a simpler plugin manifest. Includes a measured harness sketch over six example decks. Nothing is built.

- **Changed: a heatmap's callouts and band key sit where they leave the grid largest.**
  The engine lays the heatmap out with the notes beside or under the grid and the key beside or under
  it, and keeps the layout that leaves the most grid at the slide's shape: 16:9 usually keeps both beside
  the grid, 1:1 and 4:5 usually set the key (and sometimes the notes) under it. A layout that would drop
  a note never beats one that draws it. Square heatmaps with a key, and any heatmap with callouts
  where another layout keeps over 10% more of the grid, render differently; a heatmap with no callouts
  and no key, and a keyed one at 16:9, 4:3 or portrait without callouts, are unchanged. (`lib/plugins/callout/callout.docs.md`,
  `engineering/decisions/2026-10-20-callout-placement.md` § 5.)

- **Changed: callouts have a plugin of their own, `callout`, and the `legend` plugin is the key.**
  Write a note pinned to a mark as `` `@callout{{Onboarding change, row="Feb 2026", col=M2}}` ``,
  and switch callouts off with `callout: off` in the front matter, `no-callout` on one slide
  (`with-callout` turns a slide back on), or `--disable-plugin callout`. A `@legend{…}` span that pins
  a mark still draws a callout, and `lint:deck` notes the old spelling (rule `callout-spelling`,
  info). Callouts hide while keeping their detail in the speaker note.
  (`lib/plugins/callout/callout.docs.md`, `engineering/decisions/2026-10-20-callout-placement.md`.)

- **`engineering/capabilities.md` is now routed for `grep`, not for a top-to-bottom read.**
  HARD RULE #15 sends every "am I about to reinvent this?" question to that catalog, and it had
  grown past the size where reading it whole pays — so its preamble, `CLAUDE.md`'s routing row
  and `AGENTS.md` all now say to grep it and open the tool the row names. No row cap gets the
  file under the 10k read-whole budget (a 30-token cap does, by truncating 121 of 320 rows
  against a median of 27 — a list of names, not an index), so the access mode is the fix.
- **`ROW_CAP` (`tools/build-capabilities.js`) is a ratchet pinned at the widest live row**,
  failing both `capabilities:build` and `capabilities:check`. It stops a row growing past the
  worst that exists; it does not ask anyone to delete anything.
- **This shipped first as a TRIM and was reverted, which is the useful part.** Eleven rows were
  cut into a 600-character cap, validated by ten probe queries that all came back identical.
  A word-set diff then found **~130 distinct words had stopped matching anywhere in the file** —
  among them `permission`, `wink-nlp`, `cascade`, `retired` and `classifier`. `grep -i permission`
  had returned the measured finding that `--allowed-tools Read` overrides a sandbox's
  working-directory refusal: a reinvention hazard, which is exactly what #15 exists to prevent.
  The eleven rows are restored verbatim and the word-set diff against `main` is now zero. Lowering
  the ratchet needs a per-row recall check, not a probe list.
- **Fixed: a tool whose header begins with an `import` rendered that import as its description.**
  `tools/diagram-oracle.mjs`'s row read `import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';`
  instead of naming the byte oracle it is. A row that describes nothing is invisible to every grep
  but one carrying its own filename — harmless under a read-whole index, a hole under grep-first.

- **Carbone's charts and diagrams now read as distinct colors, on both faces.** Its
  categorical cycles used to step around the hue wheel in order (green, emerald, cyan,
  blue…), so the first three series of any chart read as three greens and a flowchart as
  mint on mint. The same hues now run most-distinct-first — green, blue, orange, violet,
  cyan, magenta… — the way `indaco` and `cuoio` alternate. The closest adjacent pair rises
  from 0.056 to 0.196 OKLab on the diagram marks and from 0.094 to 0.198 on the chart
  cycle. This moves the dark face too: the slot order changed, not the pigments, so the
  earlier note that carbone-dark's values are byte-identical to the pre-split palette
  holds for its surfaces and ink only.
- Carbone's light-face diagram fills moved from near-white (OKLCH L 0.97, invisible on the
  canvas) to a visible wash of each hue (L 0.89), and its light chart colors deepened from
  the 3:1 floor to 4.6:1 so they read as the pigment rather than a pastel.
- Carbone's chart `warn` and `fail` are now amber and signal red, where they were orange
  beside coral. Their worst-case separation across normal vision and the three simulated
  color-vision deficiencies rises from 0.026 to 0.075 (light) and 0.055 to 0.103 (dark).
- `npm run scorecard` moves carbone from 69.6 (D) to 84.8 (B), level with `indaco` (85.2).
- **Carbone's light face is graphite now, not indaco's blue slate.** Its paper, cards and
  ink sat at OKLCH hue 248–252 beside indaco's 256–261, so carbone light read as indaco
  with a green accent. Every lightness is held and the chroma drops to 15% (paper C
  0.0068 → 0.0013), so text contrast moves by under 0.05 and the lime is the only color
  on the slide.
- **Eight themes' dark-mode diagram boxes are jewel tones now, not raw primaries.** The
  dark `--cat-N-fill` arms of ardesia, atelier, brina, burgundy, crepuscolo, laguna,
  magnolia and mustard reached OKLCH chroma 0.215–0.256 (electric blue `#0d0dc9`, hot
  violet `#6b0dc9`), where indaco and cuoio cap at 0.150. Each is now held at 0.16 with
  its lightness and hue kept. Laguna's indigo slot also moves back to its own family's
  hue (295°), because at 270° only glare had separated it from the blue beside it.
- **Four themes no longer put near-twin colors side by side.** Ardesia (slots 5↔7),
  burgundy (5↔6), crepuscolo and laguna (3↔4) each swap one slot, so the first six
  categories of a chart or diagram stay distinct in both faces. The adjacency ratchet's
  below-floor count falls from 59 to 45, and the 45 left are the gray-by-design wash
  tier of the achromatic palettes (a11y, onyx, concrete), whose categories ride textures.
- **The palette picker now features three themes: indaco, cuoio and onyx.** The other
  eleven move to "More themes", led by carbone; nothing is removed, and every theme
  stays usable by name. The featured three scored highest in a fourteen-theme
  evaluation (onyx 89, cuoio 84, indaco 81 of 100) and cover cool, warm and black-and-white.

- `banner-tag` is now the `band` card-tag placement under its older name. It keeps working on `decision` and `compare-prose`, and now draws the same full-width strip on every tagged layout; the card keeps its own padding and reserves the band's height above the body, so a banner slide can move by a pixel or two. `lint:deck` suggests `tag-band` (`tag-alias`, advisory only).
- The list-steps `capsule` pill is now the card tag at the `inline` placement, centered: its padding follows the tag's size and venue, every pill on a slide takes one size, and the `tag:` words restyle it. It also moves from the pale `--cat-N-fill` tier to the saturated `--cat-N-mark` tier with `--cat-on-mark` ink, like every other categorical card tag. In light mode the pills get stronger; in dark mode, where the mark tier is the light one, they turn pale with dark ink, matching `decision`'s tags.

- Card tags share one recipe. The numbered corner tags on `cards-grid` and `cards-stack`, the slot-label tags and `banner-tag` bands on `compare-prose` and `decision`, the `split-compare` verdict, and the list-steps `STEP 01` label now draw from `lib/base/base.card-tag.css`. What you will see:
  - Tag padding follows the tag's own text, so a tag keeps its proportions at every `venue:` and on square, tall and strip decks. At `venue: hall` the gap between a corner tag and the card body grows from about 3px to 24px. Numbered and labeled cards reserve a little more space above the body (about 7px at 16:9, more on portrait, where the tag used to be cramped).
  - A corner label that wraps to two lines clears the card body at the default size. A longer label, or a two-line label at a large venue, can still reach it; the equal-height pass planned next sizes the space to the real tag.
  - One letter-spacing (0.08em) for every tag; the verdict and the `STEP` label were 0.12em.
  - `sketch` roughens every tag, including the `split-compare` verdict, which it used to miss.
  - `compare-prose decision` tags wear the accent pair (`--on-accent` ink). They had picked up the categorical ink meant for `decision`.

- **Sketch `list principles` row rules no longer read as the heading rule.** Under `class: sketch` the hand-drawn row rules now use the same lighter ink (55%) and the same inset to the text column as the plain rule, so the full-strength masthead rule stays the one line that marks the page.
- **The `cards:` register now reaches the rest of the card catalog.** `decision`, `pricing`, `statute-stack`, `split-compare`, `team-profile`, `matrix-2x2`, `q-and-a grid`, the default (column) `cards-stack`, `split-panel`, `regulatory-update`, `inventory cards` and `citation-card` all follow `cards: center | top | spread | stretch` and `_class: cards-*`. **Changed default:** at wide, the default `cards-stack`, `decision`, `pricing` and `statute-stack` now size their cards to their text and center them, as `cards-grid` already did — `cards: stretch` (deck-wide) or `_class: cards-stretch` (one slide) restores the old fill exactly — and `regulatory-update` centers the rows it used to pack at the top (`cards: top` restores that). `matrix-2x2`, `q-and-a grid` and `split-compare` keep their filled layouts by default, and `split-panel` keeps its spread evidence list and its filled `proof` grid.
- A component manifest's `cards` field takes a new `byClass` override for variants that are different shapes (`split-panel`: `"byClass": { "proof": "stretch" }`).
- **Changed:** `inventory cards` spaces its tiles with the same card gutter as the other card grids (`--sp-md`, 24px at 1280 wide) instead of 8px; a grid with a pull-quote below it keeps the tight gutter it needs to fit.
- **Fixed:** a `banner-tag` card sized to its content (`compare-prose` since the register, and now `decision`) no longer spills its body text out under the banner.

- **Changed:** the detail reveal's lift and 3D tilt are off for a heatmap. A matrix locates a value by the intersection of two discrete labels, and both flourishes drift the tiles off the labels beside them — the open cell sat visibly off-grid, half under its column header. The active cell is still marked: its neighbors dim to 0.45 while it holds full saturation, which is emphasis in the chart's own language.

- Chart design language: what a mark's fill ENCODES — hue, ramp, presence or layered — decides HOW a finish reaches it, not whether. A ramp is scaled into the finish's band, a layered body takes a flat alpha, a presence mark gets an on level and an edge-only off. An earlier revision let the encoding decide *whether*, which left three of the four encodings with a stroke tweak and no body.
- A finish reaches a textured mark through shade and its edge, never by repainting it: on the a11y palettes the fill is the pattern that carries category when hue cannot.
