- **Breaking:** `marks:` has no `off`, and a deck that names no finish now wears `pigment`. Every `<section>` carries a finish class, including a deck with no front matter and a chart inside a pane. `chart-finish: off` (now `marks:`) reports `unknown-marks` and renders `pigment`; the per-slide `chart-finish-off` token is gone (a slide that wants the default writes `marks-pigment`). The Studio's "As designed" option is gone, and choosing Pigment removes the key.
- **Fixed:** two things the default would otherwise have shipped to every chart deck. A heatmap's top step against its empty cell kept about half its contrast under pigment (3.54:1 fell to 1.92:1 light and 3.03:1 to 1.51:1 dark on indaco); pigment now carries the member's own span. A progress bar went near-black on a dark slide under pigment, because its readout sits on the slide past the bar's end and the bar did not need the text level; it now wears the same body as any other mark.
- **Fixed:** a gantt task, milestone or key chip with no status, a state-chart tile with no status, and a progress bar with no status kept their own gradient beside flat sibling bars under a finish. They wear the neutral finish now.
- **Added:** `tools/chart-finish-reach.mjs`, a diagnostic that renders the chart gallery per theme and mode and names every mark a finish does not reach, every reached mark that keeps a gradient, and each finish's heatmap range against the unfinished paint. `--check` gates the default finish at 0.9×. Six charts (`flowchart`, `kanban`, `risk-matrix`, `slope`, `map`, `journey`) are listed as not reached yet.
- The Playground snapshot no longer keeps every finish rule on every slide: a bar slide's snapshot is 53K units, not 100K.
- **Fixed:** the ink a text-bearing mark picks (pills, status bodies, tower and hub-spoke values) switched on OKLCH lightness, which is not luminance for a saturated hue: a red body took black text at 4.31:1 where white gives 4.87:1, and a narrow band returned a near-invisible mid-grey (1.003:1 on `rgb(210 40 70)`). It switches on CIE luminance now and is never worse than 4.58:1, checked over 140,608 bodies and in Chromium 131, Firefox 142 and WebKit 26. The tower's own ink uses the same expression.
- **Fixed:** the `--player` export dropped every finish rule written `light-dark(...) !important`, because the flag landed inside the `var()` fallback and the engine discards the declaration. A finished deck showed the shipped paint under the finish's ink: tower share values read 2.45:1 on onyx against 8.33:1 in the plain HTML export. Both exports now agree on every theme.
- **Fixed:** under a finish the radar's scale ticks fell as low as 1.60:1 (they sit on the overlap of every series), and a state tile's index numeral fell from 5.95:1 to 4.31:1 on cuoio. Ticks take the heading ink, tone's polygon alpha runs 0.32 down to 0.104 (was 0.6 down to 0.24), and an unstated state tile's numeral picks its ink from its body. No text run on any chart, theme or mode is under its threshold where the unfinished paint cleared it, on all three finishes.
- **Added:** `tools/chart-finish-reach.mjs` also measures every text run (arm `RUNS`) and compares each finish with a frozen baseline in `test/fixtures/chart-finish-baseline.json`, so the reference survives a member converging its own paint.
- A runtime `<section>` nested inside a slide is content, not a slide, and is no longer stamped. A deck with a pigment heatmap keeps the theme's own cell inks, and `lint:deck` says `chart-finish-off` was retired instead of calling it unknown.
- **Changed:** under every finish, a chart mark that carries text (a gantt bar, a state or flowchart tile, a status pill, a tower share, a journey badge) wears the chart family's curated text tier, and its text is `--text-heading`: a tint on light, a deep fill on dark, at least 5.46:1 on every palette and 13:1 at the median. Pigment is solid on the marks without text (bars, wedges, dots, lines). A key follows the tier of the marks it keys.
- **Changed:** the finish now reaches flowchart nodes, risk-matrix bands, line and ep-curve strokes, radar and bubble edges, and the neutral hub-spoke and journey marks.
- **Changed:** every theme's chart colors are now curated SOLIDS: one flat color per category, status and the new neutral, with one text ink per mode (`--chart-on-solid`). Text on every solid clears 7:1 and every solid clears 3:1 against the slide, on every palette in both modes (`test/unit/palette/chart-solids.test.js`). `tools/curate-chart-solids.js` seeded the values by moving only lightness; 174 seeds changed, and ardesia's slots 3 and 4 and onyx's slot 6 were hand-tuned to keep adjacent categories apart.
- **Changed:** pigment paints every chart mark with its concept's flat solid, text on it or not, and every label on a mark reads `--chart-on-mark`. No chart grades, mixes or filters its fill any more: the shared gradient wash (`--chart-fill-top-*`, `--palette-fill-*`) is retired, the pie, quadrant, radar, gantt, state-chart, progress, timeline and key-spine gradients are flat, journey's drop-shadow filters are gone, `--chart-cat-N-body` is the solid itself, and a mark's leading accent is its own solid. Unstated marks paint the new neutral solid. The status pill is a solid with the solid ink. The flowchart key names its chart, so its status swatches follow the nodes.
- **Breaking:** the base owns the status colors, in two jobs, and every chart fill carries ONE INK. `--pass` … `--mute` stay the status as ink on the slide, unchanged. New `--pass-mark` … `--mute-mark` are the status as a fill a label sits on: DEEP in the status's own hue under white text, like a category, at 7:1 on a light slide and 4.6:1 on a dark one, so two charts on one slide never wear two text colors. Done is a quiet sage, at risk a burnt orange, blocked a crimson, info a deep cyan-blue and deferred a deep gray. A status drawn as a line or text (a slope, a waterfall step, a kanban header) paints its slide ink, `--pass` … `--mute`, the same color the status is in every other component. Every chart fill carries `--on-mark`, white, near-black only on a colorblind palette's dark face (`test/unit/palette/chart-one-ink.test.js`). The chart-only `--chart-state-*` hooks, `--chart-on-solid`, `--on-warn` and `--on-warn-vivid` are retired: a custom theme moves those values to `--pass` … `--mute` and `--on-mark`, and builds the fills and signals in the Studio's theme builder, which derives them from the theme's inks (`node tools/curate-chart-solids.js` does the same for the themes in this repository, and reads no other file).
- **Added:** `--chart-neutral-mark`, the solid for a chart mark with no category or status, and a gate (`test/unit/palette/color-ownership.test.js`) that fails when a theme leaves any base color token to the engine's fallback. The theme contract is 128 tokens (`test/unit/palette/theme-contrast.test.js` pins the count).
- **Changed:** status pills and state-chart nodes are status fills under their status's ink rather than tinted chips. Concrete's light `--mute` moves to `#31312B` so it stays apart from `--warn`.
- **Added:** `marks:` takes a second word, the intensity: `muted` (the default) or `vivid`, in either order (`marks: pigment vivid`). Muted keeps done a quiet sage and lets the exceptions carry the color; vivid makes every status rich, done an emerald. Both keep white text. A slide's `_class: marks-vivid` changes only the intensity. The editor completes the second word, and `unknown-marks` names a typo or a second word on the same axis.
- **Added:** `--pass-vivid-mark` `--warn-vivid-mark` `--fail-vivid-mark` `--info-vivid-mark`, which every theme curates. Each theme's status set is its own: the hues are its status inks held to their bands (warn a burnt orange, fail a crimson, info in the cyan band), pass and fail lean toward its accent (a leather palette's green is olive-sage, a frost palette's red a cool rose), and saturation follows its categories.
- **Changed:** pigment, the base finish, puts color on the marks and keeps the ground under them neutral. Quadrant zones are the neutral surface, a radar series is a solid line with no translucent fill (overlapping fills mixed into colors in no palette), risk bands are the status fills with a canvas seam and critical the deepest of the four, waterfall totals and the hub-spoke hub are the neutral solid, a roadmap row header is the neutral ground, and a journey stage's top rule no longer carries a category color.
- **Changed:** every theme's chart categories are its brand colors again, as deep fills under white text: 7:1 on a light slide, and on a dark slide the lightest tone of each hue that white still clears at 4.6:1, so it stands off the slide. Cuoio's olive slot is a deep plum; onyx's olive moves to slot 5 so two grays are never neighbors. `--chart-catN-ink` is regenerated to match.
- **Changed:** a map's data picks its color. Numbers fill as one hue, low to high, and under `pigment` the top value now reaches the theme's full category color (it stopped at 64% and read as `tone`); text labels, or names with no value, fill each region with its category solid, with no class needed. `map highlight` still forces categories and is only needed for labels that are numbers; `map-highlight-implied` notes when it is redundant. Category regions are now the flat solid, not an 82% mix, and a category is its LABEL: every region with the same label wears the same color, and a list of bare names is one set in one color.

- **Changed:** charts that picked status or category colors their own way now read the shared ones. A roadmap's shipped, in-flight and missed discs are the status fills with a white glyph; a journey's mood scale is one hue in five steps (it mixed three category colors); every risk band is a status fill; quadrant dots are larger (radius 6, from 4.5) so their color shows; a matrix-grid's empty cell has a firmer outline. In print the status fills keep the one ink: dark grays under white text that darken with severity, and the two exceptions wear a mid-gray ring.
- **Added:** a status carries its SHAPE as well as its color. Every status that names a state draws its mark: a check for done, a dash for at risk, a cross for blocked, a slash for deferred (`lib/core/status-marks.js`, the `--mark-*-bold` paths). Gantt bars, hub-spoke discs, status pills, state-chart tiles and the critical risk cells carry it (a progress row's mark is its status pill, so the bar stays pure length); live, pilot and decision carry none.
- **Added:** the two exceptions wear a SIGNAL ring. An at-risk or blocked bar, pill, tile or disc is ringed in amber or coral-red (`--warn-signal-mark`, `--fail-signal-mark`, which every theme curates), in every finish; nothing else rings. The ring is an outline that takes no space: 1.3 hairlines, drawn inside the shape, so it never grows a mark or covers an arrowhead. It sits at the opposite lightness to its fill and clears 3:1 against the fill on a light slide and against the slide on a dark one. A risk matrix rings its whole critical band once; a hub-spoke alarm halo, which stands apart from its disc, wears the status edge.
- **Changed:** a risk matrix's markers are light discs with a heading-ink number and rim, so they read on the deep bands, and a progress bar is pure length from zero: its number sits just past its end on the slide, in a gutter the track reserves so a full bar's number never meets the status pill, with no plate and no threshold.
- Every component that shows a status now paints it the way charts do. A status mark (a checklist or verdict disc, a table `state-cells` disc, an inline `` `[x]` `` mark, a roadmap disc, a kpi status pill, a policy-recommendation verdict badge, a regulatory-update tier) is the deck's status fill under the one ink, with its drawn mark, a hairline rim in the status ink, and the signal ring on at risk and blocked. A rail or a status word is the slide ink (`--pass` …), and a status row or cell ground is the theme's `--pass-bg` / `--warn-bg` / `--fail-bg`, with no component-private tints. `marks: … vivid` now sets the status fills for the whole slide, not only its charts. The kpi status pill leads with its mark (check or dash) so it stays readable without color. The default disc now has a hairline rim in the status ink (`checks-knockout` is now the same as the default, and `checks-ringed` keeps a heavier rim); `checks-outline` and `checks-tonal` draw their ring and mark in the status ink, and at risk and blocked wear the signal ring there too (`engineering/decisions/2026-10-24-status-is-one-system.md`).
- **Fixed:** a progress list is one grid: every row's bar shares one lane, so bars compare on one scale on square, tall and strip slides too, and the status-pill column fits its widest pill (at `venue: hall` a pill outgrew its fixed column and overprinted the readout). A value over 100% stops at the end of its lane and still prints what was written; 0% draws no bar.
- **Fixed:** a `radar quadrant` quarter name and a `radar small-multiples` caption are text, so they take the category's text ink (`--chart-cat-N-ink`) and no longer the deep mark fill. Under the default finish they had fallen under AA on 15 palettes (worst 3.14:1, onyx dark), and on 10 of those before this change; all 33 palettes now pass.
- **Fixed:** under etch and tone an at-risk or blocked mark's signal ring was thinner than a done mark's outline (1.3px against 2-3px on gantt bars, status pills, state tiles, progress bars and key swatches), so on a dark slide the settled status was the loudest outline. The ring now scales with the finish's edge, 1.3 times it in every finish, and the exception is the heaviest line again.
- **Fixed:** an at-risk or blocked gantt milestone, and the gantt key's at-risk and blocked swatches, now wear the signal ring the bars do; they drew none. Under etch a risk matrix's critical band ring scales with its 2px cell edges.
- **Fixed:** a progress chart in a side pane kept its columns on each row, which made every row its own grid with no column gap: the label touched its bar and the bar ran under its status pill (up to 18px). The pane now sets the columns on the list, as a full slide does, and the gaps are 24px.
- **Fixed:** under etch and tone the office export kept status pills, progress bars and flowchart key swatches as pictures, not editable shapes: their wash was clipped inside a transparent border under an inset ring, which Calco cannot lift. They now have no border under those finishes (the padding keeps every box exactly where it was, measured), so the chart gallery has 29 refusals in every finish (main: 42) and the chart-finish demo none. The Calco budget now also runs that demo under etch and tone.
- **Changed:** `chart-finish:` is renamed `marks:`, and its slide classes `chart-finish-*` are now `marks-*` (`marks-tone`, `marks-vivid`), because the register sets every mark on the slide (a checklist disc, a kpi pill), not only charts. The old key and classes still render, `marks:` wins when a deck sets both, and `lint:deck` names the new spelling (`marks-renamed`, info). The Studio reads a deck on the old key and moves it to `marks:` when you pick. The demo deck is now `examples/marks.md`.

- Under `tone`, a waterfall's up and down bars and a risk matrix's four bands keep their status hue (pass, warn, fail) instead of one blue; this reverses #2887's one-hue rule for direction and severity, which the blind scorers marked down. Band strengths are unchanged.
- Under `tone`, a pie on a dark slide takes a wider ladder of its hue's ink, so neighboring wedges (and their key swatches) read apart (adjacent OKLab gaps 0.032 to 0.047 become 0.060 to 0.074 on indaco), and a matrix's reachable cell takes the one ink as its edge.
- Under `etch`, a waterfall's Plan and Actual columns take the status bars' wash and edge weight instead of a deeper wash and a hairline, and a choropleth map on a dark slide starts higher, so a valued region stands off the land (weakest region 0.051 to 0.124 OKLab from the land on indaco).
- Chart narration keeps the underscores in a name (`snake_case` in a card, task or label) instead of stripping every `_`, so a card named with code binds to its drawn part; `_emphasis_` markers still go.

- `npm run check:chart-fit` now also renders the chart fixture at the `strip` family (`size: mobile`, 1080x2340), so a later tall/strip edit to a chart no longer needs a by-hand check. It runs in the nightly integration tier only: +26s per run, green on the first run across 57 chart slides.

- **Breaking (visual):** `funnel` and `timeline-list` now draw every mark in **one hue** instead of cycling six. A funnel's stage label sits beside its own band and a timeline dot has its title directly under it, so hue had no job to do — nothing to bind a mark to a name (no legend rail, no leader line) and nothing to separate (the marks do not touch). The single hue is slot 1, the family's single-series slot, which both components already declared as their default. Decks using either member re-render with a flat palette; no authoring change is needed.
- A funnel's a11y and print bands take **one texture** (`latt-a11y-chart-tex-1`) to match, so grayscale no longer claims six categories where color says one.

- **Breaking: a chart component's `kernel` block now requires a `marks` array.**
  Every chart member declares its data marks and the three facts a chart finish
  is decided by — how the mark takes paint (`fill` / `bg` / `none`), what its
  body encodes (`hue` / `ramp` / `presence` / `layered` / `none`), and whether it
  carries text. **An existing chart folder without `marks` now fails to load**,
  which includes the folder-drop path: dropping `lib/components/chart/<name>/`
  with a `kernel` block is still all it takes to register a chart, but the block
  needs the new key. Contract and vocabulary:
  `lib/components/manifest.schema.json`; the reasoning is in
  `engineering/decisions/2026-09-07-chart-design-language/mark-declaration.md`.
- **Added: two checks behind the declarations.** `checkChartMarks` (via
  `npm run build:check`) fails on a declared class nothing under `lib/` writes
  and on a `data-paint` / `data-encodes` value the manifest does not know;
  `node tools/chart-language-census.js --check` re-measures `bears` off a real
  render and reports a painted mark that no manifest declares. The second is an
  on-demand command, not a CI gate.
- **Fixed: a scatter bubble and its size-key ring now stamp
  `data-encodes="layered"`, not `"hue"`.** Both are deliberately translucent so
  overlapping marks deepen where they cross; stamping the opaque dot's encoding
  would have told a finish it could hand a translucent mark a gradient. The ring
  is the bubble's own legend, so the two disagreeing was the drift this contract
  exists to stop.

- Every chart with a row schema now reads a row's `{…}` record through the shared row reader, in the chart and in the narrator: `bar`, `line`, `slope`, `stacked-bar`, `piechart`, `funnel`, `waterfall`, `scatter`, `map`, `word-cloud`, `radar`, `quadrant`, `heatmap` and `matrix-grid` join `bullet` and `progress`. Nothing you can see changes: 812 chart slides in the repo corpus, in the old spellings and rewritten as records, render, narrate and lint byte-identically to before.

- Chart authoring: the decision note records that a `{…}` record in a nested list row (bar, line, stacked-bar, slope, radar) narrows at phase 4; no deck in the repo writes one, and nothing changes in rendering today.

- **Seven chart pane budgets are measured now, and scatter's is tighter.** `calibrate-capacity
  --pane` builds bar, bullet, funnel, piechart, scatter, waterfall, line, stacked-bar, slope,
  radar, heatmap and map panes, and a step fails when its text falls under the type floor or the
  chart stops painting a label, as well as when it clips. bar, piechart, scatter, line, heatmap,
  map and radar turned `measured`. A scatter pane now warns past 8 points side by side (was 12)
  and 10 stacked (was 12): the ninth and eleventh points lose their labels.

- Chart design language: a directly-labelled mark may own a hue *because* it is labelled, not despite it — the label is what keeps a per-mark palette from becoming confetti. The test is G0 (does the mark carry its own name, or share a label axis with its siblings?), the cap is G1 (past six singulars, collapse to one group rather than cycling), and RULE G settles a figure that has two categorical systems competing for one palette.

- The heatmap places its callouts and key by the slide's real shape, not by its orientation name. At 4:3 a keyed heatmap keeps its key under the grid (the grid grows to 1.46 times its old area on the demo deck), and at 4:5 three callouts sit beside the grid again; 16:9 decks do not change.
- Sections of a deck that is not 16:9 carry a `data-aspect` attribute (for example `1.33`). A chart transform reads it as `ctx.aspect`; `transformChartSection` takes it as a sixth argument.

- **Every chart mark that draws an OUTLINE now draws it at one physical weight.**
  Each member had tuned its own `stroke-width` inside its own SVG viewBox, and
  those viewBoxes span 4.3× — so the family's declared marks painted at **21
  different physical weights**, from a 0.42px map border to a 2.9px pie wedge, a
  6.9× spread. Now **21 mark classes sit at exactly 1px** through one token,
  `--chart-edge`.
- **It is not one weight overall, and the remainder is deliberate.** Eight
  distinct weights remain over a 2.2× spread: the 1px outlines, one sanctioned
  `--chart-edge-strong` doubling on `state-chart`'s start and terminal nodes, and
  **seven knockouts** — `funnel-band`, `line-dot`, `quadrant-dot`,
  `quadrant-trail-after`, `radar-dot`, `scatter-dot`, `sbar-seg` — which stroke in
  `var(--bg)` to hold two touching marks apart. A knockout's width follows what it
  separates, not the family's outline weight; folding them in took quadrant's
  separator from 2.23px to 1.00px.
- The mechanism is `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` paired with the family's
  existing resolution-stable `--chart-hairline`, so the weight is identical
  across members **and** still grows with the container above HD (#180 stands).
  Export DPI is a separate transform and is unaffected.
- **The export used to lose both properties.** `flattenSvgStyles` — the path
  behind every PDF, PPTX, image-set and standalone-SVG export — carried no
  `vector-effect`, and omitted `stroke-width` whenever it equalled the CSS initial
  of `1px`, which is exactly what `--chart-edge` resolves to at HD. A pinned 1px
  edge therefore arrived in the exported file with neither, and fell back to one
  viewBox USER unit: measured by driving both versions of the flattener over the
  same live SVGs, a map edge came back at 0.84px and a scatter BUBBLE at 2.46px.
  (Not the scatter dot — that is a knockout with an explicit 0.9, which is not the
  initial and was never dropped.) A stroked element now never drops either. The
  cost is **+2.7% to +8.2% bytes per exported SVG**, and on the Mermaid path,
  where nothing carries `non-scaling-stroke`, those declarations are all no-ops.
- `chart-mark-edge-census.test.js` ties the shared rule to the marks each manifest
  declares `paint: "fill"`, so a new member joins by declaring its marks. Three
  ways around it are closed: a declared mark carrying `paint-order` (the pie
  wedge) is no longer exempt, a width written as a presentation attribute in a
  transform is now caught, and a `:hover` rule no longer qualifies a mark as a
  knockout. Each arm is mutation-proved.
- `tools/chart-structure-census.js` reports the family's widths, radii and gaps in
  **physical pixels** and `--check`s that every outline is pinned. Re-derive any
  number above with it.

- On a page read on a phone (portrait, square, story, mobile), chart text prints at one size per role in every chart kind. Key entries are 13pt on the phone; names on the drawing, values, area names and notes are 12pt; axis names, ticks, axis titles, status words and marker numerals are 11pt; and items in a roadmap, kanban or journey read at the deck's body size. Before, ticks and category names printed at 5 to 7pt. Inside the chart the text is in one face (the body face, with tabular figures). Landscape slides and charts in panes are unchanged.
- On those pages a word cloud sizes its words in five steps from 11pt to 40pt, scaled up together until the cloud fills its box, keeps its display face, and shows at most 25 words, reporting the rest. Radar small multiples run two to a row, and a risk-matrix cell keeps its markers at full size.
- On those pages a chart's layout follows its larger text: the drawing takes the shape of its box, axis titles and gutters grow with their labels, and a crowded category axis staggers its names over two rows instead of dropping or cutting them (waterfall, line, risk-matrix). A funnel's name and value columns widen, a quadrant places its names at the size they print, and a risk matrix's grid fills its box.
- On those pages bar, quadrant, risk-matrix, line, scatter, ep-curve, bullet, funnel, hub-spoke, piechart, tower, radar, map, stacked-bar, heatmap, histogram, waterfall and gantt are laid out by one shared chart form kernel: each draws once on a canvas the shape of its box, and its plot, axes, key and notes each take the room their text needs, measured with the theme's own glyph widths. A two-line category name sets whole, a row chart's names never shorten, and a grouped key sits under or beside the plot, whichever leaves it larger.
- A quadrant whose names cannot sit clear of their dots numbers its dots and lists the names in a key; a risk matrix's register runs in one to three columns or as a running line, and a crowded cell's markers shrink to the smallest disc that holds their 11pt numbers. Authored notes on these charts print at 12pt.
- On those pages a pie or hub-spoke at `claim-hero` or `claim-bleed` fills its stage. Before, a landscape height held it to 410px on a 1080px-wide page and printed its key at 3.5pt; a hero pie now prints its key at 13pt.
- On those pages an ep-curve's point values print at the value role, 12pt, and a column bar chart's axis ticks at the tick role, 11pt; they printed at 7pt and 6.4pt.
- On those pages a chart under several paragraphs, a quote or a table keeps its text size: the chart's box now allows for every block above it, not only the first paragraph.
- On those pages a radar's rim labels print at 11pt and its plot takes the width they leave; ring figures too close for 11pt print on every other ring. Small multiples draw as one grid in the column count that prints them largest, and a hero or bleed radar fills its stage.
- On those pages a map's key prints at 13pt under or beside the basemap, which takes the room the key leaves; on a 4:5 or square page it printed at 5.5 to 8.5pt.
- On those pages a chart under a long title keeps its text size: the chart's box now counts the title's real lines (a 68-character title sets on four lines on a phone page, not three).
- On those pages a deck with `venue:` keeps its chart text at its role sizes: the chart's box now allows for the larger title, eyebrow and captions the venue sets. At `venue: hall` a phone page's chart printed at 9 to 10pt, and one at 1.3pt.
- A chart these sizes cannot hold on one page at 11pt is drawn whole and scaled to its box, so no name is lost or printed over another.
- Every docs page that loads the engine downloads about 220KB less script (gzipped): the preview runtime no longer carries the chart kernels, which a preview never ran, because the engine has already drawn its charts. A map's own code is 7KB smaller.
- On those pages a gantt sets every task name whole at 12pt: inside its bar, after it, or on its own line above the bar. Its lane names sit above their bars and its status key wraps onto a second row when it needs one. At 12pt inside the old bars, names were cut to `Pilot…` and printed across bar edges.
- On those pages a state chart's tiles grow with their names, so a step number no longer prints on a name, and an edge label keeps its clearance from the lines around it.
- A state or flowchart name that breaks after a hyphen (`Counter-signature`) is now painted on the same lines the layout measured. It used to be painted on one line, wider than its tile.
- On a narrow slide (every phone, story, 4:5 and square page) a kanban board stacks its lanes full width, and every card takes the same shape: its title, then its label and status on the row under it. A `kanban tinted` lane no longer runs past the page's right edge, and a `compact` deck's card titles no longer touch the lane's edge bar. Its card titles, labels, status pills and size codes print at 11pt or more (a square page printed titles at 9pt).
- On a portrait, story or mobile page a roadmap's phase cards stack full width at their natural height, each workstream on its own full-width row; before, rows sat two across in cards stretched to fill the page.
- A journey's actor dots on a phone page grow to hold their initials. The type ladder set the initial at 11pt inside a dot sized for the old 7pt letter, and the letter spilled past the dot's edge.
- On a square page a journey stacks its stages, one per page, as it does on a phone page. The side-by-side board printed its actor dots over its task names at the 11pt text size and cut off its last stage at the page's right edge.
- On a phone or square page a kanban, roadmap or journey that fits the page stays on one page. Before, every one split into a page per lane, phase or stage, even a small board that fit: the kanban gallery at mobile was 41 pages and is now 13. One that does not fit still splits a lane, phase or stage a page.
- On a phone page a word cloud whose words do not all fit at 11pt is drawn a little smaller instead of leaving words out: the word-cloud gallery at square had dropped 18 words.
- On a phone page a two-column slope chart draws as a dumbbell (one row per name, a bar between its two values) when the slopegraph would be too narrow to read: the eight-supplier stress test printed its values over each other at square. A slope chart's names set whole on a phone page: the dumbbell's name column grows to fit them, and a chart that still cannot hold them at 11pt is drawn a little smaller. "Kestrel Group" and "Meridian Partners" printed as "Kestrel…" and "Meridian…".
- A progress chart and a timeline fit their phone pages again at the larger text size: tighter lines on a progress label and its status pill, and on a timeline entry. A square page sets a timeline top to bottom, as a phone page does, where its last entry ran off the right edge.
- On a phone or square page a flowchart's or state chart's notes print as a numbered list under the drawing at 12pt, and each note's numbered marker sits beside its shape. Inside the drawing they shrank with it to 3 to 5pt.
- On a phone or square page a timeline too tall for the page at 11pt is drawn a little smaller and stays whole. Its last entry used to run off the page.
- On a phone page, chart text is measured in the face it paints in: Inter under the `ledger`, `poster` and `festival` type sets, and the hand under the sketch finish, which had set a pie key's name under its value.
- On a phone page, a chart whose name is wider than its box (one long word, a CJK name with no spaces) is drawn whole and scaled (over capacity), where it fell back to a drawing that cut the name mid-word.
- On a phone page, a `###` heading, a second caption, and a CJK or emoji title come off the chart's box, so the chart's text keeps its size, and a no-break space no longer breaks a key name.

- The six check marks (check, dash, x, slash, question mark and the chart dot) are now drawn from Tabler Icons, the same pinned set the icons plugin uses, instead of hand-made SVG, in HTML slides, SVG charts and PowerPoint exports alike. Every check style looks the same; the one visible change is a slightly steeper slash on `[/]`, and the bold slash on SVG charts now matches the HTML one's weight.
- Every check is now the same size, height and gap as its siblings, in every style and container: the open `[ ]` and unknown `[?]` rings no longer paint larger than the solid answers, `checks-ringed` checks no longer crowd their pill's edge, and `checks-bold` discs sit centered in running text. `@check{…}` takes a pill's size, `sm`, `md` or `lg` (`@check{yes, label=Residency, lg}`), and a check pill matches an icon pill of the same size. The open and unknown rings read slightly heavier than before, and a solid disc in the default style is about 2.6px smaller on a 1280-wide slide, its rim now inside the same footprint as every other answer.

- Checks in a CLI or Studio PDF are drawn as vector paths (the disc, its rings and its mark), so they stay crisp at any zoom and in print. They used to be part of the slide's 96 ppi background photo. A pill's outline around a check is now a vector too, and a stroked chart line keeps its round corners.
- A pill whose words include an emoji no longer prints empty in a CLI or Studio PDF.

- **Breaking:** verdict-grid and pricing no longer draw a `.badge` span. A criterion is a check inside a pill (`.lat-pill > .lat-pill-lead > .lat-state`) and a pricing feature a check then its words (`li > .lat-state`), so CSS that targets `.badge` there matches nothing. Restyle the check with the `checks-*` modifiers, or target `.lat-state`.
- **Breaking:** three modules moved into the checks plugin, and their old paths are gone: `lib/core/state-marks.js` is `lib/plugins/checks/shared/registry.js`, `lib/core/check-compose.js` is `lib/plugins/checks/shared/compose.js`, and `lib/core/leading-marker.js` (where `readLeadingMarker` lives) is `lib/plugins/checks/shared/leading.js`. `STATE_WORDS` is gone from `lib/core/segno-slots.js`, with the core `state` slot it spelled.
- The six check answers (`[x] [-] [!] [?] [ ] [/]`) now live in one registry table, `CHECKS` in `lib/plugins/checks/shared/registry.js`; the stylesheet, the layout word maps and the Studio's marker picker are pinned to it by test. No rendered output changes.
- A pill can hold content a component hands it: `pillHtml` / `pillElement` take an optional `lead`, drawn before the label with a `0.35em` gap, and `pillHtmlFrom` / `pillElementFrom` build a pill from parts. Narration reads a check that leads a pill in the layout's own words ("Residency: yes"), as it reads a badge.
- verdict-grid's criteria are now a check inside a pill, and pricing's features a check then the label on one row, composed by one kernel on both render paths; a long pricing feature wraps under its own text.
- **obligation-matrix `pills` now shows words:** each marker cell is a pill with its check and the key's word (Applies, Partial, Exempt…), and a label set renames the pills, the key and the narration together. Under `heat`, every row's cells keep their burden ground.
- Narration speaks an obligation-matrix label set's words, not the defaults, and a key entry says its word once.
- **New: the checks plugin and `@check{…}`.** The six answers are now owned by an embedded plugin, `checks`. The brackets stay as shortcuts; the full form names the answer, `` `@check{pass}` ``, by id (`pass warn fail unknown todo skip`) or spoken word (`yes partly no open na`), and with a label draws the check and its words as one pill: `` `@check{yes, label=Residency}` ``. The Studio autocompletes the six answers and `label=`; lint explains an answer it does not know, and counts a full-form criterion's words like its shortcut's.
- The ten chart statuses join the check registry as its second set, so a status and a check that share a drawing are held to it by test. No chart renders differently.
- The website's plugin pages gain Checks, and six catalog facts that a comma had silently cut short now read in full (for example "Loaded: Always. Part of every deck, so it has no off switch").
- `lint:deck` warns (`check-label-code`) when a `verdict-grid` or `pricing` criterion that starts with a check holds inline code: the label beside the check is plain text, so `` [x] `@check{fail}` text `` would show "@check{fail} text".
- A check inside a pill (a verdict-grid criterion, an obligation-matrix `pills` cell, a labelled `@check{…}`) is drawn at 0.85 of its inline size and centered in the capsule, so it carries the same weight as an icon in a pill. Checks outside a pill keep their size.

- **Changed: the pre-push hook no longer runs the full unit suite.** `npm test`
  took 390s on every push in the cloud sandbox, and CI's `unit` job runs the same
  suite on every PR and again in the merge queue, so it could not stop a
  regression that CI would miss.
- **Changed: CI's `unit` job now runs on every PR, not only PRs that touch code.**
  Unit tests also read prose and config (the US-English audit walks every `.md`),
  so a prose-only PR used to meet them first in the merge queue, where a failure
  ejects the PR. Pre-commit still runs the tests affected by each
  commit. Run `npm test` yourself before calling work done.

- **CI:** `studio-smoke` no longer records a trace and a video for each of its 155 tests (`E2E_RECORD=off`, set only on that job). Recording was about a third of the job's time, and the job was hitting its 20-minute cap. The nightly e2e suite and local runs still record everything.
- **CI:** the docs Vitest suite moved out of `docs-build` into a new required job, `docs-test`, that runs beside it, and runs on 4 workers instead of 3 (387 s to 313 s on 4 cores, same 639 files passing). It was docs-build's longest step. The `ci` gate requires `docs-test` as it does `docs-build`.
- **CI:** `docs-build` and `studio-smoke` no longer run a separate root build: their `npm ci` already builds the built-not-committed artifacts (the root `prepare` script), so the step built them twice. The route-budget base build runs `npm run build:uncommitted` instead of the full build. The committed artifacts are already in the checkout, and `lint` checks them against their generators.
- **CI:** the docs horizontal-overflow guard (`npm run check:overflow`) checks its four widths at once instead of one after another: the same 40 states and the same pauses, 106 s to 62 s.

- The CLI export (PDF, PNG, HTML and `--player`) now ships the engine's flat stylesheet, the same one the Studio's Webpage player ships, instead of inlining `lattice.css` and the palette unpacked. A token that derives from another now follows each slide's own overrides, so a print slide's page number takes the print ink. Over every committed deck, that page number (`print-mode`, `finish-canvas-print-face`) is the only thing that renders differently.
- **Breaking:** in a CLI export, a deck's bare `section { --token: … }` override (front-matter `style:` or an in-body `<style>`) no longer beats a token the palette declares at `:root`, which is how Marp and every other Lattice host already behave. Write the override at `:root` (`:root { --accent: … }`), which keeps working, or on a class (`section.brand`).
- A `<section>` an author nests inside a slide is no longer styled as a slide in the CLI export. It used to pick up slide padding and chrome.
- An installed theme package that omits `@import 'lattice'` still renders on the layout sheet.
- The exported player's CSS prune now reads one-colon `:before`/`:after` (KaTeX's, and every rule in the Studio's minified sheet) as pseudo-elements, so it keeps those rules instead of dropping them or giving up on the prune.
- `tools/palette-sweep.js` re-themes a rendered export by swapping the whole deck sheet between `/* lattice:sheet-start size=… theme=… */` and `/* lattice:sheet-end */`, composed by the builder the CLI itself uses (`lib/export/cli-deck-sheet.js`), and refuses a render whose sheet that builder does not reproduce. The `/* lattice:palette-end */` sentinel is gone.
- The engine's comment stripper no longer reads a `/*` inside a CSS string as a comment. A custom layout sheet carrying `content: "/*"` lost every rule after it.

- **Changed: the command is `lattice` everywhere, and `lattice --help` fits one screen.**
  `--version` prints `lattice 1.0.0`, and the help, usage and examples show `lattice deck.md
  deck.pdf` rather than `node lattice-emulator.js deck.md deck.pdf`: the CLI stopped emulating
  Marp long ago, and its name had not caught up. `lattice --help` now shows the output formats
  and the options most decks need; `lattice --help all` (or `--help=all`) prints every option,
  as before. The package's CLI files are `dist/lattice.js` and `dist/lattice-min.js`; the
  `lattice` bin and the `@laticent/lattice` and `@laticent/lattice/min` imports are unchanged.
- **Breaking:** the CLI source file in the package is `lattice.js`, not `lattice-emulator.js`, so a
  script that ran `node node_modules/@laticent/lattice/lattice-emulator.js` must run `npx lattice`
  (or that `lattice.js`) instead; and `lattice --version` prints `lattice <version>`, not
  `lattice-emulator <version>`.

- **The code map is now easy for agents to find.** A plain search for a folder or part name now
  lands on `dist/engineering/codemap.md`: a new root `.ignore`, which only search tools read,
  re-includes that one generated file, so ripgrep and the agent Grep tool see it while git still
  ignores it. `AGENTS.md` now points non-Claude agents at the map (with a `dist-kits` link for
  readers without a clone), every roster agent that locates code is told to grep it first, and
  `CLAUDE.md`'s "Where X lives" row says to grep the map first and that it is generated.

- An empty deck now looks empty in the Studio. Compose draws no slide bar for it: it shows one line to write on and four starting slides (`title`, `content`, `cards-grid`, `big-number`) drawn with the add-slide picker's live previews, plus a link to every layout. Typing starts a `content` slide, and one Undo takes the deck back to an empty file. A Markdown deck pasted in arrives as its own slides.
- Preview shows "No slides yet" for an empty deck instead of a blank slide numbered 1. The slide counter and the deck menu say "No slides" instead of "1 / 0" and "1 slide", and Present says "Add a slide to present." instead of opening a blank slide.
- Compose names the default layout `content`, as Source and the docs do, on the layout button, the layout menu, its Undo notice, the pane chip, the slide strip and the slide map. It said "text", which names no component.
- Compose draws the Studio's own sample art (`sample:` pictures, such as the portraits in `team-profile`'s example) as the picture, as the preview does. It drew a dashed box that named the file. Web and relative images still draw as a labeled box, so opening a deck reaches no other site.

- **Compose's Placement control sets the slide, not the picture.** Picking Left side, Right side, Full slide or the new In the
  text for a picture alone on its line makes the slide `image mirror`, `image`, `bleed` or a plain content slide, and the
  picture stays an ordinary `![title](src)`; Compose no longer writes Marp's `![bg …]` keywords. An old `![bg …]` picture
  loses them the first time it is placed, and its description becomes its name (once, not as name and description both). Its other keywords go too, so a
  `contain` picture becomes cover-cropped.
  The control shows on the slide's one lone picture on a content or image slide, a modifier-only slide (`_class: dark`)
  included, not only on a `![bg]` one; it is not offered where the engine would not place the picture (a `![bg]` photo or a
  record already on the slide, an `http:` address), nor under a carried `<!-- class: … -->`, whose placement the badge now
  shows; a slide with a layout of its own, or a class written in a compound
  comment, is left to the Markdown editor. The picture's badge says where it sits (Panel · Right, Background).
- The Studio's card-ink and photo-contrast checks find a slide's photo however it is written: `![bg]`, a lone `@image{…}`
  record, or the `![…](…)` shortcut on an `image` or `bleed` slide.
- Compose, Export-to-Marp and the engine now answer one shared table of placement cases (`test/fixtures/placed-picture-cases.json`),
  and it found two more disagreements, both fixed: a `collage` slide's picture no longer shows a Background badge, and Export-to-Marp
  no longer places a picture under a bracketed deck class (`class: [bleed]`), which the engine reads literally.

- **Changed: the unit suite prints a dot per test instead of a TAP stream.** `npm test`
  emitted 657,806 o200k tokens across 70,428 lines, 70,172 of them TAP bookkeeping — and
  because the pass/fail counters land at the *end*, a reader with a truncated view lost the
  one part that said whether the run was green. The unit scripts now default to
  `--test-reporter=dot`: **1,182 tokens on a green run, 557x smaller**, with the full
  assertion diff, stack and exit 1 intact on a failure (1,371 tokens for the same suite with
  one seeded failure). `npm run test:tap` gives back the TAP stream. `test:watch` and the
  `test:integration*` scripts deliberately keep the default reporter — dot never flushes its
  failure block under `--watch`, and the nightly job summary greps `^not ok` to find a red
  integration run.
- **Changed: the SessionStart hook prints setup output only when a step fails.** Its npm,
  build and apt chatter came to 3,763 tokens of every web session's opening context and
  reported nothing a reader acts on when setup worked. Each step now logs to a file; on
  failure the hook prints that step's own output and names the log. A working setup costs 29
  tokens, and a broken one is *louder* than before, because its error is no longer buried in
  a hundred lines of successful noise.

- **The two most-routed-to docs are now index-first, so finding something costs a fraction of
  the context it used to.** `engineering/gotchas.md` was ONE 290 KB file (75k tokens) whose own
  opening line told the reader to "read top-to-bottom" — on the single most common trigger in
  `CLAUDE.md`, "something behaving strangely". Its 145 entries now live in 10 topic files under
  `engineering/gotchas/`, and `gotchas.md` itself is a generated symptom index: one line per
  gotcha, linking straight to the entry (27 KB / **7k tokens**, a 10× cut on the landing read).
  `engineering/decisions/README.md` rendered every note summary in full (395 KB / 96k
  tokens); each row is now a one-line gist — first sentence, capped at 140 characters, `…`
  marking any cut — for 90 KB / **26k tokens**, with the full summary staying where it always
  was, in the note's own front-matter. Both indexes are one line per item, which makes them
  **greppable**: `grep -i mermaid` now returns lines rather than paragraphs.
- **Added `npm run gotchas:index` / `gotchas:index:check`**, wired into `npm run build` and
  `build:check` beside the decision index. The symptom index is generated from the entry
  headings in `engineering/gotchas/`, so it cannot drift — a stale map is worse than no map,
  because it misdirects confidently and the reader pays for the wrong file anyway. Its `--check`
  is deliberately relaxed the same way `decisions:index:check` is (per-entry rows, no row order,
  no totals), which is what keeps two concurrent PRs from ejecting each other from the merge
  queue (#1547).
- Anchor generation uses `github-slugger` — the implementation GitHub's own pipeline uses —
  rather than a local transcription. A hand-rolled version was written first and measured
  against it: **38 of 144 anchors disagreed**, because the reference also strips non-ASCII
  punctuation (em dash, `→`, curly quotes) and maps each space to its own hyphen instead of
  collapsing runs (`Marp / Chromium` → `marp--chromium`).
- One mis-leveled `##` section in the old `gotchas.md` ("G-gen merge must use non-G file's G-gen
  block") is now an entry under **Lattice internals**, where its Symptom/Cause/Mitigation shape
  says it always belonged.
- **Both indexes carry headings and gists only, so grep them for a SYMPTOM or a TOPIC — not for
  an API name.** `grep z-index engineering/gotchas.md` found 7 entries before the split and 0
  after; the words live in the entry bodies now. `CLAUDE.md`, the index prose, `workflow.md` and
  `design/skill.md` all name the second path: `grep -rn <term> engineering/gotchas/` (and
  `grep -rln <term> engineering/decisions/`), which costs the same because you pay for the hits,
  not the haystack.
- **Adding a gotcha now has one correct place, and the wrong one fails loudly.** Entries go in
  `engineering/gotchas/<topic>.md`; anything written into the generated `engineering/gotchas.md`
  used to be deleted on the next regeneration without a word, and now fails `gotchas:index:check`
  with a message naming the topic file to move it to.
- Heading extraction uses **markdown-it** rather than scanning lines, so the index agrees with the
  renderer about what a heading is. The line scanner silently dropped every entry after an
  unbalanced fence — the shape a gotcha about a swallowed fence quotes — while the gate stayed
  green, and it also disagreed about HTML comments, indented headings, setext underlines and
  closing sequences. Two headings that would slug to the same anchor are now rejected outright,
  so no anchor is positional and no deep link rots when a sibling entry is inserted.
- A decision-index row no longer stops on an abbreviation (`…surface vs.`) or on a first sentence
  too short to identify anything (`G8 Studio performance.`) — both rendered as complete claims
  with no truncation marker — and a cut can no longer leave an unbalanced code span.

- **Breaking:** **Studio crash recording is now off by default and must be turned on** in Workspace → General → Crash reports. It previously recorded unconditionally. Nothing is recorded until you enable it — no session record, and no `console.error` capture — so a crash before you turn it on leaves no trail. Reports already saved stay readable and clearable with the switch off, and turning it off mid-session also drops the partial record of the session in progress.

- **Studio: the crash toast is gone.** Returning to a Studio tab the browser had unloaded while it sat in the background announced "The Studio stopped unexpectedly" — a crash notice where nothing had crashed. From inside a page an ordinary background unload and a dead renderer are the same observation, so that alarm was wrong most of the times it fired. Recording is unchanged and still unconditional; the report is now reached at **Workspace → General → Crash reports** and nothing interrupts you.
- **Studio: crash reports now capture `console.error`.** `window.onerror` only sees exceptions nobody caught, so a session that logged a stack trace seconds before it died used to report no errors at all. Console errors are recorded with their stacks and printf-style format strings substituted, and are labeled as errors the page survived. Console output itself is untouched.
- **Studio: crash reports lead with what failed.** Errors and files that failed to load come first; memory, freezes and tab identity follow. A session that ended while its tab was in the background now says so — "The Studio stopped while the tab was in the background", with "nothing to do" as its next step — instead of "stopped unexpectedly", and a tab the browser froze and never resumed is reported as an unload rather than a stop.

- **Breaking:** every minified file Lattice builds or ships now uses a `-min` suffix instead of
  `.min`, because the dotted form trips tools that read the part after the first dot as the file
  type. `dist/lattice.min.css` is now `dist/lattice-min.css`, `dist/lattice-runtime.min.js` is
  `dist/lattice-runtime-min.js`, and the same holds for `lattice-default`, `lattice-dagre`,
  `lattice-emulator`, `lattice-pdf-compose`, every `dist/themes/<name>-min.css`, the vendored
  `mermaid-v11-min.js`, and the Marp kit on the `dist-kits` branch. The package subpaths
  (`@laticent/lattice/css/min`, `/runtime/min`, `/default/min`, `/min`) keep their names and
  now point at the new files. **Update any `<link>`, `<script src>`, CDN URL, or
  `markdown.marp.themes` entry that names a `.min` file.** Third-party files read from
  `node_modules` (KaTeX's `katex.min.css`, Mermaid's `mermaid.min.js`) keep their upstream names.
- Decks and package galleries written before the rename keep working where Lattice reads them
  back: re-exporting a deck baked with the old `.min.js` runtime tags to Marp swaps them for the
  new `-min.js` block instead of stacking a second one, the CLI still strips an old-name runtime
  tag from its export HTML, and a gallery that loads `mermaid-v11.min.js` still passes the
  vendored-script gate.

- `engineering/decisions/README.md` lists notes A–Z by topic slug inside each status group, not newest-first. Two PRs that each add a decision note now rarely conflict on GitHub (5 of 354 replayed pairs against 88 before), which ignores the file's `merge=union` driver and left such PRs `dirty` with no CI run. For the newest notes, run `ls engineering/decisions/20*.md | tail`.

- **Breaking: the deck scorecard reports TWO grades — Craft and Style — instead of one
  overall number.** `scoreDeck()` now returns `{ craft, style, profile, categories }` where
  it previously returned `{ overall, band, categories }`, and the five categories became
  seven split across the halves (`structure` · `craftProse` · `contract` in Craft;
  `brevity` · `framing` · `data` · `pacing` in Style). The single grade averaged three
  incommensurable things — does it render correctly, did the author do the work, and does it
  match one genre's house style — so a well-made teaching deck with zero lint findings and
  zero craft findings scored C+, the joint lowest of the 198 scorable committed decks. **Craft is
  genre-blind and holds the same bar for every deck; Style is measured against a named
  profile and always reported with it.**
- **Added: deck profiles — `profile: general | teaching | mission` in front matter,
  declared only.** `general` is the default and reproduces the pre-profiles universal bar
  exactly (70 words / 6 bullets / a 14-word heading, both structural rules graded), pinned
  by a test against those constants. A profile can therefore only ever loosen a number for a
  deck whose author asked by name — never for a deck that said nothing. `teaching` relaxes
  prose density (measured: two thirds of its slides clear 70 words) **and softens `no-ask` /
  `agenda-missing` to 40% of their usual cost** — a lesson asks the learner to practice
  rather than the room to approve, and its progression is its agenda. Softened, not switched
  off: those two rules are Framing's only deductions, so zeroing them pinned the whole
  category to 100 and guaranteed any deck declaring `teaching` at least Style 77, whatever
  was in it. `mission` relaxes
  the heading budget only (17% of nonprofit headings clear 14 against corporate's 2%).
  Neither can touch Craft.
- **Fixed: the density penalty no longer floors a category, and cannot be gamed by deck
  length.** `wall-of-text` deducted 12 points per slide, uncapped, so nine dense slides took
  108 points off a 100-point category and any long-enough deck could reach zero — after
  which the score stopped telling "slightly over budget everywhere" from "genuinely
  unreadable". Every rule family now deducts a bounded, saturating amount in the finding
  COUNT, with no deck-length denominator: padding a deck with empty slides no longer raises
  its score, and a deck the slide splitter cannot see through is no longer penalised the
  full ceiling on its first finding.
- **Fixed: `Contract` was still uncapped, in the highest-weighted Craft category.** Thirteen
  lint warnings floored it and 20 versus 60 were indistinguishable — the same saturation bug
  this change exists to end, left in the one category that varies on a real, un-linted
  draft. It is now ONE saturating curve over a severity-weighted finding count, so it
  approaches a ceiling it never reaches: a lint-swamped draft bottoms out near 12 rather
  than clamping to 0, and every additional finding still costs something. (The first cut of
  this fix gave it two per-family curves whose ceilings summed to 125, so it still floored
  at roughly twenty errors plus twenty warnings — bounded per family is not bounded per
  category.)
- **Changed: `density-crowd`, `density-overflow` and the verbose-chrome findings now count
  toward the grade.** They were surfaced to authors and silently ignored by the scorer, while
  `wall-of-text` — which measures nearly the same thing — was scored uncapped.
- **Changed: Pacing is `n/a` unless a talk length is set or the deck runs past 40 slides.**
  It read 100 on 197 of the 198 scorable decks while carrying 19% of the grade's weight — and, like `Contract`, that flatness turns out to be an input artifact rather than proof the category is worthless: `length-vs-time` fires only when a talk length is set, and no caller supplies one to the scored review. `n/a` is the right answer to missing input.
- **Fixed: a front-matter `profile:` naming a JavaScript prototype member silently disabled
  the prose budgets.** `profile: __proto__` (and `constructor`) resolved through
  `Object.prototype` to a profile whose every budget was `undefined`, so `wall-of-text` and
  `long-heading` stopped firing entirely — a deck of twelve 220-word slides scored Brevity
  100 and Style 78 against the default bar's 49 and 50, and the Coach displayed "Style — vs
  undefined". It was also silent: the misspelled-profile warning did not fire, because the
  lookup reported success. Any name that is not one of the three profiles now falls back to
  `general` **and** is reported as invalid.
- **Fixed: `Structure` could be driven to 0, and `monotone-openings` ignored how many times
  it fired.** Structure summed five bounded penalties to a ceiling of 122, so a
  sufficiently broken deck clamped and stopped distinguishing "bad" from "much worse" — the
  same defect as the `Contract` one above, in the highest-variance Craft category. Both
  categories are now a single saturating curve over a weighted finding count: Structure
  bottoms out at 6, Writing craft at 22, and a repeated heading cadence now costs more when
  the deck has two of them than when it has one.
- **Added: the Coach can write a profile into your front matter.** The profile control was a
  session-only lens — it never persisted, so the CLI and anyone you shared the deck with kept
  seeing the old score, and the choice was lost on reload. "Keep in front matter" writes
  `profile: <name>` into the deck (checkpointed, so ⌘Z and History undo it). Without it,
  declared-only profiles had no adoption path at all: the two decks that prompted this change
  only scored well because their front matter was edited by hand.
- **Added: the Studio Coach names the profile it judged Style against, says whether that was
  declared or the default, and lets you view the deck through another profile.** The control
  overrides a declaration (it previously lost to one, which made it a silent no-op on exactly
  the decks that declare a profile); the profile you pick is session-only until you press **Keep in front matter** (above), which is the only thing that writes to your deck.
  A misspelled `profile:` value is reported rather than swallowed.

- The Diagnostic Protocol spec (`spec/diagnostics.md`, published at `/spec/diagnostics/`) is now version 1.1. Its rule registry lists all 178 rule IDs the linter can report, up from 13, plus three families of IDs generated at run time, grouped by what they check. It adds two severities, `info` and `suggestion`. A test now fails when the linter and the registry disagree on an ID, a severity or whether a rule can autofix.
- `lint:deck --discover` findings (`narration-acronyms`, `narration-passthrough`) now carry `severity: suggestion`, which the protocol requires on every finding.

- The docs test suite runs ~8% faster (233.3s to 214.0s mean, on a 4-core box). 136 of its
  test files touch no DOM and were building a jsdom window they never used; they now
  declare `// @vitest-environment node`. All 313 files and 4,483 tests still pass, and
  no test behavior changed.
- Added `npm run dom:bakeoff` and `npm run dom:bakeoff:speed` — a correctness and
  throughput bake-off of six Node HTML parsers against this repo's own rendered markup.
  Its verdict is to keep jsdom: happy-dom breaks DOMPurify (it leaves `<script>` in the
  sanitized output, which HARD RULE #22 depends on) and linkedom still lowercases every
  camelCase SVG element name. See
  `engineering/decisions/2026-09-20-dom-library-bakeoff.md`.
- The bake-off field widened to ten parsers plus the Chromium the export path already
  launches (`npm run dom:bakeoff:chromium`). Two near-winners are recorded and declined:
  domino (4.5x faster, but DOMPurify deletes all markup on it and its NodeList is not
  iterable, which `withDom`'s fail-closed catch would turn into silent transform
  no-ops), and Chromium (fastest measured, but CDP is async and `withDom` is not).
- Correction, recorded because the note asserted it three times: **basichtml does not
  lowercase camelCase SVG element names.** That claim was an artifact of a broken adapter in
  the bake-off harness, which left every parsed document empty. Driven correctly basichtml
  preserves all seven and scores 19/34, not 1/34. It is still declined — deprecated upstream
  into linkedom, last published 2022.

- **CI skips draft pull requests.** `ci.yml`, `platform-suites.yml` and `docs-preview.yml` run no job while a PR is a draft; marking it ready (`gh pr ready`) runs CI once on the head. Park an open PR with `gh pr ready --undo` while iterating, so intermediate pushes no longer start runs that a newer push cancels. The merge queue still runs the full suite on every group.
- The CI-green beacon no longer posts from a run that a newer push superseded, so a "green" comment for an old commit with every tier canceled can no longer stand as the PR's newest wake event. Marking a PR ready again with no push queues CI behind the run already on that head instead of canceling it into a red check. A run a push canceled before its path filter started now passes instead of reading red on the old commit.

- **The CLI guide now says what an editable `.pptx` needs from the reader's fonts.** An app that ignores embedded fonts (LibreOffice, Keynote, Google Slides) substitutes the deck's fonts, so lines run wider or narrower and a small picture inside a sentence (an icon, spark or avatar) can sit off its words. With the fonts installed the file matches the slide. Install the fonts, or use the picture `.pptx` or the PDF when the layout must hold exactly.

- **Changed: the deck editors draw the site's own focus ring again.** The Playground's
  deck editor, the Studio's deck Editor and the component-page Specimen now show a 2px
  `var(--accent)` ring while focused, flush with the editor's edge. They had no ring at
  all: the site's one focus rule selects `input`/`textarea`/`[tabindex]`, and
  CodeMirror's editable surface is a `contenteditable` div that matches none of those,
  so the largest text surfaces we ship sat outside the focus language every other
  control shares. The caret alone did meet WCAG 2.4.7, so this is a consistency fix
  rather than a conformance one — the argument, the two measurements that killed the
  conformance framing, and why the ring is a pseudo-element rather than an `outline` are
  in `engineering/decisions/2026-09-13-editor-focus-ring.md`. An embedded `CodeField`
  declines it, because its host already paints the affordance or scrolls the editor.
- **Changed: the focus ring's right edge insets 1px** so a strip of canvas separates it
  from the pane splitter. The splitter paints `--border`, which sits too close to
  `--accent` to separate from it on most palettes — under 3:1 on 29 of 36 palette-modes,
  and byte-identical on onyx/dark. Flush, the two fused into one band and the edge read
  identically focused and unfocused (1.11:1). Both of the ring's sides now face the
  canvas and it clears 5.24:1 on every palette.

- **Changed: the editors' selection contrast is now read from a browser on all 18
  palettes, not one.** `editor-selection-parity.spec.ts` drove only the default
  palette, so 17 of 18 rested on a sweep of the token files — the kind of arithmetic
  this surface has twice shipped a wrong number from. It now loops every palette in
  both color modes on both editors, reading `::selection`, the caret, the active-line
  backdrop and the six inks these editors paint off the live DOM, and holds primary
  ink to AA (4.5) and secondary to AA-large (3.0).
- **Fixed: a contrast spec read `NaN` for any token the stylesheet minified to
  three-digit hex.** The helper sliced `#rrggbb` at fixed indexes, so `#fff` and
  `#000` parsed as `NaN` and every ratio built on them was meaningless. It only stayed
  invisible because cuoio — the one palette the spec drove — has no shorthand token.
- **Added: `tools/screenshot.js --storage k=v`** seeds localStorage before the first
  navigation, which is what it takes to photograph the docs site on a non-default
  palette (no route accepts one as a query parameter).

- An emoji in a CLI or Studio PDF is real text now, and so is the paragraph around it: it can be selected, searched and read aloud. Before, any paragraph holding an emoji was part of the slide's background picture.

- **Changed: `@laticent/lattice` now publishes from `packages/lattice/`.** The engine's
  published fields (`name`, `version`, `bin`, `exports`, `files`, `dependencies` and the rest)
  moved out of the repository root `package.json` into `packages/lattice/package.json`, so
  Changesets can version the engine as a workspace. Its `prepack` builds at the root and
  `tools/stage-engine-package.js` links the shipped files in. The tarball holds the same 2,202
  files as before; the one file that changes is the shipped `package.json`, which no longer
  carries the repository's 309 npm scripts, its `devDependencies` or its `workspaces`. Nothing
  changes for a deck or a consumer.

- **Changed: the Studio and the docs site load less JavaScript before they paint.** The Studio's
  startup JavaScript drops from 668KB to 493KB gzipped: the lint core now loads after first paint.
  The engine every app page loads drops from 551KB to 325KB gzipped (1.58MB to 931KB to parse): it
  bundles one copy of markdown-it instead of two, and the docs site now loads it as ES modules
  whose 24 chart kernels arrive only when a deck uses that chart. Output is byte-identical across
  all 276 example and baseline decks. A chart kernel that cannot load (a tab left open across a
  deploy) now says "part of the app didn't load" and offers a reload, instead of failing the render.
- **Changed: the route budget counts the engine and the preview runtime.** A new `engineJsGz`
  metric in `docs/route-budget.json` covers the files under `/playground/v/<hash>/` that
  `eagerJsGz` never saw.

- Noto Color Emoji is now self-hosted like every other font, as 11 `unicode-range` woff2 slices (about 2 MB together) in `dist/fonts/`, and it leads every emoji fallback. A deck draws the same emoji on every machine. An export embeds the font only when the deck has emoji, and the HTML player and the plain `.html` cut it to those emoji (about 2 KB each; see `font-embedding:`). PDF, PowerPoint and image sets draw emoji into the slide picture and carry no emoji font.
- `dist/lattice-emoji.css` and `npm run fonts:emoji` are retired. The file stays, empty, so existing imports resolve.

- **Editable PowerPoint and LibreOffice exports now say which fonts they could not embed.** A font used in a deck was left out of the file silently when no font file was available (a system font such as Arial) or its license forbids embedding, and the reader's office suite then substituted its own font. The command line now prints one warning per font on stderr (`font "Arial" is not embedded (…)`), and the Studio adds it to the "ready" message. None of the fonts Lattice ships (Playfair Display, Outfit, JetBrains Mono, Caveat, Shantell Sans, KaTeX) forbids embedding.

- **PDF, the offline player, PowerPoint and LibreOffice now shrink big pictures by default.** In the PDF and the player, a photo or screenshot over 150 KB is capped to 2560 px on its long edge and re-encoded as JPEG (quality 90), but only when that saves at least 30% (a format change) or 10% (a resize). A file that does not win, a transparent PNG, a GIF and an SVG are embedded exactly as before. On a 52-slide deck of 21 PNG screenshots (23.9 MB), the PDF went from 33.5 MB to 6.0 MB and the player from 66.6 MB to 12.6 MB; a deck of photos that were already tight JPEGs came out the same size.
- **A 4K deck now exports its PDF, PowerPoint and LibreOffice file at HD by default.** The design is the same at either size; the pixels are what make the file big (typically 1.6x for a PDF and 2x for PowerPoint, measured on a 52-slide photo deck). `--size 4k` on the command line, or **4K** in the export panel's new Resolution control (shown only for a 4K deck, with the cost), keeps 4K. The command line says when it lowered the size, and both hosts show the finished file's size. The deck's own `size:` is never rewritten.
- **One JPEG quality, 90, for every picture an export writes**: source photos, PowerPoint and LibreOffice slide pictures, and the PDF's slide-photo layer (it was 92 for the last two). The Studio and the command line read it from the same place.
- **You decide, per deck or per export.** `images: original` in the front matter, `--images original` on the command line, or **Original quality** in the Studio's Pictures control embeds every picture as added and keeps PowerPoint and LibreOffice slides as lossless PNG (13.7 MB becomes 26.3 MB on that deck). A number on the same line sets the JPEG quality, 1 to 100: `images: optimized 90` or `--images "optimized 90"`. The Studio and the command line read the same keys and run the same plan (`lib/core/image-policy.js`) with Chromium's JPEG encoder.
- `--size deck` renders on exactly the size the deck declares, never lowered. The repo's own gallery, golden, contrast and fit renders pass it, so a `size: 4k` deck is still measured at 4K while an author's export defaults to HD.

- **The Studio and the command line now photograph a slide with the same code, so the same format comes out the same from either.** Before, the command line took a native Chrome screenshot and the Studio redrew the slide through the html-to-image library (which shrinks every font by up to 1px and mis-drew some backgrounds). On a 52-slide deck, all 52 slides differed between the two tools, the Studio's PNG set was 52% larger, and a topic slide's bottom shelf was missing from the Studio. The shared camera (`lib/core/slide-camera.mjs`) lays the slide out again with the page's own stylesheet instead of copying styles. Measured on that deck against native Chrome, at most 0.0065% of pixels differ by more than 8 levels (html-to-image: 4.3% on average); across tools, the PNG set, PowerPoint, LibreOffice and PDF pictures differ by at most 0.14% of pixels on the worst slide, and file sizes agree to 2 decimals (PNG set 25.91 MB from both).
- **PowerPoint, LibreOffice and PNG pictures now show the slide as the live preview does**, in both tools: the finish glow and a topic slide's lighter shelf are kept. The Studio used to flatten them. The PDF's photo layer keeps the flat face, because PDF viewers such as poppler draw soft finishes badly.
- **One PNG encoder.** PNGs from both tools are written by the same encoder, with per-row filtering. The browser's own encoder wrote files about 40% larger (the 52-slide deck's PNG set zip: 39.8 MB with the browser's, 28.2 MB with this one; the Studio used to write 39 MB).

- **Changed: ⌘Z undoes the last change to the deck, wherever you are in the Studio.** Typing,
  a deck setting, a slide moved on the rail, an AI edit, a lint fix and a restored version now
  share one undo history per deck, so ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z) and ⌘⇧Z (Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y) work from the
  Markdown editor, the preview, the rail, a settings panel or the page body. In the editor, the
  browser's own undo requests (the Edit menu, iOS shake) reach the same history, and on a phone
  the header carries Undo and Redo buttons. Each undo moves every pane to the slide it changed and
  says what it undid ("Undid: Theme → Cuoio") to screen readers. The history survives switching
  between Markdown and Compose and between decks for the whole session, and one deck's undo never
  reaches another deck. A text field you are typing in keeps its own undo.
- **Changed: Compose's undo is the deck's undo.** ⌘Z in Compose, and its Undo and Redo buttons,
  step the same history as the Markdown editor and the rest of the Studio. An undo lands at once
  while you type, keeps the slides it did not touch (and their folds) as they were, and can bring
  back a deck emptied by select-all and Delete.

- **`fit:` is one deck setting for everything the engine does to make a slide fit.** `fit: heal` is the default: the engine splits an overfull slide at portrait sizes, and renders a slide that does not fit the deck's `scale-l/xl/2xl` at the designed size, without losing any words. `fit: trim` also lets it cut text that does not fit. `fit: report` switches every move off: the engine only flags. It replaces `guards:`, which still works for now (`strict` means `trim`, `loose` means `heal`). `lint:deck` names the new spelling. The Studio's "Text overflow" field is now "Fit". A slide overrides the deck with `_class: fit-report`, `fit-heal` or `fit-trim`.
- **`_class: guards-strict` and `guards-loose` no longer lint as unknown classes.** They were documented as per-slide overrides but flagged by `unknown-class`.

- `engineering/decisions/2026-11-21-fleet-command-pattern.md` records how the command center and desks work: the workflow, the patterns it borrows, what heals itself, the gotchas from 2026-11-21, and a proposed frontier desk.
- `engineering/workflow.md` §Merge queue — the facts now says that drafting a queued PR does not dequeue it, and that direct merges are refused.
- New `/desk-jank` and `/desk-polish` desks own layout motion and the 10/10 bar on shipped surfaces.
- Every desk now reads its lane's follow-ups, issues, claims and gotcha file before its first pass, and writes fixes, traps and leftovers back when done (`engineering/workflow.md` §Desks).
- Five more desks for launch: `/desk-a11y`, `/desk-docs`, `/desk-devices`, `/desk-release` (never cuts a release) and `/desk-feedback` (drafts every reply for the owner).
- New `/desk-stress` finds the upper limits of what still passes (deck size, images, chart points, session length) and keeps a limits table; new `/desk-torture` drives the Studio to crash or leak on purpose and names the culprit with `perf-torture`. Both run model features against a fake model and spend on a real call only with the owner's word.

- **`/fleet` reads less and names its session.** A board now lists 40 sessions instead of 100, reads open PRs as number and last update only, starts from the last board and fetches each PR's branch only when the PR is new: a branch record repeats the repository's description, about 400 characters per PR. On every `/fleet` the command center also titles itself `🛰️ Command Center · YYYY-MM-DD` (today in US Eastern time), so today's command center stands out in the session list.

- `_focusStyle: blur` no longer scales its target or casts a shadow past it. It only defocuses the rest, so no card moves between `_focusSteps` and no outer card is clipped at the stage edge. Measured at 1280px on six card lists, the clip overhang drops from up to 14.75px to 0 and the cards move by 0px instead of up to 23px. The `--focus-pop`, `--focus-pop-shadow`, `--focus-berth` and `--focus-lift` tokens are gone with it.

- **`frameToggleSkip()` is now `sovereignFrames()`**, matching the `SOVEREIGN_FRAMES` set it derives. The old name described a Form toggle that no longer exists. The `dist/docs/forms.json` and `dist/agent-kit/reference/forms.json` field `formToggleSkip` is renamed to `sovereignFrames` with it.
- **The linear-time guard for the katex scan moved out of the blocking unit suite** to an on-demand perf tier — `test/benchmark/relationship-scaling.test.js`, run with `npm run test:perf`. It is a wall-clock measurement in a suite `node --test` runs in parallel, which is a flake generator (its own note records 3 failures in 12 runs under heavy oversubscription), and it cost 406ms of its file's 954ms. This is the posture HARD RULE #19 already sets for `bench:check`.

- **Changed: the documentation now says Form is unconditional, everywhere it used
  to describe a toggle.** `design/forms.md` leads with a new §0 setting out the
  three levels — Form (unconditional) over Medium (`2d` today, a renderer's choice)
  over Frame (the component's choice) — and its §7, §8, §10 claims are corrected.
  `README.md`, `engineering/architecture.md` and the docs-site craft pages follow.
- **Fixed: three docs-site pages said "ten layouts are sovereign" and listed
  `math`.** It is nine, and math left the sovereign set in 2026-09 — so a reader
  anchoring a rule on `section.math` was told to write one that cannot fire. They
  also described sovereign layouts as taking "neither cell", which is the exact
  conflation being removed: a sovereign Frame declares `cells: ["stage"]`.
- **Fixed: `README.md` and `design/forms.md` both claimed the browser runtime reads
  no front matter**, contradicting the shipped runtime and its own changelog entry
  since 2026-07-08. Both are moot now and both are corrected.

- **Changed: every slide now states the Form model in the DOM.** The engine, the
  emulator and the browser runtime stamp `data-form="2d"` (this slide composes as
  Form, in the 2D medium) and `data-frame="<id>"` (which Frame carves it —
  `standard`, or one of the ten sovereign ids) on every top-level slide.
  Sovereignty used to be spelled as an ABSENT `form` class, which made "which Frame
  composes this slide" indistinguishable from "is this Form at all"; a reader now
  asks `data-frame` and gets a name.
- **Unchanged on purpose: the `form` CSS class.** It is the chrome-hosting Frame's
  selector hook — what the engine rules that paint the masthead band, the bay, the
  footer Cell and the rail select on — so a sovereign Frame still does not carry it.
  So no deck changes shape because of it: the chrome injectors — the masthead band,
  the footer Cell, the progress rail, the watermark — still gate on that class,
  exactly as before. (An earlier draft of this entry said they had moved to a new
  `hostsChromeCells()` predicate. They had not; the predicate exists and names the
  question, and rewiring the four injectors to ask it is a separate change with its
  own risk, not something to claim in a changelog because it sounded tidier.)
- **Renamed: `FORM_TOGGLE_SKIP` is now `SOVEREIGN_FRAMES`,** because it is no longer
  a toggle's skip-list — it is the set of Frames that declare a single `stage` Cell.

- **Breaking:** a slide's notes are now four named comments, each named for where it shows up: `<!-- @note{…} -->` (speaker notes), `<!-- @say{…} -->` (the voice and the captions), `<!-- @alt{…} -->` (alt text) and `<!-- @handout{…} -->` (the handout and the player's Read view). A plain `<!-- comment -->` is no longer the speaker note: it reaches no rendered, spoken or annotated surface, and `--strip-notes` removes it from every export that carries the source. Run `lattice migrate notes deck.md` to rewrite a deck.
