- **Breaking:** removed with no alias, each reported by `lint:deck` with its replacement: `<!-- say: … -->`, `<!-- describe: … -->` (now `@alt`), `<!-- reader: … -->` (now `@handout`), the Studio's `<!-- note: … -->`, the front-matter `say:` map (put each line on its slide as `@say`), and a record's `note=`, `say=`, `describe=` and `reader=` fields. The lint rules `caption-key-retired` and `say-key-case` are replaced by `note-key-retired` and `note-malformed`.
- PPTX and PDF label the handout `Handout:` after the speaker note (it was `Reader:`), and the HTML player's Read view now prints each slide's handout under the slide.
- The export to Marp writes `@note` as a Marp speaker note and `@handout` as a `Handout:` note, and drops `@say`, `@alt` and plain comments, which Marp would otherwise show as speaker notes.
- `list-steps-inline-body` also flags a step written as one whole sentence on its `1.` line with no nested body, which renders as a single bold block; `examples/meta.md` had three such slides.
- A deck written the old way (no named note, two or more plain comments) gets an info finding, `plain-comment-notes`, whose fix migrates the whole deck, so the Studio's quick fix converts it in one step; every CLI export with a notes channel says so once. `lattice migrate notes` lists converted comments that read like a TODO or a draft, for review.
- `lattice migrate notes --back` writes the four notes back in the LFM 1.x forms (a plain comment, `say:`, `describe:`, `reader:`), so a deck can go back to 1.x with one command, and lists what 1.x reads differently.

- The Studio's markdown editor, slide rail, slide counter and live preview now stay in step
  through one focus hub (Fuoco, `docs/src/lib/fuoco`) instead of eight hand-written guards in
  the shell. An arrow key along a line no longer re-renders the Studio. Measured on a 123-slide
  deck against `main`, same machine: an arrow key's Event Timing drops from 24 ms to the 16 ms
  frame floor, a slide change reaches the rail in 15 ms (was 25) and the preview in 36 ms (was
  49), a rail click answers in 48 ms (was 76), and typing in a slide drops from 72 ms to 60 ms
  per key with less than half the long-task time (405 ms against 966 over 35 keys).
- A deck that splits on headings, the default, now counts the slides the PDF prints. The rail
  shows one pill per rendered slide, the counter and the deck chip count them, and the preview
  shows the heading the caret is under. Before, `# Title` with two `##` read as one slide and
  the preview only ever showed its first heading (#1570).
- After inserting, duplicating, deleting or moving a slide, restoring a version, applying an AI
  edit or appending a lesson slide, the editor lands on the slide the operation names once the
  new text is in place, rather than one animation frame later; Compose now follows these too.
- Plugin block rules declare `scansAhead` in their manifest: whether the rule decides by reading
  lines past the block it opens. `math`'s `$$` block does. The plugin resolver refuses a block
  rule without it.
- Fuoco is a standalone library, `@laticent/fuoco`, usable without Lattice: any text cut into
  units and parts (Markdown sections, transcript cues, code symbols, slides) through an
  outliner, with a general `createTextOutliner` and `byPattern` / `byHeadings` /
  `byBlankLines` splitters built in. Lattice's slide outliner is one adapter
  (`docs/src/lib/deck-outline`). A live demo with its own brand is at `/libraries/fuoco/` on the docs site.

- **The capability, decision and gotcha indexes are generated into `dist/engineering/` and no
  longer committed.** `npm install`, the SessionStart hook and `npm run build` write
  `dist/engineering/capabilities.md`, `decisions.md` and `gotchas.md` from their one-file-per-item
  sources, so two PRs that each add a tool, a decision note or a gotcha no longer rewrite the
  same file. 23 of the last 50 commits rewrote at least one of the three committed copies.
  `capabilities:check`, `decisions:index:check` and `gotchas:index:check` now validate the
  sources and still run inside `build:check`. `engineering/decisions/README.md` and
  `engineering/gotchas.md` keep their hand-written guidance. The `dist-kits` branch carries a
  copy for reading on github.com, and the npm package leaves the folder out.

- Pull requests no longer commit PDFs. The `lint` job fails a PR that adds or changes one; the nightly bless bot renders and commits every golden PDF, including the first PDF of a deck or gallery merged without one. A PR's golden-diff comment links the rendered PDF of any new deck. The pre-commit hook that rendered and staged PDFs is gone; `node tools/build-staged-pdfs.js <deck.md>` renders one locally without staging it.

- **Changed: the bless bot and the PR golden-diff job run on a pinned `ubuntu-24.04`**
  instead of `ubuntu-latest`. A new runner image now arrives as a PR that moves both jobs,
  not as a night on which every golden drifts.

- **The two adjacent blurred-`box-shadow` PDF entries in `engineering/gotchas/export.md` are
  merged into one.** They were one finding reported twice — Chromium exports a blurred shadow
  as a transparency group, and Apple PDFKit / Quartz viewers paint its bounds opaque — found
  once on small state discs and once on a whole focused card. The merged entry keeps both
  discovery contexts, both mitigations (zero-blur spread ring, zero-blur opaque offset) and the
  warning that every local rasterizer composites it correctly and so hides the bug.
- **The two 4K-geometry entries are now findable from the topic each was observed on.** They
  stay together in `lattice-internals.md` — one cause, and the trap catalog cites them as a
  pair — but `vscode.md` and `studio-playground.md` each gain a pointer stub, so the symptom
  index names them under those topics. That was the one thing the 2026-08-17 refile gave up
  when it chose not to split them.

- The gotchas topic files are re-filed so each one holds what its title claims. `ci.md` was six-sevenths Playground hydration entries and `marp.md` was 26 of 34 not-Marp — which defeats the point of a symptom index, where the group heading is the only thing a reader scans before committing to a file. All 145 entries now file under the surface or subsystem whose behavior surprised you, across 14 topics instead of 10: new `studio-playground.md`, `export.md`, `overflow.md` and `fonts.md`; `marp.md` is now 8 entries about Marp; `docs-site.md` is now the Astro build and dev server it was named for. The largest topic file drops from 21.0k tokens to 17.2k. Every entry body is unchanged byte-for-byte apart from seven repaired cross-references — the move was made by a tool that refuses to run on an incomplete plan and asserts the before/after entry set is identical. Rationale in `engineering/decisions/2026-08-17-gotchas-topic-refile.md`.

- **`heatmap` sizes its row-name gutter to the names, so they read on one line.** The
  gutter was a fixed 52 of the chart's 320 units, which wrapped ordinary cohort names:
  "February 2026" and "September 2026" each took two lines while "May 2026" took one,
  and "Product-led signup" broke mid-word. The gutter now grows to the widest row
  name on a single line, up to `bar`'s 96-unit ceiling, and shrinks for short names
  so the grid gets the width back. It never grows at the cells' expense: it stops
  where a cell value or column name that printed at the old width would be dropped,
  and past that a long name wraps as before. Demo: `examples/heatmap-row-names.md`.

- **Breaking:** `heatmap` is authored as a **markdown table**, not a nested list. The header row names the columns, each body row leads with its label, and a **blank cell is a crossing nobody measured**. Heatmap data starts in a spreadsheet, and a table is paste-compatible where the list had to be transcribed by hand — the 10×12 stress matrix is 94 authored lines as a list against 12 as a table. Every deck in this repo is migrated; a heatmap deck kept elsewhere must be converted, and until it is, the slide renders as the plain table it contains rather than erroring.
- A heatmap cell can carry its own description with a `` `note=prose` `` annotation — `` | 62 `note=dipped after onboarding` | ``. The `note=` name keeps it apart from a hex color or an issue ref in a cell.

- The docs site's home page now leads with what a deck is for: being understood by the people who decide. The hero shows a real board decision and names the rooms a deck is made for. A new "Say more with less" section sets a memo paragraph beside the same content as one live slide, and the audience cards are organized by room (the boardroom, the pitch, the briefing, the lecture hall, the mission, the review) instead of by job title. The library and spec sections moved off the home scroll into one "Building on Lattice?" line under Next steps, and the "why" cards are in plain words.
- The home page's palette carousel puts the palette name on its own line under the swatches, so a long name no longer runs off a phone's edge or moves the swatches as the carousel cycles.
- The home page's hero shows its slide above the buttons on a phone and says up front that Lattice renders what you wrote rather than guessing. "How it works" follows the thesis, the room cards swipe on a phone, the palette section shows a branded quarterly review, and a "For builders" panel beside the AI section links the open specs, the standalone libraries and CI rendering.
- The home page's hero slide is one readable board-decision number, each room card links a full worked deck for that room as a PDF, and the page says plainly that the Studio's welcome deck and the layout gallery are made with Lattice.
- The home page's hero shows the before/after itself: a memo paragraph above the live chart that says the same thing in six lines. A drawn comparison shows four blank-canvas slides drifting beside four that match, the drift and brand sections are one, each room card leads with its outcome, "For builders" answers Marp and Slidev users, and the color-blind palettes are named in plain words.

- **New HARD RULE #30 — house voice.** Everything we write *about* the work — a chat
  reply, an issue, a PR body, a commit message, a `changelog.d/` fragment, a doc, a code
  comment — is active voice with a named actor, plain words with any term of art defined
  on first use, and leads with the answer. Deliberately no word budget: a number gets a
  real explanation amputated to hit it. The contract is `engineering/house-style.md`;
  `design/editorial.md` keeps the words *on a slide*, which is a different surface with
  different rules.
- **The British-spelling backlog is swept — 1285 spellings across 406 files** in one
  mechanical pass. Overwhelmingly prose: comments, docs, manifest text, strings and test
  names. It is not purely prose, though — a handful of internal identifiers were renamed
  (`cancelled`→`canceled` in UI code, `GREY`→`GRAY`, `offences`→`offenses`), and 34
  shipped decks changed slide-visible words, so 49 committed PDFs were rebuilt with them.
- **Breaking for contributors: `checkUsEnglish` is deleted.** The repo-wide scan, the
  `US_ENGLISH_BUDGET` ratchet, its self-exempt list and its revision ledger are all gone
  from `tools/check-ownership.js` (-93 lines), and `build:check` no longer walks every
  tracked file looking for spellings. A gate that needed 1285 standing exceptions to stay
  green was more machinery than the problem; from zero, a regression is one visible word
  in a diff. HARD RULE #21 is discipline now.
- **What replaces it is ~30 lines.** The commit-msg hook warns on British spellings from
  `tools/us-english.js` and never blocks — a message may quote British-spelled text, and
  HARD RULE #14 forbids `--no-verify` as the escape. It covers the surface that measured
  real drift: 21 British spellings in the last 300 commit messages, every one under a
  green build.
- **71 British spellings remain in living prose, none of them a backlog:** ~39 are the
  `progress-centre` Form cell (tracked in #578), 15 are external strings a US-English pass
  must never touch, 4 sit in a lockfile, 3 cite a dated `engineering/decisions/` filename,
  and the rest are deliberate mentions in tests and rules.
- **Fixed three defects the sweep itself caused**, each found by review rather than by any
  gate: `ci.yml` compared CI conclusions against `canceled`, a value GitHub never emits
  (its enum is `cancelled`), leaving two allowlists dead and their branches inverted; the
  world basemap stopped resolving the OECD's real legal name, so a map region silently
  dropped; and an intent-search synonym key became unreachable while double-scoring its
  own stem, with the one test guarding it reduced to `X.toEqual(X)`.

- **Markdown's picture is the image record's shortcut.** On a slide that places a picture (an `image` slide, `image mirror`,
  a `bleed` slide), `![title](src "description")` alone on its line is now placed exactly like `@image{src, title=…,
  description=…}`: the slide's photo panel or background, with the same words for a screen reader. Before, it drew a bare
  picture in the text. Anywhere else it is still an ordinary picture; the record is what takes a frame, a finish, a tone, a
  size or `show=`. `sample:` and `asset:` names work in both. Export-to-Marp writes such a picture as `![bg]`, as it does the
  record. Only a slide's ONLY lone picture is placed, and only one that is the slide's own paragraph: two pictures, or a
  picture in a list or a quote, stay ordinary pictures, and so does one on a slide that already has a `![bg]` photo or a
  record (a logo beside a `![bg]` photo stays in the text column), one at an `http:` address, or one whose alt starts with
  Marp's `bg` keyword in any case. A deck-wide `class: bleed` makes that one picture every slide's
  background, as it already did for the record. One shipped deck moves: `styles-device-check`'s web-image slide shows its blocked picture as the panel.
- The Reading view (the article built from a deck) shows an `image` slide's photo and a `bleed` slide's background as a
  figure after the lead paragraph, when the picture is written as `![…](…)` or `@image{…}`. A Marp `![bg]` picture stays out
  of the article, as before, and so does a picture with no title (it is decorative).

- The decisions index is now budgeted per ROW, not per file. `npm run decisions:index`
  and `decisions:index:check` fail a note whose index row exceeds `ROW_CAP` (285
  characters) — the filename is rendered twice per row and paid on every read, so an
  over-long slug is the lever the message names. A file total is deliberately not
  gated: it would bill the PR that trips it for 425 predecessors' contributions,
  which is the aggregate mistake #1547 already removed from this generator.
- **New decision notes: keep the filename to 66 characters or fewer** (past that it
  depends on your summary's first sentence). `engineering/decisions/README.md`
  § Convention carries the rule.
- `2026-08-17-context-index-tiering.md` rule 1 restated with measurements. The old form
  ("an index over ~10k tokens has failed") was unreachable for a 424-note corpus and
  neither exit it proposed reached the target; the budget now depends on the access
  mode the routing prescribes — read-whole indexes hold ≤10k, grep-first indexes budget
  the row.
- `2026-08-17-component-pick-surface.md` records the discriminating follow-up it named
  as missing: 12 pre-registered briefs drawn from the confusable clusters, four Opus
  agents, one surface each.

- **Fixed: inline pill shapes now match each other.** `:circle` and `:diamond` are as tall as the capsule, so a line or a `list-tabular` row that holds one stops growing. Before, they measured 31.9px and 37.9px beside a 25.9px capsule. `:diamond` is now a flat rhombus that widens with its label, so two characters fit inside the outline at that height. A `:circle` holding a wider label becomes a capsule with room around the text. The chevrons and the diamond draw the same 1px edge as every other shape; before, they rendered as flat tint with no edge. `:tag-bordered` now draws its double stroke as a `double` border inside its own box, where the old outer ring spilled 3px onto the words beside it, and lowercase descenders clear both lines.
- **Fixed: pill labels sit on the pill's visual center in every browser**, not just on the center of the line box. Where the browser supports `text-box` (current Chrome, Firefox and Safari), the label is trimmed to its capitals and centered on them. Measured, the worst pill is now 0.58px off in Chrome, 0.21px in Firefox and 0.42px in WebKit, where Chrome used to put labels up to 1.3px high. Exported PDFs render with Chrome 131, which predates `text-box`, and take a measured fallback: the worst case in the PDF drops from 1.47px to 0.68px. The label is also no longer pushed left by the letter-spacing after its last letter.
- **Fixed:** the left chevron's flat right edge no longer disappears in WebKit (Safari and the macOS app) when the pill's width lands on a fractional pixel.
- **Changed: inline pills size themselves from the text they sit in.** In a heading, or in any text more than about twice the pill's size (a lead or emphasis paragraph, a hero line), a pill is half that text's size, so it no longer looks tiny beside a title. In a below-note, a caption or a footer it takes the small size. Pills in body text, lists, cards and table cells are unchanged. `:sm` and `:lg` still work and now scale that automatic size.
- **Changed: `lint:deck` now warns when a `:circle` or `:diamond` pill holds more than one character or a two-digit number**, and the Studio and Playground editors underline the pill itself. The limit comes from measurement: `{12}` keeps a circle round, while `{OK}` makes it an oval and `{WM}` a capsule. The check was a quiet suggestion that allowed any two characters; it is now the `pill-shape-crowded` warning in the lint core. It never blocks a deck.

- **Changed: the iOS Simulator suites for photo, jpeg, photo-memory and chat-storage run one device per job.** Each is now an `-ipad` and an `-iphone` suite in `.github/platform-suites.json`, as undo and Studio already were, so a slow simulator boot on the second device can no longer run the job past its 30-minute limit and cancel it (6 such cancels in the 14 nightlies to 2026-11-20; in 5 of them no test had failed, and the sixth had already failed on a probe bug since fixed). No time limit was raised. A dispatch that named `ios-safari-photo` and the others now names the per-device suites.

- **Changed: a chart key and its callouts share one row style.** A key's swatch is now 1.45 times
  its label (was 1.04), so every SVG chart key (bar, stacked-bar, tower, piechart, map, quadrant,
  radar, heatmap and line) draws larger swatches in slightly taller rows. A callout's marker is the
  same size (was 1.84 times the label), with its digit at about four-fifths of the label, and a
  callout's words take the key's typeface, weight and size, so the two read as one family beside a
  chart. Beside a heatmap's band key a callout holds the key's size: a label too long for three
  lines ends in an ellipsis rather than shrinking below the key's words.
  (`engineering/decisions/2026-10-20-callout-placement.md` § 6.)

- **Breaking for anyone importing by package name:** the npm scope is now `@laticent`. `@workwel/lattice`, `cadenza`, `lente`, `suono` and `vetrina` become `@laticent/*`. Nothing was ever published under the old scope — all five 404 on the registry — so no consumer is pinned and there is no deprecation path to run; the rename is breaking only for anyone building against this tree directly.
- **The org, product and dba are renamed from SlideWright to Laticent**, and the retired `@workwel` scope goes with them. `TRADEMARKS.md` and `LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS` now assert the Laticent name, and the exception document goes to **version 1.1** so two different texts never both claim v1.0; the AGPL grant and the copyright holder are unchanged.
- **"Lattice Style" is retired as the umbrella project name** — the project is Laticent. The docs stay at `lattice.style`, so the brand and the domain now differ.
- Repository, Pages and schema URLs move with it: `github.com/Laticent/lattice`, `laticent.github.io`, `laticent.io`, and the five JSON Schema `$id`s. Demo payloads and schema `$id`s point at `laticent.io`, a domain the project owns, rather than the retired `slidewright.dev`. The 31 committed demo PDFs that carried the old brand were re-rendered, so their footers and QR payloads carry the new domain.
- The old name survives in six files, for three reasons. **The rename is their subject:** `engineering/decisions/2026-08-09-org-rehost-playbook.md` (a run sheet written from inside the source org), `engineering/decisions/2026-08-09-changesets-multi-package-release.md` (keeps the scope names its dated registry check actually covered), and `engineering/decisions/2026-07-02-website-copy-positioning.md` (a dated record of the three-brand debate). **They record a shipped fact:** `CHANGELOG.md`'s frozen `## 1.0.0` section notes that 1.0.0 shipped under the former name, and [`changelog/pre-release-archive.md`](https://github.com/Laticent/lattice/blob/main/changelog/pre-release-archive.md) is untouched — it declares itself frozen, and a decision record pins it byte-for-byte. **It is generated:** `BACKLOG.md` mirrors live issue titles verbatim.

- Design notes only: `@layer` D2 measurements for the bridges note (§3.7): layers retire none of the 19 needed specificity bumps, a design keeps author CSS winning at each host, and layering changes 3,923 of 117,299 elements (3.3%) across 282 example decks. Measurement scripts and results are committed beside the note.

- **Changed: the route budget watches the code that loads on demand.** Two new metrics on the
  Studio route in `docs/route-budget.json`: `chartKernelGz`, the largest chart kernel beyond the
  engine (chart-map, 77.4KB gzipped), and `lintCoreGz`, the lint core beyond the engine (90.3KB
  gzipped). Each has a soft target and a 10% ceiling, so a kernel or the lint
  core growing past it fails the docs build.

- LFM 1.1 §3.6 gains rule 4: an inline-code span in a component's declared data slot (today the list rows of flowchart, hub-spoke and state-chart) belongs to that slot and never renders as a pill, mark, spark or icon. `dist/docs/grammar.json` now lists each component's slots as `dataSlots`, and `spec/conformance/lfm/data-slots.json` pins the rule. The engine already behaved this way; the spec now says so before ratification.

- The Library now keeps a photo as you added it by default: **Keep original** is preselected when you add photos, instead of JPEG. Location and camera details are still removed. A `.lattice` project then carries your originals, and each other export still offers **Smaller file** or **Original quality**. A choice you made before is remembered and still wins.

- **Changed: the library marks no longer share one palette.** Trama moved from sienna to brick red with a gold accent, Lente moved from blue to a periwinkle, Suono moved toward emerald, and Cadenza and Vetrina traded the shared amber accent for magenta and violet. The closest two library marks are now 0.068 apart in OKLab instead of 0.027. The demo pages of those libraries carry the new colors.
- **Fixed: library mark and demo-page colors hold contrast in light and dark.** Veduta's light accent was 2.83:1 on paper, Trama's was 3.0:1 and Fluido's was 2.96:1; every drawn color is now at least 3:1 on both grounds, and the text colors on the demo pages are at least 4.5:1. A new unit test, `test/unit/docs/library-mark-palette.test.js`, keeps it that way.
- **Changed: each library's colors are written once.** `docs/src/lib/library-palettes.json` now holds the roles behind a library's brand SVGs and its demo page. `node tools/build-library-marks.js` writes the SVG colors from it, and a test fails if they drift. On the demo pages, an explicit light or dark theme now also sets the shadow (five pages used to keep the other scheme's), and Veduta now honors an explicit dark theme.

- **The library demos moved under `/libraries/`** (`/suono` is now `/libraries/suono/`, and so on); the old URLs redirect. Each demo now opens with a plain-language promise and the first thing to try, with Demo and Learn tabs. Labels such as "owned WebAudio clock", "fails CLOSED" and "deictic strokes" are replaced with plain words. Vetrina's settings and recording tools are folded into closed sections, and interrupting its tour now ends the whole tour, not just the current step. Segno leads with its everyday notation and shows the experimental grammar engine after it. Its journey example now uses `{who=Customer, …}` instead of the retired `@Customer` form.
- **The header nav carries two plain links, Libraries and Plugins,** instead of a menu that listed every library. The mobile menu does the same. The ⌘K palette still finds every library and plugin by name once you type.

- **Studio Library: one Import button, the same on every tab.** It takes a package `.zip`, photos, videos and reference files together (and, on a phone, the camera). The Library sorts each file by what it is and opens the matching section: photos open Images, clips open Videos, a package opens Design, reference files open Files, and a mixed batch opens All. The new items sort to the top and wear a ring for a few seconds.
- **Studio Library: one row of four sections, and a filter button.** All · Design · Media · Files, with a filter button on the right whose menu follows the section: Design offers Themes, Components, Finishes and Motions, and Media offers Images, Videos and where new media goes. A dot on the button shows when the list is narrowed. Everything is sorted by date added, newest first.
- **Studio Library: packages that came from a `.zip` or `.lattice` file carry an "Imported" tag**, so they read apart from the themes, components and finishes you made in Fabricate. Items saved before this change show no tag.
- **Exported bundle READMEs** now say **Library → Import** instead of **Import .zip**.

- **Changed: the Studio loads about half as much lint code after first paint.** The lint core now
  loads as part of the engine's own module build (`esm/lint.js`) instead of as a separate bundle, so
  it reuses the engine's markdown-it and core readers instead of shipping its own: 181.7KB to
  90.3KB gzipped. It keeps its own boundary parser, so narrowing the lint to a deck's plugins never
  changes how the engine splits slides. Lint findings are identical across 278 decks.

- **CI:** the `lint` job no longer runs a separate "Bootstrap the built-not-committed artifacts" step. Its `npm ci` already builds them (the root `prepare` script runs the same `build.js --only-uncommitted`), so the step built them twice, 48 s a PR. `build:check` still flags a stale committed artifact.

- `lint:deck` warnings now read as plain author advice: each message says what is wrong on the slide and what the reader will see, and each fix names the exact edit, without engine terms, internal file paths or CLI flags. Unknown front-matter values share one shape ("`'x'` isn't a valid `key:` value — the deck ignores it and uses …"), and the typed-glyph advice is one sentence per glyph.
- `unknown-split` now names the real fallback, `headings`; it used to say the deck fell back to `rule`.

- Three lint findings drop to `suggestion`, so `lint:deck --strict` no longer fails on them: `capacity-crowd` and `pane-crowd` (a crowded slide or pane still renders whole), and `autosplit-retired` for `autosplit: off` at a landscape size, where nothing splits and the line is only stale. `autosplit: off` at a portrait, square or strip size stays an error.

- **Changed: `list` follows the `cards:` register.** `cards-top`, `cards-center`, `cards-stretch` and `cards-spread` (or the deck's `cards:` key) now place a list's rows, in every register (plain, `takeaway`, `takeaway numbered`, `principles`). Before this, every list ignored them. With no setting, a list on a wide slide now **sits centered at its content height** instead of stretching every row to fill the stage. Write `cards: stretch` (or `_class: list cards-stretch`) for the old full-height look. Square, tall and strip frames look as before (a split page still fills with its one row), and a list above a Key Insight still stretches.
- **Changed: `list` counters share one scale.** Every counter is 1.4× its row's text, sits in the same box, and clears the text by one `--sp-md` gap. The plain numbered list's counter grows to match, the empty space after a `takeaway numbered` counter shrinks from ~72px to ~26px, and `principles` steps down from 1.6× (64px to 56px) with its counter-to-text gap narrowing from 32px to 24px. A lead over a nested gloss now keeps the row's full size instead of shrinking to the size of its gloss.
- **Changed: `takeaway` and `principles` row rules no longer look like the heading rule.** The line between rows is softer (the border color at 55%) and starts where the row text starts, past the counter, so it reads as part of the list. The full-width rule under the heading and the accent line above a closing note are unchanged, and each of the three now has its own look.
- **Changed: a full `list` gives up air, never text.** Each row sits at a comfortable height when there is room, and on a full slide the rows share out what is left, down to their own text.
- **Fixed: a wrapped `list` row stays inside its pill.** A list gave every row an equal share of the height, so on a full slide a row that wrapped to two lines spilled out of its pill, or onto the rule below it in `takeaway`, and no overflow check saw it. A row now never shrinks below its text; a list with more than the slide holds overflows, and the export reports it.
- **Added: `lint:deck` warns on a `list` modifier that does nothing** (`list-modifier-inert`): `principles` over `-` bullets (which renders plain pills), `numbered` without `takeaway`, `lettered`/`roman`/`bullet` without `principles`, and `takeaway` over a `1.` list without `numbered` (which hides the numbers).

- **`list-tabular` columns size to their content.** The grid moved from each row
  onto the list, and every row is now `grid-template-columns: subgrid`, so one set
  of tracks is shared and each sizes to the widest content across the list. The
  hard `3.4375cqi 15.625cqi 1fr minmax(0,0.9fr)` tracks it replaces made a
  two-letter label pay for the longest one — "ID" wasted most of a 15.625cqi track
  while a long label wrapped to three lines beside an empty description column.
  `fixed` restores the old widths for a deck that was laid out around them.
- **New `list-tabular` column modifiers.** `fit-name` `fit-body` `fit-meta` hug one
  column; `flex-name` `flex-meta` name the column that absorbs the leftover instead
  of the description. Most ledgers need none of them — the default already fits.
- **A ruled list's rule is a separator, so it no longer draws an outer edge.**
  `list-tabular` drew a hairline above its first row and below its last; `inventory`
  drew one below its last, `--sp-xs` above the insight band's filled panel. Both now
  rule between rows only (`li + li`), which is what `list.takeaway`,
  `list.principles` and `list-steps.ghost` already did. This is #2055's table-family
  fix carried to the list family. `kpi`'s banding and its heavier last-row total
  rule are a designed treatment and are deliberately untouched, as are card stacks
  whose rows do not touch (`list-steps`, `statute-stack`).
- **`list-tabular` centers in the stage.** A four-row ledger on a full-height slide
  read as a fragment pinned under the masthead; it now sits on the stage's midline
  (`safe`, so an overflowing list still loses its tail rather than its head).
- **Fixed: a long trailing value no longer bleeds past its column.**
  `white-space: nowrap` made a pill's min-content its whole string, which floored
  the trailing track's `fit-content()` cap — one long value took most of the row.
  Trailing pills wrap at spaces now.

- **Live calls sound clearer.** Each person's voice is now sent at 64 kbit/s instead of the browser's 32 kbit/s default, which keeps more of the high end. Tavola's `session.setMedia(stream, { maxBitrate })` takes the cap.

- **Breaking:** `logo-style:`, `logo-on:`, `logo-x:`, `logo-y:` and `logo-scale:` no longer render (`logo-style:` is now `logo-finish:`, named like `finish:` and `marks:`). `lint:deck --fix` (and the Studio's Fix all) folds them into one `logo-finish:` line: `logo-on: title` becomes `title`, `logo-scale` becomes `sm` or `lg`, and a free `logo-x`/`logo-y` position becomes the nearest of the six placements.
- `logo-style: brand` becomes `logo-finish: brand` and keeps its meaning (the logo's original colors on a plate); `auto` is the default color word.

- **Breaking:** the deck logo's `brand` color word no longer paints a soft plate behind the mark: it keeps the file's own colors with nothing behind them, so a logo with a transparent background stays transparent. The plate is now its own `logo-finish:` word, `plate`, off by default: write `logo-finish: plate` (or `brand plate`) for the old look, or `_class: logo-plate` on one slide, and `_class: logo-no-plate` takes a deck-wide plate back on one slide. Decks that overrode the plate in their own `style:` can drop the override.

- **Changed: the image set's diagram re-bake no longer waits on `networkidle0`.** The
  scratch page that flattens Mermaid diagrams into a `--svg-background` look was the
  fourth and last navigation wait still on `networkidle0`. It is built with
  `setContent`, so it sits at `about:blank` and requests nothing at all — the wait only
  ever bought Puppeteer's own idle floor: **1,986 ms → 154 ms**, with the emitted image
  set byte-identical under both waits (20 assets compared).

- **A narrated export's timing track now notices an emphasis-only edit.** The Studio's bake passes
  each slide's emphasis spans into the deck's LTT, which hashes them with the slide's text, so
  re-weighting a phrase changes that slide's segment `hash`. A deck with no emphasis exports
  exactly the hashes it did before.

- A palette's parent is now DISCOVERED from one place. `themes/<name>.manifest.json` declares `extends`; the CLI, the docs Playground and the Export-to-Marp bundler walk that graph through the shared `themeChain()` instead of each re-deriving it with its own `@import` regex. The `@import 'parent'` line stays in the CSS — Marp has no manifest, and it is also still what splices the parent into the composed stylesheet at render time — and `check:ownership` fails if it disagrees with the manifest.
- Fixed: the engine's composed stylesheet was wrong on the CLI path for every `-dark` theme. The emulator registered only the leaf palette, so its `@import 'indaco'` had nothing to resolve against and `render().css` came back as ~2 KB of scaffold instead of the full ~768 KB sheet. Exported PDFs were unaffected (the CLI inlines its own flattened stylesheet), but any consumer calling the engine's composed output from a CLI-shaped setup got an unstyled deck. The whole chain is registered now.
- Fixed: three theme-import scanners had drifted apart, and the emulator's required whitespace after `@import` — so a minified `@import"indaco"` would have lost its parent there while resolving correctly elsewhere. Latent rather than live (the CLI only reads source-form themes), but the fix had reached one copy and not the others. The `check:ownership` theme gate carried the same `\s+` form and now reads the minified shape correctly too.
- Removed: `themeImportNames()` from the docs theme fetcher and the emulator's private palette flattener, both replaced by the declared chain — verified byte-for-byte identical to the flattener's output across all 32 palettes.

- **Breaking:** Share → Markdown now downloads the deck source exactly as written. It no longer adds a `<style>` block holding the theme's CSS (about 10 KB, even for a built-in theme), nor the CSS of a saved finish or component. A deck that uses a saved theme, finish or component names it in the `.md`, and the Studio says so: share a Lattice project (`.lattice`) to carry them, or the Marp bundle for Marp.

- **The overflow and "text too small" markers are now ONE pill, centered against the slide's
  bottom edge.** They used to be two separate flags stacked in the slide's top-right corner,
  where they collided with the status stamp (`confidential`, `wip`, `draft`, …) and the
  author's `logo:` mark. A slide that trips both registers now shows a single capsule with
  two segments — the clip fact in red, the type-floor fact in amber — instead of two pills;
  a slide that trips one shows a single, correctly-rounded pill.
- **What a reader receives is unchanged in kind and better placed.** The type floor is
  author-only (a reader cannot resize a figure), so a delivered deck still shows exactly one
  calm "Content clipped" pill. It now sits below the running footer rather than beside the
  status stamp — frame margin no component writes into.
- **A status stamp and a deck logo no longer displace the marker at all.** None of the
  thirteen `stamp-*` shapes shares a band with the capsule, so none reserves anything. The
  two full-bleed washes (`stamp-mark`, `stamp-veil`) still cover it from the plane above, as
  they always have and deliberately.
- **Removed:** the `--corner-stack` / `--stamp-stack` per-stamp-shape reserves, the
  `--corner-logo-reserve` / `data-logo-corner` machinery that stacked the markers to the left
  of the deck logo, and the `--slide-radius` corner inset on these two berths. Two segments
  in one container cannot collide with each other, and a single centered box has one
  neighbor set to clear instead of four — so the arithmetic that kept them apart is gone
  rather than re-derived. The Fix-Me marker is unaffected: it keeps its bottom-right corner
  and its inset.
- **New contract markup:** `.marker-rail` wraps the two markers as the last children of every
  slide (`lib/core/fit-berth.js`). It is engine-emitted, carries `data-lattice-berth`, and is
  excluded from both overflow probes by name — a marker measured as content is a marker that
  manufactures the overflow it reports.

- **Breaking:** every on/off a deck or a slide can set is spelled one way: `no-X` turns it off and `with-X` turns it back on for one slide. The old spellings no longer do anything, and `lint:deck` (and the Studio) rewrite each in place: `callout-off`/`-on` → `no-callout`/`with-callout`, `motion-off`/`-on` → `no-motion`/`with-motion`, `spectrum-off`/`-on` → `no-spectrum`/`with-spectrum`, `spectrum-edge-off` → `no-spectrum-edge`, `spectrum-card-off`/`spectrum-card` → `no-spectrum-card`/`with-spectrum-card`, `spectrum-trim-off`/`spectrum-trim` → `no-spectrum-trim`/`with-spectrum-trim`, `row-label` → `with-row-label`, `no-rule` (the pane spine) → `no-spine`, `rule-none` (the heading rule) → `no-heading-rule`, `finish-none` → `no-finish`, `backdrop-none` → `no-backdrop`, `treatment-none` → `no-treatment`, and `tag-none` / `tag: none` → `tag-bare` / `tag: bare`. Front-matter settings keep their plain words (`motion: off`, `spectrum: off`, `rule: none`).
- **Breaking:** a slide's `with-X` now wins over a `no-X` everywhere, including a deck-wide `class: no-X`. A slide that carried both used to lose the switch for `motion`, `callout` and the table row label.
- New `with-progress`, `with-header`, `with-footer`, `with-logo` and `with-note` bring the section rail, header, footer, logo or below-note back on one slide over a deck-wide `no-X` or over `silent`. `silent` keeps hiding the header, footer, page number and section rail; any one comes back with its own `with-X`. The Studio's Chrome tab shows what each slide actually shows and writes the right `no-X` or `with-X`.
- A deck-wide `class: no-row-label` now reaches every table, a deck-wide `class: no-period` now strips heading periods, and a deck-wide `class: no-spine` now removes the pane spine; all three used to be silently ignored on the engine path. `with-spine` now brings the spine back on one slide.
- `no-period` no longer trims an ellipsis: a heading that ends `...` keeps its dots.
- In an Export-to-Marp bundle, `no-pagination`, `silent` and `with-pagination` now set the page number, and `no-period` / `with-period` now set the heading period. Marp's own stylesheet processing removed the rule that hid the page number, so it always showed, and the heading period was never applied. A deck-wide `class:` now also reaches the page numbers of slides that set their own `_class`.
- New reference page, Switches, lists every switch.
- **Breaking:** an Export-to-Marp bundle keeps Lattice's deck-wide settings (`class:`, `color-mode:`, `finish:`, `logo:`, …) in ONE settings block directly under the front matter, instead of a hidden copy at the end of the file. Editing the deck's settings after export used to do nothing for every key Marp does not read, and only half of `class: no-progress` landed: Marp drops a deck class on any slide with its own `_class`, so the section rail vanished from some slides and stayed on the rest. The block is read as you edit it in marp-cli, the VS Code preview (unsaved edits included) and VS Code's Export command, and a deck `class:` reaches every slide. A `class:` written in the front matter instead still works, in marp-cli at once and in the VS Code preview once saved. Re-exporting a bundle, or rendering its deck with Lattice, folds the block back into the front matter.
- An exported bundle always says `marp: true`. A deck with front matter but no `marp: true` exported a bundle that VS Code opened as plain Markdown rather than as slides.
- A deck-wide `class: no-callout` now also silences the narrated callouts, and a deck-wide `class: no-pagination` no longer leaves a hidden page-number attribute on each slide (an exported player read it).
- Rendering a deck that uses a retired switch spelling now warns by name with the new spelling (`"finish-none" was renamed to "no-finish"`), including the four that were silent.
- In an exported Marp bundle, removing `no-pagination` from the settings block after export brings the page numbers back, and a settings block that is hand-edited into the wrong shape is ignored rather than read differently by Lattice and Marp.
- `with-period` no longer puts a period before a heading's trailing code or math (`Use .npm`).
- In an exported Marp bundle, a collage, a statement image and a claim-bleed slide now hide their page number, as they do in Lattice, and `mark-asterisks` draws its second cluster. Marp's stylesheet processing removed those rules. Marp draws its page number in the same place as that cluster, so a `mark-asterisks` slide shows no page number in Marp.

- **math:** a hero equation with no legend now takes the whole slide, centered, instead of sitting in the left column beside an empty half and a divider. The `align-left` / `align-center` / `align-right` and `align-top` / `align-middle` / `align-bottom` modifiers move it, on one slide or deck-wide. With a legend, nothing changes. Demo: `examples/math-bare-equation.md`.

- **`math canvas` and `math matrix decompose` move onto the Form frame — the last two of eight.** Every math variant now renders with the masthead band, `meta:`, the running header and footer, the progress rail and the watermark tile.
- **Fixed: `decompose`'s contract and its stylesheet described different slides.** The docs and the manifest sample author it as one combined factorization plus a legend naming the terms; every rule below the lead equation addressed a *different* shape — a lead equation, an `### h3`, and three separate `$$` blocks in a row. The committed sample got the leftovers: the variant's `text-align: center` ragged the legend around a center while `matrix`'s left rule still ran down its side, and `matrix`'s label chrome set each `$A$` in uppercase mono at `--fs-meta`. Both shapes are supported now, split by the box each rule addresses.
- **Fixed: a legend label that is a symbol is set as a symbol.** Uppercasing does nothing to rendered math and `--fs-meta` shrank `$A$` to 70% of the body text defining it — measured 14.98px inside a 21.38px list item on the shipped gallery. The scale goes on the math, not on the `<strong>`: enlarging the element would enlarge its `min-width: 4em` with it and give a slide mixing symbol and word labels two different label columns.
- **Fixed: `canvas`'s plot was sized against the slide, not against its cell.** `38cqi` is 486px of a 720px slide against a stage that is 438px at hd — a number that stopped describing anything the plot sits in once the frame took a masthead and a footer reserve out of it. The plot fills its cell at the same 55:38 ratio now, and stacked it takes 62% of the stage, which is the sovereign arm's own proportion re-based.
- **Fixed: `decompose`'s lead equation overflowed every tall size by 204px.** It is the whole factorization on one line, so it is the widest thing math ships; 1.55em at tall/strip is the measured fit. It was over on the sovereign frame too, where the overrun painted into the section's padding instead of being clipped.
- **Fixed: the bare/`feature` hero kept the sovereign arm's title clearance.** `--sp-xl` of top padding held the equation off a heading pinned above it; under Form the masthead band and its rule already do that, and the dead space was the whole 13px by which a portrait bare-math slide overran its stage.

- **`math compare` moves onto the Form frame.** The comparison's columns now live in the stage cell rather than on the section, so a compare slide gains the masthead band, `meta:`, the progress rail and the watermark tile like every other Form layout.
- **Its responsive reflow becomes per-slide.** A portrait `compare` already collapsed to one column, keyed on the deck-wide `data-orientation` stamp; it now keys on the per-slide `[data-family]` instead, and the three-column case collapses too (it previously lost a specificity race and kept all three columns in a portrait box).
- **Capacity is reduced in HEIGHT only.** The stage is about 54px shorter than the section's body region, because the frame reserves space below the content. Width is unchanged — the sovereign section already carried 64px of horizontal padding, so the column boxes measure identically before and after. The committed gallery's compare slides fit either way, with no overflow warning; a slide that only fitted by using the space below now overflows and is flagged.
- The hero equation is 1.25em (was 1.4em). This buys margin rather than correctness: at 1.4em the widest estimator already overran its column on the sovereign arm, so the shear predates the migration — what changed is that `overflow: clip` now cuts it instead of letting it paint into the section's padding.
- The `column-span: all` heading and the `break-inside: avoid` eyebrow arm are **gone**, because the boxes they governed are in the masthead now. That removes #1554's root cause structurally, so the structural fact is asserted per-PR in place of a WebKit raster guard that could no longer fail. The ghost was then checked on real (desktop) WebKit and is gone, with an oracle proven able to fire against a deliberately broken arm; iPadOS Safari — where #1554 was reported — is still unverified.

- **`math derivation` moves onto the Form frame.** The proof chain lives in the stage cell now, so a derivation slide gains the masthead band, `meta:`, the running header and footer, the progress rail and the watermark tile — none of which a sovereign math slide could render.
- **The absolutely-positioned title is gone.** The sovereign arm pinned the `h2` with `top: calc(var(--sp-2xl) + var(--sp-md))` — the masthead band's geometry, copied by arithmetic — so the table could center in the well beneath it. The frame owns the title now and hands the stage the height that is left, so centering is `justify-content` on a box that already knows where it ends.
- **The proof chain tightens its row rhythm in a tall or strip box.** The Form masthead is an in-flow band where the sovereign title was not, and at portrait a wrapped title takes 271px of it, which put the committed sample 33px over the stage. Row padding drops from `--sp-sm` to `--sp-xs` vertically at `tall`/`strip`; nothing collapses and no type shrinks.
- The base `<table>` deny guard entry narrows from `.math.derivation` to `.math.derivation.form`, because that is the granularity the component's CSS now claims. A `math derivation` section without the form class gets the universal table defaults instead of nothing.

- **Breaking:** a `math` slide can no longer opt out of the Form frame. `<!-- _class: math no-form -->` on the migrated variants now renders unstyled prose, because those variants no longer carry a second, sovereign layout. The combination has never behaved differently from a plain `math` slide — math was already chrome-exempt through `FORM_TOGGLE_SKIP`, so `no-form` was a no-op on it — and no committed deck uses it. `form` is not optional.
- The `math` layout begins moving off its sovereign frame onto the shared Form frame, one variant per commit. **`feature` and bare `math` move first.** They gain the masthead band, the `meta:` strip, the progress rail and the watermark tile — none of which a sovereign math slide could render, so `meta:` on a math slide silently did nothing until now. The hero equation and its `where` legend keep their layout.
- Two visible differences on a migrated math slide: the heading sits in the masthead band rather than in the layout's own grid, and it gains the masthead's hairline, which every other Form slide already has.
- The seven remaining variants render **byte-identically** and keep their sovereign frame until their own commit.

- **Breaking-ish: `math` no longer has a sovereign frame.** `lib/forms/frame/math/` is deleted, `math` leaves `FORM_TOGGLE_SKIP`, and the component declares `stage: "canvas"` with `conformance: "strict"`. Every math slide now renders with the masthead band, `meta:`, the running header and footer, the progress rail and the watermark tile — none of which a chrome-exempt section could produce. `meta:` on a math slide used to do nothing at all.
- **`<!-- _class: math no-form -->` and `form: off` now render math unstyled.** The sovereign arms are deleted, so there is no second shape to fall back to. That combination never behaved differently from a plain math slide (math was already chrome-exempt, so `no-form` was a no-op on it) and no committed deck uses it.
- **Math is the only component ever to leave the sovereign list**, and it is worth saying why: its claim was "drives its own `> h2` title grid" — a heading-placement preference, not the "this slide has no room for chrome" that `title`, `divider`, `image` and the split frames rest on. In practice that title grid was the masthead band's geometry copied by arithmetic, `top: calc(var(--sp-2xl) + var(--sp-md))`, in three separate variants. `compare-code` carries the same wording in its manifest and not the same substance: it builds a real four-row explicit grid and places its `> h2` at `grid-column: 1 / -1; grid-row: 1`. Math's migration is not a precedent for migrating it.
- **The eight variant summaries are complete sentences now.** All eight were cut at 70 characters with an ellipsis — several mid-word — and math was the only component in the tree with the defect (the other 195, across the 45 components that declare variants, are intact). They are read by the docs site, the agent-facing component catalog and the gallery footers, so an agent picking `decompose` was choosing from half a sentence. One also carried a British spelling (HARD RULE #21).
- The first attempt at that replaced them with FULL sentences, which broke the gallery: those summaries are injected verbatim into each slide's generated `_footer:`, and at 130–138 characters the footer band clipped them — six slides over the overflow ratchet, and a visibly ellipsed footer in both committed gallery PDFs. The 70-character cap was load-bearing and was not established as such before being removed. The summaries are rewritten to fit it as whole sentences instead, which is what the defect actually was.

- **`math matrix` moves onto the Form frame**, and is the first math variant to render clean at all five registered sizes. On the sovereign frame it clipped at portrait, story and mobile; it now clips at none of them.
- **The equation no longer scales UP in a tall box.** The sovereign reflow took it from 1.7em to 2.4em on the theory that a full-width row has room; a 4×4 `pmatrix` does not, and portrait ran 279px wide and 206px tall past the section. It is 1.15em at tall/strip now, and the width it gains from the full row is the point of the reflow.
- **Fixed: a legend value that wraps no longer returns to the left margin.** `min-width: 4em` on the label reserved the width but not the indent, so "rank — full-rank for OLS to have a unique solution" put its second line under the label instead of beside it, breaking the two-column reading on exactly the rows long enough to need it. It is a hanging indent now. Pre-existing at every size, on both frames.
- **Both grid tracks are `minmax(0, …)`.** A track's default minimum is its min-content width, so the legend's label reservation gave it a 358px minimum against a 333px track and pushed the whole stage 25px wide — while the list itself reported no overflow, because the overflow belonged to the track.
- **Fixed in the engine: a clip cell laid out in COLUMNS no longer reports phantom overflow.** `probeSectionOverflow` measured a possibly-squeezed child against "the next flowed sibling's top", which assumes the children stack. In a two-track grid the next sibling sits *beside*, so the subtraction returned the child's own height: 2px of phantom inner overflow on a KaTeX equation (its `vlist` struts make every enclosing box report hidden pixels) became `dy: 265` and a "Content clipped" badge on a slide with nothing clipped. The sibling's top is used only when it actually sits below; otherwise the limit falls back to the cell's content bottom, so a genuinely crushed child in a multi-column cell is still caught. Multi-column clip cells are built by `kpi`, `redline`, `inventory`, `citation-card` and the legal components as well as math.

- **Math is its own family in the component reference.** It used to share a heading with code under "Code & math", where it was the smaller half of someone else's family on the one surface where a reader browses by shape. It is a distinct substance — `prose` with a typeset equation as the argument, against code's `snippet` — its own engine bucket, its own URL space and its own gallery, and the only component whose body is rendered by a third-party typesetter. "Code" now covers `code` and `compare-code`; "Math" covers `math`.

- **`math` is out of the `data-viz` showcase.** That deck is generated from `buckets: ['chart', 'math']` and is now charts only. Math is rendered evidence, which is true and is not the same as being a chart: a chart plots a dataset and a math slide typesets an expression — no shared transform, no shared dataset shape, no shared reflow — and a reader walking the charting surface to compare `bar` against `waterfall` does not want an equation in the middle of it.
- It did **not** gain a showcase of its own, and that was tried first: a showcase composes one `manifest.sample` per component, so a single-component bucket makes a two-slide deck that duplicates the bucket gallery already in the tree. The eight-variant survey is the component gallery. Both facts are pinned so neither drifts back.
- **New: `examples/math-form-frame.md`** — nine slides, one per variant plus a cover, with `header:`, `footer:`, `paginate:` and `meta:` set so the chrome math gained is the thing you see. Zero overflow at 16:9; `lint:deck` clean.
- The demo deck's `decompose` equation puts its `=` at the end of the previous line rather than on its own. That is not style: a lone `=` continuation line inside `$$…$$` is read as a setext `h1` underline by `positionIsTrustworthy`, which blanks fenced code before its heading scan but not display math, and the whole deck is silently refused a supplied slide position. Filed as #2137; the deck sidesteps it.

- **`math stats` moves onto the Form frame.** The estimate / uncertainty / interpretation scaffold lives in the stage cell now, so a stats slide gains the masthead band, `meta:`, the running header and footer, the progress rail and the watermark tile.
- **The title is left-aligned now, where it used to be centered.** This is the one place in the math migration where a reader sees a considered choice change rather than an accident: the sovereign arm centered the `h2` to match the number beneath it, and the Form masthead has one alignment for every slide in a deck. The number stays centered; the title lands where every other title in the deck lands.
- **The interpretation line drops its measure cap in a tall or strip box.** `max-width: 60cqi` stops the paragraph running a 1920-wide canvas, but in a 972-wide stage it held the line to ~25 characters and 504px of height — under the comfortable measure it exists to protect, and 12px over the stage. Released, the same paragraph runs ~41 characters and several lines shorter, and the hero number keeps its full size.
- **Fixed: `evidence/stats` no longer styles a `math stats` slide.** Two components claim the class token `stats`, and the collision was invisible while math had a sovereign frame — that sheet is scoped to `> .cell-stage` and a sovereign math slide had none. The wrap made it real: measured, four of its rules landed on a migrated math slide, centering the masthead lede and putting `font-style: italic` plus `--sp-lg` of bottom padding on the estimate and the interpretation line. Every `section.stats` selector now carries `:where(:not(.math))`, which costs zero specificity — 38 committed `stats` slides across four decks render byte-identical.
- A new gate, `test/unit/components/variant-token-collisions.test.js`, enumerates every component id against every declared variant token and fails on a new collision. Three pre-existing ones (`list bullet`, `compare-prose decision`, `radar quadrant`) are recorded with their measured leak counts under #2132.

- **`math theorem` moves onto the Form frame.** The Definition / Theorem / Proof card stack lives in the stage cell now, so a theorem slide gains the masthead band, `meta:`, the running header and footer, the progress rail and the watermark tile.
- **The absolutely-positioned title is gone**, as it is for `derivation`: the sovereign arm pinned the `h2` at `top: calc(var(--sp-2xl) + var(--sp-md))` so the stack could center beneath it. The frame owns the title and the stage centers the stack against a box whose height is already right.
- **The card rhythm is re-tuned for the stage.** Vertical card padding drops from `--sp-sm` to `--sp-xs`, and the stack gap with it, at every size. `--sp-sm` was right when the sovereign frame gave the stack the whole slide and a title that cost nothing; the Form stage is smaller by the masthead band. Measured on `examples/cat-ink-tier.md`, whose title wraps to two lines in `atelier`: a 356px stage against 415px of cards, so that committed deck shipped its theorem slide 60px cut. It now fits at every registered size, as does the component's own sample.
- Re-tuned once rather than per family, because the box changed at every size. `theorem` therefore needs no `[data-family]` reflow — the re-tune clears a tall box by 71px against a 26px shortfall — and says so in `NO_FAMILY_REFLOW` with that measurement rather than with a column count.

- **Mermaid diagrams now clear WCAG's 3:1 non-text contrast floor in every palette and both
  color schemes.** `--diagram-stroke` draws the outline of fourteen Mermaid keys — node and
  actor borders, gantt bar borders, the pie outer stroke, the quadrant frame, both xy axis
  rules — and every palette declared it as a flat, mode-invariant literal, so on a dark deck
  it was a dark line on a dark canvas. A flowchart node, gantt bar, pie slice and sequence
  actor had **no discernible edge at all in 24 of 64 palette-modes** (worst 1.55:1), and the
  quadrant frame and xy axis rules sat at exactly 1.00:1 on the `a11y-*` family. Retuned to a
  mid-tone in each palette — 12 of 14 changed, `cuoio` and `carbone` already cleared it — plus
  the gantt today marker, and `cuoio`'s edge line. **Diagram colors shift slightly on every
  theme as a result; outlines are lighter, and visibly so on dark decks.**
- **Three Mermaid keys were reading the wrong tier and are re-pointed.** The gantt grid line
  borrowed `--diagram-done` (a pale BAR FILL, 1.30:1 as a line) and now reads `--muted-mark`,
  the graphical de-emphasis tier; the sequence note's border borrowed `--diagram-today` (the
  gantt marker's own hue) and now reads `--diagram-stroke`; the quadrant divider and its
  plotted points read `--cat-8-mark`, a SIBLING of the fills they sit on, and now read
  `--cat-on-fill`, the tier gated legible against them.
- **34 Mermaid theme keys the engine had never stated are now stated.** Left unset, Mermaid
  derives a color from `primaryColor`/`background` by its own mixing — which is where every
  off-palette state diagram, requirement diagram, architecture group box, venn set, C4 person
  glyph and ER row band came from. Now on-palette: the stateDiagram node/transition/composite
  set, the requirementDiagram box and relations, `archEdgeColor`/`archGroupBorderColor`,
  `venn1`–`venn8`, `personBkg`, `rowOdd`/`rowEven`, `border2`, `arrowheadColor` and
  `xyChart.dataLabelColor`. (`nodeBkg` and `compositeBorder` were tried and dropped —
  neither is consumed anywhere in Mermaid 11.14, so stating them asserted a control
  that does not exist.)
- **Known limitation, deliberately not fixed: a sankey's flows are hard to see on dark decks.**
  Mermaid paints every link through an inline `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, which darkens toward
  the backdrop — right on a white page, and on a dark canvas it drives the flow to a near-black
  smudge beside correctly colored node bars. Overriding the blend to `normal` fixes dark and
  **breaks light**: Mermaid paints ribbons ON TOP of node labels, and multiply is what protects
  them, so the labels wash from 15.66:1 to 3.32:1 — below AA. `screen` would be correct on dark,
  but a blend mode must be chosen per color-scheme and no CSS selector can query one. The
  reasoning and the measurements are recorded in `mermaid.css` so the dead end is not re-walked.
- Added `tools/audit-diagram-contrast.mjs`, an on-demand report over the non-text contrast tier
  and a census of which Mermaid color keys are actually levers (measured: it honors all 234 and
  overrides none of ours).
- Added `test/unit/palette/diagram-nontext-contrast.test.js`, which gates the tier above so it
  cannot regress. A shape passes if ANY of its candidate edges clears 3:1 — fill vs canvas,
  border vs canvas, or border vs its own fill — because a node with an invisible border but a
  separating fill is perfectly legible.
- **`state-chart` looks different on light decks.** It is the one non-Mermaid consumer of
  `--diagram-stroke`, using it for the node's leading accent edge. Re-curating that token to a
  mid-tone raises the accent on dark decks (onyx 1.35 → 3.42) and lightens it on light ones
  (onyx 15.91 → 3.44). Nothing drops below the 3:1 floor, but the light accent is visibly
  quieter than it was.

- Lint now warns on every old directive comment (`<!-- _class: cards -->`, `<!-- _footer: … -->`, …) with `legacy-directive-comment`, and its fix rewrites the whole deck as `<!-- @meta{…} -->` records: the Studio's quick fix and "Fix all", `lint:deck --fix` and `lattice migrate meta` all write the same text, and the slides render the same.
- `@meta` is the one record spelling. `lattice migrate meta` and the fix now write `<!-- @meta{…} -->` and respell a bare `<!-- {…} -->` record as `@meta`.
- `lattice migrate meta` now merges a slide's adjacent records into one, as its help always said; the merge had never run.
- The Studio editor and the editable sample on each component page complete `<!-- @meta{`: `<!-- @m` offers it, then the fields, then each register's values. The blank-line insert list offers `<!-- @meta{layout=} -->` and `<!-- @meta{} -->` in place of `<!-- _class: -->` and the bare `<!-- {} -->`. Lint fix messages teach the record.
- `lint:deck --strict`, the pre-commit deck check and the Coach's Contract score do not count the old-comment warnings yet. `lint:deck` lists them once per file. This lasts until the committed decks are converted.

- **Changed: a deck's Mermaid diagrams now render in ONE `mmdc` invocation instead of
  one per diagram.** `mmdc` boots its own Chromium, and it was booting one for every
  fence — ~2.9s each, which on the 14-fence diagram gallery was 40.7s of a 44.3s render.
  Measured across the 118 fences in the example and gallery corpus: **454.5s → 245.5s,
  a 46% cut in total render wall.** A deck with a single diagram is unaffected; the
  saving scales with fence count and wins from two fences up.
- Batching is safe across theme bands because each fence carries its own baked
  `%%{init}%%` palette, so a light fence and a dark fence in one batch still render with
  their own colors. If a batch cannot be completed the renderer falls back to one
  invocation per diagram, keeping the existing per-diagram retry and per-diagram
  fallback — one malformed fence still costs only itself.
- **Fixed along the way: every diagram now gets a unique SVG id on every path.** The id
  isolation that keeps one diagram's embedded `<style>` from overriding another's
  previously lived only in the one-at-a-time renderer. It now runs wherever a diagram
  is finished, so batched and unbatched output are identical.
- New `tools/diagram-oracle.mjs` captures a per-fence hash of every baked diagram in
  the corpus and compares two captures, so a change to the diagram path can be shown to
  alter nothing rather than asserted to.

- **Changed: the Studio's preview sub-bar is shorter on a phone, and its two pills
  are one size.** The bar dropped the word "Preview" below 700px — the pane switcher
  directly above it already says which pane is showing, so the label was ~65px of
  duplication, and losing it is what stopped the reader-view pill truncating to
  "Full de…" at 390px. The reader-view pill is now sized to the `Slide N / M`
  counter it sits beside (`px-2 py-0.5`, 12px) instead of standing ~9px taller, at
  every width including the narrow pane where it collapses to its icon. Together
  those take the phone's sub-bar from 47px to 38.2px and hand the difference to the
  slide. The two-pane tiers keep the label and their 45px bar, where the "Collapse
  preview" button sets the height.
- **Fixed: the Studio's pre-paint shell no longer misplaces the slide box for readers who
  raise the browser's minimum font size.** It reserved space for the preview sub-bar and the
  slide navigator from numbers measured once at the default size, while the bands themselves
  grow with the reader's text — so the slide jumped at hand-off, by up to 13.4px on a laptop.
  The shell now measures what the browser does to a 12px element and grows both bands with it:
  0.59px at a 24px minimum, and 0.61px at a 14px one, which no root-font-size reading could
  see. The phone keeps the frozen model — its action bar is a third fixed band whose error runs
  the other way, and correcting only the other two made the phone worse.

- **Changed: the collage lays out about six times faster, with the same layouts.** The collage
  packer moved out of `lib/core/collage-pack.js` into a new workspace library, `@laticent/mosaico`
  (`docs/src/lib/mosaico`), and Lattice's side of it now lives beside the component in
  `lib/components/imagery/collage/collage.pack.js`. Six photos in free order pack in about 9 ms
  instead of about 58 ms; ordered collages in about 0.4 ms instead of 3.3 ms. Every collage lays
  out exactly as before: a golden file of 4,128 cases pins the output byte for byte to the old
  packer.
- **Changed: `logo-wall` no longer lets a wide mark outweigh a crest 3.6 to 1.** A mark used to
  fill as much of an equal cell as its shape allowed, so a 3:1 wordmark got 3.6× the area of a 1:2
  crest (2.75× in `dense`). Now mosaico's new `rows` strategy gives the marks one shared area,
  kept between the smallest and largest of their old areas, and no mark stands taller than the old
  row: beside a crest, wordmarks come down to a square badge's area and the crest keeps its own,
  2× apart. A wall of one shape draws as before, captioned or not, in `compact` too.
  Rows are balanced and centered (ten marks break 4/3/3, not 4/4/2), in the CLI and the live
  preview alike. The wall now also fits its stage: three rows
  under an eyebrow used to spill past the slide. Three sample marks of other shapes
  (`sample:logo-pinnacle.svg` 4:1, `logo-keystone.svg` 1:1, `logo-spire.svg` 1:2) and a demo deck,
  `examples/logo-wall-equal-weight.md`, show it. `@laticent/mosaico` now has both of the users
  its first npm release waits for; the owner triggers that release.

- **Changed: `lib/base/base.table-reflow.css` is written with native CSS nesting; every shipped stylesheet stays flat.** `tools/build-css.js` lowers it, nesting only, so `dist/lattice-min.css`, `dist/styles-min/` and the VS Code sheets are byte-identical and `dist/lattice.css` carries the same 5,605 rules in the same order. The unminified sheets that carry this file (`dist/lattice.css`, `dist/lattice-default.css`, `dist/slides.css`, `dist/marp-kit/lattice.css` and its `dist/styles/` module) no longer repeat its source comments (`dist/lattice.css` is 11.4 KB smaller); read them in the source. When a nested rule starts with `&` under a parent selector list whose selectors differ in specificity, the build refuses it, because splitting the lowered `:is()` would change the cascade. The ownership gates read a nested source flat, and `node tools/css-rule-equiv.js` checks that two stylesheets carry the same style rules and at-rules.

- **The plugin notes no longer describe the superseded npm contract.** Axis 2 of the plugin-architecture note and §4.10 of the plugin-system note now say what v1 allows an npm plugin to do: render in the locked page only, return a fragment or host-sanitized data, never send code, no `bake`, no Studio or desktop loading. (`engineering/decisions/`)

- The Studio's export panel and the `--editable` reference now say to send the PDF or the plain `.pptx` to an iPhone: iPhone Preview can draw shapes from one slide of an editable PowerPoint file on another, a defect in Apple's viewer that no change to the file stopped.

- In an editable PowerPoint or ODP export, icons, avatars and sparks are stored as SVG beside their picture, so PowerPoint (2016 and later) and LibreOffice draw them sharp at any size. Older readers still show the picture.

- **Playground:** the preview loads only the engine styles a deck uses. A style loader fetches an index and the always-needed modules, scans the slides the engine rendered, and fetches the modules those slides need before the slide paints. A component added in an edit brings its module with it. `?styles=full` loads the whole sheet, as before. The Studio, the landing page and exports are unchanged.
- **Tooling:** `tools/style-loader-gate.mjs` checks the loader on the real Playground, comparing every element's computed style (screen, print, dark) against the whole sheet. `tools/style-needs-audit.mjs` now renders its baseline through the default path and feeds subsets as the minified modules, so a subset takes the same content mask as a full render. The token index drops alternatives another alternative already covers (33 KB to 14 KB gzipped).
- **Playground:** two more opt-in loader modes for comparison, `?styles=floor` (the start-up styles as one prebuilt file) and `?styles=bundle` (also later modules as one request to a composing endpoint). `docs/scripts/style-loader-bench.mjs` compares all four strategies on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2; results are in the decision note.

- **Breaking:** reading text now has one size per venue. List rows, agenda rows, q-and-a
  questions, table cells (every plain markdown table included), glossary definitions,
  list-tabular rows, actors, verdict-grid, pricing features, team-profile notes, roadmap rows
  and the premise ladder all read at `--fs-body`: 16 / 18.4 / 20.8 / 24.0pt at laptop /
  huddle / conference / hall. Before, one deck set them at 13.5, 16 and 21pt at laptop.
  Lists shrink and hold more items: a 14-word list about twice as many at laptop (3 → 7);
  agendas gain one row at laptop and huddle and more than double at conference and hall. Tables and tabular lists grow
  and hold fewer: at 12 words a cell, a table fits 10 rows at laptop (was 11), 8 at huddle
  (was 10) and 3 at hall (was 7), and a glossary fits 4 definitions at huddle (was 9). A
  slide filled to the old table budget can now clip. Each component's "By venue" line and
  `lint:deck`'s `capacity-scale` carry the re-measured numbers.
- Display text keeps its bigger size on purpose: title, divider, quote, big-number,
  closing, topic and stats; the display registers `list principles`, `list-steps ghost`,
  `q-and-a solo`, `image statement` and `citation-card margin` / `pull-quote`; and the one
  lead sentence a slide carries (the split-panel claim, the premise lead, policy-recommendation's
  impact line and quote, inventory's callout band and pull line, and a scene or video
  caption). Code stays one step down at `--fs-body-compact`, because a line of code
  cannot wrap. Support lines stay one step down too: a list item's detail line,
  `content`'s sub-bullets and split-panel `proof` / `capstone` supporting lines read at
  `--fs-body-compact` under a `--fs-body` row.
- `compare-code` sets its code at `--fs-body-compact`, the same size as `code`. It was one
  step smaller, at the chrome size. Each pane holds 17 lines at laptop (was 20) and 47
  columns (was 57); `lint:deck` warns past both.
- Pane budgets re-measured: a glossary in a side pane holds 5 terms (was 12), 3 stacked
  (was 4); a list-tabular side pane holds 6 rows (was 7).
- A `glossary: auto` appendix now pages itself by the glossary's measured budget for the
  deck's venue (9 terms a page at laptop), where it used to render every term on one slide
  and clip past about ten.
- The list-tabular and pricing ceiling specimens say what fits now: six rows, and four
  tiers of five features.
- `team-profile` portraits are a little smaller (6.25cqi, was 7cqi), and its rows sit
  closer together. That keeps six people on one slide now that each note reads at body
  size.
- New: `npm run audit:reading-size` prints each component's reading size at every venue,
  in pt with the role it lands on, and lists the named exceptions apart.
- **Breaking:** every type role now scales with the venue, slide titles included. `h1` and
  `h2` used to hold 48 / 28pt at every venue while the rest grew, so at hall display text
  outranked the title. At hall a title is now 42pt, and a long one wraps: on one 83-slide
  talk, two-line titles went from 5 to 58. Budgets above laptop fall by about one element
  where a title wraps. Laptop is unchanged.
- Code, support lines and chart keys (`--fs-body-compact`) get a venue lift (1.15x at
  conference, 1.14x at hall), so labels never read bigger than the data beside them. The
  code pane at conference / hall holds 9 / 8 lines (was 11 / 10), and fewer columns.
- `h6` takes the label lift, like the label role it matches.
- Reading text set at the chrome size (`--fs-meta`) moves to the reading size too:
  `list-steps timeline` step text and `authority-chain branching` branch lines read at
  `--fs-body`, and a `timeline-list` milestone's description reads one step below its title
  (`--fs-body-compact`). `list-steps timeline` stages now share the row equally instead of
  sitting in fixed 14cqi columns, and `timeline-list`'s line length is set in `em`, so neither
  wraps a word a line at a larger venue. A lone 16-word milestone fits at hall (it clipped).
- The rule holds in every family and finish: portrait `decision`, `compare-prose` and
  `roadmap horizons` read at `--fs-body` (they read at `--fs-message` or `--fs-meta`), as do
  `video` captions and the `sketch` finish's `split-panel`.
- `premise` rows wrap instead of cutting text. At a larger venue the term was ellipsized and
  the framing question ran past its card. A row that fit its track renders as before; a long
  row now wraps to a second line, so a premise slide holds 6 fourteen-word rows at laptop
  (it read 9 while their text was cut), and `lint:deck` warns at 7.
- `pricing` lays four tiers four across without `four`; a bare four-tier slide wrapped its
  fourth tier to a second row and clipped it.
- `inventory` holds five rows at 16:9, not six (`adapt.capacity.wide.hard`); its own gallery
  showed the sixth clipping. Portrait and square keep six.
- `lint:deck` counts `list-tabular`, `glossary`, `premise` and `timeline-list` rows at laptop
  on a 16:9 deck, and warns one past the measured budget (6 rows, 9 terms, 6 fourteen-word
  premise rows, 9 short milestones). Before, it said nothing without a `venue:`, or only past
  `capacity.hard`.
- New venue budgets, re-measured: `kanban` 5 / 4 / 4 / 3 lanes (15 words) where laptop read
  "12+"; `timeline-list` 9 / 8 / 7 / 6 (6 words) and 7 / 6 / 3 / 3 (16 words); `premise`
  6 / 5 / 4 / 2 at 14 words, the true number now that no row is cut.
- `build:check` fails when a component stylesheet sets text in `--fs-message` or
  `--fs-body-compact` without a `SANCTIONED_READING_ROLE` entry naming the exception.
- The Studio's welcome deck fits every venue; three of its slides clipped at hall.
- The line geometry `lint:deck` judges `list`, `cards-grid` and `list-steps` by is
  re-measured at one reading size and scaled titles.

- **Studio shows one side pane at a time.** Coach, Chat, Live, Reader views, Library, Slide settings and Deck settings now share one slot: opening any of them replaces the one showing, so the editor and preview are never squeezed by two docked columns (at 1100px the editor stays on screen instead of folding away). Closing a pane returns to the slide and never reopens an earlier one. When one pane opens another (Chat's "Open Library"), the new pane shows a "‹ Chat" chip back; on a phone the back chevron says "‹ Chat" and returns there. The rail marks the pane you used last, and Esc closes a docked pane when focus is inside it.
- **The open pane is easy to spot on the Studio rail.** Its icon now sits on a solid chip in the theme's heading color with a light label, the same look as the Read/Write/Craft switch. The old pale tint was almost the same tone as the rail. Measured in all 18 palettes in light and dark: the chip stands out from the rail by at least 9.88:1, and its label reads at 9.65:1 or better.
- **Compose's caret stays on its text when a pane opens or closes.** While the editor isn't focused, Compose draws its caret; it used to stay where the text had been when the column changed width, and could show outside the editor. It now moves with the text in the same frame and is clipped to the editor.
- **Every side pane has the same header.** Coach, Chat, Live, Reader views, Library and Slide and Deck settings now share one header on desktop and tablet: the pane's icon, its name, its own buttons, and a collapse button on the edge it folds toward.
