Four panes used to show only a small uppercase label with no way to close them from inside, and Settings showed its scope ("Slide 1 override") where its name belonged; that scope line now sits at the top of the pane. Search works the same everywhere: a search button that opens the field under the header, focused, and Esc closes it. On a phone, panes keep their back chevron and the Library keeps its search at the bottom.
- **The Studio rail's labels are readable on a laptop.** The words under the rail's icons are larger (10px, from 8.5px), in the body text color instead of gray, and the icons are a little smaller and lighter, so the word is no longer lost under the icon. Read/Write/Craft gets slightly larger words and lighter icons for the same reason.
- **Slide and Deck settings each have a Reset button in their header.** It puts back what you changed since you opened the pane (the slide, or the deck's settings), as one step you can undo. It stays off until you change something.

- The engine now names its style-delivery modes. `render(markdown, theme, { styles: 'flat' })`
  returns `flatCss`, the stylesheet for a host that shows slide content outside a slide. `'scoped'` is the
  default. An unknown mode throws instead of falling back. The browser-side `baked` mode is
  one exported function, `bakeSvg`, which the Studio's diagram bake, its PDF/PPTX rasterizer
  and `check:render` now all call.

- **The lessons speak in the same voice as the tours.** All of the "How do I…?" lessons were re-recorded in Gemini `Schedar`, so the Studio has one voice. `tools/record-lesson-voice.mjs` no longer needs the on-device model; it needs `OPEN_ROUTER_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_ALLOW_SPEND=1`.

- **Changed: shipped finishes are packages.** Each preset is now a folder,
  `lib/finishes/<name>/`, holding a manifest (label, blurb, picker swatch, order) and
  a recipe. The finish register, the deck linter's vocabulary, the Studio's finish
  picker and its "Start from preset" recipes are all generated from those folders.
  Adding a finish no longer takes a hand edit in four files. Its CSS is still
  written by hand, and the build fails when a package and its CSS rule don't match.
- **Fixed: "Start from preset" in the Finish faculty reproduces the shipped
  preset.** The Studio's copies of the recipes had drifted: `halo`'s spotlight sat in
  the top-right corner instead of the center, `loom`'s corner glow was on the wrong
  side, and `meridian`'s and `halo`'s line pitch was one pixel off. The recipes now
  come from the packages, measured pixel-equal to the shipped CSS for those three
  (layers only; a ghost glyph is still placed differently).

- **Changed: a Studio asset `.zip` is now the package folder.** Exporting a theme,
  component, finish or motion from the Library writes `<name>/<name>.manifest.json`
  and its files under the names a Lattice repo uses (`<name>.styles.css`,
  `<name>.gallery.md`, `<name>.recipe.json`…), with no `manifest.json` envelope. A
  bundle holds one `<type>/<name>/` folder per asset. Zips exported before this
  change still import.
- **Changed: importing a package trusts its manifest, not its file names.** A folder
  a browser saved as `harbor (1)` imports as `harbor`, and the import message says
  what it renamed or left out. A package that carries JavaScript imports only in the one
  form a code package takes, and runs only after you approve its code.
- **Fixed: a component imported from a zip keeps its manifest.** The old format
  carried only the bucket, so an imported component couldn't be re-saved until its
  function, form, substance and description were filled in again. A package carries
  the whole manifest (and its docs), and exporting it again writes the same files.

- **Changed: the Studio's pane gallery says "Keeps your text" only when the text would read as that component.** A plain list used to keep its text under `contact`, `actors`, `big-number`, `logo-wall` and `flowchart`, which turned "- A point" into a contact card. A component whose own example marks every item (a trailing label, a leading figure, a picture, an arrow) now keeps a pane's text only when the pane uses one of those marks. Otherwise the tile says "Starts with an example", with Undo.
- **Changed: Compose says why it refused a pane edit.** Typing `###` in a titled pane, or deleting a pane's hidden marker, would merge two panes, so Compose refuses it as before. It now shows one short notice naming the reason instead of doing nothing.
- **Changed: `lint:deck` warns on the experimental pane syntax** (`<!-- panes: -->`, `<!-- pane: -->`), where it used to suggest. The alias still renders. It may be retired after the next release, so rewrite it as `<!-- _class: columns -->` / `<!-- _pane: … -->`.
- **Changed: the Studio page is 8.3 KB smaller.** The pane gallery's needs map now arrives with the component catalog the Studio already fetches after the page loads.

- **A radar in a pane now lays out for the pane.** It picks the key's side and a type scale by
  the size its rim labels print, instead of scaling the slide's drawing down into the pane. In a
  35% pane the labels went from 6.3px, under the type floor, to 15.1px, and in a 65% pane from
  11.0px to 14.0px, a title-only radar slide's size. The web gives up at most a quarter of its
  size. A radar slide renders exactly as before. `examples/panes-radar.md`.

- **Changed: the Studio's PDF export is 8-10x faster, with identical pages.** Each
  slide's page image used to go into the PDF through jsPDF's `addImage`, which
  inflates the captured PNG in JavaScript and re-deflates it — about a second a slide.
  The export worker now reads the bitmap's pixels once and compresses them with the
  browser's own `CompressionStream` straight into the PDF. Measured on an 18-page
  deck: Chromium 39.6 s → 4.6 s, Firefox 56.1 s → 5.8 s, WebKit 48.7 s → 6.1 s; a
  56-page deck goes 130.8 s → 14.7 s. Pages are pixel-identical (AE = 0 across 56
  pages), the file is ~5% smaller, and the PDF now reports Lattice as its producer.
  Exporting with comments still puts each note on its own slide — and a comment
  containing a parenthesis or a backslash no longer breaks the notes on that page.
- **Changed: the PDF page-format preference is no longer a speed choice.** "Fast
  (JPEG)" is now "Photographic": with the faster lossless path, PNG measured 4.6 s /
  3.3 MB against JPEG's 4.8 s / 7.4 MB on the same deck — flat color and hard type
  compress better losslessly. JPEG still wins on photo-heavy decks.
- **Fixed: an export that fails on a missing image says so.** When a slide's image or
  `logo:` cannot be fetched, the browser hands back a bare load event with no message,
  and the Share sheet reported it as "PDF failed: unexpected error". It now names the
  cause — a path relative to the deck file resolves for the CLI but not on the web —
  so the fix is findable. Both export lanes report the same thing.

- Every docs page downloads about 6KB (gzip) less JavaScript: the performance overlay's panel now loads only when the overlay is switched on (the Studio's Workspace switch, or `?perf`).

- The home page no longer prefetches the slide preview's 461 KB runtime in its head. Measured on the real CDN, this is neutral for visitors (Lighthouse and the hero's first slide unchanged within noise); the hero fetches the runtime when it needs it.
- The Studio splits each saved deck once per load instead of five times, and the service worker lists its cache once per stored file instead of twice.
- `npm run perf:frame:check` (in `docs/`) now measures the Studio's theme or mode restyle and its full preview rewrite as separate budgets beside the typing budget, and fails if a run stops producing either.

- **Changed: the player refuses a document it cannot read, and its prune no longer passes on an
  empty check.** `assemblePlayer` now throws on a document with no Lattice slides, where it used to
  export a player with zero slides and no warning; the CLI reports "--player assembly failed". The
  prune's computed-style gate refuses when the element it watches is absent, where two empty
  snapshots used to pass. Its view-cycling is now declared data (`LATTICE_CONNECTOR` in
  `lib/export/player-prune.js`), which a reveal.js export used to show that the prune is not
  Lattice-specific. Lattice exports are unchanged.

- The nightly player-contrast sweep now audits the 75 component galleries instead of the 280 `examples/` decks, three at a time (`--concurrency auto`), and on weekdays only the galleries a change since the last green run could have moved (`tools/player-contrast-select.js`; Sunday audits all). A full gallery sweep measured 15 minutes on four cores; the example sweep took 2 hours 2 minutes in CI.
- `test/oracle/player-contrast.json` is re-keyed to the galleries (44 known findings, blessed from scratch). A sweep over a subset of decks no longer reads the baseline rows of decks it did not open as fixed, and `contrast:player:bless` over a subset rewrites only those decks' rows.

- **Changed: on the same browser build, the CLI and the Studio now write the same player file for a
  deck.** Everything matches except the time stamp, the signing hashes and the new `host` field
  (`cli` or `studio`) in the file's record. Both hosts read styles the browser computes, so a Studio
  export made in Safari or Firefox, or in another Chromium version than the CLI's, still differs.
  Measured on 25 example decks (math, diagrams, portrait sizes and a 234-slide 4K deck among them),
  with the Studio preview in light mode: every file matched byte for byte. Two exceptions remain: a
  deck with no `color-mode:` exports dark from the Studio when its preview is dark (the export panel
  defaults to what the preview shows), and a Mermaid fence inside a blockquote or a deeply indented
  list item draws in the Studio but ships as source from the CLI. Each fix:
  - Both hosts compose the deck sheet from the minified builds the docs site serves
    (`dist/lattice-min.css`, `dist/themes/<name>-min.css`). The CLI's player CSS gets shorter;
    the rules don't change, and its PDF pages render pixel-identical on the decks checked.
  - The Studio builds its document from the CLI's own scaffold (`lib/export/export-scaffold.js`),
    so its players carry the page-number rule, the deck's `style:` block, and only the texture
    patterns the page uses.
  - The Studio's Outfit 400/700, Caveat and Shantell 400/700 fonts are now the engine's files.
    Before, it drew those weights from other files, which also changes its live preview and
    image exports. `fonts:check` now holds the vendored files to the engine's bytes.
  - Studio exports record the real engine and player versions and the deck's front-matter
    settings, where they recorded `studio` and nothing.
  - The Studio's bake keeps each slide's inline style as the engine wrote it, without the
    preview's size stamps.
- **A deck with diagrams exported from the Studio as a Webpage is now the same file as the CLI's
  `--player`**, apart from the time stamp, the policy hashes and the new `host` field. The Studio
  draws a Gantt at the width the CLI draws it (784 px, where it used to span the slide) and ships
  each diagram in the CLI's baked shape. That is a trade: for Gantt and flowchart sizing, the Webpage
  export now matches the CLI's file rather than the Studio's own preview and PDF export, which still
  draw at the slide's width.

- **Changed: the Studio's Webpage export now packs a player the way the CLI does.** It glyph-subsets
  the embedded fonts (the `examples/html-player.md` export drops from 1,095,824 to 918,858 bytes),
  and its player script is now the CLI's byte for byte: the Studio's bundle had re-printed the
  inlined transport kernels, so its script and CSP hash differed. Both hosts run one prune
  orchestration (`lib/export/player-prune.js` `prunePlayerHtml`) and one assembler tail
  (`lib/export/player-seal.mjs` `sealPlayer`), and a new integration test asserts the same bytes from
  each on a fixture that fires every pass. Moving the packing into shared modules left the CLI's
  bytes as they were (the other entries for this release change them). The Studio's
  export date is pinned to the epoch, as the CLI's is.

- **Changed:** a component gallery's "When NOT to reach for X" slide now lays its anti-patterns out in columns (`cards-grid three`, or `cards-grid` for two or one) instead of a `cards-stack`, with `claim-hero` so the cards use the height the masthead and footer bands took. Cards balance across slides (4 become 2 + 2) and each column count has a word cap (60 / 100 / 200). The stack left no room: three stacked cards filled 716 of 720 px. The 99 generated slides all render clean at design size.
- The Playground preview frame sets `text-size-adjust: 100%`, so iOS Safari does not enlarge a slide's long text blocks (the cause is a hypothesis; there is no iOS surface to verify it on).
- Trimmed the anti-pattern cards that ran long (`kpi`, `gantt`, `topic`, `state-chart`, `math`); the rest of each component's guidance is unchanged.
- New agent skill `design/skills/component-showcase.md`: the slides a component showcase holds, the measured word budget for each form, and how to check it.

- **Playground:** Deck settings now use the Studio's picker. Every list opens on one `Auto — <what it resolves to>` row, each option shows a preview chip or icon, and a tap outside an open list closes it on iPhone and iPad. Theme, Preset, Finish, the look registers, Size, Venue and Slide splitting all follow this shape.

- The Playground's editor, preview and slide map now move together. Scrolling the preview scrolls the
  editor to that slide and marks it with a faint wash and a gutter bar, `---` fences included, and leaves
  your caret and selection where they were; the next key you press in the editor brings the preview back
  to the caret. Clicking a slide in the preview puts the caret at the end of its title and brings the whole
  slide into view in the editor; clicking inside the marked slide places the caret where you clicked. The
  map no longer has to be open for any of this.
- The preview and the editor have the same thin, quiet scrollbar as the rest of the page instead of the
  browser's default.
- The Playground no longer finds the caret's slide by matching words against the preview, so a repeated
  heading or a slide with no text can no longer land the preview on the wrong slide.
- In the Playground, the editor and the preview now scroll together from either side: scrolling the editor scrolls the preview and marks the same slide there with an accent bar down its left edge. Slides are kept level section for section: the first at the top, the last at the bottom, every slide between centered in both panes. The preview's scrollbar is also the same color as the editor's in every palette and mode.
- The Playground editor now scrolls past its last line, as the Studio editor does, so the end of a deck is not pinned to the bottom edge.
- In the Playground, clicking a slide in the preview, or clicking a line in the editor that sits in another slide, brings that slide to the middle of the preview (the first slide stays at the top and the last at the bottom). A click in the editor leaves the editor where it is, so the text does not move under the pointer; a click on a slide also brings the editor level with it. Typing never re-centers the preview.
- The Playground's two-pane scroll sync is lighter and steadier: the slide highlight no longer redraws the editor's lines at each slide boundary, a slide picked on the map always lands on its slide, and wheeling or dragging either pane no longer jerks back or gets pulled by the other. On a slow page the other pane follows every other frame instead of dropping frames.
- On a phone, switching between Edit and Explore no longer loses your place. Explore opens on the slide your caret is in, and your caret does not move. Going back to Edit leaves the editor exactly as it was (it used to jump to the first line and save a backup of a deck you had not changed); if you clicked a different slide in Explore, the caret goes to the end of that slide's title. The Playground also remembers where your caret was across a reload of the same deck.

- The Playground preview now splits a portrait, square or strip deck the way the PDF export does. The structural auto-split (a slide with several rows becomes a cover, one page per row, and a closing page) used to run only in the CLI export, so a `size: portrait` deck showed one tall page per slide in the Playground and one page per row in its PDF. Both now run the same preprocessor, `lib/engine/structural-split.js`: your gallery deck at portrait renders 43 pages in both. Landscape decks are unchanged, and Studio exports are unchanged. The component tour keeps one step per authored slide when a slide splits.
- The Studio preview now follows the caret through a split slide. At portrait or square, a slide that splits shows the page holding the line you are editing: the cover while you are in the heading, a row's own page while you are in its bullet, the last page for the insight. Blank lines keep the page you were on. A page pill under the preview reads `2.3 · 3 of 5`. The frame still holds one page, and the rail, comments and slide actions stay keyed to authored slides. Swipe, the arrow keys, the wheel and the ‹ › buttons step through a split slide's pages before they move to the next slide, and stepping back enters a split slide on its last page. The slide navigator under the preview keeps the current slide in view: it scrolls to center the slide when the deck moves, and holds still while you page through a split slide.
- A split slide's cover no longer jumps just after it appears in the Playground and the Studio. The live preview now paints the cover in its final layout instead of letting the runtime rearrange it after the first frame.
- A split slide's cover no longer shows a stray page number in the middle of the slide in the Playground and the Studio. The live runtime re-ran the frame lift on the cover the split had already composed, which swept its footer into the body and added a second one. The lift now leaves a section that already carries its footer cell alone, in both the runtime and the render-time kernel. The CLI export is unchanged: identical HTML and all 94 compared PNG pages pixel-identical.

- Switching between Edit and Explore in the Playground no longer flickers. After you edit a slide, the preview used to show the old preview, then a blank, then the deck at slide 1, then jump to your slide; it now shows nothing until the deck is on your slide, and it patches the preview you already have instead of reloading it when the deck has not changed. On a phone with a 60-slide deck and a throttled CPU, the switch takes about 380 ms instead of about 900 ms.

- **The Playground tour is narrated and runs on Vetrina.** It replaces the driver.js spotlight-and-popover tour with the same stops (mode toggle, component picker, walk, Step menu, editor, galleries, deck settings, theme) spoken in the tour voice, which leans toward each control. The Tour button and the first-visit offer open the same sound-test start card as the Studio. `driver.js` is removed from the docs dependencies.
- **Fixed:** the Playground tour's theme step pointed at an element (`#palette`) that never existed, so it was silently skipped. It now points at the Theme select.

- **Breaking:** the Mermaid plugin's kernels moved from `lib/integrations/mermaid/` to
  `lib/plugins/mermaid/shared/` — the init directive, the render worker, portrait reorientation,
  the motion roles and the overlong-label guard. Code that required one through the package's `./lib/*` export by its old
  path must use the new one; no deck changes.
- A shipped plugin may carry an in-tree-only `shared/` folder of modules, and the package
  walk now refuses any other subfolder in a package of a kind that carries no assets (plugin,
  finish, motion), where it used to pass unseen.

- Mermaid's browser half belongs to the Mermaid plugin now. The diagram pass that draws every ` ```mermaid ` fence in the Studio, the Playground and `--fluid` moved out of `lib/runtime/index.js` into `lib/plugins/mermaid/mermaid.hydrate.js`. The runtime drives it through the plugin registry and no longer names Mermaid in its code. Diagrams draw exactly as before.
- The plugin model replaces `render.exec.hydrate: "runtime"` with `"pass"` and adds a `highlight` contribution (LPM 0.4-draft). A pass is a `hydrate.js` that exports `createPass(ctx)`, a document pass the runtime bundles and drives. A `highlight.js` exports a highlight.js grammar, which the host registers under the plugin's code fences. Mermaid's stylesheet (`mermaid.styles.css`) and grammar (`mermaid.highlight.js`) moved into the plugin. The stylesheet now sits in the plugin slot of `dist/lattice.css`, after the math and function-plot sheets; no selector of theirs matches Mermaid's output.
- A CLI bake's context carries only the generic services in `BAKE_SERVICES` (`lib/plugins/host-bake.js`), and `bakeDeck` refuses any other. `diagramTheme` is gone. `paletteReader` replaces it, and Mermaid's bake builds its own theme variables with it. The image-set export's cross-scheme look reads the bake's generic re-bake hook (`state.rebake`) instead of Mermaid's record.

- Mermaid is a plugin now (`lib/plugins/mermaid/`): its ` ```mermaid ` fence is declared by the plugin, and the CLI's diagram bake moved out of `lattice-emulator.js` into the plugin's `mermaid.bake.js`, run by the plugin host before the deck renders. Exports are unchanged: the engine's HTML is byte-identical, and the CLI's HTML for every tracked diagram deck matches `main`.
- The plugin model gains three contribution points (LPM 0.2-draft): `bake` with `render.exec.bake`, a fence rendered `as: "code"`, and `render.exec.hydrate: "runtime"`. `mermaid` is no longer a host-reserved fence name; `lattice packages new plugin mermaid` is refused because the plugin exists.

- The plugin manifest has one "always on" flag, `embedded: true`. The `meta` plugin, which used to be always on through a separate flag the registry derived from `contributes.meta`, is now embedded like `pills`, and a plugin that contributes `meta` must be embedded.
- The Studio's Plugins tab lists every embedded plugin on its one quiet line: "Always on: Slide metadata, Pills". The line used to name only Pills, and `meta` had no mention at all.
- `--disable-plugin=meta` is refused on `lattice export-marp` and on the render CLI (`lattice <deck> -o …`), as `--disable-plugin=pills` already was. It used to be accepted and ignored, so a script that passed it now exits 1. The refusal and the render CLI's help text now name both embedded plugins.
- `lattice` shell completion no longer offers `pills` as a plugin to disable, matching `meta`, which it already left out.

- The editor's `_class:` autocomplete now completes by position, the way a shell completes a command line. The first word offers only components. Every later word offers only what THAT component accepts: its own variants first, then its family modifiers and the modifier groups as labeled sections, with the finishes last. A modifier already on the line drops out, and so does every other member of an exclusive axis once you pick one (`tone-pass` hides `tone-warn`; `us` hides `world` on a map). A dependent such as `at-tl` appears only after `tint-corner`. A bare space after the component opens no menu, so pressing Enter for the default look never picks a variant by accident. The menu opens on the first letter, or on Ctrl-Space. `_class: dark` still works: once the first word names no component, it completes as the default `content` slide.
- A modifier is offered only where the slide part it acts on exists. `big-number` has no heading, so it stops offering `rule-none` and `with-period`. `lifted` appears on the components whose cards actually lift, and after `kpi ops` but not plain `kpi`. The table modifiers appear on a table component, or on any slide whose body contains a table. No manifest lists modifiers: each component's surfaces are derived from its anatomy and corrected by a render proof, `npm run check:modifier-effects`, which renders every component with and without each modifier and records what actually changes.
- Inside each section, the modifiers authors use most in the example decks come first. A group acting on something the slide already contains, such as a table, moves up.
- A component manifest's `excludes` now takes a whole modifier group (`"table"`, `"cards"`, …) or any single universal token, not only `compact` / `accent` / `claim-bleed`.

- **Changed: a PowerPoint export no longer freezes the tab while it builds the
  file.** The whole `.pptx` document — one XML part per slide, the base64 of every
  image, the zip — now assembles in a Web Worker; the main thread only draws. On a
  56-slide deck the longest frame gap drops from 717 ms to 383 ms and the total time
  the tab cannot paint from 10.8 s to 8.4 s, which is the same floor the PDF export
  already sits on. The file is byte-identical but for its creation timestamp.

- The slide map's frame pool now reports its capacity. `PreviewPool` takes `onSettle` and a `maxSlots` a host can lower, the map rail passes the capacity to Veduta's `settle` as the live cap, and the rail's fixed ceiling of 24 is gone (both shipped rails now learn the pool's 28). The Studio rail also prices its focused preview as Veduta's stage; that price does not change what is mounted yet.
- A blank slide (two separators in a row, or a trailing `---`) is now a slide everywhere in the Studio and the Playground map, as the engine renders it and the PDF counts it: it gets a pill, a tile and a number, the slides after it keep theirs, and moving, adding or deleting a slide no longer deletes it from the source.

- `progress-rail:` front-matter key: place the section rail beside the page number (`right`, the default), in the middle of the footer (`center`) or upright on the right edge (`edge`), and draw it as `dots` or a segmented `bar`. One line, one word per axis, e.g. `progress-rail: edge bar`. `off` hides it and `on` draws it in a shorter deck. The Studio completes each word, and the Deck Inspector sets it under Chrome → Section rail. A slide moves its own rail with `_class: progress-rail-edge`.
- The section rail now draws only where it says something: in a deck of three or more sections and fifteen or more slides, on content slides inside a section. A one- or two-section deck, or a short one, no longer shows it unless it says `progress-rail: on`. Past eight sections it draws as a bar.
- Each divider now draws its own section marker (`2/4` and the rail's marks, larger) where the deck's rail sits on the slides after it, so a reader learns what the footer marks mean and where to look for them. An agenda with one item per section shows each item's marks as a legend, and a topic slide with no eyebrow names its section (`02 · Unit economics`). An agenda placed inside a section keeps its footer rail.
- The rail's current mark is in the heading's ink instead of the accent, the same cue the topic track uses for its current topic. The rail sits a fixed column's width from the page number, so the number no longer reads as one more mark.
- A `divider numbered` numeral now counts every divider, so a deck that mixes plain and numbered dividers prints the same section number the rail lights (it printed `01` on a third section).
- `npm run lint:deck` suggests `empty-section` when a divider follows a divider directly, leaving a section with no slides.

- **Adding a chart no longer means remembering nine hand-maintained lists.** Each component
  manifest now declares one `projection` block — how its rendered visual travels off the slide
  (`svg` · `flow` · `spatial` · `placeholder` · `bare` · `none`) and whether its substance is
  data — and `lib/core/projection-catalog.generated.mjs` projects that into the sets the prose
  projection, the image-set export, the Studio's single-chart export, `tools/export-chart-svg.js`
  and the deck scorecard read. Four of the nine literals it replaces held the identical twelve
  names in four different files. None of the nine went red when a chart was missing from it: an
  omission rendered chart fills black, or silently downgraded a vector export to PNG. A
  chart-bucket component that declares no `projection.figure` now fails `build:check`.
- **A deck built on a `journey`, `matrix-grid` or `roadmap` slide now scores Data instead of
  reporting `N/A`.** Those three are chart layouts the scorecard's own roster comment said
  belonged to it, and their absence was drift. This is the only behavior change in the set;
  the other eight projected sets carry exactly the members the lists they replace did.
- **A component with no curated docs family now falls back to its engine bucket** rather than
  to `other`, so a dropped chart appears in the component browser's shape lens with no edit to
  `families.mjs`. Four components that ship today move out of Other as a result: `matrix-grid`
  to Charts & diagrams, `video` and `scene` to Images, `policy-recommendation` to Legal. Six
  others stay in Other — their buckets have no unambiguous shape family, and picking one is an
  editorial call rather than a mechanical one.
- **`esm.run` is now barred by the docs no-CDN gate**, with the Studio's three AI-tier imports
  carrying a per-URL sanction and its reasoning. `esm.run` redirects to `cdn.jsdelivr.net`,
  which that gate already barred, so the host had been reachable through an alias.

- **Fixed: the CI-green beacon named tiers that never ran.** It posted the hardcoded roster
  `lint · unit · integration · docs-build` whatever the verdicts were, so on any path-filtered
  PR it announced skipped tiers as green — observed on #2242 at head `f3ccbbb`, a docs-only
  commit where unit, integration and docs-build were all `skipped`. It now groups the four by
  real `needs.*.result`: `ran:` / `skipped by the path filter:` / `cancelled:`, parenthesised
  so the groups sit below the sentence's own separators. An `UNEXPECTED:` bucket names any
  other value with its raw result, so a tier can never silently vanish from the accounting —
  the beacon no longer depends on its buckets happening to match the Verify gate's allowlist,
  which nothing enforced and which the snapshot code in the same file already contradicts.
  `cancelled` is deliberately not labelled "superseded": a manual cancel produces the same
  value with no supersession, so the step reports the state and leaves the cause to the reader.
  This is the same defect as the CodeQL overstatement the beacon's own comment records, one
  level in: that one overstated the beacon's SCOPE, this one the result INSIDE it.
- **Changed: the `queue-triage` skill warns that a hook's ✔️ is not proof a job ran.**
  `lefthook` prints an identical green tick for a skipped job and a passing one, and the
  pre-push integration tier is opt-in behind `LATTICE_FULL_PUSH=1`. PR #2239 cited it as
  green from a `✔️ integration-tests (0.01 seconds)` line — a ~4.5-minute render tier cannot
  finish in 10ms — and that claim reached a merged PR body and a pre-merge card. Name where
  a gate ran and sanity-check its duration before citing it (HARD RULE #23).

- The pre-merge card now carries `graded by` (a checker agent, never the maker), `raised` (the rounds of the raise loop) and `left behind` (follow-ups the PR adds); `npm run card` refuses a self-graded card and an unraised one below VERY HIGH.
- `npm run evidence` plans the real-surface evidence a diff owes: Playwright Chromium, WebKit and Gecko, the three widths, and which macOS / Windows / iOS Simulator suites to dispatch.
- New `followups.d/` items must say `deferred: large|blocked|off-path — <why>`; `build:check` refuses one without it.

- **Changed: an open PR is rebased only when it conflicts with `main`, never because
  it is behind.** The merge queue already re-tests every PR on top of current `main`
  before it merges, so HARD RULE #16 no longer asks for a rebase before every push.
  The Stop hook (`.claude/hooks/stop-rebase-check.sh`) now warns only when
  `git merge-tree` finds a real conflict, and `engineering/workflow.md` gains a
  §Merge queue — the facts block with the live ruleset values. In the eight days to
  2026-09-28, 67 rebases of PRs that would have merged cleanly cost ~895
  minutes of CI wall-clock time.
- **Added: `npm run queue:precheck`** (`tools/queue-precheck.sh`) — run it before the
  merge ask. It fetches `main`, merges in memory the way GitHub does (GitHub does
  not apply the decision index's `merge=union`), and exits 1 on a conflict, 0 when
  the branch only needs to wait for the queue. The Stop hook now calls it with
  `--no-fetch`.

- Reference PDFs in the Library are now stored as the file's own bytes instead of base64 text, a third smaller on disk, and the Library no longer loads every PDF into memory as a string when it opens. PDFs saved before this change are converted the next time you open the Library. Backups still carry PDFs as text, so a backup restores in any version.

- **Breaking:** the `etching` look is now `etch`, in all three places it was a value: `marks: etch` (and the `marks-etch` slide class), `icon: … etch`, and `spark: … etch`. `etching` is no longer accepted: front matter reports `unknown-marks`, `unknown-icon` or `unknown-spark`, the `marks-etching` and old `chart-finish-etching` slide classes report `unknown-class`, and an inline `^{shield, etching}` or `~{1 2 3, etching}` stops being an icon or a spark and renders as plain code (`icon-literal` / `spark-literal`). There is no alias because the language is not GA. The LFM 1.1 spec table and its conformance fixtures are updated to match. Decks that wrote `etching` need a find-and-replace.

- **Every PDF / PNG / PPTX / HTML export is faster — the render no longer idles after each
  navigation.** The export navigated with `waitUntil: 'networkidle0'`, which waits for the
  network to go quiet *after* everything the page needs has already arrived. Measured through
  the real CLI, that wait cost **0.66–0.80 s per navigation**, and a render performs one
  navigation plus one per auto-split pass plus one for the rails re-render — so the saving
  scales with how much a deck splits: `portrait-roadmap` (1 navigation) **2.14 s → 1.48 s
  (−31%)**, `auto-split` (3) **4.09 s → 1.80 s (−56%)**, `cover-paginate` (4) **5.48 s → 2.27 s
  (−59%)**. The −31% row is the typical one — 265 of the 277 shipped decks drive exactly one
  navigation, 10 drive three and 2 drive four. Sweeping all **277**: **299.4 s → 223.9 s (−25%)**
  wall clock at 4× parallelism (one sweep each way). Per-deck savings are bimodal run to run,
  because the wait this removes was itself bimodal; the corpus figure is the one to quote.
- The change is `waitUntil: 'load'` on the three `page.goto` calls, and it is safe because
  `load` was never the weaker wait for anything this document contains. Serving each resource
  kind from a local server behind a deliberate 1,500 ms delay, `load` **waits** for `<img>`,
  for CSS `background-image: url()`, for `<link rel=stylesheet>` and for the webfont fetch —
  and instrumenting five real sidecars (state-chart, function-plot, images, the 58-slide jargon
  gallery, portrait-roadmap) recorded **zero requests starting after the `load` event**, watched
  a further 2 s past `networkidle0`. Mermaid is pre-rendered in Node and inlined, deck fonts are
  `data:` URIs, and nothing in the page fetches at runtime. Font correctness never rested on the
  navigation wait: it rests on the explicit unbounded force-load that follows each one, which is
  unchanged.
- **Deferred media is now awaited after each navigation.** Chromium holds a below-viewport
  `<img loading="lazy">` past the load event, and a deck can carry raw HTML, so on `load` alone
  such an image never started loading and the export shipped **without it, silently, exit 0**.
  Every image is now decoded, and every `loading="lazy"` frame promoted and awaited, before
  anything is measured or printed — each wait bounded at 10 s, with a warning naming any
  resource that did not settle rather than dropping it in silence.
- **Known behavior change, disclosed rather than fixed: a deck-authored `<script>` that writes
  into the page on a timer may no longer make it into the export.** `networkidle0` incidentally
  granted a few hundred milliseconds of post-load grace, and `load` grants none — measured, a
  400 ms `setTimeout` that landed before now does not. This is not the same case as lazy media:
  a deferred image is markup the browser chose to defer and the export genuinely owes it, whereas
  an author timer is code racing the exporter, where no finite wait is the right answer. The
  engine emits no such scripts and the grace period was never a contract (it varied from ~0.6 s
  to ~1.9 s run to run), but if you relied on it, you will notice. Tracked as #1792, where the
  choice is a bounded settle or an explicit decline plus a warning.
- **Verified against the whole shipped corpus, not a sample.** 277 decks rendered before and
  after: **identical page counts, identical clipped-page sets, identical auto-split decisions —
  0 differences in all three.** Some decks differ in PDF *bytes*, and that channel is
  pre-existing render nondeterminism rather than anything this change caused: **a same-code
  control run differs on 19 decks, which sits inside the 9–28 range of the cross-code
  comparisons.** The count tracks machine contention, not the diff — the busiest sweep produced
  the most churn. The mechanism is Chrome's tagged-PDF accessibility node IDs (26 bytes across
  `/ID`, `/Headers` and the structure-ID name tree), and every state rasterizes
  pixel-identical.
- New opt-in bench tier, `npm run bench -- --cli`, times a whole `lattice-emulator.js` render —
  node boot, browser launch, navigation and PDF encode. Nothing measured that before: every
  other tier drives the engine in-process or calls `page.setContent` in a browser the bench
  itself launched, so a change to the CLI's navigation strategy moved no number in the file at
  all (HARD RULE #19(c)). Its three decks are chosen for navigation count (1, 3 and 4) and are
  deliberately mermaid-free so `mmdc` cannot swamp the signal. Its `slides` column is the PDF
  page count, so the row doubles as a pagination guard that fails on any machine.
- **Fixed:** three code comments that described the render inaccurately. Two credited
  `waitUntil: networkidle0` with covering the function-plot and state-chart `DOMContentLoaded`
  bootstraps — true, but stronger than the facts, since `DOMContentLoaded` precedes `load`
  anyway. A third said `measureOverflow()` "already force-loads fonts first, via the same
  `lib/core/font-settle.js` helper"; it does not — `measureOverflow` touches `document.fonts`
  nowhere, and the force-load lives in its *callers* as an inline unbounded `page.evaluate` that
  is deliberately not on the shared helper. A new call site added on the strength of that
  comment would have silently measured fallback metrics.

- **The committed demo and gallery PDFs are now written by the shared PDF writer.** Every
  `examples/*.pdf`, gallery PDF and golden was re-rendered in one pass, so the tree no longer
  mixes Chrome-printed and writer-made PDFs, and no later PR's golden diff reports the writer
  switch as its own drift. Page counts are unchanged (4963 pages over 429 files), and the
  set is 19% smaller (136.9 MB to 111.1 MB).
- **The CLI's PDF photo uses Chrome's normal PNG encoder again.** It had used the fast one, which
  made a flat deck's PDF about 2x larger. Tests still use the fast encoder (`node --test`, or
  `LATTICE_PDF_PHOTO_FAST=1`); the pixels are identical either way.

- **matrix-2x2 stacks in a narrow box and keeps each quadrant's place.** Below 24em of the content area the 2×2 becomes one column instead of squeezing each quadrant to a word per line, and every stacked card carries a small drawn 2×2 mark with its own cell filled. A portrait or mobile deck's single column carries the same mark. 16:9 slides are unchanged.
- **redline stacks in a narrow pane.** A `.three-col` redline below 40em of its box, or a `.split` one below 32em, stacks old, new and the rationale in reading order instead of squeezing each column to a word per line. On a slide, a stack that would overflow is held as the grid. Full-width slides are unchanged.
- **`lint:deck` no longer warns `pane-insight` on a paned redline.** It counted a redline's old and new blockquotes as Key Insights, though the pane carve keeps them in the pane; it now reads the same coda catalog the carve does.
- **The fluid view holds a narrow layout that would overflow the phone.** The runtime ran its fit check once, on the deck's authored box; the fluid viewer then narrowed each slide to the phone, where a pane's table could switch to cards that overflowed. It now re-judges a slide whenever its box changes size, and a slide rotated or widened back to landscape drops the portrait stamp and type scale it used to keep.
- **Charts no longer vanish in a continuous host.** radar, map, quadrant, word-cloud, piechart and hub-spoke fill a size container, which lends no height when the slide grows to its content; their chart body now takes a 16:10 box there. Slides, PDFs and every other paged output are unchanged.

- Print, PDF, PowerPoint and image exports of decks with charts are faster and no longer freeze the page for up to 3 s. Exports used to re-style every chart before photographing each slide, a workaround the current slide camera no longer needs. In WebKit, the engine behind every iPhone browser, a nine-heatmap deck prints in 57.6 s instead of 68.6 s and the 28-chart test deck's PDF takes 19 s instead of 38 s (measured in Playwright's WebKit, not on a device), and in Chromium the longest freeze during a PDF or PowerPoint export drops from about 3 s to under 1 s. Chart edges in the exported pictures are anti-aliased slightly differently; colors, sizes and layout are unchanged. The standalone chart `.svg` files in the Images (.zip) export now declare their own size (for example 539 × 225) instead of the slide's capture size, so a chart fills its file's frame instead of floating small in a wide empty box, as the CLI's and the single-chart SVG export already did.

- **The `sketch` finish now draws its lines with rough.js instead of a tiled CSS wave.** Table
  frames and row rules, the `list-tabular` ledger, `list.principles` rules, the `hr` divider, an
  agenda's active row, and the masthead↔stage divider are all real seeded rough.js strokes,
  painted into one SVG overlay per slide. The old `--sketch-wave` was a single sine path tiled at
  140px — mathematically periodic, and applied per `td`, so a table rule visibly re-phased at
  every column seam while the frame around it stayed a smooth rounded rectangle. Strokes are
  seeded from each structure's key, so two renders of a deck are byte-identical.
- **Breaking (visual): the `sketch` heading underline is retired.** `section.sketch h2` no longer
  draws its own bent `border-bottom`. Every masthead slide carried two rules — that hand-drawn
  one under the words, and the machine-straight `1px solid var(--border)` masthead↔stage hairline
  below it. The band's rule is the structural one, so it is the one that now gets the hand, drawn
  in the sketch ink at a little over half strength. `rule-none` still draws nothing; `rule-short`
  and `rule-accent` get a short drawn segment where they used to get a perfectly straight one.
- **Table frames under `sketch` lost their asymmetric `border-radius` and offset `box-shadow`.**
  At table scale the radius read as a smooth rounded rectangle and the shadow as a material drop
  shadow. rough.js draws the frame now; layering the old fakes under it read as neither. Card,
  blockquote and bordered-row boxes are unchanged and convert in a follow-up.
- **The `thead` `--spectrum-structure` strip is replaced by ink on `sketch` tables.** A hand-ruled
  table now uses one pen throughout; the header row stays distinct through its label-voice type.
- **No-script documents keep the old tiled wave.** The ink is painted after layout settles, so a
  raw `.html` sidecar opened without the runtime falls back to the previous rules rather than
  showing none. PDF, PNG, PPTX and `--player` exports all carry the ink.
- **The ink stroke is validated as a color before it reaches the SVG.** `--rough-ink-stroke` is
  read out of the cascade, which a deck author's own `<style>` participates in, and an SVG
  `stroke` accepts `url(…)` — so an authored `url(https://…)` reached the attribute and the
  browser fetched it, once per opened copy of an export. The underlying capability is not new
  (plain `background-image: url(…)` in author CSS does the same, and `sanitize-style-text.mjs`
  states that CSS-as-CSS fetching is intended), but this path must not be a second route to it.
  A non-color value now falls back to `currentColor`, so a hostile deck loses the ink's color
  rather than its rules.

- The docs build's per-route byte budget now has a soft target and a ceiling per route. Between the two the build passes and warns on the CI summary page; past the ceiling it fails. `docs/route-budget.json` changes only through `npm run route-budget:rebaseline` (in `docs/`), which records each change in `docs/route-budget.history.md`; raising a number needs the owner's OK.
- Each PR that runs the docs build may add up to 2KB of gzipped startup JavaScript to a route, measured against `main` in CI, while the route stays at or under its soft target. Every byte above soft is declared per route (`studio: +N` plus why) in the PR's own file under `docs/route-budget.d/`.
- The route budget now counts the code a page's scripts import statically, not only the scripts named in its HTML. Home, components and getting-started read 262KB, 167KB and 150KB gzipped instead of 80KB, 81KB and 77KB; their budgets were reset to match.

- **The player runtime and the engine bundle no longer carry the web-reference scanner.** `lattice-runtime-min.js` (the script every exported deck loads) bundled all of `remote-ref.js` for one constant, the blocked-image placeholder, and `sampleName`/`assetName`. Those now come from `media-sources.js`, the leaf the scanner already depended on. Measured with the build's own esbuild settings (`tools/build-runtime.js` minified options) against the merge base: the minified runtime is about 7 to 9 KB gzipped smaller, and about 8 KB gzipped smaller than the same runtime with the scanner's new checks.

- **Breaking:** Lattice's sample art moved to one folder, `lib/samples/`, and the files were renamed by kind: `photo-wide.svg`, `portrait-ada.svg`, `logo-acme.svg`, `logo-acme-mark.svg` and `video-poster.svg`. A deck that pointed into the old homes, such as `../lib/components/inventory/team-profile/ada.svg` or `lib/base/_logo/acme-logo.svg`, should now name the picture as `sample:portrait-ada.svg`. A deck saved in the Studio under an old sample name (`ada.svg`, `logo-wall/acme.svg`) keeps working: the site still serves those names.
- Adds `sample:<name>`, which names a picture in `lib/samples/`. The CLI reads it from the package wherever the deck sits, and its PDF, HTML, player and Export-to-Marp outputs carry it. The Playground, the Studio and the component pages load the copy the site serves, and the Studio's PDF, PNG, PPTX and player exports carry it too. It works in an image slide, a background, a prose image, a `logo-wall` mark, a `team-profile` portrait, a `video` poster and a deck `logo:`. The Studio's in-browser Export to Marp does not carry it yet, as it carries no local picture today.
- Fixes sample portraits and logos showing as hatched "web image" placeholders in the Studio and on the component pages. The preview counted the site's own `samples/` folder as a third-party site. A third-party picture is still refused or embedded exactly as before, and an exported file still never fetches anything, from the site or anywhere else.
- Fixes `logo-wall` marks coming out as stripes in the Studio's HTML player export. The player now embeds each mark's picture.
- Fixes the Studio's **Add slide** templates for `logo-wall` and `team-profile`, which pointed at `logo-1.svg` … `logo-6.svg` and `portrait.jpg`. None of those files existed, so every inserted slide showed broken images. The templates now show real sample logos and portraits.
- Fixes a `video` poster and a non-image `![bg]` with a relative path not loading in the website's previews. Both now resolve the way every other picture does.

- **Breaking:** the `lib/` modules that handle a slide's `say:` line no longer call it a caption. For code that deep-imports `@laticent/lattice/lib/*`: `lib/core/resolve-captions.mjs` is now `lib/core/resolve-narration.mjs`, its `frontMatterCaptions` is `frontMatterSayMap`, and `parseNarrationFrontMatter()` returns the map as `.say` instead of `.captions`. In `lib/authoring/notes-core.js`, `captionFromHtml` is `sayLineFromHtml`, `extractSlideCaptions` is `extractSlideSayLines`, `isCaptionComment` is `isSayComment`, `stripCaptionsFromSource` is `stripSayFromSource`, `stripCaptionsFrontMatter` is `stripSayFrontMatter`, `stripChannelsFromSource`'s `captions` option is `say` (the old key throws, so a privacy strip never silently skips the say text), and `slideNoteRecord` returns `say` instead of `caption`. `mergeNarration` (`lib/core/read-along-build.js`) takes `{ sayLines, fmSayMap }` and throws a `TypeError` that names the new keys when it is passed `captions` or `fmCaptions`, so an old call fails at once instead of quietly dropping every override. The rendered output does not change.
- Three CLI messages now say "say" for the spoken line: the `--captions` log line when a split remaps the front-matter `say:` map, the "nothing to narrate" message, and the warning when the Markdown attached to a PDF could not have a note or say comment removed.

- **Breaking:** a slide's spoken line is now `<!-- say: … -->`, and the front-matter map is `say:` (slide number → line). `<!-- caption: … -->` and `captions:` are retired: the engine no longer reads them, `lint:deck` reports them as a `caption-key-retired` error, and the render warns. Rename the key; the value keeps its shape. The key is lowercase only: `<!-- Say: … -->` stays a private speaker note, so a presenter's "Say: …" note-to-self is never published, and `lint:deck` warns (`say-key-case`) in case it was meant to be spoken. "Caption" now means only visible text: the on-screen band, the `.vtt` sidecar and figure captions.
- **Breaking:** `--strip-captions` is now `--strip-say`. The old flag exits with an error that names the new one. `--captions` (the `.vtt` sidecar) is unchanged. `--strip-say` also removes the retired `<!-- caption: … -->` comments (in any case, as `--strip-captions` did, so a note that starts with `Caption:` goes too) and a top-level `captions:` map from every shipped copy, and prints a line when it does.
- The Studio's per-slide field is now **Say — what this slide says aloud**, and writes `<!-- say: … -->`. Its help text no longer claims an empty field falls back to the speaker note; it falls back to the generated narration.

- **Changed: `npm run parser:bakeoff:segno` now times the inline dispatcher Lattice ships.**
  The arm compared Segno against the retired pre-Segno kernel and its own copy of the
  dispatcher, so no figure said how fast `lib/core/inline-code-directives.js` is. Every row now
  reports the shipped dispatcher's time per span as well, including the 386 spans written in
  Segno's notation, and the Segno README's § Speed quotes the 2026-10-07 run. The shipped path
  costs 136 ns on ordinary code, against 31 ns for the retired kernel. That gap is recorded as
  a followup.

- `npm run parser:bakeoff:languages:browsers` times Segno's generated CSS, HTML and Markdown
  parsers in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, before and after a generator change. The 2026-10-07
  generator changes made all three faster in every engine (Firefox 1.24x–1.56x, WebKit
  1.21x–1.55x).
- `npm run parser:bakeoff:segno` no longer counts spans written in Segno's notation as ordinary
  code. The retired kernel passes those through in about 30 ns while Segno reads them as records,
  which inflated the ordinary-code row from about 1.9x to 4.5x. They now have a row of their own.
- Segno tests a character set with more than 16 ranges above ASCII by binary search, in both
  `compile()` and `generate()`. A 32k-range set read 256k characters in 11.4 s; it now takes
  about 6 ms. No shipped parser changes.
- Checking or generating a Segno grammar that reuses a piece at every level no longer takes
  2^depth time. At depth 22, `compile()` went from 415 ms to 5 ms and `generate()` from 921 ms to 3 ms.

- **A pill reads about a third faster, and so does every other plain `{…}` span.** Segno binds a `{…}` span of bare words and `name=value` items (a pill, a chart point, a state) straight from the parser's tree, without building an object per item. A span it cannot bind that way (a quote, a nested record or list, an unknown word, any error) takes the full path, which alone words a diagnostic, so errors read as before. The slot's bind alone went from about 355 ns to 260 ns on the shipped decks' pills, and the dispatcher's decision for a pill from about 480 ns to about 370 ns (same machine, interleaved runs; `npm run parser:bakeoff:segno`). A unit test holds the two paths equal on every one-to-three-item span built from a 37-item pool, in four slots.
- **Types Segno builds are marked as its own.** A type of your own (a `read` you wrote, or a copy of a built-in with a new `read`) keeps the full bind, because its `read` may parse a span of its own and overwrite the buffer the fast read walks. `isBuiltIn(type)` is exported from `types.ts` for that check; it is not part of the published API.
- `isDirective` no longer tests the tag set for a span that opens with `{`, `isName` replaces a regular expression, and the icons plugin's `canonical` skips `trim().toLowerCase()` for a name that is already spelled as the set spells it. The pill reader keeps the canonical icon it found in the decision and reuses it to build the result, which asked the icons service a second time before.

- Segno's generated parsers read whole CSS, HTML and Markdown files about 1.3x–2x faster (CSS
  112 → 178 MB/s, HTML 117 → 156, Markdown 101 → 207), ahead of postcss's, css-tree's, parse5's
  and markdown-it's tokenizer layers on Lattice's own files. Trees and errors are unchanged.
  `npm run parser:bakeoff:languages` now also races those tokenizers like for like.

- **Segno's generated parsers finish a run over "anything but 1-3 characters" with a cached native search.** A rule such as `noneOf('|\n')` now asks `indexOf` for each stop character and reuses the answer until the cursor passes it, instead of looping per character. The trees are identical; the generated line tokenizer in the deck-pipeline bake-off reads 460 MB/s, up from 315 MB/s on the same machine. `list-text.generated.js` regenerates with the new helpers; the two notation parsers have no such run and change by one blank line.

- **Segno's generated `parse()` allocates nothing per successful call.** It reuses one result object (its tree was already valid only until the next parse, because the buffer is shared) and skips the rule-table lookup for the grammar's default rule. A pill's grammar stage went from about 270 ns to about 225 ns, and the shipped decision for a pill from about 500 ns to about 480 ns (same machine, interleaved runs of `npm run parser:bakeoff:segno`). A successful `parse()` now returns the SAME result object every time, so a caller that kept results from two parses, or wrote to one, sees the later parse's values; read `tree.buf` and `tree.top` before parsing again (the buffer was always shared). Trees and errors are unchanged; the 305 Segno tests and `inline-code-table.test.js` pass. The generated parsers in `lib/core` (`flowchart-row`, `list-text`) pick the change up too.
- **`npm run parser:bakeoff:segno` times a row's columns alternately.** It used to time the retired kernel, the arm's copy and the shipped dispatcher one after another, with one timer function whose call site the first column warmed. Each column now gets a timer of its own and the columns alternate round by round. On one quiet machine both versions read the every-span ratio at 1.2x to 1.4x (the 1.5x bar is met); the earlier 1.3x to 1.7x readings came from a busy sandbox, so the ratio was noise-bound rather than pill-bound.

- **Breaking: every inline-code notation now reads through Segno, one notation with one set of rules.** A value is a record in braces, its items separated by commas, in any order; a named item is `name=value`; a value holding a comma or `=` is quoted with `"…"`. Every deck and doc in this repo is rewritten; there is no migration tool. A deck still in an old spelling renders an old pill or spark as plain code, and an old CHART spelling is simply not read: the chart draws without that value (a quadrant point at the origin, a journey step at mood 3, a flowchart or state-chart style as part of the name), and `lint:deck` does not flag it. The changes, old → new:
  - Pill: `` `{BETA}:tag:c4` `` → `` `{BETA, tag, c4}` ``. Spark: `` `~{12 14 17}:bar:lg` `` → `` `~{12 14 17, bar, lg}` ``.
  - Quadrant and scatter point: `` `3, 70` `` (quadrant) and `` `$4.2M` `62%` `140` `` (scatter) → one record, `` `{3, 70}` ``, `` `{$4.2M, 62%, size=140}` ``.
  - Gantt: the eyebrow window and `today Q3` pills are retired; the axis line `` `[{Timeline, 2026 Q1..2026 Q4, today=Q3}]` `` is the one form. A dependency is `` `after=Design` `` (`after=[Design, Build]` for two), not `` `after: Design` ``.
  - Radar: the scale eyebrow `` `Scale · 0–100` `` → the axis line `` `[{Scale, 0..100}]` ``, which the chart reads and takes off the slide (the ring ticks already print the scale).
  - Journey: `` `@Customer` `:4` `+120` `` → one step record, `` `{who=Customer, mood=4, volume=120}` ``; `` `@Customer` `` alone still names the actor.
  - Heatmap cell note: `` `# why` `` → `` `note=why` ``.
  - Flowchart and state-chart style: `` `#api:diamond:c2` `` → `` `{#api, diamond, c2}` ``, and one word stands alone (`` `dashed` ``, not `` `:dashed` ``); a channel color is `` `fill=c3` ``, not `fill-c3`; the key drops its colons, `` `{dotted, Informal}` ``. The state chart reads its rows with the flowchart's grammar, so `start` and `end` join the same record: `` `{start, c1}` ``.
  - Waterfall: the `total` / `step` marker may now come before or after the value.
- **One number reader for every chart.** Piechart, funnel, map, progress, radar and word-cloud read values the way the cartesian charts do, so `1,25M` is 1.25M everywhere and `($1.2M)` is negative everywhere.
- **State roles (`Start`, `END`) and QR keys now fold case**, as status words and kanban sizes already did; all of them read through Segno's enum type.
- **Fixed:** a journey actor named `R&D` printed as `R&amp;D` (the name was escaped twice).
- **Known limit:** a number written with a thousands comma cannot sit inside a record, because the comma separates items and a quoted value is text. Write `{12000, 62%}`, not `{12,000, 62%}`.

- **A session is archived only after four checks.** Its work is done; every leftover item is logged durably (a `followups.d/` file, an open issue or a desk-tracked PR comment, never only a chat brief); it reports a clean tree with nothing unpushed; and no desk or scheduled task depends on it. The command center proposes the sessions that pass, names the failing check for each one that stays, and archives on the owner's `go`. Contract: `engineering/workflow.md` §Desks, "When a session can be archived"; `/fleet` step 3.

- **A session's work now lands as one PR with a commit per item, and several green PRs are
  authorized in one round.** Measured over the fortnight to 2026-08-23: 50 merges, 48 of
  them on two days — 25 on the 17th, 23 on the 18th. Each cost a human authorization, and
  each was a drift event for every other open PR, which is the same argument §Merging
  already makes for landing a migration as one squash. The default is now one PR per line of
  work; urgent, risky, different-swimlane, and gallery-graduation work still get their own.
  HARD RULE #17's independence test is clarified as *permission* to split, not an obligation
  to — taking it every time is what turned one night into 25 approvals. A batched PR is the
  sanctioned `rebase-and-merge` case, since one curated commit per item keeps per-item revert
  granularity on `main` at the cost of a single merge event. The merge gate itself is
  unchanged: a human still authorizes every merge, now in one round rather than N pings.
  (`engineering/workflow.md`)

- Studio Settings: every picker in the deck and slide panels now opens with one `Auto — <what it resolves to>` row, marked with the Auto link icon, and never lists that value a second time. Before, heads read "(default)", "Default — tab", "Finish's own", "Theme default" or just the default value with no Auto row. On the deck that value is the preset's or the engine's default; on a slide it is the deck's. Picking the Auto row removes the setting.
- Studio Settings: Color mode, Size and Venue are now the same picker as the rest of the panel, with an Auto row and icons. Venue keeps its "who it is for" line under each room.
- Studio Settings: the bar, rule, alignment, card-row, corner and fit previews drew as solid squares. The preview chip wrote an empty `background-size`, and that wiped the sizing out of every swatch that uses a `var()` in its background. Each chip now draws its real shape again.
- Studio Settings: options that pick a position, an alignment, a spacing or a fit action now show an icon from the site's icon set, sized and colored to match the color swatches. Bar and card-rail placement, headline and tag-text alignment, card rows, corners, fit, slide splitting, tag size, venue, logo position and scope, and the image card's placement and density all have one.
- Studio Settings: options for Lattice's own looks show a small drawing of the result: every stamp shape and tone shape, card tag color and placement, slide size as its aspect ratio, logo color and size, delivery, a level meter for motion speed and pace, and the image card's ink, size and shape. The heading-rule chips draw a heading with its rule beneath, the eyebrow Arrow chip draws a real chevron, Brand bar None draws the hairline it leaves, and the Claim and Sketch chips are easier to see.
- Studio Settings: the card rail's "follow the bar" value reads "Match bar", and the deck's stamp and tone shape rows record their change under their own names, so a live session can point at them.
- Studio and site menus: on iPhone and iPad, a tap outside an open picker or menu now closes it. Before, the list stayed open, and tapping another picker opened a second list on top of the first. Every dropdown built on the shared select and menu gets the fix, and a tap outside now only closes the list instead of also pressing whatever was underneath. At phone width, a list wider than its picker no longer runs off the right edge of the screen.
- Studio: Debug overlay and the Audit panel's "Style judged as" are now the same picker as the rest of Settings, with an Auto row and icons. Debug overlay was a hand-built menu, and the profile picker was a browser `<select>`.
- Engine: six per-slide restore tokens return one slide to a register's default inside a deck that set another value: `spectrum-on`, `spectrum-edge-top`, `spectrum-card-edge-left`, `rule-auto`, `eyebrow-plain` and `head-auto`. A slide in a `spectrum-edge: left` deck can now write `_class: spectrum-edge-top` to put its bar back on top, which no spelling allowed before. The Studio's slide pickers list each default as an ordinary choice and write the token. `lint:deck` warns (`conflicting-variants`) when a slide carries two tokens from one of these axes, such as `spectrum-on spectrum-solid`, because a restore token draws nothing and always loses to its rival.

- **Changed: the Studio's settings panels give a third of their height back to the
  settings.** The first control sat 414px down a 390×844 phone — half the screen was
  chrome. It now sits at 297px, and 231px in the docked desktop panel (was 352px).
  Nothing moved more than one tap away. The scope banner is one line instead of four
  stacked restatements of the same fact: its icon moved to the Slide/Deck switch (the
  same two icons the desktop activity bar already used), its `Deck-wide` badge went
  because the title beside it said so, and the title and its sentence merged. The search
  and view controls moved onto that line from a row of their own. The section strip shows
  the two most-reached sections as pills and keeps the full list behind a chevron, which
  ends a two-row wrap that six pills could never avoid in a 231px column — the chevron
  wears the active section's name whenever it is not one of the pills.

- **The Studio settings panels are regrouped, and both scopes now use one vocabulary.**
  The deck tab strip is ordered by reach — Look · Chrome · General · Accent · Motion ·
  Speech — with a new **General** tab for the deck's name, language and structure, which
  also absorbs the Developer aids. The deck's **Marks** tab is renamed **Chrome**, matching
  what the slide panel has always called the same four controls; the slide panel's
  **Status** and **Decoration** tabs merge into **Marks**, split by whether a mark carries
  meaning. Low-traffic rows in each tab move behind a **More** disclosure.
- **Row descriptions are one clause.** The paragraph each row used to carry moved behind
  its ⓘ — nothing was deleted.
- **Every settings control is the same width, aligned in one column.** Each row is now
  `label | control` at an even split with the help line beneath, so dropdowns, text fields
  and segmented controls all start at the same point and share one right edge instead of
  each sizing to its own content. Switches stay right-aligned; a control too wide for its
  half drops to its own line rather than overflowing a narrow panel.
- **"Auto" always names what it resolves to** — `Auto — Cuoio`, `Auto — English`,
  `Auto — hairline`. Three different shapes were in play (a bare `Auto`, `Auto — value`,
  and a bare value), picked by a rule no reader could see.
- **Narrow settings panels stack.** Below ~320px of panel width the label, control and help
  line become three rows so the control keeps its full width instead of truncating its own
  value. It measures the panel, not the window — the docked Inspector is resizable at any
  screen size.
- **The settings panels say "Configure", not "Editing", and speak to you directly.** You edit
  a deck's content in the editor; the panel configures it, and calling both "editing" made
  them read as the same act. The scope banners now read *Configure the whole deck* / *Configure
  slide N*, with active lines beneath, and the passive descriptions across both scopes ("is
  inherited from the deck", "the export is unchanged") now name who does what.
- **"Auto" values are capitalized**, so they read as the value the control is set to rather than
  a stray sentence fragment beside "Rainbow" and "Theme default".

- The Inspector's search field draws **one** trailing ✕, not two: it clears the text while
  there is text and closes the field once there is not. The two jobs were two buttons side
  by side — a 24px "Clear search" 19px from a 28px "Close search", same glyph, on a 293px
  phone row — and the docked desktop panel drew a third within 100px of the same 296px,
  because the panel's own collapse used the ✕ too. That one is now a panel-collapse mark,
  matching the preview pane's. Escape still leaves from either state.
- While the search field is open, the scope banner's sentence steps aside instead of
  truncating to "Set it …", so the row's words are either whole or absent, never a stub.
- Inspector search reaches a control through the word an author actually types. It stems
  ("numbers" finds "Hide page number", "captions" finds Caption), it carries a small shared
  synonym table ("font" finds Type scale, "pagination" finds the slide's page-number row,
  "margin" finds Claim), and it repairs a typo ("numbre", "capiton", "algnment"). No
  ranking: a filter draws a row or it does not, so precision-first substring matching still
  runs first. Per-row `find=` synonyms are unchanged.
- Searching "color" in the deck panel returned eleven rows — the whole Accent section, nine
  of them, plus Theme and Color mode — because that section listed a keyword its own Brand
  bar row already carries. It now returns the two rows that are about color.
- The Inspector's section strip now draws as many pills as the panel can hold instead of a
  fixed two, and the section you are in is one of them wherever there is room for a pill at
  all. A 390px phone gains one or two; the docked desktop panel keeps two, but one of them is
  now where you are. When even one pill will not fit — a long section name in the slide
  panel — the chevron wears that section's name instead of "More", so the strip still answers
  "where am I". Dragging the panel re-fits it live, on one line. The chevron still holds the
  whole list.
- Clearing the Inspector's search field now leaves the caret in the field, so the next word
  can be typed straight away (and a phone keyboard does not drop).

- **The Studio's Share → PDF and the CLI's PDF export now share one writer** (`lib/core/pdf-compose`). Each slide's background is one photo; words, charts, images and links go on top as real text in the deck's fonts, vector shapes, original images and clickable links, tagged for screen readers with the title and language. It draws several times faster in iOS Preview and Acrobat (a 9-slide finish deck: 13.1 s → 1.45 s in poppler, 335 KB → 237 KB). `--chrome-pdf` prints with Chrome as before; in the Studio, Workspace › General › PDF export › Photo per page keeps one picture per slide. Links to another slide (`#3`) become page jumps, and tabular figures stay tabular.
- **`color-mode: print` no longer draws a finish**, on screen or in any export: the black-and-white handout carries no glow, texture or margin bar.
- **Studio exports keep a slide's tone rail and finish frame** (`tone-warn`, `tone-fail` …): the PDF, PNG and PPTX exports dropped them, while the CLI kept them.
- **Card borders and rules stay sharp on a big screen**: the PDF writer draws solid borders as vectors instead of leaving them in the background photo.

- **Breaking:** the state markers now have six answers with one meaning each, in every layout: `[x]` yes, `[-]` partly, `[!]` no, `[?]` unknown, `[ ]` open, `[/]` does not apply. Three layouts read `[ ]` their own way before, and a deck written against the old reading changes on render:
  - **verdict-grid:** `[ ]` was the red cross for "not met". It is now the open ring, "not assessed". Write `[!]` for a criterion that was not met.
  - **pricing:** `[ ]` was the red cross for "missing". It is now the open ring, "coming". Write `[!]` for a feature the tier lacks, or `[/]` for "not on this plan".
  - **obligation-matrix:** `[ ]` was "exempt". It is now "undetermined". Write `[/]` for an exempt regime; the key names it "Exempt". `[!]` is "Not required".

  Three things catch an old deck. Rendering one prints a warning naming each affected slide. `lint:deck` flags the same slides with the marker to use. The new `npm run lint:deck -- --fix <deck>` rewrites every verdict-grid and pricing `[ ]` to `[!]`, which draws exactly what the deck drew before. Like any linter's `--fix`, it applies every machine fix; it names each one by rule and slide, and keeps the file's line endings and BOM. It rewrites only the slide each warning names, even when heading splits put several slides between two `---` lines. It leaves obligation-matrix alone, because an old `[ ]` there could mean exempt, not required or undetermined, and only the author knows which. None of them fires on a slide that already uses `[!]` or `[?]`, or on a label set that names `[ ]`. Every shipped deck and gallery is migrated.
- Added `[!]` (no), which draws the red cross in every layout that draws marks: checklist, pricing, obligation-matrix, `state-cells` tables, inline marks, verdict-grid and roadmap (as "missed").
- Added `[?]` (unknown): a hollow ring with a drawn question mark, for an answer somebody looked for and could not settle. It sits beside `[ ]` (open, nothing inside the ring). In roadmap it reads "uncertain".
- `pricing` draws `[ ]` as the open ring instead of a red cross. It used to borrow verdict-grid's reading, so a legend written in inline marks under a pricing slide disagreed with the cards above it.
- `state-cells` tables draw the `[ ]` ring in the neutral `--muted-mark` gray, matching every other open ring. It had kept `--text-label`, which is accent-colored.
- `roadmap status` cells no longer show a faint copy of the state mark beside the text. The corner token was the only mark meant to show.
- Speech, read-along and prose projection name each answer in the layout's own words (pricing says "coming" for `[ ]`, "missing" for `[!]`). A `state-cells` table, which narrated nothing before, speaks the universal words. An inline mark is spoken by its label instead of being skipped.
- A roadmap label set now renames the cells as well as the key. A `status` cell said "Shipped" beside a key the author had renamed "Live".
- Under `heat`, a roadmap's missed work takes the relief color like every other `[!]`, so it no longer shares the alarm red with shipped work. The `horizons` cards now follow `heat` at all, which they ignored before, and so do the roadmap and obligation-matrix keys: an obligation-matrix `heat` key showed "Applies" in green under a grid of red Applies cells.
- The `checks-outline` and `checks-tonal` variants draw the two open answers as one ring, not a double ring.
- A verdict-grid, pricing or `state-cells` label with inline HTML (`<em>`, `<b>`) keeps its text on both render paths.
- The docs-site Compose table picker offers all six markers, and the table menu holds all six too. On a narrow editor pane the inline buttons move into that menu, so the picker no longer covers the slide's Collapse and Delete buttons.
- The linter's advice for a typed ✗, ✕ or ❌ now says `[!]` instead of `[ ]`, and it coaches a typed ❓ toward `[?]`.

- The engine now owns the slide-size registry. Named canvases (`hd`, `story`, `mobile`, …) live in `lib/core/sizes.js` and a deck still selects one with `size:` in front matter. Source stylesheets no longer declare `@size` — the same 14-line table had been duplicated byte-for-byte across 32 palettes plus the base sheet, and the engine parsed it back out of its own CSS comment on every render.
- **Breaking (theme authors only):** a theme can no longer register or redefine an `@size`. The registered names are the whole vocabulary; a stylesheet that declares `@size` is rejected by `check:ownership`. In-repo themes all declared the identical table, so no deck changes shape — but an out-of-tree theme carrying a custom canvas will now render at that theme's `size:` name only if the name is registered, and otherwise at the `hd` default. A canvas we do not ship is a one-line addition to the registry.
- Export-to-Marp is unaffected: `@theme` stays in every stylesheet, and the build stamps the `@size` directives Marp reads into `dist/lattice.css`, `dist/lattice-min.css`, `dist/themes/*-min.css`, and the marp-kit. A new `check:ownership` gate fails in both directions — on source CSS that declares `@size`, and on a Marp-facing artifact whose stamp is missing or has drifted.
- `lint:deck` derives a deck's adaptive family from the same registry the renderer resolves against, in Node and in the browser alike. It previously fell back to a hand-copied name table in the browser, which a newly registered size slipped past.
- Fixed: a `size:` value naming an inherited `Object` property (`size: constructor`) resolved to a function instead of a canvas, yielding `NaN` page geometry. Unregistered names now resolve to the `hd` default, and the emulator still rejects a typo'd `size:` before launching Chrome.

- **On a `mode: sketch` slide, a framed icon's tile is drawn by hand**, like the spark beside it. The edge is inked in the icon's own color, a heavier line on the default pigment look, whose filled tile would hide a thin one. The drawing inside stays crisp, a bare icon has no tile to ink, and header and footer icons stay clean. The ink frame is square even on an `icon-rounded` tile, as a spark's is. Slides that are not sketch render as before.

- A `.pptx` or `.odp` slide picture is now a JPEG (quality 92) when the slide is a photograph or a soft gradient wash and that is under 70% of the PNG's size, and stays a lossless PNG otherwise. A 35-slide photo deck went from 76.6 MB to 16 MB, and from 44 s to 15.5 s in the CLI, because the slow PNG screenshot of a photograph is no longer taken. The Studio's PowerPoint export follows the same rule (8 photo slides: 38.2 MB and 7.4 s to 8.9 MB and 5.3 s). Flat slides are unchanged, byte for byte; a gradient title slide may become a JPEG.

- In a CLI or Studio PDF, an avatar's colored tile and ring, a sparkline's line and end dot, and the recommended card's spark are drawn as vectors, sharp at any zoom, like the face, bars and checks beside them.

- **Sparks are a plugin.** The word-sized charts you write as `` `~{12 14 17}` `` now ship as the
  `sparks` plugin (`lib/plugins/sparks/`), alongside icons and avatars, and have a page in the
  plugin catalog. Decks render exactly as before: `sparks` is on by default, the `spark:` front-matter
  key and the `spark-*` slide classes work unchanged, and a deck can name it in `plugins: [sparks]`.
  The author's reference moved from `lib/base/base.docs.md` to `lib/plugins/sparks/sparks.docs.md`.
- **Breaking:** a host that narrows the default plugin set (`createEngine({ plugins: { defaults } })`,
  `--default-plugins`, `LatticePlayground.setPluginDefaults`) or disables plugins now turns sparks off
  too, unless it lists `sparks`. A spark that is off renders as inline code, like every plugin kind.

- **Breaking:** the spectrum settings are three keys, each named for the thing first and taking one word per axis in any order. `spectrum:` sets the stripe on the slide edge (`spectrum: solid left band`), `card-spectrum:` the stripe on each card (`card-spectrum: solid top`), and `trim-spectrum:` the accent on tables, timelines and rules (`trim-spectrum: mono`). No key follows another: each has its own default (the slide edge rainbow, the cards off, the trim quiet) and names its own style. `spectrum-edge:`, `spectrum-card:`, `spectrum-card-edge:`, `spectrum-trim:` and `spectrum: on` no longer render. `npm run lint:deck` reports each as an error, and `npm run lint:deck -- --fix` rewrites it: `spectrum: duo` plus `spectrum-edge: left` becomes `spectrum: duo left`, `spectrum-card: auto` and `spectrum-trim: on`, which copied the slide edge, become the style the deck was showing (`spectrum: duo` plus `spectrum-card: auto` becomes `card-spectrum: duo`), and `spectrum-trim: restrained` becomes `trim-spectrum: mono`.
