- **Breaking:** the spectrum classes follow the keys: `spectrum-edge-left` is `spectrum-left`, `no-spectrum-edge` is `no-spectrum`, `with-spectrum-card` and `spectrum-card-rainbow` are `with-card-spectrum` (the rainbow), `spectrum-card-solid` is `card-spectrum-solid`, `spectrum-card-edge-top` is `card-spectrum-top`, and `with-spectrum-trim` / `spectrum-trim-restrained` / `no-spectrum-trim` are `trim-spectrum-rainbow` / `trim-spectrum-mono` / `trim-spectrum-quiet`. Lint fixes each in place.
- A new weight axis on `spectrum:` and `card-spectrum:`: `regular` (the default), `hairline` and `band`. A `band` slide edge is about 19px on a 1280px slide, and the slide's content, header, footer and page number stay exactly where they are.
- Deck settings label the three keys **Spectrum**, **Card spectrum** and **Trim spectrum**, with an Edge and a Weight row under each stripe, replacing "Brand bar", "Bar placement", "Card rail", "Card rail placement" and "Structural trim".
- A preset that sets a spectrum key fills only the parts the deck leaves out: on `preset: brand`, `spectrum: left` keeps Brand's solid style and moves the stripe to the left.

- **Changed: "Fix all" in the Studio and the Playground, and `lint:deck --fix`, now run through Squadra's fix driver.** Every fix that does not overlap another applies in one pass, where the old loop applied one fix and re-linted the whole deck after each. The driver never edits inside a code fence, so a fenced example of the wrong form stays as written. It never applies a fix that changes the number of slides or drops the front matter, unless the fix emptied the front matter on purpose. It reverts a fix that does not make its own finding go away. And it keeps going past a fix that cannot apply, where the old loop stopped at the first one. `lint:deck --fix` now prints each fix it refused, with the rule, the slide and the reason.

- The front-matter island: one reader for where a deck's front matter ends and which of its lines are keys (`lib/core/front-matter-island.mjs`). The engine's `parseFrontMatter`, the shared markdown-it kernel, the pane render, the register resolvers, the slide splitter, the deck model, the plugin admission and the `lattice-deck` lint language read it, where each used to carry its own pattern. `lattice-deck` gains an `fm-key` node per front-matter key (name, value and block-scalar body spans, and the key it nests under) and the `deck.settings` and `deck.registers` facts. No tracked deck renders or lints differently.
- **Fixed:** a deck whose front matter closes with `---` followed by spaces no longer reads the start of its first slide as deck-wide classes; the engine already ended the front matter there for every other setting.
- **Fixed:** a Windows (CRLF) deck that opens with two `---` lines is no longer read as having an empty front matter, which made adding a plugin in the Studio drop the author's first slide.

- The `deck` lint ruleset gains its first family: 23 front-matter register rules (`deck/unknown-finish`, `deck/unknown-mode`, `deck/unknown-pace`, the five spectrum dials and the rest of the single-value registers), ported from lint-core and held to it by the reference diff. Nothing reads them yet: lint-core still answers every consumer until the Squadra rewrite's step 5. The vocab bridge now keeps a register's names in their authored order, which the hint and the did-you-mean read.

- The lint-core rewrite's foundation (internal; no deck lints differently yet). `@laticent/squadra` gains a `./runtime` entry that loads only rules the build verified, with no compiler or fixtures (10.7 KB gzipped against 14.6 KB for the whole library), and its Markdown language nests blocks in lists, items, quotes and tables. `@laticent/segno-markdown`'s deck model lists those containers (`model.containers`). Lattice gains the `lattice-deck` language (directives with key and value spans, speaker notes, folded comments), `lintDeck`/`fixDeck`, build-time rule stamps checked by `build:check`, and `npm run squadra:reference-diff`, which holds every migrated rule to lint-core as main has it, run from a git worktree of the commit the branch left main at.

- **The standup and continuation cards now land as a comment on the PR, not only
  in chat.** Their location was never specified: `workflow.md` said "post two
  fenced cards" and named no surface, so sessions improvised — some commented on
  the ticket, most posted to chat alone. The 🚦 pre-merge card has had a location
  rule since HARD RULE #28 ("on the PR *and* in the ask, same wording"), and its
  argument — the transcript is not a durable surface, the PR is — applies to the
  continuation brief with more force: the pre-merge card is read within minutes
  by the person being asked, while the brief is addressed to a session that does
  not exist yet. Both cards now go as **one comment on the PR**, fenced there
  too, worded identically to the chat copy; where the two differ, the comment is
  the record. A ticket that stays open gets a one-line pointer comment, never a
  second copy. (`engineering/workflow.md` §Where the cards go)

- **The post-merge standup is now two fenced cards: the standup and a
  continuation brief.** The standup was drifting in and out of a code fence,
  which mattered more than cosmetics — the card is meant to be *copied*, and
  unfenced markdown is re-wrapped by the terminal renderer before it reaches the
  clipboard. Both cards are now always fenced, no exceptions. The new
  continuation brief is the second half: a paste-ready prompt that hands a fresh
  session everything the last one left pending — ticketed items and untracked
  ones alike, prioritized by downstream impact, each carrying where it lives,
  what "done" checks, the artifact that will prove it (a render, a pixel check,
  bench numbers — not "the tests pass", #23), and the verification tier it
  earned (gates, an independent checker, or the adversarial trio). The next
  session stacks the whole list into one PR with one commit per item, works it
  assuming nobody is at the keyboard, and stops at the merge gate with a green,
  review-ready PR. Its 8-agent budget is a pre-registered exemption to HARD RULE
  #25's ~10-agent human gate, which otherwise assumes a human is reachable.
  (`engineering/workflow.md` §Post-merge standup)

- The dagre layout engine no longer ships inside `lattice-runtime-min.js`. It is a
  separate `dist/lattice-dagre-min.js`, fetched only by a page that actually has a
  state chart — the shape Mermaid and the KaTeX provider already use. The runtime
  bundle drops from 243,431 to 216,937 bytes gzipped (−25.9 KiB, −10.9%) for every
  reader, including the ones whose decks have no state chart at all.
- An exported `.html` whose machines are all chains sheds a further 62.2 KiB raw /
  21.8 KiB gzipped: the CLI export inlines the engine only when a machine truly
  BRANCHES, decided by running the real dagre in Node over the deck's own topology
  rather than by asking whether the component is present. All 9 drawn machines in the
  shipped galleries are chains, so none of them pays for a layout that was computed
  and discarded. Rendered output is unchanged — 0 differing pixels across 33 pages.
- **Consumers embedding `lattice-runtime-min.js` directly:** load
  `lattice-dagre-min.js` beside it, with a `<script src>` *before* the runtime tag.
  Without it a state chart still draws, but a branching machine falls back to the
  numbered column; the runtime names the missing file on the console. Decks exported
  by Lattice carry both automatically.

- **Breaking (visual):** A state-chart state marked `live` now paints blue (info) instead of green, matching gantt: `live` is running work and `done` is finished work, and a chart that paints the status on the state has to tell them apart. The pill vocabulary shared by kanban, progress and slope is unchanged.
- The state-chart legend shows one chip per color. Words that paint alike share a chip (`on-track · done`), so a key no longer lists two identical green chips.

- **state-chart: no more snap in the Studio and Playground.** After an edit, the chart now draws in the same frame the slide appears. Before, the raw measuring column showed for two frames and then the drawn chart snapped over it. The runtime's mutation observer now draws a newly inserted state chart in its microtask, and the layout pass observes every figure, including ones inserted after install.
- **state-chart: an idle slide stops redrawing.** Each draw rewrote the SVG and probed label lines through `innerHTML`, and the runtime answered those writes with another content pass. So a state-chart slide redrew every ~160ms for as long as it was open. The pass now skips a write that would change nothing, so the cycle settles after one lap.
- **state-chart: a status now paints the state, the way it paints a gantt bar.** A node with a status takes that status's tinted fill, edge and leading accent. A node with none is a quiet neutral tile with no accent. This removes the plain slate stripe that ran down every node's left edge and carried no information. The colored disc that used to overhang the corner is gone too; the ordinal is a quiet numeral on every node. `deferred` draws hollow and dashed, as on gantt. Status tiles use the pill's stops (18/30 light, 42/54 dark), so the state name clears 4.5:1 on every theme; `tools/composed-contrast.js` now scores the name and ordinal on each status tile.
- **Breaking (visual): state-chart picks its own direction and wraps a long machine instead of shrinking it.** Every state-chart slide without `lr` re-lays out: it no longer defaults to a single top-to-bottom column. Add `tb` to keep the column. No build or authoring syntax breaks; the slide changes shape on its own. With no direction modifier, the chart now scores both directions at every row count against the real stage and picks the one that sets the state names largest, capped a step above body size. A long chain wraps in reading order: each row runs left to right, and a connector drops to the next row. Measured on a bare 16:9 stage, a 10-state chain used to set its names at 4.6px. There, four and five states stay on one row, six wrap 3 + 3, and twelve take three rows of four. The row count depends on the room the slide leaves, so a slide with a subtitle and caption may keep six states on one row or put twelve on two. Every chain now shares one visual language: labels sit beside their line, loops nest instead of crossing, and `curved` rounds corners. A branching machine still goes to dagre, which picks its direction by fit, and a wrapped layout can beat it by a clear margin. A small machine no longer blows up to poster size: the fit stops at 1.6x body text. A node is never narrower than its longest word, so a long single-word state name no longer spills out of its tile on a narrow stage. Edge labels are laid out at the size they actually paint once the chart scales down, so they no longer land on nodes or past the figure, and no two edges ever draw as one line. A new `tb` modifier pins the old top-to-bottom direction, and `lr` still pins a row; both may still wrap.
- **state-chart: the ordinal reads, and the `inline` card list lines up.** The numeral on each state now sets at the chart's text floor (the size an edge label paints at, 11px on a 1280-wide stage), with equal air above and beside it, and the tile's side padding clears it. It used to sit 2px from the corner at the engine's 1% hard floor. On `inline`, the cards form one table, numeral | name | transitions, so names and chips start at the same x on every card instead of floating right on some. A status now tints its card (a `live` card used to paint neutral while its legend chip was green), `deferred` cards are hollow and dashed, the gap between cards opened from 4px to the small spacing step, and the end state's double ring is drawn inside its card, so the last card no longer sticks out past the others.

- **Every brand theme now curates its own status colors.** On a light slide each status gets a deep fill in the
  theme's own hue, the slide's paper as the text on it, and the fill as its border, clearing 4.5:1 against every
  surface it sits on (the slide, a card, a hero tile, its own row tint, a kanban card), so it reads at the back of a
  hall. On a dark slide a status matches the category colors beside it, in the theme's own hues and at its palette's
  strength, with white text and a rim in the status color, so a status chart and a category chart read as one design
  language. Blocked is red on every theme, and on a light slide at risk sits visibly lighter than blocked,
  except on concrete, whose mid-gray slide forces every fill near-black. Done is a deep sage in the theme's own green, deferred a gray in the theme's own neutral (warm on cuoio, mustard and
  burgundy). Before, the status fills were near-identical across themes (warn was the same color in eight of fourteen).
  The `a11y-*` palettes keep their tokens. Decks need no edits.
  (engineering/decisions/2026-11-16-status-triplets.md; `node tools/curate-status-triplets.js`)
- **Status fills are no longer dimmed on top.** On a dark slide the risk matrix's bands and key, and a slope chart's
  signal lines, wear the status fill as the theme curated it instead of one taken 28-42% toward the slide, on every
  palette, the `a11y-*` ones included.
- **Under the tone finish a status keeps its curated color.** A tone status chart used to show each status as a 30% /
  35% wash, faded next to its pie on a light slide and all but gone on a dark one. It now wears the curated fill on a
  light slide and 88% of it on a dark one, with the status's own text ink on both.
- **Concrete's light status rows are a quieter tint** (10%), so a status disc stands off its row on concrete's
  mid-gray slide.

- **Breaking:** a `_focusSteps` slide is now ONE slide everywhere: one page number, one section, one rail dot. It used to be copied once per step, so a three-step table printed three pages and pushed every later page number up by two. Present walks the steps instead (the Studio, the presenter's Stage window and the exported HTML player): next lights the next target, and entering the slide backward lands on its last step. PDF, PowerPoint, images, the narrated video and the editor preview show the slide at rest, every unit even and nothing lit. For a printed walkthrough, export with `--steps` (or turn on "One page per step" in the Studio's export sheet): each stepping slide prints once per step, and every page keeps the slide's page number. Presenting live to a room carries the step, so everyone following sees the same reveal. `focusSteps` sets one slide only: front matter does not set it, and the bare `<!-- focusSteps: … -->` sets the slide it is on, like `_focusSteps`.
- `_build` now walks in Present, as `examples/build.md` always promised: entered by next, or jumped to (the rail, the overview, opening Present on it), the slide starts with nothing revealed and each click reveals the next step. Still formats show the whole slide, as before.
- `lattice <deck> --steps` and the Studio's "One page per step" switch (PDF, PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and "One image per step" for an image set) give each step of a `_build` or `_focusSteps` slide its own page, painted at that step. Every page keeps its slide's page number, and speaker notes and alt text ride on each page. Off by default.
- `lint:deck` flags a slide that carries both `_build` and `_focusSteps` (`one-stepping-directive`): a slide takes one stepping directive.
- `lint:deck` warns when a slide carries a static `_focus` beside `_focusSteps` (`focus-with-steps`): the walk owns the slide's focus, so the static one is ignored.
- A focused line of code (`_focus: line N`, a `_focusSteps` line walk, or the code block's own `focus=`) is now outlined (one box around a run of adjacent focused lines), and the dimmed lines around it stay readable at 4.5:1, so the whole slide passes WCAG AA. Before, the focused line differed from the dimmed ones by color alone, which did not read as focused on a dark code panel, and the dimmed lines were held only at 3:1.

- **Studio:** the slide menu's Move left and Move right are now **Move Before** and **Move After**, matching New Slide Before and New Slide After, and the menu's items are now Title Case. The command palette, the shortcut list and Undo use the same words in sentence case. The shortcuts are unchanged (⇧⌘← and ⇧⌘→).

- The Studio's slide map strip labels each slide with a caption pill under its picture, with the same number, component name and current-slide fill as the pill strip, so nothing covers the slide. The current slide's ⋯ menu is the caption's right-hand segment, as on a pill. Every tile keeps the 16:9 width whatever the deck's shape: a portrait, square, story or phone-shape slide sits centered in its tile, so the caption always holds its name and ⋯. The strip is 28px taller so each picture keeps its size, and live presence dots move to the picture's top-left.

- Studio: Workspace › AI is two parts. **Models in use** shows the three models the Studio runs on, each naming where it runs and what uses it: the chat model, the image reader (which reads your Library photos) and the voice model. **Connections** shows where the Studio can reach models: OpenRouter (signed in, or a pasted key), your own Gemini, Anthropic and OpenAI keys with what each can serve, and this device.
- Studio: connecting a provider never changes a model you chose. It fills only a model that is not set yet, and says what it filled. A new Studio starts with nothing set (or the free on-device voice on a desktop) instead of guessing. Downloading an on-device model makes it available; choosing it is a separate step.
- Studio: the image reader is its own choice: the chat model by default, or a model of its own on any connected provider, listing only models that read images. Its spend is shown separately from chat's.
- Studio: when a provider retires your model, the Studio moves to the newest version of the same family on the same provider (Claude Sonnet 5 → 5.5) and tells you. It never moves to another family or provider: with nothing newer, the model reads "Model retired" and waits for you. A provider that answers with a different model instead is caught and named.
- Studio: a narrated webpage export speaks in your voice model, including a Gemini voice or the on-device voice; the export panel no longer has a narrator picker of its own.
- Studio: a provider that answers "out of credit" is shown as that under Connections, with the time and a link to add billing.
- Studio: on an OpenAI key, a reasoning model that refuses tools (GPT-6.1 Terra) now answers the chat without edits instead of failing the turn; and a turn that never reached a direct provider names that provider ("never reached Gemini"), not OpenRouter.
- Studio: read-aloud and narration on a cloud voice now count toward Spend, as an estimate from the voice's per-character price ("Voice · OpenRouter ≈ $0.09"), and toward a spend cap.
- Studio: right after signing in to OpenRouter, the new key no longer reads "Key rejected" because OpenRouter had not finished setting it up: a 401 on a just-made key is checked again before it counts. When a key really is refused, the chat, image reader and voice cards all say so, not only the chat card.
- Studio: when OpenRouter refuses a key, its Connections row says what OpenRouter answered and how long after the key was made ("OpenRouter said 401: User not found, 4 s after the key was made, asked 3×").
- Studio: an OpenRouter key's usage and limit are read from OpenRouter's documented `/api/v1/key` endpoint, not the older undocumented `/api/v1/auth/key`.

- Studio chat: what the Architect did on a reply is now one tappable line under it instead of a paragraph plus a "Show work" link, and the full trace opens as a bottom sheet on a phone (a centered dialog on wider screens). The streaming thought wraps over two lines at its latest words instead of scrolling as a clipped one-line ticker.

- **The Studio chat is now an agent on a cloud model.** It used to send one prompt per turn
  carrying a ~26.5K-token list of every layout, with no tools, and it knew nothing about
  front matter, finishes, themes or deck budgets. It now starts from a ~6.7K-token core and
  reads what it needs: any component's full doc, the deck, finish, theme, lens and
  speaker-notes guides, the editorial rules, and every front-matter key. It edits a draft,
  runs the Coach's own linter and Mermaid's parser over it, fixes what they find, and shows
  you one review card for the whole turn — slides and front-matter changes together. Plain
  questions about the deck get plain answers with no tool calls. Under each reply, a line
  lists what it read and checked. On-device models keep the previous one-shot chat.
  (`docs/src/components/studio/architect-agent.ts`)
- **The chat composer no longer squeezes the text field to a sliver in the docked desktop
  column.** Its buttons now wrap below the field when the column is too narrow for both.

- **The Studio chat's change card works one slide at a time.** Each slide the AI changed is its own card,
  with Apply, Discard and a preview button; once applied, it has Undo. Apply all, Apply remaining and
  Discard all sit at the card's bottom right, and Undo all once nothing is waiting. Slides apply in any
  order: each finds its slide by its text, so applying a new slide first does not move a later change onto
  the wrong slide.
- **Undo works on one slide, any time, and never overwrites your edits.** Undo puts the slide's earlier
  text back while it still reads as the AI wrote it. A slide you have edited since says "Applied · you've
  edited it since" instead of offering an Undo, and a slide you changed before applying says "Changed since
  proposed". A refusal is said on the row it concerns. ⌘Z still undoes each action in turn.
- **Preview a change for real before applying it.** The preview button shows the slide rendered in the
  Studio's preview with the change, marked "not applied", with Before/After (or B) and Esc to leave. On a
  phone it opens full screen with Apply at the bottom. Nothing is written until you apply.
- **One History entry per AI reply.** The card's first change saves "Before AI edit · 10:42 · “your
  request” (1 of 3 applied)", and later changes update that label instead of adding entries, so a busy card
  never pushes your own saved versions out.
- **The AI knows what you did with its card.** Your next message tells it which slides you applied,
  discarded or undid, so it does not propose a discarded change again.
- **The change card reads in plain words**, with changed words marked and a rewritten line shown whole;
  Show source brings back the Markdown. A changed figure is flagged on its slide, as before.
- **The change card takes the room it needs.** It grows to the chat's height less two lines, and the chat
  slides to it when it arrives, keeping the last two lines of the reply in view.
- **The chat's cost menu answers each question in one card.** Context window shows how full it is as a bar
  ("27% used", "268K of 1M tokens"), and This session shows what you have spent (with a bar toward your cap
  when you set one). A chevron opens each card's breakdown in place. Compact conversation keeps its button
  in view.
- **Fixed: a message sent before a model is connected is now answered once one is.** Asking the chat with no
  model sends you to connect one; your message used to sit unanswered after you came back (OpenRouter's sign-in
  reloads the page), so you had to ask again. Now the chat answers it as soon as a model is ready, and the Studio
  reopens the chat after a successful OpenRouter sign-in. While it waits, the message says so, and asking
  again with the same words answers it instead of adding a second copy.

- **A Studio chat edit costs no more than the old chat did.** An edit that checks clean now
  ends the turn with its own summary instead of a third model call, the agent reads the core
  of a layout's doc instead of every variant's example, and long guides come back as a table
  of contents. Measured on the same six asks: edits $0.083 against the old chat's $0.093,
  questions 40% cheaper. (`docs/src/components/studio/architect-agent.ts`)

- **Studio chat:** the header is now one model chip with a dropdown, plus one session figure. The dropdown holds the per-turn price of a question and of an edit, the session against its cap, and the same model picker as Workspace → AI, so you can change model without leaving the chat.

- **The Studio is Compose-first.** A new visitor now writes in **Compose**, the rich editor; the
  Markdown editor is called **Source** everywhere and stays one click away for power users. The
  Studio remembers the choice, so picking Source once keeps it. Every menu lists Compose before
  Source: the editor pane's header (where the word `EDIT` used to sit), the phone's action bar, and
  ⌘K, which gains "Write in Compose" and "Write in Source". The pair keeps its words until the
  editor pane is too narrow to hold them; the header measures its own row and drops the issue
  pill's word first. Messages that said "edit this slide in Markdown" now say "in Source".
- **Fix all, its issue count, and Refine selection work in Compose.** Before, Fix all did nothing
  in Compose, its count fell back to a different estimate, and Refine was only offered in the
  Markdown editor.
- **The welcome tour and the "Write a slide" lesson lead with Compose.** A visitor who chose
  Source still hears the Markdown wording. Five new narration lines are recorded.
- **Compose's slide toolbar no longer changes size as the caret moves.** It used to grow and shrink
  with the styles the block under the caret offers (a heading offers one, an eyebrow line three),
  so the whole pill jumped. It now reserves room for the styles the current slide can offer, and
  on a narrow pane (phone, tablet) its two rows are as wide as their contents.
- **Compose looks like the signature mode without looking like an action.** Its icon and word stay gold
  whether it is selected or not, in a shade that passes WCAG AA in every palette. Selected, it takes the same
  light chip as Source, on the phone bar too. A solid accent fill stays reserved for Present.
- **The selected stop in Read · Write · Craft is an ink chip.** It used to be a faint gray tint with a
  gold hairline; it is now the inverted chip the phone bar already uses for its selected cell.
- **The Studio keeps your place when you switch panes or reload.** Compose on a slide, then Source, then Compose
  or Preview used to land on slide 1, and a reload jumped there a second after showing the right slide. The slide
  now holds through every switch and a reload, and when you move between Compose and Source the caret lands on the
  same line where it can match it (else at the slide's first line, as before).
- **You can see where you are after a switch or a reload.** With a keyboard, the editor you switch to takes focus with
  the caret where you left it; on a phone, switching straight between Compose and Source brings the keyboard up the same
  way, and arriving from the preview shows a drawn caret instead of the keyboard. A reload brings back the caret's line
  and its place on the line, as well as the slide; the place on the line also carries between Compose and Source.
  A line with a link, a repeated line, or a speaker note Compose does not show lands on the slide's first line. In a
  Live session no editor takes the keyboard on its own, and after a reload the editor waits until nothing else (search,
  chat, the command palette) has it.
- **In a Live session, Compose shows a co-editor's change at once, even while you type.** It used to hold the change until
  you left the editor, and your next keystroke replaced it, so both people lost the other's words. The one case left,
  a change that arrives while an input method (IME) composition is open, is tracked as a followup.
- **The chart, table and image lessons describe Compose when you write in Compose.**
- **Compose writes back what you wrote.** An edit in Compose used to rewrite the whole slide in one spelling of Markdown
  (`_em_` became `*em*`, `*` bullets became `-`, a table lost its padding) and dropped the deck's trailing newline. Now
  only the line you changed changes: the rest of the slide, every other slide, the separators and the trailing newline
  stay as you wrote them, and the edited line keeps your list markers and emphasis style.
- **Both editors mark the caret's line, and their carets match.** The line (Source) or block (Compose) holding the caret
  has a light accent wash, the Playground's, so the caret is found at a glance; it steps aside while text is selected.
  Compose's caret is now the body ink, like Source's, and the caret an editor shows while it is not focused looks and
  blinks like the live one.
- **A co-editor's change survives your IME typing in Compose.** In a Live session, a change that arrived while you were
  composing a word with a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method was replaced by your text when the word was done; now
  both are kept.

- **The Studio loads 8 KB less script up front.** The preview-fidelity, viewport-debug and diagram-diagnostics overlays render nothing until you turn them on, yet every visit downloaded them. Each now loads only when its switch (or its URL parameter) turns it on.

- On a phone, a lesson's caption is now a compact bar instead of a dark gradient across the bottom of the screen. The gradient covered the very button some lessons ask you to press.

- **The Studio loads faster for a returning reader with the slide map open.** The map keeps its slide pictures
  between visits and shows them instead of starting a live preview for every tile, so an unchanged deck's map loads
  no preview documents at all. A tile goes live only to draw a new picture: on a first visit, or after an edit, a
  theme change or an update. Measured at 4x CPU against the previous build, the load's Total Blocking Time fell by 39%
  (5.2 s to 3.2 s), its Speed Index by 36% (4.0 s to 2.5 s), and time to interactive by 39% (9.7 s to 5.9 s).
- **The map's pictures now use the slide's own fonts, icons and emoji,** so they match the slide instead of re-wrapping
  in a fallback face. A slide that shows a library photo keeps its live preview, so a replaced photo shows at once.
- **Typing with the map open is smoother.** The map draws a new picture of an edited slide only once you pause, and draws
  it with less work, so keystrokes wait less (at 4x CPU the slowest keystroke went from 240 ms to 104 ms, and blocking while typing fell by half).
- **`npm run perf:load`** (in `docs/`) measures a page's load with Lighthouse's desktop settings: median Total Blocking
  Time, Speed Index and time to interactive, for a first visit, a returning reader (`RETURN=1`) or with the map open
  (`MAP=1`), at any CPU slowdown (`CPU=4`).

- **Changed: notifications are one subsystem with a vocabulary, not a bare string.**
  `docs/src/lib/notify.ts` gives every floating message a kind — `status` (disposable,
  one pill, rewritten in place), `action` (text plus one affordance, its own slot) and
  `sticky` (never expires, never evicted) — and the kind carries the policy. At most
  one of each is on screen, which makes the toast cap structural rather than a number:
  three kinds, not three arbitrary messages.
- **Changed: `notify` is no longer a prop.** It reached 175 call sites through 15
  modules, which was a transport problem wearing an API's clothes. It is now a module
  import, matching the repo's existing cross-island store pattern. Every call site's
  text is unchanged; the test seam moves from a prop to `vi.mock`.
- **Changed: the Playground's two hand-rolled toasts become kinds**, and three of its
  messages leave the render-status line — a pane collapsing or a draft being restored
  is an event, not the render's state.
- **Changed: the Undo dwell is unified at 6s** across the Studio and the Playground,
  which previously used 5s and 6s with no recorded reason for the difference.
- **Added: a live region for panel messages that reached nobody.**
  `docs/src/lib/announce.tsx` gives a refusal or a terminal failure an announcement
  without moving where it renders, on five surfaces that had visible text and nothing
  in the accessibility tree. Not applied to progress that ticks, where a region would
  talk over the work it describes.
- **Fixed: a toast behind another is readable again.** The stack is expanded rather
  than collapsed, so a pill behind a newer one is no longer a 4px edge with an
  invisible but still clickable button in it. Safe now that at most one pill per kind
  can be on screen.
- **Fixed: opening a handed-off deck says so once, not twice.** The backup
  confirmation already reports the load, so the second message is suppressed.

- **Changed: the Studio's top bar is one row at every stop.** Read and Write used
  to get a slimmer desktop header than Craft, so stepping the dial swapped one
  `<header>` for another — the rules moved, the deck control changed shape, and
  the tail slid before landing back where it started. The three stops now share a
  single row: same controls, same order, same boxes, asserted across nine widths.
- **Changed: the header runs exactly three dividers, each closing a band.** Brand |
  deck, deck | view, utilities | verbs — all three gated on the same 1100px
  boundary. Two of them used to turn on at different widths, and a fourth sat
  *inside* the utilities band rather than between two bands.

- The Studio starts with about 130KB less JavaScript (compressed), down 17.8%. Six panels now load when you first open them instead of at startup: Share, Workspace settings, Chat, the Library, slide settings and reader views. Until a panel's code arrives, it shows a shell with the panel's own frame, title, tabs and search box in their final places, so nothing moves when the content fills in. Once the Studio is idle it loads all six in the background, so they usually open instantly and still open offline and after a deploy.

- At the Studio's Read stop, **Edit this slide** and a new **Read as an article** button now lead the slide navigator bar, before a divider and the slide chips. Edit this slide used to float over the bottom of the slide, and the article view was reachable only from ⌘K. Read as an article is a Read-stop action: the button and the ⌘K command appear only there. On a narrow pane both buttons show icons only.

- The Studio no longer loads code for panels you have not opened while your first slide is still coming in. Compose, Present, the reading view and the Share and Workspace panels now load after the first slide is on screen and you have not clicked or typed for 3 seconds. The editor's lint and the Coach's first assessment wait for the first slide. On a throttled phone profile the main thread is about 30% less busy in the seconds after the slide (1.3-1.6 s against 2.2-2.5 s of work in the first 3 s), and the first slide arrives a little sooner (5.8-6.4 s against 6.2-7.7 s).
- A deck that mentions math only inside code (such as `` `$x$` ``) no longer makes the Studio download the 20 math fonts and reload the theme. Exported files are unchanged.
- The Studio's preview starts loading its web-image check as soon as it loads, instead of on the first render, so the first slide no longer waits for it.

- The Studio loads its walkthrough engine when a lesson or tour first starts, not on page load: 18.5 KB less gzipped JavaScript at startup. Vetrina's React adapter gains `useLazyWalkthrough`, which takes a loader for the engine.

- **`examples/system-design-foundations.md` now carries the reader across its own
  section boundaries.** Six kit-opening slides (data, compute, network, scale,
  reliability, security) open by paying a debt instead of starting cold: five to
  the kit that just closed, and the data kit, which has none before it, to Part
  three's removal test. The compute kit answers the data kit's promise that every
  derived copy rebuilds unattended with the thing that runs the rebuild; the
  scale kit shows the cache and the replica returning as scaling moves; the
  security kit asks reliability's fail-apart question about credentials. None of
  the six referred to an earlier section before; all six do now.
- **The deck's protagonist comes back for Parts three and six.** Maya, who opens
  the deck, was last named on slide 159 and not again until the closing slide —
  a run of 60 slides. She now carries three load-bearing references in Part three
  (the twelve-minute build as three requests at three rungs; two candidates for a
  ceiling and only one that stopped PR 482; where her Tuesday sat on the
  four-movement arc) and two in Part six (nothing that broke her day was load
  either; the manual part gives out before the machine). Per-part coverage:
  Part three 0/13 → 3/13, Part six 0/20 → 2/20.
- **Six new ask-then-answer exercises break Part four's drought.** That part ran
  96 slides with four `Your turn` slides in it, three of them in the last seven,
  so the reader read 51 slides between the data kit's exercise and the security
  kit's. Six more now sit through it — two inside the data kit, then one closing
  each of compute, network, scale and reliability: run the data tree's first
  question on three teams; take or refuse three writes under a partition; place
  three workloads on a runtime; spend a latency budget on three cross-continent
  round trips; size a pool with Little's law, then break it in both directions;
  say what a page does when three dependencies go slow rather than down. Every
  one of the six kits now carries at least one. Inside Part
  four the longest stretch without the reader producing something drops from 51
  slides to 20; deck wide it drops from 51 to 45, and the longest run now starts
  in Part five.
- **Part seven now closes the loop the deck opened on.** Part zero is a Tuesday
  that fails — pull request 482 does not merge — and the deck used to drop that
  thread in Part two and never return to it. It comes back twice now: in Part
  three, where her day supplies a worked example of a ceiling, and on a new slide
  before "What to do on Monday" that says what would have made Tuesday different,
  in the deck's own vocabulary: a bounded pool of one, a deadline nothing
  inherited, and admission control twenty minutes late.

- **Breaking:** `compare-table` is renamed to `table`. Replace `<!-- _class: compare-table -->` with `<!-- _class: table -->`. There is no alias — an unmigrated slide falls back to `content`, so the table still renders with the house treatment but loses its row capacity, autosplit, portrait card reshape and focus axes. `lint:deck` now names the replacement outright — `'compare-table' was renamed to 'table'` — because the fuzzy suggester cannot: it scores edit distance, and the two names are 8 apart, which is exactly the case a deliberate rename is worst for.
- **Breaking:** a `table` slide now HUGS its content vertically and centers in the stage, instead of stretching to fill it. The old geometry stretched the table but left each cell's text pinned to the top of its band, so a short table read as a line, a gap, a line, a gap. Add `table-fill` to a slide to get the filling geometry back — now with cells centered in their bands, which is what the stretch always should have paired with.
- **Breaking:** a `table` slide picks up the universal table treatment it was previously excluded from, so it now draws the low-alpha accent zebra and uses the shared `--sp-*` cell padding rather than its own `cqi` values. `table-plain` turns the zebra off.
- `table-plain`, `table-fill`, `--table-zebra`, `--table-grow` and `--table-valign` work on the table component for the first time. They were inert on `compare-table` by construction: the component owned a near-duplicate of the universal table CSS and had to be denied that treatment to stop the two fighting. The component now styles no `<table>` element at all — it declares the contract (capacity, density, focus axes, the portrait reshape) and rides the shared treatment.
- The first column reads as a row label — 600 weight, heading ink — only when it actually is one. `lib/core/table-row-label.js` decides per table and turns the emphasis off on a single-column table, an index header (`#`, `No.`, `Ref`), an all-numeric first column, and a column of bare state markers. Measured across every markdown table under `examples/`, `exemplars/`, `test/integration/baseline-decks/` and `lib/components/` — 242 of them: every one keeps its label except four demonstration tables, two each in `examples/universal-table.md` and `examples/table-component.md`, which exist to show the rule declining. Do not retype that tuple: the corpus test prints it as a diagnostic, so `node --test test/unit/core/table-row-label.test.js` re-derives it.
- New `row-label` / `no-row-label` modifiers overrule that measurement in either direction. `no-row-label` wins a slide carrying both.
- A plain markdown table under `mode: sketch` now gets the drawn frame and wavy row rules. It previously took the hand type with no frame, because sketch's table rules named three components instead of describing the tables they decorate.
- `row-label` and `no-row-label` work on a plain table too, so a table outside the component can opt in. Both are **per-slide** tokens: a deck-level `class:` does not reach them. `examples/universal-table.md` demonstrates all three states on rendered slides: measured on, measured off over a year column, and `row-label` forcing it on over that same column.
- A table written as raw `<table>` HTML keeps its bold first column. It gets no verdict — markdown-it hands raw HTML through as an opaque block, so its rows never reach the rule — so the slide falls back to emphasizing the first column unconditionally, which is exactly what `compare-table` did. Without that fallback the rename would have quietly taken the emphasis away. The fallback is scoped to slides whose markdown actually holds a raw `<table>`, and every pipe table on such a slide carries its own verdict, so a deliberately-declined column (a year) is not swept up.
- Under `mode: sketch`, the drawn frame and wavy row rules follow the same stage-child scope as the universal treatment. A table inside `split-panel`, `split-compare`, `compare-code` or `image` is left alone, as `base.docs.md` promises, and `glossary` keeps its frame without gaining wave strips — its rows are separated by a zebra wash and it draws no cell border, so a strip there would be a line the deck never drew.
- New `examples/table-component.md` — the component's demo deck, 17 slides covering every switch on a rendered slide: the default hug-and-center, `table-fill`, `table-plain`, the measured row label both ways, `row-label` / `no-row-label`, `state-cells`, the three `_focus` axes, a raw-HTML table, `sketch`, `dark` and `compact` at six rows.

- The five remaining `@import` flatteners in `tools/` now walk the declared theme graph instead of re-deriving it. `derive-cat-ink`, `derive-chart-cat-ink`, `contrast-audit`, `cvd-audit` and `build-docs-portal` each carried their own regex for "what does this palette extend" — the exact duplication the manifest-as-contract change removed from the four shipping paths, left behind because these read source-form themes off disk where the minified-form divergence cannot bite. All five call `themeChain()` over the manifest-baked edge map now, and `build-docs-portal` asks the manifest rather than the stylesheet which palettes are selectable. No output moves: the replacement is byte-for-byte identical to each old flattener across all 32 palettes (with reversed-order and leaf-only negative controls firing), every tool's report is unchanged, and `npm run build` regenerates `dist/` and the committed theme ink blocks with an empty diff.
- The docs site's palette picker gained a test for the one question it asks. `listBasePalettes()` decides which palettes the picker offers, and the edge map it consults has two shapes — the generated one omits root palettes, the manifest builder keeps them with an undefined value — so a predicate written against one of them silently empties the picker under the other. It now routes the question through `themeChain()`, which reconciles both, and `test/unit/theme/base-palette-predicate.test.js` drives the real function with each encoding.

- A theme's name now has one owner: `themes/<name>.manifest.json`. The filename and the `@theme` directive are projections of it, and a new `check:ownership` gate fails if any of the three disagree. They agreed by discipline before, but nothing checked — `themes/foo.css` declaring `@theme bar` would pass every gate and register under a name no picker, manifest, or `@import` referred to.
- `addThemes()` accepts `{ name, css }` alongside a bare CSS string, on both the engine (`./engine`) and `window.LatticePlayground`. Passing the name is now the contract: every caller in the engine, CLI, and docs already had it and was discarding it, leaving the store to recover it by regex. A second gate keeps new callers in `lib/`, `docs/src/`, `tools/` and the emulator on the object form; it parses a real AST rather than scanning text, so a regex literal or a template can't hide a call site from it.
- Fixed: registering a stylesheet with no `@theme` directive scanned the entire buffer before giving up — hundreds of microseconds on a large sheet — and then registered nothing while returning a `false` no caller checked, so the theme vanished and the deck rendered unstyled with no signal. The legacy scan is now bounded to the file header.
- Fixed: a *named* registration could hit the same silent failure. `add(name, undefined)` discarded the name and scanned it as a stylesheet, and `add(name, null)` returned `true` while storing `null` — leaving `hasTheme(name)` permanently true, disarming the Playground's theme self-heal, while renders came back unstyled. Both now throw.
- **Breaking (narrow, external consumers only):** the bare-CSS form of `addThemes()` now looks for `@theme` in the first 4096 characters instead of the whole file. Every stylesheet Lattice ships declares it within 1005, so nothing in the package is affected — but a vendored or concatenated sheet carrying a banner longer than that before its directive will no longer register. Pass `{ name, css }` (or move the directive to the header) if you have one.
- `@theme` deliberately stays in source theme CSS, unlike `@size`: `@laticent/lattice/themes/<name>.css` is a published export documented as a Marp theme file, and Marp throws without the directive.

- `topic`: the current topic's column on the track is now lit as a filled tab in the upper band's own field, capped with a bar in the heading's ink, so the topic named above visibly reaches down into its place in the section. It replaces the thin accent bar, which sat on the spectrum seam and read as part of it. The tab needs no hue, so it also shows on the palettes where `--accent` collapses onto `--border` (onyx, concrete, a11y-achromatopsia, a11y-base).
- `topic`: the tab has one fixed height for the whole section, so it no longer changes size as the deck moves from one topic slide to the next.
- `topic`: on a nine-topic track, labels no longer break mid-word (`Postmortems` rendered as "Postmortem / s"). The columns tighten their inset at nine, and a word only breaks when it cannot fit a column at all.
- `topic`: track labels are centered in their columns, horizontally and vertically, so each topic reads as a cell and the lit one as the selected cell.
- `topic`: on the carbone light theme the slide heading is readable again. It rendered near-black on the near-black band (1.05:1); it now takes carbone's own light display ink.

- **Graph charts:** a live redraw in the Studio asks its layout worker 3–7 ms sooner a key. The pipeline no longer forces a style and layout pass before the post: it reads the pending signature after posting, skips the signature on a paint the next round replaces, and reads the type floor once a draw. Drawings are unchanged.
- **Tooling:** `tools/graph-typing-bench.mjs` times each stage of a graph chart's live redraw, key by key, in the production-built Studio, and with `CAPTURE` checks that two builds paint byte-identical drawings.

- **Changed: the type-floor alarm says what is wrong instead of quoting its own measurement.**
  The authoring tab on a slide whose figure shrank its labels below the legibility
  floor read `Type 6.6px · floor 7.2px` — two numbers, no verb, and a unit that
  changes with the deck's size. It now reads `Text too small · 4.9pt`, and carries
  the fix in a tooltip: *"Figure text renders at 4.9pt — below the 5.4pt minimum.
  Simplify the figure (fewer labels, shorter text) or give it a bigger box."*
  The size is reported in points on the standard 960×540pt slide page, so the floor
  is the same 5.4pt on every preset rather than four different pixel numbers for one
  rule, and it is directly comparable to the deck's own type roles (`meta` is
  11.25pt) on 16:9 decks — that last comparison is aspect-bound and the probe's comment
  says where it breaks. The export's `TYPE FLOOR` stderr warning names the same points.
  The tab's gating is unchanged: it appears only at `overflow-marker: author`, so no
  deck a reader receives carries it.

- Running header, footer and page number are smaller at `venue: conference` and `venue: hall`: they follow the venue's type step but no longer take the label lift, and take a further 15% cut (hall: about 19px on a 1280px slide, was about 29px). Eyebrows, captions and card tags keep the lift. Laptop and huddle are unchanged.

- `lint:deck`'s `capacity-scale` now judges a `split-panel` claim panel by the lines its eyebrow, heading, opening `*question*` and lede wrap to at the deck's `venue:`, instead of by word counts. It catches claim panels that clip at hall and that the word rows missed, and raises no new false warning on the five decks it was scored against. The finding names the line counts it found. `venueCapacity.panel` in the split-panel manifest now holds line geometry (`lines.bare` / `proof` / `capstone`), measured by `tools/calibrate-capacity.js split-panel --panel`.

- **Vetrina — the `bar` caption declares its own `box-sizing: border-box`**, so it is 24 px narrower than before and finally honors the 680 px cap its own code comments claim. The previous width arithmetic assumed `content-box`, which is wrong in any host carrying a `* { box-sizing: border-box }` reset — the commonest reset there is, in a library whose whole point is dropping into an arbitrary host.

- The Present Guide now **focuses the element it names** instead of drawing beside it: the named bullet, table row, cell or column, chart bar, wedge, line or point stays as it is while everything else in its group recedes, the same emphasis a chart gives on hover. Nothing moves or changes color, and two things are never in focus at once. Overlay ink and the cursor now appear only on an `expressive` deck's top moment.
- When the narration walks a chart point by point, the Guide follows: on a line, the other series recede and the point being read stands out within its line; each wedge, bar and heatmap cell is followed as it is read, as one moment of the preset's budget.
- `delivery: somber` now reads differently from `restrained`: a gentler recede (0.62 against 0.45), a slower 600 ms handoff that holds through a short aside, and a caption without the word-by-word crawl.
- With the captions off, the word being spoken lights inside the focused text, in step with the voice (not under `somber`).
- A bar, stacked bar or bullet chart's category names and printed values now recede with their bar, both when the Present Guide focuses a bar and when you hover one in the Playground or Studio. A focused bar on a dark theme now reads at a glance. Tapping a single-series bar's name or value opens that bar's card.
- The same holds on every chart: a heatmap cell's number, a gantt task's caption, a scatter point's name, a dumbbell row's name and a stacked bar's part values recede with their mark, and a line's name and end value recede with their line when the Guide walks another.
- While the Guide plays, hovering a chart no longer overrides it or opens a card over the playing slide. Pause to explore: the Guide steps back and the hover works as usual; press play and the Guide picks up again.
- When the narration names a chart's key row, stage or label, the Guide now focuses the mark it belongs to instead of the words alone.
- A chart whose values skip a category (a bar with no number) no longer locks the mark after the gap out of its hover card.

- **Vetrina — the `caption: 'cursor'` balloon is transient.** It appears when there is something to say and at no other time: the cursor moves (the movement is what brings the eye), it arrives, the balloon appears beside it, it holds for as long as an average reader needs, and then it takes itself down — and only then does the action run. A beat that points somewhere says its line on arrival; a beat whose only movement is a deictic stroke says it once the stroke is drawn; a beat that does not move says it immediately. `Stage.dismissCaption()` is the new seam, distinct from `say('')` in that it leaves the words in the live region rather than reverting to the take-over hint.
- **Vetrina — the cursor caption's dismissal waits out its own cross-fade** before the beat acts. Dismissing and acting in the same frame fired the action while the words were still at ~18% opacity — measured on the real page as a visible smudge under the click burst.
- **Vetrina — a word-cued beat pins its caption** (`Stage.holdCaption`). `at` means the action is timed to a word in the line, so the line is what the viewer is following — and with no voice, the caption IS the line. The step-aside was hiding it through the approach and bringing it back after the click, so the instruction arrived a second after the action it instructed.
- **Vetrina — a beat says its line before what the line explains.** A `gesture` is the say-point only when it is the beat's only doing: a `say` + `type` + `gesture` beat was typing before it said the line explaining the typing, a `say` + `until` + `gesture` beat held the advance gate — up to ~15s — with no caption on screen at all, and a beat whose `act` threw never showed its caption, because the throw leaves before the gesture block. The caption's own dwell also pins itself visible now, so a drag beat's reading window no longer depends on a side effect of `say()`.

- **Breaking:** a `video` slide names its clip with an `@video{"https://…", title="…", poster=…}` record on a line of its own, from the new `video` plugin. The bullet form (`- https://…`, with `caption` and `poster` bullets) is gone: nothing reads a slide's text into an address any more. `lint:deck --fix` rewrites old slides (`video-bullet`); the shipped decks are migrated. An address holding `=` or `,` must be quoted.
- A zip plugin's fence now draws on a `video` slide, where the shipped `video` pass used to keep it out. The address comes only from the author's own span at parse time, so a plugin's text cannot become a poster, link or code. The runtime's inline-code mirror skips everything inside `[data-lattice-plugin]`, and the Studio's video overlay and the Reading view take a poster only from the video plugin's own figure (`data-lattice-media="video"`).
- Inline kinds can be `named` (reached only as `@kind{…}`, no sigil) and `address` (resolved on the markdown-it path only, never on the DOM mirror). New lint rules: `video-bullet`, `video-not-alone`, `video-literal`.

- **On desktop, the Studio narrates with the on-device Kokoro voice by default.** The first read starts its download in the background, using the cloud voice when one is connected and captions only when none is. Later reads use the local voice, which is free per clip and works offline. A cloud model you picked yourself still takes precedence. Phones and tablets keep the cloud voice. (`docs/src/playground/voice-model.js`)
- **New Workspace switch: "Always use the cheapest voice"** (off by default). It narrates with the lowest-cost paid cloud voice, counting what a model charges for the audio it produces as well as the text you send. Within 10% on price, the better voice wins. It never picks a voice ranked below Kokoro, however cheap, so it can move to a better voice but never to a noisier one. Free, rate-limited voices are skipped, and a voice you picked always takes precedence. Hosted Kokoro stays the cloud default: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS lists $0.50/M but was billed about $18.50 per million characters once its audio output was counted, about 30× Kokoro. (`docs/src/playground/tts-cost.js`)
- **Fixed:** the narrated-export cost quote now counts the audio a voice produces, not only the text sent. It had quoted Gemini voices about 37× too low.
- **Fixed:** picking Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS or Flash Lite TTS in the voice picker failed every clip with a 400 error, because those models only return raw PCM audio. The whole Gemini TTS family is now requested as PCM.
- **Fixed:** the on-device voice failed to load on a browser that exposes WebGPU with no usable GPU (Linux without GPU acceleration, VMs, blocklisted GPUs). It downloaded the ~330 MB full-precision model and never came up. It now checks for a usable GPU first and loads the smaller ~80 MB model otherwise. It also retries on that model if the GPU load fails.

- **Changed: Present stays smooth while it reads aloud in a Gemini voice.** Gemini sends each
  spoken sentence as text-encoded audio inside a JSON reply, and the Studio decoded it on the main
  thread. On a phone-speed CPU, a 20-second clip blocked the page for 75–87 ms. A background
  worker now does the decoding, so those pauses are gone. If the worker cannot run, the Studio
  decodes on the main thread as before and the audio is the same.

- **Breaking:** `numbered` no longer numbers a `list`. The marker decides in every register: a `1.` list numbers its rows and a `-` list does not. So a `list takeaway` written as `1.` without `numbered` now shows its counters (they were hidden). A deck that wrote `list takeaway numbered` over `-` items loses its counters until the items are written as `1.`; `lint:deck` names each such slide (`list-modifier-inert`). The repo's own decks are migrated.
- **Breaking:** `ledger-inline-title` is deprecated and no longer emitted. The inline `- **Title.** body` shape on a ledger layout (agenda, kpi, list-steps, …) is now reported as `card-style-inline-title`, whose autofix keeps your marker instead of rewriting it to `1.`.
- One list contract for every layout. Each component that reads a list now declares what `1.` versus `-` means on it (`lists` in its manifest): `prose` (`content`, `list`: `1.` numbers, `-` bullets), `numbered-tags` (`cards-grid`, `cards-stack`, `list-steps`, `split-panel steps` and `watermark`: `1.` turns the number tags on, `-` leaves them off) or `neutral` (every other layout: both render the same). The engine enforces it before any layout reads the slide (`lib/core/list-contract.js`), so `agenda`, `kpi`, `stats`, `premise` and `list-tabular` no longer collapse on `-`; `cycle`, `inventory`, `glossary`, `pricing`, `logo-wall`, `big-number`, `policy-recommendation`, `verdict-grid` and `journey` no longer collapse on `1.`; and the thirteen chart kinds that read nested rows draw the same chart from nested `1.` rows.
- `list-steps-inline-body` reads every step marker (`1.`, `1)`, `-`, `*`, `+`), counts a tab-indented body as nested, keeps your marker and line endings in its fix.
- `list-steps` written as `-` renders the same step cards without the STEP tag (it collapsed to plain text), and `list principles` written as `-` draws a dot before each principle (it fell back to the default pills).
- `slot-contract` no longer reports a list marker: on every layout that reads a list, either marker renders as its contract says.
- The contract covers the list levels each layout was designed for: the item, its body or detail line, and on a few layouts one level more (a kanban card's tag line, a flowchart connection inside a group). A deck-wide `class: steps` or `class: principles` sets the contract like a slide's own class.
- New warning `list-depth-unsupported` (`lint:deck` and the Studio): a list nested deeper than its layout was designed for, or a second list after a line of prose, is not part of the layout's design. Fold it into the line above or give it its own `content` slide; `content` and `list` take any list.
- A list inside a blockquote (a Key Insight callout) keeps the weight you wrote: the bold label a layout gives its own items no longer reaches it.

- **Changed: the hand-rolled-wait nudge stays silent where its fix cannot run.**
  `.claude/hooks/warn-unbounded-wait.sh` now checks that this box can actually
  run `tools/wait-for.sh` before printing — the helper refuses with exit 69
  unless a `timeout(1)` and either `flock(1)` or perl are present, and a stock
  macOS ships neither `timeout` nor `flock(1)`. Coaching toward a tool that
  exits 69 is worse than saying nothing. The check runs last and only on a
  match, so the hook's cost on an ordinary Bash call is unchanged.

### Deprecated

- **`lexicon-single-letter-key` is no longer emitted.** A letter or digit key (`e:`, `2:`) in `terms:`, `acronyms:` or `lexicon:` now applies only to the whole word, so it can no longer rewrite every `e` inside "revenue". The rule ID stays reserved.

### Removed

- **Breaking: `dist/docs/components.json` and `dist/docs/grammar.json` no longer carry a
  top-level `count` field.** Read `components.length` — always the same number, and always
  right. The field was an aggregate over every manifest, which is the one value two concurrent
  PRs cannot both be right about: each adds a component, each writes the same N+1, git's
  three-way merge takes the identical line from both sides without a conflict, and the
  committed file lands one short — which `build:check` then rejects inside the merge queue, on
  a `main` the PR never saw, silently clearing its auto-merge. Swept the rest of the build the
  same way (replaying the merge rather than reading code) and removed four more of the same
  shape: the `**N components · M buckets.**` line in `dist/docs/components.md`, two totals in
  the §0c split-treatment footer, and the font counts in the Marp kit's `README.md` /
  `NOTICE.md`. Everything else is safe for reasons worth distinguishing — `dist/lattice.css`
  is a concatenation that merges clean *and* correct, while the esbuild bundles and
  `lattice-min.css` conflict loudly. A new gate replays the merge over the real catalog rather
  than banning a field name, so a future aggregate of any shape fails without anyone having to
  predict it. (`engineering/decisions/2026-08-11-generated-artifact-sweep.md`)

- Removed `lib/authoring/fact-check-core.js`, the unused first half of a deck fact-check feature that was never built. Nothing in Lattice called it; `engineering/decisions/2026-06-16-deck-fact-checking.md` records why it went and how to restore it.

- **Breaking:** `_focusStyle: pop` is removed. It scaled the target and dropped a shadow past its edge, which moved the layout and was clipped at the stage. `_focusStyle: highlight` does the same job without shifting anything. The lint flags a deck that still says `pop`.

- **Breaking: Form can no longer be disabled or configured.** The deck-wide `form:`
  front-matter key and the per-slide `form` / `no-form` tokens are retired, along
  with `readFormMode`, `FORM_MODES` and the mode argument threaded through all three
  render paths. Every slide composes as Form. A deck still carrying `form: off` now
  renders WITH the masthead band, bay and progress rail; `lint:deck` warns and names
  the consequence rather than refusing the deck, and the specific chrome controls
  (`class: no-progress`, `no-header`, `no-footer`, `no-pagination`) are unaffected.
- **Changed: sovereignty is a property of a Frame, not the absence of Form.**
  `FORM_TOGGLE_SKIP` is now `SOVEREIGN_FRAMES` — the ten Frames that declare one
  Cell instead of the chrome-hosting Frame's nine. `applyFormToggleToHtml` is
  `applyFormToHtml` and takes no deck source, because there is nothing left to read.
- **Changed: `form` is engine scaffolding, not an author modifier.** It leaves the
  universal `chrome` vocabulary (so autocomplete and lint no longer offer it) and
  joins `STRUCTURAL_ROOT_CLASSES` in the ownership gate, beside `chart-frame`.

- **Removed: the Form on/off controls in the Studio and the Playground.** Form is
  the composition model, not a setting — so the Studio Inspector's **Deck chrome**
  toggle, the Playground Deck-settings **Form** select, and both editors' `form:`
  autocomplete (the key hint and the `off`/`standard` value list) are gone. The
  **Section rail** control is a different register (`class: no-progress`) and is
  unaffected. A leftover `form:` line in an existing deck is preserved verbatim by
  the settings panel rather than rewritten or dropped.

- **Breaking:** the journey chart reads standard Segno only, so the `` `@sales` `` actor shortcut is
  gone. Write a task's second actor as a second step record, `` `{who=sales}` ``. A leftover `@name`
  span renders as code and drops the actor, so `lint:deck` warns on it (`journey-actor-shortcut`)
  and `lint:deck --fix` rewrites it. Every shipped deck moved and renders byte-identically.

- The deck lint no longer reports `bookend-finish-contrast`. A deck-wide `finish:` on a title or closing slide renders correctly, and the presets put a finish there on purpose, so the note flagged nothing an author needed to change.

- The deck lint no longer reports eight findings that flagged slides which render correctly:
  - `unknown-guards`: it duplicated `guards-renamed`. An unknown old `guards:` value with no `fit:` now raises `guards-renamed` as a warning instead.
  - `capacity-autosplit`: it described the engine splitting an over-full slide at a portrait, square or strip size, which is the engine working as designed.
  - `tag-alias` on `list-steps capsule`: `capsule` is a documented current modifier, not an old name. The `banner-tag` hint stays.
  - `retired-form-key` for `form: standard` and other values that were already no-ops, and `retired-form-token` for a bare `form` token. `form: off` and `no-form` still warn, because they change the render.
  - `pane-title` for a pane label past five words.
  - `pane-layout` for `no-title` on a pane that has no title.
  - `moved-empty-box`, with its render-time warning and `--fix` rewrite: `[ ]` is a valid answer on every layout.
  - `deprecated-class-color-mode`: a deck-wide `class: dark` / `class: light` still works.

- **Breaking: the `list-criteria` component is removed. Write `list takeaway numbered`
  instead.** Both took the same markdown (a numbered item with a nested `- reason`
  bullet), and `list takeaway numbered` already drew the ruled rows and fixed counter.
  `list takeaway` now also stacks a nested bullet as a muted line under a bold lead,
  where it used to set it inline on the lead's line, and `numbered` puts the counter in a
  fixed-size left gutter. The old component sized its number at 55% of the row height, so
  the number changed size as the row count changed (67px of drift in the jank census), and
  it centered the text far from the number. A slide that still says `list-criteria` renders
  as a plain `content` slide (plain numbers, no ruled rows), and `lint:deck` names the replacement. Every in-repo deck is
  migrated.

- **Breaking:** `lib/core/flowchart-grammar.js` no longer exports `readArrow` or `LABEL_MAX`. Flowchart and state-chart rows are now read by a parser that Segno generates from `lib/core/flowchart-row-grammar.js`, and `splitRow` returns the same parts and arrows as before, without the arrow's `end` offset. To read arrows, call `splitRow`. The label cap is that file's `LABEL_MAX`, which counts the label itself (61 characters); the old export was 60 and was used as the cap minus one.

- **Breaking:** `lib/core/state-marks.js` no longer exports `LEADING_MARKER_RE` or `LEADING_MARKER_PREFIX_RE`, `lib/core/matrix-grid-cells.js` no longer exports `CELL_MARKER`, and `lib/core/table-row-label.js` no longer exports `MARKER_CELL`. A parser that Segno generates from `lib/core/list-text-grammar.js` now reads leading state markers, matrix-grid cells and `_track`, and decks render as before. To read a marker, call `readLeadingMarker(text)` from the new `lib/core/leading-marker.js` (`{ marker, rest }`) or `leadingMarkerPrefix(text)` (`{ marker, length }`); `isMarkerCell(text)` replaces `MARKER_CELL.test`, and `parseCell` and `parseTrackSpec` keep their signatures.

- **The Playground's Math renderer control is retired.** Nothing in the engine reads
  `math:` — Lattice types all math with KaTeX — so the control wrote a key no renderer
  honored. A deck that already carries the key keeps it verbatim; only the control is gone.

- The Studio's four long "Show me" tours (the full walkthrough, the board deck, "It's just Markdown" and the quiet tour) are retired in favor of lessons. "First look" remains as the one tour and is now what "Watch demo" plays.

### Fixed

- `state-chart` now holds its type floor through its own self-scale. The chart letterbox-scales itself to fit the stage, and that transform multiplied the CSS floor away with everything else — so a machine scaled to 0.72 rendered its edge labels at 7.9px against a declared floor of 11px. The declared floor is now raised by 1/k where the scale factor is known, so the effective size lands on the floor instead of under it: measured on the shipped gallery, 7.91px → 11.00px and 8.30px → 11.00px on the two hard-scaled slides. Charts that are scaled UP are untouched — the compensation only ever raises the floor, never caps type that is already comfortable.

- The portrait `word-cloud` now fills the canvas it packs into, without losing words
  to do it. Word sizes are viewBox units and scale by the square root of the area
  ratio between the landscape and portrait pack boxes — but that ratio was read off
  the full canvas width on both sides, and landscape only ever packs into 62% of it
  (the rest is the key rail), so the cloud rendered 27% under-sized and clustered in
  the middle of a box it could not fill. Growing the type costs words, though, so the
  scale is a ladder rather than a constant: it is walked largest-first and keyed on
  how many words actually place, the same rule `quadrant`'s dot-label ladder uses,
  with no-scaling as the floor rung. A portrait cloud can never paint fewer words
  than an unscaled one, and every shipped slide still takes the top rung. Measured on
  a 15-phrase portrait deck: 11 words painted before, 10 at a flat derived scale,
  12 with the ladder.
- The word cloud now reports the words its packer could not seat. This is the chart
  family's worst silent loss — every other dropped label survives on `data-label`,
  in the speaker note and in the SVG description, but an unplaced word is struck
  from all three. It surfaced a real one immediately: a shipped example deck has been
  dropping a word at landscape, invisibly, since before the diagnostic existed.

- **Editing a deck's terms in the Studio no longer rewrites the rest of its front matter.** Saving the Terms list (and the older Lexicon and Acronyms lists) used to drop YAML comments and `_class:`, turn a `style: |` block into `"|"`, reorder keys and convert CRLF line endings. It now changes only its own block (#1257).

- **Fixed: four docs test files no longer depend on the order their own cases run in.**
  Each failed deterministically under `--sequence.shuffle.tests` and passed in
  declaration order, so the defect was invisible until someone enabled shuffling.
  `narration-encode.retry` let one case's successful module resolution leak into
  the next, because a hoisted `vi.mock` factory is evaluated once and cached for
  the whole file — `vi.resetModules()` does not reach the mock registry.
  `studio.controls`, `studio.refine` and `studio.fuzz` read the code-split Editor
  and Fabricate panes synchronously, so whichever case ran first saw the loading
  skeleton rather than the pane. Tightening the first of those also exposed an assertion
  that could not fail; it now can.

- **Fixed: the docs site's jsdom test suite no longer fails on its own per-test time limit under load.** The `studio.*` family failed intermittently in a full run with a different failing set each time — the failure mode that teaches you to dismiss failures, and once nearly hid a real regression. The cause was the test runner's generic 5-second default, never chosen for tests that drive a full Studio render plus ten interactions: measured at 1.8–2.0s idle and 4.9–6.1s under CPU contention, they straddled the line exactly. The suite now carries a limit sized from that measurement. A second, narrower source of flakiness in the same family — inner waits on the library's own 1-second default — is unaffected by this and is tracked separately (#1806).

- **Fixed: the Mermaid sequence autonumber badge was invisible.** `sequenceNumberColor` drew
  the badge number in `--cat-on-fill` on a badge filled from `--diagram-line`, and most
  palettes derive both from the same end of the ramp — so the number was painted in the
  disc's own color on 47 of 64 palette x scheme combos, and below AA on 57. It now uses the
  canvas ink, the same inversion the parse-error box already used.
- **Fixed: sequence note text no longer sits at 3.83:1 on the five a11y palettes in dark.**
  `noteTextColor` moves from `--cat-on-fill`, which is curated for the pale categorical band,
  to `--text-heading`, which is curated for the surface it actually lands on.
- **Changed: cuoio's dark `--diagram-line` lifted `#786A5B` → `#8C7C6B`.** The line tier now
  carries the autonumber badge's text, and this was the only palette of 32 short of AA. Every
  cuoio-dark diagram edge and arrow also goes from 3.59:1 to 4.66:1 against the canvas.

- **Fixed: internal pragmas no longer ship as the speaker note.** A `<!-- tier: short -->`,
  `<!-- galleryAuthored: … -->` or `<!-- color-mode: dark -->` comment fell through into the
  presenter-notes field of every exported format, so slides whose author wrote no note shipped
  one made of build markers. They are now classified as pragmas. Matching is constrained by
  value as well as key, so a real note that opens with one of those words — `<!-- tier: we
  should discuss the pricing tier -->` — is still a note.

- **Preview fidelity:** a deck using `logo-on: title` no longer paints its logo on every slide rendered through the single-slide (slice) route — the slide-overview grid and any other surface that renders one slide alone — on any deck whose slide index the position guard can trust. (The main slide preview renders the whole deck and narrows to one section, so it never showed this.) `logo-on: title` selects the deck's first slide, and a sliced slide is its own document's first section, so the preview showed a mark the export did not. The engine now hands the deck position down to the logo pass, the same way it already did for the SVG accessibility names. A deck the position guard declines (a `_focusSteps` deck, or one whose slide count disagrees with the render) gets no position, so it is not repaired there yet.
- **`npm run equiv:check` compares the corpus baseline directionally instead of exactly.** Deck and slide counts may grow (adding an example deck is not a regression) but may not shrink; the equivalence, refusal, prelude and skip *rates* are what get pinned. The old exact comparison failed on ordinary corpus growth with a message that read like a real regression, and — with nothing invoking it — sat red and unread from 154 decks to 158.
- **The sweep now runs in the unit tier** (`test/unit/diagnostics/slice-equivalence-baseline.test.js`), so `npm test` reads the gate that nothing was reading.
- **Every equivalence residual now reports a named cause.** The 27 previously `unclassified` residuals were 25 instances of the logo defect above plus 2 of the position guard correctly refusing, which now reports under its own name. Refusals are counted, rated and listed per deck as a baseline field.

- **Fixed: a Coach quick-read card no longer reappears after you dismiss it, and no longer shows
  the wrong chip's answer.** The chips that reach the voice of the deck — The ask, Structure and
  Pacing with a talk length — wait on a lazily-loaded chunk, so an answer can arrive well after
  you have moved on. A card closed during that wait came back on its own, and an earlier chip's
  answer could replace the one you clicked after it, chip highlight included. Answers that have
  been superseded are now discarded.
- **Fixed: Top fixes and Weakest slide no longer report a clean deck for one that was never
  assessed.** A deck with no `_class` slide is deliberately not assessed, and both chips read that
  as "nothing flagged — every slide follows the authoring contract" — directly below a Board
  readiness card correctly saying it had not assessed the deck. They now say so too.

- **Fixed: a Studio test no longer fails at random in a full suite run.** `StudioShell`'s
  "reaches Fabricate from the launcher" test waited on the code-split Fabricate pane with
  Testing Library's 1s default, which is a wait on a module transform rather than on a state
  update and runs past that budget when the machine is busy. It now carries an explicit budget,
  matching the helpers that already do this elsewhere. No product code changes.

- The docs end-to-end suite starts again when an agent runs it on astro 7. astro 7 backgrounds
  `astro preview` when it detects an agentic environment — not unconditionally, and not on a CI
  runner — and a command that exits makes Playwright report
  `Process from config.webServer exited early` before any test body runs. `npm run preview:e2e`
  goes through `docs/scripts/preview-e2e.mjs`, which serves IN-PROCESS through astro's programmatic
  `preview()`, so there is no fork to detect and CI and an agent session behave identically. It
  sets `strictPort`, so a busy port fails loudly instead of sliding to the next one and leaving
  Playwright waiting out its timeout on a URL nothing is serving.

- The docs e2e case that proves the Vetrina stage inherits the host's `--vt-*` tokens reads them as
  colors rather than as strings. astro 7's CSS minifier rewrites author color literals — the page's
  `rgb(20, 120, 220)` ships as `#1478dc` — and a custom property's computed value is the token
  stream that survived the build, not a parsed color, so a literal comparison went red on a
  difference that is purely serialization. The rendered page is unchanged; astro 6 and astro 7
  renders of the Studio, Playground and landing compare pixel-for-pixel equal at all three widths.

- Dependabot pull requests against `docs/` keep installing across the astro 7 bump. The new
  dependency tree placed `@emnapi/core` and `@emnapi/wasi-threads` to satisfy an optional peer of
  `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime`, the shape `build:check` refuses because Dependabot's lockfile writer
  deletes exactly those nodes and `npm ci` then rejects the result. `@emnapi/core` is now a direct
  devDependency of `docs/package.json`; one hard edge clears both, since the second is a plain
  dependency of the first. The built site is byte-identical across the declaration.
