It now uses the engine's own split rule, so setext headings, a heading inside an HTML block and CRLF files split as they render. Finding numbers still count the `---` chunks you wrote. `--fix` and the editor underline now land on the right slide even when the same line appears on both.
- Lint no longer ends a fenced code sample early when it quotes another fence (```` ```js ```` inside ```` ```markdown ````). It also no longer reads prose that starts with three backticks as a fence.

- A chart key sizes its value column to the values it holds. The column was sized for a number ("100%") and right-anchored, so a text value ran left across its own row's name: on five pages of `examples/global-south.md`, a `map highlight` key printed "Caribbean / Central America" over "Global South — North America". The column now grows to its widest value and wraps past about 11 characters. A key whose values are all 5 characters or fewer keeps the old column and renders exactly as before.

- Export to Marp no longer puts a panes deck's markers (`pane: list`, `panes: 35/65`) in the presenter's speaker notes. Marp cannot place two components side by side, so each panes slide exports as its two panes' content, stacked, and looks exactly as it did. Lattice splits some panes slides into one slide per pane; Marp keeps those as one slide. The markers are gone from the exported `.md`, so opening it in Lattice again gives stacked content, not panes. Keep your original deck to go on editing the layout.
- The Studio no longer shows a tooling comment such as `<!-- markdownlint-capture -->` as a slide's speaker note, matching the engine.

- A left-to-right Mermaid flowchart in a tall pane now flows top to bottom, as it does on a portrait slide, in both the exported PDF and the live preview. Before, it stayed wide and its labels shrank to about a third of a full slide's. A 35% pane is tall only under a bare headline: an eyebrow, a subtitle or a Key Insight leaves it square or wide, and the flowchart keeps your direction there.

- `progress` and `matrix-grid` in a side pane give their row names room. The label column was a share of the pane while its type stays slide-sized, so in a 50% pane every three-word name set one word per line and both charts clipped at five rows. In a pane the column now takes its slide width, capped at 40% of the pane (progress) or 24% (matrix-grid, whose `Level 1` cells must still set on one line). Their side budgets return to 6 and 4. Slides without panes, and panes squarer than the slide, are unchanged. `examples/panes-row-labels.md`.
- A status pill in any pane is sized like a slide's. Its height was a share of the pane, so a 50% pane drew each pill 9px tall around 17px of type. progress's track takes slide units in a pane for the same reason.
- A `progress` readout wider than its bar (a small percent in a narrow track) runs on past the bar's end instead of losing its first digit to the fill's clip. A readout that fits is placed as before.

- The exported player's Read · Article view draws a chart pane styled, like a chart slide. Before, it drew black bars with labels several times too large. Each pane now reads as the slide it would be on its own, in the order written, so a KPI pane reads as figures, not a numbered list.
- The Studio's Present steps through a split panes slide. On a square, portrait or story deck, Next shows the second pane before it moves on, Previous comes back to it, and the presenter's next-slide tile shows it. The arrows now count pages, so a one-slide deck whose slide splits can still reach its second pane. Autoplay still advances a slide at a time, showing a split slide's first pane while it reads both.
- Present's frame now takes the deck's shape. It was always 16:9, which cut off everything below the heading on a portrait slide. On a portrait deck the presenter's next-slide tile keeps room for the speaker notes.
- The Studio frames a deck by the size the engine actually renders. `size: 4:3`, `size: Square` and `size: STORY` are not size names the engine knows, so they render at 16:9. The preview used to draw them at the shape the name suggests, leaving an empty band beside the slide.
- A panes slide's markers no longer show up as its speaker note in the Studio, and setting a note no longer deletes them (which turned the slide back into a single component).
- The Studio's slide strip labels a panes slide "panes" instead of "text".

- Under `mode: sketch`, a `list-tabular` ledger's frame hugs its rows. It used to wrap the whole slide body, leaving three rows floating mid-frame between two empty bands. Each row now carries one rule instead of a hand-drawn one beside a straight one, and the row numbers sit clear of the frame's left edge. A `list-tabular` pane looks the same.

- The Guide's resting cursor no longer lands on a chart's labels. It used to avoid only text blocks, so on a phone, where the cursor is large against a scaled slide, it came to rest on values like "$1.8M" or "12,000" (17 of 66 resting places on the Guide test deck at 393 px wide, in WebKit and Chromium). It now avoids every painted word on the slide.

- The Studio's front-matter reference names where `venue:` lives in deck settings (Look → Venue).

- **Studio:** leaving the Studio within a frame of rotating a phone out of landscape no longer stores a preview box measured in the old layout, so the next load's instant shell no longer draws the slide 16px off and jumps when the app takes over.

- **Fixed: Compose, Present and the reading view open offline even if you never opened them online.**
  The Studio fetches both, with the modules they load once open, in the background after
  startup, so the service worker has them when the network drops. Fabricate is fetched the same
  way once you have used it. The background fetch skips Compose, Present and the reading view when the
  browser asks to save data.

- **Fixed: picking a component in the Playground with the preview collapsed shows the component.**
  The pick switches Edit to Explore, and a preview collapsed in Edit kept deferring the render,
  so Explore went on showing the previous deck under the new component's name. A pick (and a
  gallery load) now expands the preview, the same as any other `toPreview` route.
- **Fixed: a webpage export with "Strip speaker notes" ships the scrubbed deck again.** Since
  web images became placeholders (#2387), the bake read the authored render instead of the
  scrubbed one, so a note's whitespace came back in the exported slide. On a deck with a web
  image, no candidate cut could ever match either, so the export always fell back.
- **Fixed: a site palette change no longer blinks the presenter view off or resets the talk
  clock.** Rewriting the Stage let go of its host nodes, and the presenter view, its talk
  clock and the Stage pill were keyed on those nodes rather than on the Stage being open. The
  clock went blank for a frame and re-zeroed on every palette, lens or mode change.

- **The approval prompt for a code package names the right fix when AppArmor turns the OS sandbox off.** On Ubuntu 23.10 and later, AppArmor stops an ordinary user's Chrome from starting its sandbox, and the prompt told them to set `CHROME_PATH`, which cannot help. It now says AppArmor is the cause and names the two fixes: an AppArmor profile for the browser, or the `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` sysctl. Inside a container (a seccomp filter on Lattice and on the container's first process), it names the container's seccomp profile instead: Docker's default profile is what blocks the sandbox there. Each render's warning gives the same remedy, and the other OFF cases each get their own. On macOS and Windows, where the sandbox is the platform's default, a render no longer prints that line as a warning.

- A stats or kpi slide's line typed after its stat list (a `*Source: …*` note followed by a key insight) now reaches Read · Article and the narration, after the stats. Both dropped it before.
- The Studio's first load no longer holds an image slide blank while its photo loads. The preview appears as soon as its fonts are in, showing the photo's placeholder with the slide's text held back until the photo's size is known; before, the whole slide stayed hidden for up to 4 s.
- In the Studio and the other live previews, a video poster still loading now fades in once it has decoded, so a light poster on a dark slide no longer steps from dark to light. A poster already cached shows at once. Exports are unchanged.
- The Studio now offers to load a `video` slide's web `poster`. Before, the poster stayed a hatched placeholder with no way to load it.
- In the live previews, a photo panel or video poster whose picture is still downloading now shows the Underpainting, the house Nacre loader's variant for images: a canvas and soft brushwork in the deck's own colors. The painting fades away once the picture has decoded, so a slide no longer shows an empty panel beside its finished text. A late-arriving photo size now re-fades only that slide's text instead of blinking the whole preview.
- In the live previews, an image slide's card no longer snaps to its photo's shape when the photo's size arrives. While the size is unknown the card takes the common landscape shape, so most photos land without moving, and a portrait, square or panorama glides to its shape instead of jumping, even when the browser pauses to draw the photo. With reduced motion on, the card takes its new shape at once.
- In the live previews, a photo that isn't coming (a web image you haven't chosen to load yet, or one that failed) now shows the same Underpainting, muted and still, instead of a hatched box, so a slide has one placeholder style. Loading a landscape photo then moves nothing, and any other shape glides into place. Exports keep the hatch.

- A table slide narrated as "SMB — Q3: 7.8%; Q4: 9.4%" now focuses the SMB row. The Guide could not match that shape to the row, so table slides focused nothing. A chart's hidden screen-reader table is never matched.

- `authority-chain`'s docs now say which row shape holds how many tiers: five full rows (label, citation, gloss) on a laptop slide, six only as label-and-citation rows, and four when a tier label wraps in the rail. Its venue capacities rise by one tier at laptop, huddle and conference (6-word rows), because the calibration rig had been measuring a two-word label that wraps.

- Status pills (`.chart-status` in progress, timeline-list and kanban), the timeline-list date pill and the numbered `list-steps timeline` disc now take their size from their own text, so the box grows with `venue:` and with a portrait or strip deck instead of staying a fixed size while the text inside it grows past the edge. On a 1280-wide landscape slide the pill grows by 0.4px; on a 4K deck the timeline-list date pill grows from 64.8px to 72px tall, because the box is now 1.6× its text at every size (it was 1.58× at 1280 and 1.44× at 4K).
- roadmap's phase meta pills ("Q2 2026") now follow `venue:` like the rest of the meta text; at `venue: hall` they were still laptop-size.
- Portrait timeline-list: each rail dot now centers on its date pill.
- timeline-list holds one fewer short (~6-word) item at conference and hall (6 and 5, from 7 and 6), re-measured with `tools/calibrate-capacity.js` now that the date pill holds its text; `lint:deck` warns from the new numbers.
- authority-chain: a chain that outgrows the stage (four tiers with glosses at `venue: hall`) now runs long at its tail and is reported as clipped. Before, each card shrank below its own text and the citation and gloss drew over the next card. On a laptop slide the rows take their top and bottom inset from centering rather than padding, so they move by about 1px. The `pyramid` variant closes its tier gap from `--sp-md` to `--sp-sm` so four glossed tiers still fit a laptop stage.

- **Fixed: the bracket-list "cost stays linear" test no longer fails on a busy CI runner.** It
  timed one 16k parse against one 4k parse and failed on `unit (node 22)` in #2421 with nothing
  changed. It now counts the parser's character reads, which no load can move, and times the
  fastest of 40 interleaved samples per size to catch work that reads no characters. Three input
  shapes, a brace run, a mixed list and a quote run, cover every branch of the scan. A mutant that
  rescans characters and one that rescans the quote table both still fail it; 15 of 15 runs pass
  beside 8 CPU hogs on a 4-core box.

- **Fixed: an author with no OpenRouter key can export a narrated webpage with the on-device
  voice.** If the on-device voice finished loading while Share → Webpage was open, the
  "Narration audio" switch stayed disabled and the export shipped with no sound. The panel now
  notices when the voice becomes ready. With the on-device voice chosen, the panel also stops
  quoting cloud billing ("publishes no price", "bills the whole deck", "Connect OpenRouter"). It
  prices the synthesis as free, and it names the voice that will narrate.
- **Fixed: the "Narration audio" switch can always be turned off.** If the cloud voice became
  unavailable while the webpage export panel was open with audio on, the switch stayed on and
  could not be changed. It now only blocks turning audio on.
- **Fixed: an on-device narration that times out no longer says "check your connection".** The
  on-device voice makes no network request, so the export's refusal now names the real cause:
  the voice is too slow on this device.

- A `say:` line written with Markdown (`<!-- say: … **It costs more.** -->`, or a front-matter `say:` entry) now shows and speaks its words without the markup. Present's caption band, the exported player, `lattice video` and the `.vtt` used to show the asterisks. Bold, italics, code spans, strikethrough and links are all read as their text, and a `*` or `_` that is not emphasis, such as `2 * 3` or `snake_case`, is left alone.

- The shared PDF writer (the CLI's PDF export since #2404, not yet released) keeps underlines and strikethroughs. It hid each drawn word by its fill color, and Chrome paints a default-colored decoration with that fill, so the line vanished with the text: a `compare-prose rejected` or `decision` slide showed the rejected option's tag unstruck. The writer now pins each decoration's color before it photographs the slide, so the line stays exactly where the browser drew it.
- The Studio preview numbers a `glossary: auto` deck's slides as its PDF does. The appended glossary slide made the whole-deck render one section longer than the editor's slide count, so the preview fell back to rendering each slide alone, and every slide read "1".

- **A moved `--html`, `--fluid`, `--read` or `--player` export sets its math in KaTeX again.** The CLI page linked KaTeX's stylesheet by its `file://` path in the exporting machine's `node_modules`, so a copy opened anywhere else lost all 20 KaTeX faces and showed the math in Times — a small integral, bare delimiters. A deck that renders math now carries the sheet inline with its faces as `data:` URIs (the player keeps only the faces the deck paints, subset to the glyphs it uses), and a deck without math carries no KaTeX at all. The PDF exports are byte-identical for a standard install (checked on the math and KPI galleries, light and dark); where KaTeX is installed outside Lattice's own package (a hoisted install), the PDF now draws its math as vector text instead of leaving it in the photo layer.

- **Fixed: the overflow tag no longer sits on a framed finish's keyline.** On a slide that
  overflows, the "Content clipped" tag (and the author's "Overflows" tag) sits in the strip
  below the footer, and the frame keyline of `finish: gallery` or a Fabricate frame edge ran
  straight into both of its sides in every export. The keyline now stops short of the tag,
  0.8 cqi on each side. Slides that fit are unchanged.

- **Fixed: speaker notes on a `split-compare` slide now reach the export.** The layout rebuilt the
  slide from its slots and dropped every comment, so a `<!-- note -->` on it never reached the
  PDF annotations, the presenter view or the HTML player, and `<!-- stress-slide -->` could not
  keep the slide on one page. Affected decks gain the missing note: `examples/studio-present.md`
  slide 3 and `examples/stage-console-split.md` slide 2.
- **Fixed: a long footer on a portrait `split-panel` slide holds one line.** In portrait the
  panels stack and the footer spans the page, and a long caption wrapped onto a second line.
  On a page split into a run it also ran on under the k-of-N rail. It now ends in an ellipsis,
  before the page number and, on a split page, before the rail at its widest.
- **Fixed: `split-compare` reads its options and context paragraph from the slide's top level in
  every render path.** A list inside raw HTML above the options (a `<div>`, a table cell) became
  the option cards on the export path, and an option with a nested list and a trailing paragraph
  lost that paragraph to the dark panel when the slide had no context paragraph. Both paths now
  agree. No committed deck renders differently (246 decks checked).

- **Fixed: the Studio renders decks again on the local dev server.** Every preview on
  `npm run dev` showed "This preview couldn't render" because the Studio's image-size memo
  default-imported `lib/core/bg-image.js`, a CommonJS module with its own requires, which the
  dev server serves raw. The `![bg …]` pattern now lives in the require-free
  `lib/core/bg-directive.js`, and a test fails if a docs source imports a CommonJS `lib/`
  file the dev server cannot serve. The production site was never affected.
- **Fixed: a portrait `split-panel pullquote` footer was invisible.** The panels stack in
  portrait, so the footer sits on the white supporting field, and it kept the panel's white
  ink: 1.00:1 on all 32 themes. It now takes the ink of the field it lands on, at 5.05:1 or
  better. `split-panel mirror` on a portrait deck also stacks now, with the featured panel at
  the bottom; before, it stayed side by side and clipped its quote.
- **Fixed: `split-compare` no longer drops an extra paragraph.** A block the layout has no slot
  for (a second context paragraph, a note under the options) vanished from exports and sat in
  front of both panels in the Studio. Both render paths now put it in the options zone, after
  the two cards and before the verdict, and a slide that splits into pages carries it to the
  closing page after the verdict. A blockquote nested inside an option no longer replaces the
  recommendation, a verdict written above the options keeps its own bullets, and a speaker
  note that mentions `<blockquote>` or `<ul>` no longer empties the option cards.
- **Fixed: a split `split-compare` run's closing page showed a stray page number.** On portrait
  and square decks the slide's page number was carried into the closing band as if it were
  content, and the run's `1.4`-style number landed on that copy while the corner kept a bare `1`.
  The closing page now shows one page number, in the corner, with its run suffix. A split-compare
  slide with no verdict no longer ends its run on a near-empty page that held only that stray
  number.

- **`npm ci` builds Lattice on Windows.** The `prepare` step was a shell one-liner that cmd.exe could not run, so a Windows checkout started with no `dist/` and every render failed with "layout CSS not found". It is now `tools/prepare.js`, and the build steps that failed on Windows (the esbuild and tsc calls, the anatomy catalog's console encoding and CRLF output, the CLI bundle's entry path, the agent kit's `import()` of a Windows path) run there.

- **A render on Windows no longer warns "No Chrome binary detected" before rendering with Chrome.** The browser lookup read only `HOME`, which Windows does not set, and knew no Windows build of puppeteer's Chrome. It now reads the user's home on every platform and finds `chrome-win64`.

- **Fixed: a stray `]` inside a chart's bracketed axis or key list no longer swallows a comma.** A quote only protects commas when its closing partner ends a part, and a `]` in the middle of the list was mistaken for the list's own closing bracket. So `['90s cohort, Customer']s spend]` read as one axis instead of two. No shipped deck contained the pattern.

- **Fixed: `split-compare`'s verdict and `split-panel pullquote`'s quote are the first TOP-LEVEL
  blockquote on the export path too.** The string kernel (`lib/core/split-panels.js`) took the first
  `<blockquote>` anywhere and stopped at the first `</blockquote>`. A quote inside a raw `<div>`, a table or a list
  item above the slot became the slot, and a quote nested in the verdict or pull quote cut it short,
  while the preview's DOM path already read `:scope > blockquote`. A speaker note that mentioned
  `<blockquote>` above a pull quote no longer breaks it either. No committed deck changes.

- `split-panel` and `split-compare` now pick their slots the way a browser does on every render path. A quote, list or paragraph inside raw HTML the old string reader did not recognize (a `<span>`, `<main>`, `<template>`, an SVG, a `<script>`, `<style>` or `<textarea>` body, an attribute value) was taken as the verdict, options or lede in the export while the live preview left it in place. Markdown-only decks are unchanged.

- **Fixed: paging through the Print deck preview no longer builds a new preview per page.** The
  preview cells now come from the Studio's shared preview pool, which reuses its frames, and
  printing the same deck again reuses the frame it already printed. On an iPad, where the browser
  never gives a discarded preview back, paging through a long deck used to hold one preview's
  memory per page viewed for the rest of the session.
- **Fixed: the Print deck preview sits on the Studio's own dark surface, not a fixed navy.** Its
  stage now uses the theme's `--surface-inverse`, the surface the landing page's hero preview
  already uses, so it matches the Studio chrome instead of showing a navy panel no theme but
  indaco uses.
- **Fixed: the Print deck preview stage is sized to the paper.** It was a fixed 180px tall, so the
  sheet showed at 264×160 at every width, with dark bands either side, and a portrait sheet shrank
  to about 100px wide. The stage now takes its height from the paper's proportions, so a landscape
  sheet fills the drawer's width (367×223 on desktop), and a portrait sheet is capped at 420px or
  55% of the screen's height.

- CI's golden before/after (`tools/golden-diff.mjs`) now counts only the goldens a pull request moves. It used to diff against `main` as it was when the PR event fired, so a PR opened before a large re-bless rasterized every golden `main` had moved since (469 on #2503) and ran into the job's timeout.

- An Export-to-Marp bundle now follows the deck's plugin admission: a host that narrowed its
  default set (`tools/export-marp.js --default-plugins=none`, `--disable-plugin=…`, or the Studio
  under `LatticePlayground.setPluginDefaults`) writes the plugins it left off into the bundle's
  settings block, and the bundled runtime leaves those Mermaid fences as source and those charts as
  lists, and its Marp config turns Marp's own math off when math is not loaded. Default-set
  bundles are unchanged.
- Under a narrowed plugin set, the Studio's lint and slide rail now split a deck where the engine
  does (with math not loaded, a `---` inside `$$` is a slide break in both).

- The Playground page's preview re-renders when the host changes its plugin defaults
  (`LatticePlayground.setPluginDefaults`), as its editor's lint already did; it used to keep the
  render made under the old defaults until the next keystroke.

- CLI PDF export: digits set with tabular figures (`tnum`, used by tables, glossaries, KPIs and charts) now draw where the screen draws them and copy out of the PDF. Before, "24 hours" drew as "2 4hours" and the digits were missing from the text layer, so copy-paste and screen readers lost them. The 47 committed PDFs that carried the defect are re-rendered.

- The `spark-too-big` one-click resize keeps `$&` and `$'` in a span as written; it built its
  replacement with a string pattern, which would have spliced the matched span into the fix.
- A carousel page whose card title holds `$&` or `$'` (`**Cost $& more.**`) keeps it in its
  page label; the label was spliced in with a string replacement, which turned `$&` into `<section`.
- Author text holding `$&` or `` $` `` no longer corrupts the markup around it in three more places
  that spliced it in with a string replacement: a split-panel slide's class words (the section got
  two `class` attributes), a QR code's label, and the recorded address of a blocked web image in a
  shared or presented deck.
- The same fix for a `meta:` front-matter value (the masthead tile) and a roadmap's status cells
  and horizons cards: `$&` or `` $` `` in the author's text no longer pulls page markup into the slide.

- **Fixed: the required `ci` check no longer passes when the path filter never ran.**
  Every test tier waits on the `changes` job, so when `changes` did not succeed,
  unit, integration and docs-build all read `skipped`, and the gate counted that as
  a pass. `changes` got no runner on #2524's PR run and on the merge-queue groups for
  #2525 and #2535, and both of those merged with no test tier run. The gate now fails
  unless `changes` succeeded.

- **Fixed: the merge queue no longer merges a group whose test tier was cut off.**
  The `ci` gate accepted a `cancelled` tier everywhere, because on a PR a newer push
  cancels the older run. Nothing supersedes a merge-queue run, so there `cancelled`
  means a timeout. In the 39 completed queue runs from 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-05, 11
  merged with `integration` cut off at its 25-minute cap. The gate now fails a
  `cancelled` tier in the merge queue, and `integration`'s cap is 45 minutes,
  measured against a p50 of 1372s with 19 of 41 passing runs at 1461-1500s.

- **Fixed: the Studio chat agent no longer reports a slide as fitting when its diagram had
  not drawn yet.** On a slow link, a session's first diagram could miss the fit check's wait
  while Mermaid was still downloading. The slide was then measured with the diagram's source
  text in its place, and the checker told the agent it fit. The checker now says that slide's
  fit was not measured, and still reports every other slide.

- Editable office export: cards under a `stamp-veil` or `stamp-mark` state stamp now stay part of the slide picture, tinted and under the DRAFT band as the browser draws them; before, the export drew untinted native cards over the stamp. The same holds for anything a slide draws over its cards with its own `::before`/`::after`. A slide whose colors, decorations or shadows have a CSS transition no longer leaves a box in the slide picture under its native shape, or fades it back in after the export.

- The picture-only PowerPoint export (CLI and Studio) is now schema-valid: the notes master is listed where the OOXML schema puts it, and the package no longer declares a slide master per slide that it does not hold. Strict readers have nothing to repair.

- A control character (U+0001 and the like) in a deck title, a speaker note or a slide description no longer makes a PowerPoint export unreadable. The picture `.pptx` (CLI and Studio) and the editable one now drop the characters XML forbids, as the `.odp` already did.

- Studio image exports (PDF, PowerPoint, LibreOffice, Images) number slides as the preview does. Every number drawn with a CSS counter (timeline discs, agenda and step numbers, card tags, lettered milestones) used to export as `0`.

- The narrated Guide acts once per part again: under `delivery: expressive`, a paragraph read as
  several sentences gets one underline, not one per sentence. Prose slides are bound to their
  headings, paragraphs and items, and each sentence of the same part used to replay the act. The
  next sentence of a part now rests, as the unbound path always did; pausing and playing again
  still brings the part back. The exported narrated player gets the same fix.

- The Playground's first-paint snapshot of the default Edit deck drops from 245,584 to 55,829 units against its 245,760 cap: the rule filter now reads nested selectors like `:not(:is(…))` instead of keeping every rule it could not evaluate. A snapshot too large to store is now logged, and an end-to-end test keeps the default deck under half the cap.

- The Vetrina boundary gate (`checkVetrinaBoundary`) now reads side-effect imports, dynamic `import()` and `require()`, as the Suono, Lente and Segno gates already did. Before, `import './../x'` and `import('./../x')` in `docs/src/lib/vetrina/` walked around it.
- The /segno grammar playground reports a crash as a crash, not as a build that "took longer than 1.5 s" (a numeric `start` was one), and says so when its worker cannot load instead of leaving the box blank.
- The /segno playground's 1.5 s limit now times the one request in flight, so typing in the text box no longer keeps a runaway build alive, and a backlog of quick edits is never mistaken for a slow build.
- The /segno grammar reader charges a string by its length toward the 10,000-piece cap. A 25 KB grammar that reused one 20,000-character literal 2,500 times used to pass, generate 100 MB of code and put it in the page.
- The /segno playground caps what its worker sends to the page: at most 50 refusal problems plus a count of the rest, and 256 KB of generated code with a note where it was cut. A 6 KB refused grammar used to send 44,850 problems (92 MB), and a cheap helper reused 4,800 times generated 6 MB of code.
- The /segno playground no longer sends a parse tree over 2,000 nodes or 100 levels deep; it says the text parsed and that the tree is too big to draw. A 5 KB grammar plus 200 characters of text made a 96,000-node tree that froze the page for about 14 s while it was drawn, and a tree 2,400 levels deep overflowed `postMessage` and was reported as "does not build".

- A sequence diagram's participant names now show in the PDF. The shared PDF writer read an SVG `<text>`'s fill from the `<text>` itself, but Mermaid paints the name on the `<tspan>` and gives the `<text>` the box's fill, so every name was drawn in its box's color: in the text layer, invisible on the page. The writer now reads each character's fill from the element that holds it. The same fix covers any SVG label whose `<tspan>` sets its own fill.

- **Fixed: `accent` and `tone-edge` slides keep their solid top bar when a consumer bundles the
  engine CSS with Vite.** Vite 8's default minifier, lightningcss, rewrote the engine's
  `border-image: none` to an empty declaration that the browser drops, so those slides showed the
  spectrum gradient instead. The engine now resets `border-image-source`, which draws the same in
  every Lattice renderer and survives the minifier.

- `spectrum: solid|duo|mono` no longer paints over a slide's own bar. An `accent` slide and a `tone-pass|warn|fail|skip` + `tone-edge` slide keep their solid accent or tone-colored top bar, as they already did in a default-rainbow deck. Before, the deck-wide gradient covered both, so a `tone-fail` slide lost its failure color. Every other slide still carries the deck's style.

- Under `spectrum: solid|duo|mono`, `split-panel` and `split-compare` no longer get a second top bar. The register painted its full-width section border above the frame's own two-segment edge, so the bar read doubled (measured on indaco: 8px duo gradient over the 8px panel bar, in light and dark). The frames now draw their own edge alone, as they do in a rainbow deck.

- A semantic `tone-edge` on `split-panel` and `split-compare` no longer draws a second top bar. The tone border sat above the frame's own ribbon (measured on indaco at 2560 wide: a tone bar, then the 6px ribbon beneath it, in light and dark). The tone color now recolors the supporting-zone ribbon, as `accent` does, and the frame keeps one bar.

- The plugin fence door (not yet reachable from any caller) now declines a slide that holds any raw nested `<section>` (the video pass reads every list item inside one), reads selectors with commas, `:not(…)` and attribute tests correctly, and refuses a malformed plugin entry with a warning instead of throwing.

- The Studio's PowerPoint export in WebKit, the engine behind Safari, now keeps the deck's pictures. WebKit decodes a slide's photos only after the slide is first drawn, and the export shipped that first draw, so slides lost their photos while the toast still said "PowerPoint ready." The capture now warms each photo until WebKit has decoded it, then draws the slide, waiting up to 5 seconds a slide; if a photo still has not arrived, the toast says the export could not load every image. The image set, the chart PNG, the editable Office export and the PDF fallback lanes share the capture and get the same fix. Chromium and Firefox exports are byte-for-byte unchanged. Checked in Playwright's WebKit build; real Safari is not yet checked.

- **Fixed: a `collage bleed` slide on a 4:3, 4:5 or wide deck no longer crops a third of every photo.** The packer assumed a 16:9, 1:1 or 9:16 slide from the deck's orientation, so a deck of another shape had its grid stretched to fit and cropped heavily. It now packs for the slide's real shape: the CLI reads the deck's `size:` and the live preview reads the section's own box. On the demo photos a 4:3 deck drops from 33% to 4% cropped, a 4:5 deck from 24% to 7%, and a 1560x720 phone-landscape deck from 21% to 10% on its worst set. 16:9, square and 9:16 decks render byte-identical. A bleed collage also now weighs empty space more heavily when it picks a layout, so it crops less: over random sets of 4 to 6 photos, mean crop falls from 9-11% to 3.5-4.7% on six canvases. The bleed docs state the real figures in place of "a few percent". New demo: `examples/collage-canvases.md`.

- **Fixed: a JPEG stored rotated (EXIF Orientation) no longer prints sideways in the PDF.** The PDF writer embeds a JPEG's own pixels and ignored its Orientation tag, so a phone photo stored as landscape pixels came out turned a quarter. A rotated JPEG now stays in the slide photo, where the browser has already turned it upright. The `collage` demo deck gains a slide that proves it, using the new `lib/samples/photo-tall-rotated.jpg`.

- **Fixed: a mouse drag across a `collage` photo in the Studio preview no longer opens the photo it ends on.** The Studio opened a photo on any click, and a browser still fires a click when a drag ends, so on a `bleed` slide (where photos cover the slide) a drag could open one. The Studio now ignores a click whose pointer travelled more than 8 px, as the exported player already did; both read the number from `lib/core/collage-tap.mjs`.

- A semantic tone's rail and glow styles now draw on every auto-split page, not only on native ones, including under a `finish:` backdrop. Split pages (`size: story`, `square`) carry the semantic tone as `data-split-mods`, so the rail and glow rules never matched the cover or any `decision` page of a run. Measured on indaco at 2160x3840, `cards-grid tone-warn` then `decision tone-fail`, x=1 at mid-height: the cover and `decision` pages read the page color before; after, all 11 pages read the tone color (`#8A5D00` / `#550014` light, `#EDB85C` / `#E9798C` dark).

- A semantic `tone-edge` now draws its tone color as the top bar on every auto-split page, not only on native slides. Split pages (`size: story`, `square`, and any auto-split run: `split-panel`, `cards-grid`, `checklist`, `decision`, the `split-compare` cover and closing) carry the tone as `data-split-mods`, so the `tone-edge` rule never matched and the page kept the deck's rainbow bar, while a native page in the same run already drew the tone. Measured on indaco at 2160x3840, `split-panel tone-fail tone-edge`, x=300 row 2: `#005586` before; `#550014` (light) and `#E9798C` (dark) after. The same holds under `spectrum: solid`, `duo` and `mono` (the register's bar used to win on split pages), `spectrum: off`, `finish: atrium`, `size: square`, `cuoio` and `print` (ink). On an accent-field cover the 6px bar has low contrast with the field (1.5 to 2.8), as the spectrum bar it replaces did.

- The Studio's Reading view reads a plugin placeholder as a sentence instead of running the plugin's name into its caption: "The plugin `gantt-plugin` draws here once this deck's plugins: list names it.", or, when the deck lists the plugin and this browser has not approved it, "…once its code is approved in this browser." On a slide, the placeholder's caption now ends "not in this deck's plugins: list" instead of stopping on a colon, and never leaves "list" alone on a line.

- The Studio chat's budget gate now prices a picture by the model that reads it. It charged every picture a flat 800 tokens (an attached photo a flat 1,500), which was too low for most vision models at attachment size and about 10x too low for GPT-4o mini. A 3:2 picture at 512 px is 212 tokens on GPT-5 mini, 250 on Claude, 1,290 on Gemini 2.5 and 8,500 on GPT-4o mini; at 1568 px it is 258 to 36,835, a square costs up to 1.5x a 3:2 one, and a thin strip costs Gemini 2.5 up to 1.9x. The figures come from a measured table of 192 vision models (`tools/probe-picture-tokens.mjs`), a `~…-latest` alias is priced as the model it points at, and a model with its own listed image price is charged that too. A hard-stop cap now holds the picture cost on the 192 vision models measured (of 212); the other 20 could not be measured and are charged their vendor's floor (else the default).
- Gemini and other Google models no longer get prompt-cache markers. Measured through OpenRouter on the chat agent's real three-round turn, a marked request cost more than an unmarked one on every Google model tried (7% to 83% more on a cold turn, 1.4 to 4.2 times as much on a repeat turn) because Google caches implicitly. Anthropic is unchanged. The Workspace "Reuse the cached prompt" switch is now offered only for Anthropic models, the only ones a marker does anything for. The same marker was sent by the Coach's per-finding Fix; it now follows the same rule. A hard-stop cap now covers every spending action, not only the chat, whenever the price is known: `cloudBudgetBlock` waits (at most 4 seconds, stop mode with a cap only) for the price catalog when it has not loaded, the catalog is fetched as soon as a key exists (at connect, at the OAuth return, at Undo after Disconnect), concurrent requests share one fetch, and a hung fetch is abandoned after 15 seconds. Before, the first chat turn on a fresh browser profile, and the Coach's Fix and the refine and generate actions on a profile that had not opened the model tab, had no price and ran past the cap. A call that stays unpriced after the wait (the catalog down, or a router model with no price) still passes, as before. The Library's Suggest charges the picture to the budget gate by the model that reads it, too.
- A vision model the price table has not measured (released since, or whose probe failed) is charged its vendor's 90th percentile for a picture instead of the default, and `node tools/probe-picture-tokens.mjs --check` lists, with no key and no spend, the live vision models the table has not seen. The chat cost readout now applies Anthropic's cache write and read rates only to a request that carries a cache breakpoint; any other request is quoted at the base rate, an upper bound for vendors that cache on their own.

- A video clip shorter than 1.5 seconds is now refused in the chat with a plain message ("Record at least 2 seconds"), in both the device picker and the Library picker. A video model reads about one frame a second, so a clip that short gave it nothing to look at, and it answered with an invented description or said it could not see the video.
- The Architect is now told, in your message, that a clip came with it and is shown to it there. An iPhone clip is sent under the `video/mov` type that OpenRouter's guide lists.
- The message that explains why a video cannot be attached is now easy to read: full-strength text with a warning mark instead of small faded red text, and it says what to do. A clip from the Library, whose length is known, gets the length to trim to, for example "This video is 16.4 MB and the limit is 15 MB. Trim it to about 7 seconds or less, then add it again."; a clip from the device that is over the size limit is refused before it is read, so it is told to trim to a few seconds.

- The Studio chat now judges photos and video in a mixed pick separately. Before, one refusal (a full photo shelf, a clip already pending, a model that reads only one kind) dropped the whole pick, so the part that would have been accepted was lost too. Now the accepted kind attaches and the refused kind is explained in words.

- A very large deck no longer falls back to Chrome's print when the PDF writer needs more than 3 minutes. Puppeteer's 180 s per-call limit cut the writer off before its own watchdog (slides x 4 s), so a 151-slide deck such as `themes/palette-audit.md` came out as a Chrome print (Type 3 fonts) on a slow machine and as the composed PDF on a fast one. The render now raises that limit to one hour; every call stays bounded by the render guard.

- The Studio and Playground preview now clear a legacy finish's mask on a split panel, as the
  CLI export already did. The reset's selector packed to a section inside a section and matched
  nothing, so the panel painted white under its white text.

- Removed nine `:where(.lattice-exporting) section…` selector arms that matched nothing in the Studio and Playground preview (the packer scoped them as a section inside a section) or anywhere else: the export class is always stamped on the section, and each arm had a `section….lattice-exporting` sibling that does the work. Saved finishes no longer emit the dead arm; older saved CSS still works. The slide renders identically; the css-scope guard now also fails on `section :where(…) section`.

- The `/segno` playground's time-limit message no longer blames a long `alt()`, which Segno now refuses in well under the limit. It names the cause that still reaches it: a long text run through a grammar that builds a large tree per character (deeply nested `node()` calls), and suggests a shorter text or flatter nesting.

- **Fixed: the route budget no longer charges a pull request for bytes it did not add.** Two
  esbuild plugins in `tools/build-playground.js` gave modules absolute paths, and esbuild names
  the engine's shared chunks from those paths, so the engine's eager JS moved by a few bytes with
  the folder the repo sat in. `measure-route-base.sh` builds the base in a temp folder, so a PR
  with no bundled change failed the docs build on +2 bytes. The plugins now return repo-relative
  paths, and the build fails if any module path is absolute.
- **Fixed: a route's `htmlRaw` now measures the same in every checkout.** Astro's island `uid`
  hashed each component's absolute path at a variable length, so page sizes moved 1–3 bytes
  between folders. It never failed a PR, because only eager JS is compared against `main`.
  `docs/scripts/stable-island-uids.mjs` rewrites each uid after the build at a fixed length, which
  makes pages with islands a one-time 1–17 bytes larger.

- **Fixed: "Copy as HTML" keeps a `diff` line's band and a `mark=` line's tint.** The copy wrote each run's own background, so a pasted block showed the bands as ragged patches behind some words and none behind others. Each banded line now pastes as one full-width band, written as `rgba()` so a word processor or mail client reads it.
- **Fixed: `lint:deck` checks a `@code{…}` record inside a blockquote.** The render applied a record written under `>`, but the lint read only unquoted lines, so a bad field or a line range past the end of a quoted block said nothing. It now gets the same four checks as any record.
- **Fixed: a code block's copy buttons show their tooltip in the Studio preview.** The preview takes no pointer events, so hovering a button there left it dim and its label hidden. The Studio now passes the pointer's position into the preview, and the buttons and their labels respond as they do in the Playground.
- **Fixed: `code-line-clipped` judges every slide against the width it really has.** The column budgets are now measured in Chromium for every canvas and every class that moves the code panel: `claim-*` and `compact` (which the rule used to skip), a `venue:` or `scale-*` (which it ignored on a plain slide, so a 90-column line at `venue: conference`, where 68 fit, said nothing), and `align-*` or `stats`. `capacity-scale` reads the same table, so a 60-column line at `venue: hall` and an 89-column one at `venue: huddle`, which render whole, are no longer named. `node tools/measure-code-columns.js --write` re-measures the table.
- **Fixed: a code block's copy buttons no longer sit over its code.** They floated at the panel's top right, so a long first line ran under them (from about 95 columns at 16:9 and 40 at portrait). They now sit in the block's title bar, which every copy block has (empty without `title=`) in every surface, so the browser and the PDF lay the block out alike. The buttons take the bar's type size instead of the browser's 13px, which left them tiny on a 4K deck, and a long `title=` wraps inside the bar instead of running off the panel.
- **Fixed: `lint:deck` counts what a code block draws beside and above its lines.** The width rule counted the text alone, so a line with `numbers` or `diff` on was named only once its text, without the gutter, outran the panel. Under a `venue:` or `scale-*`, the line-capacity rule counted source lines alone, so a block with a title or copy bar, or with `wrap` lines that wrap to two rows, clipped at a venue with no finding. Both now count it, from a measured table of what the bar costs at each canvas and room size. `code-line-clipped` also no longer names the 48-column `compare-code` lines in the 4K galleries, which render whole: the measured 4K pane was a float error short of 48.

- `list-steps converge` keeps every band's text at 4.5:1 or better in every theme, light and dark. The second band now mixes 12% accent (was 32%) and the third 92% (was 66%); the old third band measured 3.01:1 on indaco.

- `export-marp` now ships every palette the deck's palette extends, all the way up its chain. A Marp bundle used to carry only the palette and its `-dark` companion, so a palette that `@import`s a parent rendered without its colors in Marp: `atelier-dark` shipped without `atelier`, and `a11y-deuteranopia` without `a11y-base` or `onyx`. Five example decks were affected. The Studio's export already walked the chain; the CLI now reads the same declared graph (`THEME_EDGES`).

- Mermaid diagrams in an Export-to-Marp bundle no longer go blank in the Marp for VS Code preview. VS Code's built-in `mermaid-markdown-features` extension removes every `<svg>` inside a `.mermaid` element each time it processes a Markdown preview: on load and on every update. When it ran after the Lattice runtime had drawn, the diagrams vanished and stayed blank while the source stayed hidden. The runtime now redraws a diagram whose SVG another script removed, from its cache, or re-renders it when nothing is cached. Measured on code-server 4.141.0 with marp-vscode 3.6.1 at the Disable security level: 4 blank runs in 19 before the fix, 0 in 12 after it (the strip fired in 5 of those 12, and every diagram came back).

- `actors`: a roster of five to seven rows now renders each row as one line (responsibility, body, chip), so the seven-row ceiling fits the stage when each body is one line (about 10 words); longer bodies wrap and still overflow. Before, the stage seated four two-line rows and every title overprinted its body from the fifth.

- The contrast checker reads gradient backdrops. It used to score text only against the nearest flat `background-color`, so `topic`'s dark tab labels on its light bottom band scored 1.02:1 (they now score 10.5:1), and any slide that paints a band, rail or scrim as a `linear-gradient` layer was scored against the wrong color. It evaluates each linear gradient at the text's own position (size, position, repeat, angle, hard stops, OKLab for `color-mix` stops) and composites it over the background color; the gates that share it kept their pinned counts. Radial, conic and `url()` backdrops are unchanged.

- The Architect's figure-change cue now reads `T` as trillions, so a reply that drops or swaps it (`$5T` → `$5`) is flagged, and `$5T` → `$5,000B` is not. `bn`/`Bn`/`BN` already read as billions there.

- A CLI export (PDF, PNG, HTML) now shows `![bg]` and `![bg contain]` on an ordinary slide, the same picture the Studio shows. It used to print a blank slide with no warning.
- A relative image in slide text (`![a](pic.jpg)`) now loads when `-o` writes the export to another folder. It resolves against the deck's folder, not the output folder.

- Narration and `--captions` now speak a `wifi` slide's network name and security type, not just its heading. The password is never spoken or captioned.

- The Read · Article copy of a diagram or chart nested in a blockquote, list or table now gets its own ids, so an exported player no longer holds the same `id` twice for it.

- The CLI now draws a Mermaid fence written inside a blockquote or at the second level of a list (for example under `10. Tenth step`) in the PDF, the images and `--player`, as the Studio and the preview already did. Before, it printed the source, and every later diagram's `data-mmd-idx` shifted against the Studio's file.

- **Fixed: a Mermaid diagram inside a quote or a list item draws at its natural size in the Studio.** It kept a fixed
  1152×480 box meant for pages that are not slides, filled the stage, pushed the paragraphs after it off the slide and
  flagged the slide as overflowing, where the CLI's PDF fit. The Studio's webpage export now matches the CLI's
  `--player` file byte for byte on such decks. And a diagram fence indented under a bullet now stays inside its list
  item in the CLI's PDF instead of breaking the list.
- **Fixed: a `![bg]` picture on an `image` slide lands on the slide the engine says it is on.** The engine now draws
  the image panel from its own reading of the deck, so a setext heading (`Title` over `---`), a `***` rule, a `---`
  inside `$$` or a class directive indented as code no longer puts the panel on the wrong slide or on none. A picture
  inside a line of prose on an `image` slide becomes the panel too, instead of the slide's background. Two shapes are
  now plain text, as markdown reads them everywhere else: a `![bg]` written inside a raw HTML block, and a URL with a
  space in it (write `![bg](<my photo.jpg>)`).
- **Fixed: an `image` pane on a tall deck draws its photo in the image layout's panel.** On a 9:16 (or square,
  portrait, mobile) deck, panes become one page each, and the image pane's photo filled the whole page behind its
  title. It now takes the image layout's composition, as an `image` slide does. A 16:9 deck that lays the panes out
  side by side is unchanged.
- **Fixed: a caption written straight under a diagram renders as text in the CLI's exports.** A line right after a
  closing Mermaid fence, with no blank line between, joined the drawn figure's HTML and showed its markdown raw
  (`**bold**`), and under a list item it swallowed the next item too. It now renders as a paragraph with its
  formatting, flat, inside a quote and inside a list item, as the Studio shows it.

- The Studio's PDF, images (.zip), PowerPoint and LibreOffice exports no longer print the authoring overflow marker (red ring, "OVERFLOWS", "Fix Me") into a clipped slide for the recipient; they carry the workspace's export setting, `reader` by default, which shows a calm "Content clipped" pill. A clipped slide in these files looks different from before.

- **A hand-written deck can no longer stall `--player` export, and a hand-written quote spelling no longer ships a local path.** The player's local-file inliner now works on the parsed document instead of tokenizing the HTML text by hand: a 1 MB deck of unclosed quotes (`<a "`) ran past five minutes and now takes about a quarter of a second, and `style="background:url(&#34;file:///…&#34;)"` (any numeric spelling of a quote) is baked in instead of leaving the absolute path in the shared file. A `<img <src=…>`, a duplicate `src`, a `<plaintext>` tail, a `<script><!--<script>` nest and an image inside a `-->`/`--!>` comment are no longer read as pictures. Decks the engine writes export byte-identical.
- **The player now also bakes pictures named in `srcset`, `<video poster>`, SVG `<image>` and CSS `image-set()`.** A local `file://` address in one of those positions used to ship as an absolute path in the shared file; each is now baked in or, outside the deck folder, drawn as the stand-in.

- The stylesheet safety scan no longer stalls on a sheet full of unclosed `url(`. Those 50,000 unclosed `url(` took 10.9 s, and now take a fraction of a second. The scan now also reports a `url(` left unclosed at the end of a sheet, which a browser still fetches.

- In the runtime (Export-to-Marp decks and the VS Code Marp preview), an `actors` row that ends on a spark `~{…}` or an inline state mark `[x]` now keeps it beside the bold label, as the engine does; it used to land inside the label. An avatar or icon is kept beside the label once its drawing is loaded. Fidelity probes compare the engine and the runtime bundle for each kind, with the drawings preloaded.

- The Studio preview now follows a host that narrows its plugin defaults while a deck is open: a diagram whose plugin goes off returns to its source, and draws again when the plugin comes back, with no edit and no reload.

- The Studio's Webpage (.html) export now draws the logo wall packed in equal-weight rows, as the live preview does. The Studio inlines each mark as `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,…`, and the wall's shape reader accepted only a bare or `;base64` data URI, so every wall in that export fell back to equal cells.

- **Export to Marp no longer puts Lattice-only settings in the speaker notes.** Marp shows a comment of keys it
  does not know as a presenter note, so a slide's `_focusSteps`, `_build`, `_track` or `_logo` comment reached the
  recipient's PowerPoint and PDF notes, in either spelling. The export now leaves those comments out of the bundle;
  a comment that also holds a key Marp knows stays whole. (`lib/export/marp-directives.mjs`)
- **The Studio's Export to Marp lifts `![bg]` before it bakes heading splits,** as the CLI does. Run last, an image
  slide with two headings lost its picture panel and Marp drew the photo full-bleed behind the text. Both producers
  now share one pass list, and a test fails if either reorders it. (`docs/src/components/studio/export/deck-export.js`)
- **A slide-record field that cannot reach Marp whole stops the CLI export** with its line, and the Studio says it in
  the export note, instead of the field going missing in silence. (`tools/export-marp.js`)

- **The Studio's slide panel no longer writes records into a deck that does not use them.** Adding a field to a
  slide written in directive comments writes the comment form (`<!-- _footer: Q3 -->`), and a new pane marker from
  Compose is `<!-- _pane: bar -->`, so a deck stays readable in Marp and VS Code until the cut. A slide that already
  has a record still gets the field in its record. (`lib/core/meta-edit.mjs`)
- **The slide panel no longer edits the wrong record.** It edits only a record the engine reads, never its copy in a
  blockquote or list item, and a field set in two places (two records, or a record and a comment) is read-only, as two
  `_class` comments are, because clearing one would bring the other back.
- **Compose refuses a pasted directive in any spelling.** A pasted record (`<!-- {background-image="url(…)"} -->`) or
  bare directive (`<!-- backgroundImage: url(…) -->`) could set a slide attribute, the second on every later slide;
  both are refused as a pasted `_class:` is. Compose also reads a record's class, and a comment with text after it
  can no longer pull the rest of the slide into the slide's directives. (`docs/src/lib/compose/`)
- **More readers take a record:** Present's section rail (`{layout=divider}`), the asset rename, the lint's pane split
  (`{layout=columns, class=ratio-35-65}`) and the `{stress-slide}` marker. Lint names a field set by two records of one
  slide, and checks a record that also holds a marker.
- **The D11 gate catches the write shapes it missed:** `attrPush`, `dataset`, `setAttributeNS`.
- A slide with thousands of nested records no longer takes seconds a keystroke in the slide panel.
- **Present's section rail reads a slide's class the way the engine does.** A `divider` set in a comment that holds
  several keys (`<!-- _class: divider` on one line, `paginate: false` on the next) now opens a section, and a
  `_class: divider` comment inside fenced or indented code no longer makes a phantom one.
  (`docs/src/components/studio/present-sections.ts`)
- **Editing a slide in Compose no longer changes what the slide applies.** Compose lifts a setting to the top of the
  slide only when the engine applies it there and moving it changes nothing: an example in indented code or inside an
  HTML block stays put, and a setting never moves past one that stays in place and sets the same field (a bare
  `<!-- class: dark -->`, one in a quote, or a record's other fields). Nothing after a pane marker leaves its pane,
  a record with a speaker note stays put so the notes keep their order, and a setting between two lists stays so the
  lists do not merge (also when the first list's last item runs onto more lines, lazy or indented, or several
  settings, one-line or multi-line, sit between them). A setting indented in a list item after a blank line stays,
  so a loose list is not drawn tight. A spot `_class` or a record's class still moves past a bare `class:` kept in
  place, because the local one wins in either order. A slide where a setting would be taken into a list item
  (indented under one, or right below one or its lazy next line, a note between them or not, pane markers included) opens in Markdown, because Compose would write it back as list text. A seeded test
  renders random slides before and after a Compose edit, through the editor's own parser and serializer, and
  requires the same slide class, style, panes, lists and loose or tight items.
- **Present's section rail reads a quoted divider** (`<!-- _class: "divider" -->`).
- **A speaker note no longer locks a field.** A note with a line that starts `focus:` or `class:` is not a second
  place the field is set, so the slide panel still edits the record. A field set twice shows the value that wins.
- **A record after an unclosed `<!--` inside a code block applies again.** The engine paired the fenced `<!--` with
  the record's own `-->` and dropped both as code, so `<!-- {layout=kpi} -->` after such a block did nothing.
- **A record after an unclosed `<!--` inside an inline code span applies again**, for the same reason.
- **The same holds for a `<!--` inside a double-backtick span** (``` ``<!--`` ```): spans are matched by backtick-run
  length, as CommonMark does.

- The installed `lattice` command no longer crashes with `Invalid manifest: dist/styles/manifest.json: name must be a non-empty string`. The crash hit any deck with a class the CLI checks against the deck linter, meaning anything that is not a component or a reserved name, such as `ratio-50-50` on a pane slide. The bundled component loader walked `dist/` instead of `lib/components/` and read the CSS-module index as a component manifest. The loader now resolves `lib/components/` from the package root, the same way it already finds the manifest schema.

- A photo alone in a plain `columns` or `rows` pane is now fitted to its pane and centered, never cropped. Before, a picture taller than its pane ran past the pane's edge and the export stamped "Content clipped": five of the twelve slides in a four-shapes-by-three-shares matrix (wide at 75%; tall at 50% and 75%; square at 50% and 75%); after, none do, in light and dark. The picture scales down to fit and never up past its own pixels. An `image` pane keeps its cover crop, prose that holds an inline picture still flows as text, and the pane slides of nine existing decks (74 slides) render pixel-identical.

- An export no longer slows down, or lists the same missing picture over and over, when a long `srcset` repeats an address that has no local path (a `file://host/…` share, or on Windows a path with no drive letter). The address is tried once.

- The Studio now picks up a re-imported plugin right away when only its manifest changed, such as its return fields, inline kinds or placeholder. It used to keep the old declaration until the page was reloaded, so a widened declaration did not ask for approval again in that session.
- The Studio's one-line "did not draw" strip now carries its full reason as a hover title, because a long reason was cut off at the strip's width.

- In a Live session, a person's text caret now shows on everyone else's editor when it sits at the very end of the deck (or at the start with a left-leaning position). The session's cursor check dropped the empty `item` field that a caret at the end carries, Yjs then threw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'client')", and the editor's remote-caret plugin crashed and stopped drawing every caret for that viewer. The check now keeps the empty fields in the form Yjs reads (`item`, `type` and `tname` as `null`, `assoc` as a number), and a test round-trips end, start and middle positions through it.

- **Live sessions render the deck the same way for everyone.** A deck used to follow each member's own site palette and light/dark mode, so the host could see a navy slide while a guest saw a cream one. The host's palette and mode are now frozen when the session starts and apply to every member's preview of a deck with no `theme:`, and the mode to any deck that pins none, through a host drop and a takeover. A host whose own palette is a saved theme is told it is not shared yet, and everyone sees the default theme. Each member's Studio keeps its own palette around the deck, and exports are unchanged.

- **A tour started in a live session no longer types into the shared deck.** It used to ask whether to end the session, and if you said no it went on typing into everyone's deck; it now plays on a practice deck and leaves the session alone.

- The Studio's "wants to join" toast now closes the moment the knock is resolved by any path (the Live panel's Admit or Deny, auto-admit, or the guest leaving), instead of lingering and offering to admit someone already in. It withdraws only its own pill, so a newer Undo toast sharing the slot is left alone (`dismissActionNotice` in `docs/src/lib/notify.ts`).

- The Playground now holds the previous Mermaid diagram on screen while an edited one redraws, as the Studio does, instead of leaving the slot empty for about 11 frames per keystroke.

- Reloading with the editor collapsed no longer re-shows the "Editor collapsed." toast; only a collapse the person makes does.

- Compose keeps a heading that spans two lines. A setext heading (`Title`, then `line two`, underlined with `===` or `---`) was dropped whole when its slide was edited, because a heading could not hold a line break; it now keeps both lines, its level and its break, at the top level and inside a quote or list. Where the two-line form would not read back as the same heading, Compose writes one `#` line with a space for the break. A heading that ends in an escaped `\#` keeps its escape.

- Compose no longer starts the caret inside a folded slide after the deck reloads. A reload (a rail slide op, the add-slide gallery, a Markdown round trip) rebuilt the editor with the caret at the top of the deck, then restored the folds, so a folded first slide with no heading left the caret in its hidden paragraph and the first keys edited text the author could not see. The caret now starts on the first text of a slide that is open.

- A note half typed in Compose is no longer lost when you switch decks. The field never blurred, so its words were never written; the editor now writes them to the deck you are leaving as it closes, and nothing reaches the deck you are opening.

- **A status pill in a pane holds its box when a finish drops its border.** The pane's pill sizing set `padding: 0`, so under `etch` and `tone` the pill would have shrunk 2px; it now gives back the border like the pill outside a pane.

- **Fixed: a returning visit to the Playground no longer opens on a blank preview.** On the
  published site, reloading the Playground in the desktop split view left the preview pane
  empty: the cached-slide placeholder stayed in the layout at full window height and pushed
  the live slide below the window. The placeholder now stays out of the layout once the live
  slide takes over.
- **Fixed: the Playground's instant preview of your last slide now shows on the published
  site.** The same rule clipped the placeholder to zero height while it was meant to show, so
  a returning visit waited for the full app to load before any slide appeared. The last slide
  you worked on now paints straight away.

- Browsing a deck with panes in the Studio is faster and no longer jumps. Each slide of such a deck used to load its own ~1.3 MB stylesheet, because pane rules were composed only for the components on the slide shown. The Studio's slide frame now asks for a sheet that twins every pane component, so all of a deck's slides share one (1,306 KB to 1,489 KB raw, 144 to 154 KB gzipped, for the panes example deck). Click-to-paint on the production build, median of 3 passes over the 8-slide panes deck: revisiting a slide 91 to 65 ms in Chromium and 275 to 94 ms on an emulated iPhone (WebKit); the first visit to each slide 260 to 176 ms and 381 to 259 ms; a deck without panes takes 58 ms. Only the Studio's live frame opts in: the CLI, the player and the Studio's exports keep the sheet for exactly their own panes.
- A slide no longer paints under the previous slide's stylesheet. Moving into the first pane slide put its table at the wrong height for about 120 ms (260 px, then 306 px) until the new sheet finished parsing. The restyle path now waits for the new sheet to load, then writes the frame style, author CSS and body together; a render that started in the meantime wins.

- **Explore → Edit → Explore in the Playground comes back to the slide the reader was on.** Switching to Edit
  replaces the editor's text with the deck Explore is showing, which put the caret on line 1, so Explore reopened on
  slide 1. The caret now goes to the end of the title of the slide Explore was on, as a click on that slide already
  did.

- The editable PPTX export (`--editable`) no longer hides a focused column's text. A `_focus: col N` column's tint and ring become one picture that spans every row, and the column's header and last cell were drawn under it, so they vanished. Each focused cell's text is now drawn above the picture. The default picture PPTX and the PDF were never affected.
- A highlighted card (`_focus: item N` with `_focusStyle: highlight`) exports to the editable PPTX as a native card with a blue inside edge, grouped with its title and body text. It used to be a flat picture, because Calco could not draw an inset `outline`.

- **Fixed: the phone demo no longer drops its last keystroke.** The Studio's markdown editor
  reported each text it was handed back to the Studio as an edit. When that report ran late, it
  overwrote the newer text, so "My First Deck" saved one character short (`- Sentiment \`5`, no
  closing backtick) on real WebKit. The editor now reports a synced text only when the sync changed
  it, which today means stripping a leading BOM.

- **Fixed: in a Live session, adding a slide no longer moves other people to the wrong slide.** When a
  collaborator added a slide just before the one you were watching, your view jumped to the new blank
  slide, and the person who added it was pulled back to the slide they added it after. Each slide now
  keeps its identity through adds, moves, duplicates and deletes, so everyone stays where they were and
  the author lands on the slide they added.

- **Fixed: in a deck that splits on headings, the slide actions act on the slide you see.** A deck written
  without `---` is one block that renders as several slides. Before this fix, Duplicate copied the whole block,
  Move did nothing, a new slide landed at the end and Delete was refused. Now each action cuts the block at that
  slide's heading, which renders the same, and acts on that one slide.

- **Fixed: moving, adding, duplicating or deleting a slide keeps its front-matter `say:` narration on that slide.**
  The `say:` map is keyed by slide number, so before this fix, moving slide 1 later left its words narrating the slide
  that took its place. The Studio's slide actions, and Compose's add and delete, now renumber the map with the slides.
  A deleted slide's entry goes with it, and a duplicate gets a copy.

- **Fixed: adding, moving, duplicating or deleting a slide in the Studio no longer rewrites the rest of
  the deck.** Before, every slide action rebuilt the whole file: it trimmed every slide's spacing and
  turned `***` separators into `---`. Moving the last slide of a 30-slide deck rewrote nearly all of
  it, so the editor saw one huge change. Now an action changes only the slides it involves, and keeps
  your separators and spacing everywhere else. On that 30-slide deck, the change is the two swapped
  slides and their separator: 47 of 757 bytes.
- **Fixed: deleting the last slide lands on the new last slide.** It landed on the slide before it.

- A list row on an `image statement` slide now takes the card ink, the same as the paragraph, so it reads on the scrim. Before, it kept the theme's text color, which in a light deck put dark rows on the dark scrim. The Studio's photo-contrast check now measures a statement's list rows too.

- Editable PPTX/ODP export: text lifted above a focused column's picture is now drawn right after that picture, so a box painted later stays above the text.
- Editable PPTX/ODP export: a focused table row's ring is drawn as one native outline, where it came out in pieces that did not meet (a picture in the end cells, lines in the rest).

- The editable `.pptx` and `.odp` no longer cut the last letters off a letter-spaced translucent label that sits on a translucent panel. LibreOffice dropped the tracking from the width of text with an opacity, so a dark `collage bleed` eyebrow read "THE ATELI". The reader now writes such a label in its flattened color, blended over the panel's own color, as it already did over a gradient. Plain, unspaced translucent text keeps its opacity.

- An export to `.pdf`, `.pptx`, `.odp` or `.png` no longer overwrites and then deletes a `deck.html` the author keeps beside `deck.md`, and two exports of one deck no longer collide on it. The temporary HTML page the export is captured from now has a name only that run owns (`<out>.lattice-<pid>-<random>.html`). A sibling `deck.html` survives byte-for-byte; `--keep-html`, `--player`, `--fluid`, `--read` and extensionless outputs still write `<out>.html` as before.

- The Playground editor no longer jumps when you click a line while the page is busy. The sync read its own
  preview scroll as yours when the browser delivered the scroll event late, and moved the editor to follow.

- **Fixed: the iOS Simulator platform suites now restart a device once when safaridriver cannot start a session, instead of failing at once.** Every iOS failure in `main`'s first three nightlies was a session that never started, so no test ran. `docs/scripts/ios-safari/run.mjs` now reports that case with its own exit code, and `run.sh` answers it once by rebooting the simulator, relaunching Safari and restarting safaridriver, within a time budget that keeps the job under its 30-minute limit. A failed probe is still a failure and is not retried. The Studio suite's photo check now closes the Coach sheet on an iPad with the sheet's own close button rather than a synthetic Escape, which the iPad simulator sometimes ignored. The Studio suite's photo check is now its own suite, `ios-safari-photo`, so each runs only when its own code changes and neither runs out of the job's 30 minutes.

- **The Studio stays responsive while it exports a PDF.** The vector PDF export used to read every slide in one uninterrupted task and then write the file on the page: on a 40-slide deck at phone-class CPU speed that froze the Studio for up to 4.3 s at a time. It now yields between slides and writes the file in a background worker, so the longest freeze is about 1.7 s. The PDF it produces is byte-for-byte the same.

- **Downloaded on-device models survive a site update.** The service worker's update step deleted every Cache Storage entry it did not own, including the on-device voice (about 80 MB) and the on-device chat model, so each site update made the next use download them again. It now deletes only its own stale caches.

- **histogram:** a long last edge label (`$120k`, `$250M`) no longer runs out of the chart and gets cut at the slide edge. An edge label that would cross the chart's edge now anchors inward; one that fits stays centered under its tick.

- **Fixed: a portrait `timeline-list` with status tags no longer clips its last milestone.**
  On a tall or strip deck each status tag sat on its own line under the milestone title,
  so four milestones with three tags ran 109px past a portrait slide and the fourth
  milestone's description never painted. The tag now sits at the end of the title's row,
  and the description keeps the full width beneath it.

- A theme that names a web picture the deck has not allowed no longer makes the Studio's export say "the export could not load every image". The capture refuses that picture on purpose and draws the placeholder, so the file is complete; a picture that is really missing is still named.

- The Studio's export reads each `url()` in a slide's computed style with the renderer's own CSS reader, the security spine's one reader, instead of a regex of its own. A `content` string that only spells `url(https://…)` keeps its text instead of being cleared, and an escaped address is read the way the browser reads it. Exports of ordinary decks are unchanged.

- A picture export (PNG, JPEG, and the PDF's photo layer) now draws a background written as `u\72l(…)` or with an escaped address, the way the browser does; it came out blank before. The camera reads CSS with the renderer's own reader, so a `url(` inside a comment or a string is no longer fetched. Exports of ordinary decks are byte-identical.
- In Safari, a picture written inline as a `data:` URL of about half a megabyte or more is drawn at its size in a picture export. The check for a valid `url()` gave up on a token that long and dropped the picture.

- **Fixed: a Studio notice raised just as the previous one closed no longer vanishes, and neither does the next one.**
  Sonner shows a toast one macrotask after it is raised, so a message raised a moment before the current pill's
  2.6 s dwell ended reused that pill's id and merged into it after it had started closing. The message vanished, and
  the notice slot still pointed at the dying pill, so the next message vanished too. That is how "Saved .pricing-trio"
  never showed after a component generate in studio-smoke. `notify.ts` now judges a close by the pill's id and raises
  the swallowed message again on a fresh pill.

- **Fixed: on an iPad, Safari's own undo no longer loses a word typed just after the Studio opens.** The deck editor rebuilt
  itself when the component list finished loading, a moment after the Studio painted, and replaced the text you had just
  typed with a fresh copy. WebKit's undo step still pointed at the old copy, so Edit → Undo, the keyboard bar and shake did
  nothing for that word, although the Studio's own Undo button still worked. The editor now updates its lint in place and
  keeps its view.
- **Fixed: on an iPad or iPhone, Safari's own undo works after the live preview redraws.** iOS empties Safari's undo list
  every time the preview's frame reloads, so Edit → Undo, shake, the three-finger swipe and the keyboard bar's undo key
  stopped reaching the Studio for whatever you had just typed. The Studio now keeps that list armed while it has
  something to undo, without touching your text, the caret or redo.

- **Fixed: the Studio raster-export marker spec read the wrong pixel, so its images and PowerPoint arms failed on every
  engine while the exports were right.** The reader pill ("Content clipped") is in both pictures. Its rail stands one
  spectrum-bar width above the slide's bottom edge, so on a 2560×1440 picture the pill spans rows 1400–1431, and the
  spec sampled row 1437. `docs/e2e/studio-raster-export-marker.spec.ts` now samples at 98.2% of the height, which is
  inside the pill at every size measured, and each arm also checks that the slide that fits has no pill there, so the
  oracle can fail.
- **Fixed: a Studio command palette that was already open never showed a row that started to apply while it was
  open.** "Fix all issues" joins the list once lint has counted a fixable issue, often after ⌘K opened, and an open
  palette filtered to "Fix all" never listed it, even after a retype; only closing and reopening did. cmdk took each
  row's value from its rendered text, and a row that did not match yet rendered nothing, so it never got a value to
  match on. The Actions, Layout, Switch deck and Theme rows now name their `value` (the Learn rows stay mounted, so they never hit it). `docs/e2e/studio-palette-late-row.spec.ts` holds lint back at the
  network until the palette is filtered, then waits for the row without closing; it fails on the old code in Chromium,
  Gecko and WebKit at desktop and phone widths.

- **Fixed: the Studio's browser tests no longer pass or fail on the clock.** Every fixed sleep, stopwatch and
  unseeded random draw in `docs/e2e` outside the files other work owns now waits on a signal the product
  publishes, steps Playwright's page clock, or counts work. The Compose
  undo budget is held as work (one slide replaced, a sixteenth of the deck read) instead of 16 ms, and its
  time is recorded by `npm run bench`.
- **Fixed: Vetrina's scroll-cost test could not see the work it bounded.** Its stage layer now carries `data-vt-scroll-seats`, a count of the re-seats a viewer's
  scroll has caused, so a test can prove a scroll that moved nothing re-seated nothing.
- **Fixed: in the Playground's Explore view, a sheet opened just before the address bar updated lost
  its back-gesture entry.** The walk's URL write replaced `history.state` with `null`, which wiped the
  back controller's marker. It now keeps the state it finds.

- **Fixed: `test/unit/core` no longer sleeps or races the clock (HARD RULE #32, the flaky-test audit's first folder).**
  All 59 counted hits in 34 files are gone, and `tools/flaky-test-baseline.json` drops from 563 hits in 221 files to
  504 in 187. Nine tests that slept 300 to 1,000 ms "for the runtime" now boot it on a virtual clock and return when
