  its timer queue is empty (`test/helpers/runtime-boot.js`). Timeout tests move a mocked clock across their bound. The
  "stays linear on hostile input" stopwatches count the characters each scan covered (`test/helpers/work-count.js`:
  `scanWork`, `charReads`). Where the regression is backtracking inside one regex, which nothing can count, the test
  stays a hang guard sized so the old pattern needs a minute or more, marked `flaky-ok` with both measurements. A
  stress run found four more stopwatches the census cannot see (in chart-row-record, front-matter-scalar,
  lift-bracket-span and slide-camera-faces); they are hang guards now too. Each rewrite whose old code could be rebuilt
  was shown failing on a copy of its module with the defect put back.
- **Fixed: `checkFlakyTests` read a `// flaky-ok:` mark from the wrong line after a string holding U+2028 or U+2029,**
  so every mark below one was ignored.
- **Fixed: a chart row with many trailing pills no longer slows narration with the square of the pill count.**
  `stripTrailingPills` in `lib/core/chart-narration.js` read the remaining lead once per pill (443 ms at 1,600 pills);
  it now reads it once, right to left, and gives the same result on a seeded 20,000-case comparison.

- **Fixed: reading speaker notes, reader notes, `describe:` and `say:` lines no longer slows down on a deck with many
  unclosed `<!--`.** `lib/authoring/notes-core.js` read every comment with a pattern that recheck calls polynomial, once
  per opener, so a run of unclosed openers cost the square of its length. A hand-written reader (`CommentScan`) now finds
  exactly the same comments in one pass; a seeded fuzz of 60,000 inputs holds it to the old pattern. Two smaller slow
  patterns in the same file (a trailing-newline trim and the heading-or-rule test, which used a back-reference) are
  linear too.
- **Fixed: the slice-equivalence diagnostic strips tags in linear time.** `sectionText` used a quote-aware tag pattern
  that rescanned to the end of the text from every unclosed `<`; one backward pass now gives the same result.
- **Fixed: the unit tier's stopwatches and sleeps are gone (HARD RULE #32).** 61 timing assertions and fixed sleeps in
  25 files under `test/unit/` now count work, read a virtual clock, or wait for a signal, and each was shown failing on
  the defect it guards.
- **Fixed: a unit test that needs a tool or a built file no longer skips silently in CI (the env-skip rule #3144 adds).** 33 skips in
  15 files route through `skipUnlessCI` / `skipWithoutChrome` (`test/helpers/chrome.js`), which skip on a laptop and
  fail under CI; two carry a `// ci-skip:` note naming the job that runs them instead. chart-readers asserts a pinned
  refusal instead of skipping three tests per refused chart. The `unit` CI job now installs zsh (through
  `.github/actions/apt-cached`), so the interactive zsh completion test runs in CI for the first time.

- **Export to Marp no longer hangs on a line of nested quote or list markers with no comment after it** (`> > > … text`, or `-    -    … text`). The bundle step read each line's container prefix with a pattern whose work grew exponentially with the markers: 16 bullets, each followed by four spaces, took 11 seconds, and 20 never finished. A one-pass reader in `lib/core/marp-bundle-scope.js` reads the same prefixes in linear time.

- **Raw HTML with many unclosed tables, code paragraphs or tags no longer slows a slide's render with the square of its size.** The engine read table cells, code-only paragraphs (a chart's eyebrow, a masthead's eyebrow, a label set, a legend, a split page's subtitle) and top-level tags with patterns that rescanned to the end of the slide from every unclosed `<tr`, `<td`, `<p`, `<a` or `<!--`. One-pass readers in `lib/plugins/chart-family/shared/html-tables.js`, `lib/core/code-paragraph.js` and `lib/core/tag-scan.js` read the same structure in linear time, and what a slide renders is unchanged. A chart slide that opens with 20,000 unclosed `<p><code>` renders in about 0.15 s, down from 4.8 s. Other patterns on the render path, such as headings, sections and markdown emphasis, are still being converted (`followups.d/3045-p2-regex-recheck-gate.md`).

- **Fixed: the Studio preview no longer keeps a photo's zoom cursor after the slide under a still mouse changes.**
  Turning from a collage slide to a text slide with the wheel, without moving the mouse, could leave the `zoom-in`
  cursor and the hover marker on a slide with no photo. The Studio hit-tested the pointer when the slide index
  changed, but the preview frame showed the new slide one render later, so the hit-test read the slide just left and
  nothing tested again. It now waits until the frame shows the slide the reader is on, and every render the live
  preview commits asks for one more hit-test.
- **Fixed: the slide map no longer starts a poster capture while you scroll it.** A capture checked that the rail was
  still, then loaded its code, and a scroll that landed in between got a capture mid-scroll. It now checks again once
  the code has loaded and waits for the rail to settle if a scroll landed.

- **Fixed: rendering a deck into another folder no longer refuses the deck's own relative files.** The CLI writes the page it captures into the output folder, so a deck's `<script src="…">` written relative to the deck resolved against the output folder instead. With `-o` elsewhere the diagram gallery printed `⚠ refused …/vendor/mermaid.min.js: it resolves outside the deck folder` for a file that does not exist there. The capture page now reads such an address from the deck folder, under the same confinement check; a file outside the deck and the Lattice install is still refused. The exported HTML keeps the addresses as written, and the diagram gallery's 31 pages render pixel-identical to an in-folder render.

- **Gemini keys that start with `AQ.` are accepted.** The Studio refused them as "not a Gemini key", although Gemini accepts them; it now takes `AIza…` and `AQ.…`.
- **A direct Gemini key no longer defaults to a retired model.** Gemini's model list carries no dates, so the default fell to the first model listed, `gemini-2.5-flash`, which Gemini refuses to new users. The default is now the newest model of the provider's everyday family (Flash, GPT, Sonnet).

- The prose binding gate (`test/unit/core/prose-binding.test.js`) no longer holds every deck's documents to the end of its walk. It kept ~2.0 GB live by the last deck, and under a 1.5 GB heap the file died out of heap, which the dot reporter prints as a bare `'test failed'`. Each deck is now its own test, with its own jsdom window closed when it ends and an event-loop turn after it, so the live heap stays under 0.2 GB (179–192 MB, the largest heap after a collection between decks) and a failure names its deck. Its last test now holds a floor for each kind of binding (heading, paragraph, item, row) instead of one total that headings alone cleared, and fails if any slide did not render.
- The scene binding gate (`test/unit/core/scene-binding.test.js`) had the same one-window walk. It now parses each deck, and each gallery, in its own window with an event-loop turn after it: the largest heap after a collection falls from 925 MB to 152 MB. Its floor of 1,000 bound sentences, a fifth of the real 4,719, is now a floor for each of its 23 units, and it fails if a narrated slide did not render.

- **Chat on a spend-capped OpenRouter key** (a gift link's key, or any key with a limit set at OpenRouter): when the key cannot cover the reply ceiling, the Studio asks again, once, for what the key can afford, so roughly the last quarter of a $1 gift card is no longer refused. When the key is spent, the chat says the key has used up its spending limit and offers signing in with your own OpenRouter account, instead of "your account is out of credits" or "rejected the connection". A long provider message no longer runs out of the chat's notice box.

- **Fixed: a stored OpenRouter key is no longer deleted when the browser fails to read its sealing
  key.** The key store removed a stored key whenever IndexedDB answered "no sealing key", and WebKit
  can answer a read of a stored `CryptoKey` with nothing. The store now counts the entry first: one
  that is there but could not be read is a passing fault, so the key is kept and tried again. Every
  path that removes a key now logs a `[lattice-key]` line to the console saying why.
- **Fixed: no character of a stored OpenRouter key sits in clear storage.** The sign-in's mint
  record named its key by the key's last four characters; it now uses a one-way hash. Clears
  CodeQL's clear-text-storage alert on `openrouter-key.js`.

- `npm run overflow:check` renders each deck with Chrome's PDF printer (`--chrome-pdf`) again, which cut a full sweep from 1703 s to 643-908 s on a 4-vCPU sandbox. The shared vector PDF writer, the CLI default since #2404, costs about 3 s a deck and runs after the overflow measurement, so it changed the sweep's time and never its verdict. `--writer shared` (or `--writer=shared`) renders the old way for a parity check, `--json` now lists every deck's clipped pages under `clipped`, and the `⏱ sweep cost` line names the writer it measured.

- The Reading view no longer redraws every chart when the window is resized or the Studio re-renders around it. React re-applied the article's markup on each re-render, which threw away all its hydrated figures and drew them again.

- **Fixed: a deck's own `@font-face` now draws in PNG and picture exports, as it does in HTML and PDF.** A font a deck's `style:` block (or a `--css` sheet) loads from a file beside the deck, such as `url('fonts/x.woff2')`, used to fall back to a Times-like face in `lattice deck.md deck.png` while `deck.html` and the PDF's text showed it, and the only message called the font "a picture". The slide camera now reads that font file from the same folders the PDF writer reads it from (the deck's folder and Lattice's install). A font it still refuses, from outside those folders or from a web address, prints a warning that names the font file and says why.

- Chart text now grows with `venue:` instead of shrinking. A chart drew its labels in viewBox units, so when the venue grew the title and chrome around it, its box got shorter and its labels got smaller: a bar chart's category labels printed 17.4 px at laptop and 13.0 px at hall. The chart frame now hands each kernel a venue factor (`lib/transformers/chart-text-venue.js`). The kernel draws on a canvas that many times smaller, so its labels print larger in the same box, and the room it reserves for them grows with them. The factor reads the slide's own title, eyebrow, subtitle and source line, because those decide how much box the venue takes. The frame keeps a venue drawing only when it costs no label the old drawing printed (no name cut to "…", no label dropped, no smaller unit), and otherwise steps the factor down. Bar, funnel and heatmap now hold 8 arcminutes of x-height at the back row at every venue (10.1 / 15.1 / 20.1 / 26.8 px); a bar chart's labels print 32.5 px at hall. Waterfall, stacked-bar, ep-curve, line, histogram and scatter grow too, short of that floor where the full size would cut a name. No chart prints smaller than before at any venue or slide size. Portrait, square and 4:3 slides, charts in panes, and bullet, slope, risk-matrix, tower and quadrant keep their previous drawing; `followups.d/3098-p1-chart-text-venue-remaining-kinds.md` lists every kind still short. At laptop the charts are unchanged byte for byte.

- The header, footer and page number on indaco's title, closing and divider slides now clear WCAG AA. Indaco paints those panels brand navy (#003D66), lighter than every other theme's, and its dark muted ink measured 3.5:1 there, under 4.5:1 for 15 px text, in light and dark decks. They now read 4.6:1. Other themes render exactly as before. A theme can name `--on-inverse-muted` for its own chrome on that panel, and a contrast test now holds every theme's bookend chrome to AA in both modes.

- **Fixed: closing a sheet returns focus to what opened it.** A modal Radix sheet returned focus
  only to a `SheetTrigger`, and most Studio sheets open from a plain button, so Escape on the
  phone's ⋯ menu (and the others) left focus on the page body. `SheetContent` now returns focus
  to the opener when nothing else has taken it since.

- **Fixed: a screen reader hears the same, useful description on a Studio control however it got
  there.** A tooltip hint described its button only while the tooltip was open, which a keyboard
  Tab did and a VoiceOver swipe did not; every icon-bar button lost its hint entirely; nine hints
  only repeated the button's name ("Share… Share"); Coach rows were described by their raw rule id
  (`metric-no-referent`); and the Reshape picker had no name. `Tip` now describes its trigger by
  what the hint adds to the name, from mount, and `e2e/studio-descriptions.spec.ts` fails on a
  description that repeats a name or is a raw id, and on an unnamed dialog.
- **Fixed: every row of the Studio's command palette and the site's ⌘K menu says what it does to
  a screen reader.** VoiceOver read a row's name and then its own generic option hint. Each Studio
  command now carries a one-line description (`COMMAND_DESCRIPTIONS`, one per command id, so a new
  command cannot ship without one), and the site menu's second line is read once, as the
  description, instead of running into the row's name. Both search fields have a name, and
  `CommandDialog` no longer falls back to a generic "Command Palette" title.
- **Fixed: VoiceOver no longer repeats a panel's description after every control in it.** On an
  iPhone, each Studio sheet's or dialog's description was read again after every row and button
  inside. Sheets and dialogs are now named and not described (`SheetContent`, `DialogContent`,
  `PersistentSurface`); `PanelHeader` drops its screen-reader-only `srDescription`. A visible
  description stays on screen, and a confirmation dialog keeps its question.

- An `image` slide no longer lifts an author's raw `.lattice-bg` panel out of a quote, a list item or a plugin's drawing: a quoted raw panel used to draw as the slide's photo and hide the slide's own. The slide's photo is decided by who wrote the panel: the image plugin's panel carries a marker an author cannot write, so it is lifted from anywhere; any other panel stays where the author put it, on the engine path and the DOM mirror alike. The `image` layout's panel rules now style only the section's own panel (`section.image > .lattice-bg`), and the adaptive layout measures only that one. An unclosed raw `<div>` written before the photo now holds it, as a browser nests it. No shipped deck changes.

- One rule now decides whether a lone `![title](src)` is a slide's placed photo, and every reader asks it (`lib/core/placed-picture.mjs`): the engine, Export-to-Marp, the Studio's Placement control and badge, the Studio's photo finder and the image lint. Fixed drifts against the engine: Export-to-Marp placed an indented picture inside a list item; the photo finder took a `![BG right](…)` picture, an `http:` address or a picture inside a sentence as the slide's photo; Compose missed a deck-wide `class: bleed` on a slide with its own class, a deck-wide `class: collage` and a `backgroundImage` directive.
- A `backgroundColor` directive, a `_backgroundImage: none`, and a `backgroundImage` value the slide style refuses (so the slide gets no background) no longer stop a lone picture from becoming an `image` slide's photo panel. The engine used to read any background directive as a photo already in place. No shipped deck changes.
- Export-to-Marp now writes `![bg]` for every lone picture the engine places, including one with a title in parentheses, one right under a setext heading or directly above a list, and one in a deck with CRLF line endings; and it leaves a picture alone where a `backgroundImage` carried from the front matter or an earlier slide is already the slide's photo.
- The Studio's photo-contrast underline now finds a lone `![title](src)` on an `image` slide (it read the slide's class after blanking its comments).
- `image-extra-panel` also warns when two or more pictures stand alone on an `image` or `bleed` slide with no other photo, because none of them becomes the photo.
- An Export-to-Marp bundle draws a full-bleed `![bg]` background again (a `bleed` slide's photo, or a `![bg]` on any slide that is not an `image` slide). The bundle's runtime lifted Marp's own background layer into a stage cell, which left the picture 0px tall, so every such background drew nothing.
- Firefox: the Studio's preview draws the site's own pictures again (the `sample:` photos drew nothing there, because the preview's content policy named the site's origin for fonts only).

- **On a touch screen, a closing sheet no longer hands focus back to a text field.** From Compose that field was the
  editor, so focus landed back in it after every Add slide gallery insert, which on a touch screen can bring the
  software keyboard back up (unverified on a real device: iOS Safari often refuses a keyboard on a focus made outside
  a tap). Focus goes to the button that opened the sheet instead, when it is still there, so a screen reader keeps its
  place. The insert itself already took focus only on a fine pointer; the close now agrees. A mouse still gets its
  caret back, and so does a close made from a hardware keyboard.
- **The slide menu opens on the first press right after it closed.** A closing menu stayed mounted through its fade,
  and its press-outside watcher took the next press on the ⋯ as outside, so the menu opened and shut within 9 ms. The
  strip menu now drops its exit fade, as the Insert menu already did.

- A Studio export from Safari on an iPhone or iPad (PDF, images, PowerPoint, LibreOffice) now draws a card's shadow whole. The slide camera drew each slide on a canvas scaled 2x, and WebKit then cut a negative-spread shadow short or dropped it: the image layout's lifted card lost its shadow from the left edge (Mobile Safari on the iOS Simulator drew none of its bottom edge), and the `mat`, `device` and `float` picture frames got a hard gray block down their right side. On an engine with that defect the camera now has the slide drawn at the export's own size. The lifted card was measured in Mobile Safari on the iPhone and iPad simulators, by drawing the slide camera directly; the frames and the full export paths were measured in Playwright's WebKit. Safari on a Mac shares the engine but was not run. Chromium and Firefox exports are pixel-identical to before.

- The collage lightbox no longer zooms toward the photo's top-left corner when you press `+` or `-` before the photo has loaded. A zoom key pressed in that window now waits, and applies about the photo's center once it has opened. A pinch, `ctrl` + wheel or double click in that window is ignored, because there is no photo yet to aim at. The Studio, the Playground and the exported HTML player all get the fix.

- **compare-prose:** a split page that holds one card (a hall venue puts each card on its own page) no longer draws the connector arrow in front of it. The arrow pushed the card past the slide's edge, cutting its right side. On a portrait or phone box the `axis` facet cards also take the full width and a smaller numeral, so each facet fits its page at hall.
- **compare-prose:** a lone card in `decision` or `rejected` is no longer styled as the losing option (struck label, muted text): with nothing to lose to, it stays at full strength. The `axis` docs now teach the ordered-list form (`1. Own the verb`) its numerals are generated from.

- **divider:** the gallery's "When NOT to reach for divider" slide fits at a hall venue on square, portrait and story boxes. Two anti-pattern cards were too long for a page of their own once the slide splits one card a page; they now say the same thing in about 20 words. The divider docs keep the anchor-chrome rule, now in the component's purpose.

- **matrix-grid:** on a portrait, 9:16 or phone box, a five-column grid no longer runs off the right edge (the last column read `FIELI`, and its pill `Chie`). The row-axis title now lies flat above the column title, so the columns get the width its rotated side gutter used to take, and either title wraps instead of running off the box when it is long. Landscape and square boxes keep the rotated title.

- **quadrant:** a y-axis title that wraps to two lines (`Ability to execute`) no longer loses its first line past the chart's left edge. The band beside the plane holds both lines. A long x-axis title now wraps under the plane instead of running off the right edge, because its wrap is measured as it paints: in capitals, bold and tracked.

- **stacked-bar:** a two-line period name (`Q1 FY24`) no longer loses its second line below the chart. The band under the axis grows to hold both lines. When a period word is too wide for its bar beside the name column, the part names move to the key so the names do not run together.

- Safari 17.5-17.6 (WebKit 17.4) now draws hub-spoke icons and paints the plugin painting canvas and the plugin-off chip. Each rule's `@supports` guard tested relative color on a plain `red`. WebKit 17.4 passes that test, but it drops a relative color over a `light-dark()` origin, and it rejects `calc()` in a hue channel. So the icon stroke computed to `none` and both backgrounds went blank. Each guard now tests the rule's own shape, so WebKit 17.4 takes the plain inks, while Chromium 153, Firefox 142 and WebKit 26 compute the same values as before. The topic shelf was measured and already paints correctly in WebKit 17.4; its guard now tests the rule's own `max(l, 0.34)`.
- Hub-spoke icons in Safari 17.5-17.6 now take the ink each finish curates for their disc. The finish repaints a disc on every engine, but the icon's ink waited for relative color, so in WebKit 17.4 an icon kept the plain slide's ink on a finished disc: 218 of 528 icons over 32 palettes and three finishes fell under 3:1, the worst 1.11:1. Pigment's group and neutral inks, every finish's status ink and tone's deepest-slot ink need no relative color, so they now apply everywhere; measured again, no icon falls under 3:1 in WebKit 17.4, and Chromium 153 paints every icon exactly as before.
- The same old guards also left hub-spoke icons undrawn in older Chromium and Firefox. Measured over the same 32 palettes and three finishes, Chromium 125 and Firefox 128 drew none of 576 icons before this change; now they draw every icon at 3:1 or better (worst 3.24:1). Both pass a relative-color guard on a plain `red` but drop the color over a `light-dark()` origin, as Safari 17 does.

- Compose undo and redo now keep a deck byte-exact when two neighboring slide separators are spelled differently (`---` followed by one newline, then `---` followed by a blank line). Deleting the slide between them used to drop Compose to a full rebuild, and inserting one beside such a separator could emit the deck one newline short. The narrow resync now keeps every newline the edit carried across a separator, and it falls back to the whole-source path whenever its split cannot spell back the edit.

- The authoring docs no longer teach wrong forms: the `lens` skill's `kpi` example uses a `##` heading and a real layout, `decision banner-tag` and `compare-prose banner-tag` are written as `tag-band` (the docs, both manifests and both galleries; `banner-tag` keeps working as an alias on every tagged layout), `silent` lists the section rail it also hides, `sketch` is described as a mode, and the universal-modifier docs point at the full registry (`MODIFIER_GROUPS`) instead of a 62-token subset. `AGENTS.md` no longer says `lint:deck` catches every footgun the docs warn about, and the component picker no longer contradicts itself on its length.
- The Studio's `_class:` completion offers the right modifiers again: eyebrow modifiers on `quadrant` and `scatter` (the measuring check mistook a chart's axis line for an eyebrow), heading modifiers on `premise` and eyebrow modifiers on `video`, surfaces for eight components that had none recorded (`collage`, `columns`, `ep-curve`, `gift-card`, `histogram`, `risk-matrix`, `rows`, `tower`), and no card-row modifiers for agenda's retired `cards` variant.
- The agent kit's modifier catalog no longer presents its 62 core tokens as the whole vocabulary; it points at `reference/components.json` for the full list.
- Each component guide (and so its page on the website and in the agent kit) no longer says the component accepts every universal modifier: it names the surfaces whose modifiers have no effect on that layout, measured, and links the current design-system section.
- The website's authoring guide links the component reference's own Markdown copy (`/components.md`) instead of an uncommitted repository path, and no longer lists `numbered` as a universal modifier.

- **Player:** a dark `--player` export now switches tokens a component declares on its own selector, not only the theme's `:root` tokens. 66 such declarations stayed light in dark mode; the visible one was the heatmap, whose two highest ramp steps printed near-black values on a mid-blue cell at 2.1:1 (now 4.65:1). The chart hues, flowchart and state-chart fills, hub-spoke, quadrant labels and callout inks follow the toggle too.
- **topic:** the track labels on a dark shelf take the heading ink instead of the body ink. On indaco-dark, the default palette, they measured 4.55:1 against the lifted shelf (4.49:1 in rendered pixels); they now measure 6.5:1, and every dark palette clears 6.5:1. Light shelves are unchanged.

- Studio: after a reload, a plugin block the deck lists no longer flashes its fence source or its unstyled drawing. Until the plugin's code loads, the block shows a muted afterimage of its last drawing at the size it drew, so nothing moves when the drawing arrives; a block drawn for the first time shows a muted chart skeleton instead.

- Studio: when a theme or component request to the model fails, Fabricate now says why — reconnect (401), out of credits (402), rate-limited (429) or no network — instead of "no usable palette" or "No model connected".
- Studio: a failed OpenRouter sign-in now says so and offers **Try again**, instead of returning to the Studio as if nothing happened; the dead sign-in state is cleared so it cannot replay.
- Studio: a revoked or expired OpenRouter key is now noticed. Workspace shows "key rejected" with a **Reconnect** button instead of "active" while every request fails.
- Charts: the hover card escapes a chart mark's label and value, so markup in a shared deck's chart cannot run in the page that holds your OpenRouter key.
- Studio: **Describe a finish** now works on a real model. It used to discard every cloud reply as "no usable finish recipe". Finish and Describe a drawing also say why a failed request failed.
- Docs: the features page lists the describe-it faculties and cloud read-aloud, and says plainly that the AI features send deck text to OpenRouter on your own key.
- Studio: Workspace → AI has a third tab, **API key**, to paste your own OpenRouter key instead of signing in. The key is checked with OpenRouter before it is saved, and afterwards only its last four characters are shown.
- Security: your OpenRouter key is now encrypted at rest in the browser (AES-GCM under a key the browser will not let any code export), so the profile's files on disk no longer hold it in clear. A key saved before this change is encrypted on first load.

- The four accessibility palettes' chart spectrum (`--chart-cat1..8`) is now paired. It was eight fixed grays on the claim that a fixed value reads on either canvas; measured, a `_class: dark` slide flips the canvas to `#000` while the ramp stays put, putting four of the eight slots under the 3:1 graphical floor (1.55, 1.87, 2.30 and 2.86:1). The dark arm mirrors the light one — each slot's contrast against `#000` reproduces its light-arm contrast against `#FFF` to within 0.03 — so the light arm is byte-identical and existing decks are unchanged.
- `chart-contrast.test.js` now scopes the accessibility palettes for rule 1 ("marks clear the canvas"), which was asserted for the fourteen brand themes only. Rule 2 stays deliberately waived there — under CVD the texture patterns carry category — and that split is why the hole was easy to miss.

- The tools that answer "what visually changed" no longer drop the worst pages. ImageMagick's
  `compare -metric AE` prints a changed-pixel count over 1,000,000 in scientific notation
  (`1.15966e+06`), and both copies of the parse tested for a bare integer and fell back to
  zero — so a page differing by more than a million pixels was recorded as IDENTICAL by
  `golden-diff`, the regression gate and `npm run preview`. The worse the drift, the more
  likely it vanished. Measured on `examples/gallery-jargon.pdf`: page 12 (976,578px) was
  reported, page 17 (1,159,660px, a quarter of the page) was not. An unreadable count is now
  `-1` — the sentinel every caller already treats as changed — rather than zero.

- **Fixed: an agenda's page numbers attach by name.** An agenda only shows page numbers when each line names the
  section at its position. A list reordered or renamed after it was filled, by hand or in an exported Marp bundle, used
  to get the right number of page numbers in the wrong places; it now shows none.
- A filled agenda keeps its page numbers when a section heading ends in inline code; the code is read as part of the name, not as the line's own page reference.
- Inline code inside an agenda title stays next to its words. Only a line's last inline code is its right column (a page number or a tag); before, every code span in the line stretched across the row, so `finish: atrium` floated mid-row.

- **Studio:** the Architect no longer lays out your whole deck every time it edits a slide. The fit check that rides each edit now renders only the slides the turn changed and leaves the rest empty, so the page stops hanging for as long as the deck is long (a 40-slide deck blocked the page for about 2 seconds at 4x CPU). The agent is told the other slides were not re-measured and no longer says the whole deck fits; `check_deck`, and any turn that changes front matter (a theme, a size), still measure every slide.

- The agent kit's generator wraps quoted canons in a fence longer than anything
  inside them. A fixed ` ``` ` splits the moment a payload carries one at the start
  of a line, and the remainder then parses as markup rather than as the quoted text
  — `COMPONENT_CANON` already carries inline runs, and these canons are prose anyone
  may edit.
- It calls esbuild through its API rather than spawning `node_modules/.bin/esbuild`,
  matching the other ten build tools. The shim is extensionless and not directly
  executable on Windows, and this build runs from `prepare`, so a spawn failure
  there is an install failure for a consumer.

- The agent kit's read-path table quotes a **fixed cost plus a per-component cost**
  rather than one flat figure. The single number described a one-slide deck; a real
  nine-slide deck measured 2.9× it, and that table is what an agent budgets its
  context against. The skills row is measured too — it was the one hand-typed cell,
  quoting "~3k each" against a real 3.0k–5.6k.
- `authoring/README.md` now shows deck front matter and points at the modifier
  catalog. Front matter is the one thing a deck cannot render without, and it
  appeared nowhere on the kit's deck-writing path — only in a skill file the README
  routes to for a different task.
- The skills glossary lists only rules the seven shipped skills actually cite. It
  scanned `design/skills/README.md`, which the kit replaces rather than copies, and
  so resolved two rules nothing a reader can open ever references.

- The agent kit now ships `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS`, `NOTICE.md` and
  `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt`. `review/check.mjs` is an esbuild bundle that inlines
  `markdown-it` and five transitive dependencies (MIT, and BSD-2-Clause for
  `entities`); esbuild strips their copyright notices, and both license families
  require the notice to travel with the code. The package list is derived from the
  bundle's own module banners rather than hand-kept, and the build fails rather
  than publishing a package whose license text it cannot find.
- Rewrote 428 references that resolved only inside a clone — 305 sibling
  `../../<bucket>/<name>/<name>.docs.md` links, 62 pointers at
  `design/design-system.md §6.5` (whose anchor was stale besides) and 61 links to
  gallery PDFs the kit does not carry. A test now resolves every link in the kit
  and fails on any that dangles, and on any file that tells its reader to open a
  repo path or obey a HARD RULE number.
- Added `authoring/modifiers.md`. The kit told authors to compose `tint-*`,
  `mark-*`, `tone-*` and `insight-*` onto the class and then pointed outside itself
  for the list, so the vocabulary was mandatory to use and impossible to read. It
  is generated from `UNIVERSAL_GROUPS`, so it cannot drift from what renders.

- Read · Article keeps each slide's Key Insight and below-note. The article view (the player, the `--read` export and the Studio) printed a slide's heading and body and dropped its closing insight and note: 261 of 264 across the 233 example and baseline decks. All 264 now follow their slide's body, once each. A panes slide's insight follows its panes, and a layout that keeps its trailing block in its body does not print it twice.

- **Fixed: `lint:deck` now flags a deferring inline `<script>` however its end tag is
  spelled.** The `author-script-defers` rule matched the whole element with one
  `<script …>…</script>` span, so it only ever recognized one end tag. A deck closing
  with `</script >`, `</script\n>`, `</script/>` or `</script foo>` — all of which end
  the element for a browser — walked past the rule silently. The rule now matches the
  opening tag and finds the end the way the HTML tokenizer does, which also removes the
  spanning tag regex CodeQL's bad-tag-filter query flags.
- **Fixed: the same rule no longer reads a slide's prose as script.** An unclosed
  `<script>` used to be scanned to the end of the slide, where `Worker productivity` and
  `We await sign-off` read as deferral calls the deck never made. An unclosed element is
  now left alone, and the end-tag search uses HTML whitespace rather than JavaScript's
  `\s` — the wider set ended a body on a non-breaking space, truncating it before the
  real code.
- **Fixed: linting a deck with many malformed `<script` runs is no longer quadratic.**
  Bounding the opening tag's attribute scan takes 156 KB of pathological input from
  6475 ms to 208 ms. The Playground runs this on the browser's main thread as the author
  types.

- Corrected three authoring rules that the Studio sends its model on every turn
  and that the agent kit ships verbatim as `authoring/rules.md`. The title slide
  is `# H1` → backtick eyebrow → subtitle, not eyebrow-first: the eyebrow is
  matched as the paragraph immediately after the h1, so the old order rendered it
  as a second subtitle with no error on any surface. There is no ` ```chart `
  fence — the engine rewrites `mermaid`, `functionplot` and `anima`, and the
  chart layouts are authored as nested Markdown lists. The nested-bullet rule now
  names all eleven card-style layouts plus `split-panel` / `split-compare` (it had
  drifted four behind `lint-core.js`) and states the indent width for both marker
  kinds: 2 spaces under `-`, 3 under `1.`.
- `premise`'s "Common mistakes" told authors to write each row as one flat line,
  contradicting its own slot table, its gallery and `premise.styles.css`. A row is
  a numbered term plus two bullets nested three spaces under it; a flat row leaves
  both columns empty.

- `authority-chain`: every row's citation now starts at the same left edge. The tier-label rail is one column shared down the chain, 14cqi as before and widened to the longest single word in any label, so a long label like Enforcement no longer pushes its own row's citation right of the others. A two-word label still wraps inside the rail. Applies to the default chain and `bracket`.
- `authority-chain trail`: each column stacks again at every venue. At conference and hall the citation and gloss had wrapped into a second column beside the tier label and clipped at the card's edge; the label also stood 14cqi tall, leaving an empty band above the citation; and the arrows drew inside each card instead of on the boundary between two. A trail citation now wraps at its spaces, and a card too full for the stage now runs long, where the export reports it, instead of drawing text over its own border.
- New `lint:deck` warning `trail-budget`: a citation or tier-label word longer than its trail column. The budget is measured per venue and tier count (four tiers: 26 characters a citation word at laptop, 23 at huddle, 17 at conference, 13 at hall), with its own table for the `sketch` hand face. A word ends where the browser breaks it: at a space, after a hyphen, or around a dash.

- `authority-chain`: each tier's gloss line no longer sits on the card's bottom border. The citation line takes a line box its own size, and each row pads by `--sp-sm` top and bottom, so a four-tier chain's text sits centered in its card at the laptop venue.

- **Fixed: every auto-split run now ends on ONE closing page carrying the below-note and the key
  insight together.** Five carousel strategies still shipped the placement the 2026-09-01 ruling
  replaced — the note spliced into the last body page, the takeaway on a page of its own — so a
  split `compare-prose`, `split-panel`, `decision`, `compare-code` or `list-tabular` slide ended
  with its two closing beats pulled apart. They route through one kernel builder now
  (`closingPageFromMaterial`), so a run reads the same whichever layout it came from.
- **Fixed: `split-panel` no longer loses a trailing key insight and below-note when it splits.**
  Both were dropped outright — no page, no warning. A rendered section ends with three fit-berth
  marker divs, and the reader that finds a layout's own content slot takes the section's last
  element, so it picked an empty berth instead of the panel holding the author's text. Berths are
  chrome now, and a trailing sentence after a structural block is recognized as a note at that
  depth.
- **Fixed: `kanban` and `roadmap` printed a slide's key insight once per lane or card.** Both
  re-emit a slice of the source that carries everything after the last lane, and repeat it on
  every page — a two-lane board printed one takeaway three times. The trailing beats are stripped
  from the slice and close the run instead. `redline` did the same with a below-note.
- **Changed: `compare-prose` no longer builds its own "The verdict" page**, and `list-tabular` no
  longer promotes a trailing below-note onto its cover. Both consumed the note, which is what
  split it away from the key insight; it closes the run beside it now. The unused
  `compare-split-verdict` styling is removed with it.
- **Fixed: a `redline` slide with no why-list no longer has both its passages moved off their
  pages.** The split kernel classified trailing material by element shape alone, so it read
  `redline`'s two quoted passages as universal beats and swept them onto the run's closing page,
  leaving two body pages carrying only a heading. It asks the layout's `coda.claims` now — but only
  where the claimed element rides a MEMBER, which is `redline` alone. A strategy that re-emits
  source repeats everything outside its member set on every page, so a claimed beat left there is
  duplicated rather than preserved.
- **Removed: the `insight` split role, its two page builders, and the four `.lat-split-insight`
  selectors that shipped with no emitter.** A key insight closes the run beside the note now, so
  nothing built or styled a page for it alone.
- **Fixed: a split run of `compare-prose`, `split-panel`, `decision` or `list-tabular` now names
  the page it points at.** Every body page read "→ continues" because the member's title lives in
  a labeled span the pointer's label reader did not know, so it fell through to a path that
  declined on length.
- **Added: a `journey` splits by STAGE on a tall deck** — one stage per page, carrying its own
  band label, its own task rows with their actor dots and mood faces, and both legends, because a
  page of mood faces without the mood key is unreadable. Portrait only: at landscape a journey is
  one figure over a shared axis (every task holds an absolute grid column), so a slice would draw
  tasks into columns that are no longer there — the splitter declines there and the slide rings,
  unchanged.
- **Fixed: a slide's own `_footer:` no longer disappears from every page when the slide splits.**
  The strip that removes the deck's repeated header and footer from a split run identified them by
  the section's `data-footer` — which Marp also fills from a per-slide override, so it could not
  tell the deck's band from this slide's caption and deleted the caption, which then appeared
  nowhere at all. It reads the deck's front matter now. This was live: all three journey slides of
  `portrait-journey` and both roadmap slides of `portrait-roadmap` lost their captions.
- **Fixed: a split `roadmap` pointed at the wrong thing, and a split `kanban` pointed at nothing.**
  The forward pointer resolves a page's members as the first list on it — right where the page's
  body IS that list, wrong where the page holds one sliced card with lists of its own. A roadmap
  phase page named a workstream row instead of the phase ("next: Signal Intake Scoring v2" on a
  page titled "Q2", two fields of one row run together), and a kanban lane page found no list at
  all, so those runs carried no pointer. The splitter now names the member it cut, because it is
  the only thing that knows; runs read "next: Q2" and "next: In progress".
- **Fixed: the CSS selector gate skipped the selectors most likely to be invalid.** It handed
  Chromium every rule prelude css-tree could parse, and silently dropped the ones it could not —
  which is the class most likely to be broken. The stated reason (keyframe percentages) never
  applied: those parse as ordinary selector lists. A keyframe step is now excluded by being inside
  a keyframes block, which is the real reason to skip it, and everything else reaches the browser.
- **Changed: the furniture on a split page is redesigned for a slide read small.** Owner review of
  real social-size renders. The forward pointer leaves the full-bleed ruled band it was wearing and
  becomes a marker in the bottom-right margin, with its rule dropped. The runhead that names the
  source slide loses the wide-tracked uppercase treatment it was wearing — it is fed a slide TITLE,
  and 0.2em capitals turned a forty-character title into a two-line wall; it is a normal-case
  standfirst in the body face now, and every runhead in `examples/read-across-carousel.md` fits on
  one line. The k-of-N rail's off state was a ghost at 0.22 opacity — 1.4:1 against its backdrop,
  reading as a broken hairline rather than as progress — and goes to 0.70, the first step that
  clears the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor a meaningful graphical object owes on EVERY shipped palette,
  on both surfaces the rail lands on (3.11:1 on a body page in `cuoio`, 3.34:1 on the accent
  cover in `indaco-dark`). The page's own caption
  takes the pointer's ink lift, and nothing else — a wider caption is what put CONTENT CLIPPED on
  six pages once already. Seven scoped copies of the runhead's finish now read one register.
- **Fixed: a split page's forward pointer stranded its arrow at the far left of the page whenever
  the text wrapped.** The mark was a flex sibling of the text; a text item wider than its row
  shrinks to exactly the space left over, so there is no free space for `justify-content: flex-end`
  to distribute and the mark stays at the row's left edge while the text is pushed right — 390px
  apart on a 972px row. The pointer shrink-wraps to its content now, so there is no free space
  left in the row to strand the mark across, and the mark rides the trailing edge of the box.
- **Fixed: a split `journey` stage sat high on its page with both legends stranded near the floor.**
  Three parts each took their own share of the height instead of composing: the board fills the
  cell, the stack fills the board, and the stage's rows fill the stack, so the cell's own centering
  had nothing left to center. On a split page all three stop growing and the board centers the
  stage and its legends as one group. The unsplit render is byte-identical.
- **Changed: the forward pointer is a pill.** Owner's call, on the redesigned furniture: a subtle
  on-brand pill with the drawn arrow and the label inside it, rather than bare text on the canvas.
  It reuses the universal `--pill-*` register — same radius, padding, weight and tracking as every
  other pill in the engine — and names the one axis it overrides at its own site: `--bg-alt` for
  the fill, because a signal on the page's own canvas needs to separate from it. The numbers back
  the shape: across the eight shipped decks that split there are 153 signals, median label
  thirteen characters, 71% at or under twenty, and not one of them lands on a split cover — so the pill
  never has to survive the inverse surface. `align-self: flex-end` shrink-wraps it, right-anchors
  it without a margin, and is what makes a flex row safe here: the arrow was stranded before
  because the box was full-width, and a box sized to its content has no free space to strand it
  across.
- **Fixed: the run's CLOSING pointer was built by a second producer, and drifted the moment the
  first one changed.** `closingSignal` in `auto-split.js` hand-assembled the same
  `.lat-split-rel` div that `relationship.js` builds (HARD RULE #1). The two agreed for as long as
  the element was a bare div: when the label needed wrapping in a span so the pill could ellipsise
  — `text-overflow` never applies to a flex container — the kernel grew one and the copy did not,
  so a closing pointer rendered unwrapped. Both go through the one builder now.
- **Changed: the forward pointer drops the word "next" and puts its arrow after the label.** Owner's
  call: the arrow already says it. A sequence or cycle page now reads `Trial →` rather than
  `→ next: Trial`, which is six characters of chrome removed from every one of them. The mark moved
  to the trailing edge for every kind that draws one, not just `next` — a `↻` still on the left
  while a `→` sat on the right would read as two widgets rather than one system. The WORDS stay on
  the other two kinds, and the difference is the point: an arrow carries "next", but `↓` and `↑`
  distinguish a hierarchy's two directions without naming them, so `governs` and `under` are still
  doing work. `comparison` draws no mark at all and is untouched.
- **Fixed: four hand-rolled copies of the same tag strip, three of them flagged by CodeQL.**
  `replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '')` had been written out separately in two test files and in
  `withMemberLabel`, and code scanning raised three high-severity alerts for incomplete
  multi-character sanitization on the test copies. All four call the kernel's `textOf` now, which
  strips to a fixpoint. The loop is the gate's accepted remediation rather than a fix for a
  demonstrated bypass — replacing it with a single pass leaves every test green, because
  `<[^>]*>` consumes from a `<` to the next `>` and a surviving `>` has no `<` left to pair with.
  Both the kernel comment and the new property test say so, and the property they pin — nothing
  `textOf` returns carries a tag — holds whatever the implementation.
- **Fixed: a run's closing page read as a page whose content failed to render.** Found by an
  independent visual sweep, and the measurement is the whole story: the coda cell was
  `flex: 1 1 auto`, so on a 1350px page it took 1110px and centered its hundred pixels of note
  inside that, stranding the runhead a thousand pixels above with two hairlines framing the void
  between them. The coda stops growing now, so the section's own centering composes the runhead
  and the closing note as ONE group — the same correction the split `journey` needed, and for the
  same reason: a child that absorbs the free height leaves the parent's centering nothing to
  center. The runhead also drops its rule here, because the note already draws one and the two
  became a doubled hairline 58px apart once the gap closed.
- **Fixed: five defects an independent check found in the redesigned furniture.** All measured on
  real renders, none caught by a gate.
  - The runhead register was declared on `:root` alone, so `var(--text-secondary)` was substituted
    at `<html>` against the theme's SCREEN value and inherited down already resolved — out of reach
    of `section.print`'s remap. A `class: print` split page painted its runhead the theme's blue
    (#455C7A) on an otherwise all-gray paper page. The register is on `:root, section` now, which
    is what the typography generator has emitted for the same reason since #1375. Dark mode was
    never affected: `light-dark()` inside a custom property resolves at the using element.
  - The pointer had `max-width: 100%` under the initial `content-box`, so its padding and border
    landed OUTSIDE that cap — and because the pill is right-anchored, the excess went left, out of
    the content column and into the page margin, where the column's clip cut the rounded cap and
    the first character. A split `verdict-grid` rendered a 1019px pill in a 972px column, its left
    edge 47px outside that column. `comparison` is the reachable case
    because it is the one relationship whose label has no length budget. `scrollWidth` could never
    have caught it: leftward overflow is invisible to it in LTR.
  - **Breaking-ish for anyone reading the ink:** the pointer's ink is `--text-body`, not
    `--text-secondary`. Measured on the rendered pointer across all 33 shipped palette variants,
    `--text-secondary` on `--bg-alt` is WORSE than the `--text-muted`-on-`--bg` it replaced on 14
    of them and bottoms out at 4.63:1 — under the 5.13:1 this redesign names as the problem. On
    `cuoio`, the default theme, it went 5.07 to 4.64. A "read it small in a feed" change cannot
    dim the pointer on the default palette. `--text-body` floors at 5.46:1 and beats the
    pre-branch value on 32 of the 33. The pointer stays subordinate by SIZE and placement, which
    is what was doing that job.
  - The split caption's ink lift never landed. It was written as
    `var(--marp-slide-footer-color, var(--text-secondary))`, but that token is declared
    unconditionally at `:root` and again in every theme that tunes it, so the fallback could never
    fire and the caption kept computing `--text-muted`. It sets `color` directly now — and matches
    the `premise` page's footer, which sits as a direct child of the section and which both of the
    original selectors missed.
  - `test/unit/css/split-signal-scope.test.js` passed on a pill stranded at the far LEFT, which is
    the exact failure it was rewritten to catch: `align-self`'s computed value is the specified
    keyword whatever the parent does, and `width < stageWidth` is true of any shrink-wrapped box at
    either edge. It measures the box's own edges now, and gains a long-label case covering the
    ellipsis and the box model. All three assertions were mutation-checked against the defects they
    name.
- **Changed: one dead rule block and one specificity tie removed from the split furniture.** The
  pointer's pre-pill declarations survived the pill as a second, contradictory 30-line explanation
  of the same element; a full computed-style diff with them removed changed three properties and no
  geometry at all. And the split `journey`'s `justify-content: center` tied on specificity with the
  vertical board's own `flex-start` ninety lines above it in the same file, winning on source order
  alone — it carries the board's `[data-orient]` now, so it is a real override.
- **Fixed: a split `journey`'s mood key named a color encoding the page does not use.** The five
  swatches are the categorical `--journey-mood-*` ramp, which is right on the LANDSCAPE board,
  where every face is painted from that same ramp. The vertical board encodes mood twice and
  neither way is that ramp: the row is washed off the semantic state hues and the face is plotted
  by POSITION on a numbered track in the inherited body ink. Measured on `portrait-journey.pdf`
  p6, the rows render green, every face is navy, and the key beside them shows brown, blue, blue,
  purple and red — five colors that appear nowhere on the page, on a legend this branch repeats
  once per stage. The vertical variant drops the swatches and keeps the scale's verbal anchors
  and numerals, which is what the mood track's five gridlines are numbered by.
- **Fixed: `(cont.)` — the marker on a split slide's repeated heading — was the most common
  sub-threshold text run in the engine.** At `opacity: 0.5` it bottoms out at 2.96:1 against the
  4.5:1 real text owes, measured on a real render swept across all 33 shipped palette variants;
  126 of that sweep's 162 total offenders were this one marker. It reads on `indaco`, which is
  the only palette the per-PR contrast gate renders, which is why nothing caught it. 0.65 still
  fails at 4.46:1; **0.70** is the first step that clears, at 5.09:1 worst, so it is the quietest
  this marker can be and still be text. It stays an opacity rather than an ink token on purpose:
  it rides inside an `h1`/`h2`, and a split heading is not always on the plain canvas, so the
  alpha keeps it compositing over whatever the heading actually sits on. The same sweep now
  reports 36 offenders where it reported 162, and none of them is split furniture.
- **Fixed: fourteen committed demo PDFs this branch made stale, and a rail contrast claim that was
  true on one palette.** Found by a second independent check.
  - The k-of-N rail's off state went to 0.55 on a measurement taken on `indaco` alone, and the
    changelog stated it "clears the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor". Swept across all 33 shipped variants on
    a real render it fails on SEVEN, bottoming out at **2.34:1 on `cuoio`, the default theme** —
    the same error this branch already made once with the pointer's ink. It survived because
    `tools/palette-sweep.js`, the instrument used to re-derive the pointer, walks TEXT runs and
    cannot see a rail at all. Measured directly on both surfaces the rail lands on: 0.65 still
    fails, and **0.70** is the first step where a body page and the accent cover both clear, at
    3.11:1 (`cuoio`) and 3.34:1 (`indaco-dark`). The on/off pair still reads as k-of-N at 200 dpi.
  - Dropping the journey mood swatches left the scale reading as one five-digit number: five 22px
    numerals separated by an 8.26px gap at a 39.96px type size renders `PAIN 12345 DELIGHT`. The
    vertical legend's gap is `1.1ch` now — a digit's own advance — so the ticks stay apart at every
    size the board renders at.
  - Fourteen `examples/*.pdf` that were byte-current with `main` no longer matched the engine,
    among them `split-relationship` and `split-envelope` — the decks a reviewer would open to see
    exactly this change. Regenerated; all 21 decks this branch touches are byte-current, verified
    by re-rendering and comparing. (`portrait-gantt-statechart`'s TYPE FLOOR warning is unchanged
    from `main`.)
  - Accuracy, in comments and in this file: the pill's overflow went out of the content column into
    the page margin, not "past the page edge" (its left edge lands 7px inside a 1080px page);
    `split-headings` was named among the decks that split and contributes nothing, because it has
    no `size:` and renders wide; and the guard suite's fixtures gave two carousel shapes a
    `.cell-stage` that production never emits for them — measured, four shapes attach the pointer
    to the section itself, and no closing page ever carries one.
- **Fixed: three defects the adversarial trio found in this branch's own fixes.**
  - **The k-of-N rail was tuned on the wrong quantity.** Every earlier revision measured the off
    pill against its backdrop — whether you can see the pills — and never measured whether you can
    tell which one is current, which is the only thing the rail exists to say. Those pull opposite
    ways when both states are one color at two alphas: presence wants 0.65 and up, state wants
    0.34 and down, and no value satisfies both (at 0.70 the state separation is 1.79:1 on a body
    page and 1.49:1 on the accent cover). The state is carried by LENGTH now — the off pill is
    roughly half the on pill — which spends no contrast at all and frees the alpha to serve
    presence. The **off** state is the one that shrinks, deliberately: the rail is a progress fill,
    so on a run's last page every segment is on, and lengthening the on state widened the rail 32%
    exactly when it is most complete, taking the room out of the caption beside it. Shortening the
    off state instead makes the footprint non-increasing, and `gallery-jargon` at portrait goes
    from 45 clipped captions to 43.
  - **A `:root` override of the runhead register was a silent no-op.** Declaring the ink on
    `:root, section` fixed the print remap and broke theme authoring, because a section-scoped
    declaration outranks a theme's `:root` and every shipped theme declares its ink ramp there —
    the exact sibling of the caption bug this branch documents at length. The ink is no longer
    declared in the register; its default rides as a `var()` fallback at each of the seven
    consumers, which resolves at the using element (so print still remaps) while leaving the
    property genuinely unset (so a theme wins). Verified both ways on a real render.
  - **The exporter reported the pointer pill's deliberate ellipsis as content loss.** The label is
    engine-generated and capped by rule, so "Shorten the copy" names an edit the author cannot
    make, and the false alarm trains authors to ignore the one signal export sign-off reads. It
    joins the clip probe's ignore list. The split caption deliberately does NOT: those are the
    author's own words, appearing nowhere else, and "shorten it" is exactly the right advice.

- **Fixed: the Studio's image export keeps the brand bar on finish slides.** The export redraws the top spectrum bar as a background strip, and that strip sat under the finish layer, so most finishes' own wash hid it and a `backdrop: clear` mask erased it where the clearance reached the top edge. The strip now sits in the border band, where the bar belongs.
- **Fixed: a Fabricate finish with Strength below 100% and a clearance or spotlight exports cleanly.** Poppler-based readers (Evince, Okular) drew it as a dark wedge or at full strength; the baked strength now draws as a flat canvas veil, with the same colors. A finish saved before this change needs one re-save in Fabricate.

- **Fixed: a class directive written across lines places a picture beside the text.**
  `<!--\n_class: image\n-->` is applied by the engine, but the CLI read only one-line directives, so
  the picture filled the slide instead. A front-matter `class: image`, which the engine does not
  apply as a deck class, no longer leaves an empty panel on the slide.

- The engine no longer reads the lines of a `style: |` block as deck settings. A CSS rule's
  `color: #c00;` used to set the deck-wide `color` directive on every slide, and a line named
  like a register (`lift: on`) turned that register on while the Studio showed it off. The
  engine now skips those lines as the Studio does.

- Charts read `Bn` and `BN` as billions, the same as `B` and `bn`. Before, `$5Bn` plotted at 5 with the unit `Bn`, so a chart that mixed `$5bn` and `$5Bn` drew the two a billion apart, while the narration said "five billion dollars" over the short bar. Both number readers (Segno's and `lib/core/chart-values.js`) changed together. A negative `($0.8BN)` is now also said as "down eight hundred million dollars" instead of dropping its sign.
- The Studio Guide counts `5Bn` and `5BN` as figures when it ranks what to point at, as it already did for `5bn` and `5B`.

- Corrected four false claims shipped with the bundle-era-skew fix (#2162), three of them
  in a permanent decision record: the package-root walk was never "two byte-identical
  copies" (it existed once, in `lattice-emulator.js`; the duplicate was in an unshipped
  draft), `build-anima-player.js` cannot abort on a **type** error because esbuild strips
  types rather than checking them (only a syntax error, unresolvable import or esbuild
  crash aborts it), the runtime bundle carries **167** module markers and not 1288, and
  the `loadAll()` call site is `lattice-emulator.js:2006`.
- The `LatticeManifestSchema` warning no longer claims the bundle's behavior on both
  surfaces: the loose source rethrows from the fallback `require` rather than validating
  against anything.
- Pinned the three fixes with regression tests, each proven to fail under the mutation it
  guards: the `STEPS` ordering that keeps a generator ahead of the bundles inlining it,
  the join covering every consumer of a background library dist, and the require-cache
  schema freeze (checked in a child process, because an in-file assertion is masked by an
  earlier test loading `lib/layout/gate.js`). Adds `test/unit/core/pkg-root.test.js`.

- `dist/lattice-emulator.js` no longer validates manifests against a schema frozen at
  bundle time. `lib/components/index.js` read `lib/components/**/*.manifest.json` from
  disk at run time but `require`d `manifest.schema.json`, which esbuild inlines — so a
  bundle older than the working tree rejected manifests the loose source accepted, with
  an error telling the author to add a field the schema already had. The schema is now
  read from the package root, the same directory the manifests come from.
- `npm run build` converges in one pass when an Anima source changes. `build-anima-player.js`
  ran 18 steps after `build-emulator.js`, which inlines its output, so the emulator was
  written 2.6s before the file it contained.
- The four workspace library dists now join before their FIRST consumer. `build-player-core.js`
  bundles `@laticent/cadenza` but ran six steps ahead of the join, reading a file a live
  background process could be rewriting — a race won by 5.7s of scheduling luck.

- PowerPoint and LibreOffice exports draw a curved mark's arcs correctly: Calco swapped each curve's two control points, so an arc came out as a pinched loop.

- an inline code chip (or mark) in the editable export is always a native text highlight in a color close to the page behind it, including over a finish's grid or glow, so no picture film sits over or under the words and the text stays editable.

- In an editable PowerPoint or ODP, a row whose counter is drawn in its own grid cell (`regulatory-update`'s "01") no longer hides the row's pill labels: Calco measured that counter as covering the whole row, kept the row's pills in the slide picture, and wrote that picture over their text. The counter now covers only its cell, and the pills are shapes with their labels on top.

- the editable export keeps the deck logo as its own picture on every slide, with its transparency, instead of baking it into the shared background, a photo panel's picture or a whole-slide picture depending on the slide; a finish's own full-slide layers no longer merge the pictures on a slide into one.

- an editable export no longer reads text that an opaque box or picture covers as live text (it exported a phantom page number on top of a panel), and photographs stay JPEG pictures, so a photo-heavy deck is smaller.
- an editable `.pptx` names a bold or italic face by its own family with the bold or italic flag, embedded in that family's slot, so LibreOffice and Google Slides find the font by name instead of falling back to a sans.

- **Editable `.pptx` is now schema-valid.** PptxGenJS 3.12 wrote a paragraph's properties before every run instead of once, listed the notes master out of order, and declared a slide master per slide that the file does not contain. Calco now writes the package itself, without any of the three, so a strict reader such as PowerPoint has nothing to repair. Text renders exactly as before.

- the Studio's editable export tells the author when a slide could not be made editable and is one picture in the file, instead of only logging it to the console.

- In the live preview, a wifi or video slide no longer pulls the deck's running header and footer into its content area. When the deck-wide `class:` arrived after the first pass, the browser-side layout pass put both inside the slide's stage, while the export kept them in the header and footer bands.

- The reader view and narration now carry the eyebrow of a wifi or video slide. Both components keep their eyebrow inside the card head, where the prose projection did not look, so the article showed no kicker above the heading and narration read the eyebrow after the heading instead of before it.

- The Studio editor now offers `cards-top`, `cards-center`, `cards-stretch` and `cards-spread` after `_class: cards-stack`. They already moved the default column's cards (`cards-top` lifts the first card from 206 px to 178 px down the slide; `cards-stretch` grows each card from 116 px to 135 px), but the measured modifier table still recorded them for the `horizontal` variant only, so the editor hid them on the default column.

- **Fixed: four charts said only their heading aloud.** `gantt`, `kanban`, `progress` and `timeline-list` captions (the `--captions` export and live Present) now read every task, card, bar and milestone, with statuses in words ("at risk", not "at-risk"), kanban sizes spelled out, and gantt milestones, dependencies, the plan window and "today". The radar `quadrant` variant, which also went silent, now reads each sector with its average.
- **Fixed: the Present Guide can now point at almost every sentence it hears on a chart.** Measured over the 22 chart galleries, the pointer hid on 34.5% of chart sentences and now hides on one (0.1%), and the share that lands on the exact mark or part being read rose from 21.9% to 45.0%; a sentence about the whole chart now points at the chart. Pie wedges, radar series and sectors, word-cloud words, quadrant regions and cohorts, gantt lanes, category axes (line, bar, stacked-bar, heatmap rows) and the flow charts' rows, cards and milestones now carry `data-label`. Values said by value ("six hundred thousand dollars" for `$0.6M`), signed steps, ranges and zero-thickness marks (a dumbbell bar, a 0% bullet) no longer turn the pointer away.
- **Fixed: screen readers reach every value.** Radar's description lists every score (it listed only series names), small-multiple radars are named and described, the quadrant cohort variant lists its items (it listed only cohort sizes), gantt's description names milestones, dependencies, the window and today, and heatmap and line add a hidden data table a screen reader can walk cell by cell. Kanban's size chip is announced as "size S", roadmap `horizons` rows say their status in words (shown before only by color and glyph), and progress, kanban and timeline-list rows are announced as lists.
- **Fixed: a table in Present's instant fallback reading no longer speaks its pipes and dashes** (`---------- , :--, [ ]`) in the moment before the full reading loads.
- **Fixed: chart narration that raced through numbers now says what they mean, one idea per sentence.** Radar reads each series as its shape ("Meridian is strongest on Performance and Security, at nine"); a heatmap says a peak every row shares once, then each row's low; a line reads each series' overall move, then each point, and the Present Guide points at each dot as it is read; slope and dumbbell say every move as a verb ("Northwind fell seven points, from thirty-one percent to twenty-four percent"); quadrant says where each item sits ("low on Effort and high on Reach") before its numbers; journey says its mood scale once, reads each step with who does it, and ends on the low and high points; roadmap `horizons` reads each bet with its status as a verb ("Connector v1 has shipped, in Signal Intake"); matrix-grid reads each row's placed level and what it can reach, instead of every placeholder cell. Measured over a 26-slide deck, the 90th-percentile caption cue fell from 7.6 to 5.6 seconds.
- **Fixed: "GA" is read as "general availability".** It was spoken as two letters. A map region written as a code (GA for Georgia or Gabon, TX, USA) is spelled letter by letter instead, so it is never expanded.
- **Fixed: the Present Guide lost every state on a state chart.** Since the state chart started drawing its states in SVG and hiding the list it measures, the pointer found the hidden list item and had nowhere to point, so it hid on 77 of 144 state-chart sentences. A hidden mark now hands off to the drawn one with the same `data-mark`: 144 of 144 placed. The narration also stops re-reading the state list after the transitions ("Draft start. Submitted on-track. … Published end."): it says only a state's status ("In Review is at risk.") and which states end the machine ("Published is an end state.").

- Chart SVGs now hide their marks from the accessibility tree, so a screen reader hears each chart's curated description once instead of hearing it and then walking every tick, category and value again as loose text. `role="img"` was believed to do this — ARIA calls it children-presentational and ten docblocks across nine components said so outright — but Chromium does not implement it that way for SVG: measured over the rendered gallery, all fifteen chart roots leaked their whole subtree, 24 unignored nodes under `bar` and 223 under `map`. The marks now ride in an explicit `aria-hidden` group, with `<title>`/`<desc>` left outside it so every chart keeps its accessible name.
- Nothing changes visually, and nothing changes for find-in-page: `aria-hidden` text still paints, stays in `textContent`, and is still matched by the browser's text finder.

- **Fixed:** on a dark canvas a chart's legend swatch could paint a different color from the mark it labelled — a pie wedge and its own key entry came out `oklab(0.521…)` and `oklab(0.561…)`. The family's 82% "vivid solid" wash had no token, so the recipe was retyped at ten call sites and five of them drifted onto `var(--bg)` instead of `--chart-cat-base`. Invisible on light, where the two resolve to the same color; on dark, `--bg` is the theme's canvas and the mix neutralizes warm hues toward brown. `funnel`, `piechart`, `radar`, `map`, `quadrant` and `stacked-bar` all render truer hues on dark now; light and print are pixel-identical.
- **Added:** `--chart-cat-N-body` — the 82% level as a token, beside `-fill` and `-ink`, so the recipe has one definition and cannot drift again. Charts on the mark contract read it as `--mark-body`.

- A chart caption with inline code now sets as one paragraph. `.chart-caption` was a flex column, so each text run and each code span stacked on its own line and took height from the chart above it. On the branching state-chart deck's long-labels slide, the chart's stage grows from 98px to 262px at 1280×720. A caption that starts with a code span also keeps its code chip, instead of turning into an uppercase eyebrow.

- `chart-language-census.js` matched role class names as substrings and measured container elements, so a `<g class="radar-ticks">` was reported as a second tick face that no rendered text has. It now matches whole class tokens, skips elements that hold text without painting it, covers the HTML members' labels as well as the SVG ones, and distinguishes a chart's primary figure from its secondary one — a role the family already used consistently and had never named.

- **Fixed:** a chart's authored per-mark detail no longer flashes up and vanishes as you sweep the pointer onto a mark, on the Playground, the Studio preview or Present. Radix renders the popover inside its own positioning wrapper, which kept `pointer-events:auto` while the card inside it was `none`; the reveal fires mid-gesture, the wrapper is placed at that cursor point, and the continuing motion carries the pointer into it, so the preview frame gets `pointerleave` and the layer dismisses. A hover that arrives and stops was never affected, which is why this read as an intermittent glitch. Measured on the real Playground: 7 of 9 heatmap cells closed the instant they opened.
- **Fixed:** a heatmap cell's `` `note=prose` `` annotation now reaches the hover card. The reveal layer builds the card from the `<li>`s in the mark's detail template; the cell annotation went in as bare text, so the card fell back to the compact value-only tooltip and the words were visible only in the PDF speaker note.

- A roadmap's status discs and its key now take the one status level under the `etch` and `tone` finishes, as a gantt bar does. They stayed solid green, amber and red there, the loudest status marks in the class. `pigment`, the default, is unchanged.
- The Playground repaints your last slide on reload after you move the divider, even when the reload comes soon after the page last saved that slide. A second save within 500 ms used to be skipped even when the pane had changed size, so the stored slide kept the old pane width and the next load showed an empty pane until the engine rendered.
- Inline code on a kanban card clears 4.5:1 again under the `etch` and `tone` finishes. Their card wash on a light slide is now capped at 8%. Etch's 14% put the code at 4.07:1 on carbone, cuoio, indaco and laguna; tone's 12% at 4.19:1 on carbone.
- Under `etch`, a slope chart no longer looks like `tone`: a status or signal line keeps its status ink at etch's heavier line weight, and each slopegraph dot takes etch's pale wash with an ink edge. A word cloud under `etch` keeps tone's steps, now a documented exception.

- `check:chart-fit`'s stage arm now measures only marks that are actually painted. `getClientRects()` is non-empty for a `visibility: hidden` element and `getBoundingClientRect` ignores an ancestor's clip, so a hidden measuring scaffold reported its full natural size and was counted as content cut at the stage — four false reports on one state-chart deck, with nothing visible outside the stage on any of them. The fixture's counts are unchanged, and a control that makes those same boxes visible still fires every report.

- Portrait `timeline-list` no longer clips. The date pill and the title now share one row on the rail (body and status beneath), which buys back a pill-height per entry: the four-milestone fixture with a two-line headline painted 174.1px past the stage and lost its fourth row, and now fits with 13px to spare.
- Portrait, square and strip `progress` rows sit closer (`--sp-xs` between rows, was `--sp-sm`): the five-row fixture under a two-line headline and lead painted 11.6px past the stage and now fits with 20.5px to spare. `npm run check:chart-fit` is green across landscape, portrait and square.

- **`gantt` drew `done`, `on-track` and `live` in the same green.** They shared the
  `pass` fill gradient in the kernel *and* `--state-pass-ink` in the stylesheet, so
  a legend naming three statuses painted them **pixel-identical** — measured across
  five gallery pages. Running work is now `info`, finished work `pass`.
  (`on-track` and `done` still share `pass`; five ramps cannot carry eleven status
  words, and that pair is the one collision left.)
- **A bar with no status took the same blue as a declared `pilot`.** Every gallery
  page therefore showed a blue bar the legend never named. Unstated status now
  reads as unstated — and `deferred`, which shares that neutral ramp, is drawn
  **hollow** (`fill-opacity: 0.18` over a full-strength edge) so a declared status
  and the absence of one are still two different bars. An unstated bar emits no
  legend chip, so nothing else could have told them apart.
- **The legend chip and its bars are one table now.** There were two parallel
  status→ink tables, one for bars and one for swatches, and they drifted the first
  time either moved: re-pointing `live` left the chip's edge green while the kernel
  filled its body blue.
- **The bar's leading accent was the heaviest edge in the family.** A flat `2`
  viewBox units painted **4.8px** landscape and **7.7px** portrait — and it consumed
  the inter-bar gutter, so three consecutive tasks read as one slab cut by rules. It
  is now a fraction of the frame: **4.00px** landscape, **3.38px** portrait. Above HD
  it deliberately outgrows `--chart-fill-accent`'s 7px cap (**12px at `size: 4K`**),
  because the accent is part of the mark and scales with the bar's own height and
  radius, where the DOM token is sized for a card that does not grow. The gutter is
  anchored to its landscape value, so landscape geometry is unchanged and only the
  portrait frame is normalized.
- **`kanban`'s `keyline` variant drew the same card at a 6px left rail** against
  1px on its other three edges. It now takes `--chart-fill-accent`, like every
  other leading accent in the family.
- **The neutral bar's edge is `--text-secondary`, not `--state-mute-ink`**, and
  that is a floor rather than a shade. A mute-inked edge measured **2.18:1**
  against the canvas on `onyx` and the five `a11y-*` themes and **2.87:1** on
  `concrete` — under the 3:1 graphical floor, and the body cannot carry a mark
  whose fill is a tint by design (1.15:1). An ink tier is held to a stricter
  floor than a graphical one and has headroom on the lane band the marks
  actually sit on; no declared status uses it, so an unstated bar is plainly
  visible without impersonating one.
- **The bar's leading ACCENT had a third status table**, and merging only the bar
  and chip tables left it disagreeing with both: a `live` bar painted a blue body
  with a **green** accent, a `deferred` bar drew a solid accent on a hollow
  outline, and an unstated bar kept the blue leading edge the merge was meant to
  remove. All three visible in the committed gallery. The accent now takes
  `--fill-ink` from the one table — it cannot disagree with a table it does not
  have.
- **An unstated bar has no accent at all.** The accent's only job is to reinforce
  the mark's hue at its leading edge, so with no status there is no hue and what
  it drew was a neutral sliver carrying no information — measured at 2.88:1
  against the bar's own wash on carta-dark, under the 3:1 floor. Deepening the ink
  to clear it made the bar with NO status the highest-contrast edge on the chart.
  `deferred` keeps its accent: it is a status, and on a hollow bar the accent is
  the one solid cue marking where the bar starts.

- **Fixed: hovering a chart mark no longer skews the chart or moves the data.** The detail
  reveal on the Playground, Studio preview and Present used to tilt the whole chart with
  `rotateX(7deg)`, which turned bars into trapezoids and skewed every label. It also pushed
  the hovered mark 7 units away from the chart's center, off its baseline or coordinates.
  The chart now stays flat. The hovered mark stays at full opacity while the others dim,
  and it casts a soft elevation shadow. A pie slice steps out along its own bisector, and a
