A quote now opens a value only where one can start, directly after `=`, which is what a browser does. This is the same kernel `findTopLevelH2` uses to locate a slide's title, so the masthead band was also going missing on those decks.
- **A sentence mentioning a `<style>` tag no longer blanks the deck.** An unclosed rawtext element was read as text all the way to end of file — a browser's rule, and catastrophic here: a deck stamped 0 of 3 slides because one line of prose named the tag. Rawtext is now skipped only when it actually closes.
- **`<sectionfoo>` is no longer treated as a `<section>`**, and a `>` inside a quoted attribute no longer ends the open tag early (`<section title="a>b" class="x">` now reports its class).
- **The `class` attribute is found by walking attributes, not by matching a substring.** A slide whose other attribute's value happened to contain ` class='…'` had that text read as its class and rewritten in place — tearing the neighboring value open into bogus attributes while the real class never got `form`, so the slide silently lost its chrome. A single-quoted `class='…'` is now rewritten rather than joined by a second `class` attribute, and a `$&` in a class value is no longer treated as a replacement pattern.
- **An uppercase `<SECTION>` is stamped or left alone as a whole, never half of each.** The walker reads tag names case-insensitively, as HTML defines them, but the Form stamp did not — so such a slide came out carrying the `form` chrome class with no `data-frame` at all, the exact half-stamped state the frame-identity invariant forbids.


- **The render path now says so when a deck still carries a retired Form opt-out.** `form: off`, a deck-wide `class: no-form` and a slide's `no-form` all SUPPRESSED chrome, so a deck carrying one renders differently the moment it is built against a current engine — the masthead band, the meta bay and the progress rail come back. That used to happen with a successful exit code and no other sign; `lattice` now names each shape on stderr, with the slide number and where to get the fix. The render still succeeds — we warn and coach, we never refuse an author's deck. Inert shapes (`form: standard`, a bare `form` token) stay silent, because a warning on a deck that renders identically is what teaches people to ignore warnings.

- **The Form-model z-plane legend no longer breaks its rows mid-word.** `.zlegend li` is
  a flex container, so `<b>z3</b>`, the bare text "chrome" and the `<small>` list were
  three separate flex items that shrank and wrapped independently — rendering "z 3 / chrom
  e" at 1440px and splitting `z1` at 820px. Each row's text is now one `<span>`, matching
  the `.own` legend in the same component, so it wraps as ordinary text. Verified on the
  built docs site at 1440 / 820 / 390.

- **Every hand-written list of the sovereign Frames said nine and omitted `topic`.** There are ten. The count and the names were wrong in `design/forms.md`, `README.md`, the three docs-site craft pages, `lib/components/manifest.schema.json`, the engine docstrings, a shipped slide of `examples/form.md`, and — worst — the `lint:deck` coaching that tells an author which sovereign component to reach for, where an omitted Frame is an answer the author is told does not exist.
- **The coaching list is now DERIVED** from the generated stage catalog, so it cannot drift again. The schema sentence that carried its own warning not to re-derive the set by hand no longer enumerates it at all.
- **`design/design-system.md` still advertised `form` and `no-form` as universal chrome modifiers.** The set has five members, not seven.

- **Fixed: a `<!-- _class: list bullet -->` slide gets the `.cell-stage` clip cell
  its six sibling variants already had.** The wrap decision let ANY token in the
  class list veto, and `bullet` also names the bullet CHART — a `canvas` component —
  so the list's body was left unwrapped and lost the bounded box the overflow probe
  walls. The decision now follows THE layout token (the first one naming a known
  layout, i.e. the component the slide is), the same first-match scan
  `layoutTokenFor` already uses. Measured across every component × variant
  combination the manifests declare (273): exactly one answer changes.

- **The Form gallery now carries the Lattice mark, and stops mis-stating where it lives.** `design/forms.gallery.md` taught the logo Tile in prose while rendering no logo at all — which is how it came to claim, on two slides, that the masthead bay holds the logo. It does not, and never did: the logo is frame-anchored to the slide box, which is why the mark rides the corner *above* the bay. With `logo:` set, the render now contradicts a wrong sentence on the same slide, so the next one is visible.
- Adds `lib/base/_logo/lattice-mark.svg` — the Lattice brand mark, the repo's first non-fictional logo asset (`acme-logo.svg` remains the placeholder for feature demos).

- **`logo` and `watermark` now name the Cell they actually render into.** Both Tile manifests claimed a band Cell that nothing ever docked them in — `logo` said `masthead-bay`, `watermark` said `stage` — while `base.modifiers.css` and `watermark.css` position both against the section box. The manifests said one thing and the render did another, a divergence invisible for as long as a single Frame existed.
- **They get a Cell each, not a shared one.** The two have exactly one property in common — neither docks in a band — and it is a negative one; every other Cell in the catalog names a position. A shared Cell forced a single `z`, `accepts` and `capacity` onto two Tiles that agree on none of them. `logo` is content-plane and accepts `chrome`; `watermark` is atmosphere-plane and accepts `surface`; both are `capacity: "one"`, `fill: "anchor"`.
- It also makes per-Tile suppression **expressible**, which one shared Cell made impossible: a Frame suppresses by Cell id, so no Frame could name the watermark without also naming the logo. **This is a model capability, not a behavior change** — both Cells are non-materializing and no Frame declares either, so suppressing one is inert at render today. Nothing can hide either Tile that could not hide it before.
- The Cell `region` vocabulary was defined in **three** places — the enum in `schema/cell.schema.json`, `CELL_REGIONS` in `lib/forms/index.js`, and the slicing-relocation enum in `schema/frame.schema.json` — with nothing keeping them in step; adding a region passed one and threw in another. All three now carry the same list (`coda` was already missing from the third), and a test compares them.
- `region` is now pinned **1:1 with Cell `id`**. It held by convention across all 12 Cells and nothing enforced it, while `checkSlicingIntegrity` resolves a relocation target through a region → Cell map where the first entry wins — so a second Cell claiming an existing region would have bound relocations to whichever loaded first.
- No rendered output changes: `examples/frame-chrome-and-notes.md` (logo) and `examples/form.md` (watermark) export byte-identical HTML and PDF across the change.

- Fuoco no longer cancels a pending "insert text, then go to it" when a view makes a report that changes nothing, no
  longer judges a report made during a delivery against stale focus, and `reportUnit` takes `quiet`, so a scrolled
  view that cannot centre the focused slide cannot pull the focus back. Five presses of "next" with a scrolled
  preview and a map now publish exactly once each; before, the fifth flickered 5, 4, 5. The hub's new scroll model
  and its failing arms run at 5,000 cases.

- **gantt:** bar and milestone captions are weight 500 instead of 600, so they no longer match the lane names. The lane name keeps 600 and the item inside it reads one step lighter, as `.quadrant-dot-label` and flowchart node labels already do.

- **gantt: overlapping tasks in a lane no longer hide each other.** Every task in a
  lane was drawn at one y, so two spans that overlapped on the axis were drawn on
  top of each other and only the later one survived — a lane read as a relay of
  abutting segments however much its tasks actually ran in parallel. Tasks now pack
  into sub-rows: ones that clear each other still share a row, ones that overlap get
  their own, and packing reads the bars rather than the captions, so a long task
  name never invents a row.
- **gantt: bar captions stop truncating with room to spare.** A caption's budget was
  bounded by the next task in the LANE rather than the next mark on its own row, so
  `Scoring model v2` ellipsized to `Scoring model…` against a bar more than twice as
  wide as the text.
- **gantt: a milestone that falls inside a bar's span gets its own row.** It used to
  be drawn on top of the bar; in dark mode an unstated milestone and an unstated bar
  resolve to the same fill, so the diamond all but disappeared.
- **gantt: the bar's leading accent is clipped to the bar.** It carried a smaller
  corner radius than the bar (0.83 against 3), so across the rounded corner its
  corners stood outside the bar's silhouette and the bar's own stroke ran between
  the two as a seam — the left edge read as a tab stuck to the side rather than the
  bar's own edge.
- **gantt: the status key's swatch is centered on its label.** The swatch sat at
  `ly - swatch*0.8` against a label drawn `dominant-baseline: central` on `ly`,
  putting its center 30% of its own height above the text — measured 15px out at
  200dpi.
- **gantt: the `today` rule is a neutral reference drawn behind the bars.** It wore
  `--state-info-ink`, the same ink as its own `live` / `pilot` / `decision` bars, and
  was painted over them at full strength. It now takes `--text-heading`, like every
  other reference line in the chart family, and sits under the marks.
- **gantt: two independent tasks that abut on the axis show a real gap.** The
  inter-bar gutter went 1.5 → 2.5 viewBox units; at 1.5 the two bars' strokes closed
  the gap to nothing.
- **gantt: the chart spans the full width of its box, and is as tall as its rows
  need.** `.gantt-svg` was a height-capped SVG, so a chart whose viewBox was taller
  than its stage did not clip — it letterboxed, narrowing until it fit and taking
  the whole drawing's legibility with it, which is the one failure the Fit Spine
  cannot see because nothing overflows. It is width-driven now (`width:100%;
  height:auto; flex-shrink:0`), the way the `render=html` charts beside it —
  kanban, progress, roadmap — already behave. Measured on the stress gallery page:
  60% → 100% of the chart body's width, captions 12.2px → 20.4px. An oversized
  gantt now overflows and is reported by name ("CONTENT CLIPPED — First cut on
  each: p1 'Workstream 3'") instead of shrinking in silence.
- **gantt: the chart never shrinks to absorb an oversized plan.** Bars, captions
  and row spacing are a fixed size whatever the chart carries — every gantt draws
  its bars at one height and its captions at one size, and more rows make the chart
  taller rather than smaller. An intermediate version of this change compressed the
  row band as the row count rose, which is the engine quietly covering for a slide
  carrying too much: the bars thin out, the chart still "fits", and nobody is told.
- **gantt has a stated BUDGET instead of a shrink.** Count bar ROWS, not lanes:
  overlapping tasks stack, and inclusive spans overlap more than they look
  (`Q1..Q2` then `Q2..Q3` both cover Q2), so a sequential-looking plan written that
  way costs two rows a lane. The status key costs about another lane (21 viewBox
  units). Measured with a key on a 1152x335 chart body: four one-row lanes fit and
  five overflow; on a roomier stage five fit. The numbers are in the component's
  docs and the enforcement is the render — past the budget a chart overflows and is
  named (`CONTENT CLIPPED`, with the first thing cut) rather than quietly scaled
  down. Two shipped decks were genuinely over the budget and were rewritten to
  fit (`examples/palette-cascade-flip.md`, `exemplars/government-public/rfp-response.md`);
  a third was trimmed and did not need to be, and has been put back.
- **An over-budget gantt keeps its axis.** The chart is centered in its stage with
  `safe center`, so a chart TALLER than the stage aligns to the top and loses its
  tail rather than being centered and clipped at both ends — which took the time
  axis off the top, and a gantt without its axis is unreadable in a way one missing
  its last lane is not.
- **gantt: the band is smaller, so every existing gantt redraws.** This is the
  most broadly visible line here and the earlier draft of this fragment did not
  state it. Landscape bars go 36px to 28.8px on a 1152px chart body (the band
  went 15/5/5.5 to 12/4/4.5 viewBox units); portrait goes 20/6/8.5 to 16/5/7.
  Nothing an author WRITES changes, and every committed PDF re-renders slightly
  tighter. **But "it fit before" is not a promise this release keeps**, and the
  cause is the letterbox, not the band: a height-capped chart used to "fit" by
  shrinking itself, so a deck could be over its budget and never say so. With
  the cap gone a chart draws at its natural height, and two shipped decks that
  had been fitting that way now overflow and had to be rewritten — measured on
  `examples/palette-cascade-flip.md`, which cleared its stage by 4.2px before
  and misses by 10.2px after. That is the silent shrink being withdrawn, which
  is the point of the change, but it is a real migration cost.
- **gantt: a portrait chart is no longer cut at the bottom.** Both bands were
  sized against the `max-height` cap that used to letterbox an oversized chart
  down until it fit. Deleting the cap re-derived the landscape band and missed
  the portrait one, so the canonical two-lane chart painted 9px past
  `.cell-stage` — which is `overflow: clip`, so it was cut in silence, and the
  emulator does not warn at that size. `check:chart-fit` is the gate that sees
  it: green on the base, red on the branch, green again now, with 68.7px of
  headroom where there was -9px.

- Offline in Firefox, the Studio preview, the Playground and Print now load their fonts, figures and diagrams. Firefox gave a preview frame no service worker when the frame was already on the page as it was written, so with the network gone those files failed to load. The preview now writes a new frame before it goes on the page, and on Firefox briefly takes a live frame out of the page while it rewrites it.

- Charts now read money the way global clients write it. A currency code (`EUR 4.2M`, `CHF 4.2M`), a country dollar (`US$4.2M`, `R$4,2M`), a currency after the number (`4.2M €`, `4200€`, `4.2M EUR`) and the magnitude words `Mio`/`Mrd` (and, beside a currency, `mn`, `Md` and `Cr`) used to make the value unreadable, so the chart drew nothing. They now plot, `lint:deck` flags a typo inside one (`EUR --4M`), and narration says them in the currency's name ("four point two million euros"; `¥` and `₹` too).
- Chart axes and value labels keep the currency where the author put it (`4.5M €`, `EUR 4.5M`) and print a decimal comma when every value with a decimal uses one (`4,2` gives `4,5`, not `4.5`). This reaches every chart that prints computed numbers: `bar`, `bullet`, `heatmap`, `line`, `scatter`, `slope`, `stacked-bar` and `waterfall`.
- `line`, `stacked-bar` and `waterfall` size the value-axis label column to the widest label, so `$12.5M` and `EUR 5.5M` no longer print cut short as `$12.…` and `EUR…`.
- Narration of slide text reads a decimal comma as a decimal (`4,2` is "four point two", not "forty-two") and says `Mio.`, `Mrd.` and a currency symbol after a number as words (`4,2 Mio. €` is "four point two million euros").

- The nightly golden bless no longer crashes after its full check: it reads the regression gate's `report.json` instead of the gate's piped stdout, which arrived cut off at 146,176 bytes. `regression-gate.mjs --json` now drains its output before exiting, so any caller piping it gets the whole report.

- The nightly golden bless now refreshes the docs landing page's showcase images when it re-blesses their source galleries, so its PR no longer fails docs-build on a stale showcase. Its verdict comment also links the run whose artifact holds the drift montages, which matters on nights too large for golden-diff's PR job.

- **The committed golden corpus is fresh again — 114 of 286 goldens were stale.** `npm run
  regress` on a clean `main` drifted 110 of 211 deck goldens and 4 of 75 gallery pairs
  (`comparison`, `evidence`, `kpi`, `authority-chain`). The corpus had not been swept since
  #1983 on 2026-09-01, and eight render-input PRs merged after it — the `cards:` register
  (#2011), auto-split (#2016, #2042), the universal coda (#2018), the table family's outer
  edge (#2055), `list-tabular`'s responsive columns (#2059) — each blessing what it touched
  directly and leaving the rest. Deck goldens are promoted individually rather than by a
  blanket re-render, so only what actually drifted is rewritten.
- **A red gate reports nothing, which is the reason this matters.** While `regress` is red
  across a deck it cannot surface a NEW regression in that deck. Refreshing the corpus found
  one that was hiding: `examples/gallery-jargon` slide 15 renders a `Content clipped` stamp
  and cuts row 06 in half.
- **Checked, not assumed.** No golden changed page count, so
  `2026-08-24-golden-corpus-re-bless.md` §5b ("a page-count flip is restored and reported")
  had nothing to restore — and `examples/portrait-roadmap`, the artifact that note exempts,
  matches its 8-page golden on this host. A `pdftotext` word-multiset diff leaves 113 of 118
  refreshed goldens word-identical; three of the five deltas are extraction artifacts where a
  wrap position moved (`derisk` → `de risk`).
- **Fixed: `examples/gallery-jargon` slide 15 no longer ships cut off.** #2059 capped
  `list-tabular`'s trailing column at `fit-content(26cqi)` while the description column
  kept taking every remaining pixel, so a ledger of six phrase-length metas wrapped all
  six rows to two lines where three had wrapped before, outgrew the stage, and lost its
  tail. The slide takes `flex-meta` — the modifier that component documents for a
  trailing column carrying a phrase rather than a stamp — and now renders every meta on
  one line. A 289-deck overflow sweep says it was the only slide in the corpus that
  clipped, so #2059's default is unchanged.
- **Fixed: `examples/accent-on-accent`'s golden showed the wrong theme.** The deck declares
  `theme: atelier-dark`; the committed PDF had been rendered with `indaco`, the engine
  default — measured by re-rendering at three palettes and pixel-diffing each against the
  old golden (`indaco` 10.1%, `atelier` 100%, `cuoio` 100%). The engine is not at fault:
  `resolve-palette.js` is byte-unchanged since that golden was blessed, the producer passes
  no palette argument, and the deck renders `atelier-dark` deterministically today. A CLI
  palette argument or an exported `LATTICE_PALETTE` outranks a deck's own front matter, and
  nothing reports the substitution — so a golden can be blessed against a theme its deck
  never asked for.
- **The docs site's showcase rasters follow the gallery goldens.** Re-blessing the `kpi`
  gallery left `docs/public/showcase/kpi.{light,dark}.webp` stale, which fails
  `docs/scripts/rasterize-showcase.mjs --check` and takes the `docs-build` and `preview`
  jobs with it. Regenerated. A gallery bless owes this whenever the blessed gallery is one
  of the 30 the showcase samples.
- **Fixed: `themes/palette-audit` shipped two slides that lost content.** A corpus-wide scan of
  every committed golden's text layer for the engine's `Content clipped` tag found 9 clipped
  slides across 5 artifacts. Six are deliberate — `examples/overflow-fix-me` exists to
  demonstrate overflow, `examples/marker-corner` renders the corner collision on purpose, and
  `premise.gallery` p3 is a labelled stress test of the eight-row ceiling. The other two were
  real: the audit deck's opening slide was a `title` layout carrying a six-line Key Insight
  blockquote, which the title component has no slot for, so the panel occluded the lede; and the
  scoring slide silently dropped its `Hue coverage — 5 pts` bullet. Both were `title` slides
  doing a content slide's job, and both now carry their prose on a `content` slide. The deck
  goes from 2 content-losing slides to 0, and from 1 overflow warning to none.
- **A hard-wrapped paragraph is a taller paragraph.** `lib/engine/index.js` sets markdown-it's
  `breaks: true` (matching marp-core), so every newline inside a paragraph or blockquote renders
  as a `<br>`. The audit deck's Key Insight was wrapped at ~100 columns in the source and got one
  hard break per source line, inflating the panel well past what the text needs. Unwrapping the
  source, not cutting the words, is what made it fit.
- **Fixed: a unit test enumerated scratch files as "committed decks".**
  `slide-boundaries.test.js` walks the working tree for `*.md`, and `regression-gate.mjs`
  writes transient `.regr-<name>.dark.md` sources beside the real galleries while it renders
  (it must — the emulator resolves a deck's relative assets against the OUTPUT directory).
  Running the unit suite during a corpus sweep therefore failed with a bare `ENOENT` on a file
  that had already been cleaned up. That is the exact pairing a golden refresh performs, and it
  cost a full debugging cycle before the pre-push hook caught it with the filename attached.
  Dotfiles are now excluded; 306 committed decks are still enumerated.
- **Also blessed: `list-tabular`'s gallery pair, whose drift arrived from #2066 mid-review.** The
  `{LABEL}` pill work moved the trailing meta column down by exactly 0.75pt and its committed
  golden predates that. Established as real geometry rather than cross-host rasterization by
  comparing the PDF TEXT LAYER's bounding boxes: the x-coordinates are byte-identical and every
  affected value's y shifted by the same 0.75pt — a difference in rasterization cannot move a
  text-layer coordinate at all. This branch touches no `list-tabular` file, so the drift
  reproduces on `main`; it is blessed here because this is the PR whose subject is corpus
  freshness, and merging it while knowingly leaving a stale golden would falsify its own claim.

- **Fixed: a PR that only adds an npm script no longer reads as a dependency change in the
  golden before/after comment.** `tools/golden-diff.mjs` treated any `package.json` edit as a
  dependency bump, so it rendered every gallery and skipped the base render that separates
  "this PR moved it" from "stale on main". #2583 added one `scripts` line and its comment
  listed 46 changed slides. `golden-affected.mjs` now drops a `package.json` edit confined to
  inert keys (`scripts`, `description`, `keywords` and other metadata) before either rule
  reads it. On #2583's own diff the render scope goes from `shared` (20 galleries rendered,
  69 left to the cap) to `none`. A dependency, `version`, `exports` or lockfile change still
  counts.

- `guards: strict` no longer claims a trim the delivered file does not carry. Exporting
  `-o deck.html` skips the guard — that file is written from a string before the page
  renders, so no clamp could ever reach it — and the console says so instead of printing
  `✂ TRIMMED` for a run whose only artifact is untrimmed. The `⚠ OVERFLOW` line then names
  the pages that really clip in that file, which it previously left off.
- Exporting a PDF keeps the trim and now warns that the `.html` sidecar beside it does not
  carry one, instead of leaving the two deliverables of a single export to disagree in
  silence. `--fluid` and `--player` both carry it and are named as the fix.

- `guards: strict` no longer removes more text than it needs to. The measurer read a
  slide's geometry in two units at once, so a scaled preview cut a paragraph to a sixth
  of its lines; `line-height: normal` was guessed at 1.4x the font size, which cost seven
  lines on a 16px face; and the line count was rounded rather than counted. All three are
  measured now, from the renderer's own line boxes and in the same unit the overflow
  probe uses. Every existing gate could see a cut that was too SMALL and none could see
  one that was too large — the new post-condition (a clamp never leaves a whole line of
  its box empty) is that arm. Driven on the real Playground: the same deck now clamps to
  the same line count at a 42% and a 33% preview scale, where it previously cut to three
  lines at one width and went silent — with the overflow ring on — at the other. It was not
  a preview-only defect: exporting the same deck to PDF from the Studio dropped a full line
  of copy out of the delivered file and left the room it cut it from empty. A new end-to-end
  arm exports the same deck twice and holds the floor that catches it: a `guards: strict`
  export never delivers less copy than the untrimmed one.
- The live preview and the export now reach the same verdict on a trim. They shared the
  kernel and not the policy: the export refused a cut that did not make the slide fit
  while the runtime kept it, so a `--fluid` export shipped a clamp — on a slide still
  carrying the overflow ring — that the same run's console reported as reverted.
- A residual too small for the overflow warning to see no longer passes as a fit, and a
  residual on a box the guard never touched no longer throws away a good cut elsewhere on
  the slide.
- Clamping one column no longer credits its recovered height to another. A two-up card
  the planner declared fitting came back 16px over, and the guard then threw the whole
  cut away — so `strict` was refusing fits it could have made on exactly the split
  layouts it exists for.
- An author's own `id` can no longer collide with the guard's internal one. A deck
  writing `<p id="s1tb0">` could make the guard clamp a different element than the one it
  planned, including a heading, which no role is ever allowed to be.
- A throwing overflow probe now counts as "still overflowing" rather than as a pass, and
  the export and the runtime resolve `guards-strict` with the same matcher —
  `no-guards-strict` used to enable the trim on one path and not the other.

- **Present's Guide points at the funnel band a sentence opens with.** A sentence that leads with a
  number and names the mark after it ("870 reached a proposal, and 214 signed") used to fall back to
  the whole chart; the Guide now points at the band whose value opens the sentence, when exactly one
  mark has that value and a word of its label is in the sentence.

- **Large pills in the exported PDF sit on center.** The export's Chrome takes a fallback that nudged every pill's label down 0.05em. On a pill set at 18.5px or larger, which in today's type scale means a pill in an `h1` or an `h2`, that nudge put the label low: up to 2.25px in an `h1` and 1.38px in an `h2`. Those pills now take no nudge, which leaves them within 0.63px of center. Smaller pills (body text, `h3`, and the `:sm` size in any heading) and every pill on a sketch slide keep the nudge as before. Current browsers, which center with `text-box`, are unaffected.

- **Fixed: an animated chart no longer shrinks in the `--player` export, and no longer
  trips "Text too small" once its motion mounts.** The player's CSS prune dropped every
  `.anima-live` rule, because Anima adds that class only at runtime, so the live chart
  fell back to the browser's 300×150 default size: a heatmap in a 1152×424 chart body
  drew at 300×169, with its labels shrunk to match. `.anima-live` is now on the prune
  safelist. Separately, `probeFigureLegibility` measured the hidden poster SVG as if it
  rendered at 1:1, which read a heatmap's 7-unit labels as 7px ("Text too small ·
  5.2pt") on a slide whose live chart set them at 12.3pt. It now skips any figure that
  renders no box.

- The comparison page no longer says Lattice's PowerPoint export cannot be edited. It now describes both exports as they ship: the plain `.pptx` is one picture per slide, and `--editable` (the Studio's Editable text switch) writes every paragraph as a real text box, with charts, diagrams and equations kept as pictures. The home page's pitch card now says a deck exports to PowerPoint with text you can edit.
- The comparison page catches up with the Studio. It no longer says Lattice has no live co-editing, no editor without Markdown, or nothing for presenting: the matrix marks live co-editing and no-syntax editing as partial, and the "where we're weaker" cards now name the real limits (up to four people and no video in a live session, no free-form canvas, no slide transitions). It credits Compose, live sessions, comments, on-device AI and the installable Studio, and it reads the component count from the catalog instead of the stale "fifty-six". The office suites and design tools now get partial credit for version history.
- The home page's Studio section now says you can write in Compose, a plain writing page with no Markdown, and that up to four people can edit a deck live, with an optional voice call.

- A `functionplot` figure no longer blinks while you type on its slide in the Studio: the plugin host now remembers each finished drawing (at the size it was drawn) and holds the old one while an edited plot redraws. Measured in the real Studio, six keystrokes in the heading went from 15–19 empty frames to none, and six edits to the plot's own config from 24–25 to none. The Playground runs the same runtime code; it was not measured separately.

- `engineering/house-style.md` §1 no longer contradicts itself about US-English enforcement. Its prose said the two `us-english-stem-audit` arms block; its own table called the commit-msg hook "the only automated check left." The prose was right — both arms fail `npm test` with exit 1 on a seeded British spelling — so the table and the section summary now name them, along with the paths the walk does not reach.

- **hub-spoke under `mode: sketch` measures the hand face it paints.** The width estimate billed every character at a flat 0.66em; Shantell Sans paints digits at 0.70em, `%` at 0.98em and `M` at 1.04em, so values ran past their room and a hub value like `$120M` reached past the edge of its disc. A measured per-character table replaces the flat number: every sketch label on the demo deck and both galleries now paints at or under its estimate (worst 0.975×, was 1.270×), and names wrap less often because lowercase is no longer over-billed.
- **A hub name keeps its words whole when a smaller type size fits.** `fitHubText` cut a word mid-run at full size before trying a smaller size, so a tiered hub printed `Framewor` over `k` in sketch. A hub whose name only fits by such a cut now prints in smaller type, in either face; a break after a hyphen, slash, dot or colon, or between CJK characters, is unchanged. No shipped deck's clean output changes.
- `npm run fonts:measure` re-measures hub-spoke's hand table beside `GLYPH_UPPER` and fails `--check` when an entry under-counts.

- An inline icon and the word after it now stay on one line. `^{warehouse} Snowflake` used to end one line with the icon and start the next with "Snowflake", so the icon labeled nothing; the pair now wraps as one, in the page, the PDF and the editable PowerPoint and ODP.

- A pill, an inline `code` or a bold word in the middle of a list item's text no longer splits the text into separate pieces in `list-steps`, `checklist`, `pricing`, `verdict-grid`, `matrix-2x2`, `cycle`, `cards-grid`, `cards-stack`, `kpi`, `list` and `agenda`. Before, a flex or grid item laid each piece out on its own, so a step title could become the title, a pill stretched across the card, and the rest of the title beneath it. A trailing pill or `code` still sits in its own slot. A demo deck, `examples/inline-run-labels.md`, shows it; twelve decks in the repo render differently, each from scattered to a flowing sentence.

- A plugin's inline `@kind{…}` span (and a fence) draws again on the 10 slide types the `inline-run` pass serves (`cards-grid`, `agenda`, `cards-stack` and the rest; `cycle` is still held back by its own pass). #2831 registered `inline-run` on 11 components, and the list of passes that rebuild a slide from its text, read off the registry, began refusing plugins on those slides. A pass can now say `readsText: false`; `inline-run` does, because it only wraps a label's words in a span.

- **Fixed: every export stopped issuing 37 doomed font requests per navigation.** A
  stylesheet's relative `url()` resolves against the stylesheet, and the export inlines
  `dist/lattice.css` into the deck document instead of linking it — silently rebasing its
  37 self-hosted `url('fonts/…woff2')` faces onto the output directory, where all 37
  404ed. Measured on a real sidecar: 74 declared faces, 37 `loaded` and 37 `error`. Type
  was never wrong (each doomed face had a working twin — the base64 block, or KaTeX's
  `<link>` — and the browser fell back within the family group), so nothing showed. The
  inlined copy now drops a face the document already supplies and leaves everything else
  byte for byte: **37 failed requests → 0**, ~21 ms saved per navigation against ~17 ms
  of one-off scan cost per render. For a caller-supplied `--css` sheet, every rule is
  second-opinioned by a real CSS parser before it is removed, so an unanticipated
  stylesheet degrades to the old behavior rather than losing CSS.

- `inventory` now seats four rows plus the trailing insight in the default ledger look. The Playground renders the component's skeleton, which ends in a `> insight` blockquote, and at `hd` the rows and accent band measured 429px against a 400px stage, so the band was clipped mid-line under a "Content clipped" tag. Row titles are display type but inherited the body's 1.6 line height, so each 31px title claimed a 49px line. Every look's titles now set `--lh-tight`, and the same skeleton measures 380px and centers. Wrapped timeline titles also lose the loose gap between their lines.
- The `inventory cards` pull-quote marks now sit on the sentence. They were generated on the blockquote around a block `<p>`, so each mark rendered on a line of its own above and below the quote.
- `inventory` split pages (portrait, `mobile`, `square`, and any box that cuts the run one row per page) no longer repeat the trailing insight on every page. It shows once, after the last row, and every page still reserves its space and the forward pill's, so a row sits at the same height on every page of the run, the last included (within 1px, measured at portrait, square and mobile). At `square`, `editorial` split pages stacked the insight on top of the row; they now stack it below. The `timeline` dot is sized from the numeral it holds rather than from container units: at portrait a 40px numeral used to spill out of a 29px circle, and the dot sat at the top of a page-tall row, far from its title. Now the row keeps its natural height and the dot stays on its title. The `timeline` insight follows the last row on a split page, and `editorial` split pages center like the other three looks.
- The forward "next" pill on a split page is now right-aligned in components whose stage is a grid. It stretched into a full-width bar under the row, seen on `inventory editorial` at portrait.
- `inventory` at `size: portrait` in the Playground and Studio now fits all four looks on one page. Those surfaces render in the browser with no auto-split, so a portrait inventory is a single tall page carrying every row. Measured in the Playground at 390px on the gallery's four rows, the 844px stage held cards at 866px, editorial at 934px, and a timeline still laid out as four 200px columns with its titles wrapping one word per line. At `tall` the timeline now runs vertically, with the dot beside each title and a connector between dots. Cards and editorial come down one spacing rung and set their prose at `--lh-snug`, and editorial's item titles use `--fs-h3`. The gallery deck now measures 820px (cards), 810px (timeline) and 827px (editorial), and the skeleton with its insight leaves 41–194px spare in every look. Landscape slides are unchanged.

- **Studio:** Import deck… now lets you pick a `.lattice` file on iPhone and iPad. iOS grayed it out because it has no file type for `.lattice`, so the picker there no longer filters by type. On desktop, the picker also accepts a `.lattice` saved as `.zip`.

- The agent kit's checker now runs the **linter** as well as the presentation
  reviewer. It shipped with only the second, so an invented `_class` — the single
  most likely mistake a model makes writing a Lattice deck — came back "No
  findings. The checkable half is clean" over a deck that would not render.
  Findings merge, errors first.
- `check.mjs --json` emits one envelope, `{ partial, files: [...] }`, and it
  carries the partial-check flag. The bare array suppressed that flag in exactly
  the mode a machine reads, so a check that skipped half its rules returned `[]`
  and read as clean. It also now accepts several files instead of silently
  ignoring all but the first, reports a missing path or a directory in one line
  rather than a raw stack trace, and identifies itself by real path — a consumer
  wrapper named `check.mjs` used to trigger the CLI and exit the process instead
  of importing.
- `label-title` no longer misses a heading behind a period qualifier. `## Q2
  Results` and `## Q3 Financials` are the deck canon's own worked examples of a
  label heading, and both passed clean: the digit guard fired on the `2` and
  returned before the label check ran.
- A density finding now names the element that is over budget. "A split-compare
  element runs to 19 words" left the reader to count seven candidates by hand. Its
  fix line is also a sentence again — it used to concatenate "Tighten to " with a
  description of the target, yielding "Tighten to a stacked card is a short
  paragraph at most."

- **Fixed: `kpi` draws a rule between its rows, never around them.** The support
  rail bracketed itself — a heavy rule above the first support and another below
  the last — and `compliance` carried the same defect one modifier over, a border
  under every row plus a heavy one under the last. Those are outer edges, not
  separators; `2026-09-03-table-outer-edge-rules.md` retired the same thing across
  the table family. Interior separators are unchanged at 1px `--border` and move by
  at most half a pixel at the painted edge — removing the floor takes a pixel of
  border out of the column and `compliance`'s `space-between` list hands it back to
  the gaps (+0.00px and +0.50px on the gallery). At `tall` and `strip`, where the rail linearizes
  into one ledger, the demoted hero loses the same outer top edge and the first
  support gains the separator that now divides it from the lead row.
- **Changed: the `kpi compliance` row no longer declares a status column it cannot
  fill.** The pill declared `grid-column: 3` but sat one level too deep to be a grid
  item, so the track resolved to 0px and the rule read as working while doing nothing.
  The phantom track is gone and the row is a truthful two-column grid, which
  hands its column gap back to the label: 858.9px to 922.9px, 64px reclaimed. The pill still
  trails its text: right-anchoring it needs a wrapper element around the label, which
  is a DOM change rather than a CSS one.
- **Fixed: a third sub-bullet on a `kpi compliance` row no longer prints on top of
  the second.** Every sub-bullet after the first was pinned to the same grid row.
- **Fixed: `kpi spotlight` supports sit under the rule that heads them,** and a
  fifth metric lands in the rail instead of under the hero card.
- **Fixed: `kpi trajectory` sizes its columns to the metrics authored.** The grid
  was pinned at four, so a 3-metric slide — the count the docs recommend — left an
  empty 270px track, 23% of the stage.
- **Changed: the `kpi` hero is composed as the focus it is.** Its content centers on
  both axes — value, label and status line together — instead of parking in the upper
  left, and the corner spark, orphaned once the content centers, retires. The value's
  size is deliberately unchanged: it is author-supplied text of unbounded width, and
  scaling it made ordinary figures like `$12,480,000` print over the rail. The column
  ratio is unchanged too — sweeping it showed the rail wraps at the documented density
  at every ratio worth having, so the split was never the lever.
- **Fixed: a `kpi spotlight` support's value keeps a lead under the rule that heads it,
  at `wide` and `square`.** Top-aligning the rail packed the value against its hairline —
  an accented capital measured 0.00px of white between rule and ink, at 400dpi and at 1x,
  and a `$` merged into the line at 1x. The lead is `0.12em` on the ruled rows. That is
  the ceiling a 4-metric slide allows: 0.13em is the first value that pushes the row past
  the stage (1.13px at 16:9) and the status pill starts losing ink at 0.14em, none of
  which the export's overflow warning reports. Measured at 600dpi in rail row 3 the lead leaves
  `École` 2.24px, `Ålborg` 2.40px, `Ärlig` 3.20px, `$2.4B` 6.24px and a bare `2.4` 18.72px.
  **Row 4 runs about 1.1px tighter than row 3 at the same value** — the same `École` measures
  2.36px in row 3 and 1.24px in row 4 — so 1.24px, not 2.24px, is the floor a 4-metric slide
  actually ships.
  Doubly-marked capitals stay a known miss: `Ǻ` (U+01FA, ring *and* acute — not `Å`,
  which clears) starts its ink 5.60px above the hairline, and eight more cross by
  1.9–7.9px, further than the whole lead reaches.
- **No lead at `tall` and `strip`, and the reason is capacity.** Applying it there pushed a
  dense 4-metric portrait deck at `compact` past the stage — inside the documented
  `tall.soft: 4` — where the same deck without it is clean. Two drafts of this note instead
  justified the exclusion with a measurement of the linearized ledger's rules; both were
  wrong, and the second usefully so. The export never renders that ledger: `kpi`'s metric
  list overflows a portrait box at as few as two metrics, so the Fit Spine splits it to one
  element per page — measured on main and here alike — and a single-metric page has no
  separator to cross. The crossing those drafts reported reproduces only under `--no-split`,
  which the engine documents as instrumentation rather than an authoring mode.
- **What changes at `tall` and `strip` is the outer edge, and it is visible.** The demoted
  hero loses the heavy top rule it used to carry; `examples/adaptive-sizing.pdf` shows the
  before and after. The row-2 separator added alongside it needs an unsplit two-metric
  ledger, so it reaches the runtime preview and the Studio rather than a PDF.
- **Re-blessed 46 committed deck goldens, and measured the footprint rather than reporting
  the gate's number.** Isolated — both CSS bundles built here, every deck rendered twice in
  one tree on one machine, rasterized and compared page-by-page — this change moves **77
  pages across 46 decks**, 1 to 4 per deck, and no page without a `kpi` moves at all. CI's
  `golden-diff` reports 130 slides across 52 because it compares against goldens blessed on
  other machines, where Skia's rasterization is not bit-identical; its own header documents
  that band.
- **Trade, stated with both numbers: top-aligning the rail moves its slack rather than
  removing it.** A `spotlight` row is 187.1px and a support's content is ~103px, so ~84px of
  slack exists either way. Before, that slack was split — 44.25px above the ink and 44.27px
  below — and the half above is what stranded each hairline from the number it heads. Now all
  of it sits below: the rule-to-ink gap is **0.00px** and the last row's trailing band is
  **83.72px**, against 44.27px before. Total whitespace is unchanged; only its distribution
  moves. Two candidates that zero the band were built and rejected on looking —
  `space-between` tears each number away from its own label, and content-sized rows stop the
  hero panel stretching. Closing it properly means re-deciding the rail's vertical
  composition, which is a design question rather than a padding.

- **Fixed: a `quadrant` name now says which dot it belongs to.** On the
  fourteen-initiative stress slide, six of the fourteen names sat closer to
  another initiative's dot than to their own, and the chart carried no leader
  lines — so proximity, its only attribution channel, gave the wrong answer six
  times. The leader emitter `scatter` already had moved into the shared label
  kernel and `quadrant` now draws it too: a hairline from a name that had to
  travel, back to the mark it names. Nothing is drawn where a label already sits
  against its own dot, so an ordinary quadrant is unchanged — and nothing is
  drawn where the line would have to pass through a neighbor's name, because a
  hairline through someone else's letterforms points the reader at the wrong
  entity.
- **Fixed: a column of chart labels no longer reads against the dots it
  labels.** `placeLabels` was greedy in authoring order, so a name authored
  first took the best position and a later one could end up painted above a mark
  that sits below it. Measured over 20,000 randomized layouts, 18.61% of
  the label pairs sharing a column read against their own marks, and 6.33% did
  so with marks a reader can plainly separate; the two fall to 6.04% and 2.50%.
  The order is bought with a different anchor, never by dropping or overprinting
  a name — the same corpus drops six fewer names than before.
- **Changed: the leader hairline is now `.chart-leader`, painted once for the
  whole chart family.** `scatter` emitted `.scatter-leader` from its own
  stylesheet; the class and its one rule now live in `chart-family.css` so both
  charts draw the same mark. Deck CSS targeting `.scatter-leader` should target
  `.chart-leader`.

- **Fixed: a label description over GitHub's 100-character cap aborted the whole
  label sync.** `feedback` shipped in #2215 with a 111-character description, so
  the Sync labels run on the merge commit created `needs:definition` and then
  died `HTTP 422` on the next entry — leaving the label the intake bar's
  exemption keys on absent from the repo, which is the failure that exemption
  exists to prevent. `tools/sync-labels.js` throws on the first failure, so one
  long description silently strands every label after it in file order. The
  description is shortened, and `sync-labels.test.js` now fails on any entry over
  the cap, a missing name or description, and duplicate names.

- **One image library, `@laticent/lastra`, now reads, cleans, resizes and encodes every picture an export or the Studio handles.** Lattice had four header readers, three EXIF orientation parsers and a metadata scrubber only the Studio could use; each is one function in `docs/src/lib/lastra/` now, with no dependencies, the same in Node, a browser and a worker. Exports keep their bytes on the galleries and on a photo deck of PNG, JPEG, turned JPEG and transparent PNG pictures (a PowerPoint's own run-time stamp aside, which never followed `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`).
- **A turned photo now exports the way the browser paints it.** Only a deck holding one of these pictures exports different bytes (`examples/lastra-image-reading.md` shows the first three):
  - a JPEG whose EXIF block sits after its frame header (every engine turns it) stays upright in the PDF and is sized upright by the `image` layout;
  - a PNG turned by its `eXIf` chunk (Chromium and Firefox turn it) is no longer drawn stretched in the PDF, is sized turned, and is no longer re-encoded squeezed into its stored box;
  - a turned JPEG on an `<img>` that the image policy would not shrink is embedded in the PDF at its own bytes and drawn through its turn, in all eight EXIF orientations, instead of costing a whole-slide picture. Every other turned picture stays in the slide's photo, upright as the browser painted it. The demo deck's PDF grows from 567 KB to 812 KB because its turned pictures now print upright: before, the PDF drew them sideways and stretched at their small stored size;
  - an AVIF photo on an `image` slide is now sized, where it used to fall back to the plain composition;
  - a JPEG whose first EXIF block does not turn it is no longer turned by a later one; a TIFF block with the wrong magic number or an orientation outside 1 to 8 turns nothing; junk or fill bytes between JPEG segments no longer hide a large photo from the export's re-encode.
- **A file whose first bytes only resemble a PNG, JPEG or GIF, and that no browser decodes, is no longer taken for one** by the PDF writer, the CLI's PDF asset reader or the image layout's sizing; they all read the full signature now, as the browsers do.
- **A JPEG the Studio keeps as its original, or the CLI packs into a `.lattice`, keeps only the segments a picture needs.** Before, an APP0 that was not JFIF (a `JFXX` thumbnail, which can carry anything), a JFIF thumbnail and the reserved marker segments F0 to FD survived the cleaning; now the file keeps a minimal JFIF block, the turn, the color profile, the Adobe color transform, the tables and the scans, and decodes to the same pixels.
- **The Studio's cleaned photos keep only the turn a browser applies.** A JPEG with two EXIF blocks, or a PNG with two `eXIf` chunks, could be stored turned by a later block: a photo whose first block says upright and whose second says a quarter turn was stored with only the quarter turn, so it painted turned where the original did not. It now keeps the first block's turn only, so the stored photo paints as the original did.
- **lastra decodes PNG and JPEG itself, in plain JavaScript, with the same answer in Node and every browser** (`@laticent/lastra/decode`, an entry of its own, so the player and the CLI do not carry it). Baseline and progressive JPEG decode exactly as libjpeg-turbo's C code does (including damaged files and progressive files missing their last scans), PNG of every color type and depth decodes exactly, and the inflate is lastra's own, so a damaged PNG gets one verdict everywhere. Hostile files are refused quickly with a typed reason instead of exhausting memory or time. Nothing uses the decoders for exports yet: that step waits on color management and a real-iPhone memory measurement (`engineering/decisions/2026-11-13-image-library.md` §5, slice 5).

- A `.lattice` project file now carries the Library photos the deck names, so it looks the same when opened on another device. "Lattice project" in the Share sheet opens an options step with an "Include photos" switch, on by default. Opening a `.lattice` adds its photos to your Library without overwriting a different photo that already has the same name.

- The website's home page now has a Libraries section with a card for each of the nine libraries, and the footer links to it. The header's Libraries menu now lists LTT and Tavola, which it had left out.

- A workspace backup now carries the one-line caption the chat writes for each Library photo, and a restore brings it back, so a restore no longer makes the chat look at every photo (and pay for it) a second time. Captions in a backup file are cleaned on the way in: invisible and blank-looking characters, look-alike separators and curly quotes are removed, and a long caption is cut on a whole character instead of through the middle of an emoji.
- The chat no longer stores the text "[object Object]" as a photo's caption, and a caption that is empty once cleaned (only zero-width or blank-looking characters, for example) is refused instead of silently clearing the caption the photo already has.

- **Code blocks in the Studio's and the Playground's live preview get their line numbers, copy buttons, diff bands and panel.** The code plugin's stylesheet wrote its rules as `:where(section) pre…`, which the live preview's slide scoping (and Marp's) turned into a selector that matched nothing, so `@code{numbers}`, `copy`, `diff`, `mark`, `wrap` and the panel on a plain slide drew only in the PDF and the exported players. They are now written `section :where(pre)…`, which weighs the same and scopes correctly; the PDF is unchanged.
- **Lines a `_focus: line` slide recedes stay readable in the live preview.** The code plugin's quieter color for them missed the same way and fell back to 24% opacity, which left receded code and its line numbers near blank.

- Importing a plugin clears the editor's `unknown-plugin` warning on a deck that already listed it, and removing a plugin brings it back, without a keystroke. The editor's lint and the Coach read the plugin names through a shared array and re-ran only on an edit, so a phone user who never typed kept a stale warning beside a plugin that Deck settings showed as installed.
- In the docked Library the five section pills fit one row (the last used to wrap alone).
- The notice that asks to run a plugin's code now says the same thing every time. When the code is not approved the button reads **Approve**, whether or not the deck lists the plugin (it used to read "Run it" in one case and "Approve" in the other), and approving is what lets it run. A plugin you approved earlier and then unlisted is offered **Add to deck**, with no second consent wording, since the approval stays with the code. The Library card reads "Not approved yet" and says it will ask when a deck uses the plugin.
- In the Studio preview, a plugin the deck lists but this browser has not approved yet now shows the same drawn placeholder card an unlisted plugin gets, saying "Plugin block · not approved in this browser". It used to show the plain code block with a note under it, so the two states looked unrelated. The block's own text is no longer shown while nothing runs. An inline `@kind{…}` span of an unapproved plugin keeps its code, so a sentence never loses its words in a shared file; the strip above the preview says why it is not drawn.
- The strip that asks you to approve a plugin's code (and the one that offers to add a plugin to the deck) now flashes its background twice and pulses the button's ring when it appears, then settles. It is a short highlight flash, not a loop, and it is off when the device asks for reduced motion.

- The nine `@laticent/*` libraries now point TypeScript at their built `.d.ts` files. Before, a project with strict settings such as `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` got hundreds of type errors inside our packages.
- `@laticent/ltt` reads every `1.x` timing file, as its spec's version rule says, instead of refusing anything but `1.0`. Its JSON Schema is served at its own `$id`, and its hash input follows `JSON.stringify` for sparse arrays and dates.
- `@laticent/segno` refuses a character set built from an emoji (use `lit()`), marks a stack-exhausted parse with `code: 'stack'`, keeps `instanceof SchemaError` working across its entry points, and lints a very wide alternation in milliseconds instead of seconds.
- `@laticent/trama` returns the same layout from its cache as fresh, reports input `solveStar` cannot solve, and loads dagre into its worker only from a script the page actually ran.

- **Fixed: `lint:deck` no longer prints `[undefined]` at the author.** The CLI
  report interpolated a finding's component token unconditionally, so the three
  rules that judge a `_focus` directive rather than a component —
  `focus-spec`, `focus-style`, `focus-steps` — reported
  `⚠ deck.md · slide 1 · focus-spec [undefined]`. The bracket is now omitted
  when a finding carries no token; output for every rule that sets one is
  unchanged.

- **Fixed: a dense `list-steps` strip lost the bottom border, radius and shadow off EVERY card, with no text clipped at all.** The step row is `ol { display:flex; flex:1 }` inside `.cell-stage`, a bounded clipping cell — but a flex item's default `min-height:auto` floors it at its CONTENT height, so the row refused to shrink to the cell and `overflow:clip` sheared the card chrome. `align-items:stretch` gives every card the tallest card's height, so one overstuffed step took all four cards' bottom edges with it. Measured at `size: hd`: a 460.3px row in a 438.2px stage, 22.0px shorn, and the text ended 3px above the clip — pure chrome damage on cards that were not even full, plus a spurious "Content clipped" warning on a slide that had lost nothing. `min-height: 0` on `section.list-steps ol` releases the floor, the same fix `cards-stack` already carries and documents. Landscape hits it first: a 16:9 stage is the shortest one a four-column strip has to fit into, which is why `size: hd` and `size: 4k` both showed it and `standard` (4:3) did not.
- A genuinely over-long step still overflows and still trips the export's "Content clipped" tag — the card frame closes, the excess body spills past it, and the probe fires. Giving the card its own `overflow:clip` would have bought the same clean border by hiding the overflow, so `test/integration/parity/list-steps-card-chrome-clip.test.js` asserts both halves: no card hangs past the clip edge on a dense-but-fitting strip, and an overstuffed one still reads `over:true`. Proved able to fail by mutation — removing the declaration reports "step card 1 hangs 22.05px past the .cell-stage clip edge".
- Zero pixel change across all 21 pages of the `list-steps` gallery and all 58 of `examples/gallery-jargon.md`: the released floor does nothing until the row would otherwise overrun the stage.

- **Live calls start on iPhone.** *Join with audio* failed on iOS with "Couldn't start the microphone": the page told iOS it would only play sound, and iOS then refuses to record. Joining a call now asks iOS for a recording session first. If the microphone still fails, the message names the reason.
- **Read-aloud no longer cuts a call's microphone on iPhone.** Starting read-aloud, a lesson or narration during a live call used to switch iOS back to a play-only session, which ends the microphone. Suono now leaves a recording session in place.

- Live: the "Nobody answered" message now says hotel, office and school wifi often stop two devices on the same wifi from connecting, and suggests keeping the host's screen on or putting one device on mobile data.

- **You can leave or end a live session on a phone.** The session menu (the clock, copy link, leave or end) was missing from the Live sheet on phones; it is now in the sheet's header, as it is in the panel's title bar on wider screens. Leaving or ending a session now asks first.
- **The Live panel uses its room better.** The invite is one line (copy, the link, *Can edit*), and your own call controls (*Join audio*, then Mute and a red *Leave call*) sit on your own row instead of a separate row. On touch screens these buttons are bigger.

- Live: on a phone, the **Your audio**, **Your settings** and per-person popovers now scroll when they are taller than the screen. The Studio drawer blocked touch scrolling in anything outside it, so the lower half (Hearing) was cut off and out of reach.

- Live: on desktop, tapping a switch in Your settings no longer closes the popover. The popover goes into the phone's modal sheet only when there is one, and Your settings no longer opens with the Name field focused (which opened the keyboard on a phone).

- Live: what you share is now kept across a reload, applied when a new session starts in the same tab, and no longer lets Bring everyone leave your hidden slide in presence. A host can no longer move you mid-edit when you have turned off showing when you type, and Your settings can be entered and left from the keyboard. A hidden slide still shows when you are editing.

- Live: a session now keeps the screen awake while it is live, and lets it sleep again when you leave or it ends, because a locked phone suspends the page and drops out of the room.

- **Fixed: a logo wall in the live preview no longer blanks, then jumps, each time you come back
  to it.** The preview measures each mark's shape to size the wall evenly, and it fetched every mark
  again on every visit, drawing the wall as a grid until the fetches landed. It now remembers each
  mark's shape for the session, so a wall seen before draws packed on its first frame with no
  network request. PR previews also cache the playground's content-hashed marks, themes and engine
  modules for good, where they were revalidated on every request.

- **Narrated exports: captions no longer run ahead of an on-device voice.** The Studio's bake
  now measures each clip's own silence before its first word and records it in the clip's
  `leadMs`, beside the MP3 encoder's delay, so the exported player starts the clip at the
  first word and times the caption crawl from there. Kokoro puts 290–390 ms of silence before
  every sentence, so each caption used to light about 0.3 s before the voice spoke it. Gemini's
  clips, which also pass through the bake's encoder, are trimmed the same way.
  Because the player now skips that silence, the pause between two sentences is about 0.3 s
  shorter than before, and a Kokoro-narrated deck plays about 19 s shorter over 62 sentences.
  Present in the Studio still plays each clip from its start, so it keeps the longer pause.

- **Breaking:** the `map` basemap is now drawn with a muted-ink border instead of a canvas-colored hairline. Its legibility came entirely from a fill mixed a fixed 16% away from the canvas, which is a visible grey on white and four sRGB levels away from black — measured, the land read 1.18–1.25:1 on every theme and 1.02:1 on `onyx` and `a11y-achromatopsia` in dark, where only the named countries were visible. Border-against-land now measures 2.86–6.10:1 across five themes and both modes, with no change to the choropleth ramp.

- `mark-brackets`, `mark-threads`, `mark-ticks` and `mark-asterisks` are larger or heavier so they read at viewing size, in light and dark; `mark-seeds` is larger and now paints on dark slides and under a finish (it moved from the background-image slot to `::before`, which `section.dark` and the finish backdrop were hiding). Seeds now also paints on title, closing, topic, divider and print slides, as the other marks do; on a state-stamp slide and on `title`/`closing` with `spectrum` it keeps the old slot path so the stamp and the spectrum rule are untouched. Paint stays at the 28% budget and every mark stays in its peripheral slot.
- `mark-orbit` moves left so it no longer crowds the page number.

- **Fixed: an undo can no longer pull the previous deck's document into the one you are
  editing.** The source editor was not rebuilt when you changed decks, so the swap from one
  deck's text to another's was just another undo step — create a new deck, press ⌘Z once, and
  the deck you came from was sitting in front of you, on its way into the new deck's saved
  source, and it survived a reload. Each deck now gets its own editor, so its undo history
  starts empty. A version restore or an AI apply still keeps its history — undoing those is
  the point.
- **Fixed: "Refine" is offered exactly when you have a selection to refine.** Leaving the
  markdown pane for the rich editor left the button on screen over an editor that no longer
  existed — pressing it answered "Select some text in the editor to refine first." — and
  coming back with your selection restored left it missing. The control now tracks the editor
  that is actually on screen, in both directions.

- **Fixed: a pasted deck no longer loses its front matter to an invisible byte.** A leading
  U+FEFF — what Notepad, PowerShell `>` and Visual Studio put at the head of a file — defeated
  the `^---` front-matter anchor, so the block parsed as a heading and rendered AS the first
  slide, with `theme:`, `size:` and `paginate:` silently ignored. It persisted and survived a
  reload. The deck source is now canonicalized where it enters — on paste, and when a deck is
  read from the store — so a deck saved with one before this landed opens clean rather than
  rendering its own front matter as the first slide.
- **Fixed: the slide rail names the component the engine actually renders.** The rail read a
  `<!-- _class: … -->` comment anywhere on a line, so one stray character after the `-->` — or
  a directive quoted inside a code fence, or prose before it — left the rail calling a slide
  `title` while the preview beside it painted `content`. It also took the FIRST directive on a
  slide where the engine applies the last, so merging two slides by deleting a `---` left the
  rail naming the slide that had just been absorbed. Both are gone because the rail now asks
  the kernel that already answers this question, so it also picks up the container-prefixed
  and running-global directives the old regex never saw.
- **Fixed: "Fix all issues" is offered exactly when something can be fixed.** It was gated on
  the count of unknown components while the button repairs a different set, so it was enabled
  and did nothing on a typo too far from any real name, and disabled over a finding whose Quick
  fix was underlined two inches away.
- **Fixed: undo survives a trip through Compose.** Switching to the rich editor and back
  destroyed the source editor, and its history went with it — ⌘Z did nothing, and nothing said
  why. The editor now carries its history across the switch, and drops it only when an edit
  made in Compose means it would undo the wrong thing.

- The Marp bundle export no longer breaks a deck's front matter when a list is written at its key's own column (`class:` then `- lead` on the next line, which YAML allows). The exporter's reader left the list items behind when it moved the key into the settings block, Marp then rejected the whole front matter, and the bundle lost its title, footer, page numbers and color mode in VS Code and marp-cli.

- An Export-to-Marp bundle whose deck ends inside markup it leaves open (a `<title>`, an `<svg>`, or a
  `<style>`) now still loads the Lattice runtime in marp-cli; before, Mermaid, the charts and every
  runtime-built layout came out bare. The export also says when a deck leaves a `<title>` open, which
  turns the slides after it into text, and the bundle's own comments no longer show up as speaker notes.

- The Export to Marp bundle's README now says that Marp for VS Code shows hidden slides in its preview and in its own Export Slide Deck… command, and that the *Marp:* tasks (and `npm run`) leave them out. It used to say both export routes give the same result.

- **Fixed: the `#1554` WebKit raster spec could not run.** `docs/e2e/math-compare-webkit.spec.ts` still asserted `section.math.compare > h3`, which is now zero — the column labels moved into `.cell-stage` with the rest of the body. The spec is tagged `@webkit-tablet` and runs only from the nightly, so no per-PR gate saw it, and the same change added 37 lines to its docblock explaining that the DOM had moved without moving the four assertions eleven lines below. Repointed, along with a reference to a test file that had been renamed.
- **Fixed: the variant-collision gate was blind to the selector shape the leak took.** It filtered on `startsWith('section.stats')`, which misses `section.form.stats …` — and the one selector it never checked was `section.form.stats … .cell-masthead .masthead-lede`, one of the four rules measured leaking onto a math slide. It also split the selector list on bare commas, fragmenting `:where(a, b)`. Both fixed, the matched count is pinned so a filter that starts matching *fewer* rules fails loudly, and the fix is mutation-proved against the rule that was invisible.
- **`form: off` is now named in the record.** The migration documented that per-slide `no-form` renders math unstyled but not the deck-level `form: off`, which is the first-class documented opt-out and *was* a working configuration for math. Recorded flatly, with the measured context that `stats` and `diagram` degrade the same way under `form: off` — math has joined an already-degraded mode rather than being singled out.
- **Corrected: `compare-code` does not make the same claim math did.** Four places said it was "the last frame making the same weak claim". It carries the same wording in its manifest and not the same substance — it builds a real four-row explicit grid and places its `> h2` at `grid-column: 1 / -1; grid-row: 1`, where math's title was `position: absolute` arithmetic reproducing the masthead's geometry. Math's migration is not a precedent for migrating it, and the canonical doc now says so.
- Four stale docblocks still described math as chrome-exempt (`plugins.js`, `form-default.js`, `masthead.transform.js` ×2, `base.elements.css`).
- The frame-conformance protocol's "flip `strict` only after proving the probe verdict unchanged" precondition was read as "verdicts *proven*" rather than "unchanged", because math's verdicts changed on purpose and the probe itself changed in the same branch. The departure is now recorded at the precondition instead of left for the next migration to inherit as silent precedent.
- **Fixed: un-truncating the variant summaries broke the gallery.** They are injected verbatim into each slide's generated `_footer:`, and at 130–138 characters the footer band clipped six of them — over the overflow ratchet, and a visibly ellipsed footer in both committed gallery PDFs. The 70-character cap was load-bearing and was not established as such before being removed. The summaries are rewritten to fit it as whole sentences, which is what the defect actually was.
- **Fixed: `math compact` at portrait.** The bare/`feature` tall reflow reserved for the KaTeX display's line box with `--sp-sm`, and `compact` shrinks the spacing tokens while the equation's own `em` does not — so the reserve went and the ascent cleared the stage. The reserve is `max(var(--sp-sm), 0.3em)` now, tied to the thing it reserves for. On the sovereign frame that slide clipped 3px of real ink; it now has 29px of clearance on each side.
- **Corrected a claim, and this one was load-bearing:** the record said no reflow could fit `feature`'s over-wide equation under the Fit Spine's no-scale axiom. That is false — a red team measured it fitting at 0.9em (42.28px), which is *larger* than the 37.41px the same equation is set at on a 16:9 slide. What is true is narrower: bare `math` and `feature` share one rule and bare's hero fits at the current 2.4em with 29px of clearance, so a single scale cannot serve both. The lever that serves both is breaking the expression across lines (~35%, measured) plus re-testing the scale-up — owner-ruled and tracked in #2136.
- **The family-reflow gate would have certified a reflow keyed to the wrong family.** It accepted any `[data-family]` selector, including `[data-family="wide"]` — the 16:9 default, where nothing needs to give. It now requires `tall`, `strip` or `square`, mutation-proved by re-keying a live rule to `wide`.

- A `math` slide no longer loses its adaptive reflow in a portrait, story or mobile box. The rules that collapse the equation and its legend into one column were scoped to direct children of the `<section>`; moving the body into the Form frame's stage cell made every one of them inert, and the legend ran 64px off a 1080px slide. Measured, and now covered by a gate that fails when a migrated variant has no Form-arm reflow and has not declared why it needs none.
- The hero equation in a tall box renders at 2.4em rather than 2.7em. At `size: story` the reference equation was 1029px wide against a 972px box — 57px of it clipped. That was true before this change too and had simply never been visible: math had no clip cell, so the overflow watcher never looked at it. Moving math into the shared frame is what surfaced it.

- Typing on a slide that contains math no longer re-typesets equations that did not change. The engine now memoizes KaTeX by expression. Measured in the real Studio, on one math slide: a keystroke in prose costs **0** `renderToString` calls where it cost **10**, a 13-character burst costs **0** where it cost 80-110 (a range, not a point: how many keystrokes the debounce coalesces moves run to run), and the slide's cold paint costs **5** where it cost **10** — the memo also collapses an expression repeated within a slide. Typing a genuinely new expression still costs exactly **1**, so the memo keys rather than suppresses.
- `npm run bench` gains a `math` render row and a new **edit tier** that reports what an author pays per keystroke, for a single character and for a 12-character burst. The burst case was measured nowhere before — every existing typing harness inserts a 700 ms settle between keys, which is precisely the case the frame scheduler already handles. The tier gates on typeset **counts** rather than wall clock, so it is exact on every machine. Note the bench measures the WHOLE-DECK route (90 typesets per keystroke, now 0); the Studio renders one slide, so the author-facing figure is the per-slide one above.
- **New:** `docs/e2e/math-typeset-edit-cost.spec.ts` counts typesets from inside the real Studio page rather than from a Node harness, by wrapping the KaTeX module the provider registers. It runs in the nightly. Every run identifies which bundle it measured from a repeated expression in the deck — a stale preview server served the memoized build to three consecutive "before" runs and reported the memo's `0` for unmemoized code, and that fingerprint is what caught it.

- `matrix-grid` holds its column geometry still while a deck renders, on `wide` decks. The table was `table-layout: auto`, so every column width was re-solved from cell text — and the web font landing after first paint re-laid the whole grid one frame later. Measured live in the Studio, the five columns went 258.2/165.7/175.5/216.4/304.2 to 248.7/176.9/178.9/218.9/296.6 at design scale, sliding every cell up to 11px sideways with nothing overflowing for a fit gate to report. The table is now `table-layout: fixed` there, which also makes the reach axis read as equal steps instead of sizing each column to whichever label happened to be longest.
- `square`, `tall` and `strip` keep the old `auto` behavior and render byte-identically. `--canvas-scale` raises the type as the box narrows, so the content stops fitting inside equal columns — forcing `fixed` there costs `Distinguished` 25.2px at square and 44.5px under `mode: sketch` — and `--fs-meta` is already the floor of the type scale. The font-swap re-solve remains live on those three families.

- **`npm run merge:order` no longer aborts on one PR it cannot measure.** A PR git cannot size or check (no merge base in a shallow clone, a deleted branch) is listed under `unmeasured` with git's reason and left out; the rest are still ordered, and the run exits 1 instead of 3. Found on the merge desk's first live run.

- Mermaid `click` directives now work in the live previews that take a pointer: the Playground, and the VS Code Markdown preview of an Export-to-Marp bundle. A flowchart or class diagram's `click A "url" "tooltip"` keeps its tooltip, and a gantt chart's `click task href "url"` keeps its link, when the preview reuses a diagram it already drew: after a keystroke outside the diagram, and every time VS Code's built-in Mermaid extension removes and the runtime redraws it. VS Code's extension removes the diagrams on every edit, so until now the tooltip and the gantt links stopped working there at the first edit.
- With two gantt charts on slides of the same palette, the first chart's `click` links now work on the first render too. The charts share Mermaid's gantt state, and the second chart's parse erased the first chart's links before the runtime bound them.

- The exported file now draws every Mermaid fence the engine parses, the same rule the live preview follows. A ` ```mermaid ` block inside an HTML block (such as a `<div>`) or inside a `$$` math block is no longer drawn in the PDF, PNG, PPTX or HTML export, because the engine reads it as HTML or math and the preview never drew it; the export used to draw it anyway, often clipped. The CLI now warns, naming the line, when a deck holds a Mermaid block inside an HTML block; after a `<div>`-style tag a blank line draws it, and inside a `<pre>`, `<script>`, `<style>` or `<textarea>` block it has to move out. A closed Mermaid block whose body contains a line of three asterisks is now drawn instead of exported as source. Two shapes still draw in the preview but not in the export: an info string that only starts with `mermaid` (` ```mermaid-x `) and a raw `<pre><code class="language-mermaid">` written as HTML.

- **Fixed: hand-drawn (`mode: sketch`) diagrams rendered a different picture on every
  render.** Mermaid's `look: handDrawn` paints through rough.js, whose jitter is seeded
  from `handDrawnSeed` — and Mermaid's default of `0` means "no seed, use
  `Math.random()`". So the same deck, unchanged, exported two different SVGs on two
  consecutive runs. Measured on `examples/sketch.md`: 32 of 161 SVG lines differed
  between back-to-back renders of the same commit, every one a jittered path.
- The seed is now pinned in the shared init config, so the CLI export and the live
  preview both draw the same hand. **A sketch-mode diagram now changes only when the
  diagram changes** — which is also what makes its committed golden meaningful, since a
  re-render previously rewrote the bytes whether or not anything moved.
- **Sketch-mode goldens move once in this change** and are stable from then on. Classic
  decks are byte-identical: the seed is emitted only alongside `look: handDrawn`, so a
  deck that never asked for the hand-drawn look sends the same directive it always did.

- A diagram slide's narration now speaks exactly the Mermaid diagram the slide shows: the narrator reads the same fences the export draws, as the engine parses them, so a block the engine reads as HTML, math or code is never narrated as a diagram.

- A Mermaid pie's legend and wedge percentages are larger: 20px and 22px in the diagram's own units, up from 13px and 14px. On a diagram slide with a callout the legend now draws near 12px instead of 8px, in Lattice and in the Marp bundle. Demo: `examples/mermaid-pie-legibility.md`.

- **Fixed: every node in a mindmap branch now takes that branch's color, whatever its shape.**
  The position cycle that colors sankey, flowchart, state and ER nodes also caught mindmap
  `[square]` and `(rounded)` nodes and painted them by their order in the markup. Circle,
  bang and cloud nodes lost to the flowchart default and painted blue. That cycle
  now skips mindmap, and the per-branch rule outranks the flowchart default for every shape,
  including the hand-drawn shapes under `mode: sketch`.
- **Fixed: a mindmap with more than five branches keeps coloring its branches.** Node fills
  ran through `section-4` only, so the sixth branch fell back to blue. They now follow every
  branch Mermaid numbers (eleven, after which it wraps back to the first), on the same map as
  the branch lines.
- **Fixed: a mindmap branch line now matches its boxes.** Each line took the category's
  `--cat-N-mark`, which is not the fill's hue (a sand branch drew a maroon line), and on a
  dark slide it washed out to near-white. The line now keeps its branch fill's hue: darker
  than the boxes on a light slide, lighter on a dark one.
- **Fixed: the mindmap root no longer blends into the first branch.** The root takes the
  deck accent with its paired `--on-accent` ink instead of `--cat-1`, the first branch's
  color.
