- Studio: the chat model is now one stored selection that survives a reload. The model you pick (cloud, a direct key, or on-device) answers every turn; if it cannot answer yet, the chat says why (still opening, needs a key, not loaded) instead of quietly using another model.
- Studio: a chat turn runs on one model from start to finish, and the reply, its cost and the model chip name the model that actually answered, even if you switch models mid-reply.
- Studio: another open tab follows a model change made in this one.
- Studio: the read-aloud voice is its own stored selection, independent of the chat model. Present reads in the voice you chose, on every read and after a reload: on-device Kokoro is no longer picked for you on desktop, and a cloud voice whose key is still opening waits for it instead of switching voices.
- Studio: Workspace → AI → Read-aloud voice no longer changes when you look at the chat's On-device tab. Its Cloud / On-device switch chooses the voice engine, and a badge shows whether it is ready.
- Studio: a Gemini API key now drives read-aloud too. Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS (the default) and Flash TTS speak through your own Gemini key and never bill OpenRouter; the Studio recommends the newest Flash-Lite or Flash TTS your key lists.
- Studio: each provider's recommended models are listed first, matched against the provider's live model list, so a retired model drops out on its own and a new release in the same family shows up.
- Studio: Workspace → AI shows each model as a card. Each model shows as a card with its name, where it runs, and whether it is ready; Change opens the choices in place, and choosing one makes it active at once. A missing key says "Add a key" right on the card. On a phone the readiness badge sits under the model's name, so the name is not cut short.
- Studio: Spend and standing instructions follow the chat model you selected, not the tab you happen to be looking at. Narration settings (pace, fetch ahead, audio quality, keep on device, cheapest voice) moved from General to Voice model → More narration settings.
- Studio: Workspace → AI no longer jumps when it opens: the loading frame has the real layout, and readiness changes in place.
- Studio: a selected on-device chat model whose files are already in this browser loads by itself after a reload, with its progress shown; one that is not downloaded says so and offers to load it, and never downloads without asking.
- Studio: the chat's model chip now names the model that will answer, on-device included, with an icon for where it runs, and links to "Models & keys…". Without a key it says "Add a key or choose on-device". Picking a model in the chip changes the same global chat model as Workspace → AI, and the chip reaches every source: each provider you hold a key for, and the on-device models.
- Present: the voice button names the voice that is speaking ("Heart · on-device", "Eve · OpenRouter") instead of a fixed "Aria", and shows "Loading voice… n%" while your selected voice loads, then starts reading.
- Studio: one model-name format everywhere a model is named (Workspace, the chip, the pickers, Present).
- Studio: when the browser's key store could not be reached, the Studio could spin re-reading the key and stop responding. A key that cannot be opened yet now reads "still opening" and is retried at most once a second.
- Studio: a model picked while the browser's storage is full now takes effect on the page instead of silently keeping the old one, and a selection written by a newer version of the Studio in another tab is left alone rather than reset. A key that could not be opened because the browser's key store was briefly unreachable now opens by itself once the store recovers.
- Studio: when a provider retires the voice model you chose, read-aloud turns off and tells you once where to pick another, instead of failing on every sentence; the voice card shows "Model retired". No other voice speaks in its place.
- Studio: Workspace › AI accepts Google's newer Gemini API keys (they start with "AQ."), not only the classic "AIza…" ones.
- Studio: the Gemini voice picker offers Gemini's 30 named voices (Achernar, Kore, Puck, …), read live from Google, instead of a list of raw voice ids.
- Studio: a direct provider's model list (Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI) opens on its recommended models, newest first, with All and search one step away, so the list stays short and clear; and the chat card and chip name the model that will answer ("Gemini 3.8 Flash"), not just the provider.
- Studio: an account that is out of credits or quota is named as that, for every provider and for read-aloud, with where to add billing. It used to read as a rejected key (Gemini 403), as "the model could not take this request" (Anthropic's 400 "credit balance is too low"), or not at all for read-aloud; and a region refusal no longer reads as a retired model.
- Studio: signing in to OpenRouter no longer shows "Key rejected" for the first minute or two. OpenRouter takes that long to start accepting a key a sign-in just made; the Studio now says it is activating the key, checks again every 15 seconds, and clears the note as soon as the key works. A key still refused after three minutes is marked rejected as before.

- The Studio's loading animations no longer stall on large, high-resolution screens. The "no slide yet" cloud (Nacre) drops the blur filter that Chromium re-ran on every frame and adds a faint grain against color banding, and the placeholder painted over a still-loading picture (the Underpainting) slides its brushwork instead of repainting it. Measured in the Studio at 4K: the cloud 3.5 → 18.3 fps and the picture placeholder 34.7 → 58.7 fps in a software-rendered browser; the cloud is tuned to match its old brightness, and the picture placeholder looks the same as before.

- **Fixed: an abbreviation's period no longer ends a caption cue.** `Dr. Chen approved
  it.` was segmented as two cues, so the voice said "Doctor." — full stop, real silence —
  and then "Chen approved it." A cue is one caption line, one re-anchor unit and one
  synthesized TTS clip, so each spurious break cost a line, a round-trip and an inserted
  pause, and mispriced the words either side of it. `splitSentences` now folds a break
  back when the word before it is an abbreviation or the fragment after it starts with
  punctuation that cannot open a sentence. Measured on `examples/reflow-legal.md`: 72 cues
  → 61, with `Cal. Civ. Code §1798.140(o)`, `15 U.S.C. §6501` and `16 C.F.R. Part 312`
  each now one cue instead of three.
- **Fixed: a sentence ending inside a closing quote now ends its cue.** `Setup was "3–4
  weeks." It took 11.` was one run-on clip, because the terminator sat behind the quote.
- **Removed: `voice-model.js`'s local `splitSentences`.** It was a byte-identical copy of
  Cadenza's kept for a caller that no longer exists — read-aloud segments from
  `track.cues` — and its only importers were its own two tests. Segmentation now has one
  implementation rather than two pinned together.
- **Fixed: a two-period range separator no longer ends a cue.** `gantt` spells a span
  `2026 Q1 .. 2026 Q4`, which broke into two cues on nine shipped decks. Three periods
  are unchanged — an authored ellipsis can genuinely end a sentence.

- **Studio:** narration audio kept in memory is now limited to 24 MB, not only 200 clips, and a Gemini clip is kept as a `Blob` the browser can store outside the page. The 200-clip limit was sized for MP3: Gemini voices answer uncompressed audio, about ten times larger. This is a safety limit, not the fix for the iPhone reload during narrated Present, which is still open.

- **The slide's closing beat is now narrated.** A trailing `> …` key insight or below-note is lifted into a `.cell-coda` cell that sits OUTSIDE `.cell-stage`, and every body walker in the speech projection is stage-scoped — so the most prominent editorial line on the slide was silent in captions and read-aloud. It is now spoken last, as its own paragraph beat. Over `examples/` + `test/integration/baseline-decks/`, 53 of 161 decks carry at least one blockquote; 284 of 3402 rendered slides gain narration text.
- Author emphasis now buys time: a `**bold**` phrase or a slide's closing quote holds a beat after the passage ends, once per passage rather than once per sentence. A closing quote's beat lands in the exported webpage player, which holds the gap after every line including the last; a `.vtt` sidecar cannot represent a pause after its final line and so does not show it.

- All four narration producers resolve emphasis through one shared rule: the CLI captions sidecar, the Studio's "Captions (.vtt)" download, the exported player's baked track, and live Present. Each applies spans only where the resolved narration is still the text they were measured against, so a beat cannot land mid-phrase after a caption override or a chart substitution.

- Documented two narration gotchas that cost a full investigation to find: `projectDeckToSpeech` is one stage of the narration pipeline, not the narration (both producers run `narrateChart` on top of it, so timing the projection alone reports a diagram slide at 4.3 s where the shipped caption runs 40.6 s), and per-slide dwell in Present is that narration playing to the end plus the arrival beat — not a stall, a synthesis timeout, or a starved audio buffer.

- **Fixed: an authored line break in a state-chart event label no longer reads as markup.**
  `examples/state-chart-branching.md` authors `needs<br/>second review`, which the component
  documents and draws as a break; the caption carried the markup, so the voice said it. Both
  documented forms — an HTML `<br>`/`<br/>` and a literal `\n` — now read as a space, because
  that break is there to fit the rank gap rather than to separate two phrases. A Mermaid node
  label keeps its pause, where a break usually does separate two things.

- **Fixed: one broken caption track no longer silently zeroes every later slide.** The
  deck-level `.vtt` accumulates `offset += track.durationMs`, so a single non-finite duration
  poisoned the running sum and every subsequent slide serialized as
  `00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:00.000` — a perfectly valid WebVTT file in which every caption after
  the bad one fires at time zero, with nothing anywhere saying so. Measured on an unguarded
  three-slide deck. Cadenza's `validateTrack` now runs at the serializer, so no `.vtt` this
  pipeline writes can carry a poisoned timeline, and the CLI names the slide it dropped and
  why. A sound deck's sidecars are byte-identical to before.
- **Added: the Studio's webpage-export panel warns when the chosen voice does not speak the
  deck's language.** Neither speech engine takes a language parameter, so for both model rungs
  the voice IS the language — and a `lang: es` deck read by an English voice was silent about
  it. `voiceLanguageMismatch()` shipped as the answer and had no caller; it has one now, on
  the surface where the voice is baked into every copy the recipient opens.

- **CI:** the merge queue's `unit (node 24)` job no longer hangs in `npm ci` after the install has finished. The cause was a deadlock in node 24's `process.exit()` (nodejs/node#64274): a background compile waited for a garbage collection that the exiting main thread never ran. The job now runs npm itself with V8's background tasks off (`--single-threaded`).

- In an editable PowerPoint, icons, check marks and cards with uneven corners or a wrapped accent rule draw in iPhone Preview and macOS Quick Look: Apple's Office importer drops any custom shape inside a group (an icon became a speck, a card lost its fill and border), so a card that holds one is now written as loose shapes in the same paint order. Such a card no longer moves as one unit in PowerPoint; cards made only of plain shapes stay grouped.

- A one-line text box in an editable PowerPoint states 100% line spacing, placed to match, instead of the paragraph's multiple: apps disagree about where a multiple puts the first line (Google Slides drew it about 0.3 em higher than PowerPoint), which left inline icons looking low beside their words.

- In an editable PowerPoint or ODP, a line is split into one text box per piece where an inline icon, spark or pill takes room in it, instead of holding that room with stretched character spacing, which iPhone Preview honored only in part (a word slid under the icon). Only the line the icon sits in is cut; the rest of the paragraph stays one box. Headings (so the slide's title stays whole), right-to-left, justified and indented text, math, and gaps made only of spaces are never split.

- **Studio:** the export capture frame and the webpage export's prune frame now set their document before they join the page (`writeSrcdoc`). Firefox gives a frame the site's offline worker only in that order. Today's exports already worked offline on Firefox, because the write followed the append with no pause between them; the new order no longer depends on that timing. Online exports are unchanged.

- Dark panels (`title`, `divider`, `closing`, every `split-*` rail) had three elements
  inked from the wrong tier of the on-dark ramps: the `closing` eyebrow drew from
  `--on-dark-ghost`, documented decorative chrome (2.49:1 on indaco, 2.67–2.91:1
  elsewhere) while its sibling bookends already used `--on-dark-secondary`;
  `split-panel metric`'s row rule and heading hairline drew from
  `--on-dark-watermark`, the near-invisible backdrop tier (1.40:1, and 1.27–1.46:1
  elsewhere, against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1); and `split-panel watermark`'s eyebrow and
  `h5` drew from `--on-accent-secondary`, a 70% derivation that spends the AA margin
  each palette curates into `--on-accent` (measured on all 14, sub-AA on **seven** —
  mustard 3.34:1 through carta 4.40:1; the seven that pass do so on their own accent's
  headroom, not because the accent is dark — carbone clears 5.85:1 on a bright lime).
  The first two were sub-threshold in **all 14 palettes**. All three now name the rung
  that matches their job.
- **`--on-dark-secondary` 68% → 76% white.** This is the whole fix for the reported
  defect: at 68% the eyebrow/subtitle/dek tier measured 6.08:1 on indaco — the only
  palette below AAA on that tier, because indaco's `--surface-inverse` (`#003D66`) is
  the lightest panel in the repo and the ramp is palette-blind. At 76% the worst case
  across all 19 palettes is **7.17:1**.
- **`--on-dark-ghost` 32% → 42% white**, so the rule/divider rung clears 3:1 on every
  palette's panel — at 32% it cleared it on **none** (2.49–2.90:1). `cuoio`, the one
  palette that overrides this ramp, tracks the lift (30% → 40%, 3.82:1) so its own
  value clears the same floor on the engine render path.
- `tools/check-slide-contrast.js` was blind to most of the above, and to more besides.
  It parsed only `rgb()`/`rgba()` while Chromium serializes `color-mix(in srgb, …)` as
  `color(srgb …)`, silently dropping **18 of 69 text runs (26%)** on a bookend probe.
  It also **never read SVG `fill`** — chart text is painted by `fill`, not `color`, so
  every chart label in the repo was scored against an inherited value that is not what
  renders (one word-cloud word: reported 11.96:1, actual 1.20:1). Both fixed, plus a
  1×1-canvas fallback for any color space (`oklab()` was dropping live `kanban` runs),
  a pseudo-element's own background, and sibling underlays resolved by geometry.
  Non-rendering SVG `<desc>`/`<title>`/`<metadata>` are excluded, and the
  **WCAG-exempt decorative tier** (`--text-muted`, `--border`) is now reported in its
  own bucket rather than padding the failure count — on one gallery that separated 89
  reported failures into 4 real and 84 exempt.
- `tools/contrast-audit.js` now **reads** the on-dark alphas from `base.tokens.css`
  instead of keeping a copy that could go stale, and honors the long-documented but
  never-read `minRatio` — which admits the first non-text pair, `--on-dark-ghost` vs
  `--surface-inverse` at 3:1.

- The exported HTML player no longer cuts the slide's edge off at every corner (seen in a phone's file preview, which runs the player without its script), and no longer rounds the slides of a square deck in its Read·Slides and Present views. Every surface that shows a slide — the player, the Playground, the Studio (editor preview, Present, thumbnails, pickers, Fabricate) and the docs site — now follows the deck's own `corners:` setting instead of drawing a corner of its own.
- The slide's 1px edge is now drawn by the engine, in the deck's own border color, above the slide's content and inside its corner, so no host can clip it and no full-bleed layout can cover it. It yields to the spectrum bar on whichever side the bar sits. It appears only where a slide is shown on a page; PDF, PNG and PPTX exports are unchanged.
- A title's text no longer shifts a beat after the exported player opens: the player's embedded fonts are laid out from the first paint. In the Studio, fonts that arrive after the preview's 1.5s wait now fade in rather than making the text jump.

- `npm run overflow:check` can now tell a deck that is clean from one nobody swept. The
  baseline lists only the decks that clip, so a deck missing from it read as clean —
  including seven component galleries authored after the last full bless, which carried
  a floor of zero from the day they landed. The baseline records how many decks its
  blessing run covered, and the check says so when today's corpus is larger.

- **Fixed: a clip cell that lays its children out in COLUMNS no longer reports phantom overflow.** `probeSectionOverflow` measures a possibly-squeezed child against "the next flowed sibling's top", which assumes the children stack. In a two-track grid or a flex row the next sibling sits *beside*, so the subtraction returns the child's own height. Measured on `team-profile sides`, where a genuinely squeezed 9-person roster hiding 261px was reported as 699px — 2.7× the truth, and that number feeds autosplit — and on a migrated `math matrix` slide, where 2px of phantom inner overflow from KaTeX's `vlist` struts became a 265px reading and a "Content clipped" badge with nothing clipped.
- The limit is now taken only from a sibling that **overlaps this child horizontally and starts below it**; the scan continues past one that does not, rather than stopping at it. Both halves were wrong alone, and both were measured: stopping at the first sibling silently missed 170px of overprint onto a later same-column box, and scanning without the horizontal test reached a `citation-card margin` list 640px to the right and took its top as a limit.
- Tolerances are in layout px (`K`-scaled) rather than visual px. Unscaled, the same slide answered `over: true` at scale 1 and `over: false` at scale 1.5, contradicting the scale-independence the probe asserts elsewhere.
- Blast radius measured across 232 rendered slides from nine galleries: exactly one verdict changes, the `math matrix` false positive. `citation-card`, `inventory`, `redline`, `split-panel` and `team-profile` all build multi-column clip cells and none moves.

- A theme rule that leads with `:where(section…)` now applies in the Studio and Playground preview. `:where(section.finish) .panel` used to match nothing there while the exported deck applied it, so the preview and the export disagreed. The preview now writes the slide arm and keeps the descendant arm it always had, so a raw `<section>` nested in a slide still matches too. Measured on a fixture theme: a single-arm rule went from `outline-width` 0px to 3px (the export gives 3px) and a multi-arm rule from 0px to 4px (export 4px); a rule that hits a nested raw section stays at 9px. It applies only when every arm is one compound that starts with `section`; an arm with a combinator inside it (`:where(section .wrap) .d`), a mixed list such as `:where(section.a, .b)`, and `:where(:root)` stay as before. The packed and flat sheets for all 33 shipped themes are byte-identical before and after, because no shipped selector uses the shape.

- **Fixed: the Studio's Markdown and Marp exports keep a deck's saved components.**
  The Markdown export passed an empty component list and the Marp bundle passed
  none, so a slide built from a saved component arrived unstyled on the
  recipient's machine. Both exports now embed the CSS of every saved component
  the deck uses.
- **Fixed: a Marp bundle of a deck in a saved theme ships that theme.** The
  bundler looked for the theme among the site's shipped themes, found nothing,
  and fell back to `indaco` without a word. It now writes the saved theme's own
  CSS (plus any shipped parent it extends). A theme it can't find fails the
  export with the theme's name instead of substituting another one.
- **Fixed: a saved theme or component can no longer take a shipped name.** A
  theme saved as `indaco` re-skinned every deck saying `theme: indaco`, and a
  component saved as `kpi` restyled shipped `kpi` slides. A clash now saves as
  `<name>-custom`, with its `@theme` directive or its selectors and skeleton
  rewritten to match, and Fabricate and Library import say so. A record saved
  under a shipped name before this change no longer overrides the shipped item.
- **Fixed: Library import refuses an oversized asset `.zip`.** It had no size
  caps, so a small archive that declared gigabytes of content could take the tab
  down. It now applies the same caps `.lattice` import does: 25 MB on disk, 64 MB
  inflated, and at most 2,000 entries.

- **Fixed: the `halo` and `nimbus` finishes print their accent again.** On the
  export face (PDF and the Studio's image exports), halo's vignette and three of
  nimbus's four blooms ended on the solid slide color, so each painted the canvas
  over the layers beneath it and the slide printed blank white with a gray rim. Only
  the bottom layer now ends on the solid canvas; every layer above it ends on the
  canvas color at zero opacity. Finishes made in the Studio's Finish faculty had the
  same defect in their mesh and vignette layers and get the same fix.

- **Fixed: opening a `.lattice` project never changes your saved themes, components or
  finishes.** An asset in the file that differs from one you saved is added under a new
  name (`brand-2`), and the deck you opened uses it; your other decks keep yours.
- **Fixed: a saved or installed component can't take a slide class Lattice uses**, such as
  `finish`, `print` or `dark`. It saves or installs as `<name>-custom`.
- **Fixed: the CLI checks installed packages every time it renders**, not only at
  `lattice packages add`, so a package copied into the store by hand is checked too. A
  deck naming a component nobody has now gets a warning instead of unstyled slides.
- **Fixed: a finish saved before the halo/nimbus print fix gets the fix** without being
  saved again.

- **Restoring a backup can no longer overwrite a saved theme with a scene.** A scene the Studio could not read rides in a backup with the record id it was stored under, and the restore saved it under that id, so a hand-edited row carrying one of your themes' ids replaced that theme, with no version history to recover it from. The restore now files an unreadable scene by its name, among scenes only: it updates an unreadable scene of that name, and leaves a working scene of that name alone.

- `lint:deck` no longer counts a third pane when a pane's eyebrow pill uses double backticks
  (`` ``a`b`` ``) above its `### title`. The linter now reads a pill the way CommonMark does, so it
  agrees with the engine, and its `pane-title` suggestion sees the pill too.
- `lint:deck` counts the slide's eyebrow, subtitle, Key Insight and note against a pane's budget, as
  the engine does when it sizes the pane. A stacked table that the slide's chrome leaves room for one
  row now gets `pane-overflow`. Before this, the export clipped its second row while the linter
  called the slide clean.
- Compose no longer moves a slide's `<!-- _pane: … -->` markers to the top of the slide. Before
  this, one keystroke on a pane slide with markers wrote both markers above the `##`, and the
  slide lost its panes.

- A slide built from panes (`rows`, `columns`, any host of two components) no longer prints a page number under each pane. Each pane rendered its own footer with a page number (even with `paginate: false`); the host slide owns the footer and the one page number. Clears the `rows` stress slide, `examples/panes.md` and `examples/panes-sketch.md`, which clipped because of those footers.

- The Studio preview follows a panes slide the engine splits into one slide per pane (every panes slide on a square, portrait, story or mobile deck). The slide after the split now shows with the page number the PDF gives it, instead of falling back to the slide alone numbered 1 of 1. The split slide shows the page whose pane holds the caret, and ‹ › step through both pages. Present and the narration bake keep their projected narration through a split.
- Author and package CSS reaches a pane: a rule written for a component (`section.my-card li { … }`) now styles a pane of that component as it styles its slide, for installed packages, Studio saved components and finishes, and `<style>` blocks in the deck. A component used only in a pane now ships its CSS with the deck.
- A table pane in a `mode: sketch` deck is hand-inked like a table slide. It used to lose its frame and row rules entirely once the slide's heading was inked.

- **Rendering a deck twice now produces byte-identical PDFs.** The exported PDF
  carried the wall clock in `/CreationDate` and `/ModDate`, so a re-render with
  no visual change still wrote a whole new file — four differing bytes in 1.5 MB
  was enough for git to store a fresh copy of every golden a cross-cutting CSS
  change touched. Both timestamps are now pinned, and
  `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` overrides the pinned instant if you want a real date.
  Covers the vector path, `--raster`/`--paper`, and the `--notes` / `--present` /
  `--embed-source` post-passes.

- **Fixed: an image the export cannot fetch no longer costs you the whole file.**
  One unreachable path — a `logo:` written relative to the deck file, which the CLI
  resolves and the web cannot — used to fail the PDF, the PowerPoint and the image
  set outright, with no artifact at all. The picture is now left out, the file
  lands, and the toast names the path that is missing. That covers the full-bleed
  `![bg](…)` panel too, which is a CSS background rather than an `<img>` and used to
  vanish from an export with nothing said anywhere.

- **Studio PDF:** an inline pill no longer draws over the end of the caption before it (kpi `OPS` / `GAP` pills, in light and dark). The Studio's camera re-lays a slide out with every font size rounded down, so a pill placed by the text flow was photographed early while its caption was drawn in place. The shared PDF writer now draws such a chip's fill and border as vectors at the live position and leaves it out of the photo, in the Studio and the CLI alike. In CLI PDFs a pill looks the same, with a sharper edge; a chip under a link underline, a shadow or anything painted over it stays in the photo as before.

- Bullets and numbers are back in the vector PDF. The PDF writer draws every word as real text and photographs the rest of the slide with those words hidden. A list marker took the same hidden fill as its item's words, so any list item whose words the writer drew lost its bullet or number in the command-line PDF, and numbered items lost their numbers in the Studio's PDF; an item the writer left in the photo, such as one with a symbol the deck's fonts lack, kept its marker. The writer now hides only the item's words and leaves its marker in the photo, light and dark, without moving anything a deck's own CSS lays out (`test/integration/export/pdf-list-markers.test.js`, `docs/e2e/studio-pdf-list-markers.spec.ts`).

- The CLI and Studio PDF writer draws the slide's own top edge, the spectrum bar on a light slide and the 1 px gradient hairline on a dark one, as a vector instead of leaving it in the background photo. On a 4K slide, whose photo is downsampled to 2560 px, the dark hairline came out 86 color levels off Chrome's print; it is now within 1, and the light slide's 12 px bar is crisp to its last row.
- `split-panel` and `split-compare` read the same slots on both render paths for five raw-HTML shapes that used to split them: a stray `</p>`, a paragraph inside a table before its rows, `<a><ul>…</a></ul>`, a paragraph after a `### label` (now the right zone on both paths), and a list whose `</li>` or `</ul>` is omitted. Decks written in Markdown render byte-identical engine HTML.

- **Fixed: a thin colored line keeps its color in an exported PDF.** The PDF writer photographs
  each slide's background and stored that photo as JPEG, which blurred a 1 px line on a dark
  slide (the accent rule along its top edge) into a duller color and bled it into the row below.
  The photo is now PNG on a plain slide background, and on a busier one (a photograph, a
  finish's grain) whichever of PNG and JPEG is smaller. This applies to `lattice deck.md out.pdf` and the Studio's Export to PDF. A
  plain 16:9 deck's PDF from the CLI is usually smaller than before: re-rendered, the committed demo
  decks' PDFs came out 16% smaller in total and the component galleries' 25%. CLI export takes about 5-10% longer on a 16:9 deck; a 20-slide Studio export
  about 1.3 s longer. A 4K deck's photo is unchanged for now.

- **Fixed: an unclosed `<!--` no longer freezes the render or the linter.** A pasted
  deck holding many HTML comment openers with no `-->` made several comment readers
  rescan to the end of the text from every opener. One 250 KB line of `<!--` took 148 s
  to render and 89 s to lint, and 280 KB of `a <!--` lines took 17 s to render. Both run
  on the Studio's main thread, and the Playground's layout gate did the same to a
  model-written skeleton. The readers now find each closer once and reuse it, and the
  markdown-it guard decides exactly whether upstream's comment pattern can close: those
  inputs take 0.1–0.4 s, and every example deck renders byte-identical.
- **Fixed: a cold render is about 16% faster again.** The render tier had drifted
  25–50% over its blessed baseline since 2026-09-08. Two costs were new: the section
  walker re-scanned the same document on every pass, and the CSS comment walk stepped
  through the 2.3 MB bundle one character at a time. The walker now remembers its
  answer for the last few documents, and the CSS walk jumps between the characters
  that matter.
- **Fixed: reopening Add slide no longer grows memory on Safari and iPad.** Every reopen
  used to build the gallery's preview thumbnails as fresh documents, and WebKit never gives
  those back: about 45 MB per reopen. Add slide now stays loaded after its first open and is
  only hidden when you close it, so a reopen builds none, and its previews scroll with the
  gallery exactly as before.

- Playground: a returning visitor whose saved split puts the preview under its 300px minimum no longer sees the editor pane jump narrower as the page loads (907px, then 893px at a 1194px window). The pre-paint clamp now also holds the space reserved for the preview pane before it has loaded.

- The Coach's photo-contrast warning now appears in Firefox. Firefox drew nothing when the Studio sampled part of an SVG photo, so the check never spoke there.
- On a slide that splits on its headings, the photo check reads the part you are on, on a phone too, and its fix writes the card ink into that part's own class. A slide that only inherits a running `class:` keeps it when the fix is written; before, the ink replaced the slide's layout.
- The slide strip and the map name a slide by the class the engine draws it with, including a running `class:` it inherits from an earlier slide; such a slide used to read `text`.

- The Studio no longer keeps a copy of every phone-photo slide in memory for its class editor. That memory was capped by the
  number of slides, not their size, so a deck of three phone photos kept about 15 MB and a long editing session could keep
  far more; it now keeps none of a slide past a megabyte, and reads such a slide afresh, which costs the same.
- The Studio no longer freezes when a very large piece of text is typed into the deck source rather than pasted: an IME
  commit, dictation, or a drop the browser turns into text. The browser used to lay all of it out before the editor read
  it, about 12 s for a deck of three phone photos in Chrome; the editor now applies it in one step, as it does a paste.

- The Library's "Add photo" dialog no longer moves when its file sizes finish measuring. The size bars and the summary line now keep their space from the first frame, so the dialog keeps its height and the "Add photo" button stays where it was. Before, the dialog grew by up to 32 px as the numbers came in, and a click or tap aimed at the button as they landed could hit the space above it and leave the dialog open.

- **Fixed: a deck with many Library photos no longer hangs Present or slows every full-deck surface.**
  A deck of 18 phone photos (24 MB) froze Present on a phone for up to 19 s with ~1.9 GB of memory,
  enough for iOS to close the tab and reload it. Present now opens with a 0.2 s longest block and a
  68 MB peak, the same as a deck with no photos. The Stage is built only when you open it, and loads
  the photos from the tab instead of a 34 MB copy. The Reading view opens in 2.5 s (was 15.7 s) and
  captions export in 2.7 s (was 12.3 s). PDF, PowerPoint, LibreOffice, images, webpage and print exports
  are 10–57 % faster with 3–5× less memory, and every exported file is unchanged apart from its timestamps.

- **Fixed: the Coach's photo-contrast finding no longer goes missing when the preview paints late.** The Studio measured a
  slide's photo once, 900 ms after the last change. On a phone, typing in Source and then opening Preview could run that
  measure before the preview had drawn the slide, so it came back empty and was never taken again. A slide that could not be
  measured is now measured again when the preview paints.

- The Studio's photo check no longer gives up on a slow photo. It used to stop waiting after 4 seconds and never check
  that slide again, so on a slow connection the Coach showed no "The text on this photo reads at …" finding (and the
  editor no measured warning) until you edited the slide. It now waits for the photo to load, however long that takes.

- **`lint:deck` names two pills that rendered as code with no warning.** A pill whose label needs quoting and whose icon is unknown (`` `{A|B, icon=nope}` ``) now gets one `pill-literal` warning naming both fixes. A state marker used as the label of a pill with options (`` `{x, icon=code}` ``, `` `{x, c2}` ``) now gets `pill-literal`, with the way out: another label, or an icon-only pill `` `{icon=code}` ``. The `pill-not-a-checkbox` suggestion now fires only on the bare `` `{x}` ``, so the option forms are no longer flagged twice.

- **Fixed: a status word means the same thing in every chart, whatever its
  case.** `AT-RISK`, `At-risk` and `at-risk` now color alike in `progress`,
  `timeline-list`, `state-chart` and `slope`, as they already did in `gantt`
  and `kanban`. Before, `progress` and `timeline-list` painted a capitalized word
  in the info fallback, and `state-chart` and `slope` dropped it into the label.
  The pill keeps your spelling, and the state-chart narration no longer reads
  the word as part of the state's name. All six components share one rule,
  `chartStatus` in `_chart-family/transform-utils.js`.
- **Fixed: a left-to-right `state-chart lr` no longer slices its start dot and
  end ring at the frame edges.** The row's side padding was 36px against the
  46–50px the markers reach, so the component's own documented `lr` example
  rendered both markers cut. The padding now reserves their full reach at HD
  and at 4K.

- Two `--player` exports of an unchanged deck are now byte-identical: the file's `generatedAt` stamp follows `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (else the epoch), as PDF dates and the reopenable payload already did.
- Exported players (the CLI's `--player` and the Studio's Webpage export) store a background picture the deck reuses only once, instead of once per slide. The 120-slide gallery deck drops from 2.74 MB to 2.36 MB. A picture placed with `![](…)` still ships once per use.
- An identical font file that the bundled faces ship under several weights is now embedded once, as a weight range, wherever no text the deck draws could tell the difference. The `html-player` example drops from 858 KB to 765 KB.

- **Fixed: a math deck exported from the Studio as a Webpage now carries its KaTeX fonts.** The
  Studio linked KaTeX's stylesheet, whose relative font addresses can't load in a shared file, so
  every formula drew in fallback type. It now inlines the fonts, as the CLI does.
- **Fixed: a deck with a function plot exports the same file every time.** The plot library named
  its clip paths from random numbers, so two exports of one deck differed. The names now come from
  the plot's own config.
- **Fixed: the browser runtime reads a CSS `url()` that holds an SVG `data:` address in full.** It
  stopped at the first `)` or `'`, which such an address contains, so a picture embedded that way
  failed to load wherever the runtime measured it. That included the Studio's Webpage export and
  the CLI's `--html` and `--fluid` exports.
- **Fixed: a portrait, square, story or mobile deck exported from the Studio as a Webpage is cut
  into pages, as the CLI's `--player` cuts it.** The Studio shipped each multi-element slide as one
  crowded page, so a `size: story` deck had 8 slides from the Studio and 32 from the CLI.
- **Fixed: a CLI `--player` file carries the deck's diagrams as source, not as drawings.** Its
  embedded source had every Mermaid fence replaced by the drawn SVG, so re-importing the file gave
  frozen diagrams nobody could edit. It now carries the deck exactly as written, as the Studio's does.
- **Fixed: Mermaid drop shadows draw in a CLI `--player` file.** The file's HTML pass lowercased the
  `feDropShadow` filter element, which SVG then ignored.
- **Fixed: a diagram in the Studio's preview and exports has an accessible name.** A diagram
  without `accTitle:` reached a screen reader as an anonymous graphic; it is now named for its
  type ("Pie chart", "Flowchart"), as CLI exports already named it.
- **Fixed: a Mermaid label containing the text "my-svg" keeps it.** The CLI's diagram renderer
  rewrote every "my-svg" in the drawing, label text included, to its internal id.

- The exported HTML player's toolbar now works where scripts cannot run, such as the iPhone file preview (Quick Look) in Mail, Files and Messages, which opens an HTML file with JavaScript off. Present shows one slide at a time, sized to fit the screen on both axes, with a swipe to the next. The list icon switches to the scrolling column, and the moon flips dark and light (except on a deck with a deck-wide `color-mode`). Buttons that cannot work without a script (Read · Article, notes, fullscreen, narration) now hide instead of doing nothing. With scripts on, the player is unchanged.

- An exported HTML player no longer loses its dark-mode styles when a deck's CSS holds a quoted `url("…")` with a `)` inside it.

- **Fixed: a slide background with a relative path is embedded in the player.** A `![bg]` the engine
  draws as the slide's own background (one with a ratio such as `left:40%`, for example) reached the
  `--player` file as a bare `a.jpg`, which shows nothing once the file is sent, and the run did not
  say so. It is now embedded like any other picture, a missing one is reported, and the file no
  longer carries the path of the author's own folder. A picture used as several slides' background
  is stored once.
- **Fixed: a code sample that shows a `style` attribute is shipped as written.** The player rewrote a
  relative `url()` in such a sample, in inline code, to the path of the author's own folder.

- `--player` keeps the deck's own canvas in the player again: a `size: 4k` deck's player is 3840 x 2160, not the HD canvas its PDF or PowerPoint takes. One render serves both files, so the PDF or PowerPoint beside the player is 4K too; add `--size hd` to lower both.

- A component gallery's "When NOT to reach for X" slide no longer prints the deck's running header over its heading. `claim-hero` drops the masthead and footer bands but not a deck-level `header:`, which every generated gallery sets, so the header collided with the title; those slides now clear it with `_header: ''`.

- **Fixed: the Playground's Deck settings now sets the deck's own theme.** The
  sheet used the `noTheme` field profile, which is the full set minus `theme`,
  on the reasoning that the site header's palette picker was the theme control
  for this surface. That picker is hidden below the `lg` breakpoint, so on a
  phone the near control was withheld in favor of a far one that was not
  rendered and the Playground had no theme control at all. The row is back, it
  writes the deck's own `theme:` — the authoritative axis, which travels with an
  exported `.md` — and it leads with an **Automatic** stop that clears the key
  and hands the deck back to the site palette. Palettes are named and grouped
  exactly as the header picker names them.
- **Fixed: Deck settings controls no longer fall outside the panel.** Each row
  paired a label column with a `min-width` floor against a control that refused
  to shrink, giving the row an incompressible 18.6rem minimum while the panel is
  capped in px/vw. The control was pushed out of the panel and the sheet grew a
  horizontal scrollbar — 5 clipped rows at a 320px viewport, and 4 at 390px once
  the reader scaled text up, because the failing sum is in `rem` and the panel is
  not. Controls may shrink now, and the rows stack below the width where a label
  and its control can sit side by side.
- **Fixed: opening Deck settings no longer arms the first control.** Radix
  focuses the first focusable descendant on open, which was the first row's
  `<select>`. iOS Safari opens a select's picker on the tap that *gives* it
  focus, so one arriving pre-focused swallowed the first tap and the row looked
  dead until you touched another control and came back. Focus parks on the panel
  itself; keyboard readers still tab straight in.

- **Playground: a quick Explore and back no longer leaves the preview hidden.** Switching Explore, Edit, Explore within
  a frame or two kept the preview covered while it waited on the Edit switch in between, which can only finish in
  Edit: about a second on an idle machine, several on a loaded one. Explore's reveal now drops that wait, and a switch that is overtaken stops its own wait loop.

- **Fixed: the Playground no longer drops address-bar parameters it does not own.** Walking the Playground rewrites
  the address to its position (`?c=…&view=read`), and leaving Explore cleared the query. Both threw away every other
  parameter, so a `?tier=unsupported` pin lost the race to the device-tier check that reads it once the page is idle, and
  the decline screen could vanish. The Playground now replaces only its own keys (`c`, `view`, `s`, `v`).

- Playground Edit: a map tile tapped soon after another one now takes the preview to its slide. Before, the first tap's scroll could report the slide it had stopped on in the same frame as the second tap, and that report replaced the second tap before it could scroll: the preview stayed where it was. The sync now drops a scroll report while a newer pick is still on its way.

- **Fixed: a slide-map pick in the Playground's Edit view survives a busy page.** A long task during the pick's scroll
  (a garbage collection, a heavy render) used to read as the scroll stopping. The rail then moved back to the slide
  the preview was passing, and the preview stopped there. The pick now owns the preview until it reaches the slide
  you picked.

- Collapsing and expanding the Playground preview on desktop returns it to the slide it was on, instead of slide 1. After typing in another slide while it was collapsed, it opens on the caret's slide. The frame stays covered until it is on that slide, so no frame shows another one.

- Playground editor: select-all no longer paints a light lavender slab over the
  markdown. The band is the palette's own accent tint again (measured 7.52:1 for
  body text on cuoio-dark, up from 1.21:1), matching the Studio's editor. The
  editor's theme rule was losing on specificity to `@codemirror/view`'s base
  theme, whose `#d7d4f0` selection color it could not out-specify.
- Removed a `requestAnimationFrame` reflow in the Playground editor that was
  added for this symptom on a misdiagnosis (an "iOS Safari system tint"); the
  color was CodeMirror's own, so the reflow never fixed anything.
- The selection wash drops from 22% to 18% of `--accent`, on every surface that shows
  it (prose, the Studio's deck editor, CodeField, the Playground's editor) plus the
  matching `::target-text` highlight. At 22%, body text over the band measured 4.32 on
  cuoio/light — the default palette and mode — just under AA; at 18% primary text clears
  4.61 on all 18 palettes in both modes and secondary text clears AA-large 3:1 with
  margin. The band looks all but identical.

- Typing in the Playground no longer rescans the theme CSS for remote references on every keystroke. The scan cost about 34 ms per key on a full sheet (more than the render itself); `webRefsInCss` now returns its last answer when the sheets are unchanged, measured at 0.01 ms.

- Studio: approving a plugin no longer shows its block unstyled for a moment. A preview that was already drawing when you clicked Approve filled the plugin's block without its stylesheet, so the first frame showed the right words with none of the plugin's colors. Each preview now draws a plugin only once the stylesheet it paints with has it, so the words and the colors arrive together. An approval given in another tab of the same browser now reaches this tab's previews too. Reloading the Studio with a plugin already approved no longer shows its block unstyled for a moment either.

- A highlight.js upgrade that adds a language named like a fence a shipped plugin already claims (`math`, `functionplot`, `anima`) no longer fails the build: the plugin keeps its fence and `npm run build` warns. A new plugin claiming a taken name still fails.
- A formula KaTeX cannot parse now shows on its error surface (mono, on a `var(--warn)` tint) in the `--player` Read · Article and the Studio's Read pane too, not only on a slide; there it used to show as plain body text.
- An `--html` or `--fluid` export now draws its function plots on any machine: the CLI inlines the plotting library into the page instead of linking it by a `file://` path on the exporting machine, where a copy opened elsewhere showed each plot's JSON config. PDF, PNG and PPTX output is unchanged.

- Fixed: the `.pptx` export (plain and `--editable`, CLI and Studio) opened in desktop PowerPoint with "Sorry, PowerPoint can't read". The writer used one theme part for both the slide master and the notes master, and PowerPoint refuses that once the notes master is in its schema position. Each master now gets its own theme part. Checked with the ISO 29500 schema and a PowerPoint-rules validator; not yet opened in desktop PowerPoint itself.

- **Fixed: `premise` no longer cuts off ordinary terms.** The term column was a fixed 140px, so any term past about eleven characters ended in an ellipsis — `Communication` rendered as `Communic…`, and `Prioritization` and `Accountability` did the same. The ledger is now one grid whose term column sizes itself to the longest term on the slide, so every description still starts on the same line. The claim rail narrows from 34% toward a 26% floor when the rows need the width. When a row's description and framing question no longer fit on one line, the question drops under the description instead of either being cut. Only a term wider than 40% of the ledger still ends in an ellipsis.
- `premise` spaces its rows by count: three rows get a loose gap and taller rows, four or five get a medium gap, six or seven a snug one, and eight keep the tight rhythm. A short ledger no longer floats as a thin strip in a tall slide. Square, portrait and mobile slides are unchanged — they keep their stacked layout, pixel for pixel.

- Present's chart card now has an end-to-end test: a press outside the slide closes it, and Escape closes the card before it leaves Present. No behavior change.

- **Studio: Escape always leaves Present.** When the Studio re-rendered Present while an Escape was still being
  delivered (another window key handler had changed state just ahead of it, most often on a busy machine), Present
  swapped its keyboard listener in the middle of that delivery. Chromium then ran neither copy, so the deck stayed open
  over the Studio and its toolbar took the next click. Present now keeps one keyboard listener for as long as it is
  open, and that listener always calls the newest key handler.

- Present keeps the screen awake while it is open, so a phone no longer locks and stops a deck mid-play; the lock screen and headset buttons now play, pause and move the deck.
- Previous, Next and jumps no longer stop continuous play: once Play is pressed the deck keeps playing from wherever you move it until you press Pause.
- Closing Present now stops the narration instead of leaving it playing over the editor.
- On a phone held sideways, the slide fills the screen and Present's controls float over it, fading after a few seconds; tap the slide to bring them back. Captions sit on the slide's bottom edge as closed captions, the spoken sentence whole on a see-through plate in the brand's dark tone that hugs the words and fades from sentence to sentence, scale with the slide, and read the same in light and dark mode; turning the phone fades the stage through the relayout instead of showing it jump.
- Fullscreen works on every browser: where the browser cannot go full screen (iPhone Safari), it hides Present's controls instead of showing an error.
- Narration captions no longer freeze on the first word while the selected voice is still loading: with the voice off they play at once, and with it on they start after a short wait and the voice joins at the next slide. Muting or unmuting during that wait no longer freezes the captions or sends the read back to the start of the slide, and once a voice has kept one slide waiting, the next slides do not wait for it again.
- Present's on/off controls (captions, voice, rail, guide, notes and the top-bar toggles) now read at a glance: on is a solid accent pill, off an outline.
- Tapping a faded Present screen on an iPhone brings the controls back and keeps them up, instead of flashing them and hiding them again; a tap right after a swipe hides them as it should.
- Under the slide, the caption crawl now keeps scrolling from one slide to the next instead of jumping back to the top at each slide.

- **Fixed: Present's Play no longer sticks on the first caption on a phone that has never picked a voice.** A phone
  cannot run the on-device voice, so its voice choice starts empty, and making that empty choice ready threw. With the
  Voice on, the captions never started; with it off they ran, but the error still escaped. Present now reads on its
  estimate clock until a voice is chosen.

- **Studio Present:** the progress rail and the caption highlight no longer cost a style, layout and paint cycle on every frame while a deck plays. The played range animated `width`; it now moves by `transform`, which the compositor runs without the main thread, and a word lights the moment it is spoken instead of fading in over 150 ms. On the built Studio at 3840x2160 with the CPU slowed 4x, playback went from 146 layouts and about 2.5 s of main-thread work per 3 s to 20 and about 1.5 s. The rail looks the same, apart from a slightly different sliver for the first few pixels of a slide's fill.

- Studio Present: autoplay no longer skips a spoken slide that follows a silent one. The empty-slide skip read the track of the slide it had just left, so Play from a silent title slide went straight past slide 2 when the deck had no `greeting:` to hold it.

- The Studio's pooled previews (the deck panel's preset picker and the Reshape picker) and the Fabricate specimens now paint on the docs dev server (`astro dev`). Two refs, the preview pool's `alive` flag and `DeckPreview`'s renderer, did not survive React StrictMode's dev remount. Production builds were never affected.
- The Studio no longer reads the indented lines of a `style: |` (or any `|` / `>`) block as deck settings. A CSS line named like a register, such as `  lift: on`, used to show as that setting, and a preset Reset or a change to that setting rewrote the author's CSS. The lexicon and acronym editors now keep a block scalar intact instead of flattening its lines into separate keys.

- Preview frames no longer re-solve their layout when the web fonts arrive. Every
  engine `@font-face` is `font-display: swap`, so a preview document laid out once
  against fallback metrics, painted, and shifted when the real face landed — with
  nothing to report it, because the slide box is pinned to its `@size` and no fit
  or overflow channel fires. All three preview builders (the Studio/Playground
  filmstrip, the Present stage window, and the landing-page and specimen islands)
  now hold their existing reveal until the document's own faces have settled.
  Measured on `/playground/?view=edit` with a `list` + `cards-grid` deck: a reader
  saw two layouts, at 197ms and 517ms, with the worst text run moving 330.3px
  between them — now one. Warm-cache reveal cost is ~30ms; a face fetch that never
  answers reveals anyway after 1.5s, so a dead font can cost a shift but never a
  blank preview.
- The desktop print path waits for that gate rather than a fixed 450ms beat before
  opening the print dialog. This is hardening, not a bug fix, and the measurement
  says so: driving the real Share → Print deck → Print with faces on a 600ms link,
  `.lattice` computed `visible` at the instant `print()` was called *with the wait
  removed as well*, because the reveal lands before the frame's `load` event; with
  faces hung, `load` never fires and nothing prints on either arm. What the change
  removes is a latent coupling — the print path's correctness rested on "the reveal
  happens before `onload`", which is incidental rather than guaranteed, and
  `buildSrcdoc` hides `.lattice` until that reveal, so losing the race would print
  blank pages into a file the author keeps.

- On phones and tablets, the Studio's previews (the main preview, Present, the slide overview, and the Add slide, Reshape and Print grids) now show each photo at the size it is drawn, not at its original size; on a desktop, the small previews do. A 12-megapixel photo is about 48 MB once decoded, whether it fills the preview or a small thumbnail, and an iPhone could discard the tab on decks with many photos. In a WebKit test (the engine of Safari on iPhone and iPad), ten such photos in ten preview frames went from 1,016 MB to 204 MB; Firefox saves about as much, while Chrome, which keeps the memory it used making the copies, saves little. This covers photo backgrounds (`![bg]`) and photos in the text (`![alt](…)`, what the Compose photo picker and the chat agent add), but not yet the photos of a collage, whether they come from the Library (the camera roll), the site's own samples or a web address you have allowed. A web photo you have not allowed is never fetched to make a copy. A background photo's first appearance takes slightly longer while its smaller copy is made: an image panel shows its loading painting meanwhile, and a full-slide background stays blank until the copy arrives. A photo in the text shows its original until its copy is ready, then switches in the same place; the copies of photos on nearby slides are made ahead. Zooming into the preview loads a sharper copy once the zoom settles, up to 1920 pixels wide. A desktop's main preview keeps showing the original photo. A photo from a site that does not allow it to be read keeps loading at full size, as before.

- The Studio, the Playground filmstrip and the Stage window no longer force every loading photo to decode at full size. Each photo's placeholder now waits for the photo to load rather than decode, so a picture that is not on screen, such as one in a hidden preview, is no longer held as a full-size bitmap. On WebKit, a 12-megapixel photo is about 48 MB decoded; ten such photos that were loaded but not shown measured 531 MB before and 66 MB after. This mostly helps decks with many photos on an iPhone or iPad.

- Closed Studio panels with slide previews no longer hold on to their last slides' photos. This covers the deck settings, Present's slide overview, the Print preview and Add slide. These panels stay loaded once opened, and each kept its last screenful of slides, photos included, for the rest of the session. A preview with no tile to show for 5 seconds now switches to a blank slide, which frees its photos. Previews whose tiles scrolled away but stayed in an open panel also now give up their place once their short grace period ends; before, nothing released them until something else changed.

- The Studio's Share → Print deck drawer no longer builds new preview documents each time it is reopened. The Share sheet now stays mounted after its first open, so the drawer's preview frames and its print frame are reused. Measured on Playwright WebKit, three reopens with a print each grew memory by about 45 MB instead of about 230 MB. Each open still starts from the default paper, layout and color.

- **Fixed: Print on a phone or in Firefox printed one page, a picture of the Studio, instead of the deck.**
  Those browsers print the whole page rather than the hidden print frame. On iOS, Android, any Firefox and any
  touch-first device, Print now prepares a real PDF (tap Print), then opens it to print (tap Open PDF), the path iOS
  already used. Desktop Chrome and Safari keep the print dialog.
- **Faster: printing or downloading a printed PDF no longer freezes the Studio.** Each page's image work runs in
  background workers as the slides are drawn: a 50-slide print went from 119 s to 58 s, with the longest freeze from
  2.6 s to 1.0 s, and the file is unchanged.
- **Faster: a printed PDF compresses each page once.** Print re-compressed every slide picture the Studio had just
  written; it now carries the picture's own compressed pixels, as the PDF export already did. Pixel-identical, about
  13 s faster for a 50-slide photo deck, and 2–7 % larger on disk.

- **Fixed: the canonical docs said the engine ships 53 components; it ships 61.** The
  count had drifted in four live, present-tense surfaces — `design/design-system.md`
  (the opening inventory, the §3 disk-grouping note, and the §9 bucket table),
  `design/skill.md`'s scaffolder row, `engineering/marp-independence.md`'s value-add
  summary and its Layers 1–2 auto-coverage claim, and the `player-prune` header
  describing what the player inlines. The §9 table was the worst of it: it announced
  twelve buckets, omitted `connect` (`contact` and `wifi`, both `function: statement`)
  altogether, and its per-bucket counts summed to 52. The table now carries all
  thirteen buckets and the measured counts, and the `bucket === function` split reads
  35 of 61 rather than 31 of 53. Dated measurements keep their original numbers —
  a timestamped observation is a record, not a claim about today.

- **Fixed: `q-and-a` puts its index numeral on the question's baseline, in every look.** The
  counter was an absolutely positioned mark at `top: 0`, which lands its box on the question's
  box rather than its baseline — two fonts at two sizes then put the two baselines wherever
  their own half-leading fell. Measured from the rendered PNG: 7.2px out on the default ledger,
  18.6px on `solo`, and on `grid` it varied 7.7–42.2px *within one slide* as the questions
  wrapped. The pair is a baseline-aligned flex row now, and the numeral measures 0px out.
- **Fixed: the `spine` rail begins and ends on a node.** It was one full-height mark on a
  container that fills the stage while its nodes sit centered in it, so 62px of line dangled
  above the first node and 122px below the last, and the two tails moved independently with the
  content. Each pair now draws its own segment, centre to centre; the last pair draws none.
- **Fixed: `rail` aligns its three columns on one baseline** — the answer sat 7.9px above the
  question's baseline on every row of an exhibit table — **and its numeral reads `01`,** not a
  bare `1`, so one component no longer prints two numbering styles.
- **Fixed: `grid` aligns its question tops at any question length.** The two-line header reserve
  it used instead is a minimum, so a three-line question blew through it and the row went out of
  line anyway (measured 21px apart), while costing 42px of dead air per cell when it did work.
  The cell top-packs instead, and the numeral sits over its own question rather than stranded in
  a gutter the quadrant never used.
- **Fixed: `tab` groups its pairs.** 31px of air inside a pair against 34px between two pairs is
  no grouping at all; the ratio is 2.6 now, at no cost in capacity (the overflow probe first
  flags at the same pair count either way).
- **Fixed: `solo` and `compact` can re-base the index size again.** Both set `--qa-index` on the
  section while the default declared it on `> .cell-stage`, which wins — so `solo`'s numeral
  rendered at the default ledger's 22.4px beside an `--fs-emphasis` question and its own rule was
  dead. The private tokens moved onto the section, where specificity decides.

- **`contact` and `wifi` now follow the deck's card alignment.** Both used to sit at the top of the stage whatever `cards:` or `_class: cards-*` said. They now center by default, and `top`, `spread` and `stretch` apply. `wifi` also drops a stray 21px of browser margin under its fields that pushed the card off center.

- The CLI's self-contained player (`lattice deck.md -o deck.html --player`) now embeds local pictures its own CSS tokenizer missed, though Chromium loads them: an escaped `u\72l(photo.png)` or `image-s\65t("photo.png" 1x)`, an unquoted `url(` or an `image-set()` string that the end of a style closes, and an address holding a no-break space. Each used to ship the deck's local file path in the shared file and show no picture. The export now reads CSS with `cssRefSpans`, the reader the gallery gate, the Studio's export and the narrator share (Segno R4). Every deck in the repo exports the same bytes as before.
- The CLI's player no longer ships your folder's path when the deck sits in a folder whose name holds a parenthesis or a quote (`Decks (2024)`, `Bob's decks`). A relative picture there was neither embedded nor reported missing.

- The Studio's player export now finds the pictures it embeds with the same HTML and CSS readers the web-image placeholder pass uses (`scanHtml` and `cssRefSpans` in `lib/core/remote-ref.js`), not its own regular expressions. Every deck in the repo exports byte-for-byte as before. Where the old patterns misread markup, the export now reads what the browser reads. It now embeds three pictures the old patterns missed, which shipped blank: an escaped `u\72l(…)`, an HTML `<image src>` (which the browser loads as an `<img>`), and a custom property's `url()` under any name, not only `--logo-mask`. It no longer fetches an `<img>` written inside a comment, a repeated `src` the browser ignores, or a malformed `url(…)` the browser never loads. (Segno R4.)

- The Reading view's video card finds the poster the slide paints in more spellings: an escaped `u\72l(`, an uppercase `URL(`, a comment before the address, a `background` shorthand, the last of several declarations and an `!important` one. It reads the embed's style with the same CSS reader as the export (Segno R4). Every deck in the repo reads the same poster as before.
- The Webpage export now embeds a picture whose bare `url()` holds a hex escape followed by a space, such as `url(k\29 .png)`. It used to treat that address as invalid and leave it out, though browsers load it.

- **Fixed: Read · Article keeps every chart's color in the HTML player.** Status pills on
  progress and timeline-list charts kept their color only on a slide; in the article they
  printed as plain words. The roadmap and matrix-grid header rules drew nothing, because
  they read a token that only a slide defined. And matrix-grid showed as a plain table
  that lost its filled and outlined cells. All three now match the slide, in light and
  dark, on both the CLI and Studio players. Demo: `examples/read-article-chart-paints.md`.
- **Fixed: a flow chart's own caption now appears under it in Read · Article.** The article
  used to repeat the slide heading there and drop the author's caption line.

- Read · Article: a word cloud now captions with the author's caption line instead of repeating the slide heading, and an SVG chart's caption keeps its inline markup (emphasis, code). Every figure kind takes its caption from one rule: the authored `.chart-caption` when the slide has one, else the heading.

- In **Read · Article** (the HTML player from the CLI and the Studio, and the Studio's Reading view), a word cloud now fills its figure. It used to sit in the top third of a fixed 3:2 box, with its caption at the bottom under an empty two-thirds, and its leftmost word met the figure's edge. The figure is now as tall as the cloud at full width, a portrait deck's taller cloud included, and the caption sits directly below it.

- In Read · Article, a slide's Key Insight now reads as a callout and its below-note as a closing note, and a slide whose only content is its Key Insight no longer gets a "see the slide" placeholder card.
- The Studio preview no longer shows an image slide in a provisional layout and then jumps when its picture arrives: the first reveal waits for the picture's size, up to 4 seconds, and a later arrival fades through instead of jumping.
- Tapping a video's poster in the Studio preview plays the clip again, on desktop and touch. The preview's gesture layer had been swallowing the tap.
- In an exported player, a slide's web link (a video poster, a contact or closing URL) now opens in a new tab. Before, it replaced the player in the same tab and the reader lost the deck.
- A video slide with a light poster no longer shows a near-black tile while the poster loads on a light slide: the tile under a loading poster is the slide's own surface. The no-poster placeholder keeps its dark video tile.
- An image from a site you allowed in the Studio no longer stays blank when that site redirects to one of its own subdomains (picsum.photos to fastly.picsum.photos, for example). A redirect to an unrelated site is still blocked.
- Turning to an image slide in the Studio preview no longer flashes the photo across the whole slide before it settles: the preview measures the deck's photos ahead of time and draws each slide in its final layout from the first frame. A photo that cannot load now shows the hatched placeholder instead of an empty panel.
- Changing slides in the Studio preview no longer paints the text in one spot and then moves it into place a moment later: each slide arrives already laid out. The Playground's whole-deck preview gets the same fix when it swaps a slide in.
- An image slide's text in the Studio and Playground previews now sits in the same column as in the export. The preview had been drawing the text card twice, one inside the other, which indented the text and added a second accent bar.
- In the Studio and Playground previews, an image slide whose photo is still loading now shows a loading placeholder and holds its text back until the photo's size is known. The text then appears once, in its final place, instead of moving when the photo arrives.

- The export's OVERFLOW, content-cut and chart label warnings, and the guards trim now number pages by the deck's own slides. A deck that pasted a `<section data-lattice-slide>` example, or the whole export scaffold, used to count it as a slide, so every later page number was off by one ("pages 1, 3" on a two-slide deck).
- A `functionplot` whose config holds non-ASCII text now draws it correctly. An axis label `x²` used to draw as `xÂ²` on the slide, in the PDF, in `--player` and in the `--read` article: both inflaters decoded the UTF-8 config with a bare `atob`.
- A `functionplot` fence now draws in the Studio: in the preview, the Read pane and the webpage export. No docs-site host loaded the function-plot library, so every plot there was an empty stage. The runtime now loads it on demand, only for a deck that has a plot.
- A function plot in a reading article (`--read`, the player's Read · Article, the Studio Read pane) now scales to the column instead of being clipped. At phone width only one corner of the plot used to show.

- The exported player no longer hands reader-mode tools two copies of the deck. It carries the slides and the prose article in one document and switched between them with a stylesheet rule, which Readability (Firefox Reader View and its shake-to-summarize, and the reading modes Safari and Chrome ship) cannot see — so a summarizer received every sentence twice, 2255 extracted words for a 1080-word deck. The article's container now ships marked `hidden` and `setView` maintains that attribute as the view changes. Both halves are needed, because extractors reach the file two different ways: Firefox for iOS readerizes the live page, while Firefox on the desktop re-fetches the URL and parses it with no scripts run at all, where only the shipped attribute is visible. Nothing moves on screen in either case, and with scripting off every slide is still laid out.

- The reader view and narration put a slide's subtitle after its heading. Before, a lone subtitle showed as the kicker above the heading and was read first, and a subtitle on a slide that also had an eyebrow was dropped.
- The masthead no longer lifts a code block, or a paragraph that mixes code and text, as a subtitle. A slide with a mermaid fence after its heading and a code-only note below it had the fence, the note and its body pulled into the heading band.
- The reader view keeps the words around a chart, image, diagram or equation. An image's lead paragraph, a chart's caption, a math slide's variable legend and its second equation were dropped. A chart's figure caption is now its own caption rather than a repeat of the heading.
- The reader view shows a video as a link card inside the prose column, with its poster as a thumbnail when it has one. It used to be a bare "Watch on YouTube" link hanging left of the column.
- The Studio's reader view typesets math once. It never loaded KaTeX's stylesheet, so every equation and legend symbol also printed as plain MathML text.
- The reader view keeps the caption under a journey or state chart, which it dropped along with the chart it cannot re-host.

- On Windows, ending a code-package export's sandbox browser no longer leaves a helper process behind. `reap()` lists every process naming the browser's profile and stops it, and a live browser could start a helper between the list and the stop. The sweep now repeats until a pass finds nothing, up to 8 passes in one PowerShell run.

- **`tag:` and `backdrop:` read a YAML flow list.** `tag: [plain, large]` and `backdrop: [40, clear]` now style the deck the way `tag: plain large` does. They used to stamp nothing while the value looked valid. `lint:deck` reads them the same way, and a `%` inside a word (`4%0`) is still an unknown value.

- **A `related` ("see also") entry naming a component that does not exist is now a
  build failure.** `q-and-a` pointed at `faq`, which has never been a component here,
  so its `.docs.md` carried a 404 relative link, its gallery rendered a "See also" row
  for nothing, and `dist/docs/components.json` shipped the dead name into the playground
  bundle and every exported deck — only the pick surface filtered it. That relation now
  points at `list-tabular`, and `checkRelatedTargets` (in `build:check`) stops the next one.

- **Fixed: `npm i @laticent/lattice` gives a working `lattice` command.** The installed CLI
  exited with `Cannot find module '@laticent/segno/read'` before rendering anything, and an
  install without jsdom quietly skipped the compare-code, scene, wifi and build transforms.
  The bundled CLI now inlines every workspace library it uses, and the package declares the
  libraries and jsdom as dependencies.
- **Breaking:** the npm package's public paths are named, and it carries less. The `./lib/*`
  and `./dist/*` wildcard exports are gone; the named exports (`/css`, `/runtime`, `/engine`,
  `/themes/<name>.css`, `dist/lattice-emoji.css`, `dist/docs/components.json`) remain. The
  Marp kit and the agent kit leave the tarball (take them from the `dist-kits` branch or the
  release zip). Mermaid, its CLI, ZenUML, KaTeX and function-plot are no longer installed,
  because their plugins ship their own copies. Packed size goes from 28.1 MB to 22.0 MB.
- **Breaking:** Node 22.13 or newer is required (was 22.12), because jsdom, now a runtime
  dependency, supports Node 22 from 22.13.

- **Fixed: the Chat header keeps its title beside a long model name on a phone.** A model named like "Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 4.5" squeezed the title to "C". The model chip now shortens first, so the header reads "Chat" with the model name ending in an ellipsis. The docked Library's title, which its search field hid entirely at desktop width, shows too.
- **Fixed: a `pricing` feature row wraps inside its card instead of being cut off.** Feature rows stayed on one line however narrow the tier was, so the card cut the end of any row longer than its column: the default sample lost the end of "Checks accumulate up the ladder". A long row now wraps under its own text, and its mark stays on the first line.
- **Fixed: the Studio settings panel no longer scrolls sideways in General.** The Language and "AI writes in" selects were wider than their row at tablet width, so the whole panel scrolled sideways. They now fit the row and end their label in an ellipsis.
- **Fixed: on a phone, a tap right after typing lands on the control you tapped.** Leaving a text field used to shrink the sheet and move its contents before the tap landed, so tapping a Library tab after a search, or Language after typing a deck name, hit something else. The sheet now holds still until the tap lands.
- **Fixed: the Library's header search is as tall as the Import button beside it.** On a tablet the field was 44px tall next to a 32px button and nearly filled the header. Fields in a header row now use a 32px size; the phone's search at the bottom of the sheet keeps its larger size.

- **The chat's `render_slide` look fetches only the fonts its slide uses.** It built its picture in a capture frame that force-loaded every face the engine declares (every weight of every family, all KaTeX faces, all eleven emoji slices) and embedded every vendored face: 130 font files for one title slide. The look now uses the preview's font settle (the faces laid-out text uses) and embeds only the faces its one slide draws: 30 files for the same slide, with a pixel-identical picture. It renders no faster on a machine that already has the fonts cached, and it does not fix the look sometimes running past its 15 s budget under load. Exports are unchanged.

- **The chat's `render_slide` look runs past its 15 s budget far less often on a busy phone.** Two things slowed it. On a Full device, the Studio's background warm-up (the Compose, Present and Read panels, then every vendored font) started during the chat's answer and its render and competed with both; it now waits until the chat turn has finished. And the slide camera fetched and embedded 16 font files for a title slide that draws four faces, every weight of each family in a font stack, twice over; it now leaves out the weights we ship that the slide does not draw, and embeds 4. Measured on a loaded WebKit phone profile with Full forced, 200 looks each on the same machine: renders over budget fell from 11 to 2, the median from 10.9 s to 9.3 s and the slowest 1% from 18.3 s to 13.6 s. The two that still ran over had no warm-up beside them; the machine itself was starved. The look's picture came out byte-identical for slides with emoji, every text weight and style, math, icons and photos. An author's own font files, and any deck with a `::first-line` or `::first-letter` rule, keep every face as before. Exports are unchanged.

- **A chart slide's class words keep a literal `&` as one `&amp;`.** The chart family re-escaped the class attribute it had read already escaped, so `x&y` came out as `x&amp;amp;y`.
- **The CLI's `--size` writes the size as typed.** Rewriting a deck's `size:` line used a string replacement, so a `--size` holding `$&` wrote `size: size: …`.

- A `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'`, `$1` or `$$` in an author's text now renders as written in three more places: a chart slide's `_class:` token (where a `` $` `` pasted the tag's own prefix into `class="…"`, so the rest of the token became an attribute of the `<section>`), a QR card's caption in a split panel, and a code package's failure note.

- The risk matrix's critical band is the darkest band again on the dark face of the achromatopsia, deuteranopia and tritanopia palettes. Since the per-theme status colors it had landed between low and medium there, so a palette that shows severity only by lightness read critical as the second-mildest band.
- On the a11y palettes, the risk matrix's critical key number now clears 4.5:1 in browsers without relative color (Safari 17.5 to 17.x, Firefox 120 to 127), where it had fallen to 2.97-4.42:1 on the dark face.
- In Safari 17.5 and 17.6, text whose ink a chart picks from the color under it (the risk matrix's key numbers, finished pills and labels, a tower's share values) no longer turns black. That WebKit drops a relative color whose origin is a light-dark() color, so such text painted black, 1.0:1 on the light critical band. The engine's guard now tests that shape, and Safari 17.x uses each rule's plain curated ink.
- In the HTML player, an a11y palette's dark slide now shows the palette's own near-black ink on its status marks, as the PDF does. Since the per-theme status colors, the player had used the white ink of onyx, which the a11y palettes extend, so the risk matrix's key numbers read at about 1.1:1 on their discs.
- The same player fix applies to every token an a11y palette fixes over onyx's pairs. On a dark slide in the player, the categorical ramp (`--cat-N-fill`, `--cat-N-mark`), `--cat-on-mark` and `--diagram-critical` now use the a11y palette's own values, as the PDF already did, rather than onyx's dark arms.
- An exported HTML player no longer crashes Chrome 119-122 on a slide with a picked ink, such as a dark risk matrix. Those versions have relative color but no light-dark(), and they crash on a relative color over a color-mix(). The player now keeps the @supports light-dark() probe, so they take the plain, curated ink.
