- `require('@laticent/lattice')` and `import '@laticent/lattice'` now load the render engine (the same module as `@laticent/lattice/engine`) instead of running the CLI, which exited the program that imported it. The CLI is still the `lattice` command; `@laticent/lattice/min` is no longer an import path.

- On Windows, the code sandbox now retries removing the sandbox browser's temporary profile when a file in it is still busy, instead of giving up at once. A render with a code package or npm plugin could fail with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink …\Cache_Data\sqldb0`, because Chromium's helper processes can hold a file there for a moment after the browser exits. The removal now uses Node's retry-on-EBUSY backoff, up to about 5.5 s.

- **Fixed: a finish saved in Fabricate now appears in the Studio's image, PDF and PowerPoint exports.** The live preview showed it, but every export came out as if the deck had no finish. Finishes built in Fabricate pick up the fix without being saved again.
- **Fixed: the frame line of the gallery finish (and Fabricate's Inset frame) now appears in exports.** It showed on screen but every PDF, image and PowerPoint export dropped it. The line also moved outward, so it now frames the header and page number instead of running through the header. A hand-written finish with a `frame` edge needs one more token, `--fin-frame-mark` (the line color), to keep its frame in exports.

- `NUMERIC_PILL` in `lib/core/chart-values.js` now runs in linear time. It is Segno's rewrite of the same pattern and accepts the same strings (0 disagreements on a 300,000-case fuzz). A failing match on `1` + 50,000 tabs + `x!` took about 3 s and now takes 0.2 ms.
- The /segno playground READS the grammar box instead of running it as JavaScript, and builds the grammar in a Web Worker with a 1.5 s limit. The box keeps the same `const … ; return { start, rules }` shape, and every preset builds the same grammar as before, but only grammar helpers, strings, numbers, objects and earlier names are understood. No visitor text is ever executed. A `for (;;) {}`, which used to freeze the tab, is now an error with a line and column. A grammar that reuses names until it doubles past 10,000 pieces is refused at once. Any other grammar that Segno is slow to build, such as an `alt()` of 3,000 literals, which took about 10 s, is stopped at 1.5 s while the page keeps running.

- **The linter and the editor's completion now find directive comments exactly where the renderer does.** They read the
  deck model's comment blocks instead of running a line scan of their own. A directive in a multi-line comment
  inside a blockquote or list item (`> <!--` / `> _class: kpi` / `> -->`) is now found, as the renderer always
  applied it. A `<!--` line inside an HTML block such as `<div>` is no longer taken for a directive. And an
  unclosed comment in a list item no longer hides every directive below it. A comment inside the front matter is
  no longer listed as one: the renderer reads only the front matter's keys.
- **The deck model no longer drops a token's number when its tape grows.** On a large deck, the parse that grew
  the tape could lose a comment block's mark, a fence's marker length or a heading's level for the one token
  pushed at that moment. A run of unclosed comments also no longer costs one scan of the rest of the deck per
  comment: 20,000 of them took 5.3 s and now parse about as fast as the renderer's own parser does.

- A flowchart row too long to read (more than 65,536 arrows, escapes or heads in the row, about 2,400 times the longest real row) is now refused with a `flowchart-row-too-long` error and left out of the chart, with the rows nested under it. The parser's memory on such a row is bounded, however many code spans cut it into runs.

- The Library's sample-slide check renders without warming the Mermaid draw host, so checking a gallery can no longer reopen a draw frame the preview closed.

- The web-reference scanner no longer misses an image or `<source>` that MathML `<mi>`/`<mtext>` or SVG `<desc>`/`<title>`/`<foreignObject>` let through: a `<![CDATA[` section there (terminated or not), a start tag inside one, and a `</svg>` or `</math>` the browser ignores inside one now hand the markup to the spec parser. Each fetched in Chromium as written. No deck in the corpus is affected.
- A stray `<body>` tag (`<table><td><body background=…>`) no longer carries a web address past the scanner's spec-parser check: the tree builder gives its attributes to the page's own body, which the check never looked at. Found by the browser fuzz; it fetched in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox.
- Scanning markup with many comments is linear: 400 KB of comments took 29 s and now takes milliseconds.
- Segno R3: the web-reference scanner reads markup through a parser generated from a Segno grammar (`lib/core/html-ref-grammar.js`) in place of the hand-written scanner, and reports `unsure` spans, each with a reason, where the browser's tree builder could read the markup differently. Every deck in the corpus scans to the same bytes as before.

- Segno's grammar analysis (FIRST, FOLLOW and which rules recurse) now runs in dependency order, so the order rules are listed in no longer matters: a 4,000-rule chain listed bottom-up took 12.4 s to lint and now takes 43 ms. This matters for grammars written at runtime, such as on the `/segno` page.

- The Studio's class editor and the asset rename read a slide's `_class` from the comments the engine reads, so a comment inside an HTML block (`<div>` / `<!-- _class: kpi -->` / `</div>`) no longer shows as the slide's class when the render applies none.
- A multi-line directive inside a list item or blockquote keeps the engine's inner whitespace (tabs expanded), so the lint, completion and the render read the same value.
- The `track-directive` lint warns wherever the engine applies a degenerate `_track`, including inside a list item or blockquote and after a closed `<pre>` or `<div>`, where it used to stay silent.
- The lint reads a deck that opens with a BOM, or uses lone `\r` line ends, the way the render does: its front matter is front matter, and each rule reads its own slide's directives.

- The Studio's speaker-note, `describe:` and `say:` editors find a slide's comments where the engine does: a comment in a `$$` equation or an indented code block is code, a comment in a fence inside a `<div>` block is a note, and an unclosed `<!--` in a code fence no longer hides the note after it.
- The Studio's outline and preview no longer re-read a whole deck on every keystroke when it holds a `$$` equation: an edit re-reads only its slide unless a `$$` with no closer is above it.
- Lattice now reads a deck's front matter with a generated grammar: the `---` block and each settings line, with a small reader for where a `style: |` block's text ends. No deck renders or lints differently.

- Studio and Playground pickers, menus and popovers now open above toasts. At phone width a setting change raises an Undo toast at the foot of the screen, and a picker opened while it was up opened under it: a tap on a row the toast covered closed the list and chose nothing, or hit Undo and reverted the change just made. Measured at 390px in the logo settings, where the toast covered the color list's last two visible rows. Menus and popovers follow the same rule, so the chat's Attach popover, which reaches into the same band, is covered too.

- **The Playground's Mode row now renders.** It was listed in the panel's field profile
  but its host never passed the mode vocabulary the row is gated on, so the control was
  configured and never drawn.
- **Studio lists no longer waste ~40px of every row's left edge.** The scoped island reset
  stands in for Tailwind's Preflight but never zeroed list padding, so any structural `<ul>` —
  the Speech tab's lexicon and acronym rows among them — kept the browser's default indent. On
  a 390px phone that was a tenth of the screen. Prose lists in Architect replies keep their
  bullets.

- **Fixed: the CLI's "refused … outside the deck folder" warning now names the path you wrote.** With `-o` pointing at another folder, the export's capture page asks for a deck's relative file from the output folder, so the warning named a path nobody wrote. It now adds the deck-folder path it also checked: `(from the deck folder: …)`.
- The Studio's AI and voice requests now identify themselves to OpenRouter as `Lattice Studio` instead of the retired `Lattice Drawing Board`.

- On a phone, a tap on the deck above a panel now closes it even in the panel's first moment on screen. A Library opened for the first time could ignore that tap: its real sheet replaces its loading sheet in place, the dialog library starts listening for outside taps only a moment after mount, and in iOS Safari the finger can lift on a different backdrop than it went down on, so Safari sends no click at all. The tap is now read from the finger going down and up on the backdrop, and goes through the same keep-open rules as any outside tap.

- A pasted phone photo written as `![title](data:… "description")` on an `image` or `bleed` slide renders about a third faster: the engine no longer copies the photo's whole address through the picture record's text. Measured on three 3.5 MB photos: 2.5 s → 1.6 s per render. The output is unchanged.

- On a phone, picking a result in the site-wide search now goes there. Before, every pick (a page, a docs result) closed the search and left you where you were.

- The `sketch` finish now reaches every label on the slide. Counters and card
  number badges, table column heads, BEFORE/AFTER and status chips, stamps,
  captions, chart legend values, gantt/quadrant/radar axis ticks, legal
  citations and the cell-footer page number all render in the hand face instead
  of the machine mono they kept before. 95 label-voice sites had pinned
  `--font-mono` directly, which the finish re-points nothing of — it re-points
  `--font-label`. Measured on the full gallery under `class: sketch`: 301
  mono-rendered text runs before, 72 after, and every survivor is code.
- Fixed the `redline`, `citation-card` and `regulatory-update` eyebrows, whose
  font was named on the parent paragraph but never reached the `<code>` inside
  it — so they had never worn the label voice on any theme. Only visible under
  `sketch`, where they left a machine-faced kicker over hand-drawn content.
- No visual change on any non-sketch theme: `--font-label` defaults to
  `var(--font-mono)` and no theme overrides it, so every swapped site resolves to
  the identical stack. Verified by rendering the 117-slide gallery before and
  after and comparing the COMPUTED font on every text run — 301 mono-rendered
  runs before, 72 after, all of them code — plus identical overflow markers, so
  the hand face tips nothing into new clipping.
- **Note for consumer themes:** `--font-mono` now means code voice only. A theme
  or deck that re-pointed `--font-mono` to restyle labels should re-point
  `--font-label` instead — the two still resolve identically unless you override
  one.
- Chart legend values keep their column alignment in the hand face:
  `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` does that work, not the font, and
  Shantell Sans ships the `tnum` feature.
- Known gap, unchanged: text inside a rendered Mermaid diagram still uses the
  mono stack under `sketch` — a separate, pre-existing divergence in the
  diagram theme-variable path (`engineering/mermaid.md` §5.3).

- **Fixed: the Studio's slide counter no longer widens on decks past 99 slides.** Its reserved
  width was 78px, and "Slide 100 / 999" draws 78.75px, so the row shifted by up to a pixel. The
  slot now reserves 80px, which holds every count up to "Slide 999 / 999".

- **Fixed: a speaker note containing `$1`, `$&`, `` $` `` or `$'` no longer corrupts the render.** The note's `<aside>` was spliced into the slide with `String.replace` and a replacement STRING, where those sequences are backreferences rather than literals — so a note reading "$100" expanded to the first capture group (`<section`) plus `00`. The stray tag unbalanced the HTML, the depth-aware section walker then under-counted slides, and the page/note length mismatch made the exporter drop **every** note annotation from the PDF with only a warning. Prose about money was the ordinary way to hit it. The splice now uses a replacer function, whose return value is taken literally.

- **Fixed: `spectrum-card: rainbow` keeps the theme's full ribbon in the Studio and the
  Playground.** On a deck that sets `spectrum: solid`, `duo` or `mono`, the pinned card rail used
  to draw the quieter bar in every browser preview and in the Studio's Webpage export, while the
  CLI export drew the ribbon. It now draws the ribbon everywhere.
- **Breaking:** a `spectrum:` style now sets `--spectrum-style`, and the bar reads
  `--spectrum-bar`. `--spectrum` is always the theme's own ribbon. Custom CSS that painted with
  `var(--spectrum)` and expected the slide's bar should read `var(--spectrum-bar)`.

- Choosing where the spectrum bar sits (`spectrum-edge: top|left|right|bottom|off`, or the matching per-slide class) no longer moves the slide's content or chrome. The bar used to take its width out of the content, so a `left` bar pushed the heading and cards 4px right and narrowed them, and a `bottom` bar shortened the content area. The header, footer, page number, draft/confidential stamps, `mark-*` decorations and the overflow marker moved with it. Each side's padding now gives up exactly the bar it carries, so every placement leaves the same content box and the same chrome position. It holds for every component, its manifest variants, the modifiers `footer-inset`, `fill-optical`, `claim-bleed`, `claim-hero` and `safe`, and every class the engine reserves. Centered logos (`logo-finish: top-center`, `bottom-center`) and `![bg]` background photos hold still too: a background now measures from the border box. A `finish:` backdrop still ends where the bar begins, since a backdrop reaching under the bar would hide it.
- A default deck (top placement) moves in these one-time ways and no others, measured against the old CSS: `premise` content sits 2px higher (1.5px on a narrow canvas; it has no bottom padding of its own, so it now reserves one bar width there); dark slides sit 4px lower, where light slides do; the draft/confidential/wip tab sits 4px further in from the right edge; the overflow capsule sits one bar width above the bottom edge and is about 19px narrower at 1280px wide (its height and font give up one bar width); `collage bleed` captions sit 3 to 4px higher. All scale with the canvas.
- The bar no longer shoves content when something adds or removes it. These used to move the slide by the bar's width and now leave it where the unmarked slide sits, measured against the old CSS at the default placement: `accent` and `tone-edge` slides (chart-family slides 4px higher; `title`, `closing`, `divider`, `image` and `scene` 2px higher; `topic` 1 to 4px depending on the element, its header 4px); a deck-wide `spectrum: solid`, `duo` or `mono` (chart-family and `topic` slides 4px higher; `title` and `closing` 2px higher with their running header 4px; `image` and `scene` 2px higher); and `spectrum: off`, which now keeps the 4px a default slide has at the top, so ordinary slides sit 4px lower. Dark slides do not move under any of these: the dark-slide change below cancels it. These distances scale with the canvas: the "2px" is half a bar at 1280px wide and 6px on a 3840px deck.
- The full-bleed layouts `image`, `scene`, `split-panel`, `split-compare`, a `claim-bleed` chart, diagram, video or big-number, and `collage bleed` now draw the spectrum bar as two thin overlay strips (placement and top) laid over the slide instead of a border. A border there shrank the photo or panel by the bar's width; the overlay takes no room, so those frames keep their true edge under every placement and the bar paints above the art. They show no top bar by default, as before, and a placement, a deck-wide `spectrum: solid|duo|mono`, `accent` or `tone-edge` asks for one. In an editable PPTX or ODP the bar is one native shape.`collage bleed` no longer draws a bar border at the top, so its photos reach the top edge.
- On a portrait or square canvas, `safe` no longer lifts a `progress` chart's tracks and rows by the footer offset. Its selector `[class*='progress']` matched the chart's own `.progress-track` and `.progress-row` as well as the section-dot rail. It now matches only the rail.
- Decks that already set `spectrum-edge: left|right|bottom|off` move once: their content, header, footer and page number now sit where the default (`top`) placement puts them, a 4px move.
- In engines with CSS `round()` (Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 118, Safari 15.4) the bar's width is rounded down to a whole pixel, never below 1px, so the border and the padding that gives it up are equal. On a 1080px-wide canvas it was 3.375px, and the browser drew it as 3px.
- `npm run check:edge-shift` renders every component in light and dark with header, footer and page number on, once per bar placement, and fails if any element's position depends on the placement. `--variants`, `--classes`, `--each-class` and `--front-matter` extend it to manifest variants, modifiers, every reserved class and deck-level registers; `--positions` writes element positions so two builds can be compared.
- Export-to-Marp ships the runtime that injects the full-bleed bar (checked in a real marp-cli 4.3.1 render of the Marp kit, HTML and PDF). The vector PDF export paints the bar over a `collage bleed` photo, print mode fills it in gray on every placement, and auto-split no longer adds a closing page holding only the strips.
- The spectrum bar is now the top layer of the slide: a new `--z-spectrum` plane (110) sits above the stamps, the alarm tabs and every decorative mark, so nothing paints over the bar. Everything else sits clear of it: the default draft/confidential/wip tab hangs one bar width in from the right edge in every placement (4px further in than before), and the overflow tab sits one bar width above the bottom edge.
- A dark slide now places its content where a light slide does (4px lower than before), so a deck that mixes the two no longer steps at every change.
- A manifest `spectrum` style pin no longer overrides a deck-wide `spectrum: off`.
- The PDF export keeps a `collage bleed` photo as its embedded original under every bar placement instead of flattening it into the page raster when the bar touches it.
- `npm run check:edge-shift` also fails when text or chrome sits inside the strip the bar occupies, when a dark slide steps from its light twin, and for any of the thirteen stamp styles; the integration tier now runs it. `examples/spectrum-edge-cases.md` collects every edge case in one deck for the Studio.
- A `claim-bleed` chart's title, and a `claim-bleed` video's title and caption, keep the safe inset from the slide edge instead of starting on it (under a left bar, and colliding with the running header on a chart). The chart or video still reaches the edge. A dark `accent` slide also sits where its light twin does.
- A stamp or mark on `title`, `closing`, `divider`, `image`, `scene` and `collage bleed` sits one bar width below the top edge, so it never sits under the top strip an `accent`, `tone-edge` or deck `spectrum:` style draws (4px lower than before on those frames). The `fixme-tab` holds still under every placement, a `topic`'s track band is no longer removed by a left, right or bottom placement, and the PDF no longer draws a claimed chart's masthead rule across the bar.

- **Fixed: split frames no longer draw a double line across their top edge.** A
  sovereign split frame (`split-panel`, `split-compare`) suppresses every chrome
  Cell it declares, but the deck spectrum is a `border-top` on the `section`
  rather than a Tile, so `suppresses` could not name it — the ribbon painted
  directly on top of the component's own 3px accent bar, giving a 7px two-tone
  stripe over the featured panel that stepped down to 4px at the panel seam. The
  section border is dropped on both components and the edge is rebuilt as one bar
  of the ribbon's weight in two segments that meet at the seam: the panel's own
  `--panel-mark` over the panel, the deck ribbon over the supporting zone. The
  `metric` and `steps` opt-outs that dodged the double locally are retired, and
  the `watermark` panel takes `--on-accent-watermark` so its mark stays visible on
  an accent fill.
- **Fixed: the split frames' panel edge is no longer invisible on the achromatic palettes.** The panel's top-edge mark defaults to `--accent`, which on onyx, ardesia, concrete, atelier (and the five `a11y-*` palettes that import onyx) is the panel fill itself — onyx measured 1.00:1. A new `--panel-edge-mark` token carries the color, defaulting to `--accent` everywhere it already reads and to the curated `--spectrum-end` on those four; a per-palette override rather than a new global default, because the endpoint measures worse than `--accent` on mustard. Gated by the `split-panel/edge-mark` composed-contrast surface.

- A tinted logo on a split slide no longer repeats one `<filter id>` across the run's pages. Each continuation page now owns `deck-logo-tint-N-k` (the filter and the `url(#…)` that points at it), so `url(#…)` cannot resolve to another page's filter. Measured on a 5-page portrait deck: before, `deck-logo-tint-1` appeared 8 times; after, `-1`, `-1-2`, `-1-3`, `-1-4` appear twice each.

- The running header now renders on `split-panel` and `split-compare` slides. Frame chrome (`header`, `footer`) was `position: absolute` with no stacking order, so among positioned siblings paint order fell to DOM order — and chrome is emitted around the component's subtree, not above it. The header comes first and lost to any opaque part docked at the same corner; its strip rasterized to one flat color on every non-`mirror` variant of both families. `section header` / `section footer` now sit at `z-index: 3`, above component content and below the diagnostic tabs.
- Frame chrome over a `split-panel` or `split-compare` panel takes the ink of the field beneath it instead of the canvas ink, so revealing the header does not make it unreadable: `--on-dark-secondary` on the inverse panel, `--on-accent` on `watermark`, `--cat-on-fill` on a `cat-N` tint. `metric`, `steps` and every `mirror` form put canvas under the chrome and keep the ordinary muted ink. Verified across all 61 component galleries: 511 running headers and 504 running footers, with every panel-field case now clearing AA (5.47–13.90:1) and only the three intentional canvas cases below it, at the deck's existing muted-chrome level.
- **The running footer on those layouts was already illegible, and is fixed too.** `<footer>` is emitted after the component's subtree, so unlike the header it always won paint order and has always rendered over the panel carrying canvas ink — 2.44:1 on a `cat-3` tint, 2.76:1 on the inverse panel. Pre-existing, not a consequence of the stacking fix.
- A deck-level `header:` longer than roughly 25 characters runs past the panel's edge on these layouts and loses contrast there; keep it short or clear it per-slide with `<!-- _header: "" -->`.
- `build:galleries:check` and `build:bucket-galleries:check` now flag a PDF whose *render inputs* changed, not only its own markdown. They compared one mtime — the gallery `.md` against the PDF — so a CSS or engine change with no deck edit reported every gallery current; the on-dark ink release was entirely CSS and moved 424 slides across 122 galleries while this reported all of them up to date. They ask git what changed rather than reading the filesystem clock, which is wrong in both directions (a fresh clone stamps everything at checkout time; `git checkout <ref> -- themes` made 15 palettes look newer than every PDF with identical content).
- Corrected two claims about those checks: `lefthook.yml` said they "run in CI instead", and they are invoked by no workflow, hook or build step. They are on-demand scripts; `golden-diff` is the CI gate that watches these artifacts. `engineering/capabilities.md` now says so too.

- **`split-panel` and `split-compare` keep the running header and footer on their own field.** The chrome used to span the whole slide, so a long header crossed the panel seam in the panel's ink and vanished, and on `split-compare` it printed over the option cards. Each now ends at the edge of the field it starts on and holds one line, ending in an ellipsis past that, and the field keeps that band clear so a heading can't grow into it. A cut is reported to the author (the export's `CONTENT CLIPPED` line), with no reader pill, the same policy as the standard footer band.
- **A `finish:` now shows on split slides, on both sides.** Both panels used to paint opaque fills over the deck's backdrop, so a finish deck's split slides showed no texture, wash or mark. Now the side with the cards has no fill, so the slide's finish shows under it as on any other slide, and the feature panel is finished like an anchor slide: it keeps its solid field (dark stays dark, an accent or category panel keeps its color) and the finish is painted on it, mixed for that field in the screen and the PDF face alike. `backdrop: clear` clears behind the content on both sides and leaves the finish in their margins. The finish's corner mark is left off split slides, which have no frame margin for it. Decks without a `finish:`, and `finish-none` slides, look as before. A finish whose CSS a deck wrote itself before this change shows on the supporting side and leaves the panel plain.
- **The PDF writer keeps text vector over a layer stacked below it.** A text's ancestor with an absolutely positioned fill pseudo-element was always treated as covering the text, which pushed those words into the page image. A pseudo-element provably stacked under the text (its host is a stacking context and the text's branch takes a higher `z-index`) no longer counts.
- **`split-compare` no longer drops the footer, and `no-footer` / `silent` now hide a `split-panel` footer.** The transform used to discard `split-compare`'s footer and nest `split-panel`'s inside the right column, out of reach of the chrome modifiers. An author's own `<footer>` (a quote attribution, a source line) stays where it was written.
- **A `split-panel` quote no longer loses its text to the left panel.** With no lede above it, the export moved the quotation's paragraph into the panel as the lede and left an empty quote behind.
- **A `steps` slide's phase numeral no longer sits under the running header**, and `split-panel metric mirror` inks its header for the dark field it sits on (it read 2.2:1).
- **Inline code is readable on every `split-panel` field.** The chip took the dark panel's white ink on every variant but `metric`, so on a `steps` panel and on each `cat-N` tint — including a category run's split cover — it rendered white on a light fill (the formulas on `system-design-foundations` pp. 125 and 183). `steps` now keeps the ordinary chip ink, a `cat-N` tint takes `--cat-on-fill`, and `watermark` takes `--on-accent`.

- **A machine fix no longer edits a code fence.** When a slide quoted the wrong form in a fence above the real line (a fenced `<!-- _class: … -->`, a gantt span, a `- **Title.** body` card), the fix rewrote the fenced example and left the real line alone. That happened in "Fix all", in the editor's one-click fix and in `lint:deck --fix`. The fix now edits the real line and leaves the example as written. A `- **Title.** body` line inside a fence on a card, ledger, split or number slide is also no longer reported, because it is an example, not a card.

- **Fixed: nine lint rules no longer report a fenced example.** A fenced sample of a wrong form is documentation, and the engine draws nothing from it, but the five gantt task rules, `unknown-map-region`, `statement-ol-bold`, `check-label-code` and `video-bullet` flagged it. Each now skips a top-level code fence, so a fenced gantt task also no longer counts as a task a live `after=` can name, and a fenced `@video{…}` record no longer counts as the slide's clip. They skip only a fence the renderer certainly draws as code, so a stray fence line in a list item or a speaker note never hides the live lines after it.

- verdict-grid's one-column form (a tall deck, a narrow pane, a phone) follows the `cards:` register: `center` places a centered band, `top` a top band and `stretch` fills, where every card used to fill the stage whatever the register. A lone card on its own portrait page still fills it.
- A pane's `cards:` register now sets all four of its tokens, so `cards-stretch` fills a pane's one-column matrix-2x2 or verdict-grid, which it never did.

- Eight components no longer have their card chrome sheared off by the slide's content
  clip on a dense slide. `compare-prose`, `decision`, `redline` (the plain clause),
  `matrix-2x2`, `statute-stack`, `policy-recommendation`, `citation-card` (`pull-quote`)
  and `cycle` each held a content-height floor against the bounded stage, so the stage
  cut their bottom border, radii and filled panels while every word still fitted. Each
  fix is inert while the content fits, and a body that genuinely cannot fit still spills
  where the "Content clipped" warning reports it.
- `statute-stack preemption`, `cycle` and `citation-card split` no longer lose text off
  the TOP of a slide with no warning. Each centered a box that could overflow, which
  threw content off the block-start edge where nothing in the engine can measure it —
  53.53px of real text on `statute-stack preemption`, 21.02px on `citation-card split`,
  16.75px on `cycle`. On `cycle` the return arc and the repeat mark were falling below
  the clip too, so a loop rendered as a plain row of cards.
- `examples/gallery-jargon.pdf` and the committed `compare-prose`, `cycle` and
  `statute-stack` gallery PDFs are regenerated. All four were stale against the engine
  that renders them, so a preview diff on those decks was comparing against a layout the
  engine no longer produces.

- `stamp-mark` is a faint diagonal watermark again, not an opaque slab over the slide. Its word now shrinks to fit, so CONFIDENTIAL stays on the slide.
- `stamp-bar` now prints its state (DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL…) on the bar instead of showing a blank dark rectangle.

- A state chart drawn top to bottom by dagre no longer stacks the labels of a paired edge on each other. When two states are joined both ways (`{block, to=7}` and `{unblock, to=3}`), dagre now reserves room for both labels, and a label moves off another edge's line. The machine from the follow-up drew with 15 label collisions pinned to `tb` and now has none.

- `state-chart` now declares its key swatch (`fc-key-swatch`) in `kernel.marks`, matching `flowchart`, so a chart finish can be written against it and `node tools/chart-language-census.js --check` reports no disagreement (64 rendered mark classes across 26 members agree).

- An edge label on a re-ranked state chart no longer sits on a state box. The
  clearance the layout reserves is axis-aligned, so a label on a diagonal run was
  bounded by nothing — measured across the four state-chart demo decks, 3 of 118
  labels overlapped, and one pair rendered as the single garbled token
  `reject›lock`. A label whose box collides now slides along its own edge, and
  mirrors to the far side of the line if nothing on the home side is clear.
- On a machine where nothing fits — every edge carrying a long event name — some
  overlap is unavoidable, and what it gives up is ordered: never off the canvas
  (the text would be cut), never onto a state box (the state's name goes with it),
  so at worst two labels touch and both stay readable.
- The arc-length midpoint is tried first and kept whenever it is clear, so only
  labels that actually needed to move do: 3 of 38 pages changed across the four
  decks. The third is a label that was already hanging 1.1px outside its own
  canvas before this change, where the slide clips it — the walk now treats the
  canvas as a boundary and pulls it back inside.

- Chart labels on a portrait or square deck now scale with the deck's type. `--chart-text-min`, the floor under state-chart edge labels and ordinals and roadmap phase tags, was a fixed 11px while the rest of the type grew by `--canvas-scale`. The story-sized portrait gantt/state-chart demo deck no longer prints TYPE FLOOR: its edge labels were 10.8px against a 19.2px floor, and are now at least 24px. Landscape decks keep 11px.
- A state-chart self-loop label no longer sits on its own loop. The label now moves just clear of the arc. On landscape decks, labels that touched their loop now sit slightly above it (or below it, for a loop under the node).

- **Security:** `state-chart` parsing no longer backtracks quadratically on author text. Three patterns on the path a state's lead text and a transition's event label take had polynomial ReDoS reachable from any deck — including `stripTrailingPills`, which predates this work. A 32k-character label went from ~850 ms to under 2 ms, and the growth is now flat with input size.
- The transition-token lex no longer backtracks cubically — and until it did, the bullet above was **not true of the whole path it names**. `^\s*([^=]*?)\s*=>` divided one whitespace run between three quantifiers: flat on a match, cubic on a miss, and a nested bullet whose inline code is nothing but spaces is a miss. Measured across four doublings — 2k spaces 1,159ms, 4k 7,806ms, 8k 60,373ms, 16k 502,266ms, 32k **3,894,786ms (64.9 minutes, observed)** — a consistent ~8x per doubling. That is 4,577x the 851ms defect that motivated the fix above, in the same function, left in place by it. Now flat: 0.01ms at 4,000 spaces. The linearity suite drives the failing path too, which is the one that was ever slow.

- **Fixed: a capitalized status word on a `kanban` card now paints.** `AT-RISK` was accepted as a status but stamped verbatim, so neither the card wash nor the pill matched its color rule and both painted untinted. The card and pill now take the lowercase word's color; the pill still shows your spelling.
- **Fixed: a `progress` bar marked `pilot` or `decision` now matches its pill.** The pill took the informational color while the bar stayed on categorical slot 1, so the two disagreed on any theme whose slot 1 is not blue. The bar now takes the informational color too.
- **Docs:** the pills guide now says that `gantt` paints `live` in the informational color rather than the positive one. The other positions in its "Where the status word goes" table were checked against a rendered deck and hold.

- **The Studio chat names more failures correctly.** A model that drops mid-reply now says
  the provider had an error instead of "No reply came back". A request too long for the model
  says so instead of retrying as a one-shot that fails the same way. A rate limit between tool
  rounds says to wait instead of "the connection dropped", and a moderation refusal no longer
  says to reconnect. Stopping a turn while the model was writing an edit now records that
  round's cost. (`docs/src/components/studio/chat-agent.ts`, `ai/architect-model.js`)

- **The chat's cost estimate shows a question and an edit.** The header reads a range, such
  as "≈ $0.014–0.020", from the measured cost of a question and of an edit. It used to show one
  figure priced at the longest reply allowed, about three times what a question costs.
  (`docs/src/components/studio/ChatCost.tsx`)

- **The Studio chat says why a model request failed.** A failure such as a rejected key, an
  account out of credits, a model that isn't available, or a network error used to show
  "No change suggested.", because the chat retried as a one-shot request, which reports
  every failure as an empty reply. It now names the cause and what to do about it, and it
  retries as a one-shot only when the model refused the chat's tools.
  (`docs/src/components/studio/chat-agent.ts`)

- **Studio chat:** a reply in progress now always says what it is doing. A status line under the Architect's text names the phase on every turn ("Thinking…", "Reading slides…", "Drafting the edit…", "Writing…") and admits a long silence, replacing the bouncing dots that showed only on the first turn and the pulsing bar that looked stuck.
- **Studio chat:** replies render Markdown tables (scrolling sideways on a phone), keep numbered lists numbered across blank lines and nested items, and render quotes and rules.

- **Fixed: copying and pasting in Compose no longer strips a slide's component.**
  A slide's `_class` rides the slide node's `directives` attribute, and the
  schema's `toDOM`/`parseDOM` pair — which is the clipboard contract, since
  ProseMirror serializes a copied slice through the schema rather than the node
  view — did not carry it. Select the deck, copy, paste, and every slide came
  back as an unstyled `content`: seven boardroom components gone in two
  keystrokes, with nothing on screen to say so. The attribute now bridges through
  a `data-directives` attribute on both the schema and the live node view, so a
  DOM re-read recovers it too.
- **Fixed: a folded slide in Compose stays folded.** Collapse was re-established
  by ProseMirror node identity, which carries it through an in-Compose slide op
  and through nothing else — so the rail's add / duplicate / move / delete and
  the add-slide gallery, which all rewrite the deck source, unfolded every slide
  on the resync that followed. Collapse is now restored across a re-import by
  matching each folded slide's source chunk, so it follows its slide through a
  reorder and survives an insert above it.
- **Fixed: an inserted table is one you can see.** The starter table was built
  with empty cells, which serializes to `|  |  |` and renders as two hairlines —
  invisible on a dark slide, and indistinguishable from a button that did
  nothing. Its header cells now carry `Column`.
- **Changed: Compose withholds the "Insert table" control on the 46 layouts where a
  table competes for the stage** — every chart, the diagram, code and math slides,
  the fixed grids and card anatomies, the two-sided comparisons, the picture and
  contact slides, and the bookends. It stays on the 15 where a table belongs: the
  catch-all `content`, the open list-flow layouts, and the four whose table IS the
  content. The measurement behind it: adding one three-row table costs `quadrant`
  45% of its figure height, `diagram` 36%, `piechart` 36% and `code` 35%, while the
  table itself occupies only ~20% of the slide — and on `quadrant` the engine
  reports the figure's labels dropping below the legibility floor. This withholds a
  control, not a capability: typing or pasting a table still works and still
  renders.
- **Fixed: deleting the slide you are editing lands on its neighbor.** The caret
  had no slide to re-anchor to, so the selection mapped to the end of the
  document and both the caret and the preview jumped to the last slide — walking
  you to the back of the deck each time you cleared a slide.
- **Fixed: inserting a slide from the gallery puts the caret in the new slide.**
  The rail moved and the preview painted it, but the caret stayed behind, so the
  next thing you typed went into the previous slide.
- **Fixed: a locked slide's "edit in Markdown" badge is no longer clipped by the
  delete cap.** The one piece of chrome explaining why the slide will not take a
  keystroke was cut off mid-word.
- **Fixed: pasting a multi-slide clipboard can grow the deck.** Compose's
  structural guard tells a deliberate cross-slide edit from an accidental
  Backspace-merge by reading the selection — the right question for a keystroke
  and the wrong one for a paste, where the author declared intent by putting
  slides on the clipboard. Every multi-slide paste was rejected silently, so
  there was no way to duplicate a section. The guard now exempts a paste — and
  only a paste — after the locked-slide check it still may not bypass.
- **Fixed: a slide pasted from an external page cannot inject directives into
  the deck source.** Slide directives ride the clipboard so a copied slide keeps
  its component, and `parseDOM` matches `section.cs-slide` in any pasted HTML —
  so a crafted page could put a `_backgroundImage` beacon, or a newline-forged
  slide boundary carrying a `<style>` block, straight into the deck source and
  the exported file, with nothing visible in the editor. Pasted directives are
  now believed only when they carry this session's provenance token and are
  shaped like a single-line directive comment.
- **Fixed: restoring a fold no longer snaps the preview to the first slide.** The
  transaction that re-applies folds after a re-import carries a fresh selection,
  which the editor reported as a cursor move — so the preview jumped to whatever
  slide that selection landed on, every time the rail added, moved or deleted a
  slide. The restore is now excluded from the cursor-crossing signal: it changes
  what is folded, not where you are.
- **Fixed: folding a slide next to an already-folded one no longer unfolds the
  neighbor.** The toggle matched any decoration overlapping the slide's start
  position, and a slide's fold decoration ends exactly where the next one
  begins — so folding two adjacent slides in turn unfolded the first and left
  the second open.
- **Fixed: the locked-slide badge no longer collides with the delete confirm.**
  Clearing the resting trash cap was not enough — arming the delete expands the
  group to "Delete? ✓ ✗" and re-clipped the label. The badge now stands down
  while a delete is pending, which is the one moment "edit in Markdown" is not
  the advice that matters.

- **Fixed: the Studio's Webpage export no longer ships a second set of font faces that cannot
  load.** The player removed the deck sheet's own `@font-face` rules only when they were spelled
  `url(fonts/…)`, the CLI's form; the Studio's `url(/playground/v/…/fonts/…)` slipped through, left
  eight `error` faces in Chromium and Firefox, and blocked the identical-file font merge. One rule now
  covers both hosts. The `examples/html-player.md` export drops from 918,858 to 735,536 bytes and is
  pixel-identical in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. The CLI's output is unchanged.

- **Fixed: the Studio editor's loading status is now reachable in the accessibility tree.** `EditorSkeleton` wrapped its whole subtree — including the `sr-only` "Loading the editor…" status span — in `aria-hidden="true"`, which removes the entire subtree from the accessibility tree, so the status was invisible to assistive tech. `aria-hidden` now sits on the decorative gutter/line blocks only, and the status span carries `role="status"` outside it, mirroring the `ComposeSkeleton` fix that shipped alongside it in #1727.

- On a deck that splits on headings (the default), a `---` slide with two headings and one picture under each now shows both pictures as placed in Compose, and the Studio's photo-contrast check reads them. Before, the Studio saw one slide with two loose pictures and placed neither, while the rendered deck placed both.

- **Fixed: reopening the deck settings or Present's slide overview no longer grows memory on
  Safari and iPad.** Each reopen used to rebuild the preview thumbnails inside them, and WebKit
  never gives a torn-down preview back: the deck settings' preset tiles made 8 new documents
  per reopen (+197 MB over six reopens), and the overview 14 (+260 MB). Both now stay loaded
  after their first open and are only hidden when you close them, so a reopen builds none. They
  still open fresh, at the top, with nothing left expanded, and their previews still scroll
  with the panel.
- **Fixed: closing a panel on a phone no longer pops up the hint of the button that opened
  it.** A hint now appears on keyboard focus and on hover, but not when a closing panel
  hands focus back after a tap.

- **Fixed: switching the Studio from a wide window to phone width keeps you on your slide.** The switch rebuilds the
  editor, and on a busy device the rebuilt editor could start from a slightly older copy of the deck than the one you
  had just typed. The editor and the preview then jumped back to the first slide. The rebuilt editor now starts from
  the newest text.

- **Fixed: the Studio now warns about a mistyped deck setting that `lint:deck` already
  flagged.** Before, the Studio editor and the Coach checked six of the deck's
  fixed-choice settings. Fifteen others went unchecked, including `guards:`, `cards:`,
  `claim:`, `corners:`, `pace:` and the `spectrum-*` family. So `guards: strcit` got no
  underline in the Studio and no Coach penalty, although the editor autocompleted the
  correct value. `buildVocabSets` now passes every setting's value list to the linter,
  so the Studio and `npm run lint:deck` report the same warnings.

- **Studio:** the Architect chat no longer hangs the page while a reply streams. Each streamed frame re-rendered the whole panel and re-ran the sanitizer over every earlier reply, so the cost grew with the length of the thread: at 4x CPU throttle a fifth turn produced hundreds of long tasks against 6 on the first. The reply being written now repaints alone, settled replies are never re-rendered, and the paint rate backs off when frames get expensive. While a reply streams, the transcript follows it only while you are at the bottom, so you can scroll up and reread; it returns to the bottom when the reply finishes.
- **Studio:** the live preview no longer keeps the browser busy after it loads. A deck with no diagram ran a 60 Hz frame loop for ten seconds after every preview rewrite, waiting for a Mermaid library it did not need; an idle Studio now schedules no frames at all (about 180 frame callbacks in 3 seconds before, 0 after).
- **Studio:** a collage photo now pops and its neighbors recede when the mouse is over it in the live preview, as they already did in the Playground. The preview box takes no pointer events, so the host now hit-tests the pointer and marks the photo (`data-host-hover`), the way code-block copy buttons already worked. The code-block marker also stops rewriting an attribute that has not changed on every mouse move.

- The Studio's Export to Marp now carries a deck's sample pictures. It fetches each `sample:` file the deck names, front-matter `logo:` included, into the bundle's `assets/` and points the deck at it, so a team-profile slide's portraits and the sample deck logo render in Marp. A sample the site cannot serve keeps its reference, and the export still drops any other relative `logo:`. The CLI's Export to Marp and the Studio's now share one definition of which references a bundle localizes.

- Studio chat: the context ring and "Used" figure now measure against the model you have selected, not the model that wrote the last reply, so switching to a larger or smaller model updates them at once.

- **Fixed: edits typed in the last moments before leaving the Studio are no longer lost.**
  Editor writes ran on a 400ms debounce, and leaving the page *cleared* that timer
  rather than running it — so the browser's back button, a bookmark or a closed tab
  dropped whatever you had just typed. The deck now writes through on `pagehide` and
  on a hidden `visibilitychange`.
- **Fixed: a deck you only looked at is no longer saved as if you had edited it.**
  Opening the Studio and leaving wrote a stored source for the active deck. That row's
  existence is what tells Lattice a deck carries edits, so it pinned a built-in sample
  to the copy shipped the day you first visited — later releases' improvements never
  reached it — and it armed the "back up your work" nudge for people who had done none.
- **Fixed: the Studio's top bar can no longer be left hidden after a phone keyboard
  closes.** The bar collapses while you type on a phone; nothing cleared that state if
  the window then widened to a desktop layout, leaving the Studio with no top bar and
  no way to bring it back.

- **Fixed: Studio status messages no longer pile up.** Every transient
  confirmation minted its own toast and the Toaster showed three at once, so
  anything that spoke twice inside the 2600ms dwell stacked — measured at three
  pills on the real Studio for three confirmations in a row. Status messages now
  share one Sonner id and rewrite a single pill in place, and the stack is capped
  at two so the worst case on screen is that pill beside one toast carrying an
  action (Undo, Reload), which keeps its own slot rather than being replaced by
  unrelated text.
- **Fixed: a Library bundle import reports its outcome in one message.** Refusals
  went out in a loop, one toast each, so a bundle carrying four bad scenes raised
  five pills at once and buried its own success line. The import now raises a
  single message with the refusals named beneath it.
- **Fixed: a Library import that fails now says why.** The funnel named the real
  reason and then overwrote it with a generic line in the same tick, so a corrupt
  file reported as an empty one. The reason is the headline, with whatever did land
  underneath it.
- **Fixed: a settings Undo no longer leaves a dead button on screen.** Two settings
  writes inside 5s left two Undo toasts, and the older one's action was already
  guarded off — it did nothing when clicked. The previous Undo is retired when the
  next one is raised.

- Studio: every docked pane (Settings, Coach, Chat, Live, Reader views, Library) now sits on one background, the same as their phone and tablet sheets, so the side column no longer changes tint when you switch panes.
- Studio: after the window shrinks and grows again, the side panels go back to the widths you left them at, or to the defaults if you never dragged a divider (a docked pane used to come back at 371px instead of 320).
- Studio and Playground editors: `<!--` and `-->` show as typed, no longer drawn as arrows by the font's ligatures.

- PDFs exported from the Studio now list `Lattice Studio` as their author instead of the retired `Lattice Drawing Board`.

- Tapping a result in the Studio's phone search now runs it. Before, only Enter worked: the tap took focus from the search field, the panel shrank by 54px, and the result slid out from under your finger.

- The Studio no longer freezes after a deck with phone photos lands in the editor. Every reader of the deck skipped
  nothing: the lint, the Coach, the engine's render and the preview's checks each walked every character of each photo's
  base64. They now skip it and put it back in what they return, so findings, fixes and exports are unchanged; the
  editor shows each photo's data as a small chip with its size; and the editor's lint and the Coach's assessment run off
  the page's thread. On a deck of three phone photos in Firefox, the longest freeze fell from 29 s to under 1 s after
  pasting it, and from about 6 s to about half a second after a keystroke (about 1.5 s when the keystroke is on a
  photo's own line).
- Every docs page that loads the engine downloads 4.7 KB less (gzipped). The engine carried the whole typed-glyph table,
  advice text included, for one question it asks of it; it now carries only the set of glyphs, built from the same table.
  The table moves to the Studio's lint, which loads later.
- The Share dialog's PDF options no longer show the Resolution control twice for a 4K deck. Two of its controls shared one
  React key, so a re-render could keep a stale copy beside the new one, and the Download button sat under it.

- The Studio's Webpage (HTML player) export now draws every chart in the **Read · Article** view in color. Before, a radar, pie, bar or heatmap painted solid black, and kanban, progress, roadmap and timeline charts lost all their styling. The view lifts each chart out of its slide, and the Studio handed the player a stylesheet that scoped every chart rule and palette token to the inside of a slide. The engine now returns that stylesheet in the CLI player's shape as well (`render(…, { styles: 'flat' })`), so the two export paths style Read · Article the same way. Slides render as before (278 before/after slide captures, light and dark, showed no change).
- The same Studio Webpage export now themes the player's own chrome and the Read · Article page from the deck's palette, as the CLI player always has. In dark mode both used to stay white.

- **Fixed: the Studio's Webpage export no longer shows a reader the authoring overflow marker.**
  Every player the Studio made carried the author level. A deck with a clipped slide reached its
  reader with the red ring, an "OVERFLOWS" tag and a "Fix Me" chip, where the CLI's player shows a
  calm "Content clipped" pill. The export now bakes at the workspace's overflow-marker setting
  (`reader` by default), and the CLI and the Studio run the same cleanup on the baked slides; moving
  that cleanup into a shared function left the CLI's output as it was.

- The Studio's **Download as webpage** player no longer styles a `<section>` you nest inside a slide as a slide of its own. It took the slide's 1280×720 box, clipped with `overflow: hidden`, and inside a `dark` slide painted as a white panel. The Studio player, the Reading view, `check:render` and the CLI export now unwrap the engine's flat sheet through one function, `unwrapFlatSheet` (`lib/export/unwrap-flat-sheet.mjs`), so the Studio and CLI players style the same deck the same way.

- The Studio’s first slide appears about 0.9 s sooner on a phone. Its preview frame was not marked as a preview, so the runtime downloaded every declared font face (28 files, including the emoji subsets) before revealing the slide, and the reveal waited out its full 1.5 s font backstop. The frame now waits only for the faces the slide uses, as the Playground's frames already do. Measured on the throttled phone profile over HTTP/2: slide visible at 5.8 s before, 4.9 s after, with 28 fewer requests.
- Present's audience Stage reveals sooner for the same reason: it now waits only for the faces its slides use rather than every declared face.

- The Studio preview no longer refuses a slide whose body quotes a section tag. A comment such as `<!-- <section class="title"> -->` made the slide read as "nested or unbalanced `<section>`", and the preview showed "This preview couldn't render" in place of an ordinary slide. The preview's section count now reads past comments and `<style>`/`<script>` text.

- The Studio preview no longer refuses a slide with a section tag inside a quoted attribute, such as `<p title="<section>">`. It counted the tag as a real one and showed "This preview couldn't render" over an ordinary slide. It now counts sections with the same walker the engine uses.
- The Playground preview no longer cuts a slide short at a `</section>` quoted in an HTML comment. It paired each section with the next close tag, so it patched half a slide into the live preview.

- **Fixed: the Studio's Reading view draws every chart in color.** Radar, bar, heatmap and
  quadrant charts used to paint solid black there, and kanban, progress and roadmap charts
  printed as plain text, because the view shipped no deck stylesheet. It now ships the deck's
  styles, cut down to the rules its charts use and kept off the app around the article, in
  light and dark.
  Theme fonts, animations and remote images do not carry into the view, so a shared deck
  cannot restyle the app or fetch from it.

- **The Studio refuses a plugin package by name instead of dropping it.** Importing a zip that held
  a plugin with no code imported nothing and said nothing; one with code was refused as "a plugin
  package is data". Both now get the refusal `lattice packages add` gives, from one shared string:
  plugins are in-tree only until the plugin zip channel ships.
  (`docs/src/components/studio/package-zip.ts`, `lib/packages/plugin-refusal.js`)

- **The Studio's pre-paint shell drew an EMPTY column where the Craft activity rail goes, so a
  reload at Craft on desktop showed a blank 52px strip beside a fully-drawn top bar until the
  island mounted.** The band itself was placed correctly — the seed publishes `--sh-rail` for
  desktop-Craft only — but it shipped as `<div class="ssr-band ssr-activityrail"></div>` with
  nothing inside, so hydration dropped seven panel launchers in at once. The rail is now the
  app's OWN control set at build time: it moved out of `StudioShell` into
  `chrome-parts.tsx` as `ActivityRail`, beside `BarIcon` and `PostureDial`, and both surfaces
  render that one source — the app with live panel state, the shell with every panel closed,
  which is the state the app boots with at every stop. The control-parity matrix now compares
  three chrome regions instead of two (`.ssr-activityrail` against
  `nav[aria-label="Studio panels"]`), so a launcher added to the rail and not to the shell
  fails on the first run; verified to bite by re-emptying the band, which names all seven. A
  new `@minfont` parity case at 1280x720 covers the one case where identical markup was not
  enough: at a raised browser minimum font size the rail's captions push its natural height
  (690px) past its column (666px), and only the app's rail shrank to fit — the shell's flex
  column floored the nav at its content height and the band clipped the rest, leaving the
  account chip 20px low. `min-h-0` on the shell's nav restores the app's box.

- The Studio's loading screen now shows the deck's size and slide count ("16 : 9 · 7 slides") before the app finishes loading, when it can be sure which deck will open. On a phone this brings Lighthouse's largest-paint time for /studio/ back from about 14 s to about 5.6 s; it had regressed when Undo and Redo joined the phone header (#2085).

- **Fixed: the Studio's top bar no longer jumps when the page finishes loading.** The
  pre-paint shell drew its header in the fallback font and re-laid it out when the
  webfonts arrived, so the deck-name pill — which sizes itself to its text — was about
  42px too wide until then, and the divider and Read/Write/Craft dial after it slid
  when it corrected. The two font files the bar paints with are now preloaded.
  Measured on a throttled connection: the deck title settles at its final width
  immediately, where before it shifted 41.9px.
- **Fixed: the Studio's editor toolbar no longer appears all at once when the page
  finishes loading.** The pre-paint shell drew the editor's sub-bar as a single
  placeholder while the app's own bar carries eleven controls, so the band under the
  header filled in — and grew — at hand-off. The shell now draws the same controls the
  app does at the same width. Measured on an iPad Air 4 in both orientations: 12 of 12
  controls present in portrait and 11 of 11 in landscape, each within 1px of where the
  app puts it, where before the shell drew 1.
- **Fixed: the Studio's top bar no longer slides sideways when the page finishes loading.** The
  pre-paint shell reserved space for the deck's slide count using a width measured once against
  one deck — 53px against a real 56px — so from 1280px up the Read/Write/Craft dial and
  everything after it jumped 3px when the app took over, and a deck with a different number of
  slides moved it further. The slot now reserves a fixed width that both the shell and the app
  take from one shared constant, so it no longer depends on the deck. The same change stops the
  preview bar's counter widening as you page from slide 9 to slide 10.

- Studio split panels now share one size contract: every docked panel (Settings, Chat/Coach/Live/Lenses, Library, tablet Inspector) is at least 280px, opens at 320px and drags to 480px, and the editor takes 46% of the editor|preview pair whenever a panel opens (dragging, or resizing the window, scales them from there; a resize fold and unfold restores them). Before, docks opened at their minimum (260 and 200), the editor share drifted to 41%, and at 1100px desktop and 820px tablet every panel squeezed under its own minimum, clipping the chat composer.
- When Settings and an assistant panel are open on a window too narrow for all four columns, the editor folds to its rail instead of squeezing the other panels, and unfolds when a panel closes or the window grows; "Expand editor" on a folded editor closes a dock to make room.
- The Library header's search field now shrinks, so the Import button no longer clips at the dock's default width.

- The Studio and the Playground no longer hang on their loading screen when you open them in the minutes after a site deploy. The site's host lets a browser reuse a page for up to ten minutes, and each deploy deletes the previous build's scripts, so a reused page asked for scripts that were gone and the Studio sat on its placeholder until you reloaded. The page now notices the missing script before the app starts, checks that a newer page exists, and switches to it once.

- **The Studio writes its live preview once on a first visit.** A second render that started while the first write was still loading used to write the whole document again, which parsed the 1.2 MB sheet twice at cold start (14 of 23 loaded first visits on `main`). It now waits for that write to load and patches it: 24 of 24 loaded first visits write once. On a slow device (Chrome's CPU throttled 20x) a first visit writes once and shows the slide 6.2 to 7.8 s after the first write, against three or four writes and 7.7 to 8.3 s on `main` (four logged runs each).
- **The chat chip names your OpenRouter model on a slow start.** When the Studio read the chat status before the model catalog had loaded, the chip showed only the tail of the model's id ("Model") until you opened it. It now fills in the catalog name and price when the catalog arrives.

- The Studio no longer slows down as saved work piles up. Opening a deck used to read every saved version of every deck into memory, and to read and parse every deck's text just to name it in the deck list. Now a deck's versions load when that deck opens, and the list takes each deck's name from a small record written whenever the deck is saved. Measured on the built Studio at 4x CPU slowdown with 40 decks of 25 versions each: first slide 3,442 → 2,564 ms, memory 177 → 97 MB. Details: `engineering/decisions/2026-11-11-studio-storage-pointer-records.md`.
- A deck save the browser refuses, most often because its storage is full, now tells you so with a notice that stays until you dismiss it. It used to fail silently, and your latest edits were lost on reload.

- The Studio's code editors, its chat code blocks and the public Playground editor now paint keywords, strings and numbers from a derived **syntax ink tier** (`--syntax-keyword-ink` / `-string-ink` / `-number-ink`) instead of `--pass`, `--warn` and `--accent`. Strings and numbers are seeded from each palette's own `--hljs-*` code color — so the editor and the deck's rendered code panel agree on what a string looks like — and every role is solved onto the editor's own canvas: worst 4.65:1 against `--bg`/`--bg-alt` across all 18 base palettes in both modes. Reading `--hljs-*` directly would have been worse than the status tokens: 21 of 36 palette-modes put a raw syntax color below AA on the editor canvas, worst 1.01:1.
- **Editor keywords and Markdown headings are legible on every palette.** They were painted with `--accent`, which carries no contrast guarantee against the canvas: mustard/light read at 3.89:1 and burgundy/dark at 4.60:1. The other 34 palette-modes are visually unchanged, because a seed that already clears comes back untouched.
- **On `a11y-achromatopsia` the editor painted number literals byte-identical to comments** — the shipped `--warn` and `--text-muted` are both `#6E6E6E`, on the one palette with nothing but lightness to separate anything with. The string and number inks are now held apart from each other and from the text roles.
- On the four `a11y-*` palettes the string/number seeds come from that palette's own `--pass`/`--warn` pair rather than `--hljs-*`, because the inherited syntax pair (green 144° / yellow-green 104°) sits on the red-green axis those palettes exist to avoid. Achromatopsia gets its deliberate two-step grayscale. The emitted values there are therefore the status colors themselves — the decoupling below applies to the 14 hued palettes, not to those four.
- Retuning the status trio no longer repaints code on the hued palettes. Demonstrated during this change's own rebase: #1704 moved `--pass`/`--warn` on six palette-modes, which under the old code would have silently repainted string and number literals in the Studio's editors — from a PR about the surfaces components compose, with no editor in its diff.
- The Anima scene prompt no longer teaches `var(--text)`, a token the engine does not declare. The recommended scene palette is a real list the prompt is generated from, gated against the engine's own declarations, so a phantom token cannot be taught again.

- **Typing in the Studio no longer stutters on a slower device.** Each keystroke used to re-render the whole Studio before the next one could land. At phone-class CPU speed, every key was a long task of about 160-200 ms. The editor now hands its text to the rest of the Studio as a low-priority update that yields to the next keystroke, and a burst of typing renders once for its newest text. Measured at 4x CPU over 40 keystrokes: long tasks 42-46 to 14-15, main-thread time 23-30% lower. Undo still records every edit exactly as typed.

- **Fixed: three `cards-stack` bodies in `examples/system-design-foundations.md`
  spilled past their card onto the card below.** A stack card is a fixed height,
  so a body that wraps to a second line paints that line over the next card's
  border — and nothing catches it: the slide still fits the frame, so the
  export's overflow oracle stays green and `lint:deck` only ever warns. Measured
  on this deck at this size, a body of 115 characters sets on one line and 117
  wraps; the three that spilled ran to 117, 124 and 147.

- **Fixed: a table's last row no longer draws a rule into the slide's own chrome.** Every
  `td` carries a `border-bottom`, so the final row's hairline was the table's outer bottom
  edge — measured 25.5px above the below-note hairline on `compare-table`,
  `statute-stack.lane` and a stage-filling plain table, and 25.0px on `obligation-matrix`.
  Two rules that close together with nothing between them read as one thick doubled line.
  The rule is now cleared on the table's visually last row, taking the clearance to
  133-135px;
  `glossary` and `math.derivation` already did this and are unchanged. `roadmap` and the
  `obligation-matrix` `heat` / `asymmetric` variants are deliberately untouched — in those
  a cell's bottom border is structure (a grid, a bracket rail, a card box), not a row
  separator, so clearing it would leave the last row open. A `<tfoot>` row, a `<tfoot>` placed before the
  `<tbody>`, a trailing `<thead>` and a second `<tbody>` group all behave correctly — the
  rule follows the row that renders at the bottom, not the last one in the source.

- A table too long for its slide or pane now keeps its header row and clips at the bottom. It used to be centered past both edges, so a 24-row table lost its header and first five rows, on a `table` slide and in a table pane alike. A table that fits is still centered, and every committed deck renders byte-identical.

- **A `terms:` entry is read the way YAML reads it, and lint says when one is ignored.** An unquoted key with a space (`Oct. Tenth: October Tenth`), a one-line `terms: { … }` and a `# comment` after a value now work; before, the first two were silently ignored and the comment was spoken. A field the reader does not know (`pronunciation:`, `say:`), a list item or an empty entry is reported by the new `terms-entry-ignored` warning, which names the field that was meant.
- **A deck's dotted phrase term is said as declared.** `"Oct. Tenth": October Tenth` was cut into two caption cues before terms were matched, so it never applied.
- **An abbreviation's period is not spoken as a full stop.** `Oct. 10` read "October. ten", with a pause in the date.
- **Built-in terms take plurals, possessives and compounds** (`APIs`, `CEO’s`, `KPI-driven`), as a deck's own terms do, and a plural never doubles one the expansion has (`OKRs` read "objectives and key resultss").
- **Heatmap narration names each cell by the label the chart draws.** A label with a lone `*`, `~`, an entity or a backslash escape was read differently, so the Guide could not find the cell, and `2*3 grid` was spoken "twenty-three grid".
- **`10 a.m.` reads "ten A-M" on the on-device voice, not "ten uh em".** A spelled letter `A` before another word was read as the article. Clock times (`10 a.m.`, `10 AM`, `9:30 pm`, `(10 AM)`) and the `A` in a dotted initialism (`U.A.E.`, `B.A.`) now reach the voice as letter names, in a list as well as mid-sentence.

- **Fixed: a theme that merely MENTIONED another palette in a comment inherited the whole thing.** A header comment reading `/* … like @import 'onyx'; but warmer … */` made the engine splice `onyx` — and the base scaffold behind it, 768 KB of composed output — into a theme that declared no parent, and since comments are stripped afterwards, the rest of that sentence was left behind as live CSS, read as a selector, and swallowed the rule following it (a theme's own `@font-face`, in the case that surfaced). The Theme Studio puts a user's free-text description straight into that comment, so any description mentioning a palette by name was enough. The engine no longer reads a theme's comments as imports; bytes outside an import directive come back as they went in, and composed output is byte-identical for all 32 shipped palettes at every size.

- **Fixed: on onyx-dark, the `topic` slide's lit tab now stands off the shelf beside it.** The
  shelf is the dark band lifted toward the display ink, and on a pure-black band that lift
  came out at `#161616`, so the black tab separated from it at only 1.16:1. The shelf now
  never falls below oklch lightness 0.34, which puts onyx-dark at 1.79:1. The floor also
  lifts mustard-dark, burgundy-dark, atelier-dark and carbone-dark slightly (each gains
  contrast); every other palette and every light palette renders as before.

- **Graph charts:** a live preview with no layout worker (a host that blocks blob workers, a worker that died, or dagre not loaded yet) now settles from a cold fit after the author pauses, so its drawing at rest matches the export, as the worker path already did.

- A `</section>` quoted in an HTML comment no longer cuts a slide short for five more slide transforms. Logo walls kept their raw `<img>` marks, obligation matrices drew no key, scene slides split their caption, and image slides wrote the text panel's closing tag inside the comment, so the panel never closed. A word cloud after a slide that quoted `<section` rendered as a plain list. All five now walk the shared section walker.

- **Fixed: the annotation register now reaches every layout that renders a below-note, up from 15 of 36.** An italic-only trailing paragraph (`_Source: …_`) renders as an annotation — the drawn `✦`, a dotted rule, label-size muted text. That register was a hand-enumerated opt-in union of seventeen layouts in `base.modifiers.css`, written three times over, while the below-note it decorates is opt-out. Measured through the emulator, one probe slide per component: 19 layouts that take a below-note silently rendered an annotation as an ordinary one instead — including `content`, which is what every un-classed slide resolves to. Two of the seventeen names (`timeline`, `principles`) are not components but VARIANT classes, so the union was also reaching across an axis it never declared. The register is now keyed on the `.below-note` wrapper the kernel emits and names no component, so it shares `rendersBeat` with the published `authoring.blocks` contract and the two sets cannot drift apart again.
- **Fixed: `diagram` and `big-number` render a below-note and an annotation.** Both withheld the trailing paragraph via `coda.claims` to protect anatomy they do not render. `diagram` claimed it for a `.diagram-caption` that no code path emits — what actually caught the paragraph was diagram's *dek* rule, so the author's closing sentence set as a second dek at the foot of the slide; the dead rule is deleted with the claim. `big-number` had no rule matching a trailing paragraph at all. Three further candidates were examined and keep their claims: `matrix-grid` and `state-chart` use that paragraph as their swatch `legend` (dropping the claim harvested the legend into the band and the chart lost it), and dropping `math`'s docks the band inside its equation grid at half width.
- **Fixed: a trailing italic note on a split page no longer takes the wrong size.** The split envelope carried a rule whose 16-arm `:not()` chain mirrored the annotation enumeration by hand, to size the em-only notes that enumeration missed. With the register universal there is nothing left to miss, and a stale mirror would have out-specified the register itself. Both copies (`lat-split-native`, `lat-split-cards`) are gone.
- **Fixed: `<!-- annotation: … -->` is documented as what it is.** `base.docs.md` described it as a corner overlay and `design/forms.md` mapped it to the `overlay` Cell. It renders nothing on any layout — the text is swallowed by the speaker-notes channel — so the claim is retired from both, and the `annotation` Tile manifest no longer reports `status: shipped`.

- `journey` now holds at conference and hall: at those venues not even one stage fit, because the mood band and curve stayed full size while the legend grew. A venue now tightens the band (the faces and plumb lines follow), and the legends no longer inherit a 1.6 line height.
- `progress`, `gantt`, `journey`, `matrix-grid` and `math` carried "scales to the box" exemptions that were false: each clips when it has too many rows at a larger venue. They now declare a per-venue budget (`venueCapacity`), so `lint:deck` warns, and a `venueProbe` that `check:venue-conformance` verifies at all four venues.

- `collage` holds its description at hall (its text column was a fixed 30% and held no words; it now widens with the venue). `progress` no longer cuts its percentage with its own bar track at conference and hall. `matrix-grid` no longer cuts its rotated row-axis title on a short grid. `closing qr` and `divider qr` put the code beside the heading on a wide slide and size it from the venue floor, so it is never narrower than a back row can scan.
- `logo-wall`, `citation-card`, `columns` and `rows` carried "nothing to count" exemptions that were false: `logo-wall` holds 8/8/4/4 logos across the four venues, a `citation-card` holds 117/79/55/31 words, and the two hosts hold small panes at hall. Each now declares what it holds and a `venueProbe` the conformance harness verifies.

- `contact` and `wifi` now hold at every venue and canvas. At `venue: hall` the card used to lose its QR code, phone and URL (the name alone filled the frame), and on a portrait canvas the Wi-Fi fields collapsed to slivers. The cards size their geometry in slide units and fit their text to the column, and the QR code is never narrower than the venue's floor (10 / 12 / 16 / 22% of the slide width).
- At the default (laptop) venue the Wi-Fi heading is a little smaller (64px to about 50px, now beside the code instead of full width) and the `split-panel qr` code tile is about 11% narrower (250px to 223px), because both now share the venue-aware code sizing.
- A phone extension ("ext. 23") no longer becomes part of a `qr: tel` code, and `venue-prose` ignores speaker notes and fenced code when it counts an `image` or `collage` slide's words.
- `contact` drops the accent rule before the title and stacks title and organization on two lines instead of joining them with a dot; the `wifi` caption no longer has a bullet before it.
- `contact` sets the organization in the body face, mixed case and the heading color, under the accent-colored tracked title, so the two no longer share one style.

- **Fixed: a lesson's Exit button works while a sheet is open.** Over the Share sheet, Exit was drawn but took no clicks, and a press on it went to the share row underneath. The sheet now leaves the walkthrough layer alone.
- **Fixed: lesson and tour captions are easier to read and to close on a phone.** At phone widths the caption text is 15px instead of 13.5px, and Exit takes a press anywhere in a 44px square, the touch-target size, while its drawn circle and the bar keep their size. Desktop and tablet are unchanged.

- **Vetrina — `bounds: 'host'` no longer strands Exit off screen.** The chrome is now confined to
  the VISIBLE part of the host (intersected with the window), falling back to the window when the
  host is scrolled out of view. A host taller than the window — a panel in a scrolling page, which
  is the case the option exists for — previously seated Exit up to 638px above the top of the
  window, where it could not be pressed; Exit is pointer-only, so that removed the only escape
  from a running tour.
- **Vetrina — a voiced narrator now docks the caption at the edge** rather than anchoring it to the
  cursor. A voice removes the reading trip the balloon exists to save, and what is left is a
  subtitle, which belongs at a fixed screen position. It also removes a stale anchor: a voiced
  caption never hides, so it was placed once per beat and then sat up to 493px from the pointer it
  was speaking for.
- **Vetrina — a self-dismissing caption is budgeted by reading time, not by the pacing model.**
  `caption: 'cursor'` against the default `pacing: 'legacy'` erased an 8-word line after 1900ms
  where a reader needs 3500ms. The new `Pacing.dwellMs` is the grounded rate under both models.
- **Vetrina — a caption never outlives its beat.** `instant` and word-cued (`at`) beats left their
  line standing, and the balloon then re-anchored beside the cursor on every later beat with
  nothing to say. A hold no longer survives a throwing `act` either.
- **Vetrina — `Narrator` gained an optional `dispose()`**, and `voicedNarrator` implements it,
  closing the `AudioContext` only when it created one. Building a voiced narrator per run leaked
  one context per run against a per-document cap. Both track caches are now bounded.
- **Vetrina — `gesture` records what it aimed at**, so the caption's avoid list holds the ink just
  drawn rather than the previous beat's target. `setVoiced` is now `destroyed`-guarded like every
  other stage verb.
- **Vetrina — the caption no longer comes back carrying the previous beat's line.** `say()` swaps
  the words 140ms after the call, and a performance ending inside that window revealed the bubble
  still holding the last caption, beside the new beat's cursor — measured at 96% opacity for 134ms.
  Intermittent, because it is a race against a timer.

- **Vetrina — a cue now scrolls its target into view before it points at it.** Nothing in the
  stage scrolled except the drop target of a drag, so a `point()`, a drag's pick-up or a gesture
  aimed at anything below the fold sent the cursor off-screen and played the beat to an empty
  viewport. Every verb now reveals its target first — `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline:
  'nearest', behavior: 'instant' })`, so a target already in view moves nothing and a host's
  `scroll-behavior: smooth` cannot turn the landing into a race between two animations. Two
