  deliberate exceptions: `wave` and `shake` play at the cursor and ignore the target they are
  handed, and a cue silenced through `theme.cues` draws nothing, so neither scrolls. Under
  `bounds: 'host'` the dock is re-seated after a scroll the stage performed itself.
- **Studio — the demo's typing follow asks the editor to scroll, instead of guessing which
  element does.** Typing on a phone goes through the controlled `setSource` path, which moves no
  caret and so never scrolls; the compensation set `scrollTop = scrollHeight` on
  `#studio-pane-editor .cm-scroller` — an extent CodeMirror may not have measured yet, on an
  element that is the scroller only while the editor is the height-constrained box.
  `EditorHandle.revealTail()` hands both questions to CodeMirror, which measures its own document
  and walks the real scrollable ancestors. Measured behavior is unchanged on both engines reachable
  here (worst gap between the document's end and the visible box across the whole phone tour: 0px
  on Chromium at 390px, 53px on real WebKit at an iPhone box — the same before and after), so this
  removes a fragility rather than a visible defect. It also wires up a path that had no follow at all: the
  desktop `set`, which `runner.ts` reaches for an `instant` beat, the `still` motion tier, an insert
  over ~1600 characters, or a prefix reset. No shipped tour takes that path, so it cannot be
  driven end to end; the typing channel is now a module of its own (`demo-typing.ts`) whose wiring is
  unit-tested on both channels, and the mutant that is the old state dies to that test.

- The reader view now carries the sentence under a video slide's heading. The article re-hosted only the video's poster, so the lead paragraph of a `video` or `video companion` slide was dropped even though narration read it.
- The finish backdrop now lands on slides only. The injector found sections with a pattern match, so it wrote a backdrop layer into an HTML comment that quoted a finish section, and into a `<section class="finish">` an author nested inside a slide. It now walks the slides the way every other render pass does, and the live runtime skips nested sections to match.

- `video` slides keep the deck's running header and the slide's footer. The `companion` composition used to rebuild its slide from the title and lead alone and dropped both, along with any eyebrow above the title.
- A `gallery` video no longer renders inside the masthead band. Every `video` composition now keeps its title, with its eyebrow and subtitle label, inside the card and sits in the frame's stage cell like `wifi` and `contact`, so the band never claims the title.
- The video figure no longer carries the browser's default 40px side margins, which pushed a default-composition slide past its frame.

- **Fixed: `setEditorContent` appended to the deck instead of replacing it on the
  `webkit-phone` e2e project.** Playwright resolves `ControlOrMeta` against the OS the test
  process runs on (Linux, so `Control`), while CodeMirror resolves `Mod-` against what the
  page reports — and the iPhone user agent puts it in Mac mode, where `Mod` is Meta and a
  bare `Ctrl-a` moves the caret to the line start instead. The select-all missed, so every
  deck a spec set landed on top of the one the Studio had already loaded. The helper now
  presses, checks the real selection, and takes the other modifier if the first did nothing.
  `webkit-tablet` was never affected: it reports a Mac user agent but CodeMirror keys off
  `navigator.platform` and the UA's `Mobile/` token, neither of which that project carries.
- **Fixed: tagging a `@crosswidth` spec `@webkit-phone` silently dropped it from the desktop
  project.** The `desktop` project's `grepInvert` read `@webkit` as "mentions webkit", so a
  spec that gained a WebKit run traded away the desktop run it already had. It now reads
  "webkit-exclusive", which leaves every webkit-only spec routed exactly as before.
- **Changed: the two render-target lint arms now also run on real WebKit at iPhone 15 Pro.**
  Their oracle reads a painted box and asks CodeMirror which document line sits under it, so
  it is engine text layout — the class a Chromium project cannot stand in for.

- **Accessibility, website:** the component reference's active nav item rendered its label in `--accent` on an `--accent` pill — a 1:1 contrast ratio, an invisible label — on the default palette. An unlayered `a { color: var(--accent) }` in the docs stylesheet was beating the layered Tailwind utility meant to color it, so every link in that nav ignored its own ink token. Fixed at all five call sites that had drifted off the token bridge's declared pairing.
- **Accessibility, website:** the Playground shipped with no `<main>` landmark, no `<h1>`, and two toolbar rows in no landmark at all; the Studio shipped with no `<h1>` on any of its four shells. Both now have them.
- **Accessibility, website:** scrollable code blocks and Markdown tables were reachable only by pointer at phone width, leaving anything past the right edge unavailable to a keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1). They are focusable now.
- **Accessibility, website:** the site menu's current-page row measured 4.47:1 (label) and 3.80:1 (description), and its close button was a 16×16 target under a mouse — below WCAG 2.2's 24×24 minimum. All three fixed; the same close-button floor is raised on the shared Dialog.
- **Accessibility, website:** inactive tabs used a 60%-alpha ink that measured 2.46:1 in light mode. They now use the muted text token, which is gated.
- **Accessibility, decks:** `--text-muted` — the ink for the running header, running footer and pagination counter on every slide — was the one text role the theme contrast audit never scored, its AA standing asserted only in a comment. It is now gated against both the canvas and the card in all 32 themes.
- **New gate:** `docs/e2e/axe-site.spec.ts` runs the WCAG 2.2 A/AA rule set over 12 site routes at desktop, tablet and phone widths in both color modes, plus the site menu open. An exact 1:1 contrast ratio — which axe reports as `incomplete` rather than a violation — now fails.

- On Windows, when a render with a code package or npm plugin runs out of time, Lattice no longer kills the sandbox browser by its process id. By then Windows has usually ended the browser already and may have given that id to another program, which Lattice could have killed instead. Lattice now stops the processes that name the browser's temporary profile folder, its helper processes included, and then removes the folder. It falls back to the process id only when that search cannot run.

- **Windows: npm plugins are no longer refused because a renderer was still starting.** The code sandbox reads Chromium's `chrome://sandbox` page to confirm its OS sandbox is on. A renderer that is still starting is listed there as not sandboxed for a moment, and one such reading made the sandbox measure OFF, so the npm plugins in a deck were refused on a machine whose sandbox was on. It now reads the page again and counts a renderer as unsandboxed only when it stays that way, as every renderer does in a browser started without the sandbox.

- A split-panel point whose title carries its own bold run (`- **6** again`) no longer leaves a `<strong>` open on the split page. The split now reads the title as a balanced element, so later slides stop rendering bold, the export finds every slide again, and the title keeps its trailing words ("6 again", not "6").
- A `<style>`, `<pre>`, `<textarea>` or `<script>` block closed with a space before the bracket (`</style >`) now ends at that tag. It used to run on, swallow the next `---`, and merge two slides into one, so a lens export could show a withheld slide's body under the next slide's lens tag.
- A front-matter key nested under a block, such as a lens named `footer` under `lenses:`, is no longer read as the deck's directive. That lens registry used to print in every slide's footer and could overwrite the real `footer:`.
- When a deck's front matter repeats a top-level key, Lattice now reads the **last** one everywhere, as the engine always rendered it. That covers the shared front-matter readers (every register such as `finish:`, `motion:` and `class:`), the linter, the Studio, the CLI export's `size:`, `style:` and `logo:`, the Export-to-Marp `class:` and `paginate:`, the color-mode band, block keys such as `lexicon:` and `say:`, the Studio's own front-matter reader and writer (so its controls show and edit the line that counts), and the Studio's lens list; they used to read the first. The render-target keys (`fluid:`, `player:`, `present:`, `read:`) keep their deliberate rule, on if any line says on. A top-level line now also beats a nested one of the same name. `key :` (a space before the colon) counts as the same key, as it does in YAML. `lint:deck` warns on each earlier line (`duplicate-key`), since the deck ignores it. The writers act on every copy too: resetting a setting in the Studio ("Theme default", motion off, a preset) removes every top-level copy of its key, clearing the plugin list removes every `plugins:` line, rather than letting an earlier one take effect again, and the auto-glossary and heading-split exports strip every `glossary:` and `split:` line, so a re-import does not add a second glossary. `--print` export collapses every `color-mode:` line into `color-mode: print`, `color-mode :` included.

### Security

- **Fixed a cross-site-scripting hole in the slide runtime.** The verdict-grid and obligation-matrix badge transforms read their label with `textContent` — which decodes entities — and wrote it back with `innerHTML`, re-parsing markup the sanitizer had deliberately neutralized. A table cell in a shared or AI-generated deck could run script in the Studio/Playground preview origin. Both now build the badge with DOM APIs, so there is no parse step.
- The Playground's last-slide snapshot now guards its **stylesheet** as well as its markup (HARD RULE #22). The snapshot's CSS is produced by serializing the live CSSOM, which normalizes the `<\/style` escape back into a live element terminator, and it crosses `localStorage` into the top docs document. Guarded at both captures and the storage boundary; no real stylesheet's bytes change.
- New `checkRuntimeMarkupSinks` gate: every place `lib/runtime` writes markup into the live preview frame must declare where that markup comes from. A new injection point — or a second one hiding behind an already-legitimate one — now fails the build instead of landing silently.
- New behavioral coverage for the Mermaid render path on the real Playground: nine script shapes that must not execute out of a node label, the `click … javascript:` vector, and the `<br/>` line break in node labels that `securityLevel: 'strict'` was once wrongly believed to cost.
- New behavioral coverage for an imported theme's CSS reaching the Studio preview's `<style>`, driven through the real Library import.

- The docs site's dev dependency tree now resolves `brace-expansion` at 1.1.18, picking up the v1
  backports for CVE-2026-13149 and GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg. It reaches the tree only through
  `minimatch`, so nothing the Lattice package ships changes; the bump landed by hand because
  Dependabot's own PR for it (#1489) has been unable to regenerate itself since 2026-08-10.

- **A shared deck can no longer add fake slides to the exported player.** A slide that carried its own `<div class="lp-frame">` or a nested `<section data-lattice-slide>` made the `--player` export count extra slides, show a fragment of one slide when Next was clicked, and play the next slide's narration over it. The player now finds its slides only inside its own stage, and the exporter frames only top-level slides. Every player export's script, and so its CSP hash, changes; markup and styles do not.
- The browser check for forged player chrome (`npm run verify:narrated-player`) now runs every night, and its two checks that could not fail now assert what the player actually bound.

- **A Studio tab coming to the front no longer writes deleted data back.** After "Delete Everything" in one tab, a second Studio tab that missed the wipe broadcast rewrote its crash-sentinel session record, deck title included, the moment it became visible. The visibility handler now checks the durable wipe mark first, as the resume, page-cache and heartbeat paths already did.

- **Fixed: a `</style>` in a deck's CSS no longer breaks out of the exported document.**
  The CLI's page scaffold embedded three caller-supplied stylesheets — the palette, the
  `--css` layout sheet, and the deck's own front-matter `style:` block — raw in one
  `<style>` element. A `<style>`'s content is HTML RAWTEXT, so it ends at the first
  `</style` even from inside a well-formed CSS comment: the element truncated (3,632
  bytes lost in the measured case, about 3,400 of them the engine's own layout rules) and
  the remainder was parsed as markup. In the emitted `.html` an injected
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="…">` fired a cross-origin request the moment a recipient
  opened the file; in a `--player` export the assembler harvested that `<link>` into the
  shipped artifact, so it rode in every copy. Every `<style>` the emulator builds from
  caller CSS now runs it through `sanitizeStyleText`, which escapes only the element
  terminator. **Exported bytes are unmoved:** no stylesheet in the 179-sheet committed
  corpus contains the sequence, and the guard returns its input by identity — the `.html`
  and `.pdf` for two demo decks in light and dark are byte-identical before and after.
- **Fixed: the Studio's "Download as webpage" shipped the same beacon.** Its CSS prune
  (`player-prune-browser.ts`) is the browser twin of the CLI's and re-wraps pruned CSS into
  a fresh `<style>`. `prunePlayerCss` is a css-tree parse→generate, and css-tree normalizes
  `<\/style` straight back into a live terminator — so the guard applied where the document
  was assembled was undone at the re-wrap, in a document that is mounted in a same-origin
  frame and then handed to a recipient. Both re-wraps now re-sanitize.
- **Fixed: two more `<style>` blocks spliced into shared markdown carried the same hole.**
  A saved library theme's CSS (`embedThemeInMarkdown`) and a library component's CSS
  (`componentBlock`) are embedded in the markdown a recipient receives, in byte-identical
  shape to the finish block beside them that was already guarded. Rendering the theme
  block's own output through the CLI produced a live `<link rel="stylesheet">` and turned
  the theme's remaining CSS into markup. Both now guard the whole element body, since the
  theme/component name rides in the comment header and is free text too.
- **Changed: the HARD RULE #22 stylesheet gate now covers the export pipeline.** It scanned
  `docs/src` alone, so `lattice-emulator.js` and `lib/export/**` were not checked at all. Its
  roots are the three shipped document assemblers, and a new per-site check catches a
  `<style>` rebuilt from css-tree-pruned CSS — the shape a document-assembly marker cannot
  see. The one entry in `SANCTIONED_STYLE_SINK_EXEMPT` is gone: the export player's generator
  is guarded, so the exemption had become a sanction for a fix that already landed.
- **Added: `npm run test:diagnostics` and `npm run test:runtime`.** Both directories had
  tests but no `test:<scope>` script, so a commit staging only files in one of them failed
  the pre-commit hook with `Missing script`. A test now asserts every `test/unit/<dir>` has
  one, so the next gap fails a test rather than someone's commit.

- **Theme and component CSS can no longer break out of the element it is embedded in.** A
  Theme Studio theme's `label` and `description` — free text, model-populated in the normal
  flow — landed unescaped in the emitted stylesheet's comment header, and that sheet is
  concatenated into a same-origin, un-sandboxed preview `<style>`. Because a `<style>`
  element's content is HTML RAWTEXT, a `</style>` carried in CSS text ended the element and
  the remainder was parsed as markup in the live frame — script execution in the origin that
  holds the user's own OpenRouter key. Closed on both sides: the serializer neutralizes the
  CSS comment terminator in both fields (losslessly — no character is dropped), and every
  module that assembles a document now passes its stylesheet through the new
  `sanitizeStyleText`, which escapes the element terminator and nothing else. Verified
  pre/post on the shipped bundle in Chromium 131. (#1709)
- **The same guard now covers the Share → Webpage export.** Its self-contained document is
  mounted in a same-origin frame inside the docs site before it is downloaded, and a
  `</style>` in saved component CSS could pull an external stylesheet into that origin *and*
  bake it into the shipped file. The embedded-fonts block and the baked-finish `<style>`
  spliced into exported markdown are guarded too. Exported bytes are unchanged for every real
  deck — the guard returns its input unmodified unless the CSS actually contains `</style`,
  which none of the repo's 179 committed stylesheets does.
- **HARD RULE #22 and its `build:check` gate now cover the stylesheet channel**, not just the
  markup one, and discovery is keyed on assembling a whole HTML document rather than on the
  preview-frame idiom — which is what let the export assembler slip past.
- **A caller-supplied `--css` layout sheet's `@import` is no longer lost to a comment opener
  inside a string.** `flattenCssImports` scanned with a naive comment regex, so `content: "/*"`
  earlier in the sheet swallowed every `@import` up to the next real comment close and the
  parent silently did not inline. It now uses the same comment walk the rest of the engine
  does — which also learned that `url(…/*…)` and a string ending at a raw newline (including a
  form feed) are not comments. The import grammar is unchanged.

- **Security: a downloaded `.html` or `--fluid` deck no longer phones home when someone opens
  it.** A deck's remote image, `<video>`, `url()` in an inline style, or a webfont its front matter declared fired on the
  **recipient's** machine, on every open, leaking their IP and confirming they opened the file —
  measured at two requests per artifact. Both now carry the same narrow policy the docs-site
  preview frames use, and it lives in one shared kernel so an author's preview and their
  reader's file cannot disagree. The exported `--player` was already contained. The deck's OWN
  local images and its math fonts still load — measured on Blink, Gecko and WebKit, counted at a
  real socket rather than through a devtools hook, and pinned nightly on the two non-Blink
  engines. WebKit is the strict one there, which is the engine that matters for this question.
- **Unchanged on purpose: PDF, PPTX and PNG still fetch.** There the request happens on the
  exporting author's machine and the recipient receives baked pixels, so containing it would
  blank a picture the author asked for and buy the recipient nothing. The policy is applied
  after rasterization, so those bytes do not move.

- **Security: the Playground preview's remote-subresource containment is now measured on the
  real app.** The narrow CSP that stops a deck beaconing out of a preview frame shipped with
  its Playground round trip unverified — asserted on the assembled document, never driven
  through the running Playground. It is now driven: 4 outbound requests with the meta removed,
  0 with it, the payload still in the frame's DOM both times. Pinned by
  `docs/e2e/preview-remote-subresource.spec.ts`.

- **Fixed: a deck can no longer beacon the viewer out of a preview frame.** A slide's image —
  a markdown image, a raw `<img>`, or `url()` in an inline style — made the docs-site preview
  fetch an arbitrary external URL on open, leaking the viewer's IP and User-Agent and
  confirming they had opened the deck. Every preview-frame document now carries a
  content-security policy closing images, media, fonts and connections to same-document
  sources. Script and style loading are unchanged, and no deck this repo ships references a
  remote image. **Exports are deliberately not affected**: the Studio's offscreen render frame
  for Download PDF / PPTX / PNG opts out, so a deck's remote image still resolves into the file
  you download, exactly as it does from the CLI. The boundary is that a preview is a surface
  you browse, while an export is a file you asked for.

- **Fixed: an exported player no longer advertises that a deck had speaker notes.** With
  `--strip-notes` the note text was already gone, but the player still answered the `n` key
  with a sheet reading "No notes for this slide." — telling the recipient the notes had been
  there. The button, the panel and the key now appear only when the file actually carries
  notes, which is also the honest chrome for a deck that never had any.
- **Fixed: the shared-file manifest no longer records whether `--strip-notes` was used.** Its
  `notes` field was set from the FLAG, so a deck that never had a note reported `true` and only
  a stripped one reported `false` — a one-bit answer, in plain base64 at the bottom of a file
  you email to someone, to "were there notes here?". It now describes the artifact: a stripped
  deck and a note-free deck both report `false`. Applies to the CLI export and the Studio's
  "Download as webpage" alike.

- **Fixed: `--strip-notes` no longer ships the speaker note in the `.pptx`.** The PowerPoint
  writer received the notes array as authored rather than the stripped one, so the note
  survived in `ppt/notesSlides/*.xml` — the one format whose native viewer shows it to anyone
  who opens the file. Two sibling leaks went with it: a `--raster` or `--paper` render wrote
  the unstripped note to its `<out>.notes.txt` sidecar, and that run's log line reported the
  notes it had just removed.

- **A string spelling `/*` could blank an exfil payload out of the component
  gate.** Every scanner in `lib/layout/gate.js` blanked comments with a naive
  `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//` — the exact regex `lib/core/css-comments.mjs` exists to
  abolish. Comments and strings are not independent layers, so a
  `content: "/*"` paired with the next real closer and blanked everything
  between: `gateCss` returned **zero findings** over CSS carrying both a remote
  `@import` beacon and a remote `url()` exfil, in the gate that decides whether
  CSS reaches a same-origin preview frame holding the user's OpenRouter key. The
  scanners now read comments through the canonical walk.
- **The CSS safety scanners moved to `lib/core/css-scan.js`**, shared by the
  component gate and the new theme gate. Reaching them through the component gate
  pulled a 41 KB manifest schema into the theme browser bundle for two regex
  scanners that know nothing about components.
- **`findCssExfil` no longer reports against the wrong line** when a stylesheet
  carries CSS escapes (it was counting lines in the shortened decoded copy), and
  both scanners index line numbers once instead of per finding — a 260 KB sheet
  went from 9.4s to 45ms, and a 20 000-statement paste from 17.2s to 0.5s, in
  scanners a live editor runs on every keystroke.

- **Security: an imported `.zip`'s CSS is checked before it is stored — themes and
  components both.** A shared `.zip` is the one path in the threat model where the
  author and the victim are different people, and it reached storage with no CSS gate
  at all. The component arm was the wider half: hostile component CSS reaches the same
  same-origin preview `<style>` and every export, and the intended workflow — import,
  then insert the skeleton — is what fires it. A finish needs no gate by construction
  (its CSS is discarded and regenerated from the clamped recipe).
- **Refused per item, not per bundle.** The whole import used to sit in one
  `try`/`catch`, so one bad asset silently dropped every asset after it *and* left the
  shelf unrefreshed, which read as "nothing happened". Each refused item is now named
  with the reason, and everything else still imports.
- **Only unambiguous off-device fetches refuse.** A theme missing a contract token, a
  token whose *name* contains `javascript`, or a component class called `.javascript`
  all import as before — the exfiltration rules are what veto: a remote `url()`, a
  remote or unresolvable `@import`, `expression()`, `-moz-binding`.

- **Security: a theme import the registry cannot resolve is dropped, not hoisted
  to the top of the composed sheet.** `ThemeStore.resolveThemeImports` leaves an
  unknown or cyclic theme-name import in place, where CSS ignores it — but
  `composeCss`'s `hoistImports` then lifted every surviving quoted import to
  position 0 precisely so it would survive the "@import must come first" rule.
  At position 0 the browser resolves a bare name as a relative URL and fetches
  it, so composition turned a reference the registry had already declined into a
  live request. The judgment decodes CSS escapes first, so `@import '\61 rdesia'`
  — which the raw-byte resolver cannot match but the browser reads as `ardesia` —
  is dropped too. Real `@import url(…)` and quoted-path imports still hoist
  unchanged, and all 32 shipped themes compose byte-identically.

- **Three defects found by CodeQL on deck input are fixed.** Stripping the `debug` attribute took time that grew with the square of a deck's whitespace (over a second for 60,000 spaces); it is now linear. A chart's speaker-note detail turned an author's literal `&lt;` into `<`. The Playground's front-matter panel wrote a value ending in a backslash in a form that swallowed its own closing quote; a value holding `\` or `"` is now written in a quote form the engine reads back unchanged (single quotes, or raw double quotes when the value holds an apostrophe).
- Nine chart and slide helpers that strip tags from labels now strip to a fixed point, and four regex builders escape every special character. Neither changes the output of a real deck; both close CodeQL findings (#1958).

- The Playground's engine, KaTeX and fence-grammar loaders now refuse a script URL that is empty, carries a quote, an angle bracket, a backtick, a backslash or whitespace, or resolves off the page's own origin and scheme, before it reaches a `<script src>` or `import()`. Only the resolved URL is injected. This closes the CodeQL `js/xss-through-dom` paths through the preview's build-time asset URLs; a well-formed same-origin asset URL is unaffected. The notes mask's raw-text HTML-block end test (`<!-- strip-notes -->`) was rewritten off a regex while kept byte-for-byte in agreement with markdown-it, so note stripping is unchanged.

- **Security: `--strip-notes` no longer says which slides had notes.** The export used to
  remove each note's comment node from already-rendered HTML and leave the whitespace behind,
  so a stripped slide carried exactly one byte more than the same slide written without a
  note. The shared player ships the deck's own scrubbed source for re-import, so a recipient
  could re-render it, diff, and read off which slides carried a note (never what it said).
  The flag now scrubs the source and renders that, so the exported slides are byte-identical
  to a deck written without notes. Both export paths changed — the CLI and the Studio's
  Webpage export.

- **`--strip-notes` no longer ships notes written inside a list item, a blockquote or a broken code span.** The code mask read a fence in a list item, a code span that crosses a line break, and an HTML block nested in a container as code, so a real speaker note there shipped and the audit stayed silent. `maskCodeRegions` now asks the engine's own markdown-it parser which comments are live and gives those back to the scrub and the audit. Measured over 100,000 generated documents: 1,278 hidden live notes before, 0 after (the scrub too, with an unclosed `<!--` shown in code ahead of the note); the 3,927 other markdown files in the repo mask exactly as before.

- **Fixed: `--strip-notes` / `--strip-captions` no longer leave a blank line where a comment
  ended the deck.** A whole-line note or caption comment at the end of the source lost its own
  line but left the blank line above it, so the scrubbed source shipped one byte the same deck
  written without the comment does not have — in the player envelope and in the PDF
  `--embed-source` attachment. End-of-file counts as blank on the right, but it is the file
  ending rather than a line that can be taken, so "one of the two blanks goes too" took neither.
  At end of input the whole trailing run of blank lines now comes off, from either side: there is
  no block below for any of it to be separating, and a trailing blank is itself the anomaly —
  1318 of the 1325 markdown files in this repo end with a single newline. Measured against the
  repo's own hand-written note-free twin fixture, which the scrub had been missing by exactly
  that byte — under both cuts, so it was never the `preserve`/`drop` tie-break's to fix, as it
  had been recorded.
- **Fixed: the Markdown attached to a PDF by `--embed-source` is scrubbed under a cut measured
  on the document it actually ships.** The boundary was measured against the re-rendered source
  (after the Mermaid pre-render and the auto-glossary append) and then applied to the author's
  original, which is deliberately a different document and which the fidelity guard never
  checked. Nothing in the tree was affected — of the 45 markdown files that carry a comment and
  get pre-processed, the two cuts produce identical bytes on every one — so this closes an
  unguarded join rather than a shipped artifact. The check short-circuits on that equality, and
  only renders to measure when the choice could genuinely change what ships.

- **Security: a video URL is matched on its parsed host, so a foreign origin can no longer wear a provider's badge.** The `video` component resolved its provider by testing the whole URL for a substring, so a provider name anywhere in it counted — including in a fragment or a query. `https://evil.example/#instagram.com/reel/X` resolved as Instagram, and because TikTok and Instagram use the author's URL verbatim as their watch target, the slide rendered a "Watch on Instagram" badge and a **QR code encoding the attacker's origin**. Provider rows now declare their hostnames as data and the parsed host is matched against them. A player `src` was never affected — those have always been rebuilt from the parsed video id.
- **Changed: the video provider table is one registry, `lib/core/video-providers.mjs`.** The static render (poster link, provider badge, QR target) and the parent-hosted playback lightbox each carried their own table with their own id regexes, so adding a provider meant two edits in unrelated trees and missing the second silently degraded playback to "opens a tab". Adding a provider is now one row, read by every consumer. Merging the two also folded in what each knew separately: a YouTube `live/` link now plays in the lightbox, and a `youtube-nocookie.com/embed/` or `instagram.com/reels/` link now resolves on the static path.
- **Security: a video URL's watch target is re-serialized, so a QR scanner cannot reach a different host than the one we checked.** A backslash ends the authority under the WHATWG URL standard (every browser) but is userinfo under RFC 3986, so `https://instagram.com\@evil.example/p/X/` passed the host check and was then used verbatim as the poster link **and the QR payload** — which a phone parses with its own URL library. The target now comes back out of the parser that validated it.
- **Fixed: a video URL with no id in it no longer renders a dead link and a dead QR.** A channel page, playlist or profile built a truncated `…/watch?v=` target. It now falls back to the URL the author wrote, which the verified host makes a real link to that provider. A mixed-case hostname (`https://YouTube.com/watch?v=…`) hit the same truncation and now resolves, as does a fully-qualified name with a trailing dot.
- **Fixed: a test helper escaped dots but not backslashes when building a regular expression.** Caught by CodeQL (`js/incomplete-sanitization`). Nothing was exploitable — the input is a hostname — but the partial escape is replaced by a complete one.
- **Security: video id extraction no longer matches a hostname with a regular expression.** Each extractor embedded its provider's host in an unanchored pattern, so `instagram\.com\/p\/` also matched `https://evil.example/instagram.com/p/x` — harmless in place, because the host had already been established separately, but a redundant check that is wrong on its own. Extraction now reads the parsed path and query, which also removes an unbounded `.*` from the YouTube matcher.

- A component package whose sample slide (`gallery.md`) loads anything from the network is now refused on import — by the Studio's Library and `.lattice` import and by `lattice packages add`, `check` and `list` — with the URL in the message. The check renders the slide through the engine and reads what a browser would load: images, `<image href>`, `url()` in styles, the `logo:` front matter key, a component's own poster, Mermaid image shapes, and remote link reference definitions. Links, relative paths and `data:` images are still fine, and every shipped gallery still imports. Fabricate warns about it live while you edit a component.
- Motion art (`art` / `poster`) no longer keeps remote references: `<image href>`, `<feImage href>`, `xlink:href` and remote `url()` values are stripped when a scene is saved and again when the Library reads it, so a scene saved before this fix is drawn without them too.
- `lattice` now depends on `parse5`, the HTML parser behind jsdom, for that check.
- A component's sample slide may not use, in a Mermaid diagram, any construct that can load a resource — an image shape, an HTML media tag, a `click` directive, `url()`, `themeCSS`, `@import`, `//` or an entity code — nor contain an `iframe`, `object`, `embed` or other nested document. These are refused whatever they point at, instead of by URL spelling. No shipped gallery or example deck uses any of them.
- A component's sample slide may not carry script: an inline `<script>`, a script whose `src`, `href` or `xlink:href` is a `data:` or `javascript:` URL, an `on…` event handler, a `javascript:` link, or a `<meta http-equiv="refresh">`. An empty script loaded by a relative path, as the shipped diagram gallery does, is still allowed.

- **Security: a component's sample slide may load only Lattice's own vendored scripts.** An
  empty `<script>` with any relative `src` used to pass the import gate; in the Studio that path
  resolves against the Studio's own origin. The gate (the Studio's Library import and
  `lattice packages add` alike) now allows only the vendored Mermaid, dagre and runtime builds
  and refuses any other script source. No shipped gallery or tracked deck is affected.
- **The CLI's offline render is now tested against a live proxy listener.** The resolver rule
  behind `--allow-remote`'s default also stops the browser reaching the proxy port at all, and
  a new integration arm fails if the rule is removed.

- **Security: a workspace backup from someone else now meets the same import gates as a Library
  zip.** Restore used to save every theme and component in a backup straight to the Library, so
  a backup file someone sent you skipped the CSS and sample-slide gates. Restore now checks each
  item: a theme or component that would reach the network is skipped and named in the restore
  message, and every deck and every other item still comes back. A `.lattice` file's deck and
  manifest are now read under the same size budget as its packages, so an archive that
  understates an entry's size can no longer make the Studio inflate it in full.

- **A code package's worker can no longer load a font, so a font load can't carry data out.** `new FontFace(name, 'url(…)').load()` and `self.fonts.load(…)` reached a loopback server from the worker in Playwright's Gecko build (Firefox 142), where the frame's content-security policy (`font-src data:`) did not hold, just as it had not for `EventSource`. Stock Firefox 156 applied the policy to both. `FontFace`, `FontFaceSet` and `self.fonts` are now removed with the worker's other network tools, so the wall no longer depends on the policy for them: both reach nothing in stock Chrome 154, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6, and in Playwright's Chromium, Gecko and WebKit builds. A package that loaded a font in its worker now gets "FontFace is not a constructor"; the guide never offered that, and `kit.measure` still measures with the installed fonts.
- The worker's network tools are now removed from every prototype above its global, not only from the global. Chromium defines `fetch`, `importScripts` and `indexedDB` on `WorkerGlobalScope.prototype`, not on the global, so the old wall only shadowed them and `WorkerGlobalScope.prototype.fetch.call(self, …)` reached them (the policy still stopped the request). `navigator.storage` and `navigator.storageBuckets` go too, and the wall checks itself: a package does not load if any name survives.

- **A code package can no longer hold a dynamic `import()`.** `import()` is syntax, so the worker's wall, which removes names, could not take it away; it rested on the frame's content-security policy alone, and with no policy it reached a local server on Chromium, Gecko and WebKit. Lattice now parses a package's `transform.js` (with acorn, as the script the worker runs) and refuses one that holds an `import(…)` call when you add it, list it, render with it, and when the Studio imports it or runs it. The word in a string or a comment is fine. A transform that does not parse is refused too.
- **Nothing in a code package's worker turns a string into code.** `eval`, `Function` and the `constructor` of every kind of function now throw an `EvalError` when called (they still exist, so `Function.prototype` and `instanceof Function` keep working), `ShadowRealm` is gone, and `setTimeout` and `setInterval` throw when handed a string. Code built at run time therefore cannot bring an `import()` back. None of the shipped code packages used any of them. Measured with no content-security policy at all, the worker now reaches nothing in Playwright's Chromium, Firefox and WebKit builds or in stock Chrome 154, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6.
- `acorn` is now a runtime dependency of the CLI (it was a development one).

- **Security: the vendored Mermaid is now 12.3.0, so diagram labels go through DOMPurify 3.4.17.** Mermaid 11.17.2 bundled DOMPurify 3.4.12, which five published advisories still cover (GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7 critical, GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr high, three low or moderate). The CLI export's render page moves to `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` 12.2.0's, and ZenUML to `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml` 1.0.1. ZenUML still bundles DOMPurify 3.3.1, because no ZenUML release carries 3.4 yet.
- **Diagrams keep the drawing they had.** Mermaid 12 changed its own defaults: every diagram drew in the new `neo` look, flowcharts and state diagrams laid out with elk, nodes got a 120-unit minimum width, mind maps turned into top-down trees, and swimlanes would have lost their lanes. The engine now states `look: classic`, `layout: dagre`, `minNodeWidth: 0`, a radial mind-map layout and the swimlane layout, so the diagram gallery renders as it did on 11.17. An author's own `%%{init}%%` still overrides each of these.
- **Block diagrams draw by hand on a sketch slide.** Mermaid 12 draws `block` through rough.js, so `mode: sketch` and `_class: sketch` now reach a block diagram's shapes, as they already did for flowcharts, state, class, ER, mind map, requirement and C4.
- **Use-case diagrams take the deck's font.** Mermaid 12's `usecase` diagram has its own font keys; the engine sets them like the other families'.
- **A theme pinned inside a diagram section is honored.** Mermaid 12 reads `%%{init: {"flowchart": {"theme": "forest"}}}%%` as a pin, and the engine now stands its palette down for it, as it already did for a top-level `theme`.

- **The Studio's Compose editor takes the `prosemirror-view` paste fix.** `prosemirror-view` 1.42.1 had a paste-handling XSS (GHSA-c8x8-7fp4-3x9w, fixed in 1.42.3); the Studio now bundles 1.42.8 with `prosemirror-model` 1.25.12. A hostile clipboard could otherwise run script in the Studio origin, where API keys live.

- An author's raw HTML can no longer write the plugin host's figure markers: wherever author markup
  spells `data-lattice-hydrate`, `-config`, `-settle`, `-final` or `-off`, the engine renames it
  `data-author-lattice-…`, so a deck cannot forge a pending figure that a plugin draws from a config
  the author packed. Other
  `data-lattice-*` attributes, such as a motion asset's `data-lattice-motion`, are kept.
- On a host that narrowed its default plugin set, an author's raw-HTML
  `<pre><code class="language-mermaid">` of a plugin the deck did not load stays code: its class
  becomes `language-off-mermaid`, which nothing draws.
- The Playground page's editor lint follows the deck's plugin admission, as the Studio's does, and
  re-lints when the host changes its defaults: with math off, a `---` inside `$$` is a slide break
  there too.

- An Export-to-Marp bundle now refuses an author's forged plugin markers, as the engine has since
  #2557: raw HTML in the deck that spells `data-lattice-hydrate`, `-config`, `-settle`, `-final` or
  `-off` is renamed `data-author-lattice-…` in the bundle's Markdown. That includes a `header:` or
  `footer:` directive that spells one only after YAML decodes it (`data-lattice\x2dhydrate`), which
  Marp renders as HTML. A deck with no such markup exports byte-identically.
- In a bundle whose producer left a drawing plugin off, an author's raw
  `<pre><code class="language-mermaid…">` stays code, including one spelled
  `language-mermaid-source`, which the runtime used to draw; so does a ```` ```mermaid-source ````
  fence Marp renders.

- A forged icon drawing in a flowchart or state chart can no longer paint over the whole chart: the repainted icon is clipped two units past its 24-unit grid, and Trama's `drawing()` also drops a shape whose geometry holds a number past 1e4 or one that is not finite. Every one of the 265 shipped icons still paints whole, and the red team's other probes of the repaint are now pinned by tests.

- The Export-to-Marp bundle's two checks of a deck's HTML (the script strip and the forged-marker refusal) no longer miss everything after a front-matter value that opens a code fence. That line made the rest of the deck read as code to both, while Marp rendered it as live HTML.
- The Export-to-Marp bundle's `marp.config.cjs` no longer sets `html: true`. It lists the HTML a deck may carry (text, tables, images, video, `https:` frames, inline SVG with its gradients), and an engine plugin lets through only the bundle's own runtime tags. A tag not on the list shows as text, and no `<script>` of the deck's runs even if the export's strip missed it. The export prints any tag or attribute the list will refuse. Render a bundle with its own `npm run pdf`: `--html` replaces the list with "everything". 421 of the 422 shipped decks render the same; `design/forms.gallery.md` lost two stray lines its last slide carried.
- The bundle's checks now find a deck's front matter by Marp's own rule (a longer `----` opener, a word after the dashes, a longer closer), so those spellings no longer hide the deck from them.

- **Export-to-Marp keeps its runtime and its notes clean when a deck ends in markup left open.** A deck that ended in an unclosed `<iframe>` made the browser read the bundle's runtime `<script>` lines as the frame's text, so the runtime never loaded; the bundle engine now closes an open frame first. A deck that ended in an unclosed `<!--` ran on into the bundle's guard comment, so the guard text appeared in the speaker notes; the note is now cut at the guard. An open `<math>` (`</svg>` does not close MathML) and a nested `<svg>` each lost the runtime or the Mermaid tag too, and are closed the same way. A sweep of 47 hostile tails (open `<textarea>`, `<style>`, `<xmp>`, `<noscript>`, `<noembed>`, `<plaintext>`, `<title>`, nested `<svg>`/`<math>`/`<foreignObject>`, tables, `<template>`, `<select>`, `<form>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<frameset>` and more, at the end of the deck and mid-deck) through real marp-cli and Chromium found no script run, no event-handler attribute, no `<base>` and no unlisted resource.

- **A plugin's fence drawing can no longer paint over the rest of the slide.** An approved zip plugin whose renderer returned a `position:fixed` box covered the whole slide, heading and page number included. The plugin's root now contains its own paint (`contain: paint`), so anything the renderer positions stays inside the plugin's block, and the door drops `popover` and `command` attributes, which would open the browser's top layer over everything. Two layout effects follow for plugin drawings: anything drawn outside the plugin's box is now clipped at its edge, and a child's margins no longer collapse through the root, so a drawing whose first or last child has a margin grows by that margin. Decks without plugins are unaffected.

- **A picture a deck names can no longer reach outside the deck folder through a symlink or a typed `file:///…` address.** The CLI checks the real path of every local file it reads: the PDF/PNG/PPTX render, the `--player` inliner, logo-wall marks and the SVG rasterizer all refuse a file whose real path is outside the deck's folder and Lattice's install, draw the missing-picture stand-in, and name the address on stderr. Before, a symlink to `/etc/hostname` or a stranger's `file:///` address was loaded into the render and baked into the shared player. Decks whose pictures sit inside their folder export byte-identical.

- The CLI now draws function-plot figures for its PDF, PNG, PPTX, `--player` and `--read` exports in a locked page: a fresh, isolated context of the export's own browser, with no network and a strict content policy. It sanitizes each drawing before inserting it into the page being captured. That page no longer loads the function-plot library, and no extra browser starts; an export with plots takes about half a second longer. The plain `.html` export still carries the library, so its plots keep zoom and drag. Exports are byte-identical.

- The CLI and the library API now typeset math with KaTeX behind a wall: QuickJS compiled to WebAssembly, in the same process, with no browser, no access to files, the network or the process, and hard limits on memory (128 MB) and time (5 s per formula). Each result is checked against what KaTeX emits before it is used. Exports are byte-identical. A formula past those limits (nested about 100 deep, or a matrix of thousands of cells) shows its source. A math-heavy deck takes about a quarter of a second longer to render.

- The CLI now draws Mermaid diagrams in a locked browser page: Chromium's OS sandbox where the machine allows it, no network, and a page that can load only Lattice's own Mermaid files. Before, the bake ran with the OS sandbox off on a `file:` page. Exports are byte-identical.

- A package stylesheet that holds a network address in a custom property (`--q: "https://…"`, read by `image-set(var(--q))`) or in an `@property` `initial-value` is now refused. Before, the gate passed it and the export fetched the address. The `image-set()` check now reads past an earlier `url(data:…)` or `type()` option. A plugin's `styles.css` is held to the same rules in the CLI and in the Studio import, ahead of the step that applies it.
- The code-package door's markup filter now reads an address with a tab or newline escaped into it (`ht\9 tps://…`), and a style attribute that uses a form feed or a bare CR as a line break. Both used to slip an address past it.

- **Breaking:** a background image may no longer build a URL from another value: `image-set(var(--header) 1x)` (and `src()`, `image()`, `cross-fade()` beside `var()`, `env()` or `attr()`) is dropped. That route turned a `header:` string into a URL of any scheme (measured: Chromium fetched `http://127.0.0.1/…`). A plain gradient that reads a token (`linear-gradient(var(--accent), red)`) is unchanged.
- A slide's `_backgroundImage: url(…)`, the photo an `image` or `bleed` slide places and the deck `logo:` now follow one scheme allowlist (`lib/core/url-scheme.js`): relative paths, `https:`, `data:image/…`, `sample:` and `asset:` render; `javascript:`, `file:`, `http:`, `data:text/…`, `blob:` and protocol-relative `//host/x` are dropped, and the render carries a `meta/url-scheme` diagnostic (an `image`-slide `![bg]` is dropped silently). Before, a hostile scheme reached a real `background-image` or `<img src>` unchecked. A Windows drive path (`C:\logo.png`) and `http://localhost` are refused too.

- **A deck's own script can no longer stand in for the CLI's slide camera.** The camera ran in the deck's JavaScript world and skipped loading its code when `LatticePdfCompose.captureSlide` already existed, so a deck that defined that global first was handed the export's picture reader and could replace every slide picture in a PNG set, PowerPoint or LibreOffice export. The camera now runs in an isolated world (a second JavaScript context over the same page, the one browser extensions use), and its file reader is bound to that world alone. A deck can still see a picture the camera has already read for one of its slides, as the PDF export already lets it. Every export's pictures are byte-identical to before.
- Two Studio exports started at once (a double click on PowerPoint and LibreOffice) no longer swap picture settings. The `images:` choice was held in one shared variable, so the export that started last decided every picture of both; each export now carries its own.
- An emoji drawn only by a pseudo-element (`h1::before { content: "🎉" }`, or the escape `"\1F389"`) now keeps its emoji font slice in the Studio's exports and in every picture the camera takes, instead of drawing in a fallback face. On the command line this covers CSS in the front matter's `style:` and a `--css` stylesheet, whose emoji used to bring no emoji font into the export at all.
- The slide camera no longer rewrites the word `body` or `html` inside a CSS string or comment: `content: " body "` drew as ` .__lc-body ` in PNG, PowerPoint, LibreOffice and the PDF's photo layer.

- The Studio export's missing-picture check no longer asks for a web background the deck has not allowed. It used to set an image to every background address, so the frame's policy refused it and the export could name it as a missing picture.
- A `<!-- _backgroundImage -->` value written with a CSS escape is refused by the URL scheme check itself, and its diagnostic now says so. The slide renders as before: the engine already dropped such a value.
- A deck with panes now widens its `<style>` blocks only where the browser reads a style element: a `<style-x>` tag, a `<noscript>` body and a style ended early by `</styles>` no longer get pane rules, and a style after `<!-->`, `<!--->` or `--!>` does.

- **The Stage now refuses any script it did not write.** The presenter's Stage window seals itself with the same nonce `script-src` policy the Studio preview carries, and stamps each of its own scripts with the page's nonce. A `<script>` or inline handler that gets past the sanitizer in a shared or AI-written deck no longer runs there. Before, the sanitizer was the only wall.
- New test (#2024): an export made with `--allow-remote` now proves in a real browser that `media-src` and `connect-src` refuse remote video, audio, `fetch`, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource and `sendBeacon`, with a control run that shows the same requests arriving when the policy is removed.

- **Security: a deck of unclosed raw HTML no longer stalls the Studio.** The markup walk that reads a slide's structure scanned its whole open-element stack for each tag, so a pasted slide of 32,000 unclosed `<div>` lines took 11 s to walk and 16,000 lines took 3.4 s to render. The walk now keeps a count of open elements per name and skips a scan whose target is not open: 32,000 lines walk in 24 ms, and the 16,000-line render takes 56 ms. Inputs that open a scope boundary first (`<object>`, `<button>`, an SVG `<foreignObject>`) and then thousands of unclosed tags are still slow, about a second at 16,000 lines; that is recorded for a follow-up.

- **Security: raw HTML can no longer add or remove a slide.** A raw `</section><section>` in a deck closed the engine's slide and opened a new top-level one, which the engine framed and numbered, so every later slide's number moved up by one; a lone `<section>` swallowed the next slide. The engine now renames a raw `<section>` or `</section>` to `<x-section>` / `</x-section>` in every raw-HTML token, the way it already renamed the split's reserved attributes. The content still shows; group it with a `<div>` instead. Speaker notes, descriptions and say lines that mention `<section>` still read as written.

- **A deck full of unterminated `<![CDATA[` sections no longer stalls the web-reference scan.** Inside `<svg>` or `<math>`, each unclosed section searched for its `]]>` to the end of the text again, so 3.4 MB of them held `blockWebImages` for 18 s. Segno's generated readers now remember an `until` search across the reader's calls on the same text; the same input takes under a second, and the scan's result is unchanged.
- **A long run of spaces on a prose slide no longer stalls the render.** Splitting off a trailing running `<footer>` retried a pattern from every space of the run: 128 KB of spaces in a code block took 6.5 s. It is now one pass.

- **`lattice packages add` refuses a zip with a hostile entry name.** An archive whose entries name `..`, an absolute path, a drive letter or a backslash is now refused whole (a harmless `./` prefix is still accepted), before anything is read. Before, JSZip quietly cleaned such names up and the package installed; nothing was written outside the package store, but the archive was accepted. The store's own `install` and `uninstall` now also refuse a package type or name that is not one plain path segment, so a future importer cannot write or delete above the store by skipping the manifest checks.

- The CLI now installs puppeteer 25.17 (it was 23.11), which clears ten high-severity advisories in what
  `npm install @laticent/lattice` pulls in: zip symlink path traversal in `extract-zip`, the proxy-agent
  chain, and `zod` under `chromium-bidi`. The Chrome that puppeteer downloads moves from 131 to 157; PDFs
  rendered on the same Chrome are byte-identical, and the newer Chrome blends translucent tinted fills a
  few color levels differently.
- `image-size` 1.x (with infinite-loop advisories) no longer installs with Lattice: it came only through
  pptxgenjs, which Lattice no longer uses (Calco writes PowerPoint itself; see the native PPTX writer entry).
- Behind a company proxy, puppeteer's Chrome download needs `proxy-agent` installed alongside Lattice;
  puppeteer 25 made it optional.

- **The theme, layout and package gates refuse an address inside `image()`.** A stylesheet that wrote a web address as a
  string inside a function other than `url()` or `image-set()` (`src: image("//…")` in an `@font-face`) passed the gates,
  and Chromium, WebKit and Firefox all fetched it. The gates now refuse an address-shaped string inside any function.
- **The gates and the code door read CSS with the renderer's own reader.** They used to walk CSS by hand to find an
  address held in a custom property; they now read it from the shared CSS reader, which reports the declaration each
  string sits in. Nothing a shipped theme, layout or package does changes.

- **Security: DOMPurify 3.4.11 → 3.4.16 and esbuild 0.28.0 → 0.28.1.** The sanitizer behind
  the Studio's slide preview, the self-contained HTML export and the caption
  projection takes its upstream patch releases,
  which Dependabot's security PR (#1497) could not land because the bump changes three
  committed export bundles. Those bundles are rebuilt here.

- **Breaking:** the plain `.html` export now refuses scripts, frames and stylesheets from anywhere but itself. A deck that puts its own remote `<script src>`, `<iframe>` or `<link rel=stylesheet>` in the `.html` has it refused unless you export with `--allow-remote`; inline scripts, local files, `data:` and `blob:` still work. A script running inside an exported deck could load another script, a frame, a stylesheet or `@import`, or a prefetch from any host; the export's policy now carries `default-src`, `script-src`, `style-src` and `frame-src` limited to the file itself. Measured on real exports in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox: those five loads stop reaching a server, and five decks (KaTeX, Mermaid, function-plot, charts) render with no policy violation and identical screenshots. Navigation, `window.open`, WebRTC, a meta refresh and `target=_blank` links stay possible for a running script in every export, because no content-security directive covers them; that is accepted in the npm-plugin threat model note (§5.4). (`lib/core/export-load-lock.js`, `lattice.js`)

- **Photos no longer carry their metadata out of an export.** A PDF, a self-contained player (`--player`) and an `export:marp` bundle used to embed a photo's own file as it was whenever the image policy did not re-encode it, so a camera JPEG's location, camera name and comments, or a PNG's text chunks, went out with the deck. Every photo now passes through the same cleaner the Studio's Library and the `.lattice` writer use: the metadata is removed and the pixels stay exactly as they were. A photo that was already clean, which includes every photo from the Studio's Library, comes out byte for byte, so only decks whose photos carried metadata export different bytes. A file the cleaner cannot read is never shipped as it is: the PDF keeps it in the slide's picture, the player shows the drawn stand-in, and the Marp bundle leaves it out, each with a note. One exception remains until a follow-up lands (the owner chose to clean it): a photo pasted into the Markdown itself as `data:` text rides verbatim wherever the deck's source travels (the player's embedded source, a `.lattice` file's `deck.md`, `--embed-source`, the Marp bundle's `deck.md`), metadata included.
- **The player cleans every picture a browser draws, and the pictures inside an SVG.** A `data:` picture written as `image/jpg`, in upper case, with a `;name=` parameter, wrapped across lines or percent-encoded used to ship with its metadata, and so did a JPEG inside an SVG, in the player and in an `export:marp` bundle. Each now meets the same cleaner, decided by the file's own bytes; the SVG around it is otherwise unchanged. An address spelled with a CSS escape (`data\3a image/…`) or, inside an SVG, an XML character reference (`data&#58;image/…`) is read the way the browser reads it and cleaned too, and the drawn stand-in for a picture the cleaner cannot read no longer breaks a single-quoted SVG attribute or CSS rule.

- Raw HTML in a deck can no longer carry the `data-split-*` or `data-fluid-*` attributes the engine stamps on split pages. The engine renames them to `data-x-split-*` / `data-x-fluid-*` before rendering, so a deck cannot forge a split page's role, label or page budget.

- **Fixed a script-injection hole in the Export-to-Marp bundle's math.** Marp typesets `$…$` with MathJax, which writes an unescaped `"` into an attribute for `\style`, `\cssId` and similar commands, so a deck could run a handler or load a remote resource in the recipient's `npm run pdf` or VS Code preview, with no click. The export now typesets every equation itself with Lattice's own KaTeX, rebuilds the markup through a strict grammar, escapes every other `$` in the deck (a `header:` or `footer:` directive included), and turns Marp's math off in `marp.config.cjs` and `.vscode/settings.json`.
- Math in an Export-to-Marp bundle now looks like Lattice's own render (KaTeX instead of MathJax) and carries MathML for screen readers. A `math` fence now renders as an equation instead of a code block. The TeX is kept inside each equation's annotation; edit equations in the source deck and re-export.
- In VS Code, open an Export-to-Marp bundle's folder as trusted: in Restricted Mode the extension turns HTML off and the typeset equations lose their layout.

- **The Export-to-Marp bundle no longer runs a deck's own script on the recipient's machine.** The bundle's `marp.config.cjs` needs `html: true` to load the Lattice runtime, and that same flag let marp-cli run a deck's `<script>`, `on…` handlers and `srcdoc` frames during `npm run pdf`. One of them could reach the network. Both the CLI and the Studio's Share sheet now drop those from the bundled deck, along with `javascript:` URLs, and keep Lattice's own runtime tags. Code samples are untouched, and the CLI says what it removed.

- A Mermaid label longer than 500 characters no longer reaches Mermaid's markdown renderer, which could take minutes on crafted text: an 8 KB label rendered in 26.7 s and a 16 KB mindmap label in 16.7 s; both are now refused in under 2 s. Labels are measured across lines (quoted spans in every diagram; bracket labels and lines in mindmap, kanban and architecture). The CLI shows the refused diagram's source as code with a warning; the live preview shows the diagram error box. The longest label in any shipped diagram is 83 characters.

- The Mermaid render worker's own Chromium page now applies the deck-folder file confinement: a flowchart image node (`A@{ img: "file:///…" }`) naming a file whose real path is outside the deck folder gets the missing-picture stand-in, and the CLI names the refusal on stderr. `fileConfine` joins the generic bake services.

- **The door now enforces the owner's admission rules for npm plugins.** A plugin entry marked `source: 'npm'` is admitted as bytes against its pinned SHA-256 and refused if it leaves a dependency external (`import`, `export … from`, `import()`, `import.meta`, any use of `require` or `importScripts`); it does not run where the OS sandbox layer reads OFF or cannot be measured on Linux (code packages keep today's behavior); and nothing in admission or render loads it in Node. No npm door exists yet, so nothing user-facing changes. (`lib/packages/npm-plugin-admission.js`, `lib/core/os-sandbox.js`, `lib/packages/code-door.js`)

- **A hostile-plugin test now guards the code sandbox.** `npm-plugin-canary.test.js` runs a deliberately hostile plugin renderer through the real plugin door and checks that a local HTTP, WebSocket and UDP listener sees nothing and that no storage read returns data; a control arm proves the listener can see each exit. A second test, `npm-plugin-export-check.test.js`, opens the real `--player` and plain HTML exports in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox and lists the exits they leave open. It is marked `todo` until the export policy gaps are closed. (`test/integration/export/`)
- **The code-package door's sanitizer no longer keeps an address hidden in a CSS variable.** A plugin could return `style="--q:'https://x/y'"` on one element and `background-image:image-set(var(--q) 1x)` on another, and the door kept both, so an online page fetched the address. `cssRefTargets` now lists an address-shaped string (a network scheme, `//` or a backslash pair) from any custom property; a label that merely holds `/` or `:` (`--sep:"/"`) is left alone. The package stylesheet gate has the same hole and is logged. (`lib/core/door-attr.mjs`)

- **A small file can no longer make the Studio or the CLI build millions of values.** The size caps bound how much a backup, a `.lattice` file or a package zip inflates to, but not what `JSON.parse` builds from it, and a value can be two bytes: a 3 MB file could ask for a million objects, and a 256 MB one for 134 million numbers. Every JSON file those doors read (a workspace restore, a `.lattice` manifest, and every package manifest, theme `essentials.json`, finish recipe and scene spec, in the Studio and in `lattice packages add`) now has its values counted first, and is refused past one million, far above anything real.
- **A backup with oversized or broken reference docs still restores your decks.** The reference docs and any unreadable scenes in a backup are now skipped when they are too large, unreadable, or hold more than 2,000 rows, and everything else comes back. What was skipped is listed in a notice that is shown again after the Studio reloads and stays until you dismiss it, where it used to vanish with the reload. Only the backup's core (its decks, settings and library) refuses the whole restore, and the message says which part.
- **A backup too large to restore in full now says so when you make it.** If your reference docs are over the 256 MB a restore reads, or your library or settings over their limits, the backup still downloads, and a message that stays up long enough to read says what will not come back. No message means no size limit will refuse the file.
- **Restoring a backup, and saving any new Library item, no longer reads every stored PDF.** The Library store looked up records by reading the whole shelf, reference docs included; it now reads only the kind it needs. A restore with many scenes and a few large reference docs went from about 2 seconds to under 20 ms in the measured case.

- **A workspace backup no longer inflates without bound.** Restoring a backup used to inflate `workspace.json`, the side files and the nested `library.zip` in full, so a few-KB file whose `workspace.json` was a deflate bomb could exhaust the Studio tab's memory. Every read now goes through a size budget: the Studio's own text shares the 64 MB package cap, `library.zip` the 25 MB asset-zip cap, and `refdocs.json` its own 256 MB cap, because reference docs are the one legitimately large part of a backup (a 5 MB PDF rides as 6.7 MB). An oversized backup is refused with "That workspace backup is too large to restore." before any deck or setting is imported, and so is a backup whose `refdocs.json` does not parse.

- **Fixed: `--palette` and `LATTICE_PALETTE` took a PATH, not a name.** The value is joined onto the
  themes directory to build a file path, and the front-matter reader has always constrained it with
  `SAFE_PALETTE_NAME` — but the CLI argument and the environment variable did not. So
  `--palette ../../elsewhere/sheet` loaded a stylesheet from anywhere on disk, measured carrying a
  `section:nth-of-type(6)` rule into an exported artifact. All three sources take the same
  constraint now.
  **It refuses rather than falling back**, because a silent fallback to the default palette is the
  failure `lib/core/resolve-palette.js`'s own docblock was written about: a deck rendering in indaco
  while its author believes they asked for something else. The error names the source that carried
  the bad value.

- **`build:check` now fails when plugin or component code uses the network, storage or our key.** `checkPluginPurity` (G1 of the npm-plugin threat model) parses every source file under `lib/plugins`, `lib/components` and `lib/runtime` and fires on `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `EventSource`, `sendBeacon`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `indexedDB`, `importScripts`, `WebTransport`, `RTCPeerConnection` or an OpenRouter key name, including `window['fetch']` and `process.env.OPEN_ROUTER_KEY`. A file named `.min` or `.generated` is scanned like any other. One use is sanctioned, with its justification: the runtime fetching the deck's own markdown. It adds about 0.3 s. (`tools/check-ownership.js`)

- The package gallery gate (`lattice packages add` and the Studio's Library import) now reads a rendered sample slide with the same `scanHtml` reader the preview and every export use, instead of a parser of its own (parse5 in the CLI, `DOMParser` in the Studio). Where that reader cannot be sure how a browser builds the markup, the gallery is refused, and the reason names the character where it starts. That refuses some sample slides the gate used to admit: an inline SVG that carries a `<style>` or a `<foreignObject>`, a `<select>`, a `<noscript>`, and an HTML Mermaid `<div>` whose text holds markup such as a `<br>`. No shipped gallery is affected: the 96 shipped galleries still import, and all 446 rendered decks and galleries in the repo give the same references as before.

- **Fixed: the inline-run transformer no longer turns an attribute's text into markup.** Its string path read a tag with a regex that stopped at the first `>`, so `<li title="a><img src=x onerror=…>">` ended the tag inside the quoted value and the transformer wrote its `<span class="lat-run">` there, which made the `<img onerror>` a live element. `lib/core/inline-run.js` now reads tags with a small state machine that follows the HTML tokenizer: a quoted value is one piece, an unquoted value ends at whitespace or `>`, a `<script>` body follows the script escape rules, `<title>` and `<style>` are ordinary elements inside SVG and MathML, and a slot's class comes from the `class` attribute itself rather than from any text that looks like one. It also tokenizes a section once instead of once per list item, so a long list or a comment-heavy item no longer costs quadratic time. No shipped deck's output changes: all 322 example and gallery decks render byte-identical HTML. A seeded differential fuzz checks that the string path and the DOM path build the same tree on 800 items full of `>`, `<`, quotes, SVG and script edge cases.
- **Fixed: the Studio preview no longer parses sanitized slide markup twice.** When it patched a new slide into the live frame, `patchSlideBody` parsed DOMPurify's output into a holder, serialized it, and parsed the text again into the same-origin frame. That round trip is where mutation XSS lives: a tree that does not survive it can come back holding an element the sanitizer never saw. The function now moves the holder's parsed nodes with `replaceChildren`, so the frame shows exactly the tree DOMPurify's verdict covers.
- **Fixed: an unterminated `<!-- class:` directive no longer freezes the Studio.** The prose counter stripped class directives with a regex whose three side-by-side whitespace quantifiers backtracked in cubic time when no `-->` followed: 4000 spaces after `<!-- class:` took 24 s, on the main thread, and a shared or imported deck could carry it. `stripClassComments` in `lib/authoring/prose-budgets.js` now does the strip with a linear scan, and `review-core.js` uses that one copy instead of its own. The same input takes under 0.1 ms, and 20,000 unterminated directives take under 1 ms. A differential test pins the scan to the old regex on a seeded corpus and on every Markdown file the repo ships.

- **Security dependency bumps.** DOMPurify 3.4.17 (a critical advisory) and markdown-it 14.3.3 (four quadratic-time advisories), with linkify-it, undici, ws, js-yaml and the rest of `npm audit fix`'s non-major set, at the root and in the docs site. `npm audit --omit=dev` goes from 19 (1 critical) to 11 at the root and from 16 (1 critical) to 4 in docs/; what is left needs a major (puppeteer 25, image-size 2, sharp 0.35, esbuild 0.28). markdown-it 14.3 is linear on unclosed inline `<!--` by itself, so Lattice's own `html_inline` guard is retired. One authoring edge moves with it: a `<!-- … -->` directive opened in a list item and closed after a blank line now runs to its `-->` and applies, as CommonMark says; before, the item's end cut it off.
- **The vendored Mermaid moves to 11.17.2**, so diagram labels are sanitized by DOMPurify 3.4.12 instead of 3.3.1 (21 published advisories down to 5). C4 diagrams now draw people as a head and body, and honor `mode: sketch`. Mermaid 11.17 writes C4 box colors inline, out of the stylesheet's reach, so the engine now sends the deck palette through Mermaid's own C4 color keys. A block diagram's cylinders size to their labels. C4 relationship labels, and their `[technology]` line, now sit centered just above their line, with a halo, instead of drifting into the target box or onto the arrowhead.
- **Raw HTML can no longer forge a slide's number.** An author's `data-lattice-slide` in raw HTML becomes `data-x-lattice-slide`, the way `data-split-*` and `data-fluid-*` already did, so a quote carried across two HTML tokens cannot plant a slide index the split, the slide rail or the Studio would trust. Other `data-lattice-*` names an author writes, such as `data-lattice-motion`, are untouched. The rename also reaches an author `<style>` block, so a selector like `section[data-lattice-slide="2"]` there no longer matches; give the slide a `_class` and select that. Only that exact name is reserved: `data-lattice-slides` passes through. A front-matter `header:`, `footer:` or `class:` that mentions `data-lattice-slide=` no longer switches off slide numbering in the Studio's split preview. A speaker note that mentions one of these reserved names is now stripped by `--strip-notes` too; before, the rename made the note's rendered text differ from its source, and the strip left it in the embedded source.
- **The Export-to-Marp bundle carries its license texts.** Every bundle, from the CLI and from the Studio, now ships `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` with the full MIT and SIL OFL 1.1 texts for Mermaid, dagre-d3-es, Lodash, Tabler Icons and the fonts, and its README names the file. The Marp kit ships the same file from the same source.
- **Live says who sees your IP address.** The Start live session card and the lobby now say that a guest's browser connects directly to everyone in the session, before being let in, and that the public servers that help browsers find each other see the address too.

- **`lint:deck` warns on raw HTML and CSS the preview blocks.** `web-image` now also names a web address in raw HTML
  (`<img src>`, `srcset`, `<video poster>`, SVG `<image href>`, `<link href>`, a refresh `<meta>`), in a `style`,
  `<style>` or `@import`, in a style directive (`backgroundImage`, `color`, …), in a `<style>` inside `<svg>`, in the front matter's `style:`, and in a Mermaid diagram.
  Three new warnings join it: `web-request` (`ping`, `action`, `formaction` to another site), `stripped-markup`
  (`<script>`, `<iframe>`, an `on…=` handler, a `javascript:` address) and `style-ends-early` (a `</style` in the front
  matter's `style:`), plus `markup-unsure` for markup a browser may read differently. The video plugin adds
  `video-web-poster`. Each finding names the exact address. All are warnings, so `lint:deck --strict` fails on them.
- **A repeated front-matter `header:` is read the way the engine reads it.** `web-image` used to check the first
  `header:` or `footer:` and the engine draws the last; it now checks the last.

- **One security policy table.** The tags and attributes the slide sanitizer strips, the attributes that fetch an
  address, and the style tests now live in one file, `lib/core/content-policy.js`, which the renderer reads and the
  linter's coming HTML and CSS rules will read. Nothing a deck renders or exports changes.
- **`lint:deck` warns on a web image.** A new `web-image` warning names each Markdown image (a slide's placed photo
  included) or header and footer image that loads from another site, which the preview shows as a placeholder and the CLI export
  leaves out unless it is run with `--allow-remote`. It is a warning, so `lint:deck --strict` fails on it.
- **A pasted drawing can no longer call another site through an escaped `url(`.** Motion's paste intake strips every
  attribute that fetches from somewhere else, and it now reads them with the web-image scanner's own CSS reader. Its
  old patterns let through `u\72l(…)`, `url( "http:\/\/…" )` and other spellings the browser decodes: 284 such values
  fetched in Chromium, 208 in WebKit and 170 in Firefox, and none get through now.

- The Studio's Reading view no longer lets an escaped `u\72l(https://…)` in a theme's CSS through its last guard. The view drops every web address from the deck sheet it puts in the Studio's own page, and that check matched a literal `url(` only. It now reads CSS with `cssRefSpans`, the reader the exports and the scanner share, and judges each address the way the refusals do, so a tab inside the scheme, a `\\host`, or a non-web scheme such as `chrome-extension://` is caught too. It also drops a nested rule written without `&` (`.a{+ p{…}}`), which it could neither fence nor read, and it reads an escaped at-rule name (`@\70roperty`) as the at-rule, so neither can reach the Studio around the article. The theme gate and the web-image block in front of it already refused a web address unless you had allowed its origin.
- Both player exports (the CLI's `--player` and the Studio's Webpage export) now embed a picture written as `url("photo.png" crossorigin(anonymous))`, as `url("photo.png" /* note */)` or as a `url("photo.png` that the end of a style closes. Chromium loads all three, and the export used to leave the picture out and ship its local path. A picture whose address reaches `image-set()` only through a custom property's string is still not embedded; write it as a `url()` inside the property. The CLI's stand-in for a picture outside the deck folder now paints in a `url('…')` too, where its own quotes used to end the string.

- The docs site no longer loads any runtime dependency from a third-party CDN. Mermaid and KaTeX were self-hosted on the Studio and Playground but fell back to jsdelivr wherever a host did not pass a URL — including the landing page, which renders diagrams and passed none, so it executed a floating `mermaid@11` with no `integrity` check inside the preview frame. Every host now passes the locally-vendored copy, the CDN fallbacks are gone, and a missing URL leaves the diagram unrendered rather than reaching out.
- Exports no longer fetch a stylesheet from a third party at export time. The Studio's `.html` export inlines KaTeX CSS; it used to fall back to a CDN URL when the caller passed none, making a third-party request part of building a file the author hands to someone else.

- **Agent skills and agent instructions we ship are now scanned nightly for security problems** with NVIDIA SkillSpector: the 19 skills in `.claude/skills/`, and every file in the agent kit, exactly as users download it (`dist-kits`): its skills, the files an agent loads on its own (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `lattice.mdc`, the plugin manifests), the paste-in instructions, the component catalog and the bundled deck checker. A finding the reviewed baseline does not excuse opens a tracking issue and lands in the repository's code scanning tab. Run it locally with `npm run scan:skills`.
- Eight sentences across the skills and the component catalog are reworded so the scanner's checks stay fully on: the `lattice-theme` skill writes "deltaE" for the Greek "ΔE", the `cli` and `import` skills no longer use the phrase "no warning(s)" to describe a clean build, and five catalog sentences (bar, gantt, list-steps, team-profile, the chart-family notes) lose "no warning", "without checking" and "without asking".
- **The agent skills now run Lattice as `npx @laticent/lattice`.** They used to say `npx lattice`, and the unscoped `lattice` package on npm belongs to an unrelated publisher, so an agent following a skill outside a Lattice project downloaded and ran someone else's code.
