- **Plugins draw on every layout, and no built-in pass reads their output as an address.** A zip plugin's fences and `@kind{…}` spans used to stay code on the 42 layouts a shipped pass rebuilds from its bullets (the charts, `kanban`, `roadmap`, `team-profile`, `logo-wall`, a `qr` closing slide…), because a pass such as `qr` would have turned a plugin's bullet into a QR code. Every pass that turns slide text into something the viewer loads or scans (the `contact`, `wifi` and `qr` codes, the `video` poster, logo masks, roster and collage photos, the runtime's data probe) now reads through a mask that skips `[data-lattice-plugin]`, on the engine's pass and the runtime's DOM pass alike, so the door draws everywhere. `contact` and `wifi` still keep only their card, as they always have for any code block.
- New `checkSlideTextAddressReaders` gate (`build:check`): a source file that reads slide text (`textContent`, a walk over `<li>`s, a regex hunting `href=`/`src=` in markup) and writes an address (a `src`, `href`, `url()`, poster or QR code) fails the build unless `SANCTIONED_SLIDE_TEXT_ADDRESS_READERS` lists it with its reason. Each entry pins its address writes and its guard calls by COUNT, so a new write or a deleted guard in a large file fails too, and a stale entry fails. Today's 19 readers are listed: 8 that skip plugin output, 11 that build no address from slide text (export readers of a finished document, the consent gate, resolvers that never invent an address).
- **Fixed: a plugin's list item can no longer leave its box.** A plugin fence written inside a bullet, whose output held a bare `<li>`, had that item moved by the browser out of the plugin's box and into the author's list, where the live preview's `qr` pass encoded it (found by this change's red team, before release). The door now refuses an `<li>`, `<dd>` or `<dt>` outside its own list, in the Studio and the CLI; the block stays code with a note saying why.
- A plugin `@kind{…}` span that a chart layout turns into label text (`piechart`, `funnel`) now gets a warning instead of silently showing as written.
- The Reading view and the webpage export's reading document now copy a plugin's drawing whole, with its `[data-lattice-plugin]` root, instead of lifting its lists and paragraphs as if the author had written them.
- Every reading surface (the Studio's Read view, the webpage and player article, `lattice --read`) contains a plugin's paint as a slide does: a `position:fixed` box or the plugin's own stylesheet stays inside the plugin's box, and a wide drawing scales to the reading column.

- **Studio: the slide preview refuses any script it did not write.** The preview frame's Content Security Policy now carries a per-page nonce `script-src` with `'strict-dynamic'`, so an inline event handler or `<script>` in a shared deck cannot run there even if the slide sanitizer missed it. The author's AI keys no longer rest on the sanitizer alone. The CLI export and the other preview surfaces are unchanged.
- **Runtime: `lattice-runtime.js` no longer trusts a clobbered `document.currentScript`.** A deck element named `currentScript` could stand in for the runtime's own `<script>`, and the runtime would load its dagre and plugin-data files from that element's URL. It now accepts only a real `<script>` element.

- **Closed 30 ways a deck's CSS or HTML could load a web resource past Lattice's web-reference checks.** A CSS string a form feed or carriage return ends, escaped or string-only spellings of a URL, character references and attribute separators the HTML parser accepts, an SVG `<style>` the regexes read as plain text, and an address in an SVG paint attribute, an SVG filter image or a table's `background` each let a stranger's gallery past the Library's Insert gate or a deck's images load in the Studio's Reading view without the reader's say-so. Every check now reads CSS with one tokenizer and HTML tags with one scanner, and markup inside `<svg>` that the scanner cannot model is checked with the page's own HTML parser.
- In the Studio's Reading view, which has no content-security policy behind it, a deck's web fonts now wait for the reader's choice like its web images.
- A crafted deck could freeze the Studio while its web images were being blocked: two regexes took 25-50 seconds on 1,000 repeated fragments. The scanner that replaces them reads the same input in milliseconds.

- **The web-reference scanner now removes a web `ping`, `action` and `formaction`.** They send a request when the reader clicks a link or submits a form, not when the page renders, so the scanner had left them in place; the Reading view and the preview frame stopped them with the slide sanitizer and the content-security policy, but a host with neither (the `fonts: true` mode) did not. A web address in one now goes, with its attribute, and appears in `blocked` with its origin so a host can offer to approve it; a relative address, a fragment or an approved origin stays. Exported files change only for a deck that carries a web `ping`, `action` or `formaction`: all 384 decks under `examples/`, the baseline decks and `exemplars/` export byte for byte the same.
- **An allowed origin no longer vouches for an address that only begins with it.** `blockWebImages` decoded an attribute value a second time before reading its origin, so `https://own.example&amp;sol;@evil.example/x` read as the allowed `own.example` where Firefox and Safari read `own.example&sol;` as userinfo and fetch from `evil.example`. It now decodes once. This is a live leak in the Reading view (which allows its own origin) for a `srcset`, a `src` or a style `url()` on Firefox and Safari, found by the checker on the click-time change; Chromium refuses a credentialed subresource, so it did not show there. `attributionsrc` is removed with the other click-time attributes.
- **A `<noscript>` no longer hides an address from the scanner in the Playground's preview.** The scanner read `<noscript>` content as text; the sanitizer that runs after it reads it as markup and keeps the elements, so `<noscript><img srcset=…></noscript>` came out as a live image that Firefox fetched despite the preview's content-security policy. A `<noscript>` now sends the markup to the page's own parser, as a `<select>` does.
- **`&Tab;` and `&NewLine;` split a `ping` or `attributionsrc` list as the browser does.** The scanner decoded both named references to nothing, so `ping="/x&Tab;https://evil.test/p"` joined into one relative address and passed, while a browser reads two addresses and pings the second. They now decode to a real tab and newline, as `&#9;` already did.
- The fuzz now generates `attributionsrc` on an image and a link and clicks the link; Chromium fires them, and the scanner before the click-time change leaked 29 of 3,000 inputs where it now leaks none.
- **A drawn Mermaid diagram is no longer counted as a web image for its XML namespace names.** The scan read `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` as an address, so every deck with a diagram printed "3 web images from http://www.w3.org were left out" in the CLI and showed a Studio notice. An image or link the diagram draws is still counted.

- **The web-reference scanners now refuse five more ways a deck could make the browser fetch from the web.** A seeded fuzz of `blockWebImages` and `blockWebCss` found them: a `<base href="https://…">` (it re-points every relative address on the page), a refresh `<meta>` (it navigates the page; a refresh to a `data:` or `blob:` page is removed whatever its target), an address written without its slashes (`http:host`, `http:/host`, absolute to the URL parser on a `file://` or https page), and, where no content-security policy sits behind the page (the Reading view), an `<iframe srcdoc>` or `data:` page in an iframe, object or embed, and an SMIL animation that sets a link's address. A `<select>` now makes `blockWebImages` ask the page's own parser, because newer browsers parse its content differently. The gallery gate now lists a `<base>` element.
- New `npm run fuzz:web-refs`: generates CSS and HTML from the tokenizer rules, rewrites each input, loads it in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox against a loopback server, and fails on any request. A seeded 600-input slice runs in the integration tier on every PR.
- The fuzz now also generates `<picture>` sources, `xml:base`, a one-second delayed refresh and a two-candidate `srcset`, and waits for late requests; the scanners hold across all of them.
